name: ThunkToThumb
signature: int ThunkToThumb(int arg1, code * arg2, int arg3, int arg4)

name: std_ConstructArray
signature: void * std_ConstructArray(void * base, void (*ctor)(void *), u32 elemSize, u32 count)
summary: Runs a constructor callback once per element of a raw array, advancing by elemSize and stopping after count elements; returns the array base, never the callback result. This is the helper every array-of-objects constructor in the binary was compiled down to.
evidence: Body: iVar1 = base; while (arg4) { (*arg2)(iVar1); iVar1 += arg3; } return base. Disassembly shows an actual `blx r6` per element, so the second argument is a code pointer, not a fill value. 593 callers including Engine_Initialize@0x101b74, 0x109990 (2 slots of 10 bytes at +0x31ce), 0x1064d8 (5 slots of 0x10 at +0x34), 0x1064d8/0x15cdc4. Every code-pointer argument used with it dereferences to a code address in code.decompressed.bin: g_0010672c -> 0x107f6c, g_00109d94 -> 0x10f3b4, g_0010e42c/30/34 -> 0x116798/0x1167b0/0x116780, g_00114270 -> 0x11982c, g_001144b0 -> 0x119838, g_0011deac -> 0x1235e0, g_00124478 -> 0x1150a0, g_001221bc -> 0x106a10; and the object each ctor fills starts with a vtable pointer (e.g. g_00106728 -> 0x7821c8). This is the array-of-objects construction helper, not memset/memcpy (N_081's merge note guesses memcpy for this address - that is wrong).

name: std_RunTerminateHandler
summary: C++ terminate path: fetches the lazily created terminate-state object, invokes the installed handler (or the built-in default at obj+8 when none is installed), then calls the no-return runtime abort routine 0x11C810.
evidence: NEW: the callee is now the named maybe_std_GetTerminateState (still maybe_, but its body is the lazy terminate-state builder), and the shape (clear the handler slot, call it, then jump into the abort routine that never returns) is the standard terminate definition. It sits in the Thumb CRT block, so it is library code.

name: maybe_std_AllocRuntimeBlock
summary: Allocates one 0x88-byte block through Mem_Alloc and clears its first byte. The terminate-state holder (0x00100102) stores the result at its +0x1C field.
evidence: The allocator is the confident Mem_Alloc, so the allocation is certain; the 0x88 size exists only in the disassembly (movs r0,#0x88) and the C++ type behind it is not recoverable, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: std_Abort
summary: Low-level CRT abort entrypoint in thumb mode; invokes the core runtime abort handler func_0011C810 without returning.
evidence: Thumb wrapper jumping directly to func_0011C810, the runtime abort/terminate handler; called on unrecoverable CRT exceptions.

name: maybe_std_GetTerminateState
summary: Lazily creates the CRT terminate-state record: allocates 0x20 bytes, stores the default terminate handler 0x001000FD at +8, clears the remaining fields and attaches the 0x88-byte scratch block from 0x001000BA; returns the cached record.
evidence: The callee is the confident Mem_Alloc (0.75) and the caller is std_RunTerminateHandler, so the record/handler shape is clear; but that caller is itself only 0.45, and the scratch-block helper at 0x001000B8 is unnamed, so the 'terminate' semantics are not independently confirmed.

name: std_tolower
summary: ctype tolower: returns c+0x20 when the locale ctype mask for c has bit 4 (the 'upper' class) set, otherwise c. Used by the Squirrel native that lowercases a script string.
evidence: Body is `p = ctype_table(); return (table[c] & 0x10) ? c + 0x20 : c` (assembly: ldrb, lsls #0x1b, bpl, adds #0x20) via the table accessor 0x002FF68C. Only non-self caller 0x0014F008 walks the 4-byte string it obtained from 0x005B5C6C and stores the converted bytes through 0x00245CF0/0x006111A4, i.e. a script-visible string transform; 0x0014F10C is the matching toupper native.

name: std_toupper
summary: ctype toupper: returns c-0x20 when the ctype mask has bit 3 (the 'lower' class) set and c is not 0xDF (Latin-1 sharp s, which has no single-byte uppercase), otherwise c.
evidence: `(table[c] & 0x08) && c != 0xdf ? c - 0x20 : c` (lsls #0x1c, cmp #0xdf). Callers 0x0014F10C (script string uppercaser, mirror of 0x0014F008) and 0x005FB388.

name: std_ThrowNarrowRange
signature: void std_ThrowNarrowRange(const char* msg, int len)
summary: Fixed-kind variant of the narrow throw helper: builds the [msg, msg+len) range and throws it with this entry's own literal.
evidence: Its parameterised sibling 0x001001C4 is now readable as the same three-step sequence (range build, throw, cleanup), confirming the family; only the literal's error class is missing.

name: std_ThrowNarrowRangeEx
signature: void std_ThrowNarrowRangeEx(const char* msg, int len, void* kind, void* typeinfo)
summary: Parameterised C++ runtime throw helper: builds the [msg, msg+len) range in a local exception object and throws it with the caller-supplied kind/typeinfo and a fixed per-function literal.
evidence: All callers are now visible (the narrow-string format constructors and two script-string sites) and the body only wraps the range, confirming the throw-helper family; only the exception class literal is unknown.

name: std_ThrowWideRange
signature: u32 std_ThrowWideRange(const u16* msg, u32 len, void* kind, void* typeinfo)
summary: Throws/format-checks a UTF-16 range for the basic_string<wchar_t> layer: builds the two-byte-stride range end (msg + len*2 - 2) and returns the formatted length or 0xFFFFFFFF when the range did not fit.
evidence: All 18 call sites are the std_WString format constructors (maybe_std_WString_FormatCtorA..G and std_WString_FormatInitA..E) calling it as std_ThrowWideRange(out + 1, capacity, ...), i.e. the same wide-string range primitive; the 16-bit stride in the body matches the wchar_t buffer those ctors build.

name: std_ThrowNarrowFixed
summary: Throw helper for a single already-built message object: wraps it in a one-element range and throws without a following cleanup call.
evidence: Readable as the same throw primitive as its siblings with the length implied; the family is certain and the individual error class is not.

name: std_ThrowNarrowRange2
signature: void std_ThrowNarrowRange2(const char* msg, int len)
summary: Byte-for-byte twin of 0x0010018A with a different fixed literal: the same narrow range throw reporting a different error class.
evidence: The two bodies compare as identical apart from the literal pointer, exactly the six-function throw family shape; only the literal meaning is missing.

name: maybe_std_ThrowWideRange2
signature: void maybe_std_ThrowWideRange2(const u16* msg, u32 len)
summary: Wide-character twin of 0x00100272: builds a two-byte-stride range over the message, throws it through std_vprintf_flags1, and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when the formatted length does not fit in len.
evidence: Identical to 0x001001FC apart from the literal, completing the narrow/wide range/fixed matrix of six throw helpers; the shared body is the only evidence, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: std_FormatPutStringNarrow
signature: void std_FormatPutStringNarrow(FormatStream* stream, const char* text, u32 precision)
summary: Writes a narrow (char) string into a printf-style format sink, honouring the field precision and updating the remaining-width and written-count fields; each byte is handed to the sink's putc callback.
evidence: Called by 0x100C3C's narrow path; body loops text[0..precision] and calls (*stream->putc)(byte, stream->cookie) inside 0x2FF71C/0x2FF748 (padding begin/end); stream layout matches the printf stream used by std_PrintfFormatInt (0x1003F8, N_001) and std_PrintfFormatFloat (0x300090, N_001).

name: std_PrintfFormatInt32
signature: void std_PrintfFormatInt32(FormatStream* stream, int conv, va_list* ap)
summary: Formats a 32-bit signed/unsigned decimal integer (%d/%u/i) for the printf core: extracts the value from the va_list, builds the sign/space/plus prefix, converts digits and emits them through the shared padding writer.
evidence: conv==0x75 ('u') takes the unsigned path via 0x2FF780 (va_arg), otherwise 0x2FF76A (signed divmod) with sign detection and prefixes at 0x1003B0/0x1003B4/0x1003B8/0x1003BC; calls 0x2FF798 for digit extraction and 0x2FF7C4 (padding/zero-fill writer). Sits immediately before std_PrintfFormatInt (0x1003F8, N_001) which is the 64-bit variant.

name: std_PrintfFormatInt
signature: void std_PrintfFormatInt(PrintfStream* out, int conv, s64 value)
summary: Emits one integer conversion for printf: writes the decimal digits of the 64-bit value into the stream buffer at out+0x24, chooses the sign prefix from the stream flags (minus / plus / space) and hands it to the padding writer. Used by the %d/%i/%u family; conv == 0xf5 skips sign handling.
evidence: Stream layout matches the CRT printf state: [0]=flags (bit1 = negative, bit2 = plus), [4]=putc callback, [0x18]=field width, [0x1c]=precision, [0x20]=chars written, +0x24=digit buffer. Tail call to std_PrintfEmitPadded (0x002FF7C4); digit loop calls 0x002FF874 (u64 divide by 10); sign strings "-" "+" " " live at 0x0010045C/0x00100460/0x00100464.

name: std_strtol
signature: long std_strtol(const char* s, char** endptr, int base)
summary: strtol: skips leading ctype-space bytes, consumes an optional '+'/'-', delegates the digits to 0x002FF91A, restores *endptr = s when no digit was consumed, sets errno (via 0x002FF9C4) to 2 (ERANGE) on overflow and negates the magnitude for '-'. Returns the value in the low half of the Ghidra u64.
evidence: Skip loop `while (ctype_table()[*p] & 1)`; sign characters 0x2b/0x2d; `*__errno_location() = 2` plus the classic 0x80000000 clamp on positive overflow (LONG_MIN); `if (endptr && *endptr == digits) *endptr = s`. Caller 0x00165004 (Squirrel standard library).

name: std_PrintfFormatHex64
signature: void std_PrintfFormatHex64(FormatStream* stream, int conv, u32 hi, u32 lo)
summary: Formats a 64-bit value as hexadecimal (%x/%X), building digits from the 64-bit hi:lo pair and emitting the selected '0x' prefix plus zero padding.
evidence: Nibble loop over arg3/arg4 with shifts (hi:lo 64-bit), digit table selected by the 0x800 flag (0x1004F0/0x100504), '0x' prefix added when conv==0x70 ('p'), then 0x2FF7C4. Same calling convention as std_PrintfFormatOctal64 (0x100E18).

name: std_PrintfFormatHexArg
signature: void std_PrintfFormatHexArg(FormatStream* stream, int conv, va_list* ap)
summary: va_arg wrapper for the hex formatter: fetches a 32-bit argument from the va_list and delegates to std_PrintfFormatHex64 with a zero high word.
evidence: Body is exactly `uVar1 = func_002FF780(*arg3, arg1); func_001004E0(arg1, arg2, uVar1, 0);` - va_arg helper 0x2FF780 (the same helper used for 'u' in 0x100354) plus the 64-bit hex formatter; mirrors std_PrintfFormatOctalArg (0x100E5C).

name: std_strtoul
signature: unsigned long std_strtoul(const char* s, char** endptr, int base)
summary: strtoul: same skip/sign/errno front end as strtol but it saves and restores errno around the conversion and negates the magnitude for a leading '-', which is exactly the strtoul unsigned-wraparound contract.
evidence: Saves `*__errno_location()` into iVar2 and restores it unless the callee set 2, then `if (sign_flag) result = -result`; otherwise byte-identical to 0x00100468. Called from 0x005FBAC0 (script string->number).

name: std_strtodThunk
signature: double std_strtodThunk(const char* text, char** end)
summary: Eight-byte pass-through trampoline into std_strtod (push {r4,lr}; bl std_strtod; pop {r4,pc}) that leaves all argument registers untouched, so it is an alternate entry point to the double parser rather than atof (which would clear the end pointer).
evidence: NEW: the only callers are the 0x50xxxx math/format block (0x502E20, 0x503298), not the printf core, and the disassembly shows no argument setup at all - which confirms the trampoline reading and rules out atof. (Change corrected because the older spelling "Strtod" is fixed to std_strtod's own name.)

name: std_mbstowcs
signature: int std_mbstowcs(u16 * dst, const u8 * src, u32 maxChars, mbstate * state)
summary: Converts a multibyte byte string (current locale encoding) into a 16-bit wide-character buffer, one character per call to the locale decoder, stopping at the terminating NUL or after maxChars characters, and returns the number of wide characters stored.
evidence: Loop reads one byte, calls 0x2ff9d0 (locale mbrtowc dispatch: it tail-calls the encoding function at state->f_103) and stores the resulting wchar with `*(short*)(arg1 + i*2)`; loop exits on wchar==0 or i>=arg3; callers 0x502650/0x502928 are in the libc string/format block next to std_mbrlen@0x100658 and std_mbrtowc@0x10067c.

name: std_mbrlen
signature: int std_mbrlen(const char* s, int n, mbstate_t* ps)
summary: C89 mbrlen: measures how many bytes of a multibyte sequence are consumed, using the caller's mbstate and returning -2 for an incomplete sequence and -1 for an illegal one.
evidence: Tail-calls 0x10067C (mbrtowc) with pwc=NULL, i.e. func_0010067C(0,s,n,ps); handles the NULL-s default ('\0' one-byte sequence); both return codes -1/-2 are the C standard's (size_t)-1/-2 conventions.

name: std_mbrtowc
signature: int std_mbrtowc(u16* pwc, const char* s, int n, mbstate_t* ps)
summary: C99 mbrtowc: decodes one multibyte character into a wide character using the current locale's converter, returning the bytes consumed, 0 for a null character, -2 for an incomplete sequence and -1 (setting errno EILSEQ) for an invalid one.
evidence: Uses the locale hook 0x2FF9D0 (same converter the printf code uses) with the caller's mbstate; sets errno through 0x2FF9C4 ('*puVar2 = 4') on invalid input; signature (pwc,s,n,ps) and -1/-2 returns match the C standard; callers are std_mbrlen (0x100658) and the wide/multibyte printf paths.

name: std_qsort_internal_quicksort
signature: void std_qsort_internal_quicksort(void* base, u32 arg2, size_t count, size_t size, int (*cmp)(const void*, const void*))
summary: The recursive half of the C library qsort: median-of-three quicksort over byte-sized elements with an explicit 32-entry stack, swapping whole elements with 4-byte-word copies when both pointers are aligned and byte copies otherwise, recursing only into partitions larger than 10 elements.
evidence: Element swaps are `size` bytes wide with a word fast path when `(size|ptr)&3 == 0`; median-of-three pivot; partition loop compares with `(*cmp)(a,b) > 0`; the larger partition is pushed on auStack_134/auStack_b4 and the smaller iterated; `if (uVar3 < 0xb)` is the 10-element cut-off that matches 0x00100906; element index arithmetic goes through 0x0011CFAC.

name: std_qsort
signature: void std_qsort(void* base, size_t count, size_t size, int (*cmp)(const void*, const void*))
summary: qsort entry point: for 10 elements or fewer it runs the inlined insertion sort (shifting each element while the comparator says it is smaller), otherwise it hands the array to the quicksort at 0x001006F0.
evidence: `if (count > 10) func_001006F0(...)` then the textbook insertion sort `while (base <= p && cmp(p, p+size) > 0) p -= size;` with element moves as 4-byte or byte copies; 23 callers spread over the whole program, which is what a libc qsort looks like.

name: std_strncat
signature: char* std_strncat(char* dest, const char* src, int count)
summary: Appends src to the NUL-terminated string in dest, copying at most count bytes and always writing a terminator when the budget runs out. This is the Thumb CRT strncat used all over the model/UI code.
evidence: Thumb leaf: first loop scans dest for its NUL, second copies src bytes until count hits 0 then writes 0. 12 callers including 0x00222E90, 0x002232FC, 0x002C5E40 and CRT callers at 0x006105B4/0x00707A7C; exact strncat semantics.

name: std_strstr
signature: char* std_strstr(const char* haystack, const char* needle)
summary: strstr: returns a pointer to the first occurrence of needle in haystack (haystack itself for an empty needle) or NULL. Naive restart-at-next-character loop.
evidence: Nested compare; on mismatch it restarts at `pcVar4` (candidate+1), returns the candidate when the needle byte is NUL and returns 0 when the haystack byte is NUL. 15 callers (0x00165004, 0x004B3604, 0x00576CC0, ...) all string handling.

name: std_MemCmp
signature: int std_MemCmp(const void* s1, const void* s2, size_t n, u32 alignMask)
summary: Optimized CRT block memory comparison; performs 32-bit word comparison when word-aligned and byte-by-byte comparison otherwise.
evidence: Compares 4 bytes per loop when (alignMask & 3) == 0, evaluates byte difference upon word mismatch, then finishes trailing unaligned bytes.

name: std_wcsncpy
signature: u16 * std_wcsncpy(u16 * dst, const u16 * src, int count)
summary: Copies at most count wide characters and zero-fills the remainder: once the source NUL is copied the source pointer stops advancing, which is exactly the wcsncpy contract.
evidence: Body: while (count--) { *dst++ = *src; if (*src) src++; } return dst; the conditional advance is the c89 wcsncpy padding idiom. 16 callers include Actor_CompareNames@0x147dc4, Text_LayoutPage_BuildLines@0x2fd45c and 0x1918 0x19180c (seven-character short-name field of a text page).

name: std_wcsncat
signature: u16* std_wcsncat(u16* dest, const u16* src, int count)
summary: Wide-character strncat: finds the end of dest, appends at most count wide characters from src and terminates the result.
evidence: Body: scan dest for 0, copy up to count src elements, write terminating 0, return dest. Exact wcsncat semantics; sibling 0x100AD6 was named std_Utf16CompareN by N_032 so the UTF-16 vocabulary is already established.

name: std_Utf16CompareN
signature: int std_Utf16CompareN(const unsigned short* left, const unsigned short* right, int count)
summary: Compares two UTF-16 strings for at most `count` code units and returns the difference of the first differing unit (0 at the end of `left`). Used by the script/text layer to compare wide-character names with a bounded length.
evidence: Body walks `u16*` pairs: `while (count) { u = *a; if (!u || u != *b) break; a++; b++; count--; } return u - *b;` - exactly wcsncmp over 16-bit units. Callers 0x005142CC, 0x007116A0, 0x007118CC are script/name lookup helpers.

name: Str_WcsPbrk
signature: wchar_t* Str_WcsPbrk(const wchar_t* str, const wchar_t* accept)
summary: Scans a 16-bit null-terminated wide string for the first occurrence of any character from a given accept set.
evidence: Outer loop scans 16-bit characters in str until null terminator; inner loop tests membership in wide char string accept; returns matching character pointer or NULL.

name: Str_WcsStr
signature: wchar_t* Str_WcsStr(const wchar_t* haystack, const wchar_t* needle)
summary: Finds the first occurrence of wide substring needle in wide string haystack.
evidence: Iterates over 16-bit characters in haystack comparing substring against needle; returns pointer to first match or NULL if haystack ends.

name: std_RunPreinitArray
summary: Calls every entry of the CRT pre-initialiser table (0x00799C94..0x0079AA18). Each slot stores an offset relative to its own address, so the runner adds the slot address to the word before calling it - the position-independent form of .preinit_array/.init_array used by the statically linked C++ runtime.
evidence: ResetVector (0x00100000) calls it 5th, after the heap region has been committed by 0x00104400 and before the other two init-list runners. Assembly: push {r4,r5,r6,lr}; ldr r4,[pc,#0x18]; add r4,pc; ldr r5,[pc,#0x18]; add r5,pc; loop: ldr r0,[r4]; add r0,r4; blx r0; adds r4,#4; cmp r4,r5. Literals at 0x00100BBC/0x00100BC0 give 0x00799C94 and 0x0079AA18, i.e. 865 slots (0xD84 bytes). Only caller besides itself: ResetVector.

name: std_operator_delete_array
summary: operator delete[] for arrays of class objects: destroys the elements through the array cookie (size at p-8, count at p-4) using 0x00100BE0 and then releases the allocation with 0x0010F69C.
evidence: `func_00101A80(p, dtor)` (= destroy through the cookie) followed by `func_0010F69C()` (heap free). 24 callers, all object teardowns; e.g. Ui_ListWindow_Teardown 0x0029ED50 does `func_00100BCC(self->f_3c, g_0029EEF0); self->f_3c = 0;`.

name: std_destroy_range
signature: void* std_destroy_range(void* first, void (*dtor)(void*), size_t elemSize, int count)
summary: Destroys an array of class objects backwards (i = count-1 .. 0 calling dtor(first + i*elemSize)) and returns first-8, the allocation pointer behind the 8-byte array cookie. This is the 4-argument form the compiler emits for every array destruction; 239 call sites.
evidence: `iVar1 = arg4*arg3 + arg1; do { iVar1 -= arg3; (*arg2)(iVar1); } while (arg1 != iVar1); return arg1-8;`. Typical call 0x0017CF60: `func_00100BE0(arg1+3, g_0017D040, 0x24, 5)`.

name: std_GetErrno
summary: Retrieves current thread errno value from the thread-local storage errno pointer returned by __aeabi_errno_addr.
evidence: Calls func_002FF9C4 (__aeabi_errno_addr) and dereferences the returned pointer; adjacent to func_00100C16 which sets errno.

name: std_SetErrno
summary: Stores err into the C library errno cell. Called by the soft-float and libm routines when they detect a domain/range error, so the value is what the caller sees in errno afterwards.
evidence: func_002FF9C4 returns the address of the per-process errno word (ldr r0,[pc,#0] -> 0x007F3020); this wrapper just does *errno_location() = arg1. 11 callers, all math/format helpers (sqrt, atan family, printf float formatting).

name: std_FormatPutStringNarrowDispatch
summary: Chooses how to emit a narrow %s argument: if the stream is in byte mode it writes the bytes verbatim, otherwise it converts the multibyte text to wide characters first.
evidence: Checks stream+0x14 (wide-mode flag) and calls 0x1002F8 (byte writer) when 0 or 0x100D28 (multibyte-to-wide) otherwise, returns 1; identical dispatch shape to 0x100FB4 (maybe_std_FormatSinkPutString, N_037) which handles %ls.

name: std_FormatSinkPutNarrow
signature: void std_FormatSinkPutNarrow(void* sink, const u16* src, int count)
summary: Copies a UTF-16 run into a narrow printf sink: converts each unit through the locale codec, stops at the terminator or the sink's hard limit, and when the width budget would be exceeded flushes, pads with PadZero/PadSpace, emits the already-converted bytes through the callback at sink+4 and charges the budget.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named std_FormatSinkPutString and the pad helpers are named std_Format_PadZero/PadSpace, so this is unambiguously the narrow-character branch of the std printf sink family; the codec call is the only unnamed callee.

name: std_FormatPutMultibyteAsWide
signature: void std_FormatPutMultibyteAsWide(FormatStream* stream, const char* text, int count)
summary: Emits a multibyte string to a wide-character sink: a first pass counts characters with mbrtowc (honouring precision in characters, not bytes) and a second pass converts and writes each wide character.
evidence: Two passes using 0x2FF9D0 (mbrtowc); decrements stream->f_18 by the character count, then calls the sink callback with u16 values and increments f_20; the stream flags at +0x1c hold the precision limit.

name: std_FormatPutStringWide
signature: void std_FormatPutStringWide(FormatStream* stream, const u16* text, u32 precision)
summary: Writes a wide (UTF-16) string into a wide printf sink, honouring precision and updating width/count fields; the mirror image of std_FormatPutStringNarrow.
evidence: Same structure as 0x1002F8 but indexed on u16 and calling the sink with each u16; called by 0x100FB4 when the stream is in wide mode.

name: std_PrintfFormatOctal64
signature: void std_PrintfFormatOctal64(FormatStream* stream, u32 conv, u32 hi, u32 lo)
summary: Formats a 64-bit value as octal (%o), including the alternate-form leading '0' and zero padding.
evidence: Three-bit digit loop over hi:lo (`arg3 & 7` + '0'), the 0x20 flag forces the leading zero and decrements the width field, then 0x2FF7C4; direct sibling of the hex formatter 0x1004E0.

name: std_PrintfFormatOctalArg
signature: void std_PrintfFormatOctalArg(FormatStream* stream, u32 conv, va_list* ap)
summary: va_arg wrapper for the octal formatter: fetches a 64-bit argument and splits it into high/low words for std_PrintfFormatOctal64.
evidence: Body: `uVar1 = func_002FF780(*arg3,arg1); func_00100E18(arg1,arg2,uVar1>>32,uVar1,0);` - 64-bit va_arg helper plus the octal formatter.

name: std_strtod
signature: double std_strtod(const char* s, char** endptr)
summary: strtod: skips ctype-space, handles '+'/'-', calls the floating-point scanner 0x00101026, sets *endptr back to s when nothing was consumed, sets errno = 2 (ERANGE) on overflow and negates for '-'.
evidence: Same skip/sign/errno front end as 0x00100468/0x00100578 but the payload call is 0x00101026, which uses 0x003006F0 and 0x00300940 (the soft-float double helpers), and the result is returned as a double. Caller 0x001005EE.

name: std_SetLocaleCategory
summary: CRT helper that initializes or applies default locale category settings by invoking func_006740E4 with category ID 12.
evidence: Passes category constant 0xC (12) to locale handler func_006740E4; sits alongside CRT ctype/locale table helpers.

name: std_isspace
summary: ctype isspace: returns bit 0 of the locale ctype mask, the whitespace class - the exact predicate the strtol/strtoul/strtod front ends use to skip leading blanks.
evidence: `return ctype_table()[c] & 1;` using the same accessor 0x002FF68C whose bit 4 = upper (0x00100150) and bit 3 = lower (0x0010016A); the skip loops of 0x00100468/0x00100578/0x00100E88 test exactly this bit.

name: std_PrintfFormatSpecialFloat
signature: void std_PrintfFormatSpecialFloat(FormatStream* stream, u32 flags, int conv, int sign)
summary: Emits the three-character special float spellings (inf/INF/nan/NAN) for the printf core, adjusting the width by the sign character and honouring the uppercase flag.
evidence: Exactly three characters are written from one of the four 3-byte literals at 0x100F9C/0x100FA0/0x100FA4/0x100FA8, selected by conv<7 and the 0x800 uppercase flag; width field (stream+0x18) is reduced by 3 or 4; caller is std_PrintfFormatFloat (0x300090, N_001).

name: std_FormatSinkPutString
signature: u32 std_FormatSinkPutString(void* self, const u16* src, int length)
summary: Entry point of the format character sink: dispatches to the locale-converting writer (0x00100C6C) when the sink's +0x14 selector is zero and to the direct wide writer (std_FormatPutStringWide) otherwise, always reporting success.
evidence: NEW: one of the two branches is the confident std_FormatPutStringWide (0.65) and the other is maybe_std_FormatSinkPutNarrow (0.4); the sink layout ({callback, ctx, budget, written, limit}) is shared by both writers, which confirms the dispatcher role.

name: std_strtod_core
signature: double std_strtod_core(const char* digits, char** endptr, int arg3)
summary: The actual decimal/hex floating-point scanner behind strtod: accumulates the mantissa and binary exponent and scales with the soft-float double helpers, returning the double; the wrapper 0x00100E88 applies the sign and errno.
evidence: Called with the character after the sign by 0x00100E88 (strtod); writes `*__errno_location()` itself and calls the soft-float double routines in 0x0030xxxx (0x003006F0, 0x00300940), returning a value in r0/r1 (double).

name: std_StrtofCore
signature: float std_StrtofCore(FloatResult* result, const char* digits, const char* exponent, int exp2)
summary: Turns the already-scanned decimal digit string plus its decimal exponent into a float: builds the 64-bit mantissa, normalises it, scales by the power of ten, applies the current rounding mode and stores the 32-bit result, setting ERANGE when the value overflows.
evidence: Called only from std_Strtod (0x00101314). Digit strings are 0xff terminated; sign/exponent computed with a shift-subtract loop; uses 0x002FFDC0 (rounding mode), 0x00126848/0x00126878 (double mul/div by 10^k), 0x00300D50 (double->float narrowing). Result is a 2-word struct (value + status) exactly like the RVCT strtod worker.

name: std_Strtod
signature: double std_Strtod(const char* text, char** end, int* status, ScanCtx* ctx)
summary: The C library strtod: reads sign, digits, decimal separator (from the locale block), "0x" hex floats and an exponent through the ctx getc/ungetc callbacks and returns the parsed double, updating the end pointer and the conversion status.
evidence: Uses ctx callbacks at +0x18/+0x20/+0x1c/+0x10 (getc, peek, ungetc, locale); accepts i/n (inf/nan), 0x (calls 0x001015D8 hex path), decimal point from locale block (*ctx[0])->+0xc; ends in std_StrtofCore/std_DoubleConvert. Only caller 0x00300714 is the scanf float handler.

name: std_ParseHexFloat
signature: int std_ParseHexFloat(char* buf, char** end, u16* out, ScanCtx* ctx, int pos, u32 flags, int len)
summary: Parses the significand of a hexadecimal float literal ("0x1.8p3") into a double and applies the binary exponent; returns the number of characters consumed or -2 on a malformed literal.
evidence: Collects up to 16 mantissa nibbles with func_003006F0(ch,16) (digit value), keeps a 6-bit shift counter, handles "p"/"P" binary exponents with +/- and calls 0x006B8138 (ldexp) plus the rounding mode from 0x002FFDC0. Reached from strtod through the 0x001015D8 alias.

name: std_ParseInfNan
signature: int std_ParseInfNan(u32 lo, u32 hi, int* endpos, int* scanctx, int pos, u32 bits, int len, int ch)
summary: Recognises the textual 'inf', 'infinity' and 'nan(...)' forms in strtod and fills the result's float bits (infinity plus optional sign, or a quiet NaN with the parenthesised payload skipped).
evidence: Compares the current character against 'I'/'N' (mask 0xffffffdf) and expects 'nf'/'aN'; on success writes 0x7F800000-style exponent bits and 0x400000 quiet-NaN bit into the float union; sibling 0x101314 std_Strtod / 0x101100 std_StrtofCore (N_001) are its only logical callers.

name: std_uninitialized_copy
signature: void* std_uninitialized_copy(void* dst, const void* src, size_t stride, int count, void (*ctor)(void*, const void*))
summary: Copy-constructs count elements from src to dst: calls the element constructor for each pair and advances both pointers by the stride, returning dst. The compiler's uninitialized_copy loop for non-trivial element types.
evidence: `while (count--) { (*ctor)(dst, src); src += stride; dst += stride; } return dst;` - the (dst, src, stride, count, ctor) signature and the two-pointer walk are the standard shape; single caller 0x0058FF38 (script engine).

name: std_vec_delete_from_cookie
summary: Readable-C fragment of the vector-delete helper: destroys the elements of an array using the size/count pair stored immediately before the array (the ARMCC array cookie) and leaves the raw deallocation to the caller.
evidence: `func_00100BE0(arg1, arg2, *(u32*)(arg1-8), *(u32*)(arg1-4))` - the two words in front of the array are element size (p-8) and element count (p-4); only reachable from 0x00100BCC, which adds the free.

name: maybe_Thunk_Call00100F04
summary: Eight-byte Thumb thunk: `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x100F04; pop {r4,pc}`. The callee is itself a two-argument wrapper (`movs r1,r0; movs r0,#0xc; blx 0x3007B8`) that passes the original argument on with a leading 0xC, and 0x3007B8 has no readable body, so neither the thunk nor its target can be identified.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly at 0x101AA0 is exactly four instructions (8 bytes), not the 212 the function index claims, and the callee 0x100F04 is a two-argument wrapper around the CRT helper 0x3007B8 with first argument 0xC. Nothing in that chain is an abort, so the batch's previous name maybe_std_Abort is unsupported; the address-based thunk name states only what is verified.

name: Engine_Initialize
summary: One-time engine bring-up: initialises the heap system (InitHeaps), then lazily creates and wires every global subsystem singleton (resource caches, renderer, sound, task pool, input) using the repeated 'init-flag + aligned size + allocate + construct' pattern.
evidence: No callers (called from the startup/init table), it is the only caller of InitHeaps (0x102EF8) besides itself, creates ~12 globals via func_00116AE0(size, tag) + ctor (0x103724, 0x104A38, 0x1052C8, 0x104ED8, 0x103594, 0x10293C...), and finally calls func_00107D00/0x102EC0; mode 'arm' with a 0xC78 body.

name: std_RunInitArray
summary: Calls every absolute function pointer between the two bound words at 0x0079AA18 and 0x0079AA1C. In the retail image both bounds hold the same value, so the list is linked empty - it exists for libraries that register static constructors into it at link time.
evidence: ResetVector calls it after std_RunPreinitArray. Body is only `puVar1 = g_0010281c; for (puVar2 = g_00102818; puVar2 < puVar1; puVar2++) (*(code*)*puVar2)();`. Both literal-pool words at 0x00102818/0x0010281C contain 0x0079AA18, and nothing else in the image writes 0x0079AA18 (checked with a full-image pointer scan), so the array is empty in retail.

name: maybe_Os_InitStringRecord
summary: Fills a record obtained from 0x300308(0, 0x04000027) with two built-in strings: field +4 gets the first getter's result plus one (skipping a length or prefix byte) and field +0xC gets the second getter's result. The old 'Time' label was unsupported - nothing in the body reads a clock.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly 0x102828-0x102868 is `bl 0x300308` / `bl 0x105238` / `add r0,r0,#1` / `str r0,[r4,#4]` / `bl 0x105280` / `str r0,[r4,#0xc]`, i.e. a two-string record initialiser. The record id 0x04000027 and the two getters are still unidentified, so neither 'Time' nor 'Locale' can be claimed; the name now says only what the body does.

name: Os_RunLateBootSetup
summary: Last step of ResetVector: brings up the SDK synchronisation layer (0x001076A8), resets the committed memory size (0x00104510(0)), creates the application heap (Mem_InitializeMainHeap(0)) and finalises the allocator (0x0010742C).
evidence: NEW: the third call is now the confident Mem_InitializeMainHeap, which fixes the middle of the sequence and the boot-order reading of the whole function.

name: Mem_InitializeMainHeap
summary: Creates the application heap: marks the heap block ready, publishes the heap descriptor at 0x007E790C, then asks 0x00107B54 to reserve heapSize (rounded down to 8) bytes with permission word 0x300 and alignment/type 0xF. On success it maps the block (0x00119BA8/0x0010DD58/0x00119E1C) and returns 0; a non-zero return means the reservation failed.
evidence: Called with 0 from the boot chain (0x00102874). Body writes the 'initialised' byte at *(u8*)(0x007AE910+3), calls 0x00107770(0x007E790C,0x100), then `result = func_00107B54(0x300, heapSize & ~7, 0xf)` and on `result >= 0` runs the map/unmap pair 0x00119BA8 / 0x00119E1C and closes with 0x0010DD58(0). Matches the heap-carving documented in 3DS_Translate/docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md ('the game carves the linear heap into fixed heaps at boot').

name: Engine_InitializeSubsystems
summary: Runs the fixed ordered list of subsystem initialisers (OS/runtime, display, task pool, time step) that must follow heap setup; called from Engine_Initialize.
evidence: Body is an argument-free call chain 0x107024 -> 0x1071AC -> 0x107544 -> 0x1075FC -> 0x10DA2C(0x1e) -> 0x107618(3) -> 0x107608(1); called from 0x101B74 (Engine_Initialize) right after the cache/cache-set construction.

name: Snd_StreamManager_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the streamed-audio manager: advances the five fade records (f_1AB0 bitmask, f_1AB4 array), updates all stream slots and voices through Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll and Snd_StreamVoice_Update, flushes the texture uploads it owns and releases finished ones, then retires an expired handle at f_60.
evidence: The two dominant callees are the named stream helpers Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll (0x00105584) and Snd_StreamVoice_Update (0x00105AFC), and the body's fade bitmask/array and stream/voice-slot state are consistent with a stream manager frame update. The trailing Gfx upload calls are shared frame bookkeeping, not the function's purpose.

name: Mem_InitAllocatorState
summary: The one-time allocator-state reset: it clears the allocator descriptor, initialises the pool/block allocators and records the extended-memory probe result.
evidence: The body memsets the descriptor via 0x00116AE0, calls 0x00107894/0x00107880/0x00111CD8/0x00111E28/0x00111D50, tests 0x0010D68C/0x0010CC00 and stores 0x00107B1C() at +2. The touched globals are the allocator/heap-carver globals.

name: maybe_Os_IpcSendResultState
summary: Calls the locked IPC send helper 0x00107E9C and normalises its Result to a two-valued state: 1 when the result is non-negative, 2 when it is negative. It is a status wrapper, not an update-mode getter.
evidence: The body is exactly Os_IpcSendByteLocked() followed by (result >> 31) + 1, the standard 'normalise a Result to 1/2' idiom; there are still no callers, so neither the owner nor the meaning of 1/2 is proven. Renamed only to follow the corrected callee name.

name: Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks
summary: Frame callback dispatcher: runs up to four registered {fn,arg} callbacks from each of the global frame-begin/render/frame-end arrays, between the semaphore lock/unlock and the runtime-state guards.
evidence: Os_LockSemaphore, Os_ReentrantLock_Acquire and Os_TryLockSemaphore are named now, and it is called from both Engine_Initialize (0x101B74) and the main loop (0x694E18) - the per-frame callback pump is confirmed.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFramePeriod
summary: Stores one value in two fields of the context (+8 and +0x14) and then resets both timing helpers 0x107894 and 0x107880. The two helpers are shared with the allocator init path, so they are general counters rather than a frame clock, and 'Frame' is a guess.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and both callees (0x107894, 0x107880) have no readable body, so the 'frame period' reading cannot be checked. The only verified content is 'store the value twice, then reset two counters', which is what the summary now says.

name: maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one transfer channel of the large cache/heap object: stores the channel pointer at +0xE114, initialises the wait event at +0xE118 (Os_LightEvent_Init) and submits a 0x2000-byte staging buffer with mode 0x11 and handle -2 through Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit; returns 1. Called from Engine_Initialize and InitHeaps.
evidence: The body is a three-field initialiser over the +0xE1xx block (pointer, event, command buffer) and returns 1; the 'Fs_Channel' owner and the meaning of the +0xE1xx fields are still inferred from the two init callers, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: SaveWork_Container_BaseCtor
summary: Base constructor of the 0xE3C8-byte party/save work singleton at *0x007BE308: installs the base vtables 0x007602B4 / 0x007602CC, constructs the embedded 0xFF-slot and 31-member sub-arrays, runs Save_InitPartySnapshot and Ui_PartyStatus_InitMemberData, and returns self.
evidence: New context: the singleton getter 0x006F1F88 (size 0xE3C8, derived vtables 0x00782964/0x0078297C) and Main (0x00101ED8) are now named callers, and FACTS.md independently records *0x007BE308 as the 0xE3C8-byte party/save container reached through 0x00103594. The full ARM body 0x00103594..0x00103710 confirms the three std_ConstructArray calls and the two init calls; only the Ghidra body is truncated.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Initialize
summary: Builds the whole streaming-resource cache: allocates per-category slot pools and buffers for every pack category (sound, cmn_cache, weapon, PL_256/400, F_/B_ motion, sound, model, UI) and registers them in the named-table at the end.
evidence: Inline string literals in the body: s_sound_00103FD0, s_cmn_cache_00103FD8, s_weapon_00103FE4, s_PL_256_00103FEC, s_PL_400_00103FF4, s_F_PLmotion_00103FFC, s_F_Cache_00104008, s_Cache1/2, s_B_PLsound/PLmotion/ENsound/ENmodel/ENmotion; then 0x10928C registers Common/ModeCmn/CacheCmn/Weapon/FldPlayer/BtlPlayer/BtlEnmMdl/BtlEnmMot/BtlPSound/BtlESound/Field/UICmn/UI/SoundCmn/TempSct/Fails (count 0xF). Slot pools come from 0x108624/0x108750/0x1086CC/0x1087F4 with sizes 0x80000/0x40000/0x64000/0x12C000/0xBC0000.

name: maybe_Engine_SubmitFrameEntries
summary: Frame step: pumps the sound voice list (maybe_Snd_UpdateVoiceList), then, when the global 0x007AE18C is set, calls vtable +0x20 on every object in the self->f_54..f_58 array (8-byte stride) with the fixed frame arguments (0x3F, stack buffer, 0x100, 10). Called once from Engine_Initialize; the queued object class is not identified.
evidence: The body is only the sound voice-list pump plus an indirect 8-byte-strided vtable+0x20 loop; there is no draw-list construction, so the old Gfx_SubmitDrawList wording was unsupported, and 'submit frame entries' remains a description of the loop rather than a proven role.

name: Gfx_ReleaseRenderContext
summary: Releases the frame's display channel (Pack_HandleTable_Get on the caller handle followed by Gfx_ReleaseDisplayChannel) and destroys the renderer object stored at self->f_18 through its vtable slot +4, clearing the pointer. Part of the engine teardown path.
evidence: The body is the two-step release (display channel, then vtable+4 destruction of f_18) and the only direct call site is 0x001026A8 inside Engine_Initialize, i.e. the engine shutdown path. The renderer at f_18 is only ever destroyed here, so the name describes the visible effect.

name: Fs_MountDefaultArchives
summary: Lazily mounts the built-in archives once: initialises the archive device, opens the system file handle, registers the default mounts (name,size) and aborts through 0x118924 on failure.
evidence: Guarded by g_001042A8; calls 0x106AC0, 0x10BDF8 (Os_AcquireSharedSession), 0x106A6C, 0x1074AC(g_001042B0,g_001042AC) (Os_CreateEvent with a literals pair), 0x107514; error path func_00118924(iVar2, 0x104298); mirrors 0x1042B4 which undoes it.

name: Fs_UnmountDefaultArchives
summary: Undoes Fs_MountDefaultArchives: closes the event/device handles and clears the mounted flag.
evidence: Guarded by g_001042FC; calls 0x107470(g_00104300) (Os_CheckHandleClosed), 0x106A38 (Os_CloseHandleIfOpen), error path 0x118924(...,0x1042EC), then clears *pcVar1; exact mirror of 0x104240.

name: Mem_SetCommittedSize
summary: Grows or shrinks the committed part of the linear heap through svcControlMemory, then records the new size. Growing uses memory operation 3 (commit) with permission 3, shrinking uses operation 1 (free) with permission 0; size must be 4 KiB aligned, otherwise the previous result is returned unchanged.
evidence: `if ((size & 0xfff) == 0) { cur = *(u32*)(state+8); if (cur < size) rc = func_001053D0(&out, cur+0x8000000, 0, size-cur, 3, 3); else rc = func_001053D0(&out, size+0x8000000, 0, cur-size, 1, 0); if (rc >= 0) *(u32*)(state+8) = size; }`. 0x001053D0 is a 6-argument wrapper around svcControlMemory (MEMOP_FREE=1 / MEMOP_COMMIT=3 / MEMOP_PROT=6, 0x8000000 = the process virtual base), also used by 0x00104400 with op 0x10003/3. Called from 0x00104400.

name: Mem_CommitFreeRegion
summary: Commits everything the process may still use: takes the FCRAM size (0x0010439C), subtracts the reserved block (0x001043AC), clamps the committed size to 2 MB via Mem_SetCommittedSize, and then commits or frees the remainder page-aligned so that 0x007AEA7C holds the base and the length of the committed region.
evidence: ResetVector calls it before the init arrays. Body: total=func_0010439C(); reserved=func_001043AC(); func_00104304(0x200000); `want = (total - reserved - 0x200000) & 0xfffff000;` then two svcControlMemory calls (op 0x10003/perm 3 to commit, op 1/perm 0 to free) and the bookkeeping `g_0010450c[1] = want; g_0010450c[0] = out;` (0x007AEA7C).

name: Mem_ResizePageBlock
summary: Grows or shrinks the global page-granular memory block: when the size changes it maps the delta (0x1053D0 with flags 0x10003/3) or unmaps it (flags 1/0), then stores the new base/size pair at 0x7AEA7C. Rejects unaligned sizes and cross-64K resizes with 0xE0E01BF2.
evidence: Confirmed: the body compares the requested size with the stored one, then calls the same map/unmap helper with the two different flag sets and updates base+size - there is no other reading of that sequence. NEW: the 0xE0E01BF2 rejection code (page-error class) and the 64K-alignment condition are stated in the summary because they are what a modder needs to know.

name: Fs_CacheSet_UpdateEntries
summary: Per-frame cache-set update: walks the entry lists, sorts them by the 0x84 priority byte, applies pending visibility transitions through the entry vtable (+0x10/+0x14), releases unloaded entries (+0xC/+0x28) and merges the done-list.
evidence: Uses intrusive lists at self+0xC (head self+0x30) and self+0x34; entry vtable slots +0xC/+0x10/+0x14/+0x28; entry byte +0x84 is the sort key and +0x85/+0x86 the visible/pending flags; calls 0x1235A4 (list splice) and 0x109600 (list clear); called from 0x101B74 and main loop 0x694E18.

name: Fs_CacheSet_BeginEvict
summary: Asks every currently loaded cache entry to prepare for eviction (entry vtable slot +0x18).
evidence: Iterates the list at set[0]/set[1] and calls (*(*entry+0x18))() when entry byte +0x85 is set; sibling trio 0x1048BC (+0x1C), 0x10490C (+0x20) with the same loop; called around the main-loop frame in 0x101B74/0x694E18.

name: Fs_CacheSet_ReleaseEntries
summary: Releases cache entries that are no longer visible: unloads them (vtable +0x14), clears the visible/pending bytes, destroys the object (+0xC) and frees it (+0x28) until the done-list is empty.
evidence: Loop terminates when the list cursor equals self->f_1C; unlinks via 0x109620/0x109658; calls slots +0x14/+0xC/+0x28 exactly like 0x104520; called from 0x101B74, 0x55AD28 and the main loop.

name: Fs_CacheSet_EndEvict
summary: Second eviction phase: calls entry vtable slot +0x1C on every loaded entry (commit/discard prepared evictions).
evidence: Same 3-line list walk as 0x1047B0 but slot +0x1C; part of the 0x1047B0/0x1048BC/0x10490C slot-0x18/0x1C/0x20 family.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Flush
summary: Third eviction phase: calls entry vtable slot +0x20 on every loaded entry (final flush of cached blocks).
evidence: Same list walk as 0x1047B0/0x1048BC but slot +0x20; the three functions are always called together from 0x104520 and the main loop.

name: Fs_CacheSet_Shutdown
summary: Destroys all remaining cache entries: unlinks each block from the free list, detaches its buffer, releases the underlying allocation (0x10F6CC) and empties the set.
evidence: Walks self->f_1C..f_14 list via 0x115358/0x115390, frees f_34 via 0x10F69C, detaches f_10 records with 0x10EC00/0x10EC14 (intrusive-tree unlink), then 0x10F6CC(entry); called from Engine_Initialize and main-loop teardown.

name: Gfx_Display_Initialize
signature: void Gfx_Display_Initialize(GfxDisplay* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Initialises the dual-screen display: allocates 2-3 framebuffer/wave buffers per screen, four 0x200x0x200 and 0x100x0x200 render targets, the GPU shared block and the frame-timing counters.
evidence: Allocates 3 buffers per i in 0..1 with sizes n*96000, n*0x12C00, n*96000 (n=2 or 3 from Gfx config), two 0x100000-byte target blocks with 0x100 sub-entries, then 0x10944C(&f_C4,0x200,0x200,...) x4, and finally (config<<0x12) bytes for f_1E4 with svc 0x28; called from 0x101B74 with the display singleton; the 400/0x140 screen constants appear in 0x109FB0.

name: Gfx_Display_Shutdown
summary: Releases everything Gfx_Display_Initialize allocated: the shared block, the six per-screen buffers, the two 0x100000 target buffers and the two mapped regions.
evidence: Frees f_1E4 (0x10F69C), then 3 pointers x 2 screens at self+4, then f_44/f_48 for 2 entries, then 0x10E66C(...,f_BC/f_C0); exact inverse of 0x104A38; called from Engine_Initialize and the main loop.

name: Gfx_Display_PresentFrame
signature: void Gfx_Display_PresentFrame(GfxDisplay* self, u32 flags, u32 timestamp)
summary: Frame presentation: waits for the vsync deadline, DMA-copies the finished framebuffer lines (0x400 stride x 0xF0 rows) to the visible buffer, then swaps the active buffer index.
evidence: Computes elapsed ticks with g_00104EC8/g_00104ECC, spins with 0x11CC94, copies with 0x10AD60(0x400, buf, buf, 0xF0) and 0x10AD60(g_00104ED4, buf[1], 0, 0xF0), then `f_1D=f_1C; f_1C=~f_1C&1` and 0x108430; 0x400x0xF0 is exactly a 3DS top-screen 400x240 framebuffer.

name: Gfx_InitDefaultTexture
summary: Creates the engine's 16x16 default texture: stores the renderer handle from cfg+4, opens the graphics/OS session, allocates 16x16x1 storage through the renderer callback, registers it with Fs_MountByName and marks the slot valid.
evidence: The only caller is the named Engine_Initialize and it pairs explicitly with Gfx_ReleaseDefaultTexture (0x00104F58), which unmounts and frees the same slot; the fixed 16x16x1 allocation identifies the texture, though no string names its purpose.

name: Gfx_ReleaseDefaultTexture
summary: Releases the default texture created by 0x00104ED8: unmounts it with Fs_UnmountByName, runs the renderer object's virtual destructor on the handle at +0x10, frees the OS resource and clears the valid flag, handle and owner pointer.
evidence: The named Engine_Initialize/Engine_ShutdownAllSubsystems call it on the same global slot initialised by 0x00104ED8 and the mount/unmount calls mirror each other exactly.

name: Gfx_InitDisplay
summary: One-shot display bring-up called from Engine_Initialize: records the current lock depth, queries the display timing with 0x00107298 and, when a display is present and the lock was taken, registers the 0x3000-byte command buffer at 0x007E4000 (Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers) and selects display mode 10 (Gfx_SetDisplayMode). Sets the 'initialised' flag 0x007AE724 and returns 1, or 0 when the display check fails.
evidence: Both callees are now confidently named (Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers, Gfx_SetDisplayMode) and the single caller is the confident Engine_Initialize, which calls it once during start-up - that is exactly a display initialiser. Renamed from 'InitDisplayDriver' to 'InitDisplay' because no driver object is involved, only buffers and the display mode.

name: Input_Initialize
summary: Initialises the input state object: verifies the three global pad/touch/timer records are constructed (asserting through 0x10009C), then binds the pad and touch sub-states.
evidence: Asserts g_00105180[4]/[8]/[0xC] thread flags, then 0x108A00(self+4, g_001051A0-0x58) (pad sticks) and 0x108878(self+0xEC, g_00105194) (button masks); called from Engine_Initialize and the main loop with the global input object.

name: Gfx_ReleaseRenderer
summary: Tears the renderer down: clears the 'initialised' byte, and if the session was owned it releases the session (Gfx_IsChannelReady / 0x10C534), shuts the global state down and frees the frame buffers at 0x7E7DE0.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named - Gfx_IsChannelReady, maybe_Gfx_ShutdownGlobalState, maybe_Gfx_FreeFrameBuffers - and they form the exact mirror of the init path, which is what confirms this is the release/exit half. The flag pair (byte 0 = initialised, byte 1 = owns session) is visible in the body.

name: maybe_Engine_InitRecordPair
summary: Constructor for a pair of 0xE8-byte records: stores the id in the header word, initialises the record at +4 and the one at +0xEC with 0x108C00, and returns the object base (the +0xE8/-0xEC arithmetic cancels out because 0x108C00 returns its argument).
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is Engine_Initialize (0x101B74), so the 'Gfx' prefix was inherited from the unproven neighbour maybe_Gfx_InitE8Record (0x108C00) and has no support of its own; the pair-of-0xE8-records layout is provable from the body. Renamed to the subsystem of the one caller that is actually known.

name: maybe_Os_GetDefaultLocaleString
summary: Returns a pointer into the built-in string area, or 0 when an override name is supplied and resolves through 0x10540C. Its sibling 0x105280 does the same for a second string, and 0x102828 stores both into one record. Which strings they are (locale? region? font?) is not visible.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x102828 (the two-string record initialiser in this batch), which confirms the pair is used together but not what the strings mean. The return arithmetic is damaged - Ghidra shows `0x00694910 + 0x006948FC`, which is not a valid address - so the 'locale' label stays a guess and the confidence drops.

name: maybe_Os_GetRegionString
summary: Second built-in string getter, structurally identical to 0x105238 but reading the second literal pair and testing 0x6949D8+0x1052A4. Returns 0 when an override name resolves through 0x10540C.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x102828, which calls this getter immediately after 0x105238 and stores the two results in fields +4 and +0xC of one record - so they are a related pair of built-in strings, not two independent config values. The identity of the strings is still unproven, so 'Region' stays a guess.

name: Gfx_GetRenderContext
summary: Lazily creates and returns the process-wide 0x1F8-byte render/graphics context singleton (guard g_001053B4, instance g_001053B8).
evidence: 28 callers, all in the battle UI flow and the gfx passes (Battle_UiFlow_Open*Window, 0x5668A0-0x56AFFC, 0x616DB4), plus the same 0x100050-ctor shape used by the other lazy singletons - confirmed as the shared context getter.

name: Os_WaitFlagByte
summary: Spins (sleeping between polls) until the byte flag at self+0xE3C5 becomes non-zero.
evidence: Body: while (arg1->f_E3C5 == 0) func_0011CC94(0,0); 0x11CC94 is the sleep/yield helper used by every polling loop in this region (e.g. 0x107D00, 0x10D884); recovered-only entry point.

name: maybe_Os_ClearThreeWords
summary: Zeroes the three words at the given pointer and returns that pointer unchanged. The callee 0x10B258 is `mov r1,#0; mov r2,r1; mov r3,r1; stm r0,{r1,r2,r3}; bx lr`, a three-word zero store - there is no flag and no wait anywhere in the function.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of the callee 0x10B258 shows a three-word zero store, and 0x105570 is `push {r4,lr}; mov r4,r0; bl 0x10B258; mov r0,r4; pop {r4,pc}`. The old 'ClearWaitFlag' reading is therefore wrong, not merely unproven; the new name states the verified effect.

name: Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll
summary: Per-frame update of the six banks of streamed-audio slots (6 x 0x20 slots of 0x24 bytes at +0x110). For every slot whose state bits are set it validates the slot's pack handle, completes or cancels the pending async transfer, releases the pack record and adjusts the busy counters.
evidence: Slot records are 0x24 bytes at self+0x110 (index = bank*0x20 + slot, six banks, f_d4/f_d8/f_dc are the busy counts, f_f8/f_e0 the per-bank bitmasks); state word at +4 with bits 2/4; pack handle at +5 is validated against g_00105aec/g_00105af0 exactly like Pack_FreeHandleEntry@0x1241d0; transfers go through 0x10df00 and complete via 0x10ef64/0x10efb8; gain changes via Snd_FadeChannelToGain@0x114cfc. Callers 0x10293c (frame tasks), 0x1ecd08, 0x1ecd6c, 0x1edab4 (sound).

name: maybe_Snd_StreamVoice_UpdateFragment
summary: Ghidra mis-split: this entry is the tail of the ARM streamed-voice routine 0x00105584, so the C shown is the stop/fade/async-transfer part of that routine rather than an independent function.
evidence: The address sits inside ARM code exactly at the end of 0x00105584 (the ARM twin 0x00105AFC follows it), the body starts mid-state-machine and contains coprocessor_movefromRt, and no caller exists.

name: Snd_StreamVoice_Update
summary: Drives one streamed-audio voice for a frame: consumes the 64-entry command ring at +0x1848 (start / set-buffer / stop / fade / delay), submits pack-streamed chunks into the voice's two buffers, advances the fade timer at +0x1a54 and runs the nine-state machine at +0x1a50.
evidence: Called by Snd_RequestBgmPlay@0x1ec1d0 and Snd_RequestBgmStop@0x1ee4f8 plus 0x10293c; ring of 0x40 records of 8 bytes at +0x1848 read via f_1a48/f_1a4c, states 0..8 in f_1a50, fade compares f_1a54 with f_1a58, calls 0x10df00 (async read into a buffer), Snd_FadeChannelToGain@0x114cfc, 0x116e44 (per-voice parameter), and the pack free path 0x1241d0.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseFinishedUploads
summary: Reaps completed uploads: for each of the four queues it walks the live-slot bitmask, releases the finished block through 0x0010EF64/0x0010F044 under the renderer monitor, returns the slot to the free list and records the completion.
evidence: Its only caller is the per-frame maybe_Snd_StreamManager_Update (0x0010293C), which owns the queue array and calls this when the live count f_8C is positive; the slot/free-list bookkeeping is clear, but the two release helpers and the object type are unnamed, so 'upload' stays inferred - maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Os_SetRuntimeFlag
summary: Small one-shot hook: takes the runtime lock object at 0x007AE4A0 through 0x00111D50 and sets the byte at 0x007AE49D to 1. The flag owner is not visible, so the exact runtime state it announces is unknown.
evidence: NEW: disassembly confirms the lock object is loaded from the literal 0x007AE4A0 immediately before the call (ldr r0,[pc,#0x14] at 0x0010643C) and the store is the byte at 0x007AE49D, so 'lock + set runtime flag' is exactly right; the meaning of the flag is still unknown and the function has no caller, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Os_GetInitPhase
summary: Returns 1 when the global byte at 0x7AE939 is zero and 2 otherwise. 0x1146F0 reads that byte (`ldrsb r0,[r0,#1]`) and 0x114700 sets it to 1, so it is an initialisation/phase flag, not a thread property.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly is `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x1146F0; cmp r0,#0; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#2; pop {r4,pc}` - 24 bytes, not the 120 the index claims - and 0x1146F0 is `ldr r0,=0x007AE938; ldrsb r0,[r0,#1]; bx lr` while 0x114700 stores 1 to the same byte. Nothing in the chain mentions a thread, so 'GetThreadClass' is replaced. The dossier's 35 callers are an xref artefact (they branch to 0x1064D4, inside the claimed 120-byte range); the exact-target scan finds none.

name: maybe_Os_OwnerTable_Init
summary: Initialises an owner/handle container: stores the caller vtable, chains seven 0x30-byte nodes through func_00109558, puts vtable 0x007821C8 on the last node and default-constructs five 0x10-byte records at +0x34.
evidence: Still no caller and no named callee (0x00109558 is unnamed). The only named neighbour is maybe_Gfx_GetMemoryRegion (0x001094C0), so the OS/resource-owner reading rests on layout and neighbourhood only.

name: Os_SequenceTask_Ctor
summary: Constructs a task/sequence object: initialises three intrusive list heads, installs the task vtables (0x007824E0 then 0x0075CACC), sets the state fields (+0x21=3, +0x85/+0x86=0, +0x87=1, +0x24=-1, +0x29=0xFF) and names it 'SequenceTask' (clamped to 31 characters).
evidence: NEW: the object's own name literal s_SequenceTask is now resolved in the readable source and the caller is the confident Fs_Task_Create (0.55); the string is copied with strlen+memcpy into +0x19, so the class name is the game's own.

name: maybe_Fs_SetTransferPriority
summary: Enables or disables the twelve transfer channels listed in the object's +0x20..+0x50 fields using the 5-bytes-per-mode table at 0x0072D710, and when the mode reaches 4 arms the bulk transfer (0x0010E5D8) with the pair at +0x10/+0x14 or cancels it (0x0010E64C).
evidence: The only in-engine caller is the named Fs_CacheSet_Initialize (0x00103724), so a cache-set transfer setup is plausible, but nothing in the body names a priority or the channels - the wording stays a hypothesis, maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Os_CloseHandleIfOpen
summary: Closes the remembered kernel handle once (svc CloseHandle) and clears the stored handle.
evidence: Body reads *g_00106A68, performs software_interrupt(0x23) (3DS svc 0x23 = CloseHandle), returns the negative result on failure, otherwise zeroes the global and returns 0; mirror of 0x107470 and 0x10EA00's handle teardown.

name: Fs_OpenGlobalFile
summary: Lazily opens the data file whose name and archive live at 0x7354B5 / 0x7AF904: waits for the runtime, takes the name length with 0x11CCA0 and calls the open-by-name routine 0x1192C0, returning the SDK error code.
evidence: Confirmed: NEW named callees - Os_WaitRuntimeReady is now confident and 0x11CCA0 is the strlen used by every lazy open in this region - and the 'only if the cached handle is zero' guard is the lazy-open pattern of 0x106AD0/0x10BFB0/0x112050.

name: Fs_Initialize
summary: Brings up the filesystem subsystem: waits for runtime init, opens the "fs:USER" service session, stores the archive/file handles, initialises the intrusive list and flushes one system-info query.
evidence: The string passed to 0x0011CCA0 is the literal "fs:USER" (read from code.bin at 0x0072FC13, not visible in the decompiler output), which makes this nn::fs initialisation rather than a generic file open; the old name's 'OpenSubsystemFiles' is close but the session string pins it down.

name: maybe_Os_InitTimeoutBase
summary: One-time init of the global timing record at 0x007AEA48: stores 10x the tick period returned by 0x0010BE98 as a 64-bit value at +0x18, sets the 'have time source' byte at +1 when 0x0010BE20 succeeds, and sets the 'usable' byte at +0 when either is set. Called once from the graphics init path.
evidence: The asm confirms the 64-bit store (add r0,r0,r0,lsl#2 then lsl r0,#1 = x10, strd r0,r1,[r4,#0x18]) and the two readiness bytes, and the only caller is Gfx_InitDefaultTexture; but 0x0010BE98/0x0010BE20 have no readable body, so whether the record is a timeout base or a tick-rate record is still inferred from the x10 scaling.

name: Fs_UnmountByName
summary: Looks up a mounted archive by its 8-byte device name (text before ':' or 8 chars) in a 32-entry mount table and unmounts it, releasing the mount object.
evidence: Parses up to 8 chars into a 64-bit key (same loop as 0x10B6D4), scans g_00106D50 (0x20 entries of 0x10 bytes) for the key, zeroes the entry, calls the object's virtual slot +0x30, and clears g_00106D58+8 when it was the default; returns the table's error sentinel g_00106D54 on miss; callers include 0x104F58's teardown path.

name: Fs_MountByName
signature: u32 Fs_MountByName(const char* name, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Opens a service/archive handle for a named mount and registers it in the mount table (0x10B6D4); on any failure closes the temporary handle and reports through 0x11ED40.
evidence: Calls 0x10B830(&local) to create the mount object, then 0x10B6D4(name, object, 0, 0, ...), and on negative results closes the object via its +0x30 slot and calls 0x11ED40(result, 0x106DEC); called from 0x106BFC's counterpart and by the renderer init.

name: Os_ReentrantLock_Acquire
summary: Reentrant lock acquisition: if the current thread id (TPIDRURO) differs from the recorded owner it runs the slow path (0x10BD34), then records the owner and increments the recursion count.
evidence: Reads coproc p15 thread/process id, compares lock+4, calls 0x10BD34(lock) when different and returns 0 on failure, writes the current id back, `++*(lock+8)` and returns 1; called by every global init/teardown block in this region (e.g. 0x102BA4).

name: maybe_Os_CacheBootQueryWord
summary: Caches one word in the global 0x007AF8E4: if it is still zero, calls the svc 0x21 wrapper 0x0010B210 and stores the returned word. Runs first in Os_InitMemoryManager, so the word is created during memory-manager bring-up.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0010B210 is a five-instruction wrapper around `svc #0x21` (the SVC numbering is calibrated by 0x001112E0 = `svc #0x28` svcGetSystemTick and by FACTS' 0x23/0x24), so the cached word is whatever that SVC returns, not a boot parameter; the caller Os_InitMemoryManager only fixes the timing.

name: maybe_Os_GetLockDepth
summary: Asserts that bit 0 of the global lock object's +4 word is set (calling 0x0010009C otherwise) and returns the object's first word.
evidence: Its only caller 0x00104FDC uses the returned value as the runtime-flag byte, so 'read a counter out of the global lock object' is confirmed; 'depth' is still a guess about that counter's meaning, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Os_InitMemoryManager
summary: Memory-manager boot entry: caches the boot parameter, opens the SDK session, measures the free FCRAM window, sets up thread-local storage, and finally hands the 48 MB (0x03000000) application heap size to 0x0010BDB0. Reached from ResetVector through 0x00113420.
evidence: Body is 0x24 bytes: bl 0x106EC8; bl 0x107010; bl 0x106FFC; bl 0x106F94; bl 0x11697C (returns 0x03000000); then a tail branch to 0x10BDB0 with r0 = 0x03000000. 0x106F94 is the linear-RAM scan, 0x11697C initialises TLS for the main thread. 0x03000000 = 48 MB is exactly the total the AGENT_GUIDE's 44 MB main heap plus the smaller heaps add up to.

name: Mem_ComputeLinearHeapRange
summary: Finds how much of the FCRAM linear heap the application may use: walks svcQueryMemory downwards from 0x0FFFF000 in 4 KiB steps until the block that contains 0x0E000000 is found, then records the range [0x0E000000, top) in the range descriptor at 0x007F2B88.
evidence: `uVar2 = 0x10000000; do { uVar2 -= 0x1000; rc = func_0010B228(&base, &state, uVar2); } while (rc >= 0 && state != 0 && base > 0xe000000); if (uVar2 < 0xe000000) uVar2 = 0xe000000; func_00110C90(0x007F2B88, 0xe000000, uVar2 + 0xf2000000);` - the last argument is the wrap-around form of (top - 0x0E000000). func_00110C90 stores exactly (base, base+size) in the descriptor, i.e. it is the range/allocator descriptor init.

name: Snd_OpenDspService
summary: Opens the DSP service session and initialises its state block: waits for the runtime, resolves the "dsp::DSP" service name (0x0072FBC0) through srvGetServiceHandle, stores the handle, clears the service tables and registers the wait list entry.
evidence: NEW: the service name pointer 0x0072FBC0 is documented in the confident Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen as the literal "dsp::DSP", and the same two helpers it uses (0x0011CCA0 = strlen, 0x001192C0 = srvGetServiceHandle) appear here, so the service being opened is known.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSyncObject
summary: Waits on the global synchronisation object: validates the eight wait-slot words at 0x007E7978, spins on the semaphore 0x007AEA10 (sleeping 1,000,000 ticks), then dispatches the queued Gfx_IpcCmd120000 request, clears the pending byte and signals the semaphore.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives and Gfx_IpcCmd120000 is named, so the wait/dispatch flow is real; what the transferred value means is still unclear, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Snd_InitDspTimeouts
summary: Initialises the DSP state block at 0x007AEA00: sets the two default period values (+0x1C/+0x20), writes 0xFF into the two 16-bit fields at +4/+6, issues the DSP IPC command 0xC2 and, when it succeeds, sets the ready byte at +3.
evidence: The caller is the confident Engine_InitializeSubsystems and the block is the same 0x007AEA00 state that 0x00107208 tears down, but the DSP reading still rests on the IPC command (the named maybe_Svc_IpcCmd1100C2) rather than on a named service. The two fields at +4/+6 are written as 0xFF, not 0xFFFF as the first pass said.

name: Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives
summary: Tears down the synchronisation primitive: flushes the wait object, closes the kernel handle (svc 0x23), stores the final tick and releases the global spinlock.
evidence: Calls 0x107628 (sound shutdown) and 0x107100 (Os_WaitSyncObject), releases eight slots via 0x11C814, 0x10CC30(g_00107288) list-remove, svc 0x23, copies g_00107290+4 into the record, then spins on hasExclusiveAccess(g_00107294) and clears it; called from Engine_Initialize and the main loop.

name: maybe_Os_ShutdownSyncObject
summary: Tears the global sync object down: closes every registered handle through 0x0011C814, unlinks the node at 0x007E79D8, issues svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) for the pending handle and clears the state word under the exclusive-access lock at 0x007AEA10.
evidence: The body closes the registered handles (svc 0x23), unlinks 0x007E79D8 and clears the state word under the exclusive-access lock at 0x007AEA10, but the object's identity is still unknown; the xref caller Input_Initialize does not reference this entry in its body, so it is a mid-function attribution and is not used as evidence.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitChannelQueue
summary: Initialises a channel record: stores the handle, initialises the two sub-objects (0x10C4B8 twice), sets the sentinel -1 in the queue slot, links the shared object returned by 0x1125BC (a plain getter for the global at 0x7E7DE0) and sets the state words (+0x40 = 1, +0x48/+0x4C = -1).
evidence: NEW: 0x1125BC is `ldr r0,[pc]; bx lr`, i.e. a getter for the global at 0x7E7DE0, so the 'links the shared object' step is now identified; the other two helpers (0x10C4B8, 0x10C660) still have no readable body, so the record type and the 'Channel' label remain inferred.

name: Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers
signature: void Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers(void* base, u32 size, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Registers the two 0x1000-byte GPU command buffers at base and base+0x2000, maps the shared memory block and stores the display timing block.
evidence: Guarded by g_001073AC; asserts size<0x3000 through 0x11C814, calls 0x11E80C(handle, base,0x1000,0,3) twice, 0x111E28(g_001073B8), 0x10BA30(base+0x1000); called from 0x104FDC with g_00105040 and size 0x3000.

name: Gfx_ShutdownGlobalState
summary: Tears the GPU state down once: if the running flag is set it takes the state lock, calls the named Gfx_ShutdownChannel, releases the lock, marks the state dead (-1), closes the two kernel handles and clears the flag.
evidence: NEW: the middle call is now the named Gfx_ShutdownChannel (0x0010BA40) and the only caller is maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderer, so this is the flag-guarded process-wide wrapper around the channel teardown rather than a second shutdown implementation.

name: Os_SendIpcRequest1
summary: Sends one request to the game's main IPC service: fills the thread command block with the fixed header from 0x1127A4 (0x00060040 = command 6, one normal parameter) and the parameter 6, issues `svc 0x32` (svcSendSyncRequest) and returns the result word, initialising the runtime first when needed.
evidence: `thread = CP15 c13 c0 3; thread->f_80 = g_001127a4 (=0x00060040 IPC header); thread->f_84 = 6; result = *g_001127a8; software_interrupt(0x32); if (result >= 0) result = thread->f_84;` - 0x32 is svcSendSyncRequest in the CTR ABI, and the 0x00060040 literal is an IPC header (command 6, one normal parameter). Guarded by func_00113990/func_0010CB18 (already-up checks).

name: Os_CheckHandleClosed
summary: Closes a handle if the 'pending close' flag is set and reports the stored status: returns the handle value on failure, 0 after a successful close.
evidence: Body: if (*g_001074A4) { svc 0x23; result=*arg1; if (result>=0) {*g_001074A4=0; result=0;} }; called by 0x1042B4 as the undo of 0x1074AC.

name: Os_CreateEvent
summary: Creates a named kernel event once: waits for the runtime to be ready and registers the event with 0x1192C0; sets the created flag on success.
evidence: Guarded by g_0010750C; calls 0x113430(0) then 0x1192C0(arg1,arg2,strlen(arg2),0); sets *pcVar1=1; called by 0x104240 with two literal-pool arguments (name/size pair).

name: Os_IpcSendSyncRequestCmd21
summary: Issues an IPC round trip with command header 0x00210000 (command 0x21, no parameters): writes the header into the thread's TLS block at +0x80, takes the session handle from the global 0x007AEAB0, executes svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest) and returns the reply word at TLS+0x84 on success.
evidence: NEW: the ARM body is mrc p15 (read TLS), str #0x210000 to [tls+0x80], ldr r0,[0x007AEAB0], svc 0x32, then ldrge r0,[tls+0x84]; so the handle is a fixed global and the function takes no arguments (the old pseudocode made the global look like the result). Caller Fs_MountDefaultArchives shows the archive-mount use; what driver command 0x21 means is still unidentified beyond the header value.

name: Snd_Initialize
summary: One-shot bring-up of the sound subsystem: waits for the runtime, creates the stream context (maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext), then initialises the channel buffers, the voice/system state (Snd_InitSystemState) and registers the DSP command blocks, finally setting the ready flag.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named (Os_WaitRuntimeReady, maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext, Snd_InitSystemState) and the caller is the confident Engine_InitializeSubsystems, so this is the sound subsystem's init entry.

name: Snd_Shutdown
summary: Flag-guarded shutdown of the sound runtime: releases the DSP block, flushes pending commands, stops the voice group, releases the channel objects and tears down the stream context.
evidence: NEW: the body calls the named voice/stream teardown helpers (maybe_Snd_StopVoiceGroup, maybe_Snd_TeardownStreamContext) and is called from Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives right after the sync-object wait - a single 'tear the audio runtime down' entry point.

name: Snd_OpenService
summary: Opens the sound service session (result stored in the 0x007F2358 service block at +0xC) and starts the worker thread with Os_CreateThreadWithStack (entry 0x0010BDF4, 0x228-byte stack); a negative handle is reported through 0x00118100.
evidence: NEW: the whole 0x107544..0x1076AC block is the Snd family (Snd_Initialize, Snd_Shutdown, Snd_UpdateState, Snd_IsRunning), and both callees are named (Svc_SendRequestIpc, Os_CreateThreadWithStack). Open-session + start-worker is exactly the body; the only uncertainty is which nn service name the request carries.

name: Os_ListAppendNode
signature: int Os_ListAppendNode(OsListNode* node, unsigned int key)
summary: Appends `node` to the intrusive circular list rooted in the global at 0x1077FC, holding the list lock (0x117E50/0x117ED0), and stamps the caller key into node+0xc.
evidence: Body is the textbook doubly-linked tail insert (`node->prev = tail; tail->next = node; ... head->prev = node`) around func_00117E50/func_00117ED0 on g_001077fc+0x1c, ending in `return 0`. Callers 0x00102894, 0x0050421C, 0x005042AC and maybe_Svc_InitSharedState all register objects at startup.

name: Os_IpcCommand2
summary: Submits the fixed request 0x00010002 (command 2, one normal parameter with value 0x20) to the session handle at 0x007AF900 and returns the first response word. Non-negative results are the service's answer; a negative value is the IPC result code.
evidence: Assembly: `mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3` (thread pointer), `ldr r0,[pc,#0x24]` (literal at 0x00107834 = 0x00010002) -> `str r0,[r4,#0x80]!`, `mov r0,#0x20; str r0,[r4,#4]`, `ldr r0,[pc,#0x18]` -> `ldr r0,[r0]` (handle at 0x007AF900), `svc #0x32` (svcSendSyncRequest), then `ldrge r0,[r4,#4]`. 0x00010002 decodes as command 2 with one parameter in the 3DS IPC header layout (bits 0-15 command, 16-20 normal params). Callers: 0x00113420 / 0x00113430, the session bring-up helpers.

name: maybe_Os_SetThreadPriorityMode
summary: Maps a small mode word onto the scheduler/GPU helpers: 0 -> helper(3) plus Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080(0), 1 -> helper(2) plus Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080(1), 2 -> helper(1) only; other values are ignored.
evidence: The disassembly shows the 0/1/2 -> 3/2/1 remapping and the two callees (0x113A40 and Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080) are now named, but which hardware mode 0x113A40 programs is still unidentified, so neither 'thread priority' nor a display-only reading is proven.

name: Gfx_UpdateDisplayState
summary: One frame step of the GPU display-command state machine: if the pending byte at 0x7AE954 is set it stops the current sequence, advances the state, notifies the registered callback (+0x38), then either waits for readiness or sends the request and restores the flag.
evidence: The named callees Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle and maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode all belong to the display/GSP command path, and the only caller is Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks, so the 'Snd_' prefix was a misnomer.

name: Gfx_UpdateDisplayStateB
summary: Variant of the display-command frame step used when a new command block must be acquired: selects a free/busy block with Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked, re-sends through Svc_RequestWithRetry or waits and sends through Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, then restores the pending flag.
evidence: All callees are GPU command-stream functions (Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked, Svc_RequestWithRetry, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080) and the caller is Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks; 'Snd_' was wrong because nothing here touches the sound driver.

name: maybe_Gfx_IsDisplayStateReady
summary: Returns true when the display state machine reports state 1 from 0x0010CC10; Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks tests it as the first gate before running the frame step.
evidence: The caller Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks and the sibling 0x00107AE8 (both Gfx_ neighbours) fix the subsystem, but 0x0010CC10 itself is still unnamed, so 'state 1 means ready' is only the most plausible reading.

name: maybe_Gfx_IsDisplayStateActive
summary: Returns true when either display state source (0x0010CC20 or 0x00113A00) is non-zero; Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks tests it immediately after 0x00107AD4 as the second frame gate.
evidence: The named caller Engine_DispatchFrameCallbacks pairs it with the other Gfx display gate and both state getters are used by the GPU command pump, so the Gfx_ prefix is supported; the exact state meaning is still unknown, keeping the confidence below 0.5.

name: maybe_Mem_QueryMemoryMode
summary: Lock-protected service query (request 0x0301/0x11) whose reply is normalised to 1 or 2 and stored as the allocator's memory-mode word.
evidence: The only caller is the named Mem_InitAllocatorState, which stores the result in allocator state +8 immediately after the extended-memory probes; the body has no sound code at all, so the old 'Snd_QueryDspState' prefix was wrong, but the exact service/mode meaning is still unidentified.

name: Mem_MapSharedBlock
signature: int Mem_MapSharedBlock(u32 type, u32 size, u32 mode)
summary: Reserves and maps one shared-memory block: lazily opens the service session at 0x007AE910/0x007AE920, requests a block of `size` bytes with request 0x00010040, keeps the returned handle, records the two capability bits from the reply, closes that session, selects the block type and then maps it with request 0x00020080 before handing the mode and both returned words to maybe_Os_OpenServiceHandle.
evidence: The body is complete and every step now uses a named OS helper (Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen, Os_IpcSendGetHandle, Os_CloseIpcSession, Os_IpcSend2Get2, Os_UnlockScheduler); its only caller is the confident Mem_InitializeMainHeap (0x00102894), which passes (0x300, heapSize, 0xF) - exactly the heap's shared block.

name: Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit
signature: int Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit(u32 arg1, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Waits for the graphics/display state machine to leave its transient states and submits a command, retrying on the busy result codes with a 10-tick sleep; returns the submit result.
evidence: The callers Engine_Initialize and Engine_ShutdownAllSubsystems are confident, and the callees now include the confident Svc_SendRequest2/Svc_SendRequestByte plus Os_UnlockScheduler, which matches a submit-with-wait helper used during engine bring-up and teardown.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock
signature: int maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock(u32 request, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
