summary: Initialises one recursive critical section: clears the owner thread and the recursion counter at +4/+8. 32 call sites, always right after an object has been zeroed or allocated, and always paired with Os_CriticalSectionEnter (0x00117E50) / leave (0x00117ED0).
evidence: Body: `func_00117C40(); *(u32*)(cs+4) = 0; *(u32*)(cs+8) = 0;`. 0x00117E50 compares `mrc p15,0,r1,c13,c0,3` (the current thread pointer) against cs+4, re-locks and increments cs+8 - the classic recursive-lock owner/count pair; 0x00117E88 releases it and clears the owner when the count reaches zero. 32 callers, all object constructors (e.g. 0x0010C738, 0x001114F4, 0x005428EC).

name: Os_CloseHandleAndUnlink
summary: Closes a kernel handle and removes its block from the owning list: when the block is linked it either just drops the link (no waiter) or waits for the pending operation, unlinks it via 0x11E7A4 and finally closes the handle with `svc 0x23`.
evidence: `if (f_14) { if (*(self+8)) { if (f_18 == 0) { *(self+8)=0; f_c=0; } else { svc 0x20; if (f_14 < 0) abort; func_0011E7A4(g_00111eac, self); } } if (f_14) { svc 0x23; f_14 = 0; } }`. 0x20 is svcCancelTimer/ReleaseSemaphore and 0x23 is svcCloseHandle; 0x11E7A4 unlinks a node under a lock. Callers 0x00509A20/0x0050F0F8 are the handle-owning managers.

name: Os_InitThreadLocalStorage
summary: Fills in the thread-local block of the calling thread: points the TLS table at +0x5C/+0x64/+0x68 at the per-thread storage, publishes the TLS destructor table, and resolves the per-thread data pointer (0x001000B8) so that thread-local destructors can run at thread exit.
evidence: `iVar1 = mrc p15,0,r0,c13,c0,3; iVar1->f_5c = &iVar1->f_60; iVar1->f_64 = g_00111f54; iVar1->f_68 = g_00111f58; f_60 = f_6c = f_70 = f_74 = f_78 = 0; iVar1->f_7c = (g_00111f50 == 0) ? 0 : func_001000B8();`. 0x001181B8 then walks 16 TLS slots and calls the registered destructor for each with the thread's slot value - the pair is the TLS manager.

name: Os_CreateThreadWithStack
signature: int Os_CreateThreadWithStack(u32* out_handle, OsThreadParams* params, u32 entry, u32 arg4, int stack_top, u32 stack_size, u32 priority, int detached)
summary: Creates a detached or joinable OS thread: computes the aligned stack top from the caller-supplied stack region, writes the thread argument block, then calls svcCreateThread (0x1112A0) with entry/arg/stack/priority and optionally patches the stack chunk header.
evidence: Readable: uVar4 = (stack_top - *params) & ~7; if (!detached) stack_top = 0; calls params->[1](arg, uVar4) (stack guard/clear hook); writes a 0x18-byte chunk header at uVar4-0x18; then func_001112A0(&local, g_0011204C, entry, entry, size, priority) - 0x1112A0 is 'svc #8' (CreateThread), verified in asm 0x1112A0. Callers include 0x1076AC, 0x10BB34, 0x119498, 0x517884.

name: Svc_Cfg_AcquireService
summary: Reference-counted acquire of the process-wide 'cfg:u' session: on first use it resolves the service name, opens the handle into 0x007AF0F8 and marks the session open, then increments the user count under the global config monitor.
evidence: NEW: two independent facts pinned this. (1) The already confident wrapper Os_AcquireSharedSession (0x0010BDF8, 0.50) is exactly `iVar1 = <this>(); if (iVar1 < 0) func_0011ED40(...)`, i.e. the assert-on-error wrapper around this call. (2) The name argument at 0x007418BC+4 is the pointer 0x0078C452, which is the ASCII string 'cfg:u'; it goes through 0x0011CCA0 (verified strlen) into 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle). So the 'shared session' is the 3DS config service, not an anonymous one. Caller 0x0010BDF8 keeps its generic name; it should be reconciled in a later merge.

name: Svc_Cfg_ReleaseService
summary: Releases one user of the config sessions: kind 0 decrements the cfg:u count and closes that handle at zero, kind 1/2 dispatch to the cfg:s / cfg:i close helpers.
evidence: NEW: the two auxiliaries it dispatches to are now identified by their service strings ('cfg:s' at 0x0078C6F3, 'cfg:i' at 0x0078C6ED), and the kind value is exactly what maybe_Svc_Cfg_EnsureService writes out. So the dispatcher is the release half of the cfg session manager.

name: Svc_Cfg_EnsureService
signature: u32 Svc_Cfg_EnsureService(u8* kindOut, u32 second, u16* resultOut)
summary: Makes sure one of the three config sessions is usable: tries the refcounted cfg:u acquire, then cfg:s, then cfg:i, writing which one succeeded (0/1/2) to kindOut; that kind is the same value the release dispatcher 0x0011212C consumes.
evidence: The named callees Svc_Cfg_AcquireService, Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceS and Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceI plus the caller Os_AcquireSharedSession confirm an acquire/ensure helper, and the old 'Os_ReleaseSharedSessionEx' claimed the opposite operation. The unaff_r4 in the tail is a damaged-decompilation artifact of the refcount release helper and does not affect the acquire dispatch, whose three open/acquire calls and kind outputs are intact in the disassembly.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelFilterParams
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetChannelFilterParams(u32 unit, u16* unitA, u16* unitB, u32 flags, ...)
summary: Writes the caller's u16 filter/pan words into the sound-unit record (unitA[0x17], [0x22]..[0x2B] and beyond) and pushes them to the command stream through the sound filter setters; the 18-byte Thumb decompilation is damaged (in_CY, overlapping varargs), so the argument list and record layout are unreliable.
evidence: This is an 18-byte Thumb function whose decompilation is damaged and whose parameters overlap; the only basis for the name is the sound filter setter tail. Per the damaged-body rule it keeps maybe_ and confidence at or below 0.3.

name: maybe_Svc_Cfg_ReleaseServiceU
summary: Releases one reference to the cfg/session service: decrements the user count at 0x007AF0EC+8 under the config monitor and, when it reaches zero, closes the handle in 0x007AF0F8 with svcCloseHandle and resets it to the sentinel. Identical to the kind==0 arm of 0x0011212C.
evidence: The globals, refcount and close sequence are identical to the kind==0 arm of 0x0011212C, so the 'release one reference' description is right; which service the handle belongs to cannot be read from the body (the named callers span sound, movie and gfx code), so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Os_CallFinalizers
summary: Runs the eight registered shutdown hooks of the table at 0x7E79B8 once, then clears the 'initialised' byte at 0x7AEA02. The hooks are per-module shutdown callbacks of one driver, not object finalisers, and the driver is still unnamed.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds a single caller, 0x10CF50 (maybe_Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer), and the sibling table at 0x7E7998 is walked by the two flush routines 0x118788/0x11ECC0 - so the two eight-slot tables are per-module hook lists of one driver. The owner is still unnamed, so the Os prefix stays a guess.

name: maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit(unsigned int handle, unsigned int enable, unsigned int unitIndex)
summary: Read-modify-write of a per-unit flag bit: builds the mask 1<<(enable+unitIndex), compares it with the cached mask at 0x7AEA0C, sends the new state through the command-0x15 stub 0x11874C and updates the cache. Returns 0xC8A0A7F8 (already in that state / no session) instead of resending.
evidence: NEW: the exact-target callers are 0x112E38 and 0x1132DC (the Snd stream-context init/teardown pair), which supports the Snd prefix, and the cached mask at 0x7AEA0C is the same driver context as the session handle at 0x7AEA08. The fourth Ghidra parameter is never read - the mask is 1<<(enable+unitIndex) - so the signature is corrected to three parameters and the confidence stays below 0.5.

name: Hid_DispatchPadReport
signature: void Hid_DispatchPadReport(HidCalibration* cal, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d)
summary: Dispatches a raw pad report to one of three calibration/decoding paths depending on the report-type byte at +0xC (0 = 0x11FBCC, 1 = 0x11A810 circle-pad, 2 = 0x11A914 touch/other), passing the two pairs of 16-bit axis values.
evidence: Body: cVar1 = *(char*)(arg1+0xC); if 0 -> func_0011FBCC(arg2,arg3,arg4,arg5,*arg1,arg1[3]); if 1 -> func_0011A810(...,arg1[1],arg1[4]); if 2 -> func_0011A914(...,arg1[2],arg1[5]). Callers 0x10C2D4 and 0x112640 are the two pad-reader paths; 0x11A810 is the 936-byte circle-pad calibration routine.

name: Os_SendIpcQuery6
signature: int Os_SendIpcQuery6(unsigned int* out0, unsigned int* out1, unsigned int* out2, unsigned int* out3, unsigned int* out4, unsigned int* out5)
summary: Queries the service for six related values in one request (request id 0xA0000) and copies them out of the thread command block; the six results are used to size the six regions that 0x10BFB0 carves out of the shared buffer.
evidence: `thread->f_80 = 0xa0000; result = *g_0011263c; svc 0x32; if (result >= 0) { *arg1 = f_8c; *arg2 = f_90; *arg3 = f_94; *arg4 = f_98; *arg5 = f_9c; *arg6 = f_a0; result = f_84; }`. 0xA0000 is the request id of the 'memory/surface layout' query of this service; the six returned words are exactly the number of buffers 0x10BFB0 then carves out.

name: Hid_ReadPadState
summary: Reads one pad snapshot from the HID service (0x11ABB8) into out_state, computes the newly-pressed / newly-released masks against the previous state, applies the circle-pad calibration and returns 1 when a report was produced, 0 otherwise.
evidence: Readable: if (func_0010C51C()==0) { ...; func_0x0011ABB8(*(u32*)(*arg1+4),arg2,1,local...); if (local[0] > 0) { func_00112518(...); *arg1[2]=*arg2; uVar2=*arg2&~0x2000; arg2[1]=(uVar2^arg1[2])&~arg1[2]; arg2[2]=arg1[2]&~uVar2; ... return 1; } } The pressed/released masks in arg2[1]/arg2[2] are the classic HID button-edge computation.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd60040
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0006 with one translated parameter; returns the service result or the output word on success.
evidence: asm 0x112774: header 0x00060040 (cmd 6, 1 translate), TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32, returns TLS+0x84. No callers in decomp/readable; grouped with the other GSP stubs by the shared request layout and the 0x60040 header.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd140040
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0014 with one translated parameter; returns the service result or the echoed output word.
evidence: asm 0x1127B0: header g_001127E0 = 0x00140040, TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32, returns TLS+0x84 on success. No callers; same family as 0x112774.

name: maybe_Snd_InvalidateChannelObjects
summary: Marks all 24 channel slots unused: for each of the 24 pointers in the table at context+0x18DC it takes the object at +0x68 and stores 0xFFFF into that object's 16-bit field at +0x6C. The callee 0x11EE6C is exactly `mvn r1,#0; strh r1,[r0,#0x6c]; bx lr`, so this is an invalidate loop, not a release.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x11EE6C shows it only stores 0xFFFF into the halfword at +0x6C and returns, so the old 'ReleaseChannelObjects' name overstated what happens. The 24-entry stride and the +0x18DC table are the same ones the Snd_SetChannel* setters use, which keeps the Snd prefix.

name: maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnits
signature: void maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnits(unsigned char* block, unsigned char value)
summary: Fills a 12-byte parameter block with the given byte, then clears the filter-info halfword (+2, stride 0x14) and the filter-coefficient halfword (+0x2A, stride 0x34) of unit 0 and unit 1 and re-submits both through Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields and maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor. The state pointer comes from the getter 0x1129F4 (the global at 0x7F2BA0).
evidence: NEW: 0x1129F4 is `ldr r0,[pc]; bx lr`, a getter for the global at 0x7F2BA0, so the state the loop edits is a global channel-state block rather than a caller argument; the companion 0x112888 performs the same two field clears without the 12-byte fill. No exact caller exists, so the 'Reset' wording stays inferred.

name: Snd_ResetChannelUnitsInPlace
summary: Clears the filter-info halfword (+2, stride 0x14) and the filter-coefficient halfword (+0x2A, stride 0x34) of unit 0 and unit 1 directly in the caller's channel state and pushes both zeroed records to the command stream through Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields and maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x118E58 is now the confident Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields and the driver context 0x7EF414 is the same one the Snd_SetChannel* setters use, so both the Snd prefix and the 'reset the two filter fields of both units' reading are supported by named code. Ghidra removed four unreachable blocks but the surviving loop is complete.

name: maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnitsToDefault
summary: Restores both units to the default value 0xFFFF: writes it to the filter-info field at +0 (stride 0x14) and the filter-coefficient field at +0x28 (stride 0x34), then re-submits both through 0x118E58/0x118FD4.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x00112FAC, inside maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext (0x00112E38), so it is one step of the stream-context setup; the 0xFFFF default is visible in the body. The two re-submit callees are still only partly named, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Snd_GetCommandBlock
summary: Forwards the command-block getter 0x001129F4 and returns its result; the readable C shows `result = func_001129F4(); return result;`, so this is a getter, not a flush.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body returns the callee's result (Ghidra typed the thunk void and dropped it), so 'FlushChannelBlock' describes an action the code does not perform; 0x001129F4 is the command-block getter used by 0x00112848/0x00112888. No caller in the current graph.

name: Snd_EnsureStateInitialised
summary: The sound-state lazy-init guard: it initialises the +0x34 critical section and sets the flag byte exactly once.
evidence: The whole body is `if (*arg1 == 0) { func_00111E28(arg1+0x34); *arg1 = 1; }`; its single caller Snd_InitSystemState passes the .bss singleton 0x007F2C3C.

name: Snd_InitChannelState
summary: Resets a full sound-channel state block to its defaults: writes the two unit records and the per-unit DSP words through the named Snd setters, clears the filter/pan/ADPCM bytes, seeds the volume pair (-1 / 0x7F) and arms the enable flags.
evidence: NEW: its caller is the confident Snd_InitSystemState (0x0010C738), which allocates the state object and then calls this to default it, and every callee is a named per-unit Snd setter (SetChannelDataAddress, SetUnitLoopInfo, SetUnitAdpcmWord, SetChannelRate, SetChannelVolume). That pins both the subsystem and the 'default a fresh channel state' role.

name: Snd_RestoreChannelState
summary: Re-applies a saved channel state to the driver context 0x007EF414: gain, per-unit gain/active/ADPCM state for both units, pan, format, length, output select, rate, volume and level, then clears the saved pending word at +0x2C.
evidence: Every setter it calls is now a named Snd_Set* member of the same family (Snd_SetUnitActive, Snd_SetChannelRate, Snd_SetChannelLength, maybe_Snd_SetChannelGain/Format/AdpcmState/UnitGain/Level), and it writes them from the saved record in a fixed order before clearing state->f_2C - the mirror of the save half at 0x112A9C.

name: Snd_SetOutputMode
summary: Stores the speaker configuration byte at +2 of the sound state and forwards the mode to the mixing layer under the global sound lock; returns 0 when the lock cannot be taken.
evidence: Called from the now-named Snd_InitSystemState (0x10C738) with the 3DS output mode byte and the callee is the already named maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan on the global sound system, so the old guess is supported.

name: maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext
summary: Creates or attaches the streaming context: opens the kernel handle at *ctx if absent, tags it through maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit, queries the unit count (0x00112384) into ctx[1], sets the 0x2000 transfer buffer, resets the 24 channel objects and restores channel/unit defaults on the re-init path. Returns 0 or a Horizon error code.
evidence: The init half is readable through the named maybe_Snd_* channel helpers and the 24-channel/0x2000-buffer layout, but the context type is not named by any caller (no named caller in the readable tree), so 'stream context' and the 'Snd_' prefix remain hypotheses.

name: maybe_Snd_SetupChannelBuffers
summary: One-time layout of the stream buffers: optionally uploads the 0x1080-byte wave buffer, asks the driver for the buffer count/size through two queried commands, splits the shared region into 24 blocks of 0xC0, 24 of 0xC and 24 of 0x20 bytes, stores the six pointer arrays and finally latches the double-buffer index into +0x1322.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x00112F68, inside maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext (0x00112E38), and the 0x1322 selector it writes is the field every Snd_SetChannel* setter reads. The callees are still only partly named, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Snd_TeardownStreamContext
summary: Tears a streaming context down: sends stop request 2 with mode 1 or 3, waits for the transfer-done flag, clears the active byte f_4C7, releases the 0x1080-byte sample buffer when asked, closes the handle (svcCloseHandle) and returns the cached error at ctx[1].
evidence: The request/wait/close sequence mirrors the init path and the 0x1080-byte buffer release matches the sample buffer; no named caller pins the owning service, so the 'Snd_' prefix stays a hypothesis.

name: Os_InitSrvClient
summary: Brings up the srv client at boot: initialises the memory manager, then opens the "srv:" port (name string at 0x00741AD8) with a retry loop that keeps retrying while the result is 'session closed', and finally sends the srv handshake request (0x00107800) once. Returns the last result code.
evidence: `func_00106F70(); if (*g_00113538 == 0) { ...init...; *g = 1; } func_00117E50(lock); ... while (1) { uVar5 = func_001169C4(g_0011354c, 0x00741AD8 /* "srv:" */, arg3, arg4, ...); if (level != -5) break; if (module != 4 || desc != 0x3fa) break; func_0011CC94(0x0007A120, 0); } if (ok) { uVar5 = func_00107800(); count++; }`. g_00113544 = 0x3FA is the error description the loop retries on (module 4, i.e. the srv module) and g_00113550 = 0x0007A120 (500000 ns) is the retry delay. g_00113540 = 0x00741AD8 is the "srv:" string. Called directly by ResetVector, so it is the first service the CRT brings up.

name: Os_WaitRuntimeReady
summary: The runtime-ready wait: it initialises the wait objects once, polls the service completion word and caches the ready state.
evidence: The body initialises g_0011353C and six words, then loops on func_001169C4 until the error class leaves -5, calls func_00107800 on success and increments the ready count. Fourteen lazy-open callers (Gfx/Snd/Svc/Fs) use it.

name: Svc_IpcCmdB0000
summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x000B0000 on the session handle at 0x7AF900; on success it copies the second reply word (TLS+0x88) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84).
evidence: Confirmed as a command stub: header 0xB0000 and the 0x7AF900 session handle are both in the code. NEW: the literal pool of the neighbouring initialiser holds the 'srv:' name string, so this is the srv session - which is what makes the 0x7AF900 global meaningful, but the command itself still has no name, and the name does not claim one.

name: Gfx_InitDrawState
summary: One-shot initialisation of the shared GPU draw-state object: opens the gsp::Gpu session, publishes the handle, clears the 28-word state block at 0x007A1C40 and installs it as the singleton's f_1c, then starts the IPC worker.
evidence: The caller is the named Gfx_InitializeContext (0x00109FB0), the one-shot flag is 0x007AF178, the handle comes from the 'gsp::Gpu' literal at 0x007AF17C, and the 28-word block at 0x007A1C40 is installed as singleton->f_1c - the slot maybe_Gfx_ExchangeSlotValue hands out.

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegs
signature: void Gfx_WriteHwRegs(u32 addr, u32 value, u32 count)
summary: Writes GPU hardware registers through the GPU service: obtains the session handle from the thread-local GSP state and calls 0x1196B0, which issues command 0x00010082.
evidence: Body: uVar1 = func_0011F730() (current GSP session); func_001196B0(uVar1, arg1, arg2, arg3). 0x1196B0's header is 0x00010082 - the GSPGPU WriteHWRegs command (addr/value/count are exactly the three parameters).

name: Gfx_QueueCommand
signature: void Gfx_QueueCommand(u32 queue_id, u32 opcode, u32 arg3, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e)
summary: Appends a 0x1C-byte command to one of the two renderer command queues kept in thread-local storage, writes the six parameter words, issues a data-synchronisation barrier and sets the entry's valid/pending bit with an ldrex/strex.
evidence: Readable: if (arg1 < 2) { pbVar4 = *(u8**)(tls + 0x5c + arg1*4); idx = 1 - *pbVar4; pbVar4 += idx*0x1c + 4; write arg2..arg7; coproc_moveto_Data_Synchronization(0); ldrex *pbVar4 = (*pbVar4 & 0xffff0000) | idx | 0x100; }. Caller 0x110C70; the queue base at TLS+0x5c is filled by 0x1136D8's session setup.

name: Os_IsInHeapRange
summary: Returns 1 when addr lies inside either the main heap or the second (linear/VRAM) heap range, otherwise 0; used by the debug/assert path to decide whether a pointer is a real allocation.
evidence: Readable: uVar1 = func_001180F0(); iVar2 = func_001180E0(); if range1 contains arg1 -> 1; else uVar1 = func_00122CD8(); iVar2 = func_00122CC0(); if (uVar1==0 || arg1<uVar1 || iVar2+uVar1<=arg1) return 0; return 1. The two (base,size) pairs are the engine heaps; no callers because it is called from an inline assert macro.

name: maybe_Os_SignalAndClose
summary: If the runtime object exists, wakes its waiting thread and then sends the close/notify request (svc 0x32 wrapper); part of the service-call bracketing shared with 0x10CDE0/0x10D430.
evidence: Its three named callers (Sound_Driver_Shutdown, Svc_RequestWithRetry, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest) use it as a teardown step, but the svc-0x32 stub is itself only maybe_ named, so the 'signal and close' reading is not fully fixed.

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegsWithMask
signature: void Gfx_WriteHwRegsWithMask(u32 addr, u32 value, u32 mask, u32 count)
summary: Writes GPU hardware registers with a bit mask through the GPU service by calling 0x11979C, whose command header is 0x00020084 (GSPGPU WriteHWRegsWithMask).
evidence: Body: func_0011979C(func_0011F730(), arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4); 0x11979C issues header 0x00020084 with (addr,value,mask,count). Pairs with 0x1136D8 (plain write).

name: maybe_Gfx_ExchangeSlotValue
summary: Atomically exchanges one of seven 32-bit slots at +0x10 of the draw-state object (singleton 0x007AF178->f_1C) under that object's monitor and returns the previous content; slot >= 7 is ignored and returns 0.
evidence: The seven-slot array, the monitor and the returned old value are all explicit in the body; the meaning of the slots (surfaces, command slots, ...) is still unknown, so the name stays at mechanism level and keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitInterrupts
summary: Clears the caller's flag byte, then, when the incoming zero flag allows it, arms three interrupt sources through 0x00113A40(3) and programs the locked command 0x3E0080.
evidence: Still a damaged decompilation: the body reads the condition from in_ZR and uses unaff_r4, and no named caller or callee beyond Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080 exists, so neither the parameter list nor the arming order can be trusted.

name: Os_IsSessionRunnable
summary: Returns 1 only when the service session is open and its status word has both the connected (0x20000000) and ready (0x10000000) bits set.
evidence: The open-flag query and the two status bits are the whole body, and its only caller 0x0010D430 uses the result to decide whether to arm the in-call flag.

name: maybe_Gfx_ProcessFrame
summary: Per-frame service loop of the graphics/audio IPC library: services the retrace and should-close callbacks, handles a command from the 0x0079C000 command ring (kinds 2/5/8/9, 8/9 call Snd_SetMasterEnable) or runs the render state machine (modes 0..4) over the callback table at 0x007AE954.
evidence: Named callees now split the body into the Gfx IPC half (Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer/Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer/Gfx_IpcCmdF0100Query/Gfx_IpcCmd3F0040Call) and the Snd half (Snd_SetMasterEnable/Snd_FlushChannels), so the summary is confirmed but the name still over-narrows the routine to 'Gfx'; it has no named caller (entered from a thread/vtable), so it stays maybe_ and the summary now says it also services audio.

name: Os_ServiceThreadProc
summary: Service-thread body: builds a three-word handle table, then loops waiting on inter-thread handles with svc 0x18/0x19 and dispatching through Os_MutexLock, Os_SignalSemaphore, Os_InvokeCallbacks and the Gfx IPC commands.
evidence: Disassembly (0x00113F2C) is a real thread entry, not a truncated stub: it fills the three handle words from 0x00113F48's pool, waits with svc 0x18/0x19 and stalls when *0x007E7781-style suspend bytes are set. 0x0010D6CC passes it to Os_CreateThreadWithStack as the thread function, and Svc_RequestWithRetry/sound/gfx callers only create that thread.

name: maybe_Snd_SetSuspendState
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetSuspendState(unsigned int suspend, void* state)
summary: Level-triggered suspend/resume switch: when the stored flag at state+3 is set it clears it and calls Snd_RequestResume, otherwise it sets the flag and calls Snd_RequestSuspend; the two 'already in that state' results 0xD8A02A05/0xD9001BF7 are accepted and a negative result goes to the error reporter.
evidence: The entry condition is a damaged `in_ZR` register, so the guard cannot be trusted; the two branches call the named Snd_RequestResume/Snd_RequestSuspend and accept the two 'already in that state' results. Kept honest as maybe_.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd50100
summary: Thin wrapper that submits one 32-bit value as command 0x00050100 through Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call(7, ...).
evidence: The sibling name Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call identifies the command-table family, so the old 'Svc_' prefix implied a kernel SVC that is not used here; only caller is the display-transfer state machine 0x10CF50.

name: Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080
summary: Runs the GPU IPC command 0x3E0080 under the global scheduler lock: acquires the lock, takes the service handle, invokes Gfx_IpcCmd3E0080(handle, arg1), asserts on a negative result and unlocks.
evidence: The body neither returns the lock nor leaves it held: it locks, calls the now-named Gfx_IpcCmd3E0080 and unlocks, so 'Os_LockScheduler' named a helper step instead of the actual operation.

name: maybe_Svc_DispatchTwoRecordRequest
summary: Builds a two-entry, 0x10-byte-stride request array through std_ConstructArray(type 0x00119838), initialises it and dispatches it with the caller's request value through 0x00119B44/0x00119C30 before returning the result. The readable C stops at the array construction because Ghidra marks the std_ConstructArray blx as noreturn.
evidence: Disassembly shows the 2 x 0x10 std_ConstructArray call then further calls 0x119B44/0x119C30 with the r0 (request) argument; the only caller is Svc_RequestWithRetry, which passes its request and stores the return in result. 'StaticInit' was wrong - this is a stack request dispatch, not static initialisation.

name: Svc_SendRequest3
signature: int Svc_SendRequest3(u32 sessionHandle, int commandWord, u32 payload)
summary: Sends one raw IPC request on the given session handle: writes the fixed header 0x002C0044 and three payload words into the calling thread's IPC buffer (TLS+0x80), the descriptor commandWord<<14|2, then issues svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest) and returns the reply word. It is the terminal 'send it' step of the session layer; the caller decides the command word.
evidence: NEW: its only caller is the now-confident Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest (0x10CDE0), which calls it as the very last step after its poll loop and error check, and the sibling Svc_RequestWithRetry (0x10D430) brackets it with its retry counters. The header literal 0x002C0044 decodes as command 0x2C with one normal and four translated words, so the '3' in the old name is the number of payload words written (f_84/f_88/f_8c), not a command id.

name: Svc_QuerySessionInfo
signature: int Svc_QuerySessionInfo(u8 commandByte, u8 * out0, u32 * out1, u32 * out2, u32 * out3)
summary: Sends a one-byte command (header 0x00050040, command 0x05, one normal parameter) and copies the four reply words TLS+0x88..+0x94 into the caller's four outputs; the session layer uses it to poll a session's state before sending a request.
evidence: Confirmed: the confident caller Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest (0x10CDE0) calls it with command 0xff and four outputs and only proceeds when it returns non-negative, and 0x10D388 - already named Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked - is its second caller, i.e. the pair is the locked/unlocked query. Header 0x00050040 confirms the single-parameter command.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd1010000
summary: IPC stub with header 0x01010000 (no parameters) to the same session as the other GPU stubs; returns the result and writes the byte at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: asm 0x114584: header literal 0x1010000, TLS+0x80 = header, load handle from 0x7AF0D8, svc 0x32, if success *out = *(u8*)(TLS+0x88). The 0x7AF0D8 handle is shared by all stubs in this batch.

name: Svc_SendRequest4
signature: u32 Svc_SendRequest4(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int descriptorWord, u32 payload)
summary: Sends one raw IPC request with four payload words (header 0x001F0084 = command 0x1F, two normal + four translated words), descriptor arg3<<14|2, then svc 0x32 and returns the reply. The four-word sibling of Svc_SendRequest3.
evidence: NEW: named caller Svc_RequestWithRetry (0x10D430) calls it inside its retry loop with the request block built by the game's service wrapper, exactly as 0x10CDE0 calls Svc_SendRequest3 - so the pair is the session layer's generic request sender with 3 and 4 payload words. Header 0x001F0084 confirms command 0x1F.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd3B0040
summary: IPC stub for command 0x003B with one byte parameter and one translated parameter; returns the service result or the echoed value.
evidence: asm 0x114614: header g_00114648 = 0x003B0040, TLS+0x84 = arg1, svc 0x32, return TLS+0x84. Sole caller 0x10DA64 in the input/display code.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd2B0000
summary: IPC stub for command 0x002B (no parameters) to the shared GPU session; returns the service result or the TLS output word.
evidence: asm 0x114650: header &LAB_002B0000 = 0x002B0000, svc 0x32, return TLS+0x84. No callers; grouped by the 0x7AF0D8 handle.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd190040
summary: IPC stub for command 0x0019 with one translated parameter; returns the result or the echoed value.
evidence: asm 0x114680: header 0x00190040, TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x10D884 (display code).

name: Gfx_IpcCmd4F0080
summary: IPC stub for command 0x004F with two normal parameters; returns the result or the first output word.
evidence: asm 0x1146B8: header 0x004F0080, TLS+0x84=a, +0x88=b, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x10DA38 (display/HDMI-ish path).

name: Svc_PollStatusFlags
summary: Refreshes a pair of one-byte status flags: queries commands 0x3B and 0x3C, ORs both reply bytes into 0x7AF0DC, and when the 0x13 command returns 0xC9405001 it acknowledges with the 0x3D command.
evidence: Three named callers (Sound_WriteWaveBuffer, Svc_RequestWithRetry, Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest) call it before their service request, and the four command stubs it uses are named (Svc_QueryStatus3B/3C, Os_IpcSendCommand13/3D).

name: maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve
signature: u32* maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve(u32* ring, int count, u32* out)
summary: Reserves count contiguous free words in the sound command ring used by Snd_QueueCommandBuffer, tracking the ring read/write positions across the wrap and returning a pointer to the free run (or 0).
evidence: The ring helper it calls is the same Os_QueueTryPop (0x0011B57C) block as the sound/stream command ring, which supports the subsystem; but Ghidra gave up on most of the body (unaff_r4, coprocessor_function, halt_baddata), so the reserve arithmetic cannot be verified and the name stays a low-confidence maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcStubFragment
summary: Not a function start: the bytes here are the continuation of the IPC stub in front of it (store a byte at (arg2>>1)+0x10, svc 0x32, read the reply at (arg2>>1)+4). Kept only so the coverage table has an entry for this address.
evidence: NEW: no branch target reaches 0x001149AA, which confirms it is a Thumb mis-seed inside the previous routine rather than a callable entry. The body is a textbook SendSyncRequest stub tail, so the owner stays Svc_ and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker(u32 arg1, u32 mask, int count, u32* d, int header, int* state)
summary: Normalises a command-list state counter modulo 8 and validates the list header/count before copying command payloads; the decompiler hit bad instruction data at the first branch, so only the header check is trustworthy.
evidence: The body contains 'Bad instruction - Truncating control flow' and halt_baddata(), and the only listed caller (Input_ReadPadState) is a table neighbour rather than a real call; no named callee clarifies the format, so the name stays a guess.

name: maybe_Svc_ThumbFragment
signature: void maybe_Svc_ThumbFragment(u32 arg1, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d)
summary: Not a function start: the decoded bytes are a byte-swap idiom (rev of arg1, then stores of d at +0 and c at +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24/+0x28 of the swapped pointer) belonging to the routine that begins before this address. Kept only for coverage bookkeeping.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller and no data pointer to this address, which confirms the first pass's finding that it is interior code of the preceding routine. The name still says 'fragment, not a function', which is the only useful information available.

name: Mem_PoolDestroy
signature: void Mem_PoolDestroy(Pool* pool, u32 block, u32 count, u32 flags)
summary: Empties a pool: walks its four sublists, detaches every chunk through the chunk callback 0x0011B034, then re-initialises the pool descriptor and marks it reset (f_86=1).
evidence: NEW: the caller set is now named (Sound_StreamBuffer_Dtor, Sound_StreamPlayer_Release, Snd_StopVoiceByHandle, Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer) and the callees are the named Mem_PoolInit/Container_ListAppend, so 'empty and re-init a pool' is confirmed; the three trailing parameters are unused by the recovered body, hence the reconstructed prototype.

name: Snd_FadeChannelToGain
summary: Starts (or stops, when gain <= 0) a channel: stores the ramped gain, marks the channel dirty, inserts it into the mixer's priority list (0x11FD1C when the channel has an owner at +0x10) and calls the channel's vtable start slot; a stopped channel goes through the vtable stop slot instead.
evidence: `if (arg2 > 0 && *(self+0xa1) != 2 && ((char)self[0x26] || *(self+0x99))) { lock; s = (float)arg2 * volume; ... self[0x1a] = gain; self[0x1b] = g_00114dcc; self[0x1c] = (int)gain; self[0x1d] = 0; if (self[4]) func_0011FD1C(self[4], self); (**(code**)(*self + 0x24))(self); ... } else (**(code**)(*self + 0x10))(self);`. Callers 0x00105AFC/0x00105ACE/0x00105584 are the BGM player helpers and 0x1EC1D0 (Snd_RequestBgmPlay) passes volume*60.0f into it, which fixes the second parameter as a gain.

name: Fs_ArcHeader_Parse
summary: Parses a three-section archive header: checks the 'CGRP' magic and a size field in 0x01000000..0x01000100, resolves the three sub-blobs and returns pointers to their payloads (+8 past each header word).
evidence: Magic 0x50524743 ('CGRP'), three named section locators and two named callers (Container_ForEachPair, Sound_WaveArchive_LoadAndCache) all agree on an archive header parser.

name: Os_WorkQueue_Push
signature: u32 Os_WorkQueue_Push(WorkQueue* q, int wait, u32 arg3, int* node)
summary: Publishes the next work item on a queue: reserves a free node, and while none is free drains the completion queue (folding the finished item id into q->f_178/f_188), links the node at the tail, then either tries a non-blocking push or waits on the queue's send primitive; returns the sequence number or 0.
evidence: The body is built from the named Os_QueueTryPop/Os_QueueTryPush primitives, keeps an explicit head/tail pair (f_16C/f_170) and a sequence counter (f_174), and has seven callers including the sound-stream submit paths - that is a producer side of a queue, so 'Push' is descriptive rather than speculative.

name: Os_WorkQueue_Drain
summary: Discards every pending completion of a work queue: pops each finished node with Os_QueueTryPop, stores its item id in q->f_178, walks to the tail of the node chain and records the last in-flight id, clearing it when it matches q->f_184.
evidence: The body is the same completion-folding block that Os_WorkQueue_Push runs while waiting for a free node (identical code at 0x00114E60), now as a stand-alone loop built on the named Os_QueueTryPop; one caller is Sound_StreamThread_Main, i.e. a queue-owner thread draining before shutdown.

name: Os_QueuePopUntilId
summary: Blocks on the queue embedded at owner+0xB4 and pops entries until the one whose id field equals the requested id arrives, refreshing the owner's current-entry fields +0x178/+0x184/+0x188/+0x18C and clearing them when the last entry is popped.
evidence: The callee is the named Os_QueuePopBlocking and the seven callers span sound (Snd_QueueWaveCommand, Sound_StreamPlayer_Shutdown), archive (0x00543484) and the container/RB-tree helpers, so this is a generic queue primitive; the old 'Snd_' prefix named only one user.

name: std__Rb_tree_rebalance_for_erase
signature: void std__Rb_tree_rebalance_for_erase(RbTreeNode* z, RbTreeNode* header, RbTreeNode* leftmost, RbTreeNode* rightmost)
summary: libstdc++ red-black tree erase fix-up: handles the red-leaf case, the single-child splice case and the two-children case (find successor, copy colour, rotate with 0x11B9B0) so the tree invariants and the header's leftmost/rightmost pointers remain valid.
evidence: Body matches _Rb_tree_rebalance_for_erase case-by-case: 'if (z->left == 0) y = z->right; else if (z->right == 0) y = z->left; else { y = min(z->right); ... }'; colour byte +0x10; uses func_0011B9B0(node,bool,header) for rotations and func_00115114(...) for the successor transplant. Companion of 0x10EE9C/0x115290; reached through map erase sites (no direct call because it is inlined at most call sites).

name: std__Rb_tree_rebalance
summary: libstdc++ red-black tree rebalancing after insertion: recolours parent/uncle/grandparent and performs the left/right rotations through 0x11B9B0 until the root is black again.
evidence: Textbook _Rb_tree_rebalance: while (x != root && x->parent->colour == red) { if (parent == grandparent->left) { y = grandparent->right; if (y->colour == red) { recolour; x = grandparent; } else { if (x == parent->right) { x=parent; rotate_left; } parent->colour=black; grandparent->colour=red; rotate_right(grandparent); } } ... } root->colour = black. Sole caller 0x10EE9C; rotate helper 0x11B9B0 and node layout +0x4/+0x8/+0xC/+0x10 match the insert routine.

name: Save_BuildSectionList
summary: Builds the save-snapshot block list: walks the 0x274C-byte handler table at self+0x34, invokes each handler, chains the returned blocks into a list with a running id and pushes the head through Os_QueueTryPush.
evidence: The callers are the named SaveData_ResetAllSaveData and Item_ValidateAndCompactStorage, and the table dispatch plus the tagged list chained at self+0x16C..+0x174 matches save-snapshot construction; the handler block format is still unknown.

name: maybe_Queue_SubmitEntry
summary: Appends a buffer entry to the owner's submission chain, publishes it with a memory barrier and either pushes it to the OS queue or the ring buffer, then assigns and returns the next sequence number.
evidence: The body is a damaged fragment that reads the owner and flags from unaff_r4/r5/r7, and the header's '2920 Thumb bytes' does not match the 20-statement body, so the decompilation cannot be trusted. The callers span Container_ForEachPair, Gfx_InitCommandLists, Gfx_InitSubsystems and Sound_WaveArchive_LoadAndCache, so the Snd_ prefix was unsupported; only the queue/ring-buffer submit shape is visible.

name: Container_NewListNode
summary: Allocates a 0x28-byte list node from the global block allocator at 0x007AE8EC and zeroes all ten words; returns NULL when no allocator is installed or the allocation fails. The real function starts at 0x115F74 (the batch seed is 4 bytes late).
evidence: asm 0x115F74: ldr r0,[0x7AE8EC]; if (!*r0) return 0; blx *r0 with r0=0x10000, r1=0x100, r2=0, r3=0x28; then ten 'str r1,[r0,#0..0x24]'. Called by 0x10F74C to create the list sentinel; the 0x10000/0x100 signature is the engine's heap allocator ABI.

name: Gfx_AdvanceCommandList
summary: Consumes the next entry of the active GPU command list: bumps the read cursor under the renderer lock, invokes the list's completion callback when the last entry (or an end marker) is reached, and restarts the DMA through 0x116104.
evidence: Readable: fa0 = g_001160A8->f_a0; iVar4 = fa0->f_18 + fa0->f_28*0x1c; lock 0x1197FC; ++fa0->f_28; if (fa0->f_38 && (entry[1] || (count==f_20 && f_3c))) callback = fa0->f_38; if (entry[2]==0) { if (count<f_20) 0x116104(); else f_11=0; } else {...} unlock 0x11980C; indirect call. Same 0x1c-byte command records as 0x116104.

name: Mem_CommitAllocation
summary: Allocator slow path after a free block was split: stores the remainder size in the block trailer, returns the unused tail through 0x1193AC, sets the allocated flag 4 and clears the heap scratch begin/end words.
evidence: Both callers (0x110A28, 0x6BA234) are the two identical heap allocator instances and the body writes the 8-byte-unit trailer plus flag 4; the operation is the commit half of the split.

name: Gfx_ExecuteCommandList
summary: Drains the pending GPU command array: for every record from the read cursor to the write cursor it dispatches on the record type (0 = texture copy, 1 = surface fill, 2 = textured quad/blit, 3/4 = display transfer) to the corresponding 0x11C86C/0x11F28C/0x11C8A0/0x11C880/0x11C8C0 hardware command builder.
evidence: Readable switch on *record (0x1c-byte entries): case 0 -> func_0011C86C; 1 -> func_0011F28C; 2 -> func_0011C8A0(...); 3 -> func_0011C880(...); 4 -> func_0011C8C0(...). Those five are the GPU command builders (0x11C86C etc. are the batch entries that tail-call 0x11F12C/0x11F21C/0x11F35C/0x11F518). 12 callers incl. 0x109FB0, 0x110A28, 0x6B9D5C.

name: Gfx_NewCommandList
summary: Allocates and initialises a 0x1CC-byte command-list object: 0x2600 default words, a 0xFFFFFC18 sentinel, zeroed state and eight 0x44-byte slot descriptors (stride 0x44) tagged with the capacity argument.
evidence: Readable: alloc(0x10000,0x100,0,0x1cc); memset(0x1cc); result[0]=result[1]=0x2600; result[2..3]=g_00116428; result[5]=0xfffffc18; loop i=0..7: result[i*0x11+0x1d]=arg1 (0x44-byte stride). Caller 0x110470 (Gfx_InitCommandLists); companion 0x116430 builds the 0x78-byte single-slot variant.

name: Gfx_NewCommandListSlot
summary: Allocates and initialises a 0x78-byte single-slot command-list object (0x2600 defaults, 0xFFFFFC18 sentinel, one 0x44-byte descriptor at +0x74 tagged with the argument).
evidence: Readable: alloc 0x78, memset 0x78, result[0..1]=0x2600, result[2..3]=g_001164C0, result[5]=0xfffffc18, result[6..0xa]=g_001164C4, result[0x1d]=arg1. Called by 0x110470; pairs with 0x116368 (multi-slot).

name: Gfx_FreeCommandList
summary: Releases a command-list buffer: compares the list's slot address against the bound slot, calls the release callback with the target address/size and clears the three bookkeeping words.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_InitCommandLists and the 0x10000/0x20000 offsets it compares against are the two framebuffer slots that routine sets up, so the teardown reading is supported.

name: maybe_Gfx_NewRenderQueue
summary: Allocates and initialises a 0x348-byte render-state queue: 16 slots, each with a 0x18-byte and a 0x10-byte descriptor; the texture/handle words at +0x188/+0x18C/+0x194 are cleared and a 0.5f is stored at +0x288 in each 0xC-byte tail. Returns 0 when the allocator hook is null.
evidence: The 16 slots with per-slot texture handles and a 0.5 float match a 16-texture-unit render-state table, and the allocator hook is called through the caller-supplied vtable (+0), i.e. library-side allocation; there is no caller, so the 'render queue' label stays an interpretation - maybe_ at 0.45.

name: std_RingBuffer_Push
signature: void std_RingBuffer_Push(BufferQueue* queue, unsigned int value)
summary: Blocking push into a bounded producer ring: waits on the "not full" semaphore while the write index equals the capacity, stores the value, advances the write index and signals the consumer; a separate counter guards concurrent callers.
evidence: The body uses only Os_LockMonitor / Os_SemaphoreAcquire / Os_SemaphoreRelease on a plain index/capacity record - there is no sound-specific call, so the "Snd_" prefix of the first pass was a guess from its neighbours. Generic container code uses the std_ prefix, hence the new name.

name: Container_NameMap_FindNodePair
signature: void Container_NameMap_FindNodePair(void* outNodePair, void* tree, const void* hashAndNameKey)
summary: Searches an RB-tree keyed by (u32 hash, char name[0x20]): finds the lower-bound node for hashAndNameKey->u32_00, scans equal-hash nodes comparing the 0x20-byte label at entry + 0x1C (0x00123660), and writes {matchedNodeOrEnd, lowerBoundHint} to outNodePair.
evidence: ARM 0x1167C8..0x116960: truncates key[1] C-string to 0x1F chars + NUL on stack, finds RB-tree lower-bound r6 for hash key[0] (node+0x14), iterates equal-hash nodes via RB-next (0x115390 / 0x115358) comparing 0x20-byte node name via 0x123660; writes {r5, r6} on match (0x1168C4) or {endHeader r4, hint r6} on miss (0x116958). Used by Container_HashTableInsert and Container_NameMap_Find.

name: Os_InitMainThreadTls
summary: Prepares the thread-local storage for the main thread (0x00111EB0 then 0x00111EFC) and returns the default application heap size 0x03000000 (48 MB) that the caller hands to the heap setup.
evidence: Body is three statements: func_00111EB0(); func_00111EFC(); return 0x3000000; - i.e. the same TLS pair as 0x0011CC30's thread trampoline. Its only caller 0x00106F70 passes the return value straight to 0x0010BDB0, which is the heap-size commit.

name: Container_ResizeArray
summary: Resizes an inline array to count 4-byte elements: destroys the old storage through the virtual at +0x10, allocates count*4 bytes from heap self[0xB] and zeroes the whole buffer with an unrolled 8/4/2/1-word pattern.
evidence: Readable: (*(code**)(*self+0x10))(self); self->f_10=(char)count; puVar1 = Mem_AllocAligned(count<<2, self[0xb], 4) (0x10F6EC); self[0xf]=puVar1; unrolled zero loop with size-0x20 steps, then 16/8/4/2/1 tails. This is a vector-like container resize used by the command-list objects.

name: Actor_LoadParams
summary: Copies the 0x50-byte parameter record for actor id self->f_768 from the world actor table into the instance fields at +0x30..+0x78.
evidence: func_006F20C0 returns the world singleton; func_0035EB98(world, self->f_768) returns the actor record (same helper used by every actor getter in this batch). The body copies record +0x10..+0x5c into self +0x30..+0x78 field by field.

name: std_memcpy
signature: void * std_memcpy(void * dst, const void * src, u32 bytes)
summary: memcpy: copies bytes with an unrolled 32/16/8/4/2/1-byte ladder, loading eight words at a time while more than 0x20 bytes remain; returns the end of the destination in the second return register.
evidence: Body: while (bytes > 0x1f) copy 8 words (ldm/stm via HintPreloadData hints), then a bit-test ladder for 0x10 / 8 / 4 / 2 / 1; 385 callers, all record/struct copies (e.g. 0x10f448 copying 0x168-byte blocks, 0x1926d4 copying a 0x84-byte text-style record).

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseCommandBuffers
summary: When the list's 'owns buffers' bit (byte +4, bit 0) is set, releases the three buffer pairs (+0x58/+0x34, +0x60/+0x3C, +0x64/+0x40) through 0x116DA4. That helper is `cmp r2,#0; bxeq lr; ...`, i.e. it does nothing when the size is zero, which is exactly how a (pointer, size) release behaves.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x116DA4 shows an early `bxeq lr` when the size argument is zero, confirming it is a (pointer, size) release rather than a plain free; the three released pairs match the command-list objects built by 0x116368/0x116430. No exact caller exists (it is reached through a vtable), so the object type stays inferred.

name: maybe_Game_ApplyValueToHandle
signature: void maybe_Game_ApplyValueToHandle(u32 arg1, u8 recordIndex, int* handle, u32 value)
summary: Game data layer: if the caller holds a live handle, resolves the record for the given index through the data manager (0x0011BAC0) and, unless that record is still in state 1, writes the value into the handle's object (0x0011B530).
evidence: Re-read: the first callee is the confident Game_GetDataManager, so this is the game's data layer, not the pack/file layer the old 'Pack_' prefix suggested, and the record state test (+4 == 1) is the same one used by 0x00116E44 and 0x0011AE88, i.e. 'skip records that are still loading'. No caller, so it stays maybe_.

name: Pack_ApplyToLoadedHandles
summary: Pushes a value into every live handle of a streamed slot - the two buffers at +0x34/+0x3C, the pack-backed one at +0x40 and each 0x14-byte record of the bitmap table at +0x7C - but only when the corresponding pack record reports type 2.
evidence: The shared type-2 test (0x0011BAC0 record lookup) is repeated for each handle and the bitmap walk honours the 0x18 skip bits, which pins this as the "apply to all loaded handles" helper; the same four callers as the voice/stream code use it. The applied value's meaning is unknown, so 0.5.

name: maybe_Os_SendIpcCmd0863Request
summary: Builds the request block with 0x117098 and sends the fixed command 0x0863 through 0x11DED4, writing the reply to *out. The old 'ServiceInit' label was unsupported: the header 0x08630000 carries no parameters and nothing in the body mentions a service initialisation.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x1114F4 (maybe_Svc_Object_InitFromReader), and the callee 0x11DED4 sets TLS+0x80 = 0x08630000 and issues svc 0x32 with no parameter words, so the verified content is 'build the block, send command 0x0863'. The command number is the only hard fact, hence the name and the sub-0.5 confidence.

name: maybe_Os_AssertAndGetState
summary: Asserts that *object is non-zero (routing to 0x11ED40 with 0xE0A046DB otherwise) and then returns the second word of the global at 0x7AEA38. It proves the pointer is non-null but tests no readiness, so the old 'object ready' wording was already dropped.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and 0x11ED40 has no readable body, so the assert target cannot be identified. The returned word is the same 0x7AEA38 global the Snd_* driver code uses as its context slot, which is why the name keeps the Os prefix and stays below 0.5.

name: Save_AsyncReadWorker
summary: Asynchronous save/load read worker: waits on the work event, reads length-prefixed records through Fs_ReadRecordBlock, and drives the shared work state at 0x007B0080/0x007B00E0 until the request is complete or times out.
evidence: Uses SVC 0x28 (GetSystemTick) and the 1,000,000 constant g_0011798c, calls Fs_ReadRecordBlock (0x122938), the deadline helper 0x11DF50 and the state check 0x11E374. The globals 0x007B0080/0x007B0086/0x007B00E0 are the same work object updated by Save_InitPartySnapshot's callers, and *g_00117990=5 marks completion.

name: maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker
summary: Walks the 32-bit occupancy bitmap of a render/surface table (bitmap at +0x80, count at +0x88, records at +0x7C stride 0x14) and re-submits every live record whose flags (+0x11) clear bits 0x18 and whose first word is non-zero (0x11B530).
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and the body reads its table pointer from unaff_r4, so the object is a caller register rather than a parameter - the function index's 0x568-byte size is also wrong (the prologue is earlier). Per FACTS.md a body with unaff_ registers keeps maybe_ at 0.3 or below; the record stride and flag bits are the only readable facts.

name: maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry
summary: Reads a 0x40-byte parameter header through the chunked table reader, searches its four 0x10-byte entries for type byte 0 and unpacks the two 12-bit fields plus payload word; falls back to the 0x400-offset scan and finally to the fixed 0x800/0x800/1.0 defaults.
evidence: The only caller is the damaged maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveTailArm (0x00111C58), which uses the returned word as a packed rotation/format value; the calibration-like defaults (centre 0x800, scale 1.0f) still do not identify the table, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd90000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0009 with no parameters; returns the service result or the TLS output word.
evidence: asm 0x117AB8: header 0x00090000, svc 0x32, return TLS+0x84. Sole caller 0x1221C0 (GPU bring-up code); same handle family as the other GSP stubs in this batch.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd20000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0002 with no parameters; returns the service result or the TLS output word.
evidence: asm 0x117AE8: header 0x00020000, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x11E54C (session teardown), which calls it before closing the session handle.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd40000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0004 with no parameters; used as the 'wait for GPU interrupt' request (0x111BAC).
evidence: asm 0x117B18: header 0x00040000, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x111BAC, which maps the 0xFFFFF9 result to 'retry'.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd30000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0003 with no parameters; used as the 'acknowledge/release interrupt' request (0x111BEC).
evidence: asm 0x117B48: header 0x00030000, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x111BEC, paired with 0x111BAC/0x117B18.

name: Os_LockSemaphore
summary: Blocks until the semaphore/lock word at *lock becomes 0, then atomically sets it to -1; when the count is positive it arbitrates through 0x11CC10 (svcArbitrateAddress) until the state word is free.
evidence: Readable: loop { iVar3=*arg1; if (iVar3==-2) {0x11CC10(*g,arg1,1,0,0,0); return;} if (iVar3==0) { do { if (*arg1) goto got; } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(arg1)); *arg1=-1; got: if (!iVar3) return; } else if (iVar3==1) return; 0x11CC10(*g,arg1,1,0,0,0); }. 13 callers including 0x102BA4, 0x11896C and 0x517884; the 0x11CC10 helper is the kernel address-arbiter wrapper.

name: Os_TryLockSemaphore
summary: Attempts to take the semaphore: if the state is 1 it enters the waiting path, decrements/negates the counter under ldrex, and only arbitrates when the count becomes positive; returns the owner/state pointer.
evidence: Readable: if (*arg1 != 1) { result=*arg1; if (!result) { spin until ldrex, *arg1=-1; } return result; } result=arg1+1; func_0011E614(); spin *arg1=-2; iVar4=*result; *result=-iVar4; if (iVar4 != -1 && 0 < iVar2) func_0011CC10(...). Same state values (-1/-2/1) as 0x117B78.

name: Os_EventSetAll
summary: Signals an event/light-lock: atomically negates the counter, and when it had waiters (old value != -1 and the new value > 0) wakes them with the kernel synchronisation call 0x11CC10.
evidence: Confirmed: the atomic negate + 'if it had waiters, wake with count 1' sequence is the canonical CTR event signal, and both callers (0x114E60 and 0x117E88, the unlock half of the monitor pair) use it as the wake step. The name matches the code, so the maybe_ prefix is dropped.

name: Os_SemaphoreAcquire
summary: Blocks until the semaphore count is positive, then atomically decrements it; waiters are registered with the kernel wait call so a release wakes exactly one of them.
evidence: `while (*arg1 < 1) { ClearExclusiveLocal(); waiters++; func_0011CC10(*g_00117dc0, arg1, 1, 1, 0, 0); waiters--; } *arg1 -= 1;` with an exclusive-access loop protecting both fields. This is the counterpart of 0x117DC4 (release) and is used by the blocking ring push in 0x1166B4.

name: Os_SemaphoreRelease
summary: Releases `count` units of a semaphore (clamped at the capacity), then signals the kernel so a waiting thread can proceed; returns the previous count.
evidence: `do { result = *arg1; iVar2 = (short)*(arg1+6); if (result <= iVar2 - arg2) iVar2 = result + arg2; } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(arg1)); *arg1 = iVar2; if (result < 1 || (short)arg1[1] > 0) func_0011CC10(*g_00117e38, arg1, 0, arg2, 0, 0); return result;`. The clamp/count logic is the semaphore release; callers 0x110FD8 and 0x006E74AC.

name: Snd_LockSystemMonitor
summary: Locks the sound system's monitor: calls the sound-system accessor 0x5177DC, adds 0x34 to the returned object and falls into the monitor-lock body at 0x117E50. Its mirror 0x51864C adds the same 0x34 and branches to the monitor unlock 0x117ED0, which is what proves the pair.
evidence: Corrected from 'Os_Abort': 0x5177DC is not a panic routine but `ldr r0,[pc,#0x90]` into the sound-system accessor 0x5177E0 (which returns the object at 0x7F09C8 after an init assert), so nothing here aborts. NEW: its eight callers are the movie-track create/pause/start/update functions, which lock this monitor in the else branch of the movie manager's own lock, and the exact mirror 0x51864C (add 0x34, branch to 0x117ED0 = unlock) is called by the same functions for the release half.

name: Os_LockMonitor
summary: Enters a recursive monitor: when the calling thread is not the owner it blocks in the kernel wait (0x11E614) and records the new owner, then increments the recursion count.
evidence: `iVar1 = CP15 c13 c0 3; if (iVar1 != *(int*)(arg1+4)) { func_0011E614(arg1); *(u32*)(arg1+4) = GetThread(); } *(int*)(arg1+8) += 1;` - used 98 times across the binary as the standard lock/unlock pair with 0x117ED0.

name: Os_UnlockMonitor
summary: Recursive monitor release used at the end of locked sections: takes the monitor lock, and when the state byte f_76 is not 2 it marks the monitor contended, releases the raw lock (0x00117ED0) and waits on the semaphore at +100; otherwise it clears f_76, decrements the recursion count at +8 and, when that reaches zero, clears the owner at +4 and wakes all waiters (Os_EventSetAll).
evidence: 91 call sites (70 named) are always paired with Os_LockMonitor, and the body is the recursive unlock protocol (f_76 state, +8 recursion, +4 owner, EventSetAll). The earlier objection is consistent with the name: 0x00117ED0 is the raw release used inside this wrapper, while this function also handles the contended/waiter hand-off.

name: Os_AcquireSemaphore
summary: Waits until the semaphore's counter is positive, then increments it atomically; used to claim one of the engine's counted resources.
evidence: Readable: while (*arg1 < 1) { ClearExclusiveLocal(); func_0011CC10(*g,arg1,1,0,0,0); } ldrex/strex ++*arg1. The loop/arbitrate pattern is identical to the other Os semaphore helpers; no direct callers in the readable tree (used from inline code).

name: Os_ReleaseSemaphoreAll
summary: Waits for the resource to be free, negates the counter and wakes every waiter by arbitrating with 0xFFFFFFFF until the state reaches -1.
evidence: Readable: while (*arg1 < 1) { ClearExclusiveLocal(); 0x11CC10(*g,arg1,1,0,0,0); } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(arg1)); *arg1 = -*arg1; while (*arg1 != -1) func_0011CC10(*g,arg1,1,0xffffffff,0,0);. Complement of 0x117EF0.

name: Os_ReleaseSemaphore
summary: Decrements the semaphore count (or moves a negative count towards zero) atomically and signals the address arbiter with -1 when the last user releases it.
evidence: Readable: do { iVar2=*arg1; iVar2 = (iVar2<0) ? iVar2+1 : iVar2-1; } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(arg1)); *arg1=iVar2; if (*arg1 == -1) func_0011CC10(*g,arg1,0,0xffffffff,0,0);. Mirrors 0x117EF0/0x117F5C.

name: Os_SignalSemaphore
summary: Negates the semaphore counter and immediately wakes all waiters through the arbiter, without first waiting for the counter to reach a positive value.
evidence: Readable: spin ldrex; *arg1 = -*arg1; func_0011CC10(*g,arg1,0,0xffffffff,0,0);. Same primitive as 0x117F5C but unconditional; used by 0x1180xx mutex paths.

name: maybe_Os_CheckSemaphoreResult
signature: void maybe_Os_CheckSemaphoreResult(u32 result, u32 arg2, OsSemaphore* syncObject, char* pendingFlag)
summary: Result filter for a synchronisation primitive: when the object's +0x14 bit 0 is clear and the caller's pending flag is unset it maps result class -1 to the assert handler 0x1188EC and then runs the completion helper 0x11C814; otherwise only the classes -7 (invalid) and 1 (success) are accepted, everything else goes to the assert path.
evidence: NEW: no branch target reaches 0x00118108, so it is dead code and no caller can confirm the role; the body is a hand-written result filter (it decodes the nn::Result module/description fields) rather than a getter, which is why the name is not a predicate. The owner stays Os_ and the name keeps maybe_.

name: Os_InitEventFlag
summary: Initialises an event/flag object: takes the kernel lock (svc 0x24), validates the handle, then marks the object as initialised. Called from the shutdown path 0x11F764.
evidence: Readable: if (*(char*)(arg1+4)==0) { software_interrupt(0x24); if (*arg1 < 0) func_00118100(); *(u8*)(arg1+4)=1; }. 0x118100 is the panic/assert helper (used by 0x110FD8 too). Sole caller 0x11F764.

name: Os_RunTlsDestructors
summary: Runs the thread-local destructors for the thread that has just finished: walks the 16 destructor slots, and for each slot that is both present in the thread's mask and non-null it calls destructor(thread->slot[i]). Called by the thread trampoline immediately before svcExitThread.
evidence: `mask = g_00118208; table = g_00118204; for (i = 0; i < 0x10; i++) { pc = table[i]; if (i < 0x10 && ((*mask >> i) & 1) && pc != 0) { tp = mrc p15,0,r0,c13,c0,3; pc(tp[i]); } }`; caller 0x0011CC30 = the thread entry trampoline (its next call is svc #9, svcExitThread).

name: Svc_Cfg_CloseServiceS
summary: Drops one user of the lazily opened 'cfg:s' session; when the count reaches zero it closes the handle in 0x007B2CFC and restores the cached handle word into 0x007AF0F8.
evidence: NEW: pairs with 0x001182FC, whose IPC open call passes the literal 0x0078C6F3 = 'cfg:s' (verified: bytes 'cfg:s\0' at 0x0078C6F3), and the release dispatcher 0x0011212C calls it for kind 1. The old 'A/B' suffix was a placeholder; the service name is now known.

name: Svc_Cfg_CloseServiceI
summary: Drops one user of the lazily opened 'cfg:i' session; at zero it closes the handle in 0x007B2CF8 and copies the cached handle into both 0x007AF0F8 and 0x007B2CFC.
evidence: NEW: the matching open 0x001183A4 reads the pointer stored at 0x00754F90, which is 0x0078C6ED = 'cfg:i' (verified bytes 'cfg:i\0'), and 0x0011212C calls this for kind 2. So the second 'shared session' is the cfg import session.

name: Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceS
summary: Reference-counted open of the 'cfg:s' session: on first use it opens the service handle into 0x007B2CFC and publishes it as the current config handle, then increments the user count; the 'already open' error code is passed through.
evidence: NEW: the IPC open call receives the pointer stored at 0x00754F98, which is 0x0078C6F3 = 'cfg:s' (verified: 'cfg:s\0' at 0x0078C6F3) and the strlen/srvGetServiceHandle pair is the same one the confident Svc_Cecd_OpenService uses. The old 'A' suffix is replaced by the actual service name.

name: Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceI
summary: Reference-counted open of the 'cfg:i' session: on first use it opens the handle into 0x007B2CF8, copies it into the two current-handle slots and increments the count.
evidence: NEW: the open call reads the pointer stored at 0x00754F90, which is 0x0078C6ED = 'cfg:i' (verified bytes 'cfg:i\0'), the twin of the 'cfg:s' open. Both are called from maybe_Svc_Cfg_EnsureService.

name: Os_InitializeOnce
summary: Classic one-shot initialisation with a published state: the first caller atomically flips the flag from 0 to 1, initialises the global object 0x007EF0A4 and then stores its address in the flag (state 2); every other caller sleeps 1 ms until the flag reaches 2. Returns the published pointer/state.
evidence: `do { uVar3 = *flag; if (uVar3 != 0) { ClearExclusiveLocal(); goto done; } } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(flag)); *flag = 1;` then `if (uVar3 == 0) { *g_001184e8 = 0; func_00111E28(g_001184e8); ...; *flag = (u32)puVar2; } else { while (*flag < 2) func_0011CC94(0x000F4240 /* 1e6 ns = 1 ms */, 0); }`. g_001184ec = 0x000F4240 is that sleep argument.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd10082
signature: u32 Gfx_IpcCmd10082(u32 buffer, int size, u32 addr)
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0001 with 2 normal + 2 translated parameters, used to feed a memory range (buffer/size/address) to the GPU; command 0x00010082 is GSPGPU's register/block write request.
evidence: asm 0x1184F4: header 0x00010082, TLS+0x84=arg2, +0x88=arg3, +0x8c=arg2<<4|0xC, +0x90=arg1, svc 0x32. No callers in the readable tree; 0x1196B0 is a sibling with the same header used by 0x1136D8 (Gfx_WriteHwRegs).

name: maybe_Snd_QueryChannelInfo
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_QueryChannelInfo(unsigned int command, unsigned int in, unsigned int size, unsigned short* outCount)
summary: Forwards a channel query to the driver when the session at 0x7AEA08 is open; when it is not, writes 0 to *outCount and returns the 'no session' code 0xC8A0A7F8. The actual IPC goes through 0x11EBD8, which submits a buffer descriptor with command 0x10.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x11302C (maybe_Snd_SetupChannelBuffers), which calls it twice - once for the buffer count and once for the size - confirming the 'query with an output count' reading. The caller is itself still maybe_, so the Snd prefix and the 'Channel' wording stay inferred.

name: maybe_Hid_GetEventObject
signature: u32 maybe_Hid_GetEventObject(HidObject* object, u32* out, u32 defaultValue, u32 b)
summary: Stores its third argument in *out, then, if the object owns a session handle at +8, sends command 0x0C through 0x0011EC40 and lets it overwrite *out with the reply. Always returns the constant 0xC8A0A7F8, so the return value carries no information.
evidence: 0x0011EC40 (command 0x0C) has this function as its only caller, so the pair is a single command wrapper; the Hid_ owner is still only an inference from the surrounding input code, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd130082
signature: u32 Gfx_IpcCmd130082(u32* session, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0013 with 2 normal + 2 translated parameters; used to configure a shared buffer (a/b/c are address, size and offset).
evidence: asm 0x11867C: header 0x00130082, TLS+0x84=arg3, +0x88=arg4, +0x8c=0, +0x90=arg2, svc 0x32. No callers; same shared-buffer shape as 0x1184F4.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd120000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0012 with no parameters; returns the result or the TLS output word.
evidence: asm 0x1186B8: header 0x00120000, svc 0x32. No callers; part of the same GSP command set.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd170040
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0017 with one translated 16-bit parameter (typically a display/lcd selector).
evidence: asm 0x1186E0: header 0x00170040, TLS+0x84=arg2, svc 0x32. No callers.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd160000
summary: IPC stub for GPU-service command 0x0016 with no parameters; returns the service result and copies the 0x8C output word to *out.
evidence: asm 0x118718: header 0x00160000, svc 0x32, if success *arg2 = TLS+0x8c. No callers.

name: maybe_Snd_IpcCmd15
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_IpcCmd15(unsigned int* session, unsigned int unitFlag, unsigned int unitIndex, unsigned int c)
summary: IPC stub for command 0x15 (header 0x00150082 = two normal + two translated words): stores a/b/c in the thread IPC buffer and returns the reply. Its only caller uses it as the write half of a read-modify-write over a per-unit flag mask.
evidence: NEW: the two branch targets are 0x00112404 and 0x0011242C, both inside the unit-flag setter 0x001123B0, which passes the handle from 0x007AEA00+8 - the same context as the flush pair. The stub itself only forwards the words, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Snd_FlushChannels
summary: Per-frame flush of the active channel bank: if the 'active' byte at 0x7AEA00 is set, reconfigures the two unit records through 0x11E9C4, runs the eight registered flush callbacks of the table at 0x7E7998, clears the flag and finally sends the per-session teardown command 0x20.
evidence: NEW: it walks the same eight-hook table at 0x7E7998 as 0x11ECC0 (the stop-time variant), while 0x11233C walks a different one at 0x7E79B8 - so the two tables are per-module hook lists of one driver. The 0x7AEA00 owner is still unnamed, so the Snd prefix stays a guess.

name: Os_InvokeCallbacks
summary: When a pending-event bit is set, invokes up to eight registered callback slots and, if the pending byte is still set, waits for the runtime event to drain, sends the close request and clears the pending flags.
evidence: Shared with 0x0050DCB0 and its callers are the service wrappers 0x10CDE0/0x10D430/0x119AF4; the eight-slot table plus pending/handled mask is an explicit callback dispatch loop.

name: maybe_Os_WaitIpcTransferDone
summary: Waits for an asynchronous IPC transfer to finish: under the global monitor 0x007E7A70 it polls the completion object at 0x007AEA24, sleeps while the status is the 0xD0401834/busy value, then retires the record with 0x0011CC7C and re-sends it through Svc_SendRequestBuffer128; re-arms the wait object when the record is not in state 2 or 5.
evidence: The body uses only OS primitives (Os_LockMonitor, Os_LightEvent_Init, Os_LockSemaphore, Svc_SendRequestBuffer128) and is tail-entered from 0x00118918/0x0011895C in the 0x00118814 path; there is no sound-specific call, so the 'Snd_' attribution had no support. The record states 2/5 and the busy code are generic IPC states.

name: Mem_InitBlockPool
signature: void Mem_InitBlockPool(Pool* self, int blockBytes, int usedBytes, int totalBytes, int align, u32 flags)
summary: Turns a raw buffer into a pool of fixed-size blocks: computes the aligned block stride, the block count and the first/last block addresses, then links every block into a singly linked free list and records head/tail. No allocation happens here - the caller supplies the memory.
evidence: `self->f_14 = flags; iVar1 = align_up(blockBytes, align) * align; self->f_18 = iVar1; n = align_up(usedBytes, align); self->f_1c = n * align; blocks = align_up(usedBytes + totalBytes - self->f_1c, iVar1); self->f_20 = blocks * iVar1; ... do { *p = prev; p -= self->f_18; } while (p >= self->f_1c); self->f_24 = p;` - the loop writes each block's 'next' pointer, so f_24 is the free-list head. Called with (0x20 block, ...) and (0x18 block, ...) by the archive loader 0x001114F4.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelLevel
summary: Stores a 16-bit value in the channel block's field at +0xBC and sets bit 0x10000 of the second dirty word at +0xC0. The field is channel-wide (no unit index) and sits right after the two per-unit records; its meaning is still unknown, so the 'level' reading stays a guess.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly is `strh r5,[r0,#0xbc]` - a halfword, not the 32-bit word the old summary claimed - and there is no unit index, so 'SetUnitLevel' named the wrong scope. The dirty bit 0x10000 lives in the +0xC0 word that also carries the per-unit record bits 0x400/0x800/0x1000/0x2000 (0x118E58, 0x118FD4), while the other setters use the +0 word. Callers pass the saved state byte +3.

name: Snd_SetUnitActive
signature: u32 Snd_SetUnitActive(ChannelBuffer* context, int unit, u16 active)
summary: Publishes the per-unit enable flag of the current sound channel: stores `active` in the halfword at channel+0x28+unit*2 and sets dirty bit 0x100 (unit 0) or 0x200 (unit 1) so the driver re-reads it. Returns 0 when the driver lock is not held.
evidence: NEW: both named callers publish exactly this flag - Sound_Channel_SetActive (0x5185E4) writes the per-slot active byte at self+slot+0x30 and then calls this with the same slot, and Sound_Channel_SetDecodeHook (0x518550) calls it with 0 or 1 depending on whether a hook is installed; Snd_InitChannelState (0x112A9C) replays the saved per-unit bytes state[0x30]/state[0x31]. The old 'SetChannelHalfword' only described the store.

name: Snd_SetChannelRate
signature: unsigned int Snd_SetChannelRate(ChannelBuffer* context, unsigned int rate)
summary: Writes a channel's 16-bit rate field (+0x22), clamped to 0x8000, and marks that field dirty (bit 0x80000000) in the channel block's flag word. The 0x8000 ceiling is the DSP's 32 kHz sample clock, which is what identifies the field as a rate rather than a volume.
evidence: NEW: the save/restore pair 0x112A9C (init) and 0x112CAC (restore) feed it the saved state word f_2a, i.e. it is one of the fields replayed when a channel state is applied. The clamp to exactly 0x8000 (= 32768 Hz, the 3DS DSP sample rate) is the evidence that the field is a sample rate; the old 0.40 was only 'a rate-like setter'.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelFormat
summary: Stores a 16-bit value in the channel block's field at +0x18 and sets dirty bit 0x8000000. Snd_InitChannelState publishes 1 here and the restore path replays the saved state byte +1, so it is one of the channel-state fields; that the field is a sample format is still an inference.
evidence: NEW: Snd_InitChannelState (0x112A9C) sets state[1] = 1 and publishes it through this setter, and maybe_Snd_RestoreChannelState (0x112CAC) replays state+1 - so the field is confirmed to be a saved channel-state byte, but nothing in the code names it a format. Kept below 0.5.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelGain
summary: Stores a float in the channel block's field at +0x04 and sets dirty bit 0x10000. The value is a VFP single (Ghidra dropped it as in_s0); Snd_InitChannelState publishes 1.0f, so it is a gain-like scalar rather than an address.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly is `vmov.f32 s16,s0` + `vstr s16,[r0,#4]` - a float store - and Snd_InitChannelState (0x112A9C) publishes 0x3F800000 (= 1.0f) through it. 'SetChannelDataAddress' is therefore impossible: a data address is never a 1.0f VFP value. Gain vs playback-rate is still open, so maybe_ stays.

name: Snd_SetChannelLength
signature: unsigned int Snd_SetChannelLength(ChannelBuffer* buf, unsigned int length)
summary: Writes a channel's loop length: clamps the value to 0x7FFF, stores it as a halfword in the channel block and sets the 0x20000000 update bit.
evidence: The clamp, the halfword store and the dirty-bit set are explicit; which channel register the field is remains inferred from the 24-channel bank layout shared with the other setters.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmState
signature: u32 maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmState(ChannelBuffer* context, int unit, u16 value)
summary: Stores a 16-bit value in the per-unit halfword at channel+0x24+unit*2 and sets dirty bit 0x40 (unit 0) or 0x80 (unit 1); any other unit index writes the field without a dirty bit. Returns 0 when the driver lock is not held.
evidence: NEW: maybe_Snd_RestoreChannelState (0x112CAC) replays the two saved bytes state[0x24]/state[0x25] through it one per unit, and Snd_InitChannelState clears both, so the two-slot shape is confirmed; the 'ADPCM decoder state' reading still rests only on the 0x40/0x80 bit pair, so maybe_ stays.

name: Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields
signature: unsigned int Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields(void* buf, int index, unsigned short* info)
summary: Copies a mask-selected set of fields from a descriptor into one 0x14-byte channel record (bit0 one halfword, bit1 one word, bit2 five halfwords) and sets the dirty bit 0x400 for unit 0 or 0x800 for unit 1.
evidence: The two callers are the channel-unit reset paths (maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnitsInPlace, maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnitsToDefault), and the body copies the mask-selected fields into the 0x14-byte record under the driver lock (func_0011E99C/func_0011E9A8), OR-ing the mask into +0x2C and setting the dirty bits 0x400/0x800.

name: maybe_Snd_SetUnitGain
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetUnitGain(ChannelBuffer* context, int unit, float gain)
summary: Stores a float in the per-unit field at channel+0x08+unit*4 and sets dirty bit 0x1000000 (unit 0) or 0x2000000 (unit 1). Snd_InitChannelState publishes 1.0f for both units, so these are per-unit gain scalars, not loop information.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly is `vmov.f32 s16,s0` + `vstr s16,[r1,#4]` with r1 = block+4+unit*4, i.e. a float store at +0x08/+0x0C, and Snd_InitChannelState (0x112A9C) publishes 0x3F800000 (= 1.0f) for both units. 'Loop info' cannot be a 1.0f VFP value; the two units are the channel's main/aux wave buffers (Sound_Channel_SetWaveBufferMain/Aux).

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor(ChannelBuffer* buf, int index, unsigned short* info)
summary: Copies a mask-selected descriptor into one 0x34-byte channel record of the +0x10A4 table (bit0 one halfword at +0x56, bit1 five words at +0x5C..+0x6C, bit2 twelve halfwords at +0x5A..+0x86) and sets the dirty bit 0x1000 for channel 0 or 0x2000 for channel 1.
evidence: Largest of the channel field writers; the mask semantics are certain but the old 'FilterCoefficients' guess named the content, so the neutral copy-only name stays at maybe_ 0.4.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan(ChannelBuffer* context, unsigned short pan)
summary: Writes the halfword at +0x16 of the channel block and sets dirty bit 0x4000000.
evidence: 0x00112CAC (restore) replays the saved state byte +2 through it immediately before the format write, and 0x00112D98 (SetOutputMode) copies the same field from saved state, so it is confirmed to be a per-channel state field written from saved data; 'pan' remains the best guess for a 16-bit field between rate and volume, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelVolume
summary: Stores a 16-bit value in the channel block's field at +0x10 and sets dirty bit 0x8000. Snd_InitChannelState publishes 2 here and the restore path replays the saved state word f_32, so it is a channel-state field; the volume reading is still an inference.
evidence: NEW: Snd_InitChannelState (0x112A9C) sets state[0x32] = 2 and publishes it, and maybe_Snd_RestoreChannelState (0x112CAC) replays state->f_32 through it last before the unit level - so the field is confirmed to be saved channel state, but a default of 2 does not prove it is a volume. Kept below 0.5.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelField1A
summary: Writes the 16-bit field at +0x1a of the current channel block and marks it dirty (bit 0x10000000), returning 1 on success and 0 when the driver is not ready. Same channel lookup as the Snd_SetChannel* setters; which logical field +0x1a is, is not proven.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x00112E10, inside maybe_Snd_SetOutputMode (0x00112D98), so it is one of the channel-state setters; the block selection (double-buffer selector at ctx+0x1322 into the 24-entry pointer table at ctx+0x10a4) is identical to the named Snd_SetChannel* family. The field's meaning is still unknown, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput(ChannelBuffer* context, unsigned int outputSelect)
summary: Writes the channel's output/bus selector (value must be < 2) at +0x1e and marks it dirty (bit 0x40000000).
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x00112D60, inside maybe_Snd_RestoreChannelState (0x00112CAC), which replays the saved byte f_27 through it - so it is confirmed to be one of the channel-state fields.
