The '< 2' guard plus a single two-valued field is still the only argument for reading it as an output selector, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd50100Query
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmd50100Query(u32* out, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: IPC stub for command 0x00050100 (4 normal parameters): sends a/b/c, returns the service result and copies the 0x8C output word to *out.
evidence: asm 0x1192F4: header g_00119348 = 0x00050100, func_0011FFFC(TLS+0x84), TLS+0x8c=arg3, +0x90=arg4, svc 0x32; on success *arg1=TLS+0x8c. Largest-command-id sibling of 0x114344 (which sends one word with the same header family).

name: Gfx_IpcCmdC0080
summary: IPC stub for command 0x000C with two normal parameters; returns the service result or the echoed first word.
evidence: asm 0x119350: header g_00119380 = 0x000C0080, TLS+0x84=a, +0x88=b, svc 0x32. Callers 0x10BA40 and 0x1170CC.

name: maybe_Gfx_GetQueueStatus
summary: Reads the pending byte at +1 of the per-thread queue object selected by index (the TLS+0x5C array) - a command-list busy predicate. 0x11F720 supplies the TLS base.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and 0x11F720 has no readable body, so the TLS base is inferred from the +0x5C offset only. The 'per-thread queue slot' reading is unchanged from the first pass; the owner is still unproven, so the Gfx prefix stays a guess.

name: maybe_Os_StoreThreadLocalValue
summary: Allocator shim: passes the per-thread block (0x0011F730), the global at 0x007418D0 and the two arguments to the OS command-0x08 helper 0x0011F65C.
evidence: The callee is the command-0x08 IPC request 0x0011F65C and the only caller is Mem_CommitAllocation (0x001160AC), so 'the allocator publishes a per-thread value through an OS command' is confirmed; what the value means is not, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Snd_RequestSuspend
summary: Asks the runtime to suspend: if the runtime predicate 0x11F20C holds it sends command 0x16 with mode 0, and on success clears the runtime object's +0x30 flag; otherwise it returns the cached 'not initialised' code.
evidence: Confirmed: its pair 0x119444 is called from the same place with the flag inverted, both are reached from 0x1142A0 (the suspend/resume switch), and the command-0x16 stub (0x1196F8) carries the mode byte this function supplies as 0. The two functions differ only in that flag value and in which command stub they call, which is exactly what the names claim.

name: Snd_RequestResume
summary: Counterpart of Snd_RequestSuspend: if the runtime predicate holds it sends the parameterless resume command (0x17) and on success sets the runtime object's +0x30 flag.
evidence: Confirmed together with 0x1193DC: same structure, flag value 1 instead of 0, command 0x17 instead of 0x16, and the caller 0x1142A0 uses the two as the two branches of one switch. NEW: the flag pair (+0x30 = 0/1) is written through 0x11F584 in both.

name: maybe_Engine_InitIpcWorker
summary: Brings up an IPC worker block: clears the state words, creates or reuses the handle at f_2C, initialises its event, queries the IPC state flags, sends the unit/status request, installs the 0x1000-byte transfer buffer (0x0011E6F8) and the completion callback, then creates the worker thread 0x0011F3C0 with this block as argument and releases the monitor.
evidence: The body is a complete worker bring-up and its tail calls Os_CreateThreadWithStack(&self->f_6C,...,0x0011F3C0,&self), which fixes the init/loop pair. The inherited 'Snd_' prefix had no support in the body, and the Gfx attribution also came from neighbours the asm does not confirm (Gfx_WriteHwRegsMasked is only called from 0x00113894), so the subsystem stays unnamed.

name: maybe_Os_DestroyThreadLocal
summary: At thread exit, fetches the thread-local object (0x0011F20C) and destroys it with 0x0011F730 followed by 0x0011F698.
evidence: No callers (it is reached from a destructor/exit hook) and the two callees are still unnamed, so 'thread local' is supported only by the TLS accessor shape, not by a named neighbour; maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegsBlock
signature: u32 Gfx_WriteHwRegsBlock(u32* session, u32 addr, u32 value, int count)
summary: Sends a GPU register write block: 2 normal + 2 translated parameters, count encoded as ((count<<14)|2), through command 0x00010082.
evidence: asm 0x1196B0: header 0x00010082, TLS+0x84=arg2, +0x88=arg4, +0x8c=arg4<<14|2, +0x90=arg3, svc 0x32. Called by 0x1136D8 (Gfx_WriteHwRegs); identical structure to 0x1184F4 but with the count packing.

name: Snd_SendIpcSuspend
signature: unsigned int Snd_SendIpcSuspend(unsigned int* session, unsigned int value, unsigned char mode)
summary: IPC stub for driver command 0x16 (header word 0x00160042): stores the mode byte, the value and a zero word in the thread-local block, sends svc 0x32 and returns the reply.
evidence: The header word 0x00160042 encodes driver command 0x16 with one parameter, and the only named caller Snd_RequestSuspend (0x001193DC) passes mode 0 and compares the reply against the two 'already suspended/resumed' results; the second caller (maybe_Gfx_InitDrawState) uses the same stub during driver init.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcCmd19
summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x190000 (command 0x19) on the session word passed in; returns the reply word. Its caller uses it as the final notification before closing the session.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x00113830, inside maybe_Os_SignalAndClose (0x00113814), which signals an event and then closes the session - so this is the last message of that sequence. The session owner is still not identified, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Gfx_IpcCmdB0040Session
signature: unsigned int Gfx_IpcCmdB0040Session(unsigned int* session, unsigned char value)
summary: Sends GPU-service command 0x000B (header 0x000B0040, one translated parameter) on the session handle passed in and returns the reply word. Its only caller is Gfx_EnsureGpuSession, which passes the gsp::Gpu handle it just opened.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is inside Gfx_EnsureGpuSession (0x0051BCE0, 0.55) - asm 0x0051BD00 and 0x0051BD3C both target 0x00119764 - and that function opens 'gsp::Gpu' into 0x007AF188 and passes 0x007AF18C (the handle copy) as the session. So the old 'Snd_' prefix was wrong. The header 0x000B0040 is unchanged; the 'Session' suffix distinguishes it from the fixed-session Gfx_IpcCmdB0040 (0x0011A42C).

name: Gfx_WriteHwRegsMasked
signature: u32 Gfx_WriteHwRegsMasked(u32* session, u32 addr, u32 value, u32 mask, int count)
summary: Sends a masked GPU register write: 2 normal + 2 translated parameters plus the count packing, through command 0x00020084 (GSPGPU WriteHWRegsWithMask).
evidence: asm 0x11979C: header 0x00020084, TLS+0x84=arg2, +0x88=count, +0x8c=count<<14|2, +0x90=arg3, +0x94=count<<14|0x402, +0x98=arg4, svc 0x32. Called by 0x11386C.

name: Gfx_WaitGpuEvent
signature: int Gfx_WaitGpuEvent(u32* arg1, u32* b, u8* c, int d, u32* e, int* f, int mode)
summary: Waits for a GPU service reply: selects the event object (0x11F758 or 0x11F804), takes the scheduler lock, polls 0x11F9CC (command 0x000D) with timeout handling, unlocks and returns the reply, optionally signalling the event via svc 0x23.
evidence: Readable: iVar1 = mode ? 0x11F804() : 0x11F758(); 0x11F73C(iVar1); lock 0x119BA8/0x1198CC; func_0011F9CC(a,event,b,c,d,e,f); unlock 0x119E1C; if (local_34) svc 0x23. Caller 0x11A50C; the 0x11F9CC header is 0x000D0080, i.e. the GPU service's 'wait for event' command.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call(u32 mode, u32* buf, int size, int arg4, int b, u32* out)
summary: Takes the scheduler lock and issues GPU command 0x004B (3 normal + 2 translated parameters, built by 0x11F810) with the caller's buffer; asserts on failure and releases the lock.
evidence: Readable: local zeros; lock 0x119BA8; if (!arg2 || !arg3) arg2=&local; result = func_0011F810(arg1,arg2) - 0x11F810 header is 0x004B00C2 (cmd 0x4B, 3 normal/2 translate); if (result<0) 0x118924(result, site); ... unlock 0x119E1C. Sole caller 0x114344.

name: maybe_Snd_SetMasterEnable
summary: Switches the driver's global output on/off: enable (arg 0) requires the ready predicate 0x0011E9B4 and arms the stream through 0x00118814; disable (arg non-zero) requires the current flag and stops it through 0x0011ECC0; the flag byte at 0x007AE910+4 is then updated.
evidence: The body arms the stream through 0x00118814 (enable) or stops it through 0x0011ECC0 (disable) and updates the flag byte at 0x007AE910+4, which fits a master on/off switch, but the owner is still inferred from that flag rather than from a named service; the xref caller Sound_Driver_BuildTwoEvents does not reference this entry in its body.

name: Os_GetTimeSnapshot
summary: Copies the eight words produced by Os_QueryTime (0x0011F5C0) into the caller's 8-word buffer - a thin public wrapper around the OS time query.
evidence: NEW: the producer is now the named Os_QueryTime (0x0011F5C0, 'queries the current system time into eight words and normalises the packed date flags'), and the body is a pure 8-word copy of its output, so the old 'Gfx_GetEventData' name was wrong on both counts (no graphics, no event). The wrapper adds nothing but the copy.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSharedBlock
summary: Waits on the handle stored in *state with svcWaitSynchronization1 (svc 0x24), asserts on a negative result, then re-opens the SDK session with Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen.
evidence: No callers; the two parts (svc 0x24 wait plus the named Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen) confirm the sync/session shape, but what is being waited on is still unknown, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Gfx_IpcCmdF0100Query
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdF0100Query(u32 arg1, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d)
summary: Issues GPU command 0x000F (4 normal parameters) and returns the byte result written by the service; asserts on failure.
evidence: Readable: lock 0x119BA8; iVar1 = func_0011F8E4(a,b,c,d,local_1c) - 0x11F8E4 header 0x000F0100; if (iVar1<0) 0x118924; unlock; return local_1c[0]. Sole caller 0x113A50.

name: Svc_WaitForStatusUntilDeadline
signature: u32 Svc_WaitForStatusUntilDeadline(u32 handle, u32 deadline_lo, u32 deadline_hi, u32 flags)
summary: Polls the status command 0x90040 under the scheduler lock and returns 1 as soon as its reply byte is set, or 0 once the 64-bit deadline (with a 3x margin) has passed; sleeps through 0x11CC94 between attempts.
evidence: The body only tests the reply byte of Gfx_IpcCmd90040 against a deadline; it never waits for a tick value itself, so 'WaitUntilTick' named the deadline rather than the operation.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitIpcCommand430040
summary: Flushes the pending GPU callbacks (two inner entries of Os_InvokeCallbacks at 0x00118814), submits IPC command 0x430040 through Gfx_IpcCmd430040 and aborts through 0x00118924 on failure.
evidence: NEW: the ARM bytes at 0x00119DF8 are push {r4,lr}; bl 0x00119BA8; bl 0x001198CC; bl 0x0011A3B0; error check; pop {r4,lr}, and the function returns at 0x00119E14. The svcCloseHandle/svcWaitSynchronization half Ghidra printed in the same body belongs to a separate function at 0x00119E1C (hidden mid-symbol boundary), so 'SignalEvent' described that neighbour instead of this wrapper. Body is a merged/damaged decompilation, hence 0.35.

name: Os_UnlockScheduler
summary: Releases the scheduler/GPU lock taken by 0x1143C8/0x119BA8: restores the saved event word, signals the owner with svc 0x23 if needed, and drops the thread priority with svc 0x14.
evidence: Readable: iVar2=*g_00119E7C; if (iVar2) { svc 0x23; *g_00119E7C=*g_00119E84; iVar1=iVar2; } if (iVar1<0) assert; if (*g_00119E88) { svc 0x14; if (*g_00119E88<0) 0x118100(); }. 33 callers - it closes the lock around every GPU/IPC call.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitGpuEventLoop
summary: Polls the transfer command in a loop: each pass calls Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer with the context at 0x00119F7C, invokes the registered callback (table 0x00119F84, slot +0x48) when the returned event differs from the expected one, and ends on error or when the third stage reports the requested event.
evidence: The callee Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer is confident, which fixes the GPU-event framing, but the body is damaged decompilation (unaff_r9, in_ZR) so the exit condition and the parameter meaning cannot be trusted; kept at 0.3.

name: Gfx_Cmd400042Call
summary: Takes the scheduler lock and issues GPU command 0x0040 (2 translated parameters) through 0x11FA58, then releases the lock and returns the result.
evidence: Readable: lock 0x119BA8; result = func_0011FA58(arg1,arg2); unlock 0x119E1C; return. 0x11FA58's header is 0x00400042 (cmd 0x40, 2 translate). No callers.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd3F0040Call
summary: Takes the scheduler lock, calls 0x11FAA4 (GPU command 0x003F), asserts on failure and releases the lock.
evidence: Readable: lock 0x119BA8; if (func_0011FAA4()<0) 0x118924(...); unlock 0x119E1C. 0x11FAA4 header is 0x003F0040. Sole caller 0x113A50.

name: Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer(u32 id, u32 flags, u32 size, u32 offset, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 deadline_lo, u32 deadline_hi)
summary: Reads a GPU buffer through IPC command 0x000C0104 under the scheduler lock: rejects offsets above 0x1000, zeroes the request when either size or offset is empty, releases the session handles when the flag 0x10000 is set and retries on the busy status 0xC8A0CC02 until the deadline.
evidence: The single IPC call is now the named Gfx_IpcCmdC0104, and the surrounding lock/unlock, busy-status retry and deadline arithmetic match the sibling transfer wrapper; the only caller is a graphics path.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd420080
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x0042 with two normal parameters; returns the result or the echoed first word.
evidence: asm 0x11A334: header 0x00420080, TLS+0x84=a, +0x88=b, svc 0x32. No callers.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd90040
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x0009 with one translated parameter; returns the service result and copies the 0x88 output byte to *out.
evidence: asm 0x11A36C: header 0x00090040, TLS+0x84=a, svc 0x32, *arg2=TLS+0x88. Callers 0x10CDE0, 0x10DA64, 0x119C30, 0x51BEFC - the 0x119C30 use (event polling) shows it is a query command.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd430040
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x0043 with one translated parameter; returns the result.
evidence: asm 0x11A3B0: header 0x00430040, TLS+0x84=a, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x119DF8 (event signalling).

name: Gfx_IpcCmd3E0080
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x003E with two normal parameters; returns the result or the echoed word. Used by the scheduler lock helper 0x1143C8.
evidence: asm 0x11A3E8: header 0x003E0080, TLS+0x84=a, +0x88=b, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x1143C8 (Os_LockScheduler).

name: Gfx_IpcCmdB0040
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000B with one translated parameter; returns the result and copies the 0x88 output byte.
evidence: asm 0x11A42C: header 0x000B0040, TLS+0x84=a, svc 0x32, *arg2=TLS+0x88. No callers.

name: Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer(u8* arg1, u8* b, u8* c, int size, u8* data, int* out)
summary: Submits a GPU buffer write through IPC command 0x000E0080 under the scheduler lock, replacing null arguments with stack temporaries and returning the service status.
evidence: Named Gfx_IpcCmdE0080 plus the lock/unlock pair and the same null-defaulting pattern as the read/transfer wrappers; the only caller is a graphics path.

name: Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer(u32* arg1, u32* b, u8* c, int size, u32* d, int* out, u32 e, u32 f)
summary: Submits a GPU buffer transfer through IPC command 0x000D0080 under the scheduler lock, substituting stack temporaries for null arguments and retrying on the busy status with the 3x timeout; when the caller already holds the current event it forwards to Gfx_WaitGpuEvent instead.
evidence: Named Gfx_IpcCmdD0080, Gfx_WaitGpuEvent and Os_UnlockScheduler cover every step, and the null-argument defaulting pattern is the same as the read wrapper 0x0011A140.

name: maybe_Hid_UpdateCalibration
summary: When the calibration slot at 0x007AF0DC is active, reads the current calibration id with IPC command 0x13 and, if the reply is 0xC9405001, acknowledges it with command 0x3D.
evidence: NEW: the two command wrappers are now named by their headers (Os_IpcSendCommand13 reads a byte, Os_IpcSendCommand3D sends one), so the read-compare-acknowledge shape is confirmed; that the ids are HID calibration data is still an inference from the HID-side reading, and the caller Gfx_IpcCmd4F0080 does not fit that story, so maybe_ stays.

name: Hid_CalibrateCirclePad
signature: int Hid_CalibrateCirclePad(u16* out, u16* raw, int arg3, int b, int deadzone, int scale)
summary: Converts raw circle-pad samples to calibrated signed axis values: applies the per-axis min/max calibration (from the calibration blob at 0x11A8xx), clamps to the dead-zone and writes the two results to *out.
evidence: Readable: 0x11A810 (936 bytes) is called from Hid_DispatchPadReport (0x112518) for report type 1; it uses the calibration constants read by 0x11FB90 and writes two shorts through the out pointers, with separate min/max scaling per axis. 0x11A914 is the type-2 twin.

name: Hid_ReadCalibratedPad
signature: u32 Hid_ReadCalibratedPad(u32 reader, u32* outState, int count, u8* arg4, u8* b, u8* c)
summary: Reads one pad sample from the HID reader and applies the stored calibration: it acquires the pad state, scales the raw analogue values through the calibration block and writes the normalised result to outState.
evidence: Its named caller Hid_ReadPadState passes the reader's +4 block, the output state and the three scratch bytes, matching the calibrated-read signature; the readable body is partly damaged (coprocessor_store from the calibration load and two halt_baddata blocks), so only the shape is certain.

name: maybe_Hid_ThumbReader
summary: Mis-seeded Thumb entry inside the HID reader: the real prologue is before this address, so the decoded body (Ghidra's literal 'return 0x4C') is not the function. The surrounding code reads HID shared memory and 0x11AD3C is the pad reader.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and the body is a single `return 0x4C`, which cannot be a real function - the index claims 0x13E Thumb bytes that overlap the preceding routine. The name at least says 'Thumb seed, not a function', which is the useful information.

name: Mem_PoolInit
summary: Initialises a pool descriptor once: initialises its four sub-buffer entries, sets the initialised flag, clears the count and installs the sentinel begin/end pointers.
evidence: Sole caller 0x114C58 is now the teardown of the same layout; the body is the one-shot init with the f_59 flag and four Mem_Pool_DestroyAllEntries calls.

name: Container_ListAppend
summary: Appends a node to an intrusive list: splices it after the current tail (0x11AE18) and patches the list head/tail (0x11FE24).
evidence: Confirmed: its only caller 0x114C58 is the slot-release routine that 0x10F050 (small-set remove) uses, i.e. freed slots are put back on a free list with this append - which matches the pointer patching the body performs. The name describes exactly what the code does.

name: Snd_Channel_Release
summary: Releases one channel object: unlinks and frees its parameter list, recomputes the volume/pan of each remaining sub-voice, and returns all recycled list nodes to the pool.
evidence: Walks self->f_28 (removing entries of type 2 via 0x11fcf8) and the list at +4 (calling maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan@0x11b048 on each 0x108-byte owner), then recycles from a 0xc-byte, 0x80-entry bucket table at g_0011b030 after applying UnsignedSaturate(prio,7); only caller 0x10e174 (release all channels).

name: Snd_ChannelList_ReinsertByPriority
summary: Moves a channel between the mixer's priority buckets: unlinks it from the channel list and re-links it under the bucket index derived from its volume+pan priority byte, saturated to the eight priority levels.
evidence: Disassembly 0x11af14: removes the node from the list at +0xc with 0x11ad60, computes prio = usat((u8)node->0x9d + node->0x50, 7) and index = prio*3 into the 0xc-byte, 0x80-entry bucket table at g_0011b030, then inserts with 0x11fcf8(list, node). Companion of maybe_Snd_InsertChannelByPriority@0x11fd1c (N_032) and of the bucket walk inside 0x11ae88; no direct callers (reached through the channel vtable).

name: maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan(SndChannel* channel, unsigned int left, unsigned int distance, int distance2)
summary: Reconstructed 3D sound attenuation: computes the listener-to-source distance from the channel's position fields, compares the squared distance against the roll-off range and derives the left/right volume pair written through the two out pointers; also advances the channel's sub-voice state.
evidence: Snd_Channel_Release calls it for every 0x108-byte sub-voice to recompute volume/pan, which fixes the role; but the recovered body is badly damaged (coprocessor_store, unaff_r6/r9/r10/r11, in_s16) and the exact prototype/pan split is still a reconstruction, so it keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Hid_NormalizeCirclePad
signature: int maybe_Hid_NormalizeCirclePad(int axisX, int max, int axisY, int value)
summary: Circle-pad vector normalisation: subtracts the deadzone from one axis, builds the squared magnitude with the other axis, takes the integer square root (0x11CD80) and scales both components by 0x80, writing the two s16 results through caller registers and returning the radius.
evidence: NEW: the body normalises both axes - it writes two s16 outputs and returns the radius - so 'NormalizeAxis' understated it. The arithmetic is readable but the second axis arrives in unaff_r6 and the outputs go through unaff_r9/unaff_r10, so per FACTS.md the confidence stays at 0.3.

name: maybe_Mem_PoolInitFragment
summary: Mis-seeded Thumb entry decoded inside the pool-initialiser routine: the body is character-for-character the Mem_PoolInit prologue (four sub-buffer inits, the f_59 flag, the sentinel pointers), so it is a duplicate fragment rather than a function of its own.
evidence: The decoded body matches Mem_PoolInit 0x0011ADAC including the LAB_0011ae14 sentinel, and the entry address itself is suspect; the body is also damaged (coprocessor_store of cr7), so the name stays maybe_ at 0.3.

name: maybe_Hid_SetVibration
summary: Programs a vibration pattern: keeps the larger of the two float arguments at +0xB8 and the other at +0xBC, stores the pattern at +0xC0 and zeroes the phase counter at +0xC4; 0x11CBD4 snaps both floats to the hardware range.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, and the two float arguments still arrive in VFP registers (in_s0/in_s1), so the parameter list is inferred rather than read. 'Vibration' comes from the +0xB8..+0xC4 layout only, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Snd_QueueCommandBuffer
signature: void Snd_QueueCommandBuffer(CommandBuffer* self, u32 size, u32 flags, int* out)
summary: Reserves `size` words in a command ring, links the new command node into the submit queue, bumps the sequence number and advances the write pointer (wrapping at the ring end).
evidence: Named neighbours (Os_QueueTryPop/Os_QueuePopBlocking, Sound_Stream_SubmitDmaCommand, Sound_Voice_SendBufferCommand) and 22 callers in the 0x0054xxxx stream/archive code confirm a ring-buffer command submit; the 'Snd_' prefix should be read as 'sound/stream command ring'.

name: maybe_Os_EnsureInitialized
summary: Placeholder: Ghidra marks this address `missing_function` and no readable body exists, so nothing about the function is known beyond the first pass's guess. The name is kept only so the address stays covered.
evidence: NEW: decomp/ghidra/functions.jsonl records status `missing_function` for 0x0011B7EC and there is no file under decomp/readable/functions/ or decomp/readable/recovered/, so there is no body to re-read. The exact-target branch scan also finds no caller. Nothing can be confirmed or corrected.

name: Snd_QueueObjectCommand
summary: Queues a type-9 sound command carrying the value from the target object's vtable slot +0x20 plus a caller-supplied subtype byte, links it into the engine's command chain and returns the sequence number.
evidence: NEW: its three callers are the confident Sound_ArchiveStream_StartStream, Sound_Voice_AllocateAndStart and Sound_Voice_ReleaseEntryStream, all in the sound stream player, and it allocates its node through the named maybe_Snd_QueueCommandBuffer(engine, 6) - so the 'queue a sound command' role is settled.

name: Gfx_LoadDefaultState
summary: Writes the renderer's complete default GPU state: a long list of (register, value) pairs for the PICA200 pipeline (texture units, combiners, depth, fog, lighting, stencil), plus 0x100-byte and 0xE00-byte coefficient tables allocated from the frame heap and 0xBD per-channel lookup entries.
evidence: Readable: ~90 'if (cursor < end) { *cursor++=value; *cursor++=g_reg }' pairs using GPU register ids g_0011C44C..g_0011C50C; calls func_00120010(0x101,7,0), func_00120010(0x1c8,8,0) 32x, func_001200D8(0x2cc,0x200,buf), func_001200D8(0x29c,0xe00,buf); allocates 0x4000 and copies 0xBD entries from +0x1300/+0x16B1. The register-id/command-buffer pattern is the same as Gfx_ExecuteCommandList (0x116104).

name: Gfx_UpdateTextureBindings
summary: Rebuilds the 16-slot texture binding table from the render state: for each slot it either points at the default texture record, marks the slot dirty, or resolves the current texture through 0x123458 and records its address/size, handling the 0x1400/0x1401/0x1406/0x140B format classes.
evidence: Readable: for i<0x10 { iVar5 = ctx + 0x458 + i*0x18; if (!iVar5->f_15) { slots[i+0x13]=ctx+0x298+i*0x10; slots[i+0x23]=0; } else if (iVar5->f_10==0) dirty(i); else { handle = *(int*)(*g_0011C80C + i*4 + 0x810); ... uVar3 = func_00123458(*piVar10 + *piVar4); slots[i+1]=uVar3; slots[i+0x13]=...; } } - the 0x810 array is the texture handle table; caller 0x6BA4AC is engine render code.

name: maybe_Mem_FreeThroughCallback
summary: Releases one heap block through the registered deallocator: if the global slot at 0x7AE9FC is non-null it clears the slot and calls it with (0,0,0,0,0,block), then tail-calls 0x11CC28. The container destructor 0x11EE0C calls it on its two heap members, which is what identifies it as a free.
evidence: NEW: the real entry is 0x11C814 - Ghidra's 0x11C818 is four bytes late, the `ldr r2,=0x007AE9FC` prologue is at 0x11C814 - and 0x11EE0C's disassembly shows `ldr r1,[r0,#0xc] ... blne 0x11c814` then `ldr r0,[r4,#0x10] ... blne 0x11c814`, i.e. it is called with the two heap pointers. Nothing in the body is a thread exit, so the old name is replaced.

name: Gfx_CmdCopyTexture
summary: Dispatch stub for command-list type 0: forwards the recorded parameters to 0x11F12C, which builds the texture-copy GPU command.
evidence: Body: 'bl 0x11F12C; bx lr'. Called from Gfx_ExecuteCommandList (0x116104) case 0. 0x11F12C writes the 0x1C-byte command record for a texture copy; the type number comes from Gfx_PushPipelineCommand (record type 1) / the list builder.

name: Gfx_CmdBlitTexture
summary: Dispatch stub for command-list type 3: forwards to 0x11F518, which builds the textured-blit GPU command.
evidence: Body: 'bl 0x11F518; bx lr'. Called from 0x116104 case 3; 0x11F518 packs two 16-bit coordinate pairs and a texture handle into the command record.

name: Gfx_CmdUploadTexture
summary: Dispatch stub for command-list type 1: forwards to 0x11F21C, which builds the texture upload/fill GPU command.
evidence: Body: 'bl 0x11F21C; bx lr'. Called from 0x116104 case 1; 0x11F21C writes a command with two coordinate pairs and a handle.

name: Gfx_CmdSetTextureRegion
summary: Dispatch stub for command-list type 4: forwards to 0x11F35C, which builds the texture-region/format GPU command.
evidence: Body: 'bl 0x11F35C; bx lr'. Called from 0x116104 case 4; 0x11F35C writes the 0x1C-byte record with four 16-bit fields.

name: Os_QueueTryPop
signature: unsigned int Os_QueueTryPop(OsQueue* queue, unsigned int* out)
summary: Non-blocking pop: if the ring holds an entry it copies the value out, advances the read index (wrapping), decrements the count and signals the producer; returns 1 on success and 0 when empty.
evidence: `lock(queue+5); if (queue[10] > 0) { *arg2 = *(u32*)(*queue + queue[9]*4); func_0011CFAC(queue[9]+1, queue[8]); queue[9] = r1; queue[10]--; if (queue[0xc] > 0) func_00117DC4(queue+3, 1); unlock; return 1; } unlock; return 0;` - textbook ring pop; used by 0x11B57C for command allocation.

name: Os_QueueTryPush
signature: unsigned int Os_QueueTryPush(OsQueue* queue, unsigned int value)
summary: Non-blocking push: stores the value at the write index when the ring is not full, advances the index (wrapping), bumps the count and signals the consumer; returns 1/0.
evidence: `lock(queue+5); if (queue[10] < queue[8]) { func_0011CFAC(queue[10]+queue[9]); *(u32*)(*queue + r1*4) = arg2; queue[10]++; if (queue[0xb] > 0) func_00117DC4(queue+1, 1); unlock; return 1; } unlock; return 0;` - the exact counterpart of 0x11C8E0.

name: Os_QueuePopBlocking
summary: Blocking pop: waits on the queue's semaphore until an entry is available, then pops it exactly like 0x11C8E0 and returns the value.
evidence: `exclusive++(queue+0xb); while (1) { lock(queue+5); if (queue[10] > 0) break; unlock; func_00117D10(queue+1); } result = *(*queue + queue[9]*4); func_0011CFAC(...); queue[10]--; ... exclusive--(queue+0xb); return result;`. Caller 0x00548150; used by the worker loops that consume request rings.

name: Mem_PoolAllocNode
summary: Pops one node off the object pool's free list (pool+0x24), increments the live count (pool+0x2C) under the pool monitor (pool+0x30) and, when the pool flag bit 0 is set, relocates the node into the pool window via 0x00118B28; returns NULL when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: All the named callers are the Svc object constructors (0x00505058, 0x005055C8, 0x005056E0, 0x00505804 and Gfx_GetCommandSlot), and the body is the exact inverse of the named release path (push onto +0x24, decrement +0x2C, same +0x30 monitor). The node payload type is unknown, but the pool-allocator role is established.

name: Game_GetDataManager
summary: One-shot lazy creation of the process-wide game-data context that owns the master tables (monsters, items, text, maps); every 0x63xxxx table lookup takes it as its first argument.
evidence: The 998 call sites resolve to named functions across every subsystem (Actor2D_CreateFromParamB, BattleScene_BuildUnitModel, Anim_ModelLoad_ByName, ...) and all immediately pass the returned pointer to the 0x63xxxx record lookups, so the 'global data manager' role is now supported by named callers, not just by the allocation shape.

name: Os_ThreadEntry
summary: Entry point of every created thread: sets up the thread-local storage, calls the two function pointers the thread was started with (start->callback(start->arg) then start->main(arg)), runs the thread-local destructors, and finishes with svcExitThread (svc 9).
evidence: Ends with `bl 0x1181b8` (Os_RunTlsDestructors), `ldr r0,[r4,#0x10]; cmp r0,#0; blne 0x11699c`, `pop {r4,lr}`, `svc #9`, `bx lr`. The two indirect calls read `[r4+4]`/`[r4+0xc]` and `[r4]`/`[r4+0xc]`, i.e. fn(arg) pairs. 0x0011CB38 in the same block is the 'current context' getter used by 994 call sites.

name: std_memmove_backward
signature: void std_memmove_backward(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)
summary: newlib memmove's backward copy path: moves size bytes from src_end-size to dst_end-size, copying 16-byte blocks then 8/4/2/1-byte tails, for overlapping ranges where dst > src.
evidence: asm 0x11CD34: loop copying four words from [r1,#-16].. to [r0,#-16].. while size >= 0x10; then 'uVar3*0x20000000' tests bit 3 for an 8-byte block, bit 2 for 4, bit 1 for 2, bit 0 for 1 - the standard ARM memmove backward tail. No callers because it is the alternate entry of the memmove at 0x11CD2C (callers jump to this address directly).

name: maybe_Gfx_CallNoOpStub
summary: Thunk that calls 0x115E68 with argument 0. 0x115E68 is an empty 8-byte function (`mov r0,r0; bx lr`), so this is a call to a no-op/default implementation - the old 'FinalizeSubsystem' reading is not supported by the body.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of the callee 0x115E68 is `mov r0,r0; bx lr` (the ARM NOP idiom) followed by a different function at 0x115E70, so the call goes to an empty stub; the only argument is the literal 0. The dossier's 802 callers are an xref artefact (they branch to addresses inside the claimed range); the exact-target scan finds none.

name: Container_HashMap_Init
summary: Constructor of an open-addressing hash map: stores the vtable, seeds the three bucket heads with the 0xfffff000 empty sentinel and default-constructs the 31 initial 8-byte slots.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2; arg1[2] = arg1[4] = arg1[6] = 0xfffff000 (empty key sentinel); arg1[1] = arg1[3] = arg1[5] = 0; then func_00100050(arg1 + 7, g_0011deac, 8, 0x1f). No callers; sits between the queue helpers and Os_GetCurrentThreadHandle@0x11df0c.

name: maybe_Os_IpcCmd0863
summary: Sends the fixed command 0x0863 (header 0x08630000: no normal and no translated parameters) on the session in *handle, and on success copies the reply word at TLS+0x88 to *out and returns the status word at TLS+0x84.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x117078 (the request-block builder in this batch), so the pair is 'build a request block, send command 0x0863'. The header literal 0x08630000 and the svc 0x32 are both in the body, so the command number is certain; only the meaning of the command is unknown, hence 0.45.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentThreadHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a thread handle queried through command 0x0B on the driver session, closing the previous handle with svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) first and aborting through 0x0011ED40 when the query fails.
evidence: NEW: the query helper is the named maybe_Os_IpcCmd0BGetThreadValue (0x001228FC) and the body closes the old value with svc 0x23 before storing the new one; the companion 0x00122440 does the same for command 0x0A. The public nn::os API name is still a reconstruction.

name: maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline
signature: void maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline(float* now, u32* base, u32* out, u32 request)
summary: Converts the current system tick and a packed timeout field into a 64-bit deadline using the 1e6 scaling constants shared with the save worker.
evidence: It issues svc 0x28 (GetSystemTick) and does 64-bit multiplies by g_0011E0C4/CC/D0 with a shift by 0x12, and its only caller is the named Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC); the 'deadline' reading fits, but the units are inferred, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Os_ScanParamBlocks
summary: Fallback scan for a parameter entry: reads sixteen 0x40-byte blocks from offset 0x400 through Os_ReadChunkedTable, looks for a word whose low byte is 0xFE, unpacks the two 12-bit fields and the two payload words into out and returns 0; returns 0xC8810FEF when nothing matches.
evidence: Same unpacking code and windowed reader as 0x001179C0, and the return constant is the SDK error code; the record's owner is still unnamed and the only callers (maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker, maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry) are themselves guesses.

name: maybe_Os_IpcSession_PollAsyncState
summary: Polls the driver session at 0x007B2D08: reads the state bytes of the object at session+0xC, returns 0 or one of 0xF9610C02 / 0xC8A10C01 / 0xC8A10C0D / 0xC8810FEF depending on the state and pending counter, and re-issues command 0x19 when the counter is positive.
evidence: NEW: 0x007B2D08 is the driver-session struct whose handle is at +0x24 (0x007B2D2C, see Os_IpcSendCommand06), and 0x00123750 also clears its pending word. Both callers (Save_AsyncReadWorker 0x001170CC and maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker 0x00117458) are worker loops, so 'Save_CheckReadState' wrongly narrowed a shared IPC state machine; the state semantics remain unknown, hence maybe_.

name: Hid_ApplyDeadzone
summary: Turns raw circle-pad axis shorts into direction bits: scales both axes by 0x28/0x91, compares them with the dead-zone at 0x0011E548+0x20 and ORs the up/down/left/right masks (0x01000000..0x08000000) into the button word.
evidence: Readable: arg2 &= 0xf0ffffff; func_0011FBCC(&local_20,local_1e, axis[0],axis[1], 0x28,0x91) (0x28/0x91 are the 40/145 dead-zone range); iVar4=0x11CD80(local_1e[0]<<8, iVar5); then four comparisons against g_0011E548->f_20 and OR of 0x1000000/0x2000000/0x4000000/0x8000000. 0x11E98E is the Thumb twin of the same code.

name: maybe_Svc_Ir_CloseService
summary: Closes the shared ir:USER session opened by 0x00122200: sends the 0x00020000 close command, closes the shared-memory handle, releases the session handle, unmaps the shared memory and clears the open flag.
evidence: It is the exact inverse of 0x00122200 - same globals (open flag 0x7B2D08, session 0x7B2D2C, shared memory 0x7F2DE0) whose open call uses the verified 'ir:USER' literal; the old 'Gfx_FinalizeSession' name claimed a GPU session, which the string contradicts.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSemaphore
summary: Counted semaphore wait with owner hand-off: while the counter is negative it decrements and arbitrates through 0x11CC10, and when the count turns positive it flips the sign back and returns; the positive branch flips the sign and returns immediately.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller, so the primitive is only identified by its shape - the negative-count-is-waiters convention, the ldrex/strex exclusive-access loops and the 0x11CC10 arbitration call. That is the CTR semaphore pattern, but nothing names the object, so the confidence stays at 0.45.

name: Mem_MapPages
signature: int Mem_MapPages(MemPageBlock* block, unsigned int size, unsigned char flags)
summary: Allocates a page-aligned range for the block (Mem_AllocAddressRange) and maps it with svcMapMemoryBlock (svc 0x1F), recording the flags and marking +0x18 mapped.
evidence: The 0xFFF alignment check, the named Mem_AllocAddressRange and the svc 0x1F mapping step are all visible in the body, which is exactly the page-mapping idiom; no caller yet.

name: Os_ListRemoveNode
summary: Unlinks a node from an intrusive circular list under the list lock and clears the node's links and payload words.
evidence: `lock; if (*arg2 == arg2) *(u32*)(arg1+8) = 0; else { if (*(int**)(arg1+8) == arg2) *(int*)(arg1+8) = (*(int**)(arg1+8))[1]; *(int*)arg2[1] = *arg2; *(int*)(*arg2+4) = arg2[1]; } arg2[1] = *arg2 = arg2[2] = arg2[3] = 0; unlock(arg1+0xc);` - standard list unlink, used by 0x111E44.

name: Os_MapSharedMemory
signature: void Os_MapSharedMemory(OsSharedMem* mem, u32 addr, u32 size, u32 mode, u32 perm)
summary: Registers a shared-memory mapping on a descriptor: if the descriptor has no mapping yet and addr/size are 0x1000-aligned it asks the OS for the mapped address (0x0011126C), stores the handle at +0x14, the address at +8 and the size at +0xC, and raises the assert path 0x00118100 on failure. Ghidra dropped the mode/perm arguments, which the callers still pass.
evidence: Its callers are now all confidently named - Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers, Sound_Driver_Init and maybe_Snd_SetupChannelBuffer - and each passes (descriptor, base address, size, mode 0/1/3, type 3), which pins the parameter roles; the alignment tests on both values are literal. 'Maps a page-aligned buffer into the descriptor' is therefore proven, so 'maybe_' can go.

name: Os_CloseHandle
summary: Closes a kernel handle: cancels the pending operation when one is armed (non-waiting handles just drop their state), notifies the owner (0x1181A8) and finally closes the handle with `svc 0x23`.
evidence: `if (self->f_14) { if (*(int*)(self+8)) { if (self->f_18 == 0) { *(u32*)(self+8) = 0; self->f_c = 0; } else { svc 0x20; func_001181A8(self); } } if (self->f_14) { svc 0x23; self->f_14 = 0; } }` - 0x23 = svcCloseHandle; the lighter variant of 0x111E44 without the list unlink.

name: Os_CloseHandleSimple
summary: Closes a handle word and resets it to the 'empty' sentinel; returns the old handle or the 'nothing to do' code.
evidence: `iVar1 = *arg1; result = g_0011e938; if (iVar1 != 0) { svc 0x23; if (iVar1 < 0) abort; *arg1 = *g_0011e93c; result = iVar1; } return result;` - direct svcCloseHandle with the sentinel reload.

name: maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionAndSend
signature: unsigned int maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionAndSend(unsigned int* handleOut, unsigned int name, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4, int value, unsigned int flags, int third)
summary: Opens the service session stored at *handleOut on first use (name resolution 0x0011CCA0 + create 0x001192C0), then either packs three range checks into the handle word (flags bit 0x20000) or sends the request through the shared command path 0x0011EAB4 while holding the 0x007AEA10 semaphore. Returns the handle or an error code.
evidence: The callers are now maybe_Os_OpenSharedSessionA/B (0.4), which supports 'open a shared session' rather than the old Snd_ reading, but the body is badly damaged (unaff_r4/r6 and in_lr survive into the arithmetic), so the name stays maybe_ and below 0.4.

name: maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionTailFragment
signature: u32 maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionTailFragment(int pad, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Not a real function entry: a Thumb fragment that Ghidra seeded mid-routine inside 0x0011E940. It repeats the session-open tail (lock 0x001180B0, send via 0x0011EAB4, signal 0x007AEA10) and the 0x01000000/0x08000000/0x04000000 range masks, with unaff_/in_ registers for everything else.
evidence: The disassembly of the enclosing 0x0011E940 shows the same instruction sequence, so there is no controller code here; the fragment nature is the only certain fact, hence the fragment name and 0.3.

name: maybe_Svc_IpcCmd1100C2
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_IpcCmd1100C2(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Sends command 0x1100C2 on the global session object 0x007AEA00 after taking the 0x007AEA10 semaphore (waiting in 0x0011CC94) and releases it afterwards; returns 0xC8A0A7FC when the session is not connected.
evidence: The send itself is the named Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read and the callers are three different subsystems' flush/wait paths (maybe_Snd_FlushChannelsOnStop, maybe_Snd_FlushChannels, maybe_Snd_InitDspTimeouts), confirming a shared locked-command helper rather than a subsystem-specific call; the individual arguments are still not decoded.

name: Svc_IpcCmd70040
summary: Minimal IPC stub: header 0x00070040 (command 0x07, one normal parameter), session handle taken from *session, svc 0x32, reply word returned.
evidence: Confirmed as an IPC stub, not as anything semantic: the header literal 0x00070040 is in the code and the parameter count in the name matches (one normal parameter). NEW: the caller set is still empty, so which service owns the session is unknown - but that is exactly what the name claims, so it needs no maybe_.

name: Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read
signature: int Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read(int* session, u32 arg2, int b, u16 c, u16 d, u8* out)
summary: Sends command 0x11 with three normal and two translated parameters (header 0x001100C2) and copies the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out; returns the reply word at TLS+0x84.
evidence: Confirmed: the header 0x001100C2 and the descriptor b<<4|10 are both in the body, matching the name's command id and parameter counts. NEW: its three callers (0x11E940, 0x11E98E, 0x11E9C4) are the driver's query/submit helpers, all in the same 0x11E9xx block, so this is one command of one session.

name: Svc_IpcCmd20040
signature: int Svc_IpcCmd20040(int* session, u16 value, u8* out)
summary: Sends command 0x02 with one normal parameter (header 0x00020040) and copies the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: Confirmed as a command stub: header 0x00020040 and the reply copy are in the body and the name states exactly that. There are still no callers, so which service owns the session remains open - which the name does not claim.

name: Svc_IpcCmdD0082
signature: u32 Svc_IpcCmdD0082(u32* session, u32 firstWord, u32 bufferAddress, int size)
summary: IPC stub for command 0x0D with two normal and two translated parameters (header 0x000D0082): packs count<<14|0x402 as the translated-buffer descriptor, stores the address and count, sends svc 0x32 and returns the reply word.
evidence: Confirmed: the header 0x000D0082 and the descriptor count<<14|0x402 are both in the body, matching the name. NEW context adds nothing because there are still no callers; the summary now says exactly which of the four words is the descriptor.

name: maybe_Snd_IpcCmd20
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_IpcCmd20(unsigned int* session, unsigned char value)
summary: Sends command 0x0020 (header 0x00200040, one translated parameter) on the session handle passed in and returns the reply word. Both call sites are the channel-flush pair (0x00118788, 0x0011ECC0), which pass the handle stored at 0x007AEA00+8 - the same context the unit-flag setter uses.
evidence: NEW: the two branch targets are 0x00118804 (inside maybe_Snd_FlushChannels) and 0x0011ED30 (inside maybe_Snd_FlushChannelsOnStop), and both pass the handle at 0x007AEA00+8. That context is shared with the unit-flag setter, so the 'Snd_' owner is plausible but still not proven - the service that owns 0x007AEA00 is not identified anywhere.

name: maybe_Snd_SendIpcBuffer
signature: int maybe_Snd_SendIpcBuffer(unsigned int* session, unsigned int value, unsigned int zero, unsigned int address, unsigned short size, unsigned short* outSize)
summary: Submits a buffer descriptor: header 0x001000C0 (command 0x10, three normal parameters), then it temporarily overwrites the thread's two translated-descriptor words at +0x180 with size<<14|2 and the address, sends svc 0x32, restores both words and copies the reported size back.
evidence: NEW: the only exact caller is 0x1185E8 (the channel query in this batch), so the pair is 'query, then submit the buffer'. The header literal 0x001000C0 and the save/restore of TLS+0x180/+0x184 are both in the body; the service the session belongs to is still unknown, so the Snd prefix stays a guess.

name: Svc_IpcCmdC0040
signature: int Svc_IpcCmdC0040(int* session, u32 value, u32* out)
summary: Sends command 0x0C with one normal parameter (header 0x000C0040) and copies the reply word at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: Confirmed as a command stub by its header and reply copy. NEW: its only caller 0x118648 (a HID-side wrapper) ignores the returned result and only uses the reply word, which is consistent with a plain query.

name: Svc_IpcCmd10040
signature: int Svc_IpcCmd10040(int* session, u16 value, u16* out)
summary: Sends command 0x10 with one normal parameter (header 0x00100040) and copies the reply halfword at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: Confirmed as a command stub by its header and reply copy. NEW observation worth recording: the same command id 0x10 also appears in 0x11EBD8 but with three normal parameters, so the two must target different services (each takes its session from the caller's object).

name: maybe_Snd_FlushChannelsOnStop
summary: The 'stop' entry of the channel flush: clears the active byte at 0x7AEA00, and if a flush is pending submits the final unit configuration (0x11E9C4), runs the eight registered callbacks of the table at 0x7E7998, clears the pending byte and sends the session command 0x20.
evidence: NEW: the body is the same flush sequence as 0x118788 (same context 0x7AEA00, same 0x11E9C4 call, same eight-callback table at 0x7E7998, same closing command 0x20) with the active byte cleared first, so the 'stop-time variant' reading holds. The dossier's 41 callers are an xref artefact; the exact-target scan finds only 0x119AF4.

name: Svc_SendRequestBuffer128
summary: IPC request with a 0x80-byte inline payload: copies the caller's buffer into the thread command block after the 0x10800 header and issues svc 0x32, returning the reply word.
evidence: The body writes header 0x10800, memcpy's exactly 0x80 bytes, executes svc 0x32 and returns the first reply word; its only caller is the named maybe_Snd_WaitTransferDone (0x11896C), i.e. the sound transfer request path.

name: Mem_HeapAlloc
signature: void* Mem_HeapAlloc(MemHeap* heap, unsigned int size, unsigned int alignment, unsigned int low, unsigned int high, unsigned int flags)
summary: General heap allocation used by the whole game: forwards the request bounds to the allocator, carves a block with the requested size/alignment and counts the live allocation.
evidence: Calls func_00122E38/0x122E48/0x122E68 (store the three bounds) then `func_00122CF0(&heap->f_18, size, align)`; when the result is non-null it increments `heap->f_54`, the live-allocation counter. 0x122CF0 rounds the size to 4 bytes (`(size+3)&~3`), walks the free lists and splits a block through 0x123E6C, which fixes this as the allocator's public entry.

name: Container_ObjectDtor
summary: Base-class destructor of the refcounted object family: installs the base vtable, releases the two heap-owned members at +0x0C and +0x10 through the registered deallocator 0x11C814, then walks the singly linked node list at +0x10 clearing each node's two words, and returns self.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly confirms the whole sequence (`str vtable,[r4]`, `blne 0x11c814` twice, the `ldr r1,[r4,#0x10]!` list walk, `sub r0,r4,#0x10` return), and the callers are the script VM's table/value destructors plus a multiple-inheritance destructor that adjusts its pointer first - so this is a shared base destructor, not a one-off.

name: Snd_UpdateChannelState
summary: Commits one sound channel's pending updates: each dirty bit (matrix, gain, mode, loop points, ADPCM parameters, wave data) calls the matching Snd_SetChannel* writer, then recomputes the mix command size and clears the dirty mask.
evidence: The dirty-bit dispatch now calls the confidently named maybe_Snd_SetChannelMatrix / Param1 / Param2 / LoopPoints / AdpcmParams / Mode / WaveData helpers, and the caller Sound_Channel_ReleaseAll is named.

name: Gfx_SetTextureSource
signature: void Gfx_SetTextureSource(u32 handle, u32 src, u32 size, u32 format, int flags)
summary: Builds and queues a GPU texture-source command: fills a 0x1C-byte record with type 0, handle, source address/size, format word and flags, then pushes it through 0x123360.
evidence: Readable: if (flags==0 || handle in the GPU address window) { base = *(u32**)(g+4); local header = (*g & 0xff000000) | 0; local[1]=handle; [2]=src; [3]=size; [4]=format; [5]=flags; func_00123360(TLS+0x58, &record); }. Called by dispatch stub 0x11C86C for command-list type 0.

name: Gfx_SetTextureSourcePair
signature: void Gfx_SetTextureSourcePair(u32 handle, u32 src, u32 size, u16 x, u32 arg5, u32 b, u32 c, u16 y)
summary: Builds and queues a two-coordinate GPU texture command (record type 2) with the handle, source/size and the two 16-bit coordinates, then calls 0x123360.
evidence: Readable: header byte = 2; local_3c=handle, local_34=src, uStack_38=size; local_24 = x:y packed; local_28=a, uStack_30=b, uStack_2c=c; func_00123360(TLS+0x58,&record). Called by dispatch stub 0x11C8A0 (type 1).

name: maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill(u32 src, u32 size, int enable, u32 color)
summary: Queues PICA200 surface commands on the GPU message queue at 0x007B0070+0x58: optionally a type-5 record carrying the source/size, then a type-1 record with the fill colour.
evidence: NEW: it sits in the Gfx_SetTexture* family (0x0011F12C SetTextureSource, 0x0011F21C SetTextureSourcePair, 0x0011F35C SetTextureRegion, 0x0011F518 SetTextureBlit) that all push records to the same 0x007B0070 queue, so the family is confirmed; 'fill' still rests on the record types and the colour word, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_SetTextureRegion
signature: void Gfx_SetTextureRegion(u32 handle, u32 src, u32 size, u32 x0, int y0, u32 x1, int y1, u32 fmt)
summary: Queues a rectangular texture-region command (record type 4): packs the two 16-bit coordinate pairs and the format word into the 0x1C-byte record and calls 0x123360.
evidence: Readable: header byte 4; local_3c=handle, uStack_38=src, uStack_34=size; uStack_30 = x0 | y0<<16; uStack_2c = x1 | y1<<16; uStack_28=fmt; func_00123360. Called by dispatch stub 0x11C8C0 (type 4).

name: maybe_Engine_IpcWorker
summary: Worker thread body of the 0x34-byte IPC request ring initialised by 0x00119498: waits on the worker event, pops one record (with an exclusive-access index update), dispatches it through the callback table at worker+0x10 and, for record type 1, signals the waiting thread; exits when the stop byte at worker+0x77 is set.
evidence: 0x00119498 passes this exact address as the Os_CreateThreadWithStack entry (visible in that function's tail), so the two are the init/loop pair. The body itself only uses OS primitives and the callback table and has no sound-specific call, so neither 'Snd_' nor a graphics subsystem can be claimed.

name: Gfx_SetTextureBlit
signature: void Gfx_SetTextureBlit(u32 handle, u32 dst, int x, u32 src, u32 size, int y, u32 fmt)
summary: Queues a textured blit command (record type 3) with handle, destination, source/size and two 16-bit coordinates, then calls 0x123360.
evidence: Readable: header byte 3; local_3c=handle; uStack_38=dst; local_34 = x | y<<16; uStack_2c=fmt; uStack_30=size; local_28=src; func_00123360. Called by dispatch stub 0x11C880 (type 3).

name: Os_QueryTime
signature: void Os_QueryTime(OsTime* out, u32 arg2, int mode)
summary: Queries the current system time into eight words, then normalises the packed date flags: empty fields become -1 and the flag bits are split out of the values.
evidence: The taker is the named Os_IpcQueryCommand18 and the caller is maybe_Gfx_GetEventData; the 0x70/7 bit fields are the SDK packed-time flags, so 'query time' is well supported though the struct meaning stays partial.

name: maybe_Snd_IpcCmd17
summary: Parameterless IPC request with the 0x0017xxxx command header (Ghidra printed the literal as an address into 0x00170000): writes the header into the thread command buffer, sends it with svc 0x32 and returns the response word.
evidence: The only caller is the resume path (Snd_RequestResume), the counterpart of the suspend path, so the 'resume message' reading holds; the exact header word had to be recovered from the disassembly and the service is still unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Os_IpcCmd08
signature: uint32_t maybe_Os_IpcCmd08(uint32_t* session, uint32_t word1, uint32_t word2, uint32_t word3)
summary: Generic IPC request helper: fills TLS+0x80 with header 0x00080082 (command 0x08, two normal + two translated words), stores the three payload words, issues svc 0x32 and returns the TLS+0x84 reply.
evidence: NEW: the only branch target is 0x001193D4, inside maybe_Os_StoreThreadLocalValue (0x001193AC), which passes the per-thread block from 0x0011F730 plus the global at 0x007418D0 - so the 'OS layer' owner holds, but what the three words mean is not visible. The name keeps maybe_.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd1A0000
summary: IPC stub for command 0x001A with no parameters; returns the result or the TLS output word.
evidence: asm 0x11F698: header 0x001A0000, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x119688 (Os_DestroyThreadLocal), so it is the GPU session's close/unregister request.

name: maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus
signature: int maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus(unsigned int* session, unsigned int handle, unsigned int flags, unsigned int* out0, unsigned int* out1)
summary: Status query with header 0x00130042 (command 0x13, one normal and two translated words): stores the handle and flags, sends svc 0x32, and on success writes TLS+0x88 to *out1 and TLS+0x90 to *out0 - note the outputs are swapped relative to the parameter order.
evidence: NEW: the exact-target callers are the Gfx_* command/register writers (0x1136D8, 0x113714, 0x11386C, 0x1198DC, 0x11A50C, 0x11F12C, 0x11F21C), which contradicts the Snd prefix - the same command is used by the graphics command stream. The header literal and the swapped outputs are certain, the service is not, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Svc_CloseSessionHandles
summary: Closes the GPU session's three handles and its event: sets the 'closing' flag, calls svc 0x18, takes the event lock (svc 0x24), marks the event, signals it via 0x118170, then closes the event and the three handles with svc 0x23.
evidence: Readable: *g_0011F7F8=1; svc 0x18; if (*piVar1<0) assert; svc 0x24; if (*g_0011F800<0) assert; *(u8*)(piVar4+1)=1; func_00118170(piVar2); if (*piVar4) { svc 0x23; *g_0011F800=0; } for i<3 { if (piVar1[i]) { svc 0x23; piVar1[i]=0; } }. Sole caller 0x11A140 (GPU buffer read on error).

name: Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2(u32 handle, u32 buf, int size, u32 arg4, int b, u32* out)
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x004B (3 normal + 2 translated parameters): sends handle/buf/size/a and the size-packed descriptor, returning the result and the 0x88 output word.
evidence: asm 0x11F810: header 0x004B00C2, TLS+0x84=handle, +0x88=size, +0x8c=a, +0x90=size<<14|0x402, +0x94=buf; additionally swaps TLS+0x180/+0x184 to size<<14|2 and a for the duration of the call, then svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x119A10.

name: Gfx_IpcCmdC0104
signature: u32 Gfx_IpcCmdC0104(u32 handle, u32 buf, u32 size, u32 offset, int count, u32 arg6)
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000C (4 normal + 1 translated parameter) used for chunked buffer reads: sends handle/buf/size/offset plus the count descriptor and returns the result.
evidence: asm 0x11F88C: header 0x000C0104, TLS+0x84=handle, +0x88=buf, +0x8c=size, +0x90=count, +0x94=0, +0x98=a6, +0x9c=count<<14|2, +0xa0=offset, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x11A140 (Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer), which reads in 0x1000-byte chunks.

name: Gfx_IpcCmdF0100
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdF0100(u8 arg1, u32 b, u8 c, u32 d, u8* out)
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000F (4 normal parameters): sends a/b/c/d, and on success writes the 0x88 output byte to *out.
evidence: asm 0x11F8E4: header 0x000F0100, TLS+0x84=a, +0x88=b, +0x8c=c, +0x90=d, svc 0x32, success -> *arg5=TLS+0x88. Sole caller 0x119BDC.

name: Gfx_IpcCmdE0080
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdE0080(u32* out1, u32 handle, u32* out2, u32 src, int arg5, u32* out3, u32* out4)
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000E (2 normal + 2 translated parameters): submits a source/size descriptor and returns four output words (handle, offset, flags, size) to the caller.
evidence: asm 0x11F940: header 0x000E0080, TLS+0x84=handle, +0x88=a5, +0x180 swapped to a5<<14|2 with +0x184=src, svc 0x32; on success *arg1=TLS+0x88, *arg3=TLS+0x8c, *arg6=TLS+0x90, *arg7=TLS+0x98. Sole caller 0x11A470 (Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer).

name: Gfx_IpcCmdD0080
signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdD0080(u32* out1, u32 handle, u32* out2, u32 src, int arg5, u32* out3, u32* out4)
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000D (2 normal + 2 translated parameters): used as the event-wait/transfer request; returns four output words on success.
evidence: asm 0x11F9CC: header 0x000D0080, TLS+0x84=handle, +0x88=a5, TLS+0x180 swapped to a5<<14|2 with +0x184=src, svc 0x32; success fills *arg1/*arg3/*arg6/*arg7 from TLS+0x88/0x8c/0x90/0x98. Callers 0x1198DC, 0x11A50C, 0x11ABB8 - the three GPU event/read loops.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd400042
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x0040 (2 translated parameters): sends a and the descriptor b<<14|2 and returns the result or the echoed word.
evidence: asm 0x11FA58: header 0x00400042, TLS+0x84=b, +0x88=b<<14|2, +0x8c=a, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x11A0BC.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd3F0040
summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x003F with one translated parameter; returns the result or the echoed word.
evidence: asm 0x11FAA4: header 0x003F0040, TLS+0x84=arg1, svc 0x32. Sole caller 0x11A11C.

name: Svc_QueryStatus3C
summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x3C0000 (command 0x3C) on the fixed session at 0x7B0054; on success writes the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out and returns the status word.
evidence: Confirmed: the header 0x3C0000 is in the body and the name states exactly that. NEW: its only caller 0x114728 ORs this byte together with the one from 0x11FB54 (command 0x3B), so the two are the two halves of one status byte - which is why keeping the command id in the name is more useful than inventing a meaning.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand3D
summary: Sends driver command 0x3D with one normal parameter (header 0x003D0040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B0054 and returns the reply word; a negative Result is returned unchanged.
evidence: Confirmed because the name is a direct description of the code: header 0x003D0040 and the handle global 0x7B0054 are both present, and both callers (0x114728 status polling, 0x11A7D0 HID calibration) simply push a byte and ignore or check the result. NEW: the two sibling stubs 0x11FB54/0x11FADC use the same fixed handle, so the handle really is a module-level session.

name: Svc_QueryStatus3B
summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x3B0000 (command 0x3B, written as the literal 0x3AFFF4+0xC) on the fixed session at 0x7B0054; writes the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out.
evidence: Confirmed: the header value 0x3B0000 is computed from the neighbouring string literal plus 0xC, and the name states it. NEW: it is the second half of the pair ORed together by 0x114728 (the other is command 0x3C), which confirms the two are one status query.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand13
summary: Sends driver command 0x13 with one normal parameter (header 0x00130040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B0054 and returns the reply word.
evidence: Confirmed as the command sender it claims to be: the literal 0x00130040 and the same handle global as 0x11FB18 are in the body. NEW: 0x114728 (status polling) calls it with 0 after reading the 0x3B/0x3C status bytes and compares the reply with 0xC9405001, which is why it is the 'acknowledge' half of that pair.

name: Math_ClampVectorToRing
signature: int Math_ClampVectorToRing(u16* outX, u16* outY, int dx, int dy, int innerRadius, int outerRadius)
summary: Clamps a 2D offset into an annulus: computes length^2 = dx^2+dy^2, returns zero vectors when it is inside the inner radius, otherwise derives the integer square root with a bit-wise loop (0x11CD80 = unsigned division) and writes dx and dy scaled by (limit-inner)*128/sqrt to outX/outY, returning the remaining signed radial distance.
evidence: uses 0x11CD80 (__aeabi_uidiv) for the integer sqrt and the scaling divisions; fixed-point constants 0x4000 and 0x80; early-out when dx^2+dy^2 <= innerRadius^2; callers 0x112518 and 0x11E448.

name: Snd_InsertChannelByPriority
summary: Inserts a channel into the mixer's priority-ordered list: builds the channel's list node (func_0011FCBC), computes its priority as volume + pan clamped to 0..0x7F and splices it in before the first channel with a higher value (the comparison flips for tie-breaking depending on the mixer's blend flag), then links it (func_0011FCF8).
evidence: NEW: the clamp to 0..0x7F and the two tie-break variants are fully readable, and the stop/gain helper used by the same mixer is the confident Snd_FadeChannelToGain, so the priority-ordered insertion reading holds.

name: Snd_ListInsertByPriority
summary: Inserts an entry into the priority-ordered sound list at the first position whose clamped priority is lower (or equal in strict mode) than the new entry's, then links it with 0x11FCF8.
evidence: The caller is now the confidently named Sound_Voice_InsertByPriority (0.85), which does the same insertion for voices, so this is the list-level helper it uses.

name: Mem_Pool_DestroyAllEntries
summary: Destroys every entry of a small-block pool: walks the intrusive list anchored at pool+4, destroys each element body (node-0x110) with the element destructor 0x123558, unlinks the node with 0x11FCBC and finally releases it with 0x123588. Used when a pool is torn down.
evidence: callers maybe_Mem_PoolInit (0x11ADAC, N_002) and the sound stream reset pair 0x541F10/0x541F1C; loop until the sentinel at pool+4; element base offset -0x44 words.

name: Gfx_SetFrameColorParam
signature: void Gfx_SetFrameColorParam(void* self, const u8* arg2)
summary: Sets the frame's colour parameter: calls the device vtable +0x14 with (self->f_10, 2) and copies the two colour bytes into the current frame record at +0x126/+0x12A.
evidence: Four callers are now named, including maybe_Ui_ScreenEffect_ApplyFrameColor and Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateInput, and the caller builds the {3,0xFF,0xFF,...} fade record - which supports the colour reading.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows(u32 cmdWord, u32 count, const u32* src)
summary: Appends raw texture rows to the GPU command list in chunks of at most 0x80 words: writes the header ((n-1)<<20)|0xF0000|cmdWord, copies the pixels (64-byte blocks through 0x0011CD00 where possible) and advances the global write pointer 0x007AED34; on overflow it resets the pointer to the buffer end.
evidence: The callers include the confident Gfx_LoadDefaultState and Gfx_UpdateTextureBindings plus the GPU-state builders, which fits a texture upload, but the same list also contains Sound_System_Shutdown, Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels and Fs_Worker_Dtor, so either those names are wrong or the helper is more generic than 'texture rows'.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_ResetSlot
summary: Marks a slot free: calls the lock helper 0x12032C, resolves the slot with 0x120368 and stores -1 into the word 0x98 bytes before the returned pointer. 0x120368 itself is `mvn r1,#0; str r1,[r0,#0x1c]; bx lr`, so it takes a pointer and invalidates its +0x1C word.
evidence: NEW: disassembly of 0x120368 shows it takes a pointer in r0 (not an index) and stores -1 at +0x1C, so Ghidra's `func_00120368(index)` call is mis-typed and the -0x98 store is a back-reference into the slot header. No exact caller exists, so the command-list ownership is still inferred from the neighbouring 0x1200xx block.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles4
summary: Releases the four generation-tagged handle members at +4, +0xC, +0x14 and +0x1C of the object whose base is self-0x1C, then returns that base. A destructor body for a class with four handle members.
evidence: NEW: Pack_ReleaseHandle (0x12416C) is now named and returns its own argument, so the four calls are sibling members at fixed offsets, not a chain: self, self-8, self-16, self-24, base = self-0x1C. 'Chain4' described a linked list that does not exist.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles1
summary: Releases the single generation-tagged handle member at +4 of the object whose base is self-4 and returns that base. The one-handle variant of 0x00120408.
evidence: NEW: Pack_ReleaseHandle (0x12416C) returns its argument, so this is 'release the handle at self, return self-4' - one member of a class whose base is 4 bytes before it, not a chain. No caller names the class, so maybe_ stays.

name: Pack_LoadMasterTables
summary: Boot-time master-data loader. Resolves every core BXON table from the pack manager by literal name (item, player params for all party members, scenario params, level map/area, region, global flags, save points, sound arcs/groups/BGM/ME/SE, movie list, NG words, panel/panel_line, program_param) and stores the object/handle pairs in the data singleton; the player_param_* group goes through 0x124904 and the scenario_param_* group through 0x1249E0.
evidence: ~0x1CC0 bytes; 80+ s_*_bxon literals (s_item_bxon_0012076c, s_player_param_hero_bxon_00121ce4, s_scenario_param_hero_bxon_00121fe8, s_sound_se_bxon_00121560 ...); calls Pack_GetManager 0x124FA0, 0x124B24 (open by name), 0x124904/0x1249E0 per-table loaders; only caller 0x11CFE0 = startup init

name: maybe_Container_MultiList_Init
signature: void maybe_Container_MultiList_Init(Container * c, u32 u32, u32 u322, u32 u323)
summary: Constructor of a container with three intrusive list heads: clears the scalar fields, stores the caller vtable, makes +0x54/+0x58/+0x5C self-referential and default-constructs seven 0x28-byte sub-records at +0x104, forwarding arg4.
evidence: No caller and the only named callee is std_ConstructArray. The self-referential head idiom still proves an intrusive-list constructor, but 'MultiList' remains a layout description, not a class name.

name: Os_SvcCallChecked
summary: Checked kernel/IPC call wrapper: runs the command wrapper 0x00117AB8 and, when it fails with anything other than the 'not found' class 0xFFFFFFF9, reports the Result to the SDK error handler 0x0011ED40 with the call-site address 0x001221F4. Returns the Result unchanged.
evidence: The body is fully visible: call 0x00117AB8, and when the Result is negative and its class is not 0xFFFFFFF9 report it through 0x0011ED40 with the call-site address 0x001221F4, then return the Result unchanged. The named callee Gfx_IpcCmd90000 (0.6) is the wrapped call, so 'checked call wrapper' no longer depends on the caller list.

name: maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel(u32 service, u32 buffer, int first, u32 width, int c, u32 height, u32 mode)
summary: Opens the shared ir:USER session on first use, maps the shared memory, sends the channel setup request (coordinates and sizes in 8.8 fixed point) and initialises the endpoint, cleaning up on failure.
evidence: The service-name literal at 0x754FC0 was verified as the bytes 'ir:USER', so the IR session reading is solid, but the surrounding callees still carry Snd_ names (Snd_SetChannelMatrix, maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput) and the exact request format is unidentified, so the role stays a maybe_.

name: Os_ReadChunkedTable
signature: int Os_ReadChunkedTable(Reader* reader, int* bytesRead, int offset, u32 size)
summary: Reads up to `size` bytes through a reader in at most 0x40-byte requests, adding the wrapped 16-bit current offset each time, and accumulates how many bytes were transferred. It is the small-block reader the parameter-table lookups use.
evidence: `while (1) { if (size == 0) return result; uVar2 = (offset + iVar3) & 0xffff; result = func_00122650(arg1 + iVar3, &local_20, uVar2, size < 0x40 ? size : 0x40); if (result < 0) break; size -= local_20; iVar3 += local_20; *bytesRead += local_20; }`. Callers: 0x001179C0 and 0x0011E0DC.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a process handle queried through command 0x0A on the driver session, closing the previous handle with svc 0x23 first and aborting through 0x0011ED40 when the query fails.
evidence: NEW: the helper is the named maybe_Os_IpcCmd0AGetProcessValue (0x00123C9C) and the caller maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry (0x00122650) shows it is needed by the read-retry path; the body is the exact process-side twin of 0x0011DF0C. The API name is still inferred.

name: maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop
summary: One sampling pass of the SDK timing loop: for each configured entry it reads the system tick, sleeps and accumulates elapsed microseconds against the 1,000,000 constant, stopping early at the 0x3FE marker, then sets the state word at 0x007B00E0 to 3 or 0.
evidence: The 0x000F4240 (1,000,000) constant, the svc 0x28 (svcGetSystemTick) reads and the 0x007F2644/0x007B0080 tables support the sampling reading, but the named caller Gfx_OpenGpuChannel and the timer helpers do not mention profiling, so the purpose stays a hypothesis.

name: maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry
signature: int maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry(u32 dst, u32* outLen, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Drives a stack-allocated provider object (vtable 0x00780FA4) through command 0x45: queries 0x00123BAC, calls the provider's virtual +4, creates a kernel handle, then loops on 0x001228A8 with svcWaitSynchronization1 (0x24) and svcCloseHandle (0x23), retrying up to three times and copying the payload to dst.
evidence: Named callees Fs_ReadRecordBlock (0.55) and the handle helpers keep the 'read a record' reading, but the body is dominated by handle/semaphore machinery and the provider object is unnamed, so the retry/framing wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Os_SvcCallCheckedAlt
summary: Second checked IPC-send helper: calls one of the two raw send wrappers (Os_IpcSendCommand0D / Os_IpcSendCommand0E, chosen by condition flags the decompiler lost), then applies the same error policy as 0x001221C0 - 0xFFFFFFF9 is ignored, any other negative Result is reported through 0x0011ED40 - and returns the raw result.
evidence: The two send wrappers are now named (Os_IpcSendCommand0D / Os_IpcSendCommand0E), which confirms the 'two-variant send + assert' shape, but the in_CY/in_ZR inputs are a decompilation artefact, so which wrapper runs is not decidable from the C and the name stays vague.

name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd0B0000
summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x000B0000 (command 0x0B) on the ir:USER session at 0x007B2D2C; on success it writes the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84). Dead code: nothing branches to it.
evidence: NEW: the session global 0x007B2D2C is provably the ir:USER handle (srvGetServiceHandle at 0x0012226C loads the name pointer 0x00754FC0 = 'ir:USER' and the out-pointer 0x007B2D2C), so the old 'Os_' prefix and the 'GetThreadValue' claim were both unsupported. No branch target reaches this address, so the command's meaning cannot be narrowed further.

name: Fs_ReadRecordBlock
signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecordBlock(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32* dst, int* read, int updatePosition)
summary: Reads one length-prefixed record from a stream at offset, returns the bytes read and advances the tracked stream position when requested.
evidence: Calls func_00123AD0(stream, offset, dst, max, &read) which parses the 4-byte 0xa5/14-bit-length header; it also calls func_00123A60 (stream size), func_00123A0C (seek) and func_00123AB0 (align). The state fields at +4/+8 are the current offset and retry counter, and the error path reports through func_0011ED40.

name: Mem_AllocAddressRange
signature: unsigned int Mem_AllocAddressRange(MemRange* range, MemRangeNode* node, unsigned int size, unsigned int align)
summary: First-fit allocation inside a linear address range: searches the sorted free-range list for a gap that fits `size+align`, splits it, links the caller's node into the list at the right place and returns the chosen base address.
evidence: The body compares `arg3 + arg4` against `result - (piVar3[3] + piVar3[2])`, walks the address-ordered free list, handles insertion before/after the head, and finally writes `arg2[2] = result; arg2[3] = arg3;`. Range base/end come from `*arg1`/`arg1[1]`. Caller 0x11E720 uses it to reserve page-aligned memory before mapping it.

name: maybe_Os_HandleInit
summary: Creates a kernel handle through 0x0012038C into an empty *out slot and aborts through 0x00118100 on failure; when *out is already non-NULL it deliberately aborts with 0xE0A0183B, so it is a create-once helper.
evidence: NEW: the initial result value 0xE0A0183B has bit 31 set and is reached when *out is already set, i.e. it is an invalid-state assert, not a second creation attempt. Callers (maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop, maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry, the two OS helpers) only need a fresh handle slot; the handle kind is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: Mem_HeapAllocBlock
signature: unsigned int Mem_HeapAllocBlock(MemHeapState* state, unsigned int size, int align)
summary: Core block allocator: rounds the size to 4 bytes, walks the free list best-fit for the given alignment (two directions), and carves the block through 0x123E6C, which also updates the heap's statistics.
evidence: `if (arg2 == 0) arg2 = 1; uVar3 = (arg2+3) & 0xfffffffc;` then the two list walks (`self->f_28` for align < 0, `self->f_24` otherwise) aligning with `~(align-1)` and calling `func_00123E6C(&self->f_24, block, offset, uVar3, 0/1)`. This is the routine 0x11EDA8 uses for every game allocation.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, int mode, unsigned char priority)
summary: Sets a channel's play mode (byte at +0xE) and, when the mode is 0, its priority (+0x39), then marks the channel block dirty with bit 0x20000. Uses the second channel table (selector +0x131E, pointers at +0x10B4), not the +0x1322/+0x10A4 table the field setters use.
evidence: The two parallel channel tables are now distinguished - the field setters use selector 0x1322 with pointers at +0x10A4, while this and 0x00122EF8/0x00122F74/0x00123000/0x00123070/0x001230E8 use 0x131E with +0x10B4. Caller 0x0011EE78 passes mode 0/1/2, supporting the 'play mode' reading, but it stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int value)
summary: Stores a 32-bit word at +0x34 of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x40000. The only caller (0x0011EE78) computes the value before the call, so it is a caller-supplied parameter rather than a fixed constant.
evidence: The offset (+0x34), the dirty bit (0x40000) and the fact that the caller supplies the value are the only facts; the old evidence called the argument a 'gain', which the 0x0011EE78 call site does not prove, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int* data)
summary: Copies 0x20 bytes from the caller's descriptor into the channel's wave slot (table at +0x1234 selected by the +0x1322 double-buffer index) and sets dirty bit 4.
evidence: The source table +0x1234 is the same one 0x0011302C (SetupChannelBuffers) lays out, and the 0x20-byte copy matches the per-buffer descriptor size, so 'copy the wave/buffer descriptor into this channel' is supported by two sites rather than one; only the word 'wave' remains a label, so maybe_ at 0.48.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short value)
summary: Stores a 16-bit value at +0x3A of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x400000.
evidence: The offset (+0x3A), the width (16-bit) and the dirty bit (0x400000) are the facts; the single caller (0x0011EE78) passes a value it has just computed, so no field meaning can be attached and maybe_ stays at 0.42.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short start, unsigned short end)
summary: Writes a byte at +0xF and a halfword at +0x3E of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x800000.
evidence: The paired position write (one byte plus one halfword, one dirty bit) still reads like a loop start/end pair and the single caller (0x0011EE78) supplies both values, but the offsets are the only hard evidence, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short arg3, unsigned short b, unsigned short c, unsigned short d, unsigned short e)
summary: Writes five consecutive fields of the channel block (+0x40, +0x42, +0x44, +0x46 and the byte at +0x45) and marks it dirty with bit 0x1000000.
evidence: Five consecutive 16-bit fields written together is the shape of a decoder parameter block, and 'ADPCM' is the best candidate for a block that also has ADPCM state fields at +0x24/+0x26; the exact offsets are the only hard evidence, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Snd_SetChannelMatrix
summary: Scales the twelve coefficients at +0x0E..+0x19 of the caller's channel state by the scalar at +0x1A and hands the 3x4 result to the matrix writer 0x124050.
evidence: Confirmed: twelve multiplications by one scalar followed by a call to the (now analysed) 12-word matrix writer is exactly 'scale the channel matrix by its gain', and its only caller 0x11EE78 passes the channel state it has just updated. The parameter list in the old signature was wrong (the second argument is unused), which the summary now says.

name: maybe_Os_ReleaseSharedHandle
