summary: Releases one reference to the shared kernel handle at 0x007AF900: when the refcount at 0x007AF8F8+4 drops below 2 it closes the handle with svcCloseHandle, decrements the count and restores the process-handle sentinel 0x00741AD4; otherwise it only decrements and returns the 0x082067F0 status constant.
evidence: The body is the same refcount-and-close shape as the cfg helpers in this batch (count, handle in a global slot, svcCloseHandle, sentinel restore); the only caller (0x0011E0DC) is unnamed, so the handle owner stays unknown.

name: Os_MessageQueue_Push
signature: u32 Os_MessageQueue_Push(OsMessageQueue* queue, const OsMessage* msg)
summary: Lock-free push of an eight-word (0x20-byte) message into a 15-slot ring buffer: copies the payload to base + 0x20 + index*0x20, issues a data-synchronisation barrier and increments the 16-bit index field (bits 8..15, modulo 15) with LDREX/STREX. When the queue goes from empty to non-empty it wakes the consumer through 0x11F730 and 0x12412C. Rejects a null queue or a kind byte >= 0xF.
evidence: LDREX/STREX pair on *queue, 16-bit index field at bits 8..15 wrapping modulo 15 (magic 0x88888889), kind byte at +1 must be below 0xF, 0x20-byte element with 8 words, sentinel loop, empty-to-full wake path 0x11F730 + 0x12412C, two SDK error literals on the reject paths.

name: Os_VirtualToPhysical
summary: Translates a virtual address to its FCRAM physical address: VRAM (0x1f000000..0x1f5fffff, plus the 0x1f600000 alias) maps to 0x08000000-based memory, the linear heap shifts by 0x0c000000 or 0x0f000000 depending on the heap base, and unmapped addresses return 0.
evidence: Body: result = 0x123e18(address,1); if 0 and (address + 0xe1000000 < 0x600000 || address == 0x1f600000) -> address + 0xf9000000 (0x1f000000 -> 0x08000000, the classic VRAM mapping); otherwise tries 0x123db4 / 0x123dcc and the heap bounds from 0x122cd8 / 0x122cc0, adding 0xc000000 (or 0xf0000000 for heaps at 0x30000000+). 31 callers, all low-level audio/DSP buffer setup.

name: Os_IpcQueryCommand18
summary: Leaf IPC query on the SDK's shared session: writes command header 0x00180000 (command 0x18, no parameters) into the thread's IPC buffer and issues SVC 0x32 (SendSyncRequest); on success it copies the eight response words out and returns the reply result code. Used by the date/time query path.
evidence: mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3 (TPIDRURO) then str 0x180000,[r4,#0x80] (IPC buffer at TLS+0x80), svc #0x32 = SendSyncRequest per 3dbrew SVC table, result at TLS+0x84, 8 words TLS+0x88..0xA4 copied to arg2. Caller 0x0011F5C0 ('Os_QueryTime') parses the 8 words as a calendar value and 0x00119B4C re-exports them.

name: Snd_DetachChannel
summary: Detaches a channel from the mixer's list: unlinks its list node at +0x110 (0x11FCBC) and clears the active word at +0x18. The mirror of the priority insert 0x11FD1C.
evidence: Confirmed: the callee 0x11FCBC is the list-link helper whose counterpart 0x11FD1C inserts by priority, and the only caller 0x546EA0 is the voice-release path that detaches the voice from its source/decoder/queue - so 'detach this channel' is what the code does. The old 0.30 reflected the missing caller, which now exists.

name: std_Strncmp
signature: int std_Strncmp(const u8* arg1, const u8* b, u32 len, u32 aligned)
summary: Bounded string compare. While four or more bytes remain it compares whole words, using a saturating per-byte subtract against the 0x01010101 constant to detect a NUL terminator, and falls back to a byte loop for the tail; returns the difference of the first mismatching bytes (or +-1 after a byte-swapped ordering compare).
evidence: Word loop compares 4 bytes, UQSUB8 (UnsignedSaturate) against literal 0x0012374C = 0x01010101 detects 0x00, returns (word_a&0xff)-(word_b&0xff) etc.; the differing-word path compares bswap(a)<bswap(b) i.e. memory byte order; tail loop advances 2 bytes at a time while bytes are equal and non-zero; arg4 bit0..1 selects the aligned fast path.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand06AndClearPending
summary: Forwards the selector byte to driver command 0x06 (Os_IpcSendCommand06), translates a non-success result through the 0x0011ED40 assert and then unconditionally clears the pending word at driver-session+4; called once per sampling iteration by 0x00122484.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Os_IpcSendCommand06 (0x00124C64, command header 0x00060040) and the caller is the per-sample loop 0x00122484; only the store to 0x007B2D08+4 is the 'clear pending' part, so the old IpcCmd06 name was incomplete rather than wrong.

name: maybe_Os_Timer_ConvertTicks
signature: void maybe_Os_Timer_ConvertTicks(s64* outMs, int stem, s64 ticksA, int stemB, u32 perSecond, int scale)
summary: Converts a 64-bit tick delta to milliseconds: subtracts the two 64-bit stamps, scales by the per-second factor, converts through the double helper 0x00124ACC, rounds with 0x00125034 and stores value*1000. The 0x20C49BA5E353F7CF magic constant is the multiplicative inverse of 1000.
evidence: The 1000-inverse magic and the final multiply by 1000 support 'ticks to milliseconds', and the only caller is the named maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop (0x00122484); the argument list is a guess because the stamps arrive as register pairs, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Math_AlignUp
signature: u32 Math_AlignUp(int stream, int offset, int extra)
summary: Rounds extra+offset up to the stream's alignment (field +4) by forwarding to the shared align helper 0x0011CFAC; Ghidra dropped the real return value and shows only the extraout_r1 copy.
evidence: The body is a one-line forward to the shared align helper 0x0011CFAC with (extra+offset, stream->f_4); Ghidra lost the return register (extraout_r1), but the caller Fs_ReadRecordBlock uses the result to compute the next record offset, which fixes the align-up reading.

name: Fs_ReadRecord
signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecord(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32 dst, u32 maxLen, u32* read)
summary: Reads a 4-byte record header (magic 0xa5 plus a 14-bit payload length) and, if the length fits in maxLen, reads the payload into dst and returns the byte count.
evidence: Header is built as local_1c[0]=0xa5 and the length is (b1 & 0x3f) | ((b1 & 0x40) ? b2<<8 : 0). func_00124B88 is the underlying read; on success *read=result and 0 is returned, otherwise the error code g_00123B64 (0xC8610C0F) is returned. Called only by Fs_ReadRecordBlock 0x122938.

name: maybe_Os_RefreshCachedHandle
summary: Refreshes a cached kernel handle: queries the fixed IPC session (command 0x0C) for a new handle/status pair, closes the handle currently stored in *handleOut with svc 0x23, and stores the queried value there. It is a handle swap, not a counter read.
evidence: Callee Os_IpcQueryCommand0C (0.50) writes the second reply word to *out and returns the first; the body then closes *handleOut before overwriting it. Nothing in the body reads a timer/counter and no caller (Os_PerfSample_Loop, Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry) uses the value as time, so the old 'Timer' prefix was unsupported; what object command 0x0C returns is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Snd_CreateChannelBuffers
signature: int maybe_Snd_CreateChannelBuffers(unsigned int width, unsigned int height, char* mode)
summary: Creates the pair of buffers: when *mode is 0 it rounds both dimensions up (+4 below 0x40, +5 above, minimum 8), calls the buffer setup 0x122200 with the shared block sizes, and on failure calls 0x122484 and the session finaliser. Dead code: nothing branches to it.
evidence: NEW: no branch target reaches 0x00123BB0, so the two callers the old evidence cited do not exist. The +4/+5 rounding with an 8-byte minimum is buffer-size arithmetic and the two calls are the create/finish pair, but neither call is named, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand0E
summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0E with two normal words (value, 0xA|value<<4) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Returns the reply result code.
evidence: Header literal 0x00123C94 = 0x000E0042 (cmd 0x0E, 2 normal + 1 translate parameter), TLS+0x84 = value, TLS+0x88 = 0xA|(value<<4) buffer descriptor, TLS+0x8C = buffer, svc #0x32 SendSyncRequest on the handle in *0x007B2D2C (same session as 0x00123D68/0x00123508).

name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd0A0000
summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x000A0000 (command 0x0A) on the ir:USER session at 0x007B2D2C; on success it writes the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84).
evidence: NEW: the session global 0x007B2D2C is provably the ir:USER handle (srvGetServiceHandle at 0x0012226C loads the name pointer 0x00754FC0 = 'ir:USER' and the out-pointer 0x007B2D2C), so the old 'Os_' prefix and the 'GetProcessValue' claim were unsupported. The only branch target is 0x00122454, inside maybe_Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle, whose own name is a maybe_ guess.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand19
summary: Sends IPC command 0x19 (thread-local command word 0x00190040) with one parameter on the session at 0x007B2D2C and returns the reply word from TLS+0x84.
evidence: The TLS header word 0x00190040 encodes IPC command 0x19 with one parameter and the reply is read back from TLS+0x84 after svc 0x32; the doc's callers (Fs_ReadRecordBlock, maybe_Save_CheckReadState) place it in the file/save I/O path, so it is a command stub, not a thread-local store.

name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd180182
signature: unsigned int Svc_Ir_IpcCmd180182(unsigned int handle, unsigned int firstWord, unsigned int b, unsigned int c, unsigned int d, unsigned int e, unsigned char flags)
summary: Seven-word IPC submission for ir:USER command 0x18 (header 0x00180182 = one normal + six translated words): fills TLS+0x84..+0x98, puts the handle at +0xA0, issues svc 0x32 and returns the reply. Used to hand a buffer descriptor to the IR service.
evidence: NEW: the session global 0x007B2D2C is provably the ir:USER handle - asm 0x00122260/0x00122264 load the name pointer 0x00754FC0 (rodata bytes 'ir:USER') and the out-pointer 0x007B2D2C into r1/r0 before the srvGetServiceHandle wrapper 0x001192C0, and no other srvGetServiceHandle call writes that global. So the old 'Snd_' prefix was wrong. The header 0x00180182 is unchanged.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand0D
summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0D with two normal words (value, 0x2|value<<14) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Sibling of 0x00123C54; 0x001228AC picks between the two.
evidence: Header literal 0x00123DAC = 0x000D0042 (cmd 0x0D, 2 normal + 1 translate), TLS+0x84 = value, TLS+0x88 = 2|(value<<14), TLS+0x8C = buffer, svc #0x32. Caller 0x001228AC compares a value and branches to 0x00123C54 (0x0E) or this one (0x0D).

name: Os_TranslateLinearAddress
summary: Translates an address that lies inside the linear heap: validates the range against 0x124cdc/0x124cec and returns the physical address by adding the heap's base delta.
evidence: uVar1 = 0x124cec(); if (address >= uVar1 && address + size > address && address + size <= 0x124cdc() + uVar1) return *g_00123e14 + address; else 0. Only caller 0x12345c.

name: Os_TranslateMainRamAddress
summary: Returns the physical address corresponding to a range that overlaps the main-RAM window, or 0 when the range lies completely outside it.
evidence: Named callee Os_VirtualToPhysical (0x12345C family) and the main-RAM base/size getters; three of the callers are sound-buffer setup paths that must convert ARM pointers to DSP addresses.

name: maybe_Os_MainRamRangeFragment
summary: Not a function start: the address lies 0x196 bytes inside 0x123E18 (the main-RAM address translator) and repeats its bounds compare plus the 'base + addr' return. It only appears in the batch because a 0xB5xx halfword matched the Thumb-push scan.
evidence: NEW: exact-target branch scan finds no caller and no data pointer to this address, confirming it is interior code of 0x123E18. The body also depends on caller registers (unaff_r5, in_CY), which per FACTS.md keeps the confidence at 0.3 or below.

name: Snd_WriteChannelMatrix
signature: unsigned int Snd_WriteChannelMatrix(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int* matrix)
summary: Copies twelve 32-bit words (three groups of four, from matrix-2, matrix+0xE and matrix+0x1E) into the channel block at +2, +0x12 and +0x22, then marks the block dirty with 0xE000000.
evidence: Confirmed: three four-word copy loops into three consecutive 0x10-byte slots is a 3x4 transform write, and its only caller 0x123174 scales exactly twelve coefficients before calling it. NEW: the odd source offsets (-2, +0xE, +0x1E) are now stated, because they are what a reimplementation has to match.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand0C
summary: Sends the parameterless IPC command 0x0C (TLS command word 0x000C0000) on *handleSlot and returns the reply word from TLS+0x84. Issued by Os_MessageQueue_Push as the wake-up call.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Os_MessageQueue_Push (0.6), which fixes the meaning (wake the waiting thread after a push); the command word 0x000C0000 and the svc 0x32 sequence are visible in the body.

name: Pack_Handle_Dtor
summary: Releases the pack handle owned by a game object (a destructor helper): frees the handle's table entry, then overwrites the handle word with the 'empty' sentinel.
evidence: 0x30c3f0() first (subsystem-specific pre-release), then validates *arg1 against the pack handle table (g_001241c4 mask / g_001241c8 table, entry[1] == handle>>12) and calls Pack_FreeHandleEntry@0x1241d0; finally *arg1 = *arg1 & g_001241cc | g_001241cc (sentinel). 39 callers, all over UI/field object destructors.

name: Pack_ReleaseHandle
summary: Releases a pack/resource handle: looks the generation-tagged handle up in the global handle table, destroys the entry when the generation matches, then overwrites the caller's word with the 'null' encoding (all low bits set) and returns the slot.
evidence: body masks *handle by g_001241C4>>8 and compares *piVar1[1] with value>>12 (generation check) before calling 0x1241D0; then '*arg1 = *arg1 & g_001241CC | g_001241CC'. 269 callers, always immediately before overwriting a stored handle (e.g. 0x17DAD8 self->f_70/f_68/f_7c)

name: Pack_FreeHandleEntry
summary: Slow path of the handle release: decrements the entry reference count, and when it reaches zero either recycles the entry through the free list at g_0012419C or returns it to the pool allocator (0x11CFAC/0x116AE0) before unlinking it from the live list.
evidence: decrements self->f_74, branches on *g_00124298 (pool-empty flag), allocates 0x10-byte node with func_0011CFAC/0x116AE0, sets vtable LAB_001242a8, calls list link 0x1235A4; 156 callers all from handle-release paths

name: Pack_HandleEntry_Init
signature: void Pack_HandleEntry_Init(PackHandleEntry * entry, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor of a pack-handle entry: installs the vtable pair at +4/+8, clears the state words, and default-constructs the twenty 0x28-byte sub-handles at +0x18.
evidence: piVar1 = 0x10e8c0(arg1 + 4) (base-object ctor); piVar1[-1] = g_00124470; *piVar1 = g_00124470 + 0x18; then [1]=0, [2]=g_00124474, [3]=0, [4]=g_00124474, [5]=0 and func_00100050(piVar1 + 6, g_00124478, 0x28, 0x14). Callers 0x10af94 (lazy global table) and Pack_FreeHandleEntry@0x1241d0.

name: Pack_LoadTableObject
signature: void Pack_LoadTableObject(uint32_t* scratch, PackTableRef* out, const char* name)
summary: Loads one logical table (e.g. player_param_hero.bxon) from the pack by name, validates that it is an object node (0x124E04) and stores the owned object pointer + a reference-counted handle in the 8-byte destination pair.
evidence: calls 0x124FA0 (pack manager), 0x124B24(manager, key, name), walks node children to the object node, checks 0x124E04, fills arg2[0]=object and arg2[1]=handle via 0x124F60/0x124D48; called ~60x from 0x120464 with s_player_param_*_bxon

name: Pack_LoadTableTyped
signature: void Pack_LoadTableTyped(uint32_t* scratch, PackTableRef* out, const char* name)
summary: Same as 0x124904 but for tables whose root node must validate against type id 0xA2 (0x124E30 + node->f_20 == 0xA2); used for the scenario_param_* family.
evidence: in 0x120464 every call passes s_scenario_param_*_bxon and the code enforces 'iVar3 == 0xa2' before storing the pair; 10 call sites, all inside 0x1249E0 and 0x120464

name: Fs_ResourceFindInBucket
signature: int Fs_ResourceFindInBucket(ResourceTable* self, int bucket, u32 name)
summary: Scans one hash bucket of the resource table and returns the first entry that Fs_ResourceFindByName matches, or null.
evidence: The callee is now the confidently named Fs_ResourceFindByName (0.65) and the body is exactly that lookup over one bucket; no direct caller, but the helper's role is no longer in doubt.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand06
summary: Sends driver command 0x06 with one normal parameter (header 0x00060040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B2D2C and returns the reply word.
evidence: Confirmed: the literal 0x00060040 and the handle global 0x7B2D2C are both in the body, so the name is a direct description of the code. NEW: its only caller is 0x123750, which forwards a per-sample byte and then clears a pending word - consistent with a 'submit one byte' command.

name: Os_IpcQueryCommand0C
summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x000C0000 (command 0x0C) on the fixed session at 0x7B2D2C; on success copies the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84).
evidence: Confirmed: the header 0x000C0000 and the two reply words are in the body, and the name states exactly that. NEW: its only caller 0x123B68 uses the pair as 'new handle + status' while swapping a stored handle, which is consistent with a handle/query command.

name: Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign
summary: Move-assigns a pair of pack handles: releases both handles currently held by dst (validating them against the two handle tables) and then takes over src's handle, leaving src untouched.
evidence: For each of *arg1 and *arg2: if (mask != handle>>12) look up the table entry and, when entry[1] == handle>>12 and entry[0] != 0, call Pack_FreeHandleEntry@0x1241d0 / 0x124dd0; finally *arg1 = *arg2. 51 callers including Pack_LoadMasterTables@0x120464 and the UI resource loaders.

name: Fs_ResourceFindByName
signature: int Fs_ResourceFindByName(ResourceTable* self, const char* name, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up a packed resource by name in the global resource table: hashes the bucket, then compares the 0x40-byte name key of each candidate and returns the matching record.
evidence: Field_LoadNpcTables (0x184EF8) calls it with s_npc_list_bxon_00185220 ("npc_list.bxon") and 0x1849B4 calls it with "npc_ie.bxon" and "book_ie.bxon". The body indexes g_00124F54 (0x007BA2D0) by (hash & 0xFFFFF)>>8, compares piVar2[1] with hash>>12, and compares each record's +0x14..+0x50 key via func_00123660 with size 0x40.

name: Pack_GetManager
summary: Returns the lazily created global pack/resource manager: an array of 0x220-byte manager slots whose first element receives the vtable at creation; every pack load goes through the returned pointer.
evidence: Named callers do exactly pack register/lookup (Pack_HandleTable_Acquire, Gfx_EffectPack_LoadById, Field_LevelVisualData_Load, Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type1), confirming the manager role beyond the allocation shape.

name: maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine
signature: u32 maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine(void* state, void* ucb, void* context)
summary: ARM EHABI personality routine: calls the unwind bytecode interpreter 0x1250BC, whose inline opcode words follow the call site, and returns an unwind reason code. The whole 0x125098-0x125738 region is C++ exception support, not game code.

name: Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock
summary: Decodes one block of transform coefficients: picks the DC predictor from the block-type bits, then walks the block row by row feeding every bit through the two interleaved VLC case bodies (0x001351C8 when the bit is set, 0x00135104 when clear) and refilling the bit reservoir as needed. Returns the number of bits consumed, which the caller uses to advance the stream. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0013B4E4 (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_B): 2 of 544 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.
evidence: NEW: its two case bodies are now named (Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven/Odd, 0x00135104/0x001351C8) and they are the only two entries the coefficient loop dispatches to; together with the 16-coefficient row counters (iVar9/iVar17 -= 0x10) and the returned bit count this fixes the function as the per-block entropy decoder. Its _B twin at 0x0013B4E4 differs in 2 of 544 bytes. DISASSEMBLY (raw ARM words at 0x00134EE4): `e92d5ff0 push {r4-r11,lr}`, `e5901000 ldr r1,[r0]`, `e3a02000 mov r2,#0`, `e0d130b2 ldrh r3,[r1],#2` (16-bit code fetch), `e1a03803 lsl r3,r3,#16`, `e0933003 adds r3,r3,r3`, `2a000046 bcs` (the carry tests Ghidra prints as CARRY4), `e2522001 subs r2,r2,#1`, `bb000257 bllt 0x00135868` (reservoir refill), `e5904048 ldr r4,[r0,#0x48]`, `eb00025a bl 0x0013587c` - and the two group decoders are reached by a computed branch, which is why they do not show up as BL. The readable C is damaged (unaff_r6), so the reading is taken from the disassembly.

name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven
signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
summary: VLC case body of the MPEG-style block decoder: takes three bits from the bit reservoir, remaps the escape code, jumps through the 16-entry table at 0x135418 to decode up to four coefficients of one interleaved group, and uses the per-subblock flag byte at 0x1350C4 to decide whether another coefficient or a block end follows.
evidence: NEW: no direct branch target reaches 0x00135104, so the earlier 'callers are 0x134EE4/0x13B4E4/0x141AE4' claim cannot be confirmed - the body is reached through the computed jump it performs itself, which is why the call graph shows nothing. The body still reads unaff_r6/unaff_r11 for the subblock pointer, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd

summary: The other case body of the same block decoder: takes a 4-bit prefix, clamps the code index against the subblock's remaining counts (f_51/f_58), rewrites the four current-code bytes and jumps through the shared 0x135418 table. Selected when the first bit of the subblock is set.
evidence: NEW: no direct branch target reaches 0x001351C8 either, so the pair is reached only through the decoder's own computed jump; the body is heavily damaged (Ghidra removed 17 unreachable blocks and reads unaff_r6/unaff_r11), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Video_DecodeSubblockMask
summary: Walks the current sub-block's coefficient-presence mask: reads the mask byte for the sub-block index left in r6 and calls the per-slot decoder 0x0013562C once for every set bit (bits 1..0x20). Runs before the VLC decoding of that sub-block. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x00141EA0 (Video_DecodeSubblockMask_C): 10 of 660 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.
evidence: NEW: the mask source and the one-call-per-set-bit shape are confirmed in both copies, and the per-slot body it calls sits in the same coefficient block; no caller passes a different index, so the "sub-block mask" reading is the only one that fits. _B twin differs in 18 of 660 bytes (literal words and the relocated table base). DISASSEMBLY (raw ARM words at 0x001352A0): `e92d5010 push {r4,fp,ip,lr}`, `eb000163 bl 0x00135838`, `e24fc050 sub ip,pc,#0x50` (mask table base), `e7dcc006 ldrb ip,[ip,r6]` (mask byte indexed by r6), then `e31c0001 tst ip,#1` / `1b0000da blne 0x00135630`, and the same tst/blne pair for #2, #4 and #8 - exactly one call per set bit. The readable C is damaged (unaff_r6), so the reading is taken from the disassembly.

name: Video_IdctBlock8x8
summary: Reconstructs one 8x8 luma block: zeroes the 64-word coefficient array, lets 0x001377A0 fill it, then runs the integer inverse transform (8-point butterfly with the >>1/>>2 twiddle approximations and a >>6 output scale) and writes the 8 samples of each of the eight 0x400-spaced lanes. Three block-type thresholds select a DC-only, a reduced-coefficient and the full transform path. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0013BC3C (Video_ResidualBlockAdd_B): byte-identical (152 bytes).
evidence: NEW: the body is an IDCT, not a lane blend - the coefficient array at self+0x1b8..+0x2b4 (64 words) is cleared, the DC-only path copies one sample per lane, and the other two paths run the classic butterfly (iVar10+(iVar10>>1), +-(>>1), +-(>>2), then >>6 with 0x20/0x40 rounding). The old name "ResidualBlockAdd" described only the final sample write. Byte-identical to its _B twin at 0x0013BC3C (0 of 152 bytes differ). DISASSEMBLY (raw ARM words at 0x0013563C): `e92d5c00 push {sl,fp,ip,lr}`, eight `mov r4..r11,#0`, `e280cf6e add ip,r0,#0x1b8`, eight `e8ac0ff0 stmia ip!,{r4-r11}` (the 64 coefficient words cleared), `e280c078 add ip,r0,#0x78`, `eb000844 bl 0x001377a0` (coefficient fill), `e35c007c cmp ip,#0x7c` / `d1a0f004` (DC-only fast path) - then the 8-point butterfly with the >>1/>>2/>>6 scales. The readable C is damaged (unaff_r11), so the reading is taken from the disassembly.

name: Video_McPredict1ReadMv_B
signature: void* Video_McPredict1ReadMv_B(McCtx* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Motion-compensated prediction, "new vector" path: reads a fresh motion-vector delta from the decoder state, adds it to the stored predictor, writes the resulting vector through the caller's out pointer, then copies and filters the luma block through bank 0x00133810 (8 x-phases x 2 y-phases) and both chroma blocks through bank 0x00133850 (8 x-phases x 2) into the reference frame. This is prediction variant 1 of four (same code, coarser filter bank each time). Byte-compared with the twin at 0x00133890 (Video_McPredict1ReadMv): 7 of 376 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

name: Script_ArrayAppend

name: Script_ArrayRemove
summary: Implements the Squirrel array method array.remove(index): validates the receiver and index, releases/compacts the 8-byte elements (refcount at +4), shrinks f_1C and reallocs f_18, and throws 'index out of range' on bad input.
evidence: Uses sq argument accessors (0x005B5C6C with self->f_34..), VM error 0x006BD988 with the literal 'index out of range' at 0x0014AE58; array object layout {f_18 = elements, f_1C = size, f_20 = capacity, 8 bytes/element, refcount at +4}; vector grow helper 0x0014CE14; sibling 0x14B0D8 uses 'size must be a number'.

name: Script_ArrayRemoveAt
summary: The native behind array.remove(index): checks the argument is an integer in range, releases the element's reference, shifts the tail down with memmove, shrinks the array and reports 'wrong type' / 'idx out of range' otherwise.
evidence: Body: 0x5b5c6c(self, f_34) -> array, 0x5b5c6c(self, f_34+1) -> index value, checks tag bit 0x4000000 (integer), errors via 0x6bd988(self, s_wrong_type_0014b0b8) and 0x6bd988(self, s_idx_out_of_range_0014b0c4), releases refs, memmoves with 0x11cd00, decrements f_1c and shrinks the capacity via 0x14ce14. Neighbours Script_ArrayResize@0x14b0d8 and Script_ArrayCopyRange@0x14b36c.

name: Script_ArrayResize
summary: Implements array.resize(n [, fill]): reads the new size (number or float), grows or trims the element vector, fills new slots with the supplied value and throws 'wrong type' / 'idx out of range' / 'size must be a number'.
evidence: Error literals 'wrong type' (0x0014B0B8), 'idx out of range' (0x0014B0C4), 'size must be a number' (0x0014B304) inside this and the following function; type tag 0x5000004 handled as float; same 8-byte element array layout as 0x0014ABCC.

name: Script_CallAllArgs
summary: Calls the closure currently on top of the VM stack with every pushed argument (top-1 parameters) and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now the confidently named Script_Vm_CallClosure (0.8) and the body is the standard 'resolve stack top, call with that many parameters' adaptor.

name: Script_ArrayCopyRange
summary: Copies a [start,end) range of elements from one Squirrel array/string into another, growing the destination and copying each referenced slot with the VM memory helper; throws 'wrong indexes' and 'slice out of range'.
evidence: Literals 'wrong indexes' (0x0014B5AC) and 'slice out of range' (0x0014B5BC); reads three arguments (array, start, end), normalises negative indices by the source length (local_2c[5]), then 0x006111A4(self->f_8c, src+start+0x1c, end-start) + 0x005B5660 push; array layout as 0x0014ABCC.

name: Script_Native_NewSlot
summary: Squirrel native closure for the VM's newslot operation: forwards its untouched argument registers to Script_Vm_NewSlot and maps success to 1 (one value on the VM stack) and failure to -1 (error), the native calling convention.
evidence: Disassembly is the 24-byte native shape: push {r4,lr}; bl Script_Vm_NewSlot; cmp r0,#0; movge r0,#1; mvnlt r0,#0. It sits in the 0x00148xxx..0x00166xxx block of Script_Native_* bound natives (compare Script_Native_TokenizeString) and has no direct bl caller, i.e. it is registered by address. The old 'Script_NewSlot' duplicated the VM routine's own name.

name: Mem_AllocSubHeapA

evidence: `func_0011EDA8(g_0014bb34, arg2, 4, arg1, arg1, arg1);` - the literal at 0x14BB34 holds 0x007C840C, a .bss heap object; 0x11EDA8 is the game's heap allocator (size, align, bounds). No callers inside the decompiled code, so it is most likely reached through a native/function table entry. A byte search of build/code.bin for the entry addresses (with and without the Thumb bit) finds no pointer to this function anywhere in the image and the decompiled call graph has no caller, so it is an unreferenced allocator stub - most likely a per-subsystem 'operator new' that the linker kept but the game never calls.

name: Event_DispatchHandlerByte6

evidence: Checks the initialised flag *g_0014BBDC, indexes g_0014BBE0 + *(u8*)(cmd+6)*8, and calls entry->fn(*event, cmd) when entry->type == *(u8*)(event+2). Called from the event timeline updater 0x2A8CCC, which walks five parallel command lists.

name: Event_DispatchHandlerField39

evidence: Checks *g_0014C040, indexes g_0014C03C + *(u8*)(cmd+4)*8, and compares entry->type with *(u8*)(event+2). Called from 0x2A8CCC for the f_16 command list.

name: Script_ArrayPrepare
summary: Prepares a result array sized from the array passed in (2*n+2, minimum 12) and stores it into stack slot -2 so the following helper can fill it element by element.
evidence: Named Script_Vm_PushStackFrame/Script_Vm_PushStackSlot calls with slot 0xFFFFFFFE and the clamp to 0xC make the array-preparation role explicit; the filling helper at 0x14EF80 follows it.

name: Script_Native_GetInstanceUserPointer
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure, so the script sees one result value or an error.
evidence: Disassembly: push {r4,lr}; bl Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer; cmp r0,#0; movge r0,#1; mvnlt r0,#0. Same 24-byte bound-native shape and register forwarding as the other Script_Native_* wrappers; no bl caller, so it is table-registered. The callee is confidently named (0.75), which fixes the operation.

name: Script_ArrayCallWithElementsNoThrow
summary: Identical to Script_ArrayCallWithElements except that the final Script_Vm_CallClosure is made with raiseerror=0, so a failing call returns -1 instead of raising a Squirrel error; the array elements are pushed the same way.
evidence: New context: the confident Script_ArrayCallWithElements (0x0014CD5C, 0.50) is the immediately preceding native-table entry (0x007AFD0C vs 0x007AFD1C) and this body is byte-for-byte the same 136 bytes with only the last call flag changed from 1 to 0, which the disassembly shows directly. The old '_2' suffix did not say what the difference was.

name: std_string_tolower
summary: Squirrel string method tolower(): copies the receiver string byte by byte through 0x00100150 (ASCII tolower) and pushes the converted string.
evidence: Reads the string object at arg0 (length +0x14, chars +0x1C), allocates with Container_Vector_Reserve, maps every byte through 0x00100150, then 0x006111A4 copies and 0x005B5660 pushes; sibling 0x0014F10C uses 0x0010016A (toupper).

name: std_string_toupper
summary: Squirrel string method toupper(): identical to 0x0014F008 but maps each byte through 0x0010016A (ASCII toupper).
evidence: Only difference from 0x0014F008 is the per-byte mapper 0x0010016A instead of 0x00100150; same string layout (len +0x14, data +0x1C) and push path.

name: Mem_AllocSubHeapB
signature: void* Mem_AllocSubHeapB(unsigned int tag, unsigned int size)
summary: Same allocator trampoline as 0x14BB08 but for the heap object at 0x007C83B4 (literal pool entry at 0x14FB60).
evidence: `func_0011EDA8(g_0014fb60, arg2, 4, arg1, arg1, arg1);`; the literal at 0x14FB60 is `b4 83 7c 00` = 0x007C83B4 (checked in build/code.bin and in asm/text/text_00140048.s). The four trampolines differ only in their heap object (0x7C840C, 0x7C83B4, 0x7C8464, 0x7C835C). A byte search of build/code.bin for the entry addresses (with and without the Thumb bit) finds no pointer to this function anywhere in the image and the decompiled call graph has no caller, so it is an unreferenced allocator stub - most likely a per-subsystem 'operator new' that the linker kept but the game never calls.

name: Script_ArraySortSift
signature: int Script_ArraySortSift(ScriptVm * vm, ScriptArray * array, int start, int end, int closure)
summary: One sift-down step of the heapsort used by array.sort(): compares the node with its children (through the comparator closure when closure >= 0, or the VM's built-in comparison) and swaps until the heap property holds.
evidence: Loop over i = 2*start and i+1 within end, calling 0x5b5e3c (Sq_VmObjCmp) in the no-closure path or pushing the closure plus both values and calling 0x6bb0f4/0x6bba70 in the closure path, then swapping the two 8-byte slots; returns 0 on a failed comparison (callers treat that as failure). Caller 0x147750 (Script_ArraySort).

name: maybe_Script_ArraySortSiftAlt
summary: Second copy of the array-sort sift step: compares two array slots either with Sq_VmObjCmp (when no comparator closure is set) or by pushing both slots and calling the closure, swaps the two 8-byte slots when the result is negative and continues the heap sift; errors are reported through 0x005B3DA4 with the sort error strings.
evidence: Re-read: the body uses the named VM helpers (Sq_VmObjCmp, Script_Vm_CallClosure, Script_Vm_GetFloatDirect, Script_Vm_SetTop), which makes the sift-and-swap reading solid, and the function is a native-table entry at 0x007AFD5C. The loop variables are still unaff_* and the top-level helpers 0x005B5C6C/0x006BB0F4 are unnamed, so it stays maybe_.

name: Script_ArraySort_CompareCall

evidence: Located at 0x00153280 inside the array sort implementation; surrounded by error literals 'compare func failed' and 'numeric value expected as return' at 0x0014CD12/0x0014CD1C.

name: Battle_UpdateEncounterTransition
summary: Per-frame driver of the battle-encounter transition, reachable from the script native EncountEventEx. On frame 1 it rebuilds the 0x1348-byte transition object from its static template (copying 0xDC bytes over a zeroed block) and resets two flags in the game singletons; on later frames it compares the frame counter against half the active screen extent minus 15 and, at the matching frames, flips the two 2D layers through their vtable entry +0x28. Returns 1 once the transition is over - that return value is what ends the script's frame loop.
evidence: Squirrel caller (game_assets/scripts/packs/script/base/script.decompiled.nut): `for (local frame = 0; EncountEventEx(battleID, false, frame) == false; ++frame) suspend(1);` and EncountEventEx passes its third argument straight to this function (EncountEventEx_0014da1c.c line 50). Body: one-time build guarded by the flag at 0x0015E0E4 - `size = align(0x1348, 0x10); memset(block, 0x1348); *block = vtable 0x0015E0FC; memcpy(block+4, 0x005329E0, 0xdc, 3)`; the two half-extents come from `(int)(self->f_11a0 * 0.5f) - 0xf` and `(int)(self->f_119c * 0.5f) - 0xf` with 0.5f = the literal at 0x0015E498; the layer toggles are `(**(code**)(*(*(ptr+0x14)+0x10) + 0x28))(ptr,0,1)` and the +0x1c variant, where the object comes from func_006F229C, which sibling batch N_021 names Ui_GetCore. The two game-singleton fields it resets are Os_GetGameWork()+0x74 and +0x78 (0x006F1EEC, N_077). Other callers 0x003686B8/0x00368704 are the same battle-transition helpers.

evidence: Calls (**(code**)(*self->f_e4+4))() then clears f_e4. Walks piVar3=self->f_110 while *piVar3 != self->f_10c, calling (**(code**)(*elem+4))() on each. The +0x10c/+0x110 pair is an intrusive sentinel list; the slot +4 is the virtual destructor.

name: Battle_FreeCommandList
summary: Destroys every node of the manager's queued-command list (+0x110) through the node vtable slot +4. Called when a battle ends or the queue is rebuilt.
evidence: walks self->f_110 circular list; for each node calls (**(code**)(*node+4))(); no other side effects. Callers are 0x16BA4C (queue reset) and 0x16E3E0 (battle teardown), both command-list lifecycle points.

name: Battle_BackupUnitActions
signature: u32 Battle_BackupUnitActions(Battle * battle, ActionRecord * out, int slot, int actorId)
summary: Snapshots the battle action table: copies all 80 action records (each holding five 0x8c-byte per-member sub-records) from the staging array to the backup array, clears the staging array, and copies the record belonging to actorId (optionally filtered by slot) into the caller's buffer.
evidence: The two 0x50-entry tables are self->f_e8 (staging) and self->f_ec (backup), each record 0x2c8 bytes with 5 sub-records of 0x8c; the record key is at +0 and the action id at +0x88 (0xffffffff = empty, otherwise validated through 0x63fd24(work, id) and the record's f_191 byte). Returns 1 when a matching record was copied. Callers 0x4009f0, 0x42c7f8, 0x47d47c, 0x47efe8, 0x4b8258 (battle UI/effect code).

name: Battle_ExecuteItemAction
signature: void Battle_ExecuteItemAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Resolves a battle action that uses an item: reads the item id from the acting unit (vtable+0x84), looks up the item record, hands its id/effect data to the unit, then queues the item-use action (0xf) or its extended variant (0x10). The special item 0x120 (288) with world+0x4e64==0x45 forces a scan of the four unit lists for item 400, i.e. a scripted battle item event.
evidence: 0x61BD4C (Item_LookupRecord) is called with (vtable+0x84)(unit); 0x63DF9C resolves the item data; special case world+0x4e64==0x45, unit+0x768==0 and item==0x120 scans 4 lists at world+0x428c for id 400 with states 0x9e/0x9f; pushes 0xf via 0x16B810 or 0x16F28C, and 0x10 when the scan succeeded.

name: Battle_CountActionTargets
signature: int Battle_CountActionTargets(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
summary: Counts how many candidates an action may hit: walks the ally container (world+0x4254) and the enemy container (world+0x4270), keeping units whose side matches the action's target mode (vtable+0xa8) and that report targetable (vtable+0x24). Returns the total count.
evidence: two loops over 0x5797D8(world+0x4254/0x4270,0) with 0x2AB62C(index); filters (vtable+0xa8)(action) against 2/3 (side selectors) and (vtable+0x24)(unit) targetable. Sibling 0x16FA10 does the same with vtable+0xac and extra state 10.

name: Battle_Update
summary: Main per-frame battle update: clears finished command objects, runs the queued action processing, executes the AI pass when this frame is not an interrupt, resolves the current action queue, updates the camera/scene hooks, and advances the phase/action counters. Also handles the 'battle over' hand-off to the next state.
evidence: teardown calls 0x16D854/0x16BEDC; then 0x16EB54 (unit action processing), 0x16C7F8 (AI), 0x16B810; 0x171DA4/0x171944/0x1739A0/0x174674 are the scene/camera updates; 0x169ED8/0x16901C finish the frame; resets f_124 (action slot) and f_2f0. Called from the battle state machine in 0x606xxx.

name: Battle_Start
summary: Virtual battle-start entry: clears the current action slot, initialises the world battle interface, resets the action flags, syncs the unit model transforms, releases the previous battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable +0x2C to finish initialisation.
evidence: The callees Battle_SyncUnitModelTransforms, Menu_ResetSlotRecords, Ui_BalloonPool_Reset and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseChildren are all confident and are exactly the per-battle reset set; it has no direct caller because it is reached through the manager vtable.

name: Battle_Initialize
summary: Battle initialisation used when the battle scene is created: same resets as Battle_Start, syncs unit transforms, hides the field view, releases the old battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable+0x2c. Called by the battle-scene setup routine 0x607B7C before its per-slot checks.
evidence: identical body to 0x16E65C minus the 0x1BBECC preamble; single caller 0x607B7C starts with func_0016E680() and then configures the four battle slots (0x3238BC); resets self[0x46], f_3d/f_3e and calls 0x16BA64, 0x3247B0, 0x2E0D60, vtable+0x2c.

name: Battle_UpdateActionQueue
summary: Advances one battle action: asks the manager's virtual predicates whether an action is pending/ready, builds the action queue for the current unit (0x16BBF4) and the default/AI passes, and when the action completes marks the unit list dirty and starts the next action. Returns 0 (the caller keeps ticking).
evidence: calls vtable+0x158/0x15c/0x160/0x18c/0x194/0x1b8/0x1a8 in sequence; when slot+0x2c5 is set calls 0x16BBF4, 0x168AA4, 0x16A78C, 0x16932C (queue building); then 0x16C52C/0x16A3F8 when idle, and 0x16EA5C; f_3d marks 'action list built', f_124 is the slot index.

name: Battle_FindActiveUnit
summary: Scans the manager's command/unit list (world+0x4260) and returns the first unit that is active, not dead and not suppressed, packaged into a small descriptor (0x176948/0x175F80/0x176134). Returns NULL when no unit qualifies. Used to pick 'whose turn is it'.
evidence: iterates world+0x4260..0x4264; checks vtable+0x18 (active), vtable+0x24 (alive), vtable+0x1c (busy), vtable+0xd8 and unit+0x108; calls 0x176948 then 0x175F80(&desc,unit,self->f_148) and 0x176134. 0x175F80 is also used from 0x16E75C for each queued unit.

name: Battle_ProcessUnitActions
summary: Per-unit action pass for the ally-side unit list: for each live, non-suppressed unit it resolves the data id, dispatches the pending action (or the fallback action with the unit's category) and decrements the unit's remaining-action counter.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Battle_Update, and the callees now include Ui_Widget_CountChildren and Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted, i.e. the tick also runs the queue widgets; the unit-list walk (+0x5C to +0x4254) and the counter decrement are visible in the body.

name: Battle_QueueCommandByCategory
summary: Queues the default command entry for a battle unit: lets the action object fill its six-byte descriptor, maps the unit's category byte (+0x31) to action id 0xE/2/3 in the auto-battle mode (work+0x4244) and otherwise uses id 1, then pushes or inserts the entry via Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry / Battle_InsertActionSlot according to the unit's +0xB0F7 flag.
evidence: Both queue functions and the action-id ladder are now readable, so the routine does not merely resolve a type - it enqueues the entry. It is itself a handler in the action dispatch table at 0x726AB0 (between maybe_Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant and Battle_QueueAbilityAction), i.e. the 'queue this unit's default command' slot.

name: Battle_QueueAttackActions
summary: Enqueues the two-step attack sequence for a unit: action 0xD (attack) followed by 0x2E (finish), appended through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry or inserted through Battle_InsertActionSlot depending on the unit's +0xB0F7 mode, with the follow-up flag derived from the alive/state bytes.
evidence: In the action-handler table at 0x726AB0 it sits between Battle_QueueAbilityAction and Battle_ExecuteItemAction, i.e. it is the normal-attack handler, and both queue calls are now named with the exact action ids 0xD and 0x2E.

name: Battle_ResetUnitStates
summary: Clears transient battle state on all units: empties the command list (calling each node's vtable+0x174/0x48 and 0x1CD53C), zeros the per-unit delay fields (+0x8e0/+0x8dc), and resets the four unit-group lists' animation/attack counters. Called between battles or on a full battle reset.
evidence: walks world+0x4260 list calling vtable+0x174(0), +0x48(0), 0x1CD53C(node); zeroes unit+0x8e0/+0x8dc for the 4 units of world+0x4254; for each of the 4 group lists (world+0x428c) calls vtable+0xb8 and zeroes +0x8dc/+0x8e0.

name: Battle_InsertActionSlot
signature: void Battle_InsertActionSlot(BattleManager* self, int index, BattleAction* action, uint32_t actionId, int arg5, uint8_t arg6)
summary: Inserts one 0x2c8-byte action slot at the given index of the manager's 0x50-slot action array: first snapshots every slot into the backup array (+0xec), shifts the range [index..0x4e] up by one, zeroes the new slot, then hands the action descriptor to 0x3CDF74 which fills the slot and its five 0x8c sub-records.
evidence: copies all 0x50 slots from f_e8 to f_ec (5x0x8c each plus the +0x2c0..0x2c6 tail), shifts slots, writes 0xffffffff headers and +0x2c4=6/+0x2c6=1 for the new slot; final call func_003CDF74(f_e8+index*0x2c8+arg5*0x8c, action, 0x2c8, index*0x2c8+700, self, index). Callers use it for action ids 0x14/0x15/1..0x10/0x2a/0x2d/0x2e.

name: Battle_CheckActionSlotFree
signature: u32 Battle_CheckActionSlotFree(Battle * battle, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Checks whether the current unit's action slot is usable: validates each of the five per-member sub-records, and rejects the slot when the candidate actor id already appears in one of the record's ten target id fields.
evidence: Reads record arg1[0x3a] + arg1[0x49]*0x2c8 and the per-member entries at +0x88 (empty = -1) and +0x8c*index; the not-empty ids are validated with 0x63fd24 + f_191; then walks the caller's actor list (intrusive list at arg1[0x44], head arg1[0x43]) and compares each id with the target fields f_20/f_24 ... f_58/f_5c, returning 0 on a match and 1 after all five slots. Only caller maybe_Ui_CmdQueue_ProcessSlots@0x16932c.

name: Battle_CountActionCandidates
signature: int Battle_CountActionCandidates(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
summary: Second target-count helper: counts units in the four battle groups plus the ally container that match the action's target mode (vtable+0xac, values 0/1) and are selectable, excluding units with state 10. Used to size/validate target lists.
evidence: 4x26 loop over world+0x428c and a loop over world+0x4254; selects on (vtable+0xac)(action)==0 with (unit vtable+0x18) or ==1 with (unit vtable+0x10); the ally loop additionally requires 0x639954(unit,10)==0. Sibling of 0x16E228 which uses vtable+0xa8/0x24.

name: Battle_QueueGroupAction
summary: Builds a combined action for up to four party units - first pass prefers units that are active and not already acting, second pass fills the rest - and inserts it at the current action index with action id 0x2D through Battle_InsertActionSlot.
evidence: NEW: the insert callee is now the confident Battle_InsertActionSlot, and the readable body shows exactly the documented shape (two scans of battleWork+0x4260, at most four pointers, action id 0x2D). The action id and the 'group action' reading are therefore no longer guesses.

name: Battle_QueueAbilityAction
signature: void Battle_QueueAbilityAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
summary: Queues a spell/skill action: reads the ability id (vtable+0x7c), resolves its data through 0x18C184, copies the data flags to the unit, then chooses the action id from the ability's category byte (+0x298: 6,7,8,9,10,0xb) or the default 0x1f/0x20. Also emits the special 0x30/0x31/0x32/0x2e variants for healing/revive/status abilities.
evidence: 0x18C184(abilityId) returns the ability record; (vtable+0x58)(unit, record+0x1f8); record->f_2f3 and first char switch produce 0x30/0x31/0x32/0x2e; record->f_298 switches 0..5 to action ids 7,6,8,9,0xb,10; otherwise 0x1f/0x20. All pushes go through 0x16B810/0x16F28C.

name: Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant
signature: void Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant(BattleManager* self, uint32_t not, BattleAction* action)
summary: Queues the action for an ability record from the second ability table (0x0018C1B8): resolves the ability id through vtable +0x78, applies the record to the unit and queues action 4 or 5 depending on record byte +0xEB, falling back to 0x25/0x26 for invalid records.
evidence: NEW: both callees are now named - Battle_InsertActionSlot (0.65) and Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry (0.6) - which fixes the queue-vs-insert split the first pass guessed; the record table 0x0018C1B8 is still unnamed, hence 'Variant'.

name: Battle_ResetLineupState
summary: Resets the battle line-up bookkeeping (counters f_c0/f_c4/f_cc/f_d0/f_d4/f_d8/f_dc/f_e0 to 0xffff/0, flags f_f2/f_129, f_148) and then calls 0x16D438 to (re)spawn the unit entry effects. Used when the battle line-up changes or a battle is initialised.
evidence: writes self->f_f2=1, f_148=0, f_fc/f_c4/f_d0/f_cc/f_d8/f_d4/f_e0/f_dc/f_c0/f_129 then calls 0x16D438(self) (the effect-spawn pass over the unit lists) and stores g_00170410 in self+0x130.

name: Field_Gimmick_NotifyInit
summary: Sends initialization event type 1 to the gimmick controller state machine at +0xE4 if non-null.
evidence: Checks self->f_e4 != NULL and invokes virtual method +0x14 on self->f_e4 with event code 1.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionScene
summary: Presentation state machine for the current battle action: driven by the state word at +0x134 (0xB0F/0xB43/0xB47 sentinels) it waits for the acting unit to become idle, spawns the hit effect at the unit's node, picks the model/animation by unit id and advances the camera/scene state; returns 1 while frames are still needed.
evidence: Callers Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty_00640348; The named callees Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty, maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnUnitEffect and * Effect_FindOrCreateInstance identify the "wait, spawn, advance" phases, but the state constants and the * f_E4/f_F0 fields are not named, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Battle_CheckUnitsCondition
signature: int Battle_CheckUnitsCondition(BattleManager* self, uint32_t mode, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Battle-condition query used by the state machine: mode 4 compares the two values, mode 5 asks the world, mode 6/7 require every unit in the four groups to pass a state test, mode 8 returns the world flag at +0x4252.
evidence: The switch over modes 4..8, the four 0x1C-stride unit lists at world+0x428C and the unit-state callees match the documented battle work layout; one named caller passes four stored command ids.

name: Battle_QueueUnitListAction
signature: void Battle_QueueUnitListAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleUnit** outUnits)
summary: Collects up to eight targetable units from the +0x4260 list (active, allowed to act, no disabled state 8/10) into the caller's array and queues action 0x2F with the source unit computed by 0x0016815C.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Ui_GetScaledValue (source-unit value) and maybe_Ui_CmdQueue_PushEntry (the shared action-queue push) plus the "max 8 candidates" cap make the multi-target reading solid; the twin 0x0016FBF8 does the same with the prefer-idle pass. Which action 0x2F is remains open, so 0.5.

name: Battle_HasPendingAction
signature: u32 Battle_HasPendingAction(Battle * battle, ActionRecord * record, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Scans the staging action array from the current index for a record belonging to the given actor whose action id is still valid, and reports whether one exists.
evidence: Loops i from self->f_124 to 0x4f over self->f_e8 + i*0x2c8: record[0] must equal arg2, then the id at +0x88 is either 0xffffffff (match) or validated through 0x63fd24(work, id) with record->f_10 and the f_191 byte; returns 1 on the first match. Callers Battle_BuildTargetSlots@0x1723e8, Battle_BuildTargetSlotsForCommand@0x172ed8 and 0x26acf8.

name: Battle_SelectActionTargets
signature: int Battle_SelectActionTargets(BattleManager* self, BattleUnit** out, int groupIndex, uint32_t arg4, uint32_t arg5)
summary: Chooses the concrete target(s) of an action: dispatches on the action's target-mode virtual +0xa4 (single, one group, all, self, random) and range checks via +0xb0, then fills out[8..] with the selected unit pointers and returns the count. This is the routine behind every 'who gets hit' decision.
evidence: first calls (vtable+0xa4)(action) and switches modes 3/4/5: mode 3 collects all units from the four group lists (world+0x428c) plus allies (world+0x4254); mode 4 returns the acting unit; mode 5 picks one ally or, for groupIndex<0, all allies; modes 1/2 delegate to 0x16E228/0x16FA10; +0xb0(x,y) calls are the shape/range validity checks.

name: Battle_CollectGroupTargets
signature: uint32_t Battle_CollectGroupTargets(BattleManager* self, BattleAction* action, BattleUnit* source, int groupIndex)
summary: Collects the units of one group (work+0x428C + groupIndex*0x1C) that match the source's target mode (unit vtable+0x10/+0x18) into action+0x20 and returns their count; when the group's first unit is valid it becomes the action's primary target, and with no primary target the walk repeats over all four groups.
evidence: Caller Battle_SelectActionTargets (0x170E28) and callee Battle_IsTargetValid show the routine filling the action's target array, and the return value is the number of targets, so 'Collect...Targets' describes the work better than 'Select', which is the caller's job.

name: Battle_FinishBattleScene
summary: Shuts down the battle presentation: tells the battle scene object to hide/animate out, creates its closing popup, calls the scene vtable+0x2C and closes the battle target window.
evidence: Named callees Battle_PopupEntry_Create and Ui_BattleTargetWindow_CloseIfNotEnemyTurn plus the scene vtable calls make the teardown explicit; the scene pointer is world+0x4320 as documented.

name: maybe_Battle_DetachCurrentActor
summary: Calls the current battle actor's vtable+0x28 (a no-argument teardown slot) and hides the battle target window at battleWork+0x431C. Called at the start of BattleScene_AttachPrimaryUnitModels, i.e. it detaches the previous actor presentation before the models are re-attached; it touches no scene state.
evidence: The only caller is the named BattleScene_AttachPrimaryUnitModels (0.50), which calls it immediately before re-attaching every unit's model, and the sibling Battle_FinishBattleScene (0x001714D4) is the real scene teardown (it drives the scene object at currentActor+0x204 through vtable+0x18/+0x74 and creates a popup). 'CloseBattleScene' therefore overstated what this 80-byte function does.

name: Battle_UpdateActorModels
summary: Per-frame update of the battle scene's actor-model set (Event_ActorModels_Update on the set at self+0x35C with the frame counter at self+0x304); when the battle work has a current actor (+0x4320) whose +0x404 byte is set, it also pushes state 8 into the object at self+0xE4 through vtable+0x14. Always returns 1.
evidence: The callee Event_ActorModels_Update is now named (0.50) and is the per-frame cutscene actor-model update; the same +0x35C model set is used by BattleScene_AttachPrimaryUnitModels, so this is the battle's model-set tick rather than an action animation. The +0xE4 object's vtable+0x14(int) is the same state setter that 0x0016C128 calls with 9.

name: maybe_Battle_SetControllerState8
summary: When the battle scene object at (work+8)->+0x5C +0x4320 exists and its +0x404 flag is set, switches the manager's controller (f_E4 vtable +0x14) to state 8 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
evidence: The body only tests the battle scene object (+0x4320/+0x404) and sets the controller to state 8 - nothing checks an animation end, so 'CheckActionAnimEnd' described a condition that is not in the code.

name: maybe_Battle_ScanUnitIntro
summary: Battle presentation scan at state 0xBF5: walks the battle groups/units, tests each unit with func_00632694 and vtable+0xE8(status), and pushes a message for status ids 8 and 0x90 while advancing the group cursor; finishes after group 4.
evidence: The group/unit walk, the 0x120 entry bound and the two status constants are readable, but no named caller confirms whether this is the battle intro or a generic status announcement pass.

name: Battle_SelectTargetsThunk
summary: Register-preserving thunk to Battle_SelectActionTargets, used where the caller has already placed the arguments in r0-r4.
evidence: The disassembly is `bl 0x170D4C; bx lr` with untouched registers, and its only caller maybe_Battle_RunTargetSelection (0x20A19C) reaches it directly. A thunk with no locals is exactly what the name says.

name: Battle_QueueCommandMenuEntries
summary: Builds the command entries the battle menu consumes: for every valid unit of the party list, the all-unit list and the four group lists it pushes action 0x28 (row) and 0x33 (group header) with a descending priority starting at 100 (0x557/0x55C for the group variant).
evidence: The named maybe_Ui_CmdQueue_PushEntry is the only queue call, and the three passes plus the separate group action ids (0x557/0x55C) show exactly how each character/monster row reaches the command list. Only the action ids remain unexplained, so 0.55.

name: Battle_RebuildUnitActions
signature: void Battle_RebuildUnitActions(Battle * battle, ActionRecord * record, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Rebuilds the staging action array: copies it to the backup, clears the staging copy, then removes every record whose key equals the given actor (clearing its five sub-records and decreasing the live count) and compacts the remaining non-empty records upwards.
evidence: Full 0x50 x 0x2c8 copy loop plus the five 0x8c sub-record clears; removal matches `*(int*)(f_ec + i*0x2c8) == arg2` and clears the record, then `self->f_124--`; the tail loop copies each record whose first byte is non-zero from f_ec back into f_e8. Callers Battle_SelectAiActions@0x16c7f8 and Battle_Update@0x16e3e0.

name: Battle_QueueCommand0x00
summary: Pushes battle command 0: when the unit's vtable +0xE8 reports state 0x7D the same entry is pushed twice (the following action lands one slot later), otherwise once; the turn-order priority is computed identically for both.
evidence: NEW: the callees are the confident Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry and Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority, the pushed id is the literal 0 and the 0x7D state test is visible; command 0 being an idle/no-op command is still an inference, so the name stays id-based.

name: Battle_BuildTargetSlots
summary: Fills one of the battle's 16-byte target-slot records with the units that satisfy the current action's target pattern: it iterates all four groups, computes each unit's remaining HP/effect amount through 0x495E04/0x490994/0x488638/0x491E3C, sets the selection flags (bit 1 = invalid, 2 = dead, 4/8/0x10 = status), and writes the chosen pattern index into the slot. Called from the attack sequence (0x173CD0/0x173D04).
evidence: reads (action+0xa0) then its vtable+8 for a scaling factor (g_00172828); 0x6297D8 decides 1 or 2 target 'layers'; 0x495E04/0x490994/0x488638/0x491E3C compute per-unit amounts for modes 4/5/other; flags at slot+1 (+1/+2/+4/+8/+0x10), slot+2/3 mark dead/status; copies the group/pattern table from g_00172848.. and stores slot->f_20.

name: maybe_Battle_BuildTargetSlots_Continuation
summary: Not a function: the second half of Battle_BuildTargetSlots (0x001723E8). The prologue at 0x001723E8 pushes {r0,r4-r8,sb,sl,fp,lr} and reserves 0x560 bytes of stack, and nothing pops before 0x00172698; the code here keeps using that frame (sp+0x550, live r4/r5) and the real epilogue is at 0x00172EC4. Ghidra split the function at this address, so the 'dispatch table' reading and the halt_baddata body are both artefacts.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly at 0x00172698 is a plain 'bl 0x11FE8C' with no prologue, and the enclosing Battle_BuildTargetSlots (0x001723E8, 0x2B0 bytes) ends exactly here without an epilogue - its push {r0,r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,sb,sl,fp,lr} / sub sp,#0x560 at 0x001723E8 is still in effect and the matching vpop/pop is at 0x00172EC0/0x00172EC4. The mutual 'caller/callee' edge with Battle_BuildTargetSlots is the split symbol calling back into its own head. Same trap as the documented 0x003C3594 / 0x001664AC mid-function splits.

name: Battle_BuildTargetSlotsForCommand
signature: uint32_t Battle_BuildTargetSlotsForCommand(BattleManager* self, BattleAction* action, BattleUnit** out, int groupIndex, int mode, uint8_t arg6, char* arg7)
summary: Same target-slot construction as Battle_BuildTargetSlots but scoped to one group and command mode (4/5/other): it runs the ability/item range test, sets the per-unit selection flags, then dispatches the resulting table through 0x100906 with a pattern-specific callback (g_001734c4..d4).
evidence: if action->f_b0f5 is set it first tries 0x627800(self,action,ally) and stores the ally as action->f_20; then 0x627610(self,action,&group); loops group units (world+0x428c), calls 0x18C1B8 + 0x488638/0x491E3C/0x490994 for modes 4/5/other, and finally 0x100906(table,count,0x10,callback) with the callback selected by *arg7 (0..5).

name: maybe_Battle_AreAllUnitsDefeated
signature: uint32_t maybe_Battle_AreAllUnitsDefeated(uint32_t arg1, void* target, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Returns 1 when `target` is in status 0x9A and no live battle unit (vtable +0x10 == 0) in the 4x26 lists at +0x428C is in status 0x9B.
evidence: The unit walk and the two vtable tests are the same ones Battle_AreAllUnitsIdle uses, but status ids 0x9A/0x9B are still unidentified, so 'defeated' remains a hypothesis.

name: Battle_SelectTargetsMode8
signature: void Battle_SelectTargetsMode8(Battle* battle, u32 arg2, u32 group, u32 output)
summary: Mode-8 target-selection entry: forwards to Battle_SelectActionTargets(battle, out, groupIndex, 8) and then default-constructs the four 8-byte target descriptors with the 0x005906C0 constructor. Reached only through the mode table at 0x00726B18 (no direct callers).
evidence: Battle_SelectActionTargets is now named (0.60) and takes (self, out, groupIndex, arg4, arg5); this wrapper forwards its own arg4 as the `out` array and passes 8, then builds the same 4x8-byte descriptor array (std_ConstructArray with ctor 0x005906C0) as 0x00174674. It has no direct callers, consistent with a dispatch-table entry.

name: maybe_Battle_SelectCommandTarget
signature: void maybe_Battle_SelectCommandTarget(void * action, u32 u32, u32 u322)

name: maybe_Battle_StartActionSequence
summary: Starts the visual/sequence part of an attack or ability action: resets the effect/track objects, picks the first non-empty battle group and a random unit, then drives the model animation list and sets the state to the 'running' constant when done.
evidence: Callers Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty_00640348, Anim_UpdateModelAnimList_004d2374; Named callees (Battle_BuildTargetSlots, Anim_UpdateModelAnimList, Event_ActorModels_Update, * Ui_BalloonPool_SetFlag) and the RNG pick through 0x1CA438 support 'start action sequence'; the state * constants g_00174128/g_00174148 are still unnamed.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionSequence
summary: Continuation of the battle action-sequence state machine: the state at self[0x4D] starts at 0xB7B, scans the four battle unit lists (+0x428C) for the first non-empty one, picks a random unit through the battle RNG, sets the primary target self[0x51] and drives the target/hit stages, finally moving the unit's secondary state machine (+0x14) to 5/6/7.
evidence: The body is the same state machine as maybe_Battle_StartActionSequence (0x00173CD0) without * its opening effect reset, and uses the documented battle offsets (RNG +0x4218, unit lists +0x428C, flag * +0x4244); the sibling 0x00173CD0 is still a maybe_, so calling this the 'update' half is descriptive * rather than proven.

name: Battle_SpawnResultPopupEntry

evidence: The only callee is the now-named Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnActorSpanEntry (0.50), a popup-entry builder (Mem_AllocAligned_2 of a 0x20C entry plus Ui_PopupEntry_ClearAll), not an effect spawner; the branch is on the battle result code f_128, which Battle_Update also tests.

name: Battle_FinishCommandPhase
summary: Closes the command phase: confirms the unit commands (0x0016C740), rebuilds every group unit's descriptor, clears the action slots, then moves the battle actor to state 8 or 3 depending on vtable+0x18C and the self[0x4A]/+0xF6 flags. Always returns 1.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Battle_FinalizeUnitCommands and maybe_Battle_ClearActionSlots bracket the body, and the "state 8 on success / 3 on retry" tail is the same state pair the battle sequence uses; the function is reached from the battle update path, so it is the phase-completion step.

name: maybe_Battle_ClearActionSlots
summary: Resets the four 0x58-byte slot records at self+0x150 (zeroing the id/flag words and clearing the 0x38-byte tail) and then refills one slot per active party member through Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionSlots.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Battle_FinishCommandPhase (0x00174324) and the fill callee is Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionSlots (0x00495F10), so the 'reset the slots at the end of the command phase' role holds; whether the records are command slots or unit-condition slots is still open, so maybe_ stays.

name: Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition
summary: Looks up which of the four stored command slots (f_fd, f_100, f_103, f_106) matches the given command id and evaluates its condition via Battle_CheckUnitsCondition(0x170A0C) with the slot's two parameters. Returns the last evaluated result.
evidence: four sequential comparisons self+0xfd/0x100/0x103/0x106 against arg2; each match calls func_00170A0C(self,slotId,slot+2,slot+1); the f_106 branch returns immediately. Slots f_fd/f_100/f_103/f_106 are also compared in 0x16C128.

name: maybe_Battle_CollectActionTargets
signature: void maybe_Battle_CollectActionTargets(Battle* battle, u32 arg2, u32** selection)
summary: Takes the 8-slot target-marker selection array: spawns the primary entry's action effect (vtable+0x80 + Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init + Actor_SpawnEffectBlock), collects up to four further units whose data id (+0x768) differs from the primary's into slots 1..4, computes the minimum Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority over them and pushes the command-queue entries (event ids 0x11/0x12/0x13/0x32).
evidence: The disassembly (Ghidra truncated the body after the vtable+0x80 call) shows `strne r5, [r4, r8, lsl #2]` writing the collected units into the caller's array slots 1..4, then Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority per slot and Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry with event ids 0x11/0x12/0x13/0x32. Battle_Update passes the array filled by Battle_TargetMarker_Update, so the function fills targets; 'ClearTargets' was the opposite of what it does.

name: Battle_Destroy

name: Field_SetupNpcActionScript

evidence: 0x4E4 bytes; strings action/appear/disappear/notice at 0x00177D10..0x00177D38; allocates through 0x00109DC8, parses with 0x0011142C/0x0011CCA0 and calls 0x00177720 (vtable setup) plus 0x001D0B50/0x001D101C.

name: Field_SetupEnemyAi

name: Field_NpcCheckSight
summary: NPC perception test: returns 1 when the actor can see the player (or another actor) this frame. It checks the actor's enable/awareness flags, distance, the view cone (Field_IsPointInActorViewCone at 0x178DD0) and, for actors with the 'group sight' bit, compares the nearest group member positions.
evidence: checks (self+0x2aa) bits, world+0x44, distance g_001787b0, then calls 0x178DD0(self,&playerPos,1,...) (named Field_IsPointInActorViewCone in N_001); second pass walks actors with flag 0x20 in self+0x2aa and calls 0x178DD0 for each, using 0x63DCA4 to compare sizes; returns 1 and stores the found actor id in self[0xc3].

name: Container_HashMap_FindEntry
summary: Look up an entry by key and hash in the global hash map g_00178878, traversing collision bucket chains.

name: Field_NpcMoveTowardTarget
summary: Moves an NPC one step toward its current move target: clamps the direction vector to g_00178af4, asks the level collision system (0x2E7F08) whether the position is free, and sets movement state 1 (move) or 2 (blocked), with an extra 'path blocked' state 4 when the path object is active.
evidence: target = actor position (f_9c/a0/a4) + g_00178ae8; direction from 0x63451C(world+0x48); normalises if length > g_00178aec else uses g_00178af0; 0x2E7F08(pathObj,&pos,0)!=0 -> (vtable+0xb4)(self,1,0) else (...,1); extra (vtable+0xb4)(self,4,0/1) when world+0x54->f_1c != 0 and 0x46E7AC()==0.

name: Monster_SetupEcology

name: Field_IsPointInActorViewCone
signature: u32 Field_IsPointInActorViewCone(Actor* self, float* point, int allowHeightCheck, int scaleRadius)
summary: Tests whether a world point lies inside an actor's sight cone: it checks the height band (+0x308), the radius (+0x304, optionally scaled by +0x2FC), the angle against the facing vector using the cosine threshold at +0x300, and if everything matches queues an event through the 0x002E7F08 curve manager. Returns 1 when the point is visible.
evidence: Geometry: f_94/8C/90/98 = facing basis, f_9C/A0 = position, f_300 = cos limit, f_304 = radius, f_308 = height. Uses 0x00672A14 (acos) for the angle and 0x0011CB38/0x002E7F08 for the event queue. Both callers (0x0017843C, NPC range logic and 0x004C5F48) are field/NPC code.

name: maybe_Map_RefreshLevelGrid
summary: Cached-revision refresh: compares self->f_31C with the revision counter at 0x007A36E4+8 and, when they differ, rebuilds the shared 0x98-byte UI object and forwards the new revision to 0x0017C9E4(object+0x9C, self->f_31C), then stores it.
evidence: NEW: the four callers (maybe_Ui_Anim_SetPose/StopPose, maybe_Actor_OnStateChanged/StopStateAnim) are all maybe_ and disagree about the owner, so they do not confirm a map grid; the rebuilt object is the generic 0x98-byte UI object and 0x0017C9E4 is unnamed. maybe_ stays.

name: Map_UpdateGridCallback
summary: Trampoline callback that refreshes the current map-grid level instance with Map_UpdateGridInstance and returns 1 so the caller keeps it registered.
evidence: The callee Map_UpdateGridInstance (0.50) resolves a level's placement record and submits its transform; this 16-byte body is exactly that call plus 'return 1', the per-frame callback shape. There is no direct caller because it is installed as a function pointer.

name: Map_UpdateGridInstance
summary: Refreshes the instance of the current level in a map grid: when the level revision changed it lazily creates the 0x98-byte grid object, resolves the level's placement record with Map_FindRecordById, asks the record for its transform (vtable +0x14), computes the object transform and submits it (vtable +8).
evidence: NEW: both callees are now confident (Map_FindRecordById, Map_ComputeObjectTransform), which confirms that the function resolves a map placement record and pushes its transform - the 'grid instance' wording is the only remaining interpretation, and it matches the +0x31C revision check.

name: Map_ComputeObjectTransform
signature: void Map_ComputeObjectTransform(MapObject * obj, int mode, MapVec3 * outPos, MapVec3 * outDir)
summary: Composes an object's world position and facing: copies its local position, looks up the referenced locator/rotation record, multiplies the two quaternions and optionally scales the result by the record's factor for mode 3.
evidence: *arg3 = self->f_9c/f_a0/f_a4; *arg4 = g_00179394[0..2] (default direction) then a full quaternion product of the object's rotation (f_8c..f_98) with the locator record's rotation (record fields f_34/f_38/f_3c, looked up by the u16 id at self+600 through 0x63eeac); if mode == 3 the vector is scaled by record->f_84. Callers maybe_Map_UpdateGridInstance@0x179154 and maybe_Map_PlaceObject@0x1798d0.

So this is the face-table row getter, not a generic 'entry 8' accessor.

name: Ui_RegisterActor
signature: uint32_t Ui_RegisterActor(void* holder, void* actor, void* actorB, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Registers a pair of actors in a UI actor-slot holder: packs the two actor ids into holder+0xC/+0xD (0xFFFFF800 sentinel when an actor is missing), sets the initial delay 0xFFFFFFF, bumps the use counter at +0x10, binds the holder through the named Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor on the game work's +0x58 block and decrements the remaining-life counter at +0xF. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: The named callee Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor (0x00339FC0) is what makes the 'Ui actor slot registration' reading solid: this function is the code that fills the slot before binding it. The readable C is a damaged decompilation for one operand only (unaff_r7 in the sentinel expression); the disassembly at asm/text/text_00140048.s:67694-67720 shows it intact: `and r0,r7,r1` / `orr r0,r0,r1` with r1 = 0xFFFFF800, `strd r0,r1,[r4,#0x34]` with r1 = mvn #0xF0000000 (the 0x0FFFFFFF delay), the +0x40 use counter and the `subgt` life decrement at +0x3C, then `bl 0x339FC0`. The three callers (0x180B94, 0x1835AC, 0x184958) are still unnamed, so the owning window is not identified.

name: Ui_Object_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the engine's small Ui_Object base: runs Ui_Object_DtorBody (0x17C334) and then frees the block. It is the base vtable's deleting-destructor slot, not a per-class helper.

The 51 apparent callers are derived destructors that reach the 0x17C330 local entry inside this 20-byte symbol (a split-symbol artifact), which is why they were mis-read as callers of a 'thunk'.

name: Ui_Object_DtorBody
summary: Destructor body for the small engine object base: releases the embedded heap block at +0x14 when the object owns it, resets the vtable/id word at +4 and returns self for the deleting-destructor caller.
evidence: Named callers are the object destructor thunks and derived dtors (Field_Actor_DtorBody, Field_SceneObject_DtorSprite, Field_Marker_Dtor, Battle_Unit_Delete), which all use it as the shared base-destructor body; the old verb 'DestroyObject' did not say it is a dtor.

name: maybe_Ui_WorldMap_CodeFragment
summary: Not a function: a 2-byte-aligned address inside ARM code that Ghidra decoded as Thumb. The disassembly resynchronises at 0x0017F5B4 with an explicit '.arm' directive and then decodes real ARM (b, bl 0x6731EC, vmov.f32/vsqrt.f32/vmla.f32 on [r4,#0x98]/[r4,#0x9c]/[r4,#0xac]), so everything Ghidra reports here is garbage. The region sits between Ui_WorldMap_LoadVariant2 (0x0017EDE0) and Ui_WorldMap_ReleaseResources (0x0017FBB4).
evidence: NEW: asm/text shows '/* 0x0017F5B2: 84b5 */ push {r2, r7, lr}' immediately followed by '.arm' at 0x0017F5B4 and then 'b #0x17f48c', 'bl #0x6731ec', 'vmov.f32 s26, s0' - i.e. the address is misaligned inside ARM code and the surrounding 'Thumb' decodings (b #0x17ef7e from bytes 84e5) are nonsense. There is no jump table and no battle-animation code, so 'Battle_Anim_DispatchTable' is unsupported; the callee list (Ui_MapWindow_*, Ui_MessageWindow_*) is an artefact of the misdecode.

name: Field_SetRegion

evidence: string s_param_region__s_pack_0018551c (formats 'param_region/%s.pack'), 0x63D1B0(regionObj, *arg1), 0x3882F0(..., 2, name) builds the pack entry; stores handle at arg1+4
