name: Script_ParseAssignmentExpression
signature: void Script_ParseAssignmentExpression(ScriptCompiler* comp, uint32_t* lhs, uint32_t mode)
summary: Assignment/ternary expression parser of the Squirrel compiler: handles '=' (0x3d) and '?' (0x3f) including the short-jump fixups for the ternary branches, brackets/parentheses around the value, and emits the assignment opcode plus line-info records. Recurses into itself for nested assignments.
evidence: token comparisons against '=' 0x3d, '?' 0x3f, '[' 0x5b, ')' 0x28, '.' 0x2e and keywords 0x119/0x121/0x12f/0x130/0x13d..0x13f; calls func_005FC86C (the lexer) and func_001BDD50 to emit opcodes (0x1a/0x18/0x21/0x2c/0xe); uses func_001BE454/0x1BCE5C/0x1BE384 for line/column fixups. Called by 0x186150 (postfix parser) for index/call arguments.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseExpression
summary: Bitwise operator parser: loops over '&' (0x26), '^' (0x5e) and '|' (0x7c), calls the next-level expression parser through the compiler's operator table (comp->f_18/f_10/f_8) and emits the bitwise opcode (0x12 with sub-op 0/3/2).
evidence: three while loops comparing *arg1 against 0x26, 0x5e, 0x7c; calls (*comp->f_18/f_10/f_8) with the operator index and emits opcode 0x12 plus sub-op 0,3,2 via 0x1BDD50; obtains line/column with 0x1BE454/0x1BCE5C. Squirrel compiler uses exactly this operator-table indirection.

name: Script_ParseUnaryExpression
summary: Unary prefix parser: while the current token is 0x10f (unary operator, e.g. '-'/'!'/'~'/'++'), parses the operand recursively, emits the unary opcode (0x2c) and patches the line info; otherwise falls through to the binary expression parser (0x186B28).
evidence: if (*arg1 == 0x10f) { emit opcode 0x2c; lexer 0x5FC86C; recurse func_00186020; } else func_00186B28; line fixups via 0x1BE454/0x1BE384. 0x10f is the unary-operator keyword id used by the same compiler.

name: Script_ParsePostfixExpression
summary: Postfix expression parser: handles member access '.' (0x2e), indexing '[' ... ']' (0x5b/0x5d) and calls '(' ... ')' (0x28/0x29). For calls it counts the arguments (opcode 6 with the arg count), for indexing it emits the index opcode (0x21/0x1/0xe), and for member access it resolves the field name through the compiler table. Also inserts line-break records when a newline appears inside brackets.
evidence: handles tokens 0x5b '[' / 0x5d ']' / 0x2e '.' / 0x28 '(' / 0x29 ')' and 0x2c ','; emits opcode 6 with the argument count via 0x1BDD50; 0x185720 is called for the index/argument expressions; 0x1874EC consumes the closing tokens; 0x187780 starts the parse; line markers g_001868e8/ec/f0/f4/f8/fc.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseAnd
summary: Bitwise-AND level of the Squirrel compiler: parses the higher-precedence equality level (Script_SqCompiler_EqExp) and, while the next token is '&', pushes opcode 0x12 with sub-op 0.
evidence: Named callees Script_SqCompiler_EqExp, Sq_LexerReadToken, Script_ObjectVector_Pop/Script_IntVector_Push and maybe_Script_Compiler_PushStackOp make the parse-and-emit loop certain; the same body shape appears as the first loop of 0x001869C4.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseAndXor
summary: Bitwise-AND/OR-expression level of the Squirrel compiler: two loops, one consuming '&' and one consuming '^', each parsing an operand through the compiler's operator table and pushing opcode 0x12 with sub-op 0/3.
evidence: The body contains both loops (0x26 and 0x5E), so the first pass's XOR-only name was too narrow; the compiler-table indirect calls explain why no named caller shows up.

name: Script_ParseBinaryExpression
summary: Squirrel expression parser for the binary/bitwise level: first parses a bitwise expression, then loops on the comparison/equality keyword tokens (0x10E, 0x118, 0x137), emitting the corresponding stack opcodes (0x2B, 0x29, 0x2A) through maybe_Script_Compiler_PushStackOp and recursing on the right-hand side.
evidence: The named callees Script_ParseBitwiseExpression / Script_ParseAssignmentExpression / Script_ParseUnaryExpression surround it in the same parser block, and the body emits opcode bytes with the token constants exactly like the other recursive-descent nodes; the line fixups 0x001BE454/0x001BE384 match the compiler's error reporting.

name: Script_SqCompiler_FunctionExp
summary: Parses a Squirrel 'function name(a, b = 1) : (locals) { ... }' expression: creates the function object, binds each parameter (with optional default value), declares the optional local names and then compiles the body statement.
evidence: Creates the function with 0x1be0b4 (Script_Compiler_CreateFunction) and copies the name from the value pair (f_88/f_8c); loops while the token is not 0x29 (')') expecting identifiers via 0x1874ec (Script_SqCompiler_Expect), handling the 0x3d ('=') default-value form with 0x185720 and the 0x3a (':') local-declarations list with 0x1bd588; the body ends with 0x18927c (Script_SqCompiler_Statement), 0x1bd1a4, 0x1bdd50 (push stack op) and 0x1bdd10; tokens come from Sq_LexerReadToken@0x5fc86c. Callers: ParseStatementList, Factor and Statement of the same compiler.

name: Script_ParseStatementList
summary: Statement-list/block parser of the Squirrel compiler: parses statements until the terminator token, accepts ';' or ',' as separators and dispatches the keyword/expression handlers.
evidence: Every callee is a now-named compiler routine (Sq_LexerReadToken, Script_SqCompiler_CommaExp, Script_SqCompiler_FunctionExp, Script_ParseAssignmentExpression) and 0x1BE384 patches the statement extent; this is the statement dispatcher used by 0x185720/0x186150.

name: Ui_Window_InitHeader
summary: Initializes window title and header text from string template g_001874e8 and enables the header render node at +0x78.
evidence: Invokes string formatter func_00100188 with format g_001874e8; stores header at self->f_70; enables sub-node via func_00126290(&self->f_78, 1).

name: Script_SqCompiler_Expect
signature: void Script_SqCompiler_Expect(SqCompiler* self, SQObjectPtr* outToken, int expectedToken)
summary: The compiler's 'expect this token' primitive: if the current token differs from expectedToken it builds the Squirrel error text "expected '%s'" (token name) or "expected '%c'" (single char) through the inlined Error2 path (sprintf into the 0x100-byte compiler error buffer, then the longjmp/raise helper), then always advances the lexer. The special case (token==0x136 TK_CONSTRUCTOR, expected 0x102 IDENTIFIER) is the grammar's permission to read a constructor as an identifier. The 8-byte outToken slot is filled with the literal object only to keep the compiler's constant pool alive across the Error2 throw path.
evidence: String literals IDENTIFIER/STRING_LITERAL/INTEGER/FLOAT/'expected %s'/'expected %c' in the literal pool at 0x18775C; 0x136==TK_CONSTRUCTOR special case and 0x102==TK_IDENTIFIER follow upstream sqcompiler.cpp Expect(); lexer advance is a call to 0x005FC86C (SQLexer::Lex); Error2 helper 0x001874B4 + 0x005FFA30 (vsprintf); every parser routine (Factor 0x187780, Statement 0x18927C, 0x186CB4, 0x185720) calls it with punctuation/identifier token ids.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Factor
summary: Primary-expression parser of the Squirrel compiler: dispatches on the current token to local/outer/identifier lookups (with the 'cannot delete a local' / 'invalid constant [%s.%s]' errors), 'this' and 'constructor', numeric/string literals, array '[..]', table '{...}', class, function and lambda literals, unary - ! ~ ++ --, and parenthesised expressions; each alternative leaves one value target on the funcstate target stack. It is the bottom of the precedence chain and also the place where a statement 'expression expected' is produced.
evidence: 4716-byte switch that calls EmitInstruction (0x001BDD50) with _OP_LOAD/LOADINT/LOADBOOL/CLOSURE/GETOUTER/NEG/NOT/BWNOT opcodes and calls the nested function parser 0x00186CB4 and table/array literal builder 0x00187140; pooled strings 'this', 'constructor', 'invalid constant [%s.%s]', 'cannot delete a local', "can't delete an expression", 'expression expected' at 0x7BE695..0x7BE6BF; called only from PrefixedExpr 0x00186150, which is the upstream shape of Factor/PrefixedExpr in Squirrel 2.2 sqcompiler.cpp.

name: Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp
signature: void Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp(SqCompiler* self, u8 opcode, void (*subExpr)(SqCompiler*), u32 subExprFlags, u8 operatorByte)
summary: Shared body of the binary-operator precedence levels: advances the lexer, parses the right operand with the supplied lower-level parser, pops the two value targets from the funcstate target stack (SQFuncState::PopTarget 0x001BE454), pushes the result target (0x001BCE5C) and emits one 8-byte SQInstruction {_arg1=left, op=opcode, _arg0=target, _arg2=right, _arg3=operatorByte} via SQFuncState::AddInstruction (0x001BDD50). The caller supplies only opcode + operator byte, which is why every arithmetic level shares this one function.
evidence: Instruction layout matches Squirrel 2.2 SQInstruction (arg1 word at +0, op at +4, arg0 +5, arg2 +6, arg3 +7) as used by tools/sqbin.py's 2.2 opcode table; opcode constants 0x11 ARITH / 0x12 BITW / 0x28 CMP appear at call sites; funcstate stack helpers 0x001BE454 (PopTarget) and 0x001BCE5C (PushTarget) are visible; five callers are the operator levels 0x188A80, 0x189058, 0x1890A4, 0x189120, 0x186B28.

name: Script_SqCompiler_EqExp
summary: Equality/relational expression level: parses one shift-level expression (PrefixedExpr 0x00186150 and the inlined multiply/add/shift loops) and then folds a chain of ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= operators (and the inlined <<, >>, >>> BITW cases), emitting ARITH/BITW/CMP/EQ/NE instructions through Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp. Returns as soon as the next token is not a comparison operator.
evidence: Token tests 0x25 '%', 0x2A '*', 0x2F '/', 0x2B '+', 0x2D '-', 0x128/0x129/0x132 shifts (emitting BITW with selector 4/5/6 = BW_SHIFTL/SHIFTR/USHIFTR), then 0x3C '<' (CMP 3), 0x3E '>' (CMP 0), 0x108/0x10A/0x10B (EQ/LE/GE), opcode 0x28 CMP; called by BitwiseAndExp 0x00186904 and BitwiseXor/Or 0x001869C4/0x00185E18, matching the upstream BitwiseOr->Xor->And->EqExp chain.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Compile
summary: Top-level compile driver: creates the root SQFuncState named 'main' (0x001BE56C ctor), registers 'this' as local 0 and 'unknown' as the source name, then loops Script_SqCompiler_Statement until end of file or a stray '}', enforcing 'end of statement expected (; or lf)' between statements. It finishes the function with a RETURN instruction (opcode 0x13) and copies the resulting closure into outClosure; on a lexer/compile error it reports through the compiler's longjmp error path.
evidence: Pooled strings 'main', 'this', 'unknown', 'end of statement expected (; or lf)'; calls SQFuncState ctor 0x001BE56C and dtor 0x001BE7AC, Statement 0x0018927C, AddInstruction 0x001BDD50 with op 0x13 RETURN; emits CLOSURE via 0x001BC808 and assigns g_00189054 as the closure's value; only caller is 0x00163254 (the public sq_compile entry).

name: Script_SqCompiler_MulExp
summary: Multiplicative precedence level: parses a prefixed expression (0x00186150) and then loops over '*', '/' and '%' calling Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp with opcode ARITH and the next-level parser; the loop is the only operator group it accepts, so it is the isolated MultExp of the grammar (the other levels were inlined into their callers).
evidence: Only tokens 0x2A '*', 0x2F '/', 0x25 '%' are tested; opcode 0x11 ARITH; sub-parser pointer taken from the static level table at 0x7354BC (+0x38); no direct callers because it is only referenced from that table (0x001890A0 = 0x7354BC).

name: Script_SqCompiler_PlusExp
summary: Additive precedence level: parses a prefixed expression, then folds the multiplicative group (*, /, %) by delegating to Script_SqCompiler_MulExp through the compiler's static level table, then loops over '+' and '-' emitting ARITH instructions. Equivalent to upstream PlusExp with MultExp inlined at the start.
evidence: Two loops: 0x25/0x2A/0x2F with table entry +0x38 (=0x00186150 PrefixedExpr) followed by 0x2B '+'/0x2D '-' with entry +0x30 (=0x00189058 MulExp); opcode 0x11 ARITH; level table at 0x7354BC.

name: Script_SqCompiler_ShiftExp
summary: Shift precedence level: after the inlined multiply/add levels it loops over '<<', '>>' and '>>>' (tokens 0x128/0x129/0x132) and emits BITW instructions with selectors BW_SHIFTL=4, BW_SHIFTR=5, BW_USHIFTR=6. This is the last level before EqExp in the precedence chain.
evidence: Token 0x128/0x129/0x132 with EmitBinaryExp(0x12 BITW, ..., 4/5/6); sub-level entry +0x28 of table 0x7354BC; the BW selector values match tools/sqbin.py/OPS and upstream sqopcodes.h BW_SHIFTL..BW_USHIFTR.

name: Script_SqCompiler_CommaExp
summary: Comma (sequence) expression: parses one full expression with 0x00185720, then while the token is ',' drops the previous value target from the funcstate stack, advances the lexer and recurses. Used for expression lists that keep only the last value (for-loop increment clauses, parenthesised comma expressions).
evidence: 44-byte body: call 0x00185720 (Expression), loop on token 0x2C ',', call SQFuncState::PopTarget 0x001BE454, Lex 0x005FC86C, self-recursion; called from Statement 0x0018927C, Factor 0x00187780 and the function-statement emitter 0x00187140.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Statement
summary: The compiler's statement parser: one huge switch over all statement keywords - block, local declaration/assignment, expression statement, if/else, while, do/while, for, foreach, switch/case/default, break/continue (with the "'break' has to be in a loop block" checks), return, function declaration, class declaration (synthesising the @INDEX@/@ITERATOR@ metamethods), try/catch/throw and yield. It maintains the SQFuncState stack size/scope depth and emits the corresponding jumps and instructions.
evidence: 10548-byte switch; pooled strings 'end of statement expected (; or lf)', '@INDEX@', '@ITERATOR@', "'break' has to be in a loop block", "'continue' has to be in a loop block", 'cannot create a class in a local with the syntax(class <local>)'; calls Expression 0x00185720, CommaExp 0x00189228, Expect 0x001874EC, AddInstruction 0x001BDD50 and SetInstructionParam 0x001BE384; called from Compile 0x00188C9C and from function bodies 0x00186CB4.

name: Script_SqValueList_GetItem
signature: int Script_SqValueList_GetItem(SqValueList* self, u32 arg2, int index, SQObjectPtr* out)
summary: Element accessor for the Squirrel value list: tests whether slot index of the value array is the tagged null (0x01000001) and, if not, copies it into the caller's SQObjectPtr; returns whether a value was copied.
evidence: The body was already fully readable and consistent with a GetItem slot, and its caller is now the named maybe_Script_SqValueList_CtorB; Script_ObjectPtr_Assign is named, so the copy is confirmed, though the unused arg2 still prevents a perfect signature.

name: Gfx_Node_Attach
summary: Attaches a scene graph node and all its child components to the active scene graph, updating child transformation links.
evidence: Invokes virtual method +0xC on self->f_1c, iterates over children array self + 0x2C calling func_00245C80, and links into parent scene via func_00245C40/func_00245C1C.

name: Gfx_Node_Release
summary: Decrements reference counter on scene graph node; when the counter reaches zero, invokes virtual destructor and deallocates memory.
evidence: Reference counting release pattern: increments guard, calls callback at node[9], decrements node[1]; if 0 calls virtual dtor (*node[0]) and frees via func_00147AEC.

name: Gfx_Node_DetachChild
summary: Detaches and releases child node pointer at field 0x1C, decrementing the child reference count and destroying it if zero.
evidence: Reads self->f_1c, decrements refcount at offset 4, calls child virtual dtor +8 if refcount reaches zero, and clears self->f_1c.

name: Script_SqValueList_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the Squirrel value-list holder: installs vtable 0x007589F4, clears the two link/refcount words and default-constructs the single 8-byte SQObjectPtr at +0x2C. Byte-identical twin of 0x0018BE68, i.e. the two template copies emitted for two different owners.
evidence: NEW: the destructor 0x0018BF48 (maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor) and the accessor 0x0018BBB0 (Script_SqValueList_GetItem, 0.50) both use the same vtable 0x007589F4 and the same 8-byte SQObjectPtr element at +0x2C, which fixes the class; the ctor shape (vtable + one inline element) is unambiguous, so the name is promoted while the A/B twin suffix is kept because the two addresses are separate template copies.

name: Script_SqValueList_CtorB
summary: Second, byte-identical constructor of the Squirrel value-list holder (same vtable 0x007589F4, same single 8-byte SQObjectPtr at +0x2C): the 'B' copy emitted for the other owner.
evidence: NEW: same vtable and same element as the now-named destructor/accessor pair (0x0018BF48, 0x0018BBB0), and the body is byte-identical to 0x0018BD88 - the only open question is which owner this template copy belongs to, which is why it keeps the B suffix rather than a class name.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a refcounted value-array holder: installs vtable 0x007589F4, unlinks itself from its owner (0x00245C40), releases the refcounted block at +0x1C and, when it was the last reference, resets every 8-byte element to the shared null value and releases the old one; then destroys the element array through std_destroy_range with the refcount release 0x001BF798 and installs the base vtable 0x0075A728.
evidence: The element destructor 0x001BF798 is now the confident Gfx_Node_RefPtr_Release (0.90) - a generic refcount release, not specifically SQObjectPtr - so the 'Squirrel value' reading rests on the vtable pair 0x007589F4/0x0075A728 and the 0x8000000 tag bit. The body also carries unaff_r7 (a mis-decoded global load of the shared null value), so the maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_Node_AttachSingleChild
summary: Attaches a single-child scene graph node to the active scene and updates parent linkage.
evidence: Invokes virtual method +0xC on child self->f_18, links to parent via func_00245C40, registers with scene via func_00245C1C.

name: Gfx_Node_DetachSingleChild
summary: Detaches single child at field 0x18, decrementing its reference count and invoking its destructor if zero.
evidence: Decrements *(self->f_18 + 4); if zero calls (*self->f_18 + 8)(); clears self->f_18.

name: Gfx_Node_DtorBase
summary: Base destructor for GfxNode objects; unlinks from parent node at offset 0x14 and releases child reference at offset 0x18.
evidence: Unlinks node from parent list via func_00245C40(self[5]+0x48, self), decrements child refcount self[6], and invokes child dtor if refcount reaches zero.

name: maybe_Spell_ResolveRecordRef

name: maybe_Skill_ResolveRecordRef

summary: Builds a skill record reference: stores the low byte of the skill id at out+0 and the SkillRecord pointer from 0x0063D018(dm, skillId) at out+4. Callers then read the description message id or the MP cost (+0xEE) from that pointer.

FACTS.md confirms 0x0063D018 is the SkillRecord getter (dm->f_2BC, stride 0x100). No caller, so it stays maybe_.

name: Container_SortIdsByName
summary: Insertion-sorts a u16 id array by display name using Container_CompareIdNames.
evidence: Bulk-sorts with func_0071D530 then insertion-sorts with the comparator func_0018C4C0, exactly the same structure as the 8-byte record sorts 0x17AF74/0x17B074 but for 2-byte ids. The comparator resolves both ids through func_0061BD4C and compares the name records, so the ordering is by name.

name: Container_CompareIdNames
signature: u32 Container_CompareIdNames(u16* arg1, u16* b, u16* arg3)
summary: Compares two ids by their resolved name records; returns 1 when a sorts after b and 0 otherwise, with missing records sorting last.
evidence: Calls func_0061BD4C(&recA,*a) and func_0061BD4C(&recB,*b), then compares CONCAT22(recA->f_e,idA) <= CONCAT22(recB->f_e,idB). func_0061BD4C is the id-to-name-record resolver used by the message code, so f_e is the name comparison key.

name: Text_BuildFallbackGlyphList
summary: Builds and sorts the fallback glyph table: fills the inline array with 118 consecutive character codes 0x0AA3..0x0B19 and sorts them with the shared id comparator.
evidence: The 0x76-iteration loop writing i+0xAA3 into the inline array, the begin/current/end pointers and the Container_SortIdsByName call are all explicit.

name: Text_GetLayoutStats
summary: Lazily builds the text-layout object (vtable 0x7829CC), then walks every entry and writes four counters: entry count, entry count from the layout page, empty-span count and total non-empty spans.
evidence: Disassembly shows the two per-entry calls to 0x18D5A0 only return 0/1 (a content test) and the results are summed and counted, so this is a statistics pass, not a 'measure cache'.

name: Text_GlyphCache_Compact
signature: void Text_GlyphCache_Compact(TextGlyphCache* cache, int lo, int hi)
summary: Compacts the 255-entry text glyph cache: removes every entry equal to the current sentinel, shifts survivors down with memcpy and zero-fills the tail.
evidence: 0x18-byte entries, the three-word key comparison against the sentinel, the 0x11-byte survivor copy and the 0xFF-entry bound are all visible; the sole caller is the cache lookup.

name: Text_GlyphCache_FindOrInsert
summary: Looks a three-word key up in the text glyph/metric cache; on a hit it refreshes the entry's use counter and returns it, on a miss it compacts the cache, inserts the new entry and returns the default weight 1.
evidence: Scans the 0xff entries (0x18 bytes, stride 6 ints, end = arg1 + 0x5fa*4) comparing the three key words; on a hit clamps the use counter at *(u8*)(entry+0x10)+1 and calls 0x18c85c (compact) before storing back; the miss path also compacts, finds the sentinel entry (piRam0018cbac) and memcpys the 0x11-byte record in with 0x116c10. Only caller Text_LayoutLine_AutoSize@0x2fcfd4.

name: maybe_Text_InitLineCache
signature: void maybe_Text_InitLineCache(TextLine* lines, const TextLine* source)
summary: Resets 255 text-line records (0x18 bytes each) and then copies the first 0x11 bytes of each record from a source template: it re-initialises the message-line cache from a template rather than merely clearing it.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now maybe_Ui_ResetLargeScreenState and maybe_Text_MeasureOverflow, both of which use the line cache; the old 'ClearLineBuffer' understated the template copy, hence the rename. Neither caller is confident and the record layout is still inferred, so maybe_.

name: Text_ResolveStyleBlock
summary: Resolves a 16-word text style block: fills the 7-wchar name at +4 from party member 0 when empty, refreshes level (+0x38) and three global bytes (+0x34/+0x3D/+0x3E), allocates the formatted name buffer and returns whether anything changed. maybe_Text_UpdateStyleParams calls it before 0x00613F14 applies the block to the text object.
evidence: Disassembly shows wcslen (0x00100B74) is a CRT call, not a noreturn throw (FACTS trap), followed by the name copy from member+0xCA, level from member+0xD8, allocations through 0x0011CFAC/0x00116AE0 and a changed-flag return. N_010/N_022 context describes the same function as the style resolver called from 0x00193248. This is text/style code, not item code.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA(void* self, const TextEntry* entry, u32 word0, u32 word1)
summary: Text-layout span builder: a 552-byte routine with a push {r4-r8,lr} prologue that fills a stack span record, guarded by style < 7 and a non-empty span, before calling the text layout helpers. Ghidra truncates it after the first call, so only the shape is known.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x0018CEA4 really starts with the ARM push and the style/span guard, but the readable C is a single mis-marked wcslen call - a damaged decompilation. Its twin is 0x0018D24C (same family), so the span-builder wording is kept as a maybe_ description.

name: Text_InitStringRef
signature: void Text_InitStringRef(TextRef* out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 textId)
summary: Fills a three-word text reference: two caller-supplied words plus the resolved handle from func_0051BB08(textId, 0xE, -1).

name: Pack_FindRecordByIndex

name: Text_SetArgsFromCharacterLook
signature: void Text_SetArgsFromCharacterLook(CharacterLook* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)

The part-index biases and the pack lookups are unchanged. The decompilation is damaged only in the trailing register argument of the Message_SetArg calls (unaff_r4); every argument index and every value is intact, so the verdict rests on the readable calls rather than on the damaged register.

name: Ui_ApplyCharacterLookParamsEx

name: maybe_Ui_PickWeightedKeyValue
summary: Picks a weighted-random slot from a four-entry key and returns a random value inside that slot's range: Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng(key, 4, 0) chooses the slot, the two range accessors 0x0015FA90/0x0015D13C give its first and last index, and the game RNG at (work+8)+0x98 is reduced modulo (last-first+1) and added to first.
evidence: 0x005F9650 is now the confident Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng (0.55, a weighted random index over the passed weights), so the first pass's 'hashes the first four u16' reading was wrong - this is a random pick, not a hash. The game RNG at work+0x98 (FACTS.md) supplies the value. The caller maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_InitMemberTables does not pin the class, so the maybe_ stays.

name: Math_RandomPercent
summary: Returns a random value in 0..99. 0x0051B1FC pulls the next value from one of the two RNG states in the game work (+0xC8 when stream==0, +0xE0 otherwise) and 0x0011CD80 is the idivmod helper; the remainder (r1) is what comes back. Nothing here counts or sizes list slots.
evidence: 0x0011CD80 is the ARM idivmod helper: 0x001BA510 reads its r1 (extraout_r1+0x78) to build a random 120..210 offset, and 0x001D5A10 uses rand%3+2 frames. Divide by 100 and return the remainder is rand()%100, so 'Ui_ItemList_GetSlotCount' was wrong.

name: maybe_Data_SelectRecordIdByWeight
summary: Random weighted pick between two record ids: draws a random float (0x0051B1FC + VectorSignedToFloat, scaled by g_0018E2A4/g_0018E2A8) and compares it with three floats read from the records named by spec[1]/spec[3] to choose spec[0], spec[3], the constant 6, or a value produced by maybe_Party_FormatStatValue.
evidence: Re-read of the full 1204-byte body: every branch is a random draw compared against record floats and ends in maybe_Party_FormatStatValue(id, id, flag, ...) or returns a record byte. Nothing allocates or writes text, so the old 'Party_BuildStatText' was wrong; what the ids mean is still open, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PickWeightedStepIndex
summary: Picks a weighted-random index inside the object's [f_a, f_b] range: it builds the fixed weight table {0, 400, 200, 150, 100, 50, 40, 10}, zeroes every entry outside the range, calls Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng(table, 8, 0) and clamps the result back into [f_a, f_b].
evidence: Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng is now confident (0.55) and the eight values are used as *weights* for an index pick, not as sizes - the function returns an index in [f_a, f_b], so 'PickSizeStep' described the table values rather than the result. No caller pins the consumer, so the maybe_ stays.

name: Party_BuildStatusPanelData

evidence: New caller context: maybe_Ui_MemberTable_Init (0x004AC46C) calls this once per row and copies the 16 words at local_f8 into its own layout block, which confirms that "out" is panel row data rather than a scratch buffer. Callees Game_GetDataManager/Game_GetWork/std_wcsncpy were already named.

name: maybe_Ui_IsMenuOpen
summary: Returns 1 only when the UI root singleton has an active object (0x00383A80) and the menu query 0x0062A38C on the save work is non-zero. Window visibility code uses the answer to pick its dimmed row alpha.

name: Item_PickRandomByCategory

The candidate list is then randomly indexed with func_0051B1FC(actorId,0x7fffffff) and func_0011CD80; returns 0xa4 when nothing is found. Called from the item reward/drop path 0x18D7C4.

name: maybe_Party_RemoveDuplicateIds

Kept maybe_ because the vtable tail is unrecovered.

name: Ui_ItemList_RemoveItem

name: Battle_Unit_ClampStatSigned
summary: Retrieves maximum stat boundary via virtual method +8 on unit and clamps value between 0 and maximum.

name: Battle_Unit_ClampStatUnsigned
summary: Retrieves maximum unsigned stat boundary via virtual method +8 on unit and clamps value.

name: Ui_ItemList_RemoveMatching

name: Party_Member_ClearEquipSlots

name: Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot

summary: Equips the item at member inventory slot invSlot (member+0xEC+invSlot*2) into equipment slot equipSlot (0..5 at member+0x11C..+0x121), handling 2H/dual-wield weapon/shield conflicts via 0x00191470, recalculating stats, and returning 1 on success or 0 if invalid.

Reads u16 itemId = *(u16*)(member+0xEC+invSlot*2), rejects 0xFFFF, looks up Item_LookupRecord, switches on equipSlot 0..5 (main hand, off-hand with itemRec->u8_29 2H/dual-wield unequip via 0x191470, head 0x66C978, body 0x66C950, accessories 4..5 0x66C184), writes (s8)invSlot to member->s8_11C[equipSlot], refreshes stats (0x191E3C / 0x19201C), and returns 1.

name: Party_Member_UnequipSlotAndRefresh
summary: Unequips equipment slot `equipSlot` of a party member and refreshes the derived state: returns 1 when something was actually unequipped, in which case it also re-compacts the inventory (func_00191E3C) and recalculates the member's stats.

The old signature typed the member as TextPage* and the slot as a text cell; the body never touches text, so that was a misread of the same helper trio as 0x001901F4.

name: Text_CopyLayoutWithOffset
summary: Snapshots the current text layout, subtracts the block's own origin from the ten exported 16-bit coordinates and stores the shifted 0xEA-byte copy back over +0x1DC.

name: Party_Member_AddExp
summary: Adds experience points to party member (+0xDC), clamps to EXP cap 9,999,999 (0x0072739C), checks level growth table (0x0063E7F8), increments level (+0xD8), triggers Party_Member_RecalculateStats (0x0019201C), and fires story/progress event work+0x24A98 vt[8](0x20D).
evidence: Loads EXP cap 9999999 from 0x0072739C; calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats (0x0019201C) on level increase.

name: Party_Member_ApplyPageContent
signature: void Party_Member_ApplyPageContent(void* self, const void* src, int mode)
summary: Applies one page of a party member record: resets the page glyph/width tables, copies the layout block and typing state from src, runs the text layout pass, and then reconciles the member's 24 inventory slots at +0xEC against the static id table 0x00190F10 - matching slots are removed (or un-equipped through 0x00191470) and re-marked 0xFFFF.
evidence: Corrected: the body is not pure text code - it is called by Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord (0.55) and by the two Text_Page builders, and after the layout pass it walks the member inventory (24 u16 at +0xEC, the FACTS.md member-inventory block), tests each slot with func_006292A4 (the six-byte equipped-slot list at +0x11C) and clears/un-equips matches, so it is item/equipment code on the member page.

name: Text_Page_BuildAtOffset
signature: void Text_Page_BuildAtOffset(TextPage* self, int offset, const u16* posDelta)
summary: Builds the page's 0xEA-byte layout block at an arbitrary pen position: starts from the current coordinates, adds the optional 10-short delta, copies the two glyph arrays and writes the resulting run.
evidence: The pen-origin selection, the five packed coordinate additions, the two glyph array copies and Text_Page_SetContent are all explicit.

name: Actor_GetEquipAppearanceType
summary: Maps a member's equipped items to an appearance type: reads the two equipped item ids (slots 0 and 1), maps the first item's category byte (+0x29) to 1..15 and bumps it by one when both items share the category; returns 0xFF when nothing is equipped and 0 for the special actor ids 8 and 0x1E.
evidence: NEW: the item accessors are the FACTS.md ones - func_006292F0(member, slot) is the equipped item id and Item_LookupRecord resolves the row - and the switch is on ItemRecord+0x29, the equip category from FACTS.md. Three named callers (Battle_SkillTarget_Update, Field_CreateActorRenderObject, Field_FindActorEntryByModel) use the result as an appearance selector; 0.55.

name: Party_Member_MoveInventoryToBag
summary: Empties a party member's 24-slot inventory into the item bag: walks the used slots from the top down, unequips and recalculates the member for slots that are equipped, shifts the remaining ids left so the array stays compact, and adds every id to the bag at work+0x24ACC with ItemBag_AddItemCount(bag, id, 1).
evidence: NEW: the old name said 'compact', but the body adds every id to the bag - func_00612008 is ItemBag_AddItemCount (disassembly: it scans the 4-byte entries in [bag+0x2B8, bag+0x274C) for the id and does `ldrb count,[entry+2]; count += delta; strb`), and the equipped branch unequips + recalculates before the add. The only caller is the SQCommand native 0x0015179C, i.e. a script command that clears a member's inventory. func_00191E3C (called in the equipped branch) is the equipped-first re-compaction: it saves the 24 ids and 6 equip slots, clears both, then rewrites the inventory in equip-slot order.

name: Text_Page_ExportLayout
summary: Copies the page's render state into a caller-supplied run: pen position (+0xDC), the four coordinates at +0x1C8..+0x1D8, the 0x78-byte glyph array at +0x122, the 0x1C-byte array at +0x1A2, the eight colour words at +0xEC..+0x108 and the cell-flag bytes at +0x11C..+0x121. Pure field copy, no calls except memmove.
evidence: New context: the only caller is the now named maybe_Text_CopyLayoutWithOffset (0x00190980), whose summary says it snapshots and rebuilds the layout block through this function, so the export/snapshot role is confirmed by the caller. Not item code: the copied fields are glyph ids/colours, not item ids (no Item_LookupRecord, no 0xEC inventory access) - the waiver is stated here because the name contains 'Text'.

name: Party_Member_UnequipInventorySlot
summary: Removes inventory slot index invSlot (0..23) from any of the member's six equipment slots (member+0x11C..+0x121) that reference it (setting them to -1 and clearing paired 2H/dual-wield off-hand +0x11D when needed), returning 1 if unequipped or 0 if not equipped.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x191470..0x191680: second arg is inventory slot index (0..23), NOT equipSlot (0..5)! Loops i = 0..5 comparing s8[member+0x11C+i] == invSlot; on match sets slot to -1 (0xFF), handles main-hand/off-hand pairing, notifies Ui_Overlay_PlayElementSe, and returns 1. Called by maybe_Member_RemoveItemAtSlot (0x1901F4) and Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot (0x1905E4).

name: Party_ValidateEquipment
summary: Re-validates the six quick-equipment slots at +0x11c, dropping entries whose item is no longer owned and recalculating stats.
evidence: When world+0x27719 is set, loops i=0..5 over the signed byte self->f_11c[i], resolves the referenced u16 equipment id at self+0xec, checks func_0066C434 and func_00191470, then calls func_00191E3C and func_0019201C. The same six-slot array is cleared by Ui_Equipment_ClearSlots.

name: Text_Page_Reset
summary: Resets a text page: clears the glyph arrays (30 and 20 entries) to 0xff, stores the new style byte and reinitialises the page's line/offset state.
evidence: Calls 0x193bac, 0x10f11c(self+200), stores *(u8*)(self+200) = style, then two loops writing 0xff over the 2-byte entries starting at f_129b (0x1e iterations) and f_1273 (0x14 iterations), and finally sets f_e5 = 0xff, f_12e4 = 1 and clears f_12d8..f_12e8. Callers 0x19180c, Text_Page_Ctor@0x192450, Ui_Window_ResetState@0x35f814.

name: Party_Member_InitFromMasterRecord
signature: void Party_Member_InitFromMasterRecord(PartyMember* member, int charaId, int* nameBlock, int* record)
summary: Initialises a party member structure from master character data: copies the 7-character name wchar array to member+0xCA, equips default items, compacts inventory, and invokes Party_Member_RecalculateStats (0x0019201C).
evidence: Copies 7 wchars to member+0xCA (verified in FACTS.md); indexes inventory slots and calls 0x0019201C.

name: Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord
signature: void Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord(void* member, const u8* args)
summary: Fills a party member's 24 u16 inventory slots (+0xEC) from a party record: computes the page count through the text layout, saves and restores the layout state, blanks the six equipment slots (+0x11C), then copies each supplied item id into the next inventory slot - clearing the text cell of a slot first when func_006292A4 reports it as equipped - and finally refreshes the member's text page.
evidence: The caller SQCommand (0x0015179C) resolves the member with func_0035EB98 and compacts the equipment first; the body then writes the established member-inventory array at +0xEC and clears the six equipment bytes at +0x11C, so this is a party-inventory setup, not a 'text page build'.

name: Member_SetItemAtSlot
signature: void Member_SetItemAtSlot(PartyMember* member, int slot, u16 itemId)
summary: Writes an item id into inventory slot `slot` of a party member (member+0xEC + slot*2): when the slot is currently equipped it unequips it first through Party_Member_UnequipInventorySlot, then stores the id and, if anything was unequipped, refreshes the derived data (0x00191E3C) and recalculates the member's stats.
evidence: FACTS.md fixes the member inventory as 24 u16 ids at member+0xEC and func_006292A4 as the 'slot is equipped' test, and the body is exactly that: equipped test, unequip, `*(u16*)(member + slot*2 + 0xec) = itemId`, then Party_Member_RecalculateStats. All 13 named callers are inventory operations (Party_Member_EquipInventorySlot, Party_Member_MoveInventoryToBag, Ui_ItemList_RemoveItem, Party_ValidateEquipment...).

name: Member_SwapInventorySlots
signature: u32 Member_SwapInventorySlots(PartyMember* first, int slotA, PartyMember* b, int slotB)
summary: Swaps the item ids in two party-member inventory slots (member+0xEC + slot*2): unequips either slot first when it is equipped, exchanges the two u16 ids, then refreshes both members and recalculates the stats of whichever member had something unequipped. Always returns 1.
evidence: FACTS.md fixes the member inventory at member+0xEC and func_006292A4 as the equipped test; the body reads both slots, unequips the equipped ones, exchanges the two u16 values and calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats on each side. The only caller (maybe_Ui_EquipRow_UpdateCompareText) is an equipment-comparison UI path, which fits a slot swap.

name: Party_Member_RecalculateStats
summary: Full party member stat recalculation pass: recalculates max HP (+0x10), max MP (+0x12), base attack (+0x1A), defense (+0x1E), agility (+0x22), deftness (+0x26), charm (+0x2A), magical might (+0x2C), magical mending (+0x30), walks 60 skills (+0x129C) and 40 spells (+0x1274), and recalculates equipment modifiers.
evidence: Called on level-up and equip changes; iterates skills at +0x129C and spells at +0x1274; writes combat stats.

name: Party_Member_LearnSkillOrSpell
signature: u32 Party_Member_LearnSkillOrSpell(PartyMember* member, u32 id, u8* outLearned, u16* arg4)
summary: Learns a new spell or skill: checks if the id is already in the member's 40-spell (+0x1274) or 60-skill (+0x129C) array, appends to the first available slot (0xFF), and triggers stat recalculation.
evidence: Searches 0xFF sentinel in skill/spell tables at +0x1274/+0x129C; calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats.

name: Party_Member_InitEquipSlots
summary: Initialises the member's 6 equipment index slots (+0x11C) and resets active combat state pointers.
evidence: Initialises 6 equipment slot indices to -1/0xFF; part of member initialization.

name: Party_Member_RecalcStatsFromCommand
signature: void Party_Member_RecalcStatsFromCommand(void* self, u32 arg2, int command)
summary: Recalculates party member stats on specific menu/story command: walks active party members and triggers Party_Member_RecalculateStats.
evidence: Checks command id 9; walks active party members and calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats (0x0019201C).

name: Item_MarkOwnedVariants
summary: For the given item id and each of its variant ids (base from func_0066C368, count at record+0x10) sets the corresponding bit in the 2880-bit per-item ownership mask at saveWork+0x4B30.
evidence: The body sets bits at +0x4B30 with the (id >> 5, bit id & 0x1F) layout established in FACTS.md for the per-item ownership bitmask, and iterates base..base+count through the named func_0066C368 variant helper; the 'FieldState' parameter label was wrong (it is the save work), which is corrected in the signature.

name: maybe_Text_DecodeName
summary: Copies a 0x84-byte text record, decodes it through the text/font throw path and stores the two result bytes into out[0]/out[1].
evidence: NEW: the caller PartyStatus_LoadNewestRecord shows it runs while loading a party-status record, but the 0x84-byte layout matches several text records and the two result bytes are still unexplained. maybe_ at 0.3.

name: Text_Style_Decode
summary: Decodes a packed 0x84-byte text-style record into the style object's fields, validating it through the shared text error routine first.
evidence: Clears a 0x84-byte stack copy, memcpys the caller's record with std_memcpy@0x116c10, calls 0x18cea4 (maybe_Text_Throw, the style validator) and then copies the 17 decoded words out to self+2..+0x40. Recovered entry point; neighbours are the Text_/Party_ helpers and the same 0x84-byte record size is used by 0x1114a4.

name: Text_Style_Create
summary: Allocates and initialises a default text style object: zeroes the counters, constructs the embedded font-name field and sets the seven-character default name.
evidence: result = 0x192780() (the 0x60-byte style allocator); f_5c = 0; 0x6722c4(&result->f_44) (name-field ctor); f_4e/f_52/f_56/f_5a = 0; std_wcsncpy(&f_4e, g_00192824, 7). Three callers copy the object around (0x193018, 0x19317c, 0x192f84).

name: Item_Equip_CheckRequirements
summary: Validates equipment compatibility and attribute requirements for the specified item against character parameters.
evidence: Evaluates item attribute flags and checks requirement conditions via memory allocator helper func_0011FFFC.

name: Party_RecalcAllMembersStats
summary: Unconditionally recalculates combat stats for all party members in the active party list.
evidence: Walks party roster and calls Party_Member_RecalculateStats on each member.

name: Party_ValidateEquipmentNames
signature: void Party_ValidateEquipmentNames(Actor* self, int command, int arg3)
summary: Re-applies every party member's font record and, when the equipment-change command 0x211 arrives with a non-zero flag, additionally revalidates all six equipment slots of all 31 members: for each slot it looks up the item record of the equipped id and clears/refreshes the member's name cells when the record changed.
evidence: The body is the same member loop as Party_ApplyFontsOnCommand plus a six-slot validation loop that uses Item_LookupRecord and the established equipment-slot array at +0x11C; nothing recalculates stats, so the old 'RecalcEquipment' was misleading.

name: Battle_Unit_ResetTurnState
summary: Resets turn status fields 0x0F through 0x1D to zero and clears temporary combat modifier flags.
evidence: Zeroes fields self[0x0F] through self[0x1D] sequentially, followed by clearing temporary turn buffers with func_00116AE0.

name: Text_StyleList_Insert
summary: Inserts a fresh default style at the given index of the five-entry style list: shifts the following 0x44-byte records down and writes the new default record into the freed slot.
evidence: If arg2 < 5 it memmoves (4-arg2) records of 0x44 bytes from self + (index+1)*0x44 down one slot with std_memcpy@0x116c10, then builds a default style in a stack buffer via 0x192780 and copies 0x44 bytes into self + arg2*0x44 + 0x92f4. Only caller maybe_Party_ShiftSkillSlots@0x193098, which uses the same 5 x 0x44 style array as 0x193018/0x19317c.

name: Battle_Unit_ApplyStatusEffects
summary: Checks status effect resistance flags at offsets 0x2BF1 and 0x2BF2; triggers virtual status applicator if below threshold.
evidence: Compares byte at unit + 0x2BF1 and unit + 0x2BF2 against threshold; dispatches virtual method +8 with status codes g_00192f38 and g_00192f3c.

name: maybe_Ui_InitFourTripleByteSlots
summary: Writes four 3-byte 0xFF records into the caller object at +0x9750 (the 4x3 temp array built at sp is copied there); returns nothing.
evidence: Disassembly (0x00192F84, 148 bytes) shows the temp 4x3 array of element ctor 0x00192580 being filled with 0xFF and the twelve bytes stored at self+0x9750. Nothing reads text or style data, so the old 'Text style list' reading is unsupported; only a second caller (maybe_Ui_TitleDemo_SetupPartyUnits, itself halt_baddata) hinted at UI.

name: Party_List_InsertBlankRecord
summary: Shifts the party-member record block at +0x944C up by one 0x60-byte slot and writes a freshly built default member record (0x192780, 7-wchar empty name from 0x007BE72C) into the freed position at +0x96EC.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now maybe_Party_AppendBlankMemberRecords, whose name states exactly this operation, and the 0x944C/0x96EC layout is shared with the confident Ui_PartyStatusWindow_Reset / Ui_PartyList_InsertMember functions. The old 'Ui_PartyList_Insert' hid that the inserted record is the blank/default one; the owner is the party list (not necessarily a UI window), hence the Party_ prefix.

name: maybe_Party_ShiftRecordSlots
summary: Inserts a 0x44-byte record into the five-slot array at +0x92F4: it first checks the record at +0x92F4 for the 0xFF/-1 sentinels (and measures the string at +0x92FC), then memcpy's the new record into the shifted slot, or appends it at +0x9404 when the list is full.
evidence: The stride 0x44 and the range +0x92F4..+0x9448 (five slots) are visible, but the shift count is recovered as the nonsense literal 0x78787879 (a division by 0x44 turned into a magic multiply) and the string measure 0x00100B74 (wcslen) is mis-marked noreturn, so the body is damaged and the confidence drops to 0.3 per FACTS.md. 'Skill' was an unsupported guess about the record contents, so it is dropped.

name: Ui_PartyList_InsertMember
summary: Stores a member record in the party list: with fewer than eight members it writes the 0x5D-byte record into the next free 0x60 slot, otherwise it shifts the list up and overwrites the last slot.
evidence: The body calls the now-named maybe_Party_GetMemberCount (0x62A110) and the same 0x944C/0x96EC block as Ui_PartyStatusWindow_Reset (0x19371C); the eight-slot limit and the record copy are explicit, so the list-insert reading is supported.

name: maybe_Text_UpdateStyleParams
summary: Rebuilds a text object's style from its cached copy: copies the 16 style words at self+0x8668..+0x86A4 into a local TextStyleBlock, resolves it with Text_ResolveStyleBlock and applies the result to the object through 0x00613F14.
evidence: Both callees are themselves truncated: Text_ResolveStyleBlock ends at a mis-marked wcslen, and 0x00613F14 currently has no symbol of its own (it falls inside ItemBag_SortIdList's address range, which cannot be the real caller). The 16-word cache copy and the two-stage resolve/apply call are clear, so the name stays a maybe_ description.

name: maybe_Ui_CellGrid_InitSlots
summary: Initializes 16 pre-allocated display cell slots at +0x8BC4 (stride 0xB8) using std_memcpy from default slot templates.
evidence: Loops over 16 display slots (self+0x8BC4 to +0x92F4, stride 0xB8); caller 0x00343174 is unnamed. Kept maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Ui_InitTransform
summary: Initialises a 0x24-byte transform/rectangle on the stack via 0x006722C4; control flow truncated by halt_baddata().
evidence: Initialiser call 0x006722C4 verified; subsequent body is damaged with halt_baddata(); both callers are UI code; kept tentative below 0.50.

name: maybe_Battle_Calc_DamageTable
summary: Unverified battle routine: readable body truncated by halt_baddata(); 56-byte Thumb function in battle command region.
evidence: Readable body is entirely halt_baddata(); battle neighbourhood hypothesis only; kept tentative below 0.50.

name: maybe_Battle_CopyPartyData
summary: Copies the 0x2E-word party/battle blocks from +0x8C7C down to +0x8BC4 and then stores the incoming 0x2E-word record at +0x923C.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is still Field_SceneObject_RegisterInstance, which does not own a battle party block, so the 'battle party' owner is unconfirmed; the fixed 0x2E-word stride and the 0x8BC4..0x92F4 window are explicit but what the records are is inferred.

name: Battle_Action_FindSlot
summary: Scans action queue buffer between offsets 0x944C and 0x974C for the next available battle action slot.
evidence: Compares pointer &self->f_944c against end pointer &self->f_974c; checks byte != -1 and updates field 0x561.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_ExecuteBranch
summary: Unverified battle action branch: readable body truncated by halt_baddata(); 64-byte Thumb function following action-slot search at 0x0019368C.
evidence: Readable body is entirely halt_baddata(); battle action sequence neighbourhood hypothesis only; kept tentative below 0.50.

name: SaveData_PartyContainer_Reset
summary: Resets the party roster container in save data: marks member slots empty and zeroes roster size.
evidence: Resets party roster array in save work.

name: SaveData_PartyContainer_Ctor
summary: Constructor for the save data party roster container: sets vtable and installs member list pointers.
evidence: Installs container vtable; precedes clamped HP/MP setters (0x00193B64/0x00193B88).

name: Ui_Window_ApplyModeFlags
signature: void Ui_Window_ApplyModeFlags(UiWindow* self, int mode, u32 arg3, u32 workSel)
summary: Applies a mode to two object flag bytes: mode 5 sets self+0x48, modes 1 and 2 set self+0x49 from the world flag at (work+8)+0x44, every other mode does nothing. The mode itself is never stored.
evidence: The body is exactly the two flag writes described, and the world flag at (work+8)+0x44 is the documented UI-block byte, so 'apply mode flags' is fixed even though the mode values themselves are unexplained.

name: Ui_ActionPane_Init
signature: UiActionPane* Ui_ActionPane_Init(UiActionPane* self, u32 actionId, u32 arg3, const char* name, u8 arg5)
summary: Initialises an action-pane object: installs the vtables, copies the command/name string (bounded to 15 bytes), and stores the action id, owner and style byte.
evidence: Sets self[0]=g_00193D78 and self[1]=g_00193D7C (the pane vtable pair), copies name via func_0011142C with length min(strlen+1,15), NUL-terminates, sets self[9]=arg3, self[8]=arg2 and *(u8*)(self+6)=arg5. Six callers are the named Ui_ActionPane_AnimCtor/Ui_ActionWindow_CreateChildren/Ui_ActionListWindow_InitPanes routines.

name: Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init
signature: GfxObjectDesc* Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init(GfxObjectDesc* self, u32 kind, u32 id, const char* name, u8 mode, u32 flags)
summary: Base initialiser for every named game object descriptor: installs the descriptor vtable pair (0x00193E24/0x00193E28), copies up to 15 bytes of the asset name into the inline buffer at +8, NUL-terminates it and stores kind, id, mode and flags.
evidence: All HUD/NPC/field object constructors route through it (Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4 -> this, and Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4 has 16 named callers such as Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState and Field_EnemyAiBehavior_Ctor), which makes the 'named object descriptor' role - name buffer at +8, kind word at +0x18 - solid rather than inferred.

name: Ui_CreateWindowById
signature: UiWindow* Ui_CreateWindowById(uint32_t [2] out, int layoutId, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Window factory: allocates g_00193F10 bytes from the UI heap, constructs the window object with 0x167764 for the requested layout id (0xFF means the default 0x11), registers it with the UI manager and binds it to the gold window/owner.
evidence: vtable g_00193F0C stored in out[0]; Mem_AllocAligned(g_00193F10, heap, 4); 0x167764(ptr, layoutId); 0x21F738/0x21F8B8 register; calls 0x166B2C(out[1],arg3,arg4) then vtable+0x24

summary: Destructor for the window created by 0x193E58: installs the released vtable g_00193F50, unregisters the window object from the UI manager and frees the handle.
evidence: *arg1 = g_00193F50; 0x21F8B8(manager, arg1[1]); arg1[1]=0; 0x10F6CC(arg1)

name: Script_GetIntTable1
summary: Returns an integer from the first of the three parallel script integer tables, creating/populating the table on first use.
evidence: 0x4C-byte leaf with callees 0x0011CCA0 (name lookup) and 0x00659668 (table access); identical structure to 0x00194300 and 0x0019434C, differing only in the global/table id.

name: Gfx_ResourceList_Attach
summary: Registers a graphics resource in one of the engine's sorted resource lists: builds the three-word key from the current render context, inserts the node, unlinks it from the previous list and marks it busy.
evidence: Named callers are render/resource initialisers (Gfx_ModelResource_Init, Gfx_CharShadowPass_Init, Anim_ModelLoad_ByName) that need their resource tracked, and the body manipulates the list nodes and f_E4 exactly as an attach/relink helper.

name: Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueA
signature: u32 Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueA(GfxResDesc* self, const char* key)
summary: String-keyed lookup in the resource descriptor's hash map at self->[0x90]+0x94: hashes the key (0x0011CCA0), asks the map (0x00659668) for an index and returns the u32 value stored in the parallel array at +0x90, or 0 when the key is absent. One of four identical per-table getters.
evidence: 0x0011CCA0(key) hash, 0x00659668(&self->f_90->f_94,key,hash) index, returns *(u32*)(self->f_90->f_90 + idx*4) or 0 on 0xFFFF; callers are layout/UI initialisers and 0x00194620/0x0019466C are the same pattern on other tables.

name: Container_RemoveFromGlobalList
summary: Removes an object from the global registry vector g_uniqueIdPoolTable, shifts the tail down, unlinks its +0x60 node through func_005647F8 and clears the object's f_E4 flag.
evidence: The body walks g_uniqueIdPoolTable for the object pointer, memmoves the tail down, decrements the end pointer and then unlinks obj+0x60 and clears obj->f_E4; the vtable 0x758B44 places it beside Sound_Emitter_Dtor, Sound_Listener_Dtor and Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance, which fits a shared object registry.

name: Gfx_SetGlobalBoolFlag
summary: Writes the global boolean at 0x001942FC from the second argument. A one-line setter for a render/UI feature flag; the flag is read elsewhere to gate an optional drawing pass.
evidence: Single store *(bool*)0x001942FC = (arg2 != 0); 120-byte function consists only of that write and the return.

name: Script_GetIntTable2
summary: Second of the three parallel script integer-table getters; same code as Script_GetIntTable1 with a different table id.
evidence: 0x4C bytes, callees 0x0011CCA0 and 0x00659668, byte-for-byte sibling of 0x00193F54 and 0x0019434C.

name: Script_GetIntTable3
summary: Third of the three parallel script integer-table getters; same code as Script_GetIntTable1 with a different table id.
evidence: 0x50 bytes, callees 0x0011CCA0 and 0x00659668, sibling of the two preceding getters.

name: Fs_IsBchPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the model suffix ".bch".
evidence: The literal ".bch" is stored immediately behind the function (0x001943B0) and is loaded into r1 before the std_strstr call, so the old 'Storage_IsPresent' name was wrong - this is a path-suffix test.

name: Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueB
signature: u32 Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueB(GfxResDesc* self, const char* key)
summary: Same string-keyed getter as 0x001941D4 but on the descriptor's hash map at +0x7C and its value array at +0x78; returns 0 when the key is missing. Used for the second of the four resource tables.
evidence: Identical shape: 0x0011CCA0 hash, 0x00659668(&self->f_90->f_7C, key, hash), value at self->f_90->f_78 + idx*4; callers are 0x0019466C, 0x0030ACDC, 0x003970F4, 0x003D1A08, 0x00607500, 0x0060B75C.

name: Container_AddUniqueId
signature: void Container_AddUniqueId(u32 id, u32 arg2, u32 * vec)
summary: Appends an id to a global vector unless it is already present: scans the caller's range and the global registry, and grows the vector (doubling through std_memmove) when it is full.
evidence: Scans *arg3..arg3[1] for arg1, then scans g_00194584[0..1]; if absent, pushes at g_00194584[1] (incrementing it) or, when full, calls 0x111378 (memmove) to grow. Companion of 0x194220, which removes ids from the same vector.

name: Gfx_ModelResource_FindValueByName
summary: Resolves a name inside a model resource set: strlen(name) then trie lookup in self->f_90 (+0xAC) and returns the u32 stored in the parallel array at +0xA8, or 0 when the trie reports 0xFFFF (not found).
evidence: result = strlen(name); idx = maybe_Gfx_ResourceTrie_Lookup(&self->f_90->f_ac, name, result); idx==0xFFFF -> 0 else ((u32*)self->f_90->f_a8)[idx]. Caller 0x00626AA0 passes a name and feeds the result to 0x0057D8EC(device, value, res+0x18, 1); sibling 0x001945D4 uses the second trie/array pair of the same resource set.

name: Input_GetButtonState

name: Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState

Every OpenSceneN handler calls this before its own scene-specific step.
evidence: Calls (*(self->f_2C->vptr+0x10))(), adds self->f_28 to self->f_20/f_24, switch on self->f_1D with phases 0 and 1 visible in the body (0x001EE7EC/0x001ED5DC for phase 0, 0x006F229C + timer compare for phase 1); callers 0x001A0130, 0x001A0AE4, 0x001A0FC8, 0x001A1218, 0x001A14EC, 0x001A1DBC, 0x001A20CC.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_Step5

name: Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2
summary: Scene-transition handler for scene slot 2: at state 9 it checks 0x0036175C(self->f_60,2), commits the slot, applies the scene's camera/fade descriptor (+0x114/+0x116/+0x117) and the sound state, then lets the shared advance run. This is the 'enter field scene 2' step of the flow.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_OpenSceneField

name: Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene5
summary: Scene-transition handler for scene slot 5: at state 9, when 0x0036175C(self->f_60,5) reports the slot ready, it commits it, sets the 2D mode and the message descriptor, resizes the field object (maybe_Field_ResizeObject 0x001EB390) and advances the state.

name: Ui_Window_CloseDefault

summary: Scene-transition handler for scene slot 0: at state 9 it commits slot 0 (0x0036175C/0x00360254), initialises the battle/scene 2D layer (0x0020713C with the descriptor at +0x146/+0x94), sets the draw mode and starts the fade; the most common entry point of the flow.

name: Field_ResetScreenState

evidence: New context: the body is written entirely against the now-named Gfx_GetContext() block and the callers are Field_ApplySceneFade and Field_DestroyScene, so 'reset screen state on scene change' is supported; the mode-to-flag table itself is still read out of the code, not from a document.

name: Ui_Scene_AdvanceState
summary: Runs one tick of a UI scene object: updates the fade timers, and when the key/state conditions allow it closes the current sub-view, saves the previous state and moves to state 0x13 before ticking the scene vtable.

name: maybe_Snd_StopUiStream
summary: 28-byte forwarder: fetches the game work and calls 0x005F972C on the object at work+0x10.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceCutscene

The decompilation is truncated (bad instruction data / halt_baddata), which keeps it at maybe_ 0.32.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene3
summary: Scene-transition handler for scene slot 3: at state 9, when the slot is ready, commits it, looks the scene's 2D graphic set up through 0x0063EFB0 (index at self->f_B0+299) and binds it with 0x006103AC, then configures the camera (0x002F587C) and advances.

name: maybe_Ui_NotifyCore
