name: Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownObjects
summary: Releases the scene's runtime objects in the order effect -> item list -> scene manager -> camera -> 2D layer (0x0035F870, 0x005F9828 on two streams, 0x001C987C, 0x001C9568, 0x001C849C, 0x001C7DE8, 0x001C70F8, 0x001C7694, 0x003615A8). Returns 1; used as the 'close scene' step.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_Apply2dCommonPack
summary: Loads/keeps the shared 2dcmn.pack set for the current scene mode: shows the matching UI layer (1/2/3/4) and, when the pack is not loaded in this mode, asks the pack manager to load '2dcmn.pack', binds it to the 2D screen and runs the scene continuation.
evidence: The pooled string '2dcmn.pack' at 0x001A275C is the direct evidence, and the named callees (Gfx_Effect2D_LoadCommonPack, Pack_HandleTable_Acquire, Fs_NamedObject_LoadAndAdd) show the load path; sole caller 0x001A04A4.

name: Ui_Hud_HideSequence
summary: Step-driven HUD hide used when a full-screen message/menu opens: hides the cursor, waits for the layout animation, sets the render flag, unloads the common pack and finally clears the ten HUD element flags at +0x114..+0x11D.
evidence: Named callees Gfx_GetContext, Pack_GetManager, Ui_LoadingScreen_IsFinished and Ui_GetCore now cover every step of the state machine, and its mirror maybe_Ui_Hud_ShowSequence is documented as the inverse.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_Release2dCommonPack
summary: Counterpart of the 2dcmn.pack loader: releases the item list, message window, 2D screen and scene system, unloads the shared 2dcmn.pack when it is still mounted and resets the layer render modes.
evidence: Named callees (Gfx_Effect2D_ReleasePack, Pack_HandleTable_ReleaseObjects, Ui_SceneFlow_SetLayerVisible, Field_Level_ResetRuntime) plus the pack-manager test 0x006456A4(pack,5) confirm the 2dcmn.pack release path; callers 0x0019F908 and 0x001A04A4.

name: Ui_Hud_ShowSequence
summary: Step-driven restore of the HUD after a full-screen overlay (the mirror of Ui_Hud_HideSequence 0x001A27B0): advances the state at f_18 through the five UI/pack steps and finishes by setting all ten HUD element flags f_114..f_11D back to 1 and re-enabling the cursor.
evidence: New context: the mirror function 0x001A27B0 is named Ui_Hud_HideSequence and the two have the same five-step skeleton with the final flag writes inverted, so the 'show' half is supported; the step helper names are still low confidence, hence 0.50.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_SetOwner
summary: Re-parents a UI object: stores the new owner at +0x28, then notifies the object at +0x10 through vtable+8 and clears its active flag through vtable+0xC(0).
evidence: The owner store and the two vtable calls are visible, but the owner argument is recovered from in_s0 (the ARM hard-float register trap in FACTS.md), so the prototype is uncertain; two of the three callers are still garbage symbol names (tEb, LFb), so the class and the exact owner semantics stay unproven.

name: Field_DestroyScene
summary: Tears down a field scene: releases actors, models, effects and map data, then clears the scene's own state.
evidence: 0x440 bytes; calls 0x001980E8 (resource release), 0x0011CFAC/0x0011FE8C (frees), 0x0010F6CC, 0x002E64xx and 0x001A178C; also called by 0x001A3760.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ShowFieldData
summary: Opens the message window for a field message record: appears the speaker, picks the text id from the field/monster tables (with per-scenario overrides), sets the window style and background music and moves the scene into the message state.
evidence: Uses Game_GetWork@0x6f20c0 and the +0x24a98 block, 0x63cc1c (field text record), 0x63cd1c/0x63d85c, 0x640c64 (&self->f_50->f_5c), 0x614024, 0x6f... and Snd_ResolveSceneBgmId@0x1f3ac4 / maybe_Sound_RefreshPendingBgmVolume@0x1f353c; writes f_b0->f_149 = 0, f_14a (style), f_146 and sets self->f_1c = 10. Callers maybe_Ui_Window_Hide@0x19e9a0 and maybe_Ui_MapWindow_RefreshEntry@0x624028 - the field-message twin of 0x19e6d0.

name: Field_DeleteScene
summary: Deletes a scene object: calls Field_DestroyScene and then releases the scene descriptor itself.
evidence: 0x28-byte wrapper: tail-calls 0x001A2FEC then 0x0010F6CC on the descriptor; global g_001a3784. Callers use it as the field-scene destructor.

name: maybe_Event_PollScriptState
summary: 32-byte poll: calls the event-slot test 0x00636AFC on the event state (work+8->+0x6C) and discards the answer.
evidence: The body touches no UI scene or flow object - only Os_GetGameWork and the event-slot test - so 'Ui_SceneFlow_TickGlobal' described code that is not here; the discarded result means the visible effect is only the callee's side effect.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromTableA
signature: void Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromTableA(SpriteActor* self, const SpriteDesc* desc)
summary: Initialises a field 2D-sprite actor from a placement descriptor: resolves the sprite type/atlas through the scene object manager (0x0066A7B8/0x0062C388/0x0062C3B0), copies the placement fields, allocates the animation instance and applies the template (0x002D1304), then creates/attaches the sprite mesh and sets its model size. Called when a field placement of sprite type is spawned.
evidence: 0x001A3A40/0x001A3A44 constants, 0x0062C388(desc+0x24)/0x0062C3B0(...,desc+0x22), 0x0066A7B8(core+0xB4), 0x002D1F28/0x002D1304 (Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate), 0x005E7650, 0x005F3500 (Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize), 0x0029E41C; caller maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB 0x00353074.

name: maybe_SpriteActor_DispatchAction
summary: Per-frame dispatch: reads the current field actor, and when its state is not 0x0D and the field UI mode is 5 it plays action sequence 0x0D for the rectangle built from self+0x298, otherwise queues gadget command 0x0C with the sprite id.
evidence: Named callees Actor_TryPlayActionSeq0D, Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand and Actor2D_ReRegisterObject make the two-way choice explicit, but the sprite class is still inferred from the layout and the rectangle fields, so maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorA
summary: Shared deleting destructor of the 2D sprite family: installs the class vtable, unlinks the embedded node (func_0017C330), destroys the attached scene object 0x24C bytes back with Field_Object_DtorBase and frees the object. The vtable comes in as an argument, so one body serves several classes.
evidence: NEW: the same 56-byte sequence now appears in several readable destructors (0x001A5AAC, 0x002B385C, 0x00219938, 0x002B423C) that all end in `Field_Object_DtorBase(...); func_0010F6CC();`, and 0x001A5AAC is byte-identical - so this is the deleting-destructor template of the family, which the first-pass 'DtorA' label did not say.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshA
signature: void Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshA(SpriteActor* self, const void* size)
summary: Creates the 2D sprite mesh: builds a 200x120 rectangle/uv descriptor (0x0031A48C with mode 0), then creates the sprite mesh through Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh (0x0031A394) with the 'sprite' material name and attaches it to the actor (0x005E7650). Sets the sprite's draw order to 10.
evidence: 0x005F2B54() reset, local rectangle {200,0x78}, 0x0031A48C(&rect,0,0x20,src->f_48,&rect), 0x0031A394(&params,self,&rect,"sprite"), self->f_B8 = mesh, mesh->f_129 = 10, 0x005E7650(self,mesh); pooled string 'sprite'.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the object's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running: it returns 0 only once the phase byte has reached its terminal value 5 (release sent).
evidence: NEW: func_0064C740 is disassembled at 0x0064C740 as `ldrb r0,[r0]; cmp r0,#5; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#0; bx lr` - a pure 'phase == 5' getter, not an unknown helper. Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState writes phase 5 as the terminal state after sending the release, so `!(phase == 5)` means 'still in the touch sequence'. The old name claimed the inverse ('IsReady') and a 'handle' argument; the argument is the object itself (r0 is forwarded unchanged to both callees). Class prefix from the code region (Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorA/CreateMeshA/DtorB/CreateMeshB) and from the sibling getter 0x001A3C80, vtable slot 0x00759040, which returns self+0x4D8.

name: Gfx_CreateMultiSpriteEffect
summary: Builds the eight-sprite layered effect used for glows/shadows around an actor: takes the shape descriptor, creates the colour animator, then for i = 0..7 resolves the frame id and per-sprite transform and adds a child sprite at self+0x298+i*0x48 with flags 0xFFE.
evidence: The loop and callees are now named (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Gfx_CreateFColAnimator, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, Gfx_SpriteParts_SetFlag239), which confirms the eight-child construction and the colour animator.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds the sprite's touch record (kind 2) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x4D8..+0x4E0; returns 1.
evidence: NEW: this is vtable slot 0x0075903C of the Gfx_Sprite2D vtable, and the very next slot 0x00759040 is 0x001A3C80, which returns self+0x4D8 - i.e. the refresh slot is immediately followed by the getter for the record it fills. That slot pairing (refresh, then get) is repeated in five sibling classes (0x0075A038/0x0075A03C, 0x0075BE10/0x0075BE14, 0x0075D904/0x0075D908, 0x007677D8/0x007677DC), so 'refresh the touch record' is confirmed rather than guessed.

name: Ui_SpriteWidget_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a 2D sprite widget: runs the sprite base constructor, installs the primary vtable and its +0x9C secondary, then default-constructs the eight 0x48-byte animation slots at +0x298.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Ui_Overlay_CreateSlotWidget, which builds this widget for an overlay slot, and the vtable/secondary-vtable install matches the three sibling slot constructors below. 0.5 because the class name 'SpriteWidget' is still our own.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_DtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of the first 2D-sprite mesh variant: re-installs the two class vtables (0x00758FC0 then the base 0x0075D55C), destroys the eight 0x48-byte mesh entries at +0x298, unlinks the object from its parent list, runs the shared Field_Object_DtorBase and frees the block.
evidence: NEW: the vtable whose +0x08 slot points at this function (base 0x00758FC0) has the confident Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshA (0.55) in the next slot, so the class really is the 2D sprite with a mesh variant - the first pass only had the two vtable addresses and a generic 'sprite' guess. Its twin 0x001A4494 sits in the vtable whose next slot is Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshB, which is why the A/B/C wording is kept. Reached only through the vtable (no direct bl anywhere in asm/text).

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshB
summary: Second sprite-mesh creator: builds a 200x120 rectangle with mode 1 / material 0x29 (0x0031A48C), creates the mesh via Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh with the 'sprite' name and attaches it. The resulting mesh has no draw-order override, unlike CreateMeshA.
evidence: 0x005F2B54(), {200,0x78}, 0x0031A48C(&rect,1,0x29,0,&rect), 0x0031A394(&params,self,&rect,"sprite"), self->f_B8=mesh, 0x005E7650(self,mesh); pooled 'sprite' string.

name: SpriteActor_UpdateTouchAndPosition
summary: Per-frame touch and position step: returns 1 while an event is running ((work+8)+0x6C non-zero); when the sprite's state byte is 4 it advances the embedded Field_Object2D touch state, returns 1 if the touch query is still busy, and otherwise submits the sprite position to the current field actor (0x005F34F0 + Gfx_Actor_BuildTransformFromPosition). Returns 0 when nothing was done.
evidence: The body is fully readable through named callees - Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState (0.50) on the embedded object at +0x3B8, the touch query 0x0064C740, and maybe_Gfx_Actor_BuildTransformFromPosition - so the touch-step-plus-position-submit reading is confirmed; only the class prefix is inferred from the embedded Field_Object2D.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfoB
summary: Rebuilds the sprite's secondary touch record (kind 0x0A) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x3B8..+0x3C0; it first drops stale objects of the touch class through Ui_DestroyObjectsOfClass.
evidence: NEW: the body is the same template as 0x001A3E68 with kind 0x0A and destination +0x3B8, and the leading call is now named - Ui_DestroyObjectsOfClass (0x004DD70C) destroys every live object of the touch class before the record is rebuilt, which is why the function is not a plain getter. It is not a vtable slot (no reference in asm/rodata), so the 'B' suffix stays as the only way to tell it from 0x001A3E68.

name: Gfx_CreateQuadSpriteEffect
signature: void Gfx_CreateQuadSpriteEffect(void* self, const void* desc)
summary: Builds a four-quad sprite effect: creates the sprite from the descriptor's model ids, plays its animation, then creates one child sprite per corner rectangle (desc->f_1C f_10..f_26) into self+0x298+i*0x48.
evidence: The body's explicit i<4 loop over the four rectangle tuples in desc->f_1C, each followed by Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild into self+0x298+i*0x48, matches the name; the named helpers (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, maybe_Gfx_GetEntryByteProperty) are the same ones used by the other 2D sprite-effect builders.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_TriggerGadget
signature: void Gfx_Sprite2D_TriggerGadget(SpriteActor* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 workSel)
summary: Fires the sprite's gadget command: sets the state byte +0x3C4 to 0xFF (idle) and triggers command 0x13 with the actor's trigger id through Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand (0x00256678) on work+0x6C.

name: Ui_OverlaySlotCtor_vt1A448C
summary: Overlay-slot widget constructor (vtable 0x001A448C): base-constructs through 0x001A5A60, installs the primary and +0x9C secondary vtable, then default-constructs four 0x48-byte child objects at +0x298.
evidence: NEW: the sole caller is the confident Ui_Overlay_CreateSlotWidget, which passes the same two arguments to all four sibling constructors and then attaches the result - the factory pattern is confirmed. The name keeps the vtable address because the four variants differ only by vtable and child count.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_DtorC
summary: Deleting destructor of the second 2D-sprite mesh variant: installs the class and base vtables, destroys the four 0x48-byte mesh entries at +0x298, unlinks the intrusive node, runs the shared base destructor and frees the object. Same template as 0x001A3F24 with a different element count.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x00759080 slot +0x0C is the confident Gfx_Sprite2D_CreateMeshB (0.55), so this is the destructor slot of the sibling mesh class of 0x001A3F24 (identical body, only the vtable and the element count differ). No direct caller: the only reference is the .word at 0x00759088.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_UpdateDrawPos
summary: Recomputes a 2D sprite's screen rectangle: takes the sprite size from its model record, divides by 8, adds the actor's +0x78/+0x7C draw offset, builds the transform through 0x0031A658 and, when the debug flag +0x29D or 0x00669B98 allows it, submits the rectangle for drawing.
evidence: The size/8 arithmetic, the two transform calls and the clipping bounds are in the body and Actor_TryPlayActionSeq16 is a named caller, but whether the object is a sprite actor rather than a generic 2D field object is still inferred and the submit helpers 0x00251230/0x0022D5C4 are unnamed.

name: maybe_Actor2D_UpdateAnimationState
summary: Per-frame actor state update: refreshes the model record, returns while the active byte at +0x29B is clear, switches the actor to state 4 through vtable+0x40 when +0x29D is set, otherwise plays the shared default animation (0x00725B08) and freezes the animator on its last frame.
evidence: The body is a two-flag state dispatch over clearly named callees (Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, Anim_PlayByIdForActor, Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame). The old name Gfx_Effect_Update was wrong: nothing here is an effect; the class is a field/2D scene actor, but no caller or vtable slot fixes it further.

name: maybe_Field_CreateMapObject
summary: Creates map object from definition ID: allocates 0x16C object and resolves model definition records.
evidence: Decompilation is damaged (unaff_r4 in body). Neighbours Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType and Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable confirm map object creation, but damaged registers keep confidence at 0.40.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_Refresh
summary: Sprite refresh fragment: the 260-byte Thumb routine is only recovered as a call to the balloon anchor updater (Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition, 0x0062AE90) plus 'return 0'; the rest of the body is missing, so what it actually refreshes is unknown.
evidence: No caller and a truncated Thumb body; the only recovered callee is Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition, which does not justify naming the whole routine, so the old name is kept as a hypothesis at low confidence.

name: Field_CreateActor
signature: void Field_CreateActor(Scene* scene, const u16* def)
summary: Creates a field actor from a script definition record, initialising its transform, model and action state before adding it to the scene.
evidence: 0x270-byte object; the definition is read as u16 fields and the neighbours (Anim_Instance_CtorSprite, Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable) are the field-actor creation family. Named context in the merged C: Anim_Instance_CtorSprite, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_PlayIdleAnim
summary: Starts the sprite's idle animation when nothing else is playing: if the two state bytes f_29B/f_29D are clear it plays the id from g_001A4CD0 through Anim_PlayByIdForActor and marks f_29B, otherwise it tells the object to finish state 4.
evidence: Anim_PlayByIdForActor is named and the guard bytes are explicit, but 'idle' is an inference from the fixed animation id and the 0x100 sound cue, and no caller confirms the intent.

name: Ui_Layout_AllocSlotNodeC
signature: void Ui_Layout_AllocSlotNodeC(u32 heap, int desc, u32 p3, u32 size)
summary: Allocates a tertiary layout slot node via func_0028E630 with tag 0x4000000C and configures default link offsets.
evidence: Calls allocator func_0028E630 with tag 0x4000000C, initializes vtable at slot[0x8B], sets attributes f_a6 = 0xFFFF, f_a7 = 0.

name: Field_Object_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field object: it unlinks the two intrusive list nodes at +0x22C/+0x24C, destroys the member at +0x24C (0x0017C330), runs the Field base destructor (0x00335DAC Field_Object_DtorBase) and tail-calls the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The readable C attached to this address is stale (it shows a one-line wrapper around 0x005F4F5C); the disassembly is unambiguous: push {r4,lr}; str r1,[r0],#0x22c; str r2,[r0],#0x20; ldm/str list unlink; bl 0x0017C330; bl 0x00335DAC (Field_Object_DtorBase); pop; b 0x0010F6CC (the shared free thunk, see R3_022). That is a deleting destructor, not an animation stop.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_UpdateVisibility
summary: Decides a 2D sprite's visibility from its state byte f_3C9: state 1 derives it from the owned sprite's animation flags, state 4 sends a marker event (Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent) and hides, state 5 hides; every path ends by applying the result through 0x0062AE90.
evidence: New context: the event call in state 4 is the now-named Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent and the final apply call is a single consistent setter, so 'compute visibility and apply' is read directly from the body; only the owner type (SpriteActor) is generic.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromTableB
signature: void Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromTableB(SpriteActor* self, const short* desc)
summary: Full initialisation of a 2D sprite actor from a 16-bit table entry: stores the placement id/size/mode fields, resolves the sprite atlas/type (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable 0x00319848, 0x0062C388/0x0062C3B0), allocates the animation instance (0x002D1F28 + Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate 0x002D1304), builds the draw node (0x0031A48C), attaches the mesh and applies the model size. This is the variant used by the scripted field sprites.
evidence: Reads the short table at arg2 offsets, 0x00319848((char)arg2[0xF],arg2[0xE]), 0x0062C388/0x0062C3B0, 0x00109DC8/0x002D1F28/0x002D1304, 0x0031A48C, 0x005E7650, 0x005F3500, 0x0029E41C, 0x005F36E0; caller maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB 0x00353074.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_SelectSlot
signature: u32 Gfx_Sprite2D_SelectSlot(SpriteActor* self, const void* key, void* entry)
summary: Selects the cached sprite sub-entry for an idle animation: when the scene tick is idle and the scene is not type 0x0F it resolves the key, computes the entry's index in the +0x2A4..+0x3C4 cache and stores it in the draw-selection byte +0x3C8.
evidence: Named caller Actor_TrySelectIdleAnimation consumes the selection when picking the idle animation, matching the cache scan and the +0x3C8 store. The unaff_r7 in the C is only a register the decompiler lost across a call: disassembly 0x001A54E8 loads r8 = [work+0x54->+0x20] and 0x001A5520 reads its f_38 scene type, so the 'idle and scene type != 0xF' guard is verifiable, not damaged semantics.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren(u32 owner, int descriptor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor reached from a factory table: builds a 0x4000000C-tagged object with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x007591FC (+0x98 secondary), sets the 0xFFFF/0xFF sentinels and default-constructs four 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef children at +0x2A4.
evidence: Same constructor shape as maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact (0x0028E630 + secondary vtable at +0x98 + 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef children), and the four children are its distinguishing feature; the old 'vt1A59E4' suffix was an address fragment, not a class name.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_Dtor
summary: Sprite destructor: installs the sprite vtable 0x007591FC and then the base vtable 0x0075D55C, destroys the four 0x48-byte span entries at self+0x2A4, unlinks the intrusive node and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: the body is the same destructor template as the named Actor2D_SpriteNode_DtorDeleteB (0.55) - two vtable installs, std_destroy_range with a 0x48 stride, intrusive unlink, Field_Object_DtorBase - so the role is certain. The class behind vtable 0x007591FC is still unidentified, so maybe_.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorB
summary: Byte-identical copy of Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorA at another address (same body as 0x001A3BA8): installs the caller's vtable, unlinks the embedded node, destroys the attached scene object and frees the object. Kept as a separate entry because both addresses are real vtable slots of different classes.
evidence: NEW: the body is exactly the same 3-statement sequence as the now-understood 0x001A3BA8 deleting destructor (vtable install, unlink, Field_Object_DtorBase + free), and the two are independent vtable slots - so the 'DtorE' label is replaced by an explicit 'same body as 0x001A3BA8' name.

name: Flag_GetGlobalIndexed
signature: int Flag_GetGlobalIndexed(int flagIndex, int arg2, int arg3, int context)
summary: Global flag query: looks up the flag offset of the given index in the u16 pair table at 0x0072B20C and returns whether that byte is set in the game work's global flag block at +0x27508.
evidence: NEW: the table at 0x0072B20C is a sequence of {u16 id, u16 offset} pairs whose ids are 0,1,2,... and whose offsets are 0x17B,0x17C,0x17D,... (read from asm/rodata), i.e. a genuine id->flag-offset map, and the two callers are Ui_RecipeInfo_IsUnlocked (0.5) and maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_InitFromFlags - both ask 'is this id's flag set?'. That pins 'global flag getter indexed by id' even though the name is inherited.

name: Ui_TextStyle_GetDescriptor
summary: Lazily allocates the array of five style descriptors and returns the descriptor body for styleId (style+0x60 plus the length word); null for ids >= 5.
evidence: Three callers are now named, including maybe_Ui_Window_RefreshMessageArgsA/B and Ui_RecipeInfo_ShowCraftMessage, which all need the text style descriptor.

name: maybe_Flag_AllSlotsActive
summary: Returns 1 only when ALL five entries in the game work's parallel arrays at +0x2A198 (object pointer) and +0x2A26C (flag byte), stride 0x10, are occupied; it breaks at the first free entry and returns 0. Used by the damage/heal/MP number popups and by the recipe and Uma window code.
evidence: Read the loop again: it breaks as soon as an entry has flag 0 or a null pointer and only reaches 'return 1' after the fifth entry, so the previous 'AnySlotActive' wording said the opposite of what the code does. What the five slots represent is still unknown (battle number popups are the majority of the callers).

name: Ui_Layout_UpdateChildTransforms
signature: void Ui_Layout_UpdateChildTransforms(UiLayoutNode* node, UiTransform* out, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Walks the node's child list and combines every visible child's transform into the caller's transform via 0x53CD1C, skipping the sentinel entry.
evidence: iterates node+4's doubly-linked child list, checks child->f_11 bit 1 and vtable+8 != g_001A5D48, then 0x53CD1C(arg3,out,child,arg4)

name: Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate
signature: u32 Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate(UiWidgetGroup* self, u32 p1, u32 p2, u32 p3)
summary: Iterates over active child widgets in list self->f_14 and dispatches update virtual method +0xC to each visible child.
evidence: Traverses linked list from self->f_14 to self->f_10; checks visible flag (char)child[5] != 0; invokes (*child->vtable[3])(child, p1, p2, p3).

name: Ui_Widget_DispatchActiveChildren
signature: int Ui_Widget_DispatchActiveChildren(UiWidget* self, int ctx, int out, int* state, int frame)
summary: Draw dispatch of a widget group: walks the child ring, and for every child whose enabled byte at +0x14 is set, rebases the command pointer once and calls the child's virtual +0x10 / +0x14 draw entries; if any child drew, it closes the scope with Ui_Widget_DrawAndResetFlags and the context's virtual +0x20. Returns 1 when something was drawn.
evidence: NEW: this function is slot 0 of vtable 0x00759394 whose slot 1 is the confident Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate (0.8), and the rest of the table is Ui_Object_DtorBase (0.6) / Gfx_RenderNode_Dtor (0.85) / Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub (0.55) - i.e. exactly the widget-group dispatch table. The 'active children' wording of the first pass is what the body does, and the named neighbour now places it in the widget-group class.

name: Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchDraw
summary: Iterates over child widgets in list self->f_14 and invokes draw virtual method +0x18 on each child.
evidence: Traverses linked list self->f_14 to self->f_10, invoking virtual method +0x18 on each child node.

evidence: The paired destructor 0x001C3B10 is already named Ui_SimpleWindow_Dtor (0.50) and unwinds exactly the members this constructor builds, in reverse order; the caller Ui_Screen_CreateChildWindows allocates 0x198 bytes and calls this ctor, and vtable 0x007597A4 inherits the message-window dtor slots (0x50/0x54 = Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor/Delete).

name: Ui_SimpleWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the window class built by 0x001C3A94: installs the passed vtable word, unwinds the four members in reverse construction order (Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor at +0x56, then -0x1C, -0x10, -300) and frees the object.
evidence: New context: the matching constructor 0x001C3A94 is now cited by the named Ui_Screen_CreateChildWindows, and the reverse-order unwinding with the named Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor matches it step for step, so this is that child-window class's destructor.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_End

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Update

name: Ui_Layout_GetButtonStateAlt

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdatePagingState
signature: int maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdatePagingState(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 update, u32 force)
summary: Caches the child window's paging value (0x0065114C on child+0x184) into the message-window word +0x48, then, when the helper at +0x2C exists, forwards the page index (0x0065118C) through 0x002F6B0C and remembers the last value in the u16 at +0x4C.

signature: u32 maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateWindowStyle(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 update, u32 force)

name: Ui_MessageWindow_HideText
summary: Hides the current text object and marks it invisible, leaving the window frame on screen.
evidence: 0x003DE994(self->f_10) (the 'stop reveal' counterpart of 0x003DEA3C) then self->f_10->f_94 = 0; callers MessageEnd (0x0014732C), 0x003966A4 and 0x00396BBC.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ShowBackdrop
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_ShowBackdrop(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates and shows the 2D backdrop/frame object owned by the message window at +0x1c.
evidence: Allocation size g_001c4fe0 + ctor 0x001D750C + 0x0021F738, then f_1c->f_94 = 1; the caller 0x001634CC also calls 0x001C42FC (request end), i.e. the 'open the frame, then run the text' helper. Named context in the merged C: Ui_GetCore, Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_WantsInstantText
summary: Returns 1 for message modes 0 and any non-2 mode; only in mode 2 does it build/look up the wide-layout table and return 0 when the layout entry's +0x46 byte is 1, i.e. when the text should be revealed immediately.
evidence: NEW: there is no direct bl/b call site; the four named window builders in the previous xref were spurious. The mode byte and the layout +0x46 test are visible, so the name is kept as the honest description of the polarity the body computes; maybe_.

name: Ui_Text_ApplyTableIds
summary: Applies the two ids from the UI table (entries 2 and 1 of the table behind Ui_GetCore()->f_10) to the text object at self+0x1DE4 through Ui_StartLayoutAnimations and hands the caller both text panes (+0x1DE4 and +0x98). Returns false when the owner is not built yet.
evidence: The named callee makes this "start the layout animations for table ids 1/2", not "set message args"; the two callers (Ui_MessagePair_SetPanels, Ui_KyoukaiWindow_CreatePanes) fill their own output pair from the result, so the old SetArgs wording was misleading.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Tick
summary: Per-frame message-window tick: derives the four button flags (confirm/skip/auto/page), feeds them to the window update, and steps the text reveal state machine.
evidence: Builds local_18..local_15 from (self->f_74 bits 0x142/0x14e/1) and self->f_78 (line count), sets self->f_79 = cursor-blink, calls vtable +0x5c(f_c, f_5c == 0) then 0x001C40F8(self,&flags); afterwards drives 0x003DE8D4/0x003DE5B8/0x003DE8E8/0x003DE994 on self->f_10 and sets f_3e when finished.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseChild18
signature: void Ui_Window_ReleaseChild18(UiMessageWindowLayout* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Release callback that frees the child window stored at +0x18 and clears the field.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Open
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_Open(UiMessageWindow* self, MessageText* text, int side, u32 arg4)
summary: Opens the shared message window with a prepared text record: selects the window side, shows the frame, pushes the text record into the window and starts the reveal.
evidence: Ten callers, all script-bound message natives: TalkStart (0x00166164), MessageEnd, QuestCompletedMessage (0x0015C314), FukidashiMessage (0x00150FD0), DBOpenDialog (0x0014930C), 0x0024B998, 0x00293E5C, 0x00293F1C, 0x002F5784, 0x00306654, 0x003969F0; body = 0x001C3F54(self, side), vtable +0x18(f_c, 1) (show), +0x60(f_c, text) (set text), f_3d = 0, then 0x002183CC(work->f_10).

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseEmbeddedChild
summary: Deactivates the sub-object embedded at child+0x1C34 with 0x0061B79C(...,0) and then invokes its virtual +0x18 with 1 (destroy).
evidence: The asm is `add r0,r1,#0x1C34; mov r1,#0; bl 0x61B79C; ldr r0,[r4,#4]; add r0,#0x1C34; ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r2,[r1,#0x18]; mov r1,#1; bx r2`, i.e. deactivate then destroy; Ui_MessageWindow_Ctor destroys the same +0x1C34 sub-object with virtual +0x18(obj,0), which fixes the reading.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ClearCallbacks
summary: Runs and clears the window's eight queued callbacks (each {fn, adjustor} pair from the static table) and restores the previous key handler, then clears the 'busy' bit.
evidence: Copies the 16 words at g_001c5488 (8 {fn,adjustor} pairs, the same table format as 0x001C40F8's g_001c42f8) onto the stack and invokes each, then restores self->f_34/f_38 from g_001c5488-0x24 and clears bit 2 of f_5c; called from 0x001C40F8 and 0x001C465C.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextDirect

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextFromWork

Callers 0x00146D34, 0x0024B998, 0x002F5784; twin of 0x001C54A0 which takes the ids as arguments.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates once and shows the 0x260-byte plate window owned at self+0x18: runs the Ui_TimeWindow_Ctor class constructor, attaches its parts, sets its visible byte f_94, broadcasts to the children and switches the owner into two-plate mode (f_40=2).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructs the message-window object: installs the class vtable, seeds all text/cursor fields with their 'invalid' defaults, builds the 0x16f layout node, derives the window mode from the UI table and creates the panes.
evidence: Writes *self = g_001c57bc then 0xffffffff/0xffff/0xff defaults at +0x44..+0x58; 0x0036B45C(&self->f_18, 1, 0x16f) creates the layout node with id 0x16f; self->f_58 = 0x0062AB3C(table[2]) is the same mode field used by 0x001C4738; then 0x001C4738 and the two side hides. Callers 0x00216B5C and 0x00216DD4 (the message-window factory).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Delete
summary: Deleting destructor of the message window: runs 0x001C57E4 and then the project's operator delete.
evidence: Two-statement body: 0x001C57E4(self) followed by 0x0010F6CC() - the standard scalar-deleting-destructor shape seen at 0x001DC070, 0x001E04B8, 0x001E4908.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor
signature: void* Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Destructor of the message window: releases the ten child windows/objects (+4..+0x30) and unwinds the trailing 0x60-byte layout node, returning this-0x60.
evidence: Stamps *arg1 = g_001c5920, then ten 0x0021F8B8(work, arg1[n]) release calls clearing each field, then 0x0036B514(arg1+0x18) and this-0x60; inverse of 0x001C560C, whose 0x0036B45C member sits at +0x18 and whose fields +4..+0x30 are the child windows.

name: Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord
signature: void Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord(void* holder, const void* displayRecord)
summary: If holder+8 holds a widget pointer, makes it visible via vtable +0x18(widget, 1), applies displayRecord via vtable +0x60(widget, displayRecord), and marks *(u8*)(holder+4) = 1.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x1C5924..0x1C5968: ldr r0,[r0,#8]; cmp r0,#0; calls vt[+0x18](w, 1) and vt[+0x60](w, record), then strb 1,[r4,#4]. Callers Ui_SystemMenu_OpenConfirmPrompt, Ui_SaveLoad_ShowActionError, and Shop_ShowConfirmMessage pass a widget wrapper and stack text/display record.

name: Ui_MessageText_ResetChildren
summary: Resets the two page objects at self+8 and self+0xC by calling their virtual slot +0x18 with 0.
evidence: It is adjacent to the now-named Ui_MessageText_Update and uses the same (*(vt+0x18))(obj,0) detach idiom as the message-window constructor's child teardown.

name: Ui_MessageText_Update
summary: Advances the text reveal of a message window: reads the button/auto flags from the message record, decides between the five display states (normal, fast-forward, auto, wait, done) and drives the text object's virtual show/hide methods.
evidence: Computes uVar8/uVar10/uVar7 from f_14 bits 0x142/0x14e and f_18, then branches on vtable +0x70 (text present) and +0x6c (finished); writes the state 1..5 at self+4 and one of 1/2/5 at self+5; 0x00629128 is the 'auto mode enabled' query. Callers 0x001669F0 and 0x002CEF08 - both field-event drivers of the message system.

name: Ui_GlobalObjects_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the UI support singletons down in reverse creation order: resets the 0x28-byte task object, the 0x1EB0-byte sound sequence, the 0x80-byte icon cache and the string work, each only while its "created" flag byte is still set.
evidence: The only caller is now named Ui_Overlay_Shutdown and the callees Sound_System_Teardown/Anim_Sequence_CtorBase confirm a singleton teardown, but the name Ui_System_Shutdown is already taken by 0x00626E44 (the audio/system shutdown), so this one is named after what it actually tears down: the global UI support objects (task object, sound sequence, icon cache, string work).

name: Ui_Subsystem_Init
summary: One-time UI subsystem boot: creates the 0x37C-byte icon work, binds the icon texture set (0x383764), creates the sound work (0x1EB880), registers the SE bank with id 0xE (0x1EC504) and initialises the interface work; the pattern repeats a lazy-create block per subsystem.
evidence: calls Ui_LoadIconTextures (0x383764, N_004), Sound_InitSystem (0x1EB880, N_002), 0x1EC9A8/0x1EC504 with 0xE; allocation sizes 0x37C/0x80/0x28.

name: Ui_System_Update
summary: Per-frame tick of the UI subsystem: lazily creates the subsystem singleton (vtable 0x007829CC) and the movie/overlay controller (vtable 0x00782900), runs 0x00383DAC and then advances the movie controller when it has a player and a set mode byte.
evidence: New context: both lazily created vtables are now anchored (0x007829CC is cited by Ui_Subsystem_Init, 0x00782900 by Movie_GetFrame/Gfx_Overlay_DrawSprite/Ui_GetSceneTransitionManager) and the conditional tail call is the named Gfx_Movie_UpdateStateMachine (0x001DBB74), so 'UI subsystem per-frame update' is supported.

name: Script_CreateSystemObject
summary: Initialises the script system's 'System' object: sets up its three list heads, stamps the map/name vtables (0x007824E0 / 0x00782534) and inserts the literal "System" into the object's hash map before installing the final vtable 0x00759814.
evidence: New context: the caller is now the named Script_RegisterSystemObjects (0x001F2BC8), the name insert goes through 0x0011CCA0 (hash) + 0x0011142C (insert), which the named Str_HashName / Container_HashTableInsert also call, and the literal is s_System. So it constructs and registers the System object; the old 'InitSystemString' name understated that as a string init.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorA
summary: Deleting destructor of the class whose vtable is 0x007824E0: installs the vtable, releases the inline string at +0x1C when flag +0xB is set, unlinks the two intrusive list heads at +8/+0xC and +0x14/+0x18, then frees the block. One of four byte-identical copies.
evidence: NEW: the vtable word stored at the top of the body is 0x007824E0, and asm/rodata shows that table's slot 1 is 0x00572BBC - the same body at another address. So all four copies (0x001C635C, 0x002598B4, 0x002D5734, 0x00572BBC) are the deleting destructor of one single class, emitted four times; the old names used three different schemes (Ui_Object_DtorStringAndLists / ...DoubleListB / ...DoubleListC / Container_Node_DtorC) for identical code. The class is still unidentified - its vtable slots 0x00572B94..0x00572C48 are all unnamed and sit in the 0x00572xxx math/container region - so the maybe_ stays and the A/B/C suffixes only distinguish the copies. The body itself is confirmed: install the vtable, release the inline string at +0x1C when flag +0xB is set (0x0010EC00 walks the red-black tree, 0x0010EC14 erases the node), unlink the two intrusive list heads at +8/+0xC and +0x14/+0x18, then free the block through the allocator virtual at self-8 (0x0010F6CC).

name: maybe_Ui_PushCommandSequence
signature: void maybe_Ui_PushCommandSequence(void* queue, unsigned char* flags, u32 arg3, u32 packed)
summary: Pushes up to four command entries into a 16-slot ring queue (head at +4, end at +8): ids 0x104/0x105/0x106 when the matching flag byte is set, otherwise a single 3 or 7 entry depending on another flag; each push is refused when the queue is full or has already advanced.
evidence: The queue layout and the 0x10-slot capacity match the ring append helper 0x0070EEC4, and the only caller is the load-screen script-state updater; nothing says what command ids 0x104..0x106 / 3 / 7 mean, so the label stays maybe_.

name: Ui_SoundQueue_PopAndPlay
summary: Pops the 16-bit command at the head of the queue (memmoving the rest down), plays its low byte as an SE through 0x001F0BE4 and, when the high byte is non-zero, also advances the secondary sound work via 0x001EE018.
evidence: New context: the SE entry point and the queue head/end fields are confirmed by the body (16-bit stride, head/end at +4/+8), and the 'pop then play' role is exactly what the code does; only the 'Ui_' prefix is inferred (callers are UI sound helpers), hence 0.50 rather than higher.

name: Container_InlineVector8_PushByte
summary: push_back for a byte vector with an 8-byte small-buffer optimisation: appends at the write cursor when it is still the inline buffer at self+0x19 and fewer than 8 bytes are used, moving the last byte forward and calling 0x00111378 when it has to grow.
evidence: Callers 0x00262BA4, 0x0026319C (both Ui_RecipeBook_*). Body: fc = self->f_c (begin), puVar2 = self->f_10 (cursor); `if ((u32)(cursor-fc) < 8 && fc == self+0x19)`; if cursor >= self->f_14 it shifts and calls func_00111378 (the grow/throw helper used by every std::vector in the project); then *cursor = arg2, self->f_10 = cursor+1. Matches N_044's std_String_AppendChar shape.

name: Ui_Window_AppendControlBytes
summary: Window script-command handler: takes the command's parameter from the source record at self+0x11E4 (+0xA4), clamps it, stores it at self+0x1114 and appends the control bytes 0x09 followed by 0x11 (clamped) or 0x12 (not clamped) to the window's byte vector at self+0x10A8.
evidence: NEW: the function is an entry of the window script-command dispatch table at 0x0072B698, whose neighbours are the confident Ui_Window_AdvanceScriptCmd12 (0x002633E0), Ui_Window_AdvanceCmd13Or14 (0x00263350), Ui_Window_AdvanceScriptCmd14B/14C (0x0026387C/0x002638D8) and Ui_Window_AdvanceScriptCmd15C (0x00262998) - so the owner is the window class, not a text object. The body appends two bytes (0x09 then 0x11 or 0x12) through Container_InlineVector8B_PushByte, so the old 'AppendByte' singular was slightly off; it is not item code (no Item_LookupRecord, no member inventory).

evidence: Callers 0x001C6788 (maybe_Ui_Text_AppendByte), 0x00262648, 0x00262E88, 0x00263130, 0x002632E0 (Ui_RecipeBook_*). Byte-for-byte the same code as 0x001C6660 with the offsets shifted by 0x20 (+0x2C/+0x30/+0x34/+0x39).

evidence: Calls 0x001DAD58(self->f_118 + 0xF84, f_108C)+0x0062F680 as the 'is valid' test, then compares f_C/f_10, f_2C/f_30, f_48/f_4C, f_78 and f_69 (a -1 sentinel) before delegating to 0x001C6A9C. All 19 callers are the recipe-book UI (0x00262AD4 ..., named maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_* in N_023).

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ScriptCommandHandlerM

The disassembly (0x001C69BC..0x001C6A9C) matches the 0x002622xx handlers: drain, splice +0xF84, broadcast 1 to +0xF84/+0x804/+0x9D8, Gfx_Node_SetVisible 0 on six panes, push 0x0B. So the generic 'WaitAndRelease' wording was wrong; it is a table command handler.

name: Ui_RecipeBook_Update
summary: Updates the recipe (forge book) page: refreshes the recipe count/description message, sets message args 5/6/7 from the recipe id and swaps the detail pane when the selection changes.

name: Field_DetachObject
summary: Removes object from the field's attached-object list (head/tail at +0xD74/+0xD78): calls virtual +0x14, unlinks the node and finally calls virtual +4 (delete). Returns 1 when found or when object is null.
evidence: New context: the unlink helper 0x0010EBE4 is now cited by the named Model_AttachSlot_Hide, Ui_Sprite_DetachFromLayer and Battle_Command_AttachEquipToActor as the list-erase primitive, and the +0x14/+4 pair is the unlink+delete slot pair used by the UI/Actor classes.

name: Field_CreateActorRenderObject
signature: int Field_CreateActorRenderObject(FieldOwner* field, unsigned int modelId)
summary: Creates the larger (0x730-byte) field actor object: fills the render/appearance descriptor from the model id and allocates the object.
evidence: Descriptor init 0x00617750, record lookups func_0035EB98/func_0063EB94, Mem_AllocAligned(0x730); called from 0x20e75c and 0x606718 (field/scene code). Named context in the merged C: Game_GetWork.

name: Model_CreateAttachmentB
summary: Creates second kind of model attachment node: allocates 0x230-byte node, initializes via func_003D4974, and links into model part list at +0x170.
evidence: Direct companion to Model_CreateAttachmentA (0x001C88A4); called by confident Cutscene_CreateActorModels to attach model accessories.

name: Field_NotifyAttachedIdle8
summary: While the view work is idle (f_D84 < 1) it broadcasts virtual slot +8 to the +0xD74 list and slot +0x18 to the attached objects and the ten slot lists.
evidence: Same confirmed broadcast family; the idle guard on f_D84 and the two different slots are visible in the body, and the two callers are the named scene-flow update/teardown.

name: Field_ShutdownSlots
summary: Shuts the field owner down when it is active: detaches the two slot objects, drains the two 0xC-byte slot arrays and the ten +0x24 lists (calling vtable+8 on every entry), releases the handle at +0x18 and clears the active flag.
evidence: The named callees Field_DetachSlotObjectA/B and Pack_FreeHandleEntry now outline the whole body, and the callers are the scene teardown paths (Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll, maybe_Ui_BigView_Dtor).

name: Field_AdvanceSlotTimers
summary: Advances the view work one step: applies the pending rewind request (f_D80), decrements the timer f_D84, re-binds the attached objects (0x001C8584 + maybe_Field_BindAttachedObjects) and broadcasts slot +0x14.
evidence: The timer logic is fully visible and the bind callee is now named maybe_Field_BindAttachedObjects; the two scene-flow callers confirm a per-frame tick. Confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_WidgetWithTenChildren_Ctor
summary: Constructs a UI widget: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x007598B0, stores descriptor->+4, seeds the float sentinel 0xFFFFF000 and default-constructs ten 0xC-byte child elements at +0x24 with std_ConstructArray.
evidence: The literal vtable store 0x007598B0 and the ten 0xC-byte std_ConstructArray children are clear, so the class is a UI widget with ten child slots; the old 'vt7598B0' suffix was a raw address, not a class name, so the wording is fixed while the exact widget kind stays unknown (no callers).

name: maybe_Field_SlotOwner_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a ~0xD80-byte field object that owns three arrays of ten 0xC-byte entries (at +0x24/+0x9C/+0x128), two more entries at +0xD58, two intrusive list nodes at +0xD78 and a pack handle at +0x18; it first runs the base Field_ShutdownSlots teardown.
evidence: Disassembly 0x001C9AE8: str r1,[r0] (vptr); bl 0x001C967C Field_ShutdownSlots; unlink the nodes at +0xD78; four std_destroy_range calls with element destructor 0x006F43A0 (2/10/10/10 entries of 0xC); Pack_ReleaseHandle(self+0x18); the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC (object-8 header dispatch, not plain operator delete). The old name Ui_BigView_Dtor was unsupported: no '.word 0x001C9AE8' exists in any vtable and the model functions listed as callers actually call the following function at 0x001C9B8C (an unnamed hashing helper), so they were mis-attributed. The object is in the field-object code block, hence Field_; the exact class is unknown.

name: Object_MarkReleased
summary: Releases the child object at +0x10 when the owner lookup still resolves, then marks the child dead by setting its byte +0x25D.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_ScreenView_ReleaseAll, which releases the screen view's objects, and the body writes the dead flag after the release call.

name: Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_Reset
summary: Resets one screen-view collection entry: releases the shared row list (0x001E4B4C), destroys and nulls the child object at +0x10, clears the state words and seeds the slot id from 0x001C9DEC.
evidence: Callers 0x006227CC and 0x00622C30 (Gfx_ScreenView_ResetCollections). Body: func_001E4B4C(); self->f_c = 0; if (self->f_10) { (**(code**)(*self->f_10+4))(); self->f_10 = 0; } self->f_14 = 0; self->f_15 = 0; self->f_16 = (short)g_001c9dec; self->f_18 = 0xff; self->f_19 = 0. Slot +4 of a class vtable is the non-deleting destructor.

name: maybe_Effect_CreateVariant
signature: void maybe_Effect_CreateVariant(void* owner, u32 effectId, int variant)
summary: Creates one or more effect instances from effect ID: resolves variant table and calls Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: Connects with Effect_FindOrCreateInstance; effect variant resolution is clear, but calling subsystem remains generic. Kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Ui_Record_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI record: calls the base constructor 0x001E4B98, overwrites the vtable with 0x007598C0, clears the words at +0xC/+0x10 and the bytes at +0x14/+0x15/+0x19, sets the u16 at +0x16 to 0xFFFF and the byte at +0x18 to 0xFF.
evidence: The asm shows `bl 0x1E4B98` (a constructor that installs a vtable and clears +4/+5/+8), then `str r2,[r0]` with the literal 0x007598C0 and the field clears, so this is a derived constructor, not a pool reset: the old name's 'PooledRecord' came from misreading 0x001E4B98 as an allocator.

name: Ui_List_DestroyTwoPools
summary: Destroys two adjacent pools of ten 0x50-byte list entries at self+0x70 and self+0x3B8 by calling the entry destructor 0x003DFEC4 on each.
evidence: Two loops i<10 calling 0x003DFEC4(self + 0x70 + i*0x50) and (self + 0x3B8 + i*0x50); only caller 0x001F3F80 is the owning object's teardown.

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateBillboard
summary: Projects a UI overlay anchor into screen space: adds the animated offset at +0x6E0..+0x6E8 to the local offset, projects it, writes the quad position at self->f_30 (+0x1C/+0x20/+0x24 and the +0x44 flag), then applies a per-slot parallax offset for slots 0 and 1.
evidence: NEW: the class is supported by the callee region, not by the caller - 0x003A66BC, maybe_Ui_Overlay_IsPointBehindMove (0x003A6624) and maybe_Ui_Overlay_ComputeDistanceScale (0x003A66C4) are all Ui_Overlay_* helpers, and the body writes the same quad fields as Ui_Window_ProjectWorldSlot. The only caller is maybe_Ui_Scene_Dtor (0x001F3F80, confidence 0.40), whose own name is a guess, so it does not contradict the overlay attribution.

name: Ui_Balloon_BindParts
summary: Binds a speech balloon's layout: attaches the four panes from the static table at 0x007A89A4 via vtable+0x34 and then binds the two balloon text parts at self+0x13 (part 0) and self+0xE5 (part 1) with Ui_Balloon_BindWinParts.
evidence: The callee is now the named Ui_Balloon_BindWinParts, called twice with part indices 0 and 1 on the two embedded text-part blocks - so this is a balloon, not a generic four-part widget; the four table entries are just the balloon's panes.

name: Ui_PanelCtor_vt1CA2EC
summary: Constructor stub for a large UI panel: installs vtable 0x001CA2EC on the object returned by Ui_Object_CtorBase and default-constructs two 0x348-byte children at +0x4C.
evidence: The recovered body is exactly base ctor + vtable + two 0x348-byte children, and its caller is a composite constructor that chains this with two animation-reference lists.

name: Ui_Balloon_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the balloon widget: releases the two 0x348-byte record objects at +0x4C, runs the UI base destructor and frees the balloon.
evidence: It is slot 1 of vtable 0x007598D4 whose slot 0 is its non-freeing twin 0x001CA340 and whose other slots include the named Ui_Balloon_BindParts (0x001CA1C8); Ui_PanelCtor_vt1CA2EC (0x001CA238) constructs the same object. So the class is the balloon, not an anonymous 'Object'.

name: Ui_Balloon_Dtor
summary: Non-freeing destructor of the balloon widget: releases its two 0x348-byte records at +0x4C and runs the UI base destructor.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x007598D4, whose slot 1 (0x001CA304) frees the same object and whose named sibling Ui_Balloon_BindParts (0x001CA1C8) identifies the class.

name: Math_Random_InitState
signature: void Math_Random_InitState(RandomState* rng, uint32_t key0, uint32_t key1)
summary: Seeds a 6-word random state: calls 0x00113590 to build {key0, key1, 0x6C078965, 0x5D588B65, 0x00269EC3, 0} on the stack and stores that block at rng+8. The two constants 0x6C078965 and 0x5D588B65 are the MT19937 initialisation multipliers.
evidence: The sole call site is Field_InitSceneObjects calling it on &battleWork->f_4218, and FACTS.md places the battle RNG at battle work+0x4218 with 0x001CA474(rng,lo,hi) rolling from it; the three literal-pool words at 0x001135C0 are 0x6C078965/0x5D588B65/0x00269EC3 (RNG init multipliers). So the six copied words are an RNG state, not a colour.

name: Math_RandomChanceBelow
summary: Returns non-zero when a random fraction of the object's random state is at or below the given threshold - a probability roll used to decide whether a random effect occurs.
evidence: Takes a random 31-bit value with 0x0051B1FC(self+8, 0x7FFFFFFF), converts it to float and compares 'random * g_001CA3E0 <= in_s0'. g_001CA3E0 is the 1/0x7FFFFFFF scale, i.e. a 0..1 random roll.

name: Math_IntToFloat
summary: Converts the saturated integer returned by 0x51B1FC(valueBlock+8, INT_MAX) to float and returns it in s0 (VectorSignedToFloat).
evidence: Raw asm: 'bl 0x51B1FC; vmrs/vcvt' -> the Ghidra pseudo-C shows VectorSignedToFloat with the FPSCR rounding mode; 0x51B1FC is the clamp-to-int helper. Neighbour Math_RandomChanceBelow (0x1CA3A0) is the same maths block.

name: Math_DivideIntByCount
summary: Returns 0x51B1FC(valueBlock+8, INT_MAX) / (count+1) using the integer divide helper 0x11CD80; the result is left in r0/r1 by the divide routine.
evidence: Same clamp helper 0x51B1FC as 0x1CA3F8; divisor is arg2+1; 0x11CD80 is the __aeabi_idiv pair (called right after the clamp in both 0x1CA450 and 0x1CA48C).

name: Math_RandomRange
signature: int Math_RandomRange(void* rng, int low, int high)
summary: Rolls a random integer in [low, high] from the 64-bit random state at rng+8: advances the state with the shared step 0x0051B1FC(state+8, 0x7FFFFFFF), takes the remainder modulo (high-low+1) and adds low.
evidence: The asm is `add r0,r0,#8; mvn r1,#0x80000000; bl 0x51B1FC; add r1,r5,#1; bl 0x11CD80; add r0,r1,r4` - the same state+8 / 0x7FFFFFFF roll the confident Math_RandomChanceBelow (0x001CA3A0) and Math_Random_InitState (0x001CA378) use, followed by a modulo and the low offset. The old name's 'wrap' was wrong: nothing wraps, the value is a fresh random draw.

name: Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes
signature: void Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes(ActorModel* self, unsigned char* partRecord, ModelDescriptor* descriptor)
summary: Copies the visible model-part codes of a record into the actor's part table: record type 2 sets the 'has parts' byte +0x744, type 4 the part +0x745, type 5 the part +0x746, type 6 the u16 at g_001CA5D8 (self+0x748) and type 8 the part +0x74A. For any other type it asks the descriptor's virtual getters (+0x78/+0x7C/+0x80) for the code and falls back to 0xFF (none) when all three are unset.
evidence: Vtable slot in four sibling Actor vtables (0x759AC0, 0x76C768, 0x774D6C, 0x774EF4) next to maybe_Model_ApplyParamType5/4, maybe_Actor_SetComponentFlag and maybe_Field_Actor_QueryFlag7ByModelHandle (N_041/N_086). Part bytes +0x744..+0x74A are tested one by one by 0x1CA7E4 and 0x1CB744 in this batch, and read by Ui_PartyStatus code (0x1CA4D8 is followed in the vtable by Ui_PartyStatus_Reset at 0x1CE354).

name: Model_AdvanceAnimFrames
summary: Advances a character's animation by N frames, clamping to the remaining length; when the clip reaches its end it clears the state flags and runs the end-of-animation effects (state reset, callback, sub-system notifications).
evidence: Clamps with min(frames, vtable+0x94 minus vtable+0x90 - end vs current frame), advances the frame counter through the animation object at self+0x20 (vtable+4), then on frame 0 clears f_39D, calls 0x001CAE90/0x001CB084 and four 0x00279xxx helpers and the callback at f_3A6 (vtable+0x174).

name: maybe_Model_ApplyAttachPointParam
summary: Chance-based model parameter application: for a character model (type 0x5A) it copies the actor's parameter block, finds the entry labelled type 5, rolls 1..100 through the game RNG and stores value in the model's parameter slot when the entry's float is at or below the roll.
evidence: Re-read: the body is a probability test, not an unconditional apply - the roll is func_001CA474(battleRng, 1, 100, 0) and the store happens when param <= roll. The 'attach point' wording describes the entry's consumer, which is still not visible here, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateAttachPoints
summary: Ghidra could not decode this entry: after one read of the battle 3D-mode byte (work+8->+0x5C +0x4244) the body is halt_baddata() plus 16 removed unreachable blocks. The bytes are probably inline data or a misidentified entry.
evidence: Still undecodable: three halt_baddata truncations and 16 removed blocks, so no name can be justified; the single 0x4244 read is the only real instruction.

name: maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart
signature: int maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart(ActorModel* self, int slot, int offset)
summary: Predicate over the actor model's part record: true when the part is visible (virtual +0x10), (f_39D & 0x56)==0 and either the part code at +0x74A is 0x54 or the part letter at +0x745 is 'A'/'B'/'C'.
evidence: The named Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes cites this function and its twin 0x001CB744 as the predicates used when applying part codes, but the body is register-starved (coprocessor_function/store, in_cr*), so the slot/offset parameters and the exact part meaning stay uncertain.

name: Actor_ApplyVariantRecord
summary: Selects one of the three 0x20-byte variant blocks of a model source (flags at source+0xB0F7 / source+0xB0F9 choose block +0xB108, +0xB128 or +0xB148) and applies it through virtual +0x178 together with the source pointer; stores `source` at self+0x740. When the source has no variant data (byte +0x10 == 0) it only stores the pointer.
evidence: Twin 0x1CC96C (same body, virtual +0x18C, no source argument); 0x1CD328 resets the same three blocks (b108/b10C/b110 = 1/-1/-1) choosing by the same b0F7/b0F9 flags. Both are vtable methods next to Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor / Model_AdvanceAnimFrames.

name: Battle_ActionModel_ApplyPartParams
summary: Copies the ~30 part parameters (scale, blend, offsets, colours) from the character/model parameter record resolved by 0x0063E5C8 into the action model's f_30..f_DC fields; when randomizeScale is set (descriptor+0x1D) the first scale is multiplied by RNG[0x50,100]/100. Called once from Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor, so it is a setup copy, not a per-frame update.
evidence: The only caller is Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor (0.5), which calls it right after func_0027A4E0(self,descriptor) and before Menu_SetOwnerActor; the body is a straight field-by-field copy from func_0063E5C8(dm, self->f_76C & 0xFFFF), with the RNG only scaling one value. That makes 'UpdatePartScale' too narrow and 'Update' wrong.

name: maybe_Actor_AdjustHeightParam
summary: Adds delta to the s16 at self+0x36, clamped to [0, s16 at self+0x32], skipped when the global UI-busy flag or self byte +0xF1F is set; the delta is zeroed when virtual +0xE8(self,0x73) returns 0.
evidence: No named caller or callee was added; virtual +0xE8 with id 0x73 is the same feature query the flag setters 0x001CBB70/0x001CBDE0 use, so the guard is a per-actor feature check, but what the s16 pair at +0x32/+0x36 measures (height, length, scale) is still unknown.

name: maybe_Model_IsSpecialState
summary: Unit-model predicate used by Battle_CheckUnitsCondition modes 6/7, which require every unit of each of the four 26-unit groups to return 1: 1 when the model is visible, its f_39D flags (mask 0x56) are clear, and either the part code at +0x74A is 0x54 or the part letter at +0x745 is 'A'/'B'/'C'; 0 otherwise. Template copy of 0x001CA7E4.
evidence: New: the caller Battle_CheckUnitsCondition (0.55) uses it as the per-unit test that all units in a group are in the 'special' state, and Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes cites the same part codes. The word 'special' still stands for the undecoded 0x54/'A'/'B'/'C' combination, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_FindAndStartType9A
summary: Scans the battle party list at battleWork+0x4260 for the first unit for which the kind test Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted(unit, 0x9A) succeeds, then calls that unit's vtable+0x120(unit, 0x9A, 1) to start the state; if the unit's class chain reaches g_playerBattleActorClass it also hides the unit's attachment.
evidence: New evidence: the named caller Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility, and FACTS.md's battle-work layout (+0x5C battle work, +0x4260 party list, +0x4218 RNG) confirm the function walks battle units rather than field actors. Kind 0x9A is still an opaque state id and nothing explains why only the player actor class gets its attachment hidden, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_SetupFromTypeId
summary: Model refresh for one type id: resolves the actor's model id, for characters rolls the 1..100 parameter into self+0x28C, then re-binds up to 32 sub-model slots through their virtual +0xE8/+0xE4 pair; for type 0x116 it stores the difference between the model height and the row's +0x28 value.
evidence: Re-read: two callees are now named (maybe_Model_SelectModelIdForActor and maybe_Battle_IsUnitVisibleInBattle), so the 'resolve model, then rebind sub-models' shape is real, but the two type ids it special-cases (0x5A, 0x116) still cannot be turned into a class name. Stays maybe_.

name: Battle_AddStateFlags
signature: void Battle_AddStateFlags(void* self, unsigned int flags, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Adds state flag bits to a battle actor and, for bit 8 (visible/revive), also notifies the actor's model and plays the associated effect - unless the battle mode byte says it is paused.
evidence: Tail 'self[0x39D] |= arg2', bit-8 path calls vtable+0x30(0,1) and 0x005E7848(handle,8,0); neighbours Battle_ActorAction_ApplyAddedState and Model_AdvanceAnimFrames place it in the actor state path. Named context in the merged C: Battle_ActorAction_ApplyAddedState, Battle_ActorAction_MoveAndSpawnEffect, Battle_ActorAction_ShowDamage, Battle_Ui_UpdateItemCommand, Model_AdvanceAnimFrames.

name: maybe_Actor_SetComponentFlag
summary: Walks the 32 component slots at self+0xE9C: components whose virtual +0xE8 accepts `component` get the +0x134 then +0x120 calls, and a second loop asks every remaining component through +0xF4, falling back to +0x11C.
evidence: The loop is nearly identical to 0x001CB624 (Actor_NotifyComponentEvent), which dispatches an event id over the same 32 slots, so the 'set flag' reading is not proven; the body also has unaff_r4/unaff_r10 spills and the guard call (0x0062BB08) is misnamed.

name: maybe_Actor_QueryChildSlotState
signature: int maybe_Actor_QueryChildSlotState(ActorModel* self, u32 arg2, int slotMask)
summary: 20-byte fragment that scans the 32 child-object slots at self+0xE9C and returns the last non-zero result: for each non-null slot it calls virtual +0xF4 and, when that returns 0, virtual +0x11C.
evidence: Still unreliable: the body reads unaff_r4/r5/r10 and it is the tail loop of 0x001CAFE4 (same +0xF4/+0x11C queries), so the argument split in the signature is a guess.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateComponents
signature: void maybe_Actor_UpdateComponents(void* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned * int arg4)
summary: Updates all 32 components: for each active component it queries the two state virtuals (+0x18 / +0x10) and puts the ones that need it into the run state (+0x30), unless the global mode byte forbids it.
evidence: Callers Model_AdvanceAnimFrames_001ca5dc; Loops 0x20 over f_E9C calling +0x18/+0x10 and then +0x30(component,0,1) after testing the game * mode byte at manager+0x4244; also calls 0x005E7848 and the per-slot side effects. Named context in the * merged C: Model_AdvanceAnimFrames, Os_GetGameWork.

name: Model_BuildUiFilterRecord
summary: Builds a 12-byte filter record on the stack (leading 0xFF, the u16 at self+0x768 and the byte at self+0x74A, plus three values fetched by id 0xDF/0x7D/0x7C through the owner's vtable +0xE8 when owner[4] is set) and hands it to Ui_FilterIdListByRecord(work+0x90, record).
evidence: The single callee is the named Ui_FilterIdListByRecord and the record layout is fully visible in the body, so 'build a UI filter record' is fixed; the three vtable +0xE8 ids are the same status-query slot used elsewhere.

name: maybe_Actor_SetTwoParameters
signature: void maybe_Actor_SetTwoParameters(ActorModel* self, int first, int second)
summary: Resets the model (virtual +0x11C, clears the byte at +0x39D) and then writes two display values through virtuals +0x3C/+0x40; a value of -1 means 'keep the current value', read back through +0x94/+0x9C.
evidence: No named caller or callee was added; virtual +0x11C is the same reset slot used by 0x001CB070/0x001CAFE4, so the reset-then-apply shape is certain, but which two display values are set is not (0x001CBB70 uses the same +0x94/+0x3C pair for its negation).

name: maybe_Model_ApplyParameterBlock
signature: void maybe_Model_ApplyParameterBlock(Model* self, int frame, int stateValue)
summary: Applies a model-parameter block: resolves the record id stored at self+0x1DA through the data manager and copies the block with Model_CopyParamBlock; for its two entries (types 0/1) it checks the current frame against 0.5/0.25 of the entry duration and, when the battle RNG roll (1..100) is within the entry probability, records the supplied state id at self+0x3A5.
evidence: New evidence: the named caller Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility and the named callee Model_CopyParamBlock (a 0x10C-byte block with relocated self-relative pointers) show this is a per-model parameter block, and the two entries are timing+probability driven (frame thresholds 0.5/0.25, RNG at battleWork+0x4218). What the stored state actually selects (visual/behaviour variant) is still unclear, so maybe_ and 0.4.

name: Actor_NotifyComponentEvent
summary: Sends one event id to every component that accepts it: loops the 32 slots at self+0xE9C, gates on virtual +0xE8(eventId), then calls +0x134 and +0x120(eventId,1). Event 0x5A also clears the actor word at +0xE94.
evidence: New context: the first callee 0x00278668 is maybe_Model_SetSlotState, the per-slot notifier that the named Menu_RefreshUnitSlotFlags also calls; the same 32-slot loop is the one in 0x001CAFE4, and the +0x120(component,eventId,1) tail is an event dispatch - so the name describes the body. The class (Actor) is supported by the f_E9C/f_E94 component layout.

name: Actor_ResetComponents
summary: Resets the actor model's components: resets the model slots (Actor_ResetModelSlots), clears the state word at +0xE94 and, when the actor is active, runs the release virtual (+0x11C) of all 32 component pointers at +0xE9C.
evidence: The callee Actor_ResetModelSlots is now named and is also the only caller of this function, forming a clear reset pair; the 32-slot component loop is unchanged.

name: Actor_IsPartCode
signature: int Actor_IsPartCode(ActorModel* self, u32 code code)
summary: Returns 1 when the actor is visible, (f_39D & 0x56)==0 and the part code at +0x74A equals `code`; 0 otherwise.
evidence: New context: the named Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes cites this predicate and 0x001CA4D8 as the writer of the +0x74A code byte, so the part-code comparison is anchored. It is the simpler twin of 0x001CA7E4.

name: Battle_IsUnitKindShownInMemberUi
signature: u32 Battle_IsUnitKindShownInMemberUi(int unit, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns whether a battle unit's kind id is one of the six kinds the member-status UI lists: it resolves the unit's packed model id (f_768) to its parameter block and tests the 16-bit kind against 100, 0x7B, 0x7C, 0x74, 0x83 and 0x84.
evidence: Callers 0x003C64FC (maybe_Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActorsB), 0x004276C0 (maybe_Battle_PrepareUnitListUi), 0x00670794 (Battle_UpdateUnitUiSlots), 0x0066FC40 (Field_ActorSlots_UpdateAll). Body: iVar4 = func_0063DCA4(work, unit->f_768 & 0xffff); sVar1 = *(short*)(iVar4+8); result = (sVar1==100 || 0x7b || 0x7c || 0x74 || 0x83 || 0x84).

name: maybe_Actor_PlayEventSe
summary: Maps an actor event code to a sound effect and plays it on the handle at self+0x110: codes 2/3 -> SE 0x1B, 0x90 -> 0x1C, 8/9 -> 0x28. The handle is validated against the field object registry, and 2/3 is skipped when 0x00669250 reports id 0x1C.
evidence: New context: 0x00669250 is cited by the named Actor_EnsureActionState / * Actor_StartBehaviourFromHandle as the action-state getter, which matches the 'skip if already in that * state' guard; 0x005E7848 is still unnamed in the merged set (the header's 'play SE on object' note is * the only source), so the SE wording stays a maybe_.

name: Field_Actor_QueryFlag7ByModelHandle
summary: Queries state flag 7 of an actor's packed model handle: returns 1 when the global 'field flags disabled' byte at work+0x27C57 is clear, otherwise resolves the packed handle in actor+0x110 through the generation-checked handle table (entry index = (handle >> 10) & mask, generation = handle >> 11, entry stride 8) and asks func_005E7848(entry, 7, 0); returns 0 when the handle is stale.
