evidence: Releases the field object (0x001C863C(ctx+0x54, 4)), zeroes f_15E0/f_15E4, calls 0x00622458 on both screen blocks at +0x54 and +0xB10 and invalidates f_15EC with g_001D2338 (the handle generation helper used by 0x001D484C).

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeActorScreenPosition
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeActorScreenPosition(float* out, void* arg2, void* record, void* camera, void* arg5)
summary: Computes a camera-relative placement point for an actor: takes the camera record's rotation/position (f_8C..f_A4), the model height for the actor id from the data manager and the bytes at arg2+0x32/+0x33, then writes a 3-float point clamped by Camera_FindEntryCoveringPosition.
evidence: Three named field-NPC callers use the result as a point: Field_NpcJumpAction_PlanPath stores it into action+0x48, Field_Npc_UpdateMoveTarget and Field_NpcGetActionAnimId feed the visible-target list. 'Screen' is not literally proven (no projection matrix is built), but the rotation/height/ray-probe body matches an actor placement point, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone
signature: void Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone(void* arg1, const float* position, const float* direction)
summary: Walks the field actor list (list id 4) and, for actors of class 0x7C3684 that pass the state checks, measures the distance and the angle between the given direction and the offset; every actor inside the radius and cone receives a vtable+0x38(0x1B, 0) update call.
evidence: The named caller Ui_SpriteMarker_SetTargetFromActor (0x004772C0) passes the marker's position and direction, and the body performs exactly the list walk + vertical/horizontal/angle cone test (same 0x7A6408 angle scale and +0x38 slot as the camera variant) before notifying each matching actor; the earlier objection was about a missing billboard basis, which the name does not claim.

name: maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius
signature: void maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius(ViewWork* viewWork, float* centre, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actors around a position and detaches the matching ones: asks Field_AttachSlotObject for the actor's slot and, when that succeeds, decrements the view-entry counters +0x15E0/+0x15E4 (state-2 actors use +0x15E4), then clamps the entry height; called from the talk-camera release path.
evidence: Field_AttachSlotObject and Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork are now named, which supports 'detach actors in radius'; the ViewWork class and the counter fields are still inferred.

name: Gfx_SetActiveScreen
summary: Switches which of the two 3DS screens is active by toggling the flags on both screen blocks and refreshing the layout.
evidence: For screen == 3 it sets f_15CC = 1 and calls 0x006226D8(&f_54, 0, &f_15CC) + 0x006226D8(&f_B10, 1, &f_15CC); for screen == 0 the arguments are swapped; both paths then call 0x001D15F4. f_15CC is the screen selector used throughout 0x001D1F14..0x001D462C.

name: Camera_ApplyScreenViewTransforms
summary: Walks the active view-entry lists of the field object manager and, for every entry of render-object class 0x007C3684 that is not in state 2, resolves its state through 0x00669250 and applies the interpolated transform to the two screen views.
evidence: New: the sole caller is now the named Camera_UpdateScreenViews (0x001D50CC), so the subsystem is Camera, not Gfx; the body walks the (work+8)->f_54 lists with filter 4 and keeps only entries whose class word is 0x007C3684.

name: Gfx_ApplyScreenViewFades
summary: Applies the parameter block's fade settings to the screen views it names: for each of the four view ids at params+0x48 (0x0FFFFFFF = end) it resolves the view in the current screen block and calls Gfx_ScreenView_ApplyFadeParams on both view objects (+0x54 and +0xB10), skipping views whose +0x16D byte is set.
evidence: NEW: both callers are now named - Camera_UpdateViewTransition (0x004C82BC, 0.50) and Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C) - and the per-view action is the confident Gfx_ScreenView_ApplyFadeParams (0x00622674), applied to both screen-view blocks. So 'apply the fade parameters' is confirmed and the old 'select view' reading is gone.

name: maybe_Gfx_PlaceAlongViewDirection
summary: Places self at self+0x24 units along the horizontal direction from the camera (work+0x54+0x1C, position f_9C/f_A0/f_A4) towards the player (work+0x74, f_B0..f_C4): normalises the XZ delta, scales it, stores the result in self+0x14/0x18/0x1C and marks self+0x28 = 1.
evidence: The body is a clean direction/normalise/scale/store sequence over the camera and player transforms, and no view matrix is updated; there is no caller, so the 'view direction' wording stays a description - maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkPath
signature: unsigned int Camera_UpdateWorkPath(void* self, int index, unsigned int target, float* output, float* output2)
summary: Advances one camera-work entry along its path: interpolates the current position toward the next key with a random jitter, applies the entry's rotation offset and returns whether the entry is still running.
evidence: Entry = self + f_15CC*g_001D32A0*4 + 0x54 + index*0x1C with the per-entry flag at +0x104 and config pointer at +0x10C; uses 0x00574548/0x00575980 (rotate/transform), 0x0051B1FC (random), 0x0063EEAC (target resolve) and compares the squared distance against the entry radius, then interpolates with g_001D32A8..g_001D32C4.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkPathEx
summary: Camera path state machine helper that branches on Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteVariant and updates screen marker offsets.
evidence: Named neighbours Field_SceneNode_GetPosition and Math_QuatToForwardVector support camera path updating, but sprite marker drawing leaves specific work path role uncertain; kept maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Camera_ResetScreenEntries
summary: Releases the three per-view entry blocks at self+0x54, self+0xB10 and self+0x15F4, then re-registers every actor node (class 0x007C3684, state != 2) whose slot entry flag is still clear by calling 0x005E7848(node, 2, 0).
evidence: New: the sole caller is the named Ui_StatusWindow_ApplySlotFrames (0x001DA348), which calls it on (work+8)->f_4C right after Ui_StatusWindow_AddSlotObjects, i.e. when a status slot becomes visible; the three blocks are 0xABC apart with 32 slots of 0x1C, and the release helper 0x00622480 is a sibling of the named Gfx_ScreenView_ReleaseNamedObjects. 'Camera' is still positional and unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleaseScreenEntries
summary: The list-walk half of 0x001D4200: walks the two lists (0x001C7AD0/0x001C7560, filter 4) until the 0x007C3684 class sentinel and releases each node with 0x005E7848(node, 2, 0) when its slot flag is clear.
evidence: The nodes are class 0x007C3684 and are released through 0x005E7848, whose other callers are the Actor_Action_* state helpers, so this is a generic screen-entry release walk; nothing in the body is camera-specific, so the 'Camera_' prefix is dropped.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList
signature: u32 maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList(CameraWork* cam, int targetId, CameraTargetRecord* rec)
summary: Resolves camera target record; walks visible target slots to commit matching candidate or applies Field_ApplyNpcActionState.
evidence: Combines camera candidate commit (Camera_IsCandidateVisible, Camera_SetupFromRecord) with NPC scene node traversal, giving dual behavior; kept maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkEntry
signature: uint32_t Camera_UpdateWorkEntry(ViewWork* self, CameraOutput* out, int entry, int target)
summary: Fills one camera output record from a work entry: computes the entry address from the view id and entry index, resolves the indexed handle, copies the path/offset/orientation fields and calls Camera_UpdateWorkPath.
evidence: Three named callers (Camera_UpdateTargetList and the two follow-position functions) and the named Camera_UpdateWorkPath callee confirm the entry update, and the entry formula matches 0x001D15AC.

name: Camera_ReleaseProjection
summary: Releases the projection/render state object embedded at +0x15F4.
evidence: Single call 0x003B17C0(self+0x15F4); its twin 0x001D4828 sets that object up with 0x003B1698(&f_15F4, arg2, arg3, f_15CC, f_15CE) - the per-screen (f_15CC) and screen-count (f_15CE) arguments identify it as the projection setup.

name: Camera_SetupProjection
signature: void Camera_SetupProjection(void* self, unsigned int width, unsigned int height)
summary: Configures the projection/render state for the current screen: passes the screen size plus the screen index and count to the render helper.
evidence: 0x003B1698(&self->f_15F4, arg2, arg3, self->f_15CC, self->f_15CE) - the two u16 screen fields are passed straight into the projection setup, and the same pair is released by 0x001D47F0.

name: Camera_ReleaseTargetHandle
summary: Releases the camera's target handle at +0x15EC: resolves the generation-tagged object in g_007B80C0, checks that its class chain reaches 0x007C3684, invokes virtual +0x34 (release) and finally invalidates the handle by setting its generation to 0x1FFFFF.
evidence: New context: the named Gfx_ResetViewHandles (0x001D22D0, 0.5) calls this function as its per-handle release, and Gfx_InitScreenViews/Gfx_ResetScreenViews/Camera_Reset all call that reset routine; the release-and-invalidate shape of the +0x15EC handle is therefore anchored.

name: Camera_SetTargetFromHandle
summary: Sets the camera target for a battle transition: resolves the actor handle, increments the view-entry usage counter and clears its attachment via func_005E7848, then copies the field scene node position into +0x1618..+0x1620 and the data-manager value into +0x15D8.
evidence: Both callers are named (Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle, maybe_Battle_CreateEnemyDisplay) and the body ends by writing the three target position words - a target setter, not a handle resolver. The named Field_SceneNode_GetPosition supplies the position.

name: Camera_RebuildWorkList
summary: Rebuilds the camera work list: drains the pending list at +0x163C, then for every nearby actor of the target class allocates a 0x50-byte work node, copies its transform from func_00178880 and appends it.
evidence: The body first clears and then repopulates the +0x163C list, so "ClearWorkList" described only the first half; the per-actor copy and the named Mem_AllocAligned_2/Os_GetGameWork calls are visible and the only caller is the talk-camera release.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkList
summary: Drains the deferred camera work-request list at +0x163C: for every queued request it re-resolves the referenced camera target slot (0x1C stride, 0x20 slots) or path entry (0x10 stride, 0x10 entries) of the current screen block and commits it with Camera_SetupFromRecord; then it unlinks and frees the request nodes, leaving the list empty.
evidence: Only caller is the now-named Gfx_InitScreenViews, and the per-request commit call is the named Camera_SetupFromRecord. The previous summary ('advances each work entry and rebuilds the list') was wrong: the loop only validates the referenced entry and frees the request node, it never advances an entry. The name is vague but supported.

name: maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate
signature: void maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate(float* arg1, float* from, float* out, uint32_t mode)
summary: Small adapter used by the 'interpolate owner vector' helpers: it builds a 3-word record from its third argument (0x0039CD08) and forwards it with the second argument and the mode word to 0x0039CBBC; the first argument is never read here.
evidence: The five callers (Battle_Unit_ApplyModelParts and four maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVector* helpers) all pass (manager, from, outVector, mode) and the disassembly shows r0 is overwritten before use; the actual interpolation lives in 0x0039CBBC (currently named Text_LayoutSingleLine, an implausible name for this context), so the wrapper's own name stays a guess.

name: Camera_UpdateScreenViews
summary: Per-frame camera view update: when the current camera work is idle and the flag byte at +0x11 is set, it optionally refreshes the follow position, then resets and updates the two screen-view slots at +0x54 (+0x15CC stride 0x2AF*4) and finally calls the shared screen-view updater.
evidence: CORRECTED: 'TryStartWork' missed that the body always resets and updates both screen-view objects after the idle gate; the caller is the named Ui_SceneFlow_Update, the callee set is Gfx_ScreenView_ResetAll/UpdateAll, and the +0x15CC/+0x15DC fields are the same camera work fields used by the named camera path code, so this is the camera's per-frame screen-view update.

name: Camera_Reset
summary: Resets the whole camera object to its idle state: clears the work flags, releases both screen views, invalidates all handles and empties the work list.
evidence: Calls 0x001D22D0, zeroes f_10 and the byte at g_001D52A8+self, calls 0x00622C30 on both screen blocks (+0x54, +0xB10), writes 0xFFFFFFFF/0 sentinels into f_38..f_4C, releases 0x003B1B14 on the projection at +0x15F4 and 0x00708850 on +0x1624/+0x1630, then empties the list at +0x1640.

name: Camera_SetupFromRecord
signature: void Camera_SetupFromRecord(void* self, void* record, unsigned int flags, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Starts a camera work item: resolves the target actor from the record's id, stores the handle in the work slot and copies the target's position and rotation into the camera entry.
evidence: func_001C7370(game+0x54, record->f_C) is Field_CreateActorFromId (named), the result is stored at g_001D5424+self and resolved through g_001D5428/g_001D542C, then the target's f_2C/f_30/f_34 are copied into the work entry at +0x9C..+0xA4. Seven in-batch callers (0x001D15AC, 0x001D15F4, 0x001D1FC4, 0x001D2222, 0x001D233C, 0x001D43C0, 0x001D462C) use it as the common setup step.

name: Party_BuildStatusSnapshot
summary: Rebuilds the per-party-member status snapshot array (one 0x1C-byte entry per member) from the live party records, growing the array once when a new member appears.
evidence: Its named caller Ui_SceneFlow_Update passes self->f_4C (the scene flow's party view) and the body's Party_CountAliveMembers / Party_GetActiveMemberDataByIndex loop builds exactly the per-member entries.

name: Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt1D582C
summary: Constructor stub of a field scene object: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x001D582C, copies the 3-float transform pair from 0x001D5830, sets the class/state bytes (5, 5, 2, 1) and default-constructs the children at +0x54.
evidence: The caller 0x0019CD50 (Field_InitSceneObjects) allocates the object, calls this and stores it, which is the ctor contract; the name only claims the vtable, not a gameplay class, so it can be dropped to non-maybe.

name: Camera_Delete
signature: void Camera_Delete(void* self, unsigned int tag)
summary: Deleting destructor of the camera object: resets the type tag, unlinks the work list, releases the 0xC-byte entry array and the projection object, then frees the memory.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2 (type tag), self-links at +0x1640/+0x1644, 0x00100BE0(arg1+0x1624, g_001D58D0, 0xC, 2) frees the 0xC-byte entries, then 0x003B1EE8(arg1+0x15D8) hands back the projection base which is freed with 0x0010F6CC - the mirror of Camera_Reset (0x001D51E0).

name: Model_SetupFaceParams
summary: Applies a face/expression record to a character model: stores the face id and palette byte (or 0xFFFF/0xFF when the id is -1) and pushes it to the face subsystem.
evidence: Caller is Model_SetupCharacterModel (0x002232FC in N_022) - the named character-model setup. Reads arg2[0] == -1 for the 'no face' sentinel and writes u16 +6 / byte +8, then 0x002D6B2C and 0x0063CFC8/-0x003063E5C8 face-table lookups.

name: Model_SetFaceMode
signature: void Model_SetFaceMode(void* self, int mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Selects the face mode: mode 0 marks an automatic blink (f_18=1, f_20 = random 2..4 frames scaled by *g_001D5ADC, f_1D from maybe_Model_ApplyFaceParamQuad), mode 1 uses the stored f_19, mode 2 uses f_1A, anything else returns. If the face is enabled (byte at self+10 and f_24) it then calls maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation(self,0xFF,f_1D,...).
evidence: The three modes write the face selector f_18 and the face parameter f_1D, the automatic mode arms a random blink timer and the tail drives maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation with the selected parameter - the face reading is in the named callees, not just the layout.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyFaceAndFrameRows
signature: void maybe_Model_ApplyFaceAndFrameRows(void* self, int face, int frame)
summary: Stores one face-table row (maybe_Data_GetEntry8(face)) and one frame-table row (Svc_GetTableRow(frame)) into the 0x158-byte face record selected by self+2 of the model's face owner; 0xFF means 'leave unchanged'. Model_SetFaceMode calls it with face=0xFF, i.e. only the frame row is refreshed.
evidence: Model_SetFaceMode (0.55) passes 0xFF for face and self->f_1D for frame, and the body writes the two table rows into the f_EC (face) and f_104 (frame) halves of the face record, so 'UpdateFaceAnimation' implied animation playback the function does not perform. The body is still damaged (unaff_r4 holds the face owner), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Model_ApplyFaceTexture
summary: Selects and applies the high- or low-detail face texture (Face_high_MT / Face_low_MT) to the model's face material.
evidence: 0xB8 bytes; literal strings Face_high_MT (0x001D5C78) and Face_low_MT (0x001D5C88); calls 0x0011CCA0 (name lookup) and 0x0064179C/0x00659668 (material/texture lookup).

name: Model_UpdateBlinkTimer
summary: Ticks the character's blink and expression timers: decrements the blink countdown, toggles the open/closed state, re-arms from the randomised range, advances the expression state and calls Model_UpdateFaceAnimation when anything changed.
evidence: Four named callers (Gfx_RenderObject_Update, Model_Attach_UpdateChildren, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel, maybe_Model_AttachSlot_ReleaseNode) all run per-frame character updates, and the named Model_ApplyFaceParamQuad/Model_UpdateFaceAnimation close the face pipeline.

name: Model_ApplyFaceParamQuad
summary: Builds one face parameter from the byte at faceParams+1: default-constructs four 4-byte elements from the element constructor 0x005F9720 with that byte as constructor argument and returns the result (the real return is lost to the decompiler's noreturn marking). Called from Model_SetFaceMode for the automatic blink parameter.
evidence: Caller Model_SetFaceMode (0x001D5A10, confidence 0.55) stores the return value into the face parameter f_1D for the automatic blink mode and calls it as maybe_Model_ApplyFaceParamQuad(&self->f_18), and maybe_Model_UpdateBlinkTimer uses the same call, which fixes the face-parameter role.

name: maybe_Model_AllocFaceParamBlock
signature: extern unsigned int Model_AllocFaceParamBlock(int owner, unsigned int size, unsigned maybe_Model_AllocFaceParamBlock;
summary: Allocates an aligned block (vtable 0x00782990) and, for record type 11, sets two GPU-context float parameters (+0xDB4/+0xDB8) by a mode byte (8/9).
evidence: Ghidra decoded this mid-function (unaff_ registers) so the body is unreliable; confidence lowered to 0.30 per the damaged-decompilation rule.

name: Svc_GetTableRow
summary: Returns the address of the 8-byte table row for the given index after asserting that the table has been initialised.
evidence: Checks (*(u8*)(g_001D6050+4) & 1) and calls 0x0010009C(g_001D6058) (an assert/abort with the module name) when it is not, then 'return g_001D6054 + index * 8' - a plain 8-byte row table accessor.

name: Field_GetCurrentPlaceId
summary: Getter: returns 0 unless a map is loaded ((work+8)->+0x88 +8 != 0), otherwise the f_12 field of the scene record from 0x0066A7D8. The sibling 0x001D61D0 is the same function reading f_11.
evidence: The two callers are now named place/message paths (Field_Menu_OpenPlaceMenu, Ui_FieldMessageWindow_InitB) and both use the result as a place id, which fixes the reading; 0x0066A7D8 is the same scene-record getter Field_Npc_GetDefaultFaceIfUnset uses.

name: Model_SetFaceId
summary: Applies a face id to the model: sets it on the global face manager (work+0x4C) and stores the low byte in the model's face block at self+0x70.
evidence: The caller Field_Npc_UpdateFace and the two-call body show a setter for a face id, not a "record" read; the second call is the face-block setter. Name corrected accordingly.

name: Field_ExitTalkMode
summary: Leaves a talk session: when the record asks for mode 1 it clears the game's talk flag, otherwise it stops the running voice/sound, then notifies the message window.
evidence: Caller is maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithTalkData (0x0019E9E4). record[0] == 1 clears bit 0 of *(game+0x2A648), else calls 0x00442270(game+0x74) (the sound/voice manager), then 0x00235A50/0x006F1EEC for the message side.

name: Field_GetCurrentRoomId
summary: Twin of Field_GetCurrentPlaceId (0x001D607C): returns 0 unless a map is loaded, otherwise the f_11 byte of the scene record from 0x0066A7D8, i.e. the room id next to the place id at f_12.
evidence: NEW: the sibling 0x001D607C is now confidently named Field_GetCurrentPlaceId and reads f_12; this copy is otherwise identical and reads f_11, and its callers are the named Field_Menu_OpenJumonWindow and maybe_Ui_FieldMessageWindow_Init, which need the current room. The place/room assignment of the two bytes is consistent but still inferred.

name: Field_SetupTalkParams
signature: void Field_SetupTalkParams(void* self, void* actor, void* record, unsigned char* params)
summary: Configures a talk/event: converts the frame counts in the global tables to time, copies the parameter block into the object and forwards the actor to the message, face and effect sub-systems.
evidence: Every duration is computed as '*g_001D65B8 * 0x3C' (frames -> 60 ticks) and handed to 0x00113590 as a timer; then 20 fields are copied from arg4 into self, and the actor is passed to 0x001D9870/0x00235E0C/0x001D97B8/0x001D8E2C/0x003DA214/0x001D18E0/0x004AC050. The face-mode branch reads game+0x48+0x281 == 8/9 (the two screen/face modes).

name: maybe_Field_Talk_SetupFromRecord
summary: When record[0] is 1, lazily creates the shared 0x98-byte UI object, clears the current-map flag, initialises the talk state at self+0x14, starts the pending view and applies the object at self+0xB8.
evidence: NEW: the two callers are now Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2 and Field_EffectDesc_Build, and the named callee Ui_SetCurrentMapFlag shows the map-flag clear; this is talk/scene setup driven by a record, not creation of a 'talk record'. The object class and the last two callees are still unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: Field_ResetTalkState
summary: Resets the field talk/event state before the next scene: refreshes the UI overlay slots (work+0x48), selects the character on the field scene (work+0x88), registers the actor tables and forwards the map-jump event record at self+0x18.
evidence: The named callees (Field_HandleMapJumpEvent, Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter, maybe_Model_RegisterActorTables) and the sole caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2 now cover the whole body, confirming a talk-state reset at scene open.

name: Field_HandleMapJump
summary: Handles a map jump/area transition: frees the current map resources and loads the destination map with its entry point.
evidence: 0x1E8 bytes; calls 0x0011CFAC/0x0011CFDC/0x0011FE8C (frees) and 0x00613528/0x0063CCxx (map/area lookup), 0x00237198; globals g_001d6944..g_001d6954 hold the transition state.

name: Field_EffectDesc_Build
summary: Builds a 0x70-byte field effect/object descriptor: writes the defaults, and for each of the two global enable flags evaluates a source 3-vector pair, averages it, scales it and links the resulting block into the descriptor's list heads; returns desc+0x70.
evidence: NEW: it is called by BOTH confident descriptor builders - Field_Effect_BuildDescA and Field_Effect_BuildDescB (each 0.8) - i.e. the function the two named paths share is exactly 'build the descriptor', which is much stronger than the first pass's constant-shape argument.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectCtor
summary: Constructor of a scene object with three sub-objects: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x00759F88, seeds the default vectors/ids and the 0.3f field, then chains the sub-constructors 0x002F2678, Ui_SlotTable_Ctor (0x003DAE90) and 0x004AC9B0. No caller (factory-table constructed), so the class is still unidentified.
evidence: Ui_WindowState_Init + Ui_SlotTable_Ctor as callees show the object contains a UI slot table, so the first pass 'Field_ObjectCtor' may be the wrong subsystem; but vtable 0x00759F88 has no other user and no string/caller identifies the class, so it remains an honest maybe_ with the UI content described.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeleteThunk
summary: Bare deleting-destructor thunk: stores the given vtable word in the object's first field and tail-calls the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC. The compiler folded a self = self+0xB8-0x48-0x14-0x5C adjustment into the instruction, so the net argument is the object itself.
evidence: Nothing new beyond the now-documented meaning of 0x0010F6CC (refcounted operator delete: header at object-8, vtable+4 release), which makes 'delete thunk' safe; the owning UI class is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: Gfx_Movie_ReadThreadEntry
summary: Thread entry for the movie read pump: when the stream has its +4 word set it starts Gfx_Movie_ReadThread (the ring-buffer pump) and returns 0 so the thread exits cleanly.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the confident Gfx_Movie_ReadThread, and the 24-byte body is only the conditional pump start plus 'return 0' - the standard thread-entry trampoline. Nothing in the body releases or closes the stream, so the first-pass 'ReleaseStreamIfOpen' direction was wrong.

name: Ui_Object_DeleteThunkPlain
summary: Plain deleting destructor: the whole body is a tail call to the custom operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: New context: 0x0010F6CC is now the delete helper cited by the named Ui_Layout_DeleteSubComponent, Ui_Widget_DeleteSub and Ui_FadeWindow_Destroy, and the vtable reference 0x759F9C places this slot among the pooled UI object deleters, so 'delete thunk' is exactly what the 8-byte body does.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorPooledB
summary: Deleting destructor of a pooled object: installs vtable 0x00759FAC, destroys the child at +0x2C through vtable+4 and clears the field, releases the child at +0x28 through vtable+0xC, destroys the list at +8 when the flag at +0x18 is set, clears the pool slot 0x007B5D70[(u16 at +4) & 0x3FF] and frees the block.
evidence: Same pool-deallocator tail (func_0010F6CC) and intrusive-list destroy idiom as 0x0017C570, now that std_RbTree_EraseNode is confident (0.65); the class behind vtable 0x00759FAC is still unidentified and there are no callers, so the B suffix stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_CreateSpriteMesh
summary: Creates engine sprite mesh named 'sprite' for UI widget and links into widget draw hierarchy.
evidence: Calls confident Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh and Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance; table 0x00759FC4 has widget methods, but specific widget subclass is unverified. Kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Ui_Widget_IsTouchActive
summary: Advances the widget's touch record at +0x4D8 through Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition and reports whether it has not reached the finished state 3.
evidence: The +0x4D8 record is the touch record filled by the RefreshTouchInfo family in this batch and advanced by the named Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition, so 'sprite busy' was the wrong object.

name: maybe_ListNode_DeletingDtorA

name: Event_UpdateIdSet

name: maybe_Event_ActivateFlagAndClearSlot

name: Menu_ProcessEntryQueue
signature: void Menu_ProcessEntryQueue(int queue, u32 type, u32 id)
summary: Drains the pending-entry byte queue of a menu: for each queued id it resolves the record and, when the record matches (type, id), either re-enables the row (command 8) or pushes it as a disabled entry (command 7) and appends it to the list at work+0x10->+0xA4; the special type 0xE3 clears matching rows in all 0x5A slots.
evidence: Callers 0x0020F600 (maybe_Menu_OpenMessageWindow), 0x0020F728 (maybe_Menu_CloseMessageWindows). Body: queue begin/cursor at arg1+4/+8; `iVar2 = func_0063D338(work, byte)`; `uVar3 = *(u8*)(iVar2+8); if (uVar3 == 3) uVar3 = *(u16*)(iVar2+10); if (uVar3 == arg2 && iVar2->f_1c == arg3)`; then `(**(code**)(*list+0xc))(list, id, 8)` or `(list, id, 7)` plus `func_003F294C(*(int*)(*(int*)(*g+0x10)+0xa4), entry)`; the type 0xE3 branch loops 0x5a ids and calls `(**(code**)(*piVar12+0xc))(piVar12, id, 0)` when the record's u16 at +6 matches.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry

name: Sound_RefreshPendingBgmVolume
summary: Re-applies the pending BGM volume when it changes: reads the sound singleton (0x006F1DF8), picks field +0x58 or +0x64 depending on flag bit 2, clamps values >= 0x9E to 0xFF, compares with the cached key state[4] and calls Snd_ApplyPendingBgmVolume when they differ.
evidence: New context: the callee is the now-named Snd_ApplyPendingBgmVolume, so the 'apply pending BGM volume' half is certain; 'Refresh' plus the cache key wording is the only inference, and six scene/BGM entry points still call it without naming the state block.

name: Snd_StopPausedBgm
summary: Stops the BGM stream that was paused for a menu/loading screen: fetches the active player through 0x6F1DF8 and calls Snd_StopPendingBgm on it.
evidence: `local_8[0] = in_r3; func_006F1DF8(local_8); func_001EC55C(local_8[0]);` and caller StopPauseBGM (plus LoadRespawnJump) fix the intent; 0x6F1DF8 is the global player/work accessor used by the other Snd_* functions.

name: Snd_RequestEncounterSound
summary: Selects and requests the sound for an encounter/battle: looks the battle id up in two game tables (0x0063CC1C then 0x0063D9BC), and only when the resulting id differs from the one the sound player is currently using does it stop the old sound (0x001EE220) and request the new one (0x001EC1D0). The id is a small table value (< 0x9E) and is played back through the sound player's request queue, so this is the battle BGM / monster battle sound selection, not a script-level call.
evidence: Called from EncountEventEx with the battle id whenever the encounter is a normal one. Body: `e = func_0063CC1C(*ctx, battleId); if (e && e[5] != 0xff) { r = func_0063D9BC(*ctx, e[5]); if (r) id = r[8]; }` then `cur = (snd[4] & 2) ? snd[0x64] : snd[0x58]; if (cur != id) { func_001EE220(); func_001EC1D0(snd, id); }`. `snd` comes from func_006F1DF8, which sibling batch N_077 names Sound_GetPlayer; 0x001EC1D0 queues an id into the 64-entry ring at +0x1848 (rejects ids >= 0x9E) and 0x001EE220 flushes it. N_032 independently proposed Snd_RequestBgmPlay for 0x001EC1D0, which is consistent but not proven, hence the neutral 'sound' wording.

name: maybe_Sound_ApplyCategoryBgmState
signature: void maybe_Sound_ApplyCategoryBgmState(u32 arg1, u32 category, int soundId)
summary: Routes a sound by category: looks the id up in the sound table (func_0063F1E0), finds the 2-byte {category, mode} row and applies the mode - 1 stops the pending BGM (Snd_StopPendingBgm + 0x001EE220), 2 does nothing, anything else applies the pending volume through 0x001EE018; categories 3/4 default to mode 2 when no row matches.
evidence: NEW: the named callees are Snd_StopPendingBgm, Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle and the volume setter 0x001EE018, and the record is a category->mode table, so the function routes a sound's category; it does not select a BGM track as 'SetBgmForCategory' claimed. All eight callers are still mid-confidence menu param helpers, hence maybe_.

name: Snd_CommitPendingBgmId
summary: Commits a queued BGM id: compares it with the current and pending stream ids, chooses between 'request play' and 'request stop', then clears the pending flags.
evidence: `func_006F1DF8(&player); if (*(char*)(arg1+6) == 0) { cur = (player[4] & 2) ? player->f_64 : player->f_58; if (cur == id) goto clear; if (player->f_60 == id) { func_001EE4F8(); goto clear; } } func_001EC1D0(player, id); clear: *(u8*)(arg1+6) = 0; if (*(char*)(arg1+5) != -1) *(u8*)(arg1+5) = 0xff;` - called by PlayFieldBGM and the field event paths.

name: Sound_ResolveFieldBgmId
signature: void Sound_ResolveFieldBgmId(BgmState* state, const BgmRecord* record)
summary: Resolves the background-music track for a map/scene record: picks the day/night or field variant from the record's bytes, honours the player's music setting and stores the chosen track id in the state.
evidence: Two named field-scene callers (Ui_MessageWindow_ShowTalkData, Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2) and the named Sound_GetPlayer setting check support the BGM resolution reading, and the record/track fields are unchanged.

name: Snd_ApplyEncounterSound
signature: void Snd_ApplyEncounterSound(SoundPlayer* snd, u32 battleId, int force)
summary: Applies the sound of an encounter: looks the battle record up (0x63F1E0), compares its sound/BGM id (f_33) with the player's current id and, when they differ (or when force is set and the record's f_3A/f_39 flags allow it), stops the current effect and calls Snd_RequestBgmPlay with the record's id.
evidence: The tail call is now the named Snd_RequestBgmPlay, the sound player comes from the named Sound_GetPlayer and one caller is the named Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle; the record fields are still unnamed but the routine is clearly the 'apply this encounter's sound' step.

name: Snd_ResolveSceneBgmId
signature: void Snd_ResolveSceneBgmId(SndBgmRequest* request, unsigned short* sceneInfo)
summary: Resolves which BGM should play for a scene: looks the scene/field id up in the sound tables, walks the per-zone entries and their story/time-of-day conditions, and stores the first matching sound id (or 0 = silence) into the request.
evidence: Uses the sound tables through 0x0063CC1C/0x0063D9BC/0x0063F82C (id -> entry -> zone list), the story flags at Work+0x2A444/0x27508 via 0x006F20C0+0x0066B17C, and the per-entry condition bytes (+2/+3 = day/night, +4/+6 = condition ids). `*(char*)(arg1+4) = cVar11;` writes the result. Callers: RequestChangeFieldBGMEx, PlayFieldBGM, 0x1A0AE4, 0x1A1DBC, 0x1A342C and the battle paths.

name: Snd_PlayBgmById
signature: void Snd_PlayBgmById(SndBgmRequest* request, unsigned int soundId)
summary: Starts a BGM id directly: if it differs from the playing and pending ids it requests the play (or resumes the pending stream when it matches), then clears the pending flag.
evidence: `func_006F1DF8(&player); if (*(char*)(arg1+6) == 0) { cur = (player[4] & 2) ? player->f_64 : player->f_58; if (cur == arg2) return; if (player->f_60 == arg2) { func_001EE4F8(); goto clear; } } func_001EC1D0(player, arg2); clear: *(u8*)(arg1+6) = 0;` - called by PlayBGM (the Squirrel native) and 0x1634CC, which fixes it as the immediate-play path.

name: Ui_Widget_ResetPair
summary: When the ownership check 0x00630B04(self, self+0x980) succeeds, resets the two child widgets at +0x930 and +0x8E0 (stop the shake tween, set the frame, snap the value).
evidence: The three named animation calls and the guard are unchanged; it is a small reset helper for two child widgets, exactly as named.

name: Ui_BalloonWindow_BindLayout
summary: Loads the "hud_balloon" layout into the balloon window's sub-widget slot and enters the sub-widget, so the balloon can be shown.
evidence: self->f_108 = 1 then 0x001D85EC(self,&self->f_138,s_hud_balloon_001f3f68,0) followed by the noreturn sub-widget entry 0x0029126C(&self->f_138,0) - exactly the pattern of 0x001DA780 (background pane).

name: maybe_Ui_Scene_Dtor
summary: Teardown of a UI object that owns several child lists: checks the two state flags, releases the render node through its virtual +0x2C, destroys the sub-lists at +0x8E0/+0x930, empties the two pools at +0x138 and refreshes the overlay billboard.
evidence: The named callees Ui_List_DestroyTwoPools and Ui_Overlay_UpdateBillboard confirm the list/pool teardown, but no caller or vtable entry names the owning class, so 'Ui_Scene' remains a placeholder for 'the class that owns these lists'.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_SetAnchorVectors
signature: void maybe_Ui_Balloon_SetAnchorVectors(UiBalloon* self, float* from, float* to, u32 slotId)
summary: Validates balloon slot via func_00630B04 and passes from/to 3D coordinate vectors to func_001CA02C on self+0x138.
evidence: Operates on balloon anchor coordinates; slot validation via func_00630B04 is shared with speech balloon routines.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_BindActorHandle
signature: void maybe_Ui_Balloon_BindActorHandle(UiBalloon* self, u8 slot, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, * u32* handle)
summary: Stores the slot index in self+0x839 and sets self+0x838=1 when the passed handle resolves in the field object registry, then tail-calls 0x00100B74 with arg3.
evidence: New context: the handle test (generation at >>11, mask 0x7FF, g_007B80C0) is the same one the * confirmed Field_AttachObjectFromHandle uses, but the function does not store the handle itself and * 0x00100B74 is a shared trampoline/assert path, so 'bind actor handle' overstates what the body shows.

name: Ui_CompositeWindowCtor_vt1F4358
summary: The composite-window constructor for vtable 0x1F4358: it allocates, builds two intrusive lists, chains the panel ctor and two AnimRefLists and returns the outer pointer.
evidence: The recovered body writes uRam001f4358 as the vtable, sets up the 0x47..0x4D list heads, calls 0x001CA238 (panel ctor) and 0x003E0454 twice, and returns iVar4-0x930; the vtable address in the name is directly observed.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorChain
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a widget with a long relative member chain: releases two panes, an object array and the list heads, and returns the enclosing pointer.
evidence: It calls the maybe_ helper Ui_Object_ReleaseArray and no named ctor shares its layout; 'DtorChain' only describes the shape.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_GetSeIdForSlot
summary: Retrieves balloon sub-object for specified slot via virtual method +0x60 and maps its +0x110 attribute using func_005F5818; returns 0 if slot is empty.
evidence: Returns a value. Slot accessor via virtual +0x60; func_005F5818 resolves audio/effect attributes.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_GetSeIdForLeader
summary: Specialized version of 0x001F43E0 querying slot 0 (leader) via virtual method +0x60 and returning mapped attribute from func_005F5818.
evidence: Returns a value in r0 preserved from func_005F5818 (Ghidra dropped return in C); getter. Slot 0 counterpart of 0x001F43E0.

name: Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor
signature: void Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor(UiBalloonUi* ui, int type, BalloonTarget* target, int count, u32 flag, float delay)
summary: Shows a balloon over an actor: computes the anchor's clamped screen position, picks the balloon sprite/frame for the requested type and hands it to the balloon manager together with the count and delay.
evidence: Resolves the anchor through 0x005F5818(target->f_110) and reads its f_9c/f_a0/f_a4; looks up a vertical offset with 0x0063EEAC(target->f_768); clamps the screen position with the g_001f4c40..g_001f4c58 constants and finally 0x003246F0(balloonManager, type+flag, count, &pos). 24 callers across field and battle UI (0x003C3F5C, 0x001F4CA0, 0x001FB4A4...).

name: Ui_Balloon_SpawnByCount
signature: void Ui_Balloon_SpawnByCount(UiBalloonUi* ui, int count, u32 arg3, BalloonTarget* target, u32 flag, u32 delay)
summary: Shows a balloon for a count: plain balloon for zero/negative counts, otherwise the counted variant with the type chosen from the target's flag.
evidence: if (arg2 < 1) 0x001F4478(ui,0xf,arg4,0,arg5,arg6); else type = (arg4->f_10 != 0) ? 3 : 0 and 0x001F4478(ui,type,arg4,arg2,arg5,arg6). 26 callers - the most common entry point to the balloon system.

name: Ui_Balloon_SpawnForMember
signature: void Ui_Balloon_SpawnForMember(UiBalloonUi* ui, int count, PartyMember* member, int skipFlag, u32 seId, u32 delay, u32 extra)
summary: Shows a balloon over one party member, inserts the bookkeeping entry into the balloon list and plays the matching sound effect.
evidence: If count<1 it spawns type 0xf and inserts a local record (type 9, member, id 0xffff...) into the list at ui->f_122c->f_bc via 0x003FBE4C; otherwise it calls member vtable +0x3c/+0x90/+0x94, inserts a type-3 record with 0x003FE904 and plays 0x001EBC68 (Sound_PlaySeById) with arg5.

name: Ui_Balloon_UpdateForMember
signature: void Ui_Balloon_UpdateForMember(UiBalloonUi* ui, u32 count, PartyMember* member)
summary: Refreshes the balloon over a party member: either updates the plain balloon or re-runs the counted balloon, stopping the member's effect when it is not active.
evidence: Checks member vtable +0x10/+0x38/+0x44/+0x98 and target->f_10, clears byte +0xf21, releases/re-creates the member effect (0x0031F204, vtable+0x14 -> f_78=0xff) and uses 0x00631B24/0x00631BE0 for the counted variant.

name: Battle_Ui_Update
summary: Large per-frame update of the battle UI: consumes the queued input state, tests the 16 party/target slots through the ui::State predicates, resolves the acting member (func_0035EB98) and the current RNG roll, and dispatches to the slot reset/select, balloon and target-list helpers of the battle UI module. Returns the UI's done flag.
evidence: Every callee is now named and belongs to this module (Battle_BuildTargetSlotsForCommand, maybe_Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot, maybe_Battle_Ui_SelectBalloonSlot, maybe_Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots(Ex), Battle_QueueActionEx) and the routine is reached through a vtable slot (no direct caller), which is what a per-frame UI update looks like.

name: Battle_IsActionQueueIdle
summary: True while the battle has nothing to do: if no actor is running an action (battle work+0x4320 empty) it returns true, otherwise it defers to Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty on the current actor.
evidence: Named callee Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty is the decisive test and the six callers are the battle UI update paths (e.g. Battle_Ui_UpdateSequence); the old Ui_IsIdle name hid that the test is on the current actor/action queue, not on a window.

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForMember
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForMember(u32 ui, s16* textId, int argument, PartyMember* member, u32 extra)
summary: Starts a balloon/message on a party member, applies the member state and (for the item state 0x74) the item effect, then refreshes the balloon list entry.
evidence: The member vtable +0x2C(text id) call, the 0x74 item-state branch and the balloon-list refresh match the named sibling StartBalloonForSlot's flow.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnSoundBalloon
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnSoundBalloon(BattleBalloonUi* ui, int count, PartyMember* member, u32 delay, u32 flag)
summary: Plays SE 0x12B and, unless the UI busy flag is set, resets the member's displayed value with the count; when delay is zero it then shows the type-9 balloon at the member's anchor.
evidence: Both callees are named (Sound_PlaySeById, Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor) and the ids are literal (SE 0x12B, balloon type 9); the member vtable +0x40 reset is the same one used by the sibling balloon spawners in this family. The decompiler swapped the member/count operands, but the type-9 balloon plus dedicated SE is exactly a 'sound balloon'.

name: Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons
signature: void Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons(float* outPos, PartyMember* member, int arg3, int flag)
summary: Computes where a member's balloons go: counts the member's active slots, averages their anchor positions (single slot: use the anchor itself), lerps the result toward the camera focus and writes the 3-float position, returning it to the caller.
evidence: 19 call sites, all balloon/message placement code that consumes the position (Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchors, Battle_Ui_LayoutMessageBalloons, FieldParty_MoveActorTowardTarget), and the body is exactly the slot count + anchor average + lerp.

name: Model_GetAttachmentWorldPosition
signature: void Model_GetAttachmentWorldPosition(float * out, u32 arg2, int attachment, u32 arg4, u32 partId)
summary: Computes the world position of a model attachment point: it resolves the attachment's node record, looks the node up by name in the model, reads its local transform, rotates the offset by the model's orientation and adds the model position.
evidence: Caller 0x001F9E20 = maybe_Battle_Ui_GetPartyCenter. Body: `iVar3 = func_005F5818(attachment->f_110)` (model object); `func_0063FDAC(work, attachment->f_768)` -> model record; `func_002D6AF8(work, modelId, record->f_5e)` -> node record; `func_00633C38(root, node)` = Model_GetNodeIdByName (named in N_074 out); `func_00633DCC(root, id, &matrix)`; local = node->f_4/8/c + record->f_10/14/18; `func_00574548(&local_80,&local_38,&local_28)` (vector*matrix); then out = local_64 + model->f_9c, local_54 + model->f_a0, local_44 + model->f_a4. The f_9C/0xA0/0xA4 position triple is used identically in 0x001F9C04 and 0x001E184C.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_HideMemberBalloons
summary: Clears the balloon flag on every visible member slot (unless the UI is in hidden mode) so the balloons disappear for this frame.
evidence: It loops func_00630DC8() slots calling vtable +0x48 and clearing one flag byte per member, which matches the description, but there is no caller and the flag offset is unverified.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateMemberBalloons
summary: Updates one battle member's balloon row: takes the id pair from the object's own vtable (+0x48 and +0x60), resolves it with 0x00632760(world+0x5C,...), then compares it against the four actor lists (world+0x5C+0x4298) and the monster/actor tables (0x0063FD24, 0x0063E5C8), storing the mode byte at self+0x494.
evidence: The vtable id pair, the 0x00632760 lookup and the four-list scan are confirmed; 'balloons' is * only inferred from the surrounding 0x001F6D64/0x001F86D4 slot arrays, and no string names it.

name: Battle_QueueBattleMessage
signature: void Battle_QueueBattleMessage(void* self, u32 msgId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructs and enqueues a battle dialogue message with parameters into the battle message queue.
evidence: Calls Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry (0x003FBE4C) with message parameters.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeC
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnBalloonTypeC(BattleBalloonUi* ui, u32 count, PartyMember* member, int skipFlag, u32 delay, u32 flag)
summary: Resets the member's displayed value, appends a type-5 bookkeeping record for (member, count) to the balloon list at ui+0xBC, plays SE 0x1E and, unless skipFlag is set, shows the type-0xC balloon at the member's anchor. The old 'Cancel' label was an unverified reading of balloon type 0xC.
evidence: The body is fully readable and contains no cancellation logic: member vtable +0x40 reset, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnBalloonEntry with record type 5, Sound_PlaySeById(0x1E), then Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor(type 0xC). Its named sibling Ui_Balloon_SpawnForMember uses type 6 the same way, so the numeric balloon type is the only provable fact; 'Cancel' was invented.

name: Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots
signature: void Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots(void* self, const u8* spec, const int* ids, int count)
summary: Clears the 16 dword balloon slots at self+0x70..0xAC and refills them with the non-null unit ids; when spec[3] asks for two or more rows it first copies the ids into a 0x68-byte temporary and picks them through the battle RNG 0x001CA474(world+0x4218, 0, n-1).
evidence: The receiver is the balloon UI (the 0x001F6xxx block holds dozens of named Battle_Ui_*Balloon* routines), the callers are the named Battle_Ui_Update and Battle_ActorAction_UpdateAnchor, and the battle RNG at battleWork+0x4218 is the documented one.

name: Battle_Ui_GetBalloonAnchor
signature: void Battle_Ui_GetBalloonAnchor(float* out, PartyMember* member, int slot, int flag, u32 arg5)
summary: Computes the world position a battle balloon should float above: takes the member's record (virtual +0x40) or the module default, uses the member's f_9C/f_A4 base position and offsets it per balloon slot, then converts it with the shared 3D-to-screen transform helpers.
evidence: Both callers are now named balloon layout functions (Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchors, Battle_Ui_LayoutMessageBalloons) and the callees (Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, func_005736A0 screen transform) match an anchor computation.

name: Battle_Ui_UpdateFinishedBalloons
summary: Walks the balloon UI's 32 effect entries and, for the finished ones, plays the completion sound (0x1A/0x1B) through the balloon helper depending on the entry state.
evidence: The loop bound 0x20 over entries at self+0x164, the finished check via virtual +0x10 and the two sound ids are explicit; named callers are UI tick paths (Battle_Actor_UpdateDispatch, Battle_PartyMember_Update).

name: Battle_Ui_CanSelectBalloonSlots
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_CanSelectBalloonSlots(void* self, const char* spec, void* slotList, void* units, int unitCount)
summary: Validates the current balloon selection: counts the 16 occupied slots at +0x1C and walks them, rejecting candidates whose slot/row test fails or whose unit does not report battle state 8/10; returns 1 when the request is acceptable, 0 otherwise. It never writes a selection.
evidence: It is the gate immediately before Battle_Ui_Update proceeds with the chosen slot; 0x00639954 is the battle-status test (FACTS.md), not a text-type test, and the body only returns 0/1 - so the inherited 'Select' verb was misleading.

name: Actor_EnsureActionState
signature: u32 Actor_EnsureActionState(Actor* actor, u32 arg2, int actionId)
summary: Makes sure an actor is playing the wanted action: returns 1 when it already is, otherwise starts that action and returns the result.
evidence: if (0x00669250(actor) != actionId) return 0x005E7848(actor,actionId,0); else return 1. 0x005E7848 is the actor action dispatch used throughout the field code (0x002340B0 also calls it).

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForSlot
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, s16* textId, u32 slot, u32 argument, int argument2)
summary: Starts a balloon on the member in the given slot: resolves the member, applies the text, updates the balloon list and handles the state-0x79 (item) case.
evidence: The slot-indexed member lookup through vtable+0x48 and the item-state 0x79 branch distinguish it from the member-pointer variant 0x001F5D14.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_DismissLeaderBalloon
summary: Dismisses leader balloon: retrieves slot 0 via virtual +0x48, sets completed flag +0x108 = 1, clears active flag +0xB0F9, and increments instance counter.
evidence: Called by maybe_Battle_Ui_NotifyUnitHighlight (0x00424F5C); operates on leader balloon slot via virtual +0x48.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_GetSeIdForMemberSlot
summary: Retrieves party member balloon using func_001F9B58(self, slot, 0) and resolves attribute word +0x110 with func_005F5818; returns 0 if absent.
evidence: Returns a value. Called with 16-slot accessor func_001F9B58 used by Battle_Ui_Balloon_MoveToAnchor and Battle_ShowMonsterPairPopup.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_GetSeIdForEvent
summary: Retrieves event balloon through virtual method +0x4C and maps attribute +0x110 via func_005F5818; returns 0 if absent.
evidence: Returns a value; getter. Identical structure to 0x001F43E0 but queries accessor vtable +0x4C rather than +0x60.

name: Battle_Ui_PlayMemberSound
signature: void Battle_Ui_PlayMemberSound(void* self, int state, PartyMember* member, u32 seId, int argument)
summary: Plays the sound that belongs to a party member's battle state: maps the state codes (-1, 0, -3, -4, -5, -9, -0xB, -0x11, -0x19, -0x1A) to a small set of SE ids (0x129, 0x12A, 0x158 ...) and plays them, with a separate branch when the battle flag at work+0x4244 is set.
evidence: The state-to-SE ladder is entirely visible and every branch ends in the named Sound_PlaySeById; the seId lookup func_0063E60C on the data manager is used for the 'voice' variant, which is why 'member sound' (not 'menu SE') is the safe wording.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloon
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloon(u32 owner, int textId, BattleUnit* member, int useAnchor)
summary: Spawns the balloon effect for one member: remaps the text id to 0x46B when the member is in the item state (0x79), computes the anchor from the member model node and creates the 2-D effect instance through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: The named callee Effect_FindOrCreateInstance targets the 2-D effect manager (work+0x60), and the 0x79 state remap matches 0x001F8010/0x001F5D14; "balloon" is the project's established word for these text-carrying effects.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonEx
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonEx(BattleBalloonUi* self, int textId, int member, int* out)
summary: Variant of 0x001F7E10 that walks all sixteen member slots, averages/uses their anchor positions and spawns the balloon effect for each valid member when the battle work's +0x4244 flag is set.
evidence: Same remap and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call as 0x001F7E10, plus the 16-slot loop and the +0x4244 gate - so "Ex" means the all-slots variant.

name: Battle_QueueAction
signature: void Battle_QueueAction(BattleUnit* actor, u32 actionRef, u32 actionId)
summary: Queues a battle action for a unit: builds the action record (with the unit's slot and instance counter) and inserts it into the battle action list.
evidence: Builds a record {type = g_001f8530, instance = self->f_b4, ...} and calls Battle_InsertActionSlot(0x0016F28C)(battle, battle->f_124, record, actionId, self->f_c4, 1). 0x0016F28C is already named Battle_InsertActionSlot by another batch, and 8 action/UI functions call this helper.

name: Battle_QueueActionEx
summary: Queues a fully populated battle action record for a unit (the variant used by skills/items that need the whole parameter block).
evidence: Same skeleton as 0x001F84A4 but with a large local record (0x100-byte stack frame) filled from the caller before Battle_InsertActionSlot(0x0016F28C); 12 callers, all battle action code (0x003C2F80, 0x003CB3D0, 0x005955BC...).

name: Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlotsEx
signature: void Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlotsEx(void* self, const u8* spec, int first, int idsBase, int count)
summary: Same 16-slot wipe as 0x001F6D64, then filters the unit ids: a negative 'first' picks one id through the battle RNG, otherwise only entries whose virtual +0xD4 equals 'first' (or the random pick) are kept before the slots are filled.
evidence: Body is a superset of the now-confirmed Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots with an extra vtable+0xD4 filter per entry; both functions are called from the named Battle_Ui_Update in the balloon-target selection branches.

name: Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor
signature: void Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor(u32* out, PartyMember* member, int mode, u32 arg4, u32 member2)
summary: Returns the on-screen anchor of a member's balloon: mode 0 delegates to 0x001FA480, modes 1/2 take the cached offsets at member+0x37/+0x40, and the point is converted to screen space with the shared transform helpers.
evidence: Callers are the named balloon layout routines (Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchors, Battle_Ui_LayoutMessageBalloons) and the sibling 0x001F9874 is the same anchor family.

name: Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot
signature: void Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, const u8* filter, int* outSlot, int argument, int* outObj, int argument2)
summary: Scans the battle unit list at battlework+0x4260 for the first entry that matches the filter record (bytes +1/+2) and whose virtual queries pass, then returns the entry and its slot index through the out pointers.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Battle_Ui_Update calls it as FindTargetSlot(self,input,...,&out) inside the target-cursor update, and its plural sibling 0x003CC520 calls it to fill the multi-target list; the battle-work walk (+0x4260) is explicit in the body.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_GetFirstRowParam
summary: Retrieves row 0 via virtual row accessor +0x48 and returns its attribute word at +0x110.
evidence: Returns a value; getter. Installed across 93 UI screen vtables alongside balloon/party panel methods.

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForAll
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForAll(BattleBalloonUi* self, s16* textId, int slot, u32 argument)
summary: Starts a balloon on every member (or one member when a slot is given) and refreshes the balloon list entry for each of them.
evidence: The slot<0 branch loops over the member count and applies the same per-member balloon call as the single-slot branch, so the 'for all' behaviour is visible in the body.

name: maybe_Battle_CollectModelChildren
summary: Walks the container's slots through vtable +0x48 and registers every idle child that has a live model (f_10 == 0 and func_00279C14 != 0) with the model list at self[0x48B]+0x35C.
evidence: NEW: the count helper 0x00630DC8 is the one used by the named Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel, and 0x00279C14 is the model-alive test used by the row helpers; the registration target is still only known as an object list, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_GetFirstRowKind
summary: Returns kind byte +0x10 of row 0 retrieved through virtual method +0x48, or 0 if row is missing.
evidence: Returns a value; getter. Reads byte +0x10 used as visibility/kind gate in companion row helpers.

name: Battle_Ui_PlaySeForEvent
summary: Plays the sound for a battle UI event: events -4/-0x19 play the id 0x12A+7, events -5/-0x1A play the same id but return whether it actually started, and every other event plays 0x12A; when the battle flag work+0x4244 is set some events are suppressed.
