name: maybe_FieldParty_PlayStateSe
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_PlayStateSe(int* self, int model, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Plays a one-shot SE/voice for a model that entered state 0x76 or 0x11B, using the 32-entry bookkeeping table at self+0xB1 (stride 0x1F: model, count, already-played byte) so each model plays once; the SE id comes from the record's +0x5A or defaults to 0xA0.
evidence: Re-read: there is no attachment call anywhere in the body (the old 'PlaySeForAttachmentChange' was unsupported), and the neighbouring named functions FieldParty_PlayCommonVoice / SelectMemberVoiceById fix the module as field-party sound. No caller, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_ApplyRowCondition
summary: Iterates over all rows via vtable +0x48: for each visible row (f_10 == 0) with an active model, invokes func_00604B14(self[0x48B], row, arg2).
evidence: Companion loop to 0x001FB1A4 applying condition/state via func_00604B14 to each visible row.

name: maybe_Menu_CheckActorActionable
signature: int maybe_Menu_CheckActorActionable(void* partyGroup, int slotIndex, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Veto predicate: returns 0 when the battle 3D-mode byte is 1, the group's vtable+0x40 slot is non-null and 0x00669324() != 0xFF; otherwise 1.
evidence: Same skeleton as 0x001FC8EC with a different per-mode table and final test; the callee blob is now Model_Attach_ShouldDrawRoot's area, which does not name the condition. Caller 0x00590D44 is itself still a maybe_, so the domain wording stays at confidence 0.3.

name: Battle_QueueActionMessage
signature: void Battle_QueueActionMessage(void* self, u32 actionId, u32 targetId)
summary: Enqueues an action/skill execution announcement into the battle message queue.
evidence: Enqueues action message via 0x003FBE4C; previously misnamed as effect command.

name: Battle_QueueUnitMessageIfStatusChanged
signature: void Battle_QueueUnitMessageIfStatusChanged(void* self, void* unit, u32 statusId)
summary: Checks if a unit status changed and enqueues a notification message into the battle message queue.
evidence: Checks unit state via 0x00639954; calls Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry.

name: maybe_Battle_ResetUnitModelSlotStates
summary: Battle-wide reset pass: walks the battle party list (+0x4260) and the four lists at battle+i*0x1C+0x4298, and for every unit that is still present sets model slot states 0x75/0x76/0x77/0x11B and clears the two dwords at unit+0x237/+0x238.
evidence: FACTS.md identifies work+0x5C+0x4260 as the battle party list and +0x428C as the first of four unit lists, and the address neighbours are Battle_QueueActionMessage / Battle_QueueUnitMessageIfStatusChanged, so the previous 'FieldParty' subsystem was wrong. The slot ids still come from maybe_Model_SetSlotState, hence 0.45.

name: maybe_FieldParty_AdvanceMemberCursor
summary: Shared base-class step: counts the 16 active slot pointers at self+0x1C, and in state 0x144B walks the slot cursor at self+0x490, waiting on each slot's vt[+0x14]/vt[+0x10] and spawning an event balloon per slot; returns 1 once every slot is done and resets the cursor.
evidence: NEW: the 15 confident callers are Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn, Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateAlt, Battle_ActorAction_ShowNamePopup and Battle_ActorAction_Complete, all calling it as (self,0) from their own state machines. That confirms it is a shared sequence base method, but it is used by battle and talk windows alike, so the 'FieldParty' prefix in the old name is not supported; kept maybe_ until the base class itself is named.

name: maybe_Ui_SelectSlotByRecordId
signature: void maybe_Ui_SelectSlotByRecordId(void* self, u32 recordKey, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Shared screen method: scans up to 0x55F rows from the data-manager lookup 0x0063FD24 for the first row whose +0x147 word equals the given key and selects that index (or 0xFFFF) through the screen's virtual slot +0xD8.
evidence: NEW: the function address appears at the same slot of twelve different battle/field screen vtables (e.g. 0x0075B53C, 0x0075CD7C, 0x0075E894, 0x00760974), always immediately before maybe_Battle_CollectModelChildren, so it is a shared Ui screen method rather than a list-specific helper. What the +0x147 key actually is remains unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Item_ApplySpecialModelParams
summary: Sets up the 3D model that represents an item record in a menu: for one group of ids (2, 0x76, 0x11B, 0x79, 0xC2, 0xF6, 0x75) it resolves the display actor stored at itemRecord+0x110, then copies the shared layout row 0 via the pane virtuals +0xA4 (with 5) and +0xA0 (3-float vector from row+0x18..0x20); for the other record kind it only re-triggers the actor when ids 0x79/0x7A/0x13 are involved and the field-preview flag work+0x27C57 is set. The first guess described it as a boolean 'has any of these ids' but the function returns nothing and its job is to push model/layout parameters.
evidence: Re-read with named neighbours: Game_GetDataManager + func_0063EFF0(dm,0) returns the same * shared layout row that Battle_DamageExtWindow_ApplyLayout (0x002DB99C, named) pushes through pane slots * +0xA4/+0xA0, and the resolved object sits in the g_actorBaseClass chain, so this is model/pane parameter * setup, not a predicate. The item-id set and the work+0x27C57 preview flag are still the only evidence * for the 'item' part, so the name stays 'maybe_'.

name: FieldParty_CalcFormationPosition
signature: void FieldParty_CalcFormationPosition(void* group, int mode, int useSlot, int slot)
summary: Builds a formation transform for one party-group member: takes the member's position, rotates it by the group matrix, then offsets it by the group centre (computed from the active member count) or by the stored offset vector selected by mode.
evidence: Six callers - Battle_ActorAction_MoveToFormation, Battle_ActorAction_TurnAndMoveToFormation, Battle_Sequence_Update, FieldParty_Talk_Update, Battle2DUnit_UpdateTurnToTarget and Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_Update - all place party-group members, so the group/formation reading is backed by both the field and battle sides.

name: maybe_FieldParty_UpdateSlotTypeFlags
summary: For each of up to 8 members and each of the 7 attachment slots, stores whether the member accepts the slot's type id (0x00630CDC lookup + type test) into the 8x7 flag table at (base+0x1F2), and marks the slot used through vtable+0x120; the base register (group+0x400) is lost, so the absolute offsets are approximate.
evidence: The body still carries unaff_r6 for the slot base (assigned group+0x400), and the two named callees are Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ/0x00639954; no caller exists any more, so the FieldParty module is an inference from the slot-type array, not a confirmation.

name: FieldParty_CalcMemberWorldPosition
signature: void FieldParty_CalcMemberWorldPosition(PartyGroup* group, int mode, int slot)
summary: Computes a member's world position: takes the member transform, applies the group origin offsets (0x574044) and adds the mode-specific offset vector (0x574224).
evidence: Complete body with named transform callees and three explicit modes (member 0 / +0x37 / +0x40), which matches 'calculate member world position'.

name: FieldParty_ClearSlotTypeFlags
summary: Clears every set attachment-slot flag of the party group: for each member slot it walks the seven u16 ids at group+0x1E4 and, for each set flag byte at group+0x1F2, disables that attachment on the member (virtual +0xE4) and clears the byte.
evidence: New context: the only caller is the confident Battle_CleanupUnitActors, which is exactly where per-slot attachment flags get cleared, and the seven ids/flag bytes are walked in lockstep. The single unaff_r6 is a local spill of group+0x400, not a damaged body.

name: FieldParty_InitFromParams
summary: Initialises a party group from a parameter block: copies the ids, offsets and flags, adopts the leader actor, snapshots the leader's position when the battle/menu mode flag is set, and clears the runtime arrays.
evidence: NEW: its three callers all build battle party models (Battle_Unit_InitPartyModel 0.5, maybe_Battle2DUnit_BindPartyMember/BindMemberModel 0.45) and the two party-group vtables it appears in also hold the confident FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot (0.5) - so 'initialise this party group from params' is supported at both ends.

name: FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot
summary: Resets one group member slot: clears the embedded list/vector at +0x50 and marks the slot absent in the global lookup table.
evidence: Two operations only: func_003CDEDC(group+0x50) and *(u32*)(g_001ff220+group)=0xffffffff. Called by 48 different functions, i.e. the common per-slot initialiser/destructor. Vtable slot 0 of the 15-entry party-group table (destructor position).

name: FieldParty_AttachMemberSlot
signature: int FieldParty_AttachMemberSlot(PartyGroup* group, int slot, Actor* actor, int keepEffects)
summary: Attaches an actor to a group member slot, clears or re-adds its special attachment category (0x5E/0x5F) and plays the group's join sound when not in menu mode.
evidence: The attach vfunc +0x30(actor,slot,1), the 0x5E/0x5F category tests and the group join sound are explicit, and the function is vtable slot 9 of the party-group table.

name: maybe_FieldParty_GetMemberRideObject
signature: void* maybe_FieldParty_GetMemberRideObject(void* group, void* actor, int locator)
summary: Returns an actor's ride/mount sub-object when it has one; otherwise, for an active actor with fewer than two battle party slots, it fills a locator transform and returns a pointer to that stack buffer, so callers must copy it immediately.
evidence: The battle unit-list count guard (work+0x5C+0x4254) and the locator builders are clear and the callers are now named battle-UI code (Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForAll/ForMember/ForSlot, Battle_ActionSequence_ResetTargetPointers, maybe_FieldParty_UpdateActorAttachments), but none of them proves the object is a ride/mount, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_FieldParty_CompactMemberList
summary: Party-group fix-up: compacts the eight member ids in place (keeping only ids for which the group's virtual +0x48 returns an object), then scans the compacted members and stops at the first that is not selectable (virtual +0x28 returns 0, or +0xD8/+0x10 report a pending state), flags group+0xD2 and member+0x108, and may queue action 0x14. Returns 1 when such a member was found.
evidence: The named callers maybe_FieldParty_ResetAllMembers and maybe_Battle2DUnit_BindPartyMember plus the named Battle_QueueActionEx callee confirm the party-group vtable-slot role. The selectability contract is still read from the virtual calls and the 0x14 action is unexplained, so the name keeps maybe_ and the summary now records the validation half.

name: FieldParty_UpdateActorAttachments
signature: unsigned FieldParty_UpdateActorAttachments(PartyGroup* group, short* cmd, int slot, * Actor* actor, unsigned flags, int arg6, int arg7, int arg8)
summary: Applies one attachment/effect command (descriptor ids -5..-3 and positive ids) to an actor: resolves the actor handle, sets the category flag, spawns the effect or plays voice, and updates the actor's position through the group formation.
evidence: Installed in g_fieldPartyVtable (0x00769398) alongside FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot (0x001FF200) in FieldParty_Ctor (0x003CAE00); processes attachment descriptor commands for the field party group actors.

name: Sound_WaitForHandleOrTimeout
signature: u32 Sound_WaitForHandleOrTimeout(void* owner, float dt, u32* handle)
summary: Per-frame wait used by cutscenes and battle sequences to hold the script until a sound/voice handle has finished: accumulates dt into the float timer at owner+0x1234 and returns 1 (resetting the timer to 0.0f) once the timer reaches 1.0f or the handle reports stale, otherwise 0.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly settles it - `vldr s1,[r4,#0x234]; vadd.f32 s0,s1,s0; vstr s0,[r4,#0x234]; cmp r0,#0x3f800000; bge -> return 1`, else `Sound_GetPlayer(sp); ldr r1,[r6]` (the handle is *r1, a pointer) `bl Sound_Handle_IsStale; cmp r0,#0; beq -> return 0`. So it is a sound-handle wait with a 1-second cap, not a menu timer. The nine callers are all sequence/state machines that wait for a voice line: Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn, Battle_ActorAction_ShowDamage, FieldParty_Ui_UpdateMemberSlot.

name: Ui_Screen_CtorBase
summary: The shared base constructor of every UI screen: sets up the two intrusive list heads, installs vtable 0x002001EC, seeds the float sentinels and 'no selection' ids, chains the sub-object constructor 0x002BB828 and default-constructs 32 0x7C-byte slot records.
evidence: 49 callers, essentially every screen constructor in the project (maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt7746EC, vt775C54, vt777304, vt777348, vt7792D0, vt77A51C, vt77BA38, vt77C648, Ui_ScreenObject_Ctor_77D5CC/77D6E0/77E33C/77ED80, plus the Field_ObjectFactory_Type* entries). Body: `arg1[2] = arg1+1; arg1[3] = arg1+1; arg1[1] = arg1; *arg1 = g_002001ec; arg1[0x2c] = g_002001f0; arg1[0x2d] = 0; arg1[0x43] = 0xffffffff; arg1[0x44] = 0; arg1[0x45] = 0xffffffff; arg1[0x46] = 0; iVar3 = func_002BB828(arg1+0x47); func_00100050(iVar3+0x148, g_002001f4, 0x7c, 0x20);`.

name: Menu_ResolveEntryHandler
signature: unsigned Menu_ResolveEntryHandler(MenuState* self, Actor* actor, int entryId)
summary: Chooses the handler for a menu entry: rejects ids 3/4/0x254 while a battle flag is set, and otherwise routes to the equipment-requirement handler when the entry links to a record of type 6, to the mode-1 variant when the menu is in mode 1, and to the default (return 1) otherwise.
evidence: The three outcomes map onto named callees (Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements and its B variant) and the callers (maybe_Menu_ApplyEntryAction, Menu_LocateSkillGridCell) consume the result as a handler id.

name: Menu_CalcEquipStatValues
signature: unsigned Menu_CalcEquipStatValues(MenuState* self, int slot, unsigned mode)
summary: Computes the six displayed stat values for a menu page: reads the base stats from the character table, applies the focused equipment slot's modifier, folds the pairs into the two totals used by the status page and refreshes the skill-row availability and the stat widget.
evidence: The named callees Menu_UpdateSkillRowAvailability / Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements and the table lookups (func_0063D1F8 = base stats, func_0063FC70 = equipment entry) make the stat arithmetic readable, not just the first pass's guess.

name: Menu_BuildTargetActorSet
signature: unsigned long long Menu_BuildTargetActorSet(MenuState* self, Entry* entry, TargetSet* outSet)
summary: Builds the 16-slot set of actors an entry targets: clears the slots and then, depending on the entry's target type (all / single / random / count), fills them from the selected actor, from the entry dispatch result or from the unit list, returning the battle work's actor-set pointer (+0x4238).
evidence: Named callees Menu_DispatchEntryAction and Menu_CountSlotsByMode are the two decision points of the function, and the RNG calls func_001CA474(rng, 0, count-1) implement the "random N targets" branch - enough to keep the name at 0.5 even though the exact target-type enum values are unnamed.

name: Menu_SelectRecipeRow
signature: void Menu_SelectRecipeRow(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Chooses the list row for the current menu page: an override index wins, otherwise the type tags 8/10 select the last rows, otherwise it evaluates the per-row predicate 0x002053CC over 0x2D rows and keeps the previously selected 2-byte pair when it still matches.
evidence: Caller 0x002031A4 = maybe_Menu_UpdateSelectionPage. Body: `iVar4 = *g_00202db4; if (iVar4 != -1) { self->f_434 = iVar4; ... }` then tags 8 -> 0x2e and record->f_200, tag 10 -> 0x2d and record->f_1f5, then `do { iVar7 = iVar4; iVar4 = func_002053CC(self,iVar3,iVar7); if (iVar4 != 0) break; iVar4 = iVar7+1; } while (iVar4 < 0x2d);` and the 2-byte comparison at `iVar3 + 0x205 + index*2`.

name: Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements
signature: u32 Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements(int self, int stats, u32 itemId)
summary: Evaluates up to five requirement ids listed at record+0x54 against the equipment query and either keeps or zeroes the sixteen-word stat block, depending on the record's mode byte at +0x15F.
evidence: Callers 0x00200240 (maybe_Menu_ResolveEntryHandler), 0x002004AC (maybe_Menu_CalcEquipStatValues). Body: `iVar5 = func_0063FD24(work,arg3); f15f = iVar5->f_15f; for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i == 0) { if (iVar5->f_54 == uVar3) return 1; } else if (((u16*)&iVar5->f_54)[i] == uVar3) break; ... uVar6 = func_0063E8D4(work, uVar2); iVar7 = func_00265924(arg1+0x200,uVar6,arg2,uVar9); if (iVar7 == 0) { if (f15f == 0) goto zero; if (f15f == 1) ... } }` then zeroes arg2->f_20..f_5c.

name: Menu_CollectActorsForList
signature: void Menu_CollectActorsForList(MenuState* self, unsigned* handles, int count, int count2)
summary: Fills the two 64-entry actor lists of the selection window: first the actors resolved from the caller's handle table, then the active actors of the four party sub-lists, split by whether they already belong to the current group.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the confident Menu_UpdateSelectionPage (0.5), which is exactly the page rebuild that needs these two lists; the membership test func_0049ABCC and the four sub-lists at gameWork+0x428C are unchanged from the first pass.

name: Menu_UpdateSelectionPage
signature: unsigned Menu_UpdateSelectionPage(MenuState* self, unsigned* out, unsigned handle, unsigned count1, unsigned count2, int mode)
summary: Evaluates the menu's entry selection page: builds the candidate list, resolves the current entry, applies the page/limit rules and writes the chosen actor and sub-slot back to the caller.
evidence: The named callers Menu_ResolveSelectedEntryActors (0x0020605C), Menu_SelectRecipeRow (0x00202C50) and Battle_SelectAiActions (0x0016C7F8) all use it to turn a cursor position into the selected entry.

name: Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirementsB
signature: u32 Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirementsB(int self, int stats, u32 itemId)
summary: Second requirement-list variant: evaluates up to five requirement ids stored at record+0x4A against the equipment query and, depending on the record's mode byte at +0x15F, either returns success or zeroes the caller's sixteen-word stat block.
evidence: The confident sibling Menu_ApplyEquipmentStatRequirements (0x202DB8, same callers 0x200240/0x2004AC, byte-identical apart from the +0x54/+0x4A list offset) pins the name; this is simply the second five-entry requirement list in the same record.

name: Menu_DispatchEntryAction
signature: int Menu_DispatchEntryAction(MenuState* self, Entry* entry, u32 actor, u32 mode)
summary: Reads two mode bytes for the entry (0x0063FA60(model)[self->f_434*0xB + entry->f_68] and the 0x12-byte record from 0x0063FE6C at +0x10/+0x11) and dispatches: value pairs 0/1/2/3/4/5/6 select maybe_Menu_ApplyEntryAction(...,index,mode), while type 3 goes to maybe_Menu_BuildCandidateList; a global override at g_00203BF0 wins if it is not -1.
evidence: The body is a pure dispatch table over the two mode bytes into seven ApplyEntryAction variants plus the candidate-list branch, which matches the name exactly; the callees are still maybe_ but their role is fixed by the switch.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplyEntryAction
signature: unsigned maybe_Menu_ApplyEntryAction(void* self, int entry, int actor, unsigned mode, int arg5)
summary: Selects the action a menu entry applies to its target set: counts the entry's 16 target slots, resolves the entry's linked actor, builds the target actor set (Menu_ResolveEntryHandler / Menu_BuildTargetActorSet) and hands the chosen command to func_0038A664, with a random tie-break; large parts of the body are decompiler bad-instruction regions.
evidence: Its only caller Menu_DispatchEntryAction invokes it seven times with modes 0..5 and uses the result as the dispatched action, which supports the 'apply entry action' role; the garbled switch keeps it maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_FindActorInListByType
summary: Walks an intrusive list and returns 1 as soon as an entry reports type 0x9C; Ghidra lost the list head/tail registers (unaff_r4/unaff_r5) and prints a bogus arg1*0x2002, so only the type test and the loop shape are real.
evidence: Both callers remain maybe_Menu_* and the two unaff_ registers are still unresolved; the only solid facts are the 0x9C type id and the entry-type query 0x00639954, so the confidence floor stays.

name: Menu_LocateSkillGridCell
signature: void Menu_LocateSkillGridCell(int self, int srcEntry, int dstEntry, u32 skillId)
summary: Maps a skill/command id to its (row, column) cell in the menu grid, records the cross-cell relation in f_84 and then resolves and applies the entry's handler chain.
evidence: Callers 0x0016C7F8 (Battle_SelectAiActions), 0x00204980 (maybe_Menu_AdvanceListCursor). Body: grid lookup `func_0063FC70(work, modelId, iVar7, i)` with `if (*puVar3 == arg4) { arg3->f_68 = i; arg3->f_6c = iVar7; break; }` for i<6, iVar7<=0x2e; then `if (*(u16*)(iVar7+100) != iVar7->f_6a) { if (*(u16*)(iVar7+100) == uVar1) cVar8 = iVar7->f_68; else if (iVar7->f_6a == uVar1) cVar8 = iVar7->f_6e; }` -> f_84; then func_00630F6C / func_006319BC / func_00200240 / func_00200A5C / func_0038A664.

name: Menu_UpdateSkillRowAvailability
signature: void Menu_UpdateSkillRowAvailability(int self, int availability, int mode)
summary: Fills the six per-row availability words of the skill window by comparing each row's record level fields with the current character level and the 0x006456C4 handler result.
evidence: Caller 0x002004AC (maybe_Menu_CalcEquipStatValues). Body: for iVar9 in 0..5 `puVar6 = func_0063FC70(work, self->f_428->f_76c & 0xffff, self->f_434, iVar9)`; `if (*(char*)((int)puVar6+0xf) == 0)`; then `iVar8 = func_0063FD24(work,*puVar6)`; `bVar2 = iVar8->f_d0; uVar4 = (**(*self->f_428+0x98))(); if (bVar2 <= uVar4) goto skip;` -> `*(u32*)(arg2 + iVar9*4) = 0;`; the alternate branch compares iVar8->f_ee from func_0063D018 and calls func_006456C4(self->f_42c, self->f_428, ...).

name: maybe_Menu_AdvanceListCursor
signature: int maybe_Menu_AdvanceListCursor(MenuState* self, int entryList, unsigned actor, unsigned mode)
summary: Per-page cursor step: case 0 advances the modulo-6 cursor at self+0x438 through empty entries, case 3 dispatches the selected row through Menu_ResolveEntryHandler/Menu_BuildTargetActorSet; the other cases are decompiled as bad instructions.
evidence: The new context confirms case 3 is an entry dispatch, but the switch is still garbled (halt_baddata) and its only caller Menu_CalcEquipStatValues uses the result as an index, so the cursor-step description is partial.

name: Menu_EvalEntryCondition
signature: unsigned char Menu_EvalEntryCondition(MenuContext* ctx, int entry, int arg3, int condition)
summary: Evaluates the availability condition of a menu entry: a switch over 0x23 condition ids covering party size, actor classes, HP/MP ratios, equipment and "any member has item/skill", using the party and battle helpers and falling back to the entry's own type check.
evidence: The switch cases read cleanly against named helpers (Party_CountActive, Party_HasActiveActorInAnySlot, Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted, the battle party list at +0x4260) and the function is called through a vtable as the condition evaluator of the menu table. The readable body is damaged only in the base register (unaff_r4 = the MenuContext argument): asm 0x002049FC opens with push {r1,r3,r4,r5,lr} / adds.w r0,r3,r0 and then a cmp chain on the condition byte, so the switch itself is intact.

name: Menu_FindLinkedActorByModelId
signature: void Menu_FindLinkedActorByModelId(void* self, void* entry, u32* out)
summary: Finds the battle actor whose model/character id (node+0x1DA) matches the entry's id, prefers the caller's current actor when it fits, filters out actors already in the given state (8/10) and stores the pick in out[1], choosing randomly when several match.
evidence: The body scans the four battle unit lists (work+0x5C+0x428C, stride 0x1C) and compares node[0x1DA]; its caller is the named Menu_ResolveSelectedEntryActors and it ends by registering the pick with func_0038A5AC on the battle scene.

name: maybe_Menu_BuildCandidateList
signature: u32 maybe_Menu_BuildCandidateList(MenuState* self, int entryTable, int filter, int list)
summary: Counts the non-null entries of the 16-slot table at entryTable+0x20, then scans the self+0x0 or self+0x100 pointer array applying filter vtable+0x18 (filter 0) or vtable+0x10 (filter 1) and filling up to 0x40 records of 0xC bytes on the stack.
evidence: The count/scan/fill structure is clear and it is called from Menu_DispatchEntryAction's mode dispatch, but no named callee confirms what the 0xC-byte records mean.

name: Menu_TestEntryCondition
signature: unsigned char Menu_TestEntryCondition(MenuState* self, int entryTable, int index)
summary: Tests the per-entry condition byte at entryTable+0x205+index*2: case 1/2 compare the actor's HP/MP ratio with the threshold, case 3 tests a status bit, later cases count party members, and it returns whether the entry is usable.
evidence: Two named callers (Menu_SelectRecipeRow, Menu_UpdateSelectionPage) use the result to grey out/refuse entry rows, and the body's HP/MP/party-count branches match a usability condition test.

name: Menu_SetOwnerActor
signature: void Menu_SetOwnerActor(int self, int actor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Binds a menu/skill window to the actor whose model it displays and caches that actor's type byte from the parameter record.
evidence: Caller 0x001CC360 (Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor). Body: `self->f_428 = arg2; self->f_220 = arg2; f76c = arg2->f_76c; iVar3 = func_0063FA60(work, f76c & 0xffff); self->f_57e = iVar3->f_265;`. The same f_428/f_434/f_57E fields are used by 0x00202C50, 0x002047A0 and 0x0020605C, which all read the selection through f_428.

name: Menu_ResolveSelectedEntryActors
summary: Resolves the currently selected grid cell to its record and, for the three special party-command ids, also to the three party actors that should be highlighted, storing them in the entry.
evidence: Caller 0x002031A4 (maybe_Menu_UpdateSelectionPage). Body: `puVar3 = func_0063FC70(work, self->f_428->f_76c & 0xffff, self->f_434, arg2[0x1a]); iVar4 = func_0063FD24(work,*puVar3); if (iVar4->f_193 == 0) func_00200A5C(self,iVar4,arg2); else { ... func_006319BC(...) ... }`; then `*arg2 = self->f_428; arg2[0x1b] = self->f_434; func_00204BC0(self,iVar4,arg2);`; if the id is 0x2e / 0x31c / (id-0x300 == 0x1b) it scans three 6-entry u16 tables through func_00631A88 (Party_FindActiveActorById) into arg2[0..2].

name: Battle_ActionModel_InitSubPanel
summary: Initialises the battle action model's embedded sub-panel at self+0x200: runs the layout-state defaults, writes the 0/-1 sentinels (f_228..f_250, f_37e/f_37f = 0xFF, f_380 = -1), fills 0x11A bytes at f_264 with 1 and clears the two 0x100-byte scratch buffers at self and self+0x100; returns self.
evidence: NEW: its only caller is the now-named Battle_ActionModel_CreateBase (0x001CC3EC, 0.50), whose doc says it 'builds the sub-panel at +0x23C' and which is itself called only by the Battle_ActionModel_Create* factories and Model_CreateActorModel/Menu_CreateEntryObjects. That fixes the owner as the battle action model, so the generic 'Menu' prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Menu_InitSlotTables
summary: Resets the menu's large slot tables at self+0x158: fills 0x1F entries with 0xFF, then clears 0x9D3 four-byte entries (0xFFFF / 0) and the 0x1F stride-100 slot records plus the 4x8 paginated records to their defaults.
evidence: Called by the confident Menu_CloseWindow (0x0020AB04) when closing and by the scene-object reset path 0x00210274; the record sizes come from the explicit constants in the body. What each table stores (item slots vs. other menu records) is not stated anywhere readable, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Battle_InitWork
summary: Initialises the battle work: lazily creates its 0x194-byte, 15-state sequence sub-object (vtable 0x0075A888, per-state ctor 0x006C4350) and then sets up the shared unit list at +0x4254, the five 0x40-byte party slots at +0x1C, the four 0x1C-byte unit lists at +0x428C and the 3D/2D unit model tables at +0x4330/+0x47A0.
evidence: FACTS.md identifies +0x4254/+0x4270/+0x428C/+0x4298 (stride 0x1C), +0x4330 (3D) and +0x47A0 (2D) as battle-work fields, and the tail of the body initialises exactly those with maybe_Field_InitSharedParams and func_002AB618; the only caller (0x0019ECE4) passes self->f_5C, which FACTS calls the battle work. Nothing in the body touches field objects, so 'Field_InitObjectTable' was wrong.

name: FieldScene_RebindCharacter
summary: Resets the field actor slots and then tells the Field2D manager that the displayed character record changed, so all 2D field models are rebuilt for the new character.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithLayout passes &self->f_b0->f_146, i.e. a CharacterRecord pointer, as the second argument, and the callee Field2D_OnCharacterChanged (0.50) is documented as taking (Field2DManager*, const CharacterRecord*). The old name wrongly implied a menu selection by index.

name: Menu_ForEachActorCall148
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x148(arg2) on every valid actor of the four menu actor lists.
evidence: Loops i<4 over gamework+0x428c lists, tests vfunc+0x18(node) then calls vfunc+0x148(node,arg2). Called by 0x001FF63C.

name: Gfx_Scene_Init
signature: void Gfx_Scene_Init(GfxScene* self, u32 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one scene render path: clears the five per-frame flags (+0x423C/+0x423D/+0x423E/+0x424F/+0x4D74), creates the scene sub-objects, then either the 3D path (+0x4330) or the 2D path (viewport init + the action arrays at +0x47A0).
evidence: The branch on the global 2D-mode byte +0x4244 and the named callees Gfx_Scene2D_InitViewport / Battle_InitUnitActionArrays make both paths readable; the callers are the scene-open sequences.

name: BattleScene_SpawnMonsterUnit
signature: void* BattleScene_SpawnMonsterUnit(void* battleScene, u32 groupSlot, u32 monsterId, void* ownerUnit, int skipLimitCheck)
summary: Spawns a monster/reinforcement unit into battle formation group groupSlot (battleScene + 0x428C + groupSlot*0x1C): checks group/size capacity via 0x0020B100 and monster record 0x0063EEAC, creates the unit via Model_CreateActorModel, registers it in 3D (+0x4330) or 2D (+0x47A0) battle lists, links it to ownerUnit, and returns the unit pointer (or NULL).
evidence: Full ARM disasm 0x206C40..0x20709C (5 params + non-void return): every caller passes (*(osWork->f_08 + 0x5C), groupSlot, monsterId, ownerUnit, skipCheck) where (work+8)->f_5C is BattleScene*! Queries Party_CountActorById for duplicate-monster suffix, calls Model_CreateActorModel (0x208960), inserts into 3D/2D BattleScene unit tables and group list +0x428C+slot*0x1C, calls BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelTransforms/DispatchUnitVariant, and returns unit in r0. Old name maybe_Menu_OpenItemEntryWindow was completely wrong and poisoned callers.

name: BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant
signature: u8 BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant(int scene, u32 modelId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the model variant byte (0x9E or 0x9F) that a battle-scene unit should use, selected by a per-scene boolean table.
evidence: 22 battle-scene callers (0x004A7E58 Battle_UnitModel_SetVariantPaired, 0x004A8084 SetVariantSolo, 0x00603024 BattleScene_GetUnitModelSize, 0x00608F98 BattleScene_BuildPartyModel, 0x0060AF18 UpdateUnitModelTransforms...). Body: `iVar3 = func_0063EEAC(work, arg2); if (*(char*)(g_002070e0 + arg1) == 0) result = iVar3->f_9f; else result = iVar3->f_9e;`. The caller names in N_074's lane already call these two fields 'variant'.

name: Menu_InitFromParams
signature: void Menu_InitFromParams(MenuState* self, int mode, Param* parameter, unsigned char* flags)
summary: Initialises the menu/battle command state from an event/talk parameter block: stores the mode flags, selects the window object, resolves the actor record and resets the entry lists and counters.
evidence: Named callers Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0, BattleScene_RebuildScene and Menu_SetEntryDisplayMode all set the state up from a parameter block, and the body reads the parameter bytes into the f_4244.. block.

name: Battle_ReleaseSceneDisplay
summary: Tears down battle unit visual objects and display models from BattleWork: branches on mode byte +0x4244 to release the 3D unit model table (self+0x4330) or 2D unit model table (self+0x47a0) via 0x001690FC, and releases unit actor slots f_431c, f_4320, and f_4324.
evidence: Previous guess assumed a generic GfxScene, but field offsets (+0x4244 mode byte, +0x4330 3D / +0x47A0 2D unit models, +0x431c/+0x4320/+0x4324 actor slots) match FACTS.md BattleWork (work+8)->f_5C exactly; called by confident Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithScene (0x0019F4FC) at 0x0019F530 during combat scene teardown.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplySelectedCharacter
summary: Applies a character selection: switches the field status window (work+8->+0x88) to character id and re-attaches the menu actor models of self. Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0 calls it with the scene record's character byte.
evidence: Only caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0 (0.5) passes self->f_5C and the scene record's character byte; the body is exactly Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter(work+8->+0x88,id) plus maybe_Menu_RemoveActorAttachments(self). The second half is still a maybe_, so the exact owner ('Menu_') stays unproven.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateSubObjects
summary: Creates the scene's two helper sub-objects (and, in 3D mode, the extra 0x2d4- and 0x268-byte objects), linking the effect object to its emitter.
evidence: Allocations g_00207a84 -> 0x00269BC0 and g_00207a88 -> 0x00282238, plus the 0x0027C094 link in 3D mode; sole caller 0x00206BBC is the scene ctor. Named context in the merged C: Battle_Popup_Ctor, Gfx_SceneSubObject_Ctor, Ui_CompositeWindow_Ctor, Ui_GetCore, Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable.

name: maybe_Party_Hero_RemapSpellEntries
summary: On the hero (party index 0) replaces each of the six spell entries 0xBB..0xC0 with 0x9C through 0x00190270, clears member+0x12E0/+0x12E2 to 0xFF and recalculates the member's stats.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x00190270 shows a 40-iteration loop over the byte array at member+0x1274 (compare entry with r1, store r2 on match), i.e. the 40-slot spell list from FACTS, not battle slots; 0x00207A8C calls it six times with r1=0xBB..0xC0 and r2=0x9C. The old name Party_InitBattleSlots was wrong about the table; what the remap is for is still unclear.

name: maybe_Menu_RemoveActorAttachments
summary: Walks the actor list at world+0x4260 and the four lists at +0x428C; for every actor whose u16 tag (g_00207DE8) equals g_00207DE4 it calls vtable+0xE4(actor, tag, 1), and when the actor's monster-table value (+0x103) is at most 0x001CA474(world+0x4218,1,100,0) it also calls vtable+0x50(actor,1,0).
evidence: Re-read: the tag compare and the two virtual calls are confirmed, but 'attachments' is inferred from the (id,1) arguments of vtable+0xE4 and the only caller 0x00207890 is itself maybe_ (maybe_Menu_ApplySelectedCharacter, 0.45). Stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_BuildEffectList
summary: Rebuilds the effect/command entries shown for the currently inactive battle actors: counts them, allocates a table, fills one 0x10-byte record per actor from the item/spell records and sorts it with std_qsort before freeing the scratch copy.
evidence: Both callers are named battle-UI refresh paths (Battle_UiFlow_RebuildEffectList and maybe_Battle_RefreshBattleUi) that pass the battle work, and the body calls Menu_BuildEffectCommandList plus Item_LookupRecord; the old 'Menu_RebuildEffectList' prefix did not fit a battle-UI caller.

name: Menu_GetActorByIndex
summary: Returns the actor at a flat index across the global list followed by the UI list at work+0x427c.
evidence: Walks work->f_4260 list while vfunc+0x24 is true, then work->f_427c/f_4280, then continues the first list; returns 0 when the index is past the end. Used by 0x202F3C, 0x467E58, 0x481800, 0x63761C.

name: Menu_FindSlotForEntry
signature: u32 Menu_FindSlotForEntry(MenuState* self, u32 entryId, u32 extra)
summary: Searches the four list columns for one that accepts the given entry (delegating to the per-column check 0x0020B100) and returns the first matching column index, or 0xFFFFFFFF when no column takes it.
evidence: Five callers are now named menu open paths and the per-column predicate 0x0020B100 is the sibling of the named Menu_CheckSlotSelectable (0x0020B10C), so the small loop's meaning is fixed.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplyActorModelPattern
signature: void maybe_Menu_ApplyActorModelPattern(MenuState* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: When f_424A is set, walks the four actor lists and for every slot record with a non-zero pattern id applies it to the actor's model through vtable +0xA0, copies the companion value into the model's +0x12/+0x16, then asks the scene transition controller (work+0x74) to refresh.
evidence: Only caller is Menu_InitFromParams and the only named callee in the path is Os_GetGameWork plus 0x002AEA84 on work+0x74; the +0xA0 model getter and the f_34E4/f_34E6 id pair are consistent with a model appearance/pattern, but nothing proves what the id selects.

name: Model_CreateActorModel
signature: int* Model_CreateActorModel(int owner, int modelId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates the model instance used by a field actor, resolving the model resource and initializing the render/attachment state.
evidence: 0x280 bytes; allocates with 0x00109DC8 and resolves through 0x0010EBE4/0x0011CB38/0x001CAE90/0x001CC3EC/0x00401A00/0x004853xx; globals g_00208bd4..g_00208bdc.

name: Gfx_Scene_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the scene down: hides every child drawable, releases either the composite/sub-object set or the battle scene models depending on the mode byte, releases the six helper objects and resets the per-scene state.
evidence: Named callees now cover the teardown (Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseHandles, Ui_ReleaseSubObjects, BattleScene_ReleaseSceneModels, Container_List_DestroyAll, Gfx_Scene2D_ResetScroll) and four named field-actor reset functions call it.

name: maybe_Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId
signature: void maybe_Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId(void* self, u32 id, u32 arg3, u32 stack)
summary: If the id is not already in the five 0x40-byte slot records (+0x4C..+0x14C), claims the first free record (bytes +0x0C/+0x0D == -1 and u16 id +0x0E == 0xFFFF), stamps the id into it, clears +0x08, sets +0x10 = -1 and finally refreshes the entry's icon through maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon.
evidence: NEW: caller maybe_BattlePartyWindow_ClaimPartySlots and the five-slot membership scan make the claim role solid; whether the slots hold party members or item entries is still open (the icon refresh suggests a UI entry), so maybe_.

name: Menu_CreateEntryObjects
summary: Creates the menu's per-entry objects (0x68 of them) on the +0x4308 list and initialises the metadata block at +0x56C4.
evidence: Maybe_Menu_InitFromParams (0x0020713C) calls it while building the menu, and the body's 0x68-iteration allocation loop matches the entry count.

name: Party_BuildMemberList
summary: Builds the list of party member ids for the party/status screen: first the members that match the availability condition, then the rest, up to 0x1f entries.
evidence: Readable C: memset(buf,0xff,0x1f); loops j<ctx->f_27218 calling func_0066B0E4(ctx,j) and func_0035EB98(ctx,id), keeping ids where func_0062917C(record) is non-zero, then a second pass appending the rest until 0x1f; finally publishes the list. Callers are all party/status screens (0x208ed4, 0x20e358, 0x467e58/0x468320/0x4683f0).

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_AdvanceStartupGate
summary: Two-phase local scene start gate that always returns 1: before +0x423D is set it probes the two UI-core sub-objects through their virtual +0x34 readiness calls, then resets the field actor slots with Field_ResetActorSlots and raises +0x423D; afterwards it waits for the 0.633 s timer (0x3F222222) and reports renderer reason 0xE (or 8 when +0x424E is clear) through the renderer at +0x10.
evidence: Callees are now named (Field_ResetActorSlots, Gfx_GetContext, Ui_GetCore) and the timer/flag flow is clear, but there is no caller and the meaning of the renderer reason is unknown. Renamed from CheckState because the result is ignored and the function has side effects, so 'Check' was misleading.

name: maybe_Party_SetSelectedMember
signature: void maybe_Party_SetSelectedMember(void* party, u8 member, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Stores the selected member index at self+0x24A and bumps the bag counter at +0x30 (unless it is -1) through 0x00612D40.
evidence: The field store and the counter bump are clear, but no caller exists and 0x00612D40 is a generic counter increment, so the 'selected member' meaning is still inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseScreen
summary: Closes the screen: calls the view object's virtual +0x28 twice (once with 1, once with 0,1), then advances the screen state machine to state 0xD and returns 1.
evidence: NEW: still no callers; the two view calls and the state 0xD advance are certain, but nothing in the body mentions a fade, so 'WithFade' was dropped. The same state-0xD advance appears in the three maybe_Ui_CloseScreenIfFlag* siblings.

name: maybe_Battle_RunTargetSelection
summary: Initiates target-selection request in combat: resolves hero/actor pair and invokes Battle_SelectTargetsThunk.
evidence: Invokes confident Battle_SelectTargetsThunk and accesses game work, but menu caller context remains unconfirmed. Kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateModelFadeIn
summary: Drives the fade-in of the displayed party's 3D models: waits until all four sub-groups report ready, advances the fade step counter up to 3, and averages the per-actor fade values through the actor virtual +0x24/+0x18 calls.
evidence: The only named caller is maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay (0x002D9E00), not a camp-menu function, so the old 'Camp' qualifier was unproven and has been dropped; the fade-step and per-actor averaging are unchanged, and the display context is still ambiguous (battle display vs menu), so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Menu_Slot_StoreActorId
signature: void Menu_Slot_StoreActorId(MenuState* self, unsigned actorId, unsigned arg3, unsigned stack)
summary: Stores a character id into the first free of the five 0x40-byte slot records (or keeps an existing match) and notifies the item-icon layer when the battle flag is set.
evidence: The five-record scan, the f_4C/f_4D sentinel pair and the five f_4D/f_8D/f_CD/f_10D/f_14D comparisons are explicit; the notification path goes through the battle work flag at +0x4244.

name: Battle_Unit_AttachToColumn
signature: int Battle_Unit_AttachToColumn(void* self, int column, unsigned slot, unsigned entry, unsigned flags, int immediate)
summary: Attaches a resolved battle unit to a battle column: picks the 3D (+0x4330) or 2D (+0x47A0) scene by work+0x4244, resolves the unit from list+0x428C+column*0x1C, rejects when the party would exceed 8 members, then binds it through the scene helpers or plays SE 0x15B.
evidence: The body operates on battle work (mode byte 0x4244, unit lists at 0x428C, scene tables 0x4330/0x47A0), not on a menu window, so the old 'Menu_AttachActorToWindow' named the wrong subsystem. There is no named caller, hence 0.55.

name: Menu_Actor_PlayUiAnimation
signature: void Menu_Actor_PlayUiAnimation(void* self, u32 anim, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Plays a UI animation on the menu's actor controller (self->f_4320->f_204): enables the controller, runs vfunc+0x74 and forwards the animation parameters to func_002DFDE8.
evidence: 26 callers, all menu code, and the three call sites (vfunc+0x18(f204,1), vfunc+0x74(f204,0), func_002DFDE8(f204,anim,...)) make the operation explicit.

name: Menu_SetSelectedActorId
signature: void Menu_SetSelectedActorId(MenuState* self, int actorId, unsigned arg3, unsigned stack)
summary: Stores the selected actor id in the menu state (+0x4208, 0xFF clamped to 0) and, in 3D mode, applies it as the animation id of the scene sprite group when the group's object is of class 4 and its +0x38 is 2.
evidence: Eight named callers (Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel, maybe_Menu_InitFromParams, the party-status handlers) pass an actor id, and the callee is the named maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetAnimId.

name: Menu_CloseWindow
summary: Closes a menu window: clears its display state, sends the close notification with the window parameters, stops the associated message UI and releases the window object.
evidence: The named callees Menu_SetEntryDisplayMode, Ui_GetCore, Gfx_Scene2D_ResetScroll and maybe_Party_InitBattleSlots are exactly the close sequence in the body, and two named callers use it while tearing the menu down.

name: maybe_Menu_ResumeActorAnimations
summary: Menu helper: loops the four battle unit lists (work+0x5C+0x4254, accessor 0x002AB62C) and for each unit whose vtable+0x10 is 0 reads vtable+0x90/+0x94 and, when 0x003CE464() > 1, calls vtable+0xE4(unit, 1).
evidence: Address neighbours are confidently Menu_* (Menu_Actor_PlayUiAnimation, Menu_CheckActorAnimationDone, Menu_CloseWindow), so the Menu subsystem is right, but the per-unit virtual 0xE4(unit,1) call is still unidentified; 'resume animations' remains the least-wrong description.

name: Menu_DispatchWindowModeCommand
signature: u32 Menu_DispatchWindowModeCommand(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Translates the current menu display mode (byte at f_442C, overridable through f_4244) into a window command code and sends it to the child object's virtual +0x18; the two 'paired' modes collapse to codes 5/6.
evidence: Body: `cVar1 = self->f_442c; if (self->f_4244 == 0) cVar1 = self->f_489c; self->f_4200 = cVar1;` then a switch on 1/8 -> 2..4 (with a record lookup via func_0063F1E0 on self->f_4e64 and its f_3b/f_37 flags), 2 -> 5, 3 -> 6, 4 -> 7, 5 -> 0xb, 6 -> 0xc, and a 'paired' branch mapping 1/8 -> 5, 2/3 -> 6; every branch ends in `(*pcVar6)(piVar2, uVar5)` where `pcVar6 = *(code**)(*self->f_10 + 0x18)`.

name: maybe_Menu_CheckActorAnimationDone
summary: Returns true when the menu actor with the given id has finished its animation: it scans the four party lists, keeps entries whose f_E74 bit 0 is set, matches the actor resolved by Monster_LookupRecord (f_D4 == actorId), compares the record frame counter f_102 with the threshold in the constant block and updates a per-actor retry counter at work+0x2D54C.
evidence: The actor lookup callee is now the named Monster_LookupRecord and the counter update is visible, but 'animation finished' still depends on the unproven meaning of f_102 and the 0x2D54C counter, so it stays maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Battle_IncrementUnitCounters
summary: Walks the four 0x1C-stride battle unit rings at battleWork+0x4298..+0x42EC; for every live unit (virtual +0x10 non-zero) whose flag word +0x39D has none of 0x46 set, increments the capped u32 per-unit counter at saveWork+0x3AE4+id*4 (id = unit+0x1DA & 0xFFFF, cap 99999).
evidence: Disassembly of callee 0x00612A94 shows the per-id increment and the 0x0001869F (99999) cap, and the list offsets are the documented battle-work unit table; the inherited 'Field_RefreshActorSlots' name had the wrong subsystem and described no effect.

name: Menu_CheckSlotSelectable
signature: u32 Menu_CheckSlotSelectable(MenuState* self, int column, u32 entryId, int extra, int skip)
summary: Decides whether an entry may be put into a list column: enforces the global column limits (9/0x1B), compares the current occupancy of the column with the entry's window slot, reads the entry's f_9E/f_9F flags and may create the missing window before returning 1/0.
evidence: All callees are named now (maybe_Menu_CountVisibleSlots, Party_CountActive, BattleScene_IsModelSelectable, maybe_BattleScene_HasUnitAnimTrack, func_0063EEAC row lookup), which confirms the 'can this entry go into this column' check.

name: Menu_IsSlotBudgetExceeded
signature: bool Menu_IsSlotBudgetExceeded(void* self, u32 entryType, int limit, int count)
summary: Returns true when the entry type's slot budget (8/7/6/4 depending on type and menu mode) would be exceeded by limit+count, after counting the matching actors in the four battle unit lists.
evidence: The old name promised a count, but the function returns budget < limit+count and its only caller is the named Menu_CheckSlotSelectable (0x0020B10C), which uses exactly that not-enough-room answer.

name: Menu_ResetSlotRecords
summary: Resets the five 0x40-byte slot records (and the trailing field at +0x154) to their empty values, releasing each record's sub-object first.
evidence: Loops i<5 over self+i*0x40, tests f_4c/f_4d==-1 && f_4e==-1, calls func_0030CA34(&rec->f_14) when in use, then sets f_48/f_50=-1, f_4c/f_4d=0xff, f_4e=0xffff; finally self->f_154=0xff.

name: Party_CalcAverageLevel
summary: Returns the average level of the active party members as a float in s0: walks the ring at +0x4260/+0x4264, resolves each member record (0x0035EB98 on node+0x768), skips inactive members (0x0062917C) and divides the summed level (member+0xD8) by the count; 0.0f when nobody is active.
evidence: Disassembly shows the 0.0f initialisation, vcvt of member+0xD8, s16 += level, s17 += 1.0f and the final vdiv s0,s16,s17 - the float return Ghidra dropped. The earlier 'UpdateMemberValues' name was wrong: nothing is stored; the caller BattleScene_SpawnMonstersByProgress uses the average level to scale its spawns.

name: Menu_CountPartyActors
summary: Returns the total number of actors in the party list and the guest/second list.
evidence: Returns func_005797D8(self+0x4254,0) + func_005797D8(self+0x4270,0); called by 8 menu paths.

name: maybe_Battle_PickRandomPartyActor
summary: Collects up to 16 valid battle actors into a local array and returns one at random (or 0 when none qualify). When context+0x10 is 0 it scans the four unit lists at battle work +0x4298+i*0x1C requiring virtual +0x18; otherwise it scans only the party list at +0x4260 requiring both +0x18 and +0x24, then rolls the battle RNG for the final index.
evidence: The three callers are Battle_Message_BuildActorRowBig, Battle_Ui_RunMessageRowCommand and Battle_ActorAction_UpdateReaction, all of which need a random actor for a message/reaction; the body rolls func_001CA474 and walks the four unit lists from FACTS.md. Whether 'party' is the right scope is still unproven (the lists may include guests/enemies).

name: maybe_Ui_CreateSlotObject
summary: Resets two UI-core sub-controllers through vtable+0x1C, allocates a 0x3C4-byte object, constructs it with func_001E0024(obj,-2), stores it into the global slot table at 0x4204+slot_offset and runs its vtable+0x14.
evidence: NEW: still no callers anywhere in the readable C, and the store target is a global pointer array indexed by the raw argument (a byte offset, not a pointer). The class built by func_001E0024 is unidentified, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_CloseScreenIfChildDone
summary: Per-frame close check for a screen: polls the sub-screen object at +0x4204 through its vtable slots +8 and +0xC and, once it reports finished, plays animation 0xD on the screen's animation handle and switches the two UI context layers off (vtable +0x28 with 1, then 0/1). Always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the only callee is the confident Ui_GetCore (0.6), which shows the two layer switches go through the UI core's context+0x1C object; the polled object at +0x4204 and the animation id 0xD are unchanged from the first pass.

name: maybe_Menu_FindActorSlot
summary: Looks an actor id up in the panel's five 0x40-byte slot records (id fields +0x4C/+0x8C/+0xCC/+0x10C/+0x14C) and returns into the found-slot handling; values matching none of the five are ignored.
evidence: The body is byte-for-byte the same five-slot id test that opens the now-named Menu_AssignActorToFreeSlot (0x0020C348): it compares value against the same +0x4C/+0x8C/+0xCC/+0x10C/+0x14C fields and returns when none matches. So it is a slot lookup by actor id, not a mode-value validator; the found branch is lost after the noreturn std_ConstructArray call.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon
signature: void maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon(MenuState* menu, unsigned actorId, unsigned slot, unsigned index)
summary: Refreshes one item icon/slot record of a menu page: it walks the menu's five-slot id chain (+0x4E/+0x8E/+0xCE/+0x10E/+0x14E), builds the icon name from the inline 'it_0001' sheet literal and rebuilds the slot record through Menu_ItemIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.
evidence: The icon helpers are now named menu icon routines and the caller Menu_Slot_StoreActorId is the slot-claim path, so the reading holds; the body still carries an in_r12 artefact and the 'it_0001' sheet literal is the only hard naming evidence, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateSkillIcon
signature: void maybe_Menu_UpdateSkillIcon(MenuState* menu, unsigned actorId, unsigned skillId, unsigned slot)
summary: Refreshes a skill icon/command entry: builds the skill icon name from the inline 'sk_0155'/'sk_0034'/'sk_0104' sheet literals and updates the five-slot id chain (+0x4D/+0x8D/+0xCD/+0x10D/+0x14D) and the slot record through Menu_SkillIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.

name: Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidth

name: Ui_DrawSpriteById

evidence: NEW: the callees are now named (Ui_SpritePart_Create, Ui_GetCore, the atlas lookup func_00633560, maybe_Ui_Sprite_Draw), so the function is exactly 'fill the descriptor for one sprite id and draw it'; nothing suggests a different id source than arg2.

name: Ui_Sprite_DrawByName

summary: Resolves sprite resource by name from the global UI sprite manager singleton (0x007BE310) via func_0063D384 and submits it to generic sprite draw path func_002283FC with default flags.

name: Ui_SpritePart_Create
summary: Creates a sprite part for a UI object: releases any previous part at +4, allocates a 0x1E4-byte part from the UI core heap (func_003BEDFC), inserts it into the window through the core part factory 0x0021F738, marks it as sprite f_94 = 1, applies the draw mode and, when the owner has a draw descriptor f_C, fills the 0x3F2 mask/rect fields for it.
evidence: Ui_GetCore (0x006F229C, N_021) heap at core->f_C->f_10; Mem_AllocAligned(0x1E4,...,4) + func_003BEDFC (part ctor); func_0021F738(core,part) = Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, with cleanup via func_0021F8B8 when it fails; func_003BED3C/func_003BEAFC/func_003BED94 configure the sprite; mask 0xFFFFF800 and the 'H,W' literal are the layout rect fields. Called from maybe_Ui_DrawSpriteById.

name: maybe_Ui_SpritePart_SetParams
signature: void maybe_Ui_SpritePart_SetParams(void* spritePart, u32 valueA, u32 valueB, u32 arg4)
summary: Setter on a UI sprite part: stores the two arguments in spritePart+0x38/+0x3C and then notifies the UI core with the fixed id 0x10 (0x001A1774(work+8, 0x10, 1)).
evidence: Address neighbours Ui_SpritePart_Create/Update/CreateFromDesc confirm the class, but the body is a plain two-field setter plus a constant-id notification - nothing is released, so 'Release' was wrong. The two stored fields are not named anywhere, hence the deliberately vague name at 0.4.

name: maybe_Ui_SpritePart_Update

evidence: Two of the four callers are confident (Text_DrawToken, Ui_ShowInfoMessage) and use it exactly as the text/info sprite submit; the three draw targets and the virtual draw calls are unchanged.

name: maybe_Ui_DeactivateAttachedWidget

name: Ui_Part_DeletingDtor
summary: Scalar deleting destructor of the Ui_Part sub-object: calls the destructor body 0x00228838 (which reinstalls vtable 0x0075C3E0, releases the sprite/effect handles and destroys the embedded object at +0x2C) and then operator delete 0x0010F6CC. It is slot 1 of the very vtable 0x0075C3E0 whose slot 0 is that destructor body.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly is exactly 'push {r4,lr}; bl 0x228838; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x10F6CC', and 0x00228838 ends with 'bl 0x1cf7f8; sub r0,r0,#0x2c; pop {r4,r5,pc}' - a destructor body that returns the adjusted pointer and does NOT free. So this is the deleting variant of the pair, and the old 'CreateScoped' name is wrong: nothing is created, the object is destroyed and freed.

name: Ui_Part_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the Ui_Part sub-object: reinstalls its own vtable 0x0075C3E0, releases the three sprite handles at +0x04/+0x08/+0x14 and the effect handle at +0x34, clears a UI flag, destroys the embedded object at +0x2C and frees the enclosing allocation (returns the adjusted pointer).

The old name 'InitFromCore' described the vtable write as construction; the handle releases and the free show it is destruction.

evidence: The pattern-index guard plus the per-slot table at +0x244 and the two transform blocks make the 'pattern transform' reading explicit; callers 0x00231948 and 0x00234144 (0.45) both hand it a model.

name: Actor_HandleCollisionLanding
signature: void Actor_HandleCollisionLanding(Actor* self, int hitType, u32* hitRecord)
summary: Landing handler for a collision hit: for hit type 4 with a flat surface it normalises the actor's velocity, compares it with the hit normal through an acos, and when the impact angle is inside the limit marks the actor as landed and remembers the surface id (no value is returned, so 'Check' was the wrong word).
evidence: NEW: the containing table 0x0075C698 is the actor state/attachment dispatch table (confident Actor_InitStateModels 0.55, Model_SwitchAttachmentsByState_Show/Hide 0.5, Actor_ResetToIdleAction 0.5), so this is an actor-state handler; and the compiler left it void while it writes +0x3F4/+0x3F8, i.e. it *performs* the landing rather than testing it.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateNamedNodeAndId
summary: Debug/validation hook: when the global switch at 0x7A3168 is on it resets the model's "N_ALL" node to the default transform and re-registers the model's two record ids; when the second switch is on it re-applies the render object at f_30C.
evidence: The string literal "N_ALL" and the two global switches are the only anchors; whether this is a * debug aid or a mandatory refresh depends on how those switches are set at runtime, which is not visible * in the readable C, so maybe_.

name: Actor_PlayAnimationByState
summary: Routes an animation request to the right model: when the current player state has an attachment slot and that state's flag f_5A is set it starts the action sequence on the state model (0x00223030), otherwise it sends the animation name to the shared model node (vtable+0x84); finally it forwards to the generic scene-node setter func_005F6000.
evidence: `uVar4 = work+8+0x48+0x281; if (slot != 0) { if (func_0063D6B8(table,uVar4)->f_5A) func_00223030(slot,arg2); }` else `func_003F422C(f_30C)` + vtable+0x84(node,arg2); tail func_005F6000(actor,arg2). func_00223030 = Anim_ActionSeq_StartForActor (N_024).

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateDirectionBlend
summary: Per-frame movement integrator for the scripted action ids 0x253..0x25B: blends the actor's direction vector toward the stored target, renormalises it and adds the per-frame motion scaled by an easing factor chosen by actor[0x105], then advances the motion counter and hands the transform to Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren.
evidence: The named callees Os_GetGameWork, std_Powf and Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren confirm a movement/transform integrator rather than a pure facing blend, and the three easing curves plus the counter at actor[0x107] are visible; no caller and no named action ids tie it to a specific move, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Model_CreateBillboardPart
signature: void Model_CreateBillboardPart(Model* model, const void* partDesc)
summary: Creates a 200x120 billboard/sprite part for the model when the descriptor's f_1F flag is set and the current model id is not registered yet: builds the sprite descriptor (0x10/0xFF colour) through the billboard descriptor helper, allocates a 0x224-byte part, registers it and applies the name strings.

name: Actor_InitStateModels

evidence: The body calls the now-named Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildrenUpdate, func_005E74A0/func_00233738 (initial action) and func_00636000 (inventory-flag test) per state, then creates the per-state part at self+i*4+0x420.

name: Model_SyncAllStateAttachments

evidence: The callees are now named Model_AttachSlot_HideAll/Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll, and the per-state array at +0x244 plus the state byte from the UI manager are exactly what the name claims. The only uncertainty is the class name, which is unchanged.

name: ModelPreview_CreateAttachments

name: Actor_SelectAttractAnimation

evidence: Same branch tree as 0x00233738 with func_005E7848 instead of func_005E74A0; ~40 callers across the actor, field-action and party code (maybe_Field_Action_CanFinishCut, maybe_Field_ActorMove_Integrate, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateBehaviour, Party_Status_SetEnabled, maybe_Model_UpdateLaunchMotion, ...) - the standard 'return to idle animation' call.

name: Actor_UpdateFollowTarget
summary: Per-frame follow update: compares the actor position with the follow target, plays the walk/run animation depending on the state flag, and clears the follow offset when the actor is inside the arrival radius.
evidence: The body's target fields (+0x3D4..+0x3DC vs actor +0x9C..+0xA4), vtable+0x68/+0x6C animation switch and f_C4 reset match, and 0x003DD3E0 (UpdateFollowTargetMotion) is the continuation.

name: Actor_ResetToIdleAction
summary: Resets the actor to idle action 0x1B; when the UI overlay has no active mode it applies the scene node's motion id, and when a mode is active it copies the five display strings from the mode record into the model object and clears the 0x20000000 flag.
evidence: The action id 0x1B and the two branches are explicit, and the string copies now go through the named std_FixedString15_Ctor; the name still covers only the first action, not the display-string refresh.

summary: Builds/updates the actor's trail quad: computes the two side vertices from the current and previous positions, expands the quad by the width factor and writes the four vertices into the trail object.
evidence: Both callers are now named (maybe_Action_UpdateTrailQuadUnlessFlag, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateTrailWhenNotPaused) and the body uses the quad-vertex helper plus the 1.41421/1.25 constants, corroborating the trail role independently.

name: Actor_ApplyStateAnimName
summary: Installs a name/animation string on the actor: when the pattern byte (world+0x48+0x281) is non-zero it looks the record up with 0x0063D6B8 and passes the relative string at record+0x38, otherwise it passes the built-in g_00234BB8; either way through owner vtable+0x84, the slot 0x001BA510 uses for its completion callback.
evidence: The record lookup by the current pattern id and the vtable+0x84(string) call are both explicit, and an empty pattern falls back to a static string; that is exactly 'apply the name for the current state'.

name: Actor_CreateTaskChainB
summary: Second task-chain builder for actors: allocates and installs the state tasks (task 0x19 and the next slots) through Container_SlotReplace, then refreshes the action state and the overlay animation.
evidence: Same shape as the confirmed Actor_StartBehaviourState/Actor_CreateTaskChain (task ids 0x19/0x1A, Mem_AllocAligned + factory + Container_SlotReplace, then Party_Status_SetEnabled and the overlay trigger); callers are maybe_Gfx_Object_EnterState4 and Party_Status_SetEnabled.

name: maybe_Gfx_Object_EnterState4
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Object_EnterState4(GfxObject* self, const GfxTransform* xform)
summary: Puts a scene object into state 4, stores the caller's transform and attaches the four state components (0x44/0x2C/0x30/0x74 bytes) via Container_SlotReplace, switching the related overlay groups off.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now maybe_Battle_Sequence_UpdateSlotEffects, and the named callees Field_ActorAction_NarrowRun / Field_NarrowPassAction_Ctor / Container_SlotReplace confirm the action-component installs; the component kinds are still inferred, so maybe_.

name: maybe_ModelPreview_SelectAttachmentSlot
signature: void maybe_ModelPreview_SelectAttachmentSlot(GfxSubObject* self, const u8* slot, u8 value)
summary: Selects the model-preview attachment for a slot: if the slot already holds an attachment with the expected id it just refreshes it, otherwise it creates the attachment from the 12-entry constant table at 0x00726808 and records the slot index in f_278.
evidence: Both callees are ModelPreview_* (CreateAttachments / UpdateAttachments) and the body keys on the same f_278 slot index plus the +0x244 attachment table as 0x0023406C, so the subsystem is the model preview, not a generic Gfx sub-object. The body is damaged (unaff_r5/unaff_r6 from the 12-byte Thumb entry), so maybe_ stays.

name: ModelPreview_SelectSlot
signature: void ModelPreview_SelectSlot(ModelPreview* self, const u8* sel)
summary: Switches which previewing character model is shown: if slot sel[0] already holds the wanted variant (slot->f_126 == sel[1]) it just re-applies the pose, otherwise it builds the model for that slot from the 12-entry parameter table g_00235238 and records the slot in f_278.
evidence: Slot array self+0x244[idx]; f_278 is cleared then set to *arg2; func_00231D88 applies pose/effects for slot (it uses the bone names s_j_ude_a_l/s_j_ude_a_r and func_0035FF3C effect instances); func_002315C0 creates a 0x6e4-byte render object (Mem_AllocAligned 0x6e4 + func_00225D90) from the 12 u32 table at 0x00726808; caller 0x00239A94 is the page switch.

name: Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord
summary: Copies the five 16-byte name strings of a character record into the actor (display name, short name, ...) and pushes the first one to the view through virtual +0x84.
evidence: Six callers, all actor/model creation: 0x0022FBD8 (Actor_CreateBehaviourTasks), 0x002306B8, 0x00231D88 (ModelPreview_UpdateAttachments), 0x00232248, 0x00234614 (Actor_ResetToIdleAction), 0x00235378. Body: `iVar1 = arg1[0xf]; if (iVar1 != 0 && (iVar1->f_10 & 0x20000000) != 0) { iVar1 = func_0063D6B8(work, arg2);` then five times `iVar4 = func_006F44B0(auStack_2c, iVar1 + offset + field)` (std_FixedString15_Ctor, named in N_077 out) with offsets f_38, f_3c, f_40, f_44, f_48 written to self+0x68, +0x90, +0x7c, +0xb8, +0xcc; finally `(**(*arg1 + 0x84))(arg1, name)`. The 0x20000000 bit is the record 'has name block' flag also tested in 0x001E77FC.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_SyncSlotFromHandle
summary: When no display slot is active it resolves the object behind the slot's handle and, if it is an overlay element of the expected class, tells it to detach (vtable+0x3C with 4) and copies its slot id back into the slot object.
evidence: Callers Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord_0023523c, Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClassB_0031c0ec; The handle/class resolution helpers are now named (func_003F422C owner lookup, * Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord) but the slot/display semantics are still inferred from the written * byte, so kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_ReleaseEffectHandles
summary: Release virtual of the character-model actor: while the actor is active it walks the two effect handles at +0x420/+0x424, releases each one that is still alive in the global handle table, then runs Gfx_Node_Dtor on the node.
evidence: New context: the function is slot +0x10 of vtable 0x0075C660, whose neighbours are Model_CreateCharacterModelWithEquipment, Actor_InitStateModels and Actor_ResetToIdleAction, so the owner is a character-model actor and not a UI overlay - the old 'Ui_Overlay_FreeSlotSprites' named the wrong subsystem. What the two handles represent is still unknown, so it stays maybe_.

name: Gfx_SpriteObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a 2D sprite/particle object: allocates it with tag 0x20000001, installs vtable 0x002357D8 and seeds the position/velocity/scale/uv blocks from the shared constant tables at 0x002357DC..0x002357E0.
evidence: The body is fully readable (vtable literal, three 8-word default blocks, -0x800 sentinels), which makes the constructor role certain; there is no caller to fix the owning class beyond 'sprite object'.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the sprite-object class: stores the class descriptor, points the embedded vtable slot self[0x88] at baseClassDesc+0xB8, releases the cached scene handle through the actor manager (work+8->f_54), then runs Field_SceneObject_Delete, the widget detach/destroy helper and the allocator free.
evidence: Named callees settle the direction: Field_SceneObject_Delete (0x005F842C), Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy (0x001C7524) and the shared free tail are the destructor chain, and the function sits immediately after Gfx_SpriteObject_Ctor (0x00235494). 'InitFromClass' described only the vtable store and missed that everything afterwards deletes the object.

name: Ui_OverlayManager_Reset
summary: Resets the UI overlay manager at work+0x48: clears the row id/flag fields, copies the saved UI mode bytes into f_281/f_282, and (re)allocates its three work buffers (800/100/100 words) plus the 25-entry parameter table.
evidence: The caller Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAll passes work->f_48, and the object has the UI overlay manager's mode byte at +0x281 (established fact). The three buffers and the global pair template are unchanged, so "Party_Status_Open" was the wrong subsystem.

name: Ui_Overlay_ClearAll
signature: void Ui_Overlay_ClearAll(UiOverlay* self, const u8* mode)
summary: Full reset of the overlay manager: destroys both child sprite layers, blanks the twelve slot widgets (keeping slots 8 and 9), resets the cached per-slot ids and releases every live marker through its element's virtual release.
evidence: The body now calls the named Ui_Overlay_ClearEntries plus Field_DetachSlotObjectA/B on gameWork+0x54 and walks the slot table exactly as described; the callers include Field_ExitTalkMode.

name: Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup
signature: void Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup(UiOverlay* self, const u8* mode, const UiSlotSetup* setup)
summary: Sets self+0x11 and derives visibility flags (e.g. +0x27C) from mode bytes 0..4 before applying the slot setup on the UI overlay manager.
evidence: Neighbours Actor_ApplyModelVariant, Effect_CreateInstanceWithDefaults, and Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation; called on GameWork+0x48 UI overlay manager to configure overlay slot display parameters.

name: Ui_Overlay_RefreshActorAttachments
summary: Clears the overlay's animation flag f_284 and then refreshes the attach transform of every visible field actor whose type word f_30 carries the 0x20000040 attach bits, by walking the field actor list (work+8 -> +0x54) and calling maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateAttachTransform.
evidence: All nine callers are overlay/actor state-change paths (Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange, Ui_Overlay_RefreshSlots, Field_Object2D_RunStateSequence, Event_Rura_End, ...), and both call sites run it immediately after changing the overlay mode self->f_281. The in-loop callee is the attach-transform updater (Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection + weapon animation time), so 'ResetElementAnimation' described only the f_284 clear and missed the actual work.

name: Ui_Overlay_RefreshSlots
signature: void Ui_Overlay_RefreshSlots(UiOverlay* self, const u8* mode, const UiSlotSetup* setup)
summary: After a mode change re-posts the overlay marker transform, re-triggers/shows (or resets/hides) its element classes and rebuilds the slot list from the master table (func_0066AA7C, count +0x3218).
evidence: Directly called by Field_ResetTalkState (0x001D66F0) passing the UI overlay manager from (work+8)->+0x48 to refresh overlay slots/markers upon scene transition.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateSlotVisibility
summary: Chooses the entry's display state: mode 8 places the slot marker (0x004D78E4 on the sub-object at +0x16C plus Ui_RegisterActor), mode 9 clears self+0x280, and every other mode hit-tests the entry's cell and position against the Field2D view (0x0062F0E0/0x0062C388/0x0062C3B0/0x0062CB64/0x0062C23C) to pick state 3, else 2, which is then applied with func_005E7848(entry, state, 0).

name: Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange

evidence: Nine callers (0x001D6770 Field_HandleMapJump, 0x00235A50 maybe_Ui_Overlay_ClearAll, 0x002F493C, 0x003DD068, 0x0040DC40, 0x00448F20, 0x004C754C, 0x004C7A8C, 0x0061AF68 Ui_OverlaySlot_UpdateStateMachine). Body: `if (self->f_281 == 0) return; local_48 = self->f_281; self->f_281 = 0; ... func_0022FBD8(actor, (u8)local_48); ... func_00612CA0(&work->f_24a98, kind, ..., actor->f_14);` then `func_00238174(self,&local_48)` (create the model), copy `f_9c/f_a0/f_a4`, `f_118 = 1`, `func_005F5F54`, copy the 0xcc..0xfc colour/scale block, `func_001C7524(...)` to release the old one; the second half does the same for the effect (`func_0022C1D0`, `func_0022D8D4`, `func_006133B4`, `func_00613F54`, `func_005F34F0`, `func_005F36E0`); ends with `func_00236B50(self); func_00238818(self); func_001C839C(...); func_0023BB00(self,kind,0);`.

name: Ui_Overlay_PlayElementSe
signature: void Ui_Overlay_PlayElementSe(u32 arg1, u32 slotId, u32 seId)
summary: Plays an SE on the overlay element that owns a given slot id: resolves the slot handle to the element, checks it against the accepted element classes and forwards the sound id to that element's sound component.
evidence: Named callers maybe_Text_ClearCell / maybe_Text_UpdateCellState pass the UI-overlay manager at work+0x48 and a slot id, and the body's class-accept loop ends in the component sound call with the requested id.

name: Ui_Overlay_TryTouchSelect
summary: Touch-select step of the map overlay: bails out while a menu/mode flag is set or the overlay is not allowed to show markers, then either hit-tests the marker grid (mode 9) or projects the anchor and calls the hit function, and finally selects the marker and registers it.
evidence: The named gates Ui_Overlay_CanShowMarkers / maybe_Ui_HitTestGrid and the final maybe_Ui_RegisterActor call read cleanly, and the only caller is Ui_Overlay_Update.

name: Ui_Overlay_CreateSlotWidget
signature: u32 Ui_Overlay_CreateSlotWidget(UiOverlay* self, u32 slotKind, u8 alpha)
summary: The overlay slot widget factory: ten slot kinds each construct their own widget class and register it at self+0x50+kind*4.
evidence: The switch over slotKind 1..10 calls the named per-kind constructors (Ui_OverlaySlotObject_Ctor, Ui_SpriteWidget_Ctor, Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor, Field_Gadget_Ctor, ...), initialises each from the shared 0x58-byte style block and assigns a unique id from g_00237E48.

name: Ui_Overlay_CreateAuxWidget
signature: u32 Ui_Overlay_CreateAuxWidget(UiOverlay* self, const u8* slot)
summary: Creates the auxiliary widget for the selected overlay slot (kinds 1..7, stored at +0x20..+0x38) from that slot's sprite record and marks the element as needing a re-place.
evidence: The body switches on the slot kind and constructs the matching widget (0x002B6A08/0x0021B86C/0x002B6AB4/...), then sets element->f_59A = 1; called from the named Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange path.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_ReleaseSlotObject
summary: State-exit hook that detaches the field slot object held by the scene root (work+0x54) and always reports success.
evidence: Its sole caller is the named Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll and the callee is the named Field_DetachSlotObjectA on the field actor manager; nothing in the body is overlay-specific, so Ui_Overlay_ReleaseChildSpriteA was misleading.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectManager_DetachSlotB
summary: Calls Field_DetachSlotObjectB on the field object manager at (work+8)+0x54 and always returns 1.
