name: Ui_Overlay_FreeSpriteHandleB
summary: Releases the slot's sprite: resolves the handle at +0x4C to a scene sprite through 0x005F2EC8 and, when it is still alive, detaches and destroys it through Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy on the scene's 2D root (work+0x54).
evidence: NEW: the release path is now named (Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy on game work +0x54) which matches the 'free the slot's sprite handle' reading exactly; the twin 0x002394DC (maybe_Ui_Overlay_FreeSpriteHandleA) uses the other release call, so the A/B pair is a genuine two-call-site pattern.

name: Ui_Overlay_HideElementClass
summary: Clears the overlay manager's second visibility flag and asks every registered element of one class to hide itself (the hide half of the show/hide pair).
evidence: Body: f_285 = 0, then the registry walk on gameWork+0x54 with the class mask 0x40000040 and a per-element hide call; the mirror at 0x0023A580 sets f_285 = 1, which pins the polarity.

name: Ui_Overlay_ClearEntries
summary: Drops every live marker: releases both handles of each of the f_278 entry records, zeroes the records, resets the marker count and releases the second child sprite.
evidence: loop over f_278 entries at self+i*0xc reading +0x20c and +0x210, each released with 0x001C7570 and zeroed with 0x00672318; then f_274=0 and 0x0022DD98() when gameWork+0x54+0x20 exists; same record layout as 0x0023A0B0/0x0023E4A8

name: Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite
signature: u32 Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite(UiOverlaySlot* self, u32 kindA, u32 kindB, u32 id)
summary: Resolves which sprite an overlay slot should show: tries the first child object (work+0x54 -> +0x1C) by id, falls back to the second child (+0x20), and records the matching kind in f_3B4 and the id in f_3B8; returns 0 when neither child knows the id.
evidence: NEW: the named callees Actor_PlayActionAnimation and Os_GetGameWork plus the two child slots confirm the 'try child A, then child B' structure; the script natives 0x00159C48/0x0015A410 are its callers, so it is a native-facing resolver.

name: Party_Status_SetMemberValue
signature: void Party_Status_SetMemberValue(PartyStatus* self, u32 charId, int value)
summary: Sets a party member's current value (HP-style) to 'value', clamped to the maximum reported by the character record's vtable: it clears the record's 0x10 flag, calls the record setter, then refreshes that member's row (model colour/parameter block, UI event, list rebuild).
evidence: func_0035EB98(heap,charId) returns the character record and the function bails out when (rec->f_da & 0x10)==0; max = vtable+8(rec), setter = vtable[0](rec,value); the same idiom appears in 0x0023BA70 (value = max*ratio, clamped) and 0x00447EA4 (revive: 'if current==0 set to max'); row loop over f_274 0xc-byte entries comparing the byte at +0x214 with charId; func_005F2EC8 / func_005F4DCC apply an 8-byte colour block with a per-mode offset (self->f_27f -> 0xf..0x12 / func_0023D078); func_001C839C(core,7,0/3,rec) plus func_0023C588(self) finish the refresh.

name: Party_Status_RequestFieldActorRefresh
summary: Marks partyStatus->u8_284 = 1, refreshes the primary field actor at (work+8)->f_54->f_1C via 0x00230A90 if present, and calls 0x003E870C(actor, resetMode) on all field actors in (work+8)->f_54 whose +0x30 flags have 0x20000040 set.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x238CC8..0x238D84: saves 2nd arg mov r6,r1 (missed by Ghidra) and passes movne r1,r6 to 0x3E870C. All 17 callers pass (*(osWork->f_08 + 0x48), 0) immediately before Party_Status_SetEnabled(*(osWork->f_08 + 0x48), 1), proving r0 is PartyStatus* (neighbor of Party_Status_SetMemberValue 0x238A48), not a generic UiOverlay.

name: Ui_Overlay_AvoidCollision
summary: Nudges a map marker out of blocked map cells: tests the four direction bits through the bitmap manager, derives a -1/+1 delta scaled by the overlay step byte (+0x27F), applies it to the marker and plays the matching move action.
evidence: The four func_0062C23C bit tests, the comparison against the global last delta and the named Actor_TryPlayActionSeq10 call make the collision-avoidance role readable; caller is Ui_Overlay_Update.

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateMarkerTrail
summary: Updates one map-overlay marker: builds the marker rectangle (maybe_Ui_Overlay_GetMarkerRect), shifts the 16-entry position ring at +0x308/+0x30C by one, looks for an overlapping entry (maybe_Field_FindOverlapIndex) and, when found, plays the 8-way facing animation on the marker model; then copies the 0x80-byte history into +0x288.
evidence: Directly called from Ui_Overlay_Update (0x0023D988) to update marker position ring buffer (+0x308/+0x30C) and facing animation for overlay markers.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_RegisterSceneNode
summary: Resolves the scene-node handle at self+0x4C through 0x005F2EC8 and, when it yields a node, hands it to the field object manager so the node is linked into its per-class bucket and gets its vt[+0x64] callback.
evidence: The append target is now the confident Field_ObjectManager_RegisterByClass (0.62), whose body links fieldObj+8 into fieldObjMgr+0x9C+class*0xC and calls fieldObj->vt[+0x64] - a registration, not a release, so the old 'FreeSpriteHandleA' verb was wrong. The handle source 0x005F2EC8 is still unnamed, so the object type stays open.

name: Party_Status_AddMember
summary: Adds a character to the member list: ignores duplicates, resolves the record, inserts the id into the global id array (count at heap+0x27218) - appending at the end for ordinary members and keeping the front positions for special ones - creates that member's row/3-D preview, then rebuilds the list and the selection.
evidence: Duplicate loop over heap+0x27218 ids using func_0066B0E4; func_00612ADC(base,index,id) writes the array and f_27218 is bumped; the branch on func_0062917C(rec) and the 'i < 4' test select insert-at-end vs insert-at-front; func_0023E4A8(self,charId,mode) builds the 12-byte row (UI widget + model + char id byte) and honours the 2/4 row limits; func_0023C588(self) rebuilds; no direct callers (vtable/dispatch entry).

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_AssignEntryOrder
summary: Re-numbers the overlay entries: walks the 0xC-byte entries from index 1, writes a running counter into word +0x8A of each and calls 0x003E7110(element, index); the anchor entry is given order 0.
evidence: Decompilation contains damaged registers/blocks; The decompiler lost registers (unaff_r* / overlapping instructions at 0x00239EFC), so the * anchor handling and the exact call arguments are still guesses; no named caller or callee was found.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_SetMarkerState
signature: void maybe_Ui_Overlay_SetMarkerState(u8* slot, u8 value, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Writes a state byte into a marker slot and applies the matching animation: the same id-range switch as 0x00239D58, resolving the model effect entry and the part attribute, with the arguments destroyed by the decompiler (unaff registers).
evidence: Decompilation contains damaged registers/blocks; Only the structural twin of 0x00239D58 survives in the readable C; Gearing it to the overlay * family is an inference from that twin and from the shared 0x0017C054 call, so the name stays a * placeholder.

name: Party_Status_SelectPage
signature: void Party_Status_SelectPage(PartyStatus* self, const u8* sel)
summary: Switches the displayed page: stores sel[0] in f_281, rebuilds the per-page model widget (ModelPreview_SelectSlot on the preview holder), rebinds the secondary panel with the new selection, then walks all 12 element handles at self+0x1c removing the ones that are no longer wanted and re-adding the selected one before marking the page and refreshing the selection.
evidence: f_281 = *(u16*)arg2 (page 0..11); func_002351B4(core->f_54->f_1c, arg2) switches the 3-D model slot; func_0022D60C/func_0022D8D4 set the other panel; 12-handle loop with func_001C7570 (remove) / func_001C7658 (add) and func_00612CA0 / func_00613354 to reset the manager slots (0xffff); page 8 additionally writes 0xff at heap+0x2d54a; ends with func_0023BB00(self,f_281,1), func_0023C9DC(f_281) and func_001C839C(core,6,2,0).

name: Ui_Overlay_ApplyMarkerAnimation
summary: Applies the pending animation/effect of an overlay marker: if the cached id (+0x4B32) is not 0xFFFF it switches on the id range (0x9E0/0x9D6/0x14/0x600/0x6FE/0x700), resolves the model effect entry and the part attribute, and plays the direction animation; clears the cache afterwards.
evidence: Directly called by Ui_Overlay_Update (0x0023D988) on overlay element update; checks cached effect ID at +0x4B32 and triggers corresponding animation/effect on the marker.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_SetStateByte
summary: Stores the byte at self+0xC1C and then broadcasts message 8 to group 0 of the field object manager's object lists, i.e. stores a state and tells the field objects to refresh.
evidence: The second callee is now the named Ui_Widget_DispatchToGroupedChildren (0.50) and its body walks the ten 0xC-byte child groups at +0x24 calling vt[+0x38] on every element, so the old 'part group 8' reading was wrong: 8 is the message id and 0 the group. The object class is still unverified, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_Overlay_RemoveEntry
summary: Removes the marker with the given id from the overlay list: detaches its sprites, releases both handles, re-numbers the remaining markers and decrements the count.
evidence: Scans self->f_274 entries for f_214 == arg2; on a hit calls 0x0064A090(&out, element) + 0x0022DB5C(gameWork+0x54 child, sprite) to detach, releases with 0x001C7570, re-assigns [0x8a] order through 0x003E7110 and ends with f_274 -= 1 - exactly the inverse of 0x0023E4A8

name: Actor_UpdateIdleAnimationPair
summary: Updates the two actor-manager slots (work+8 -> +0x54 -> +0x1C and +0x20) with Actor_SelectAttractAnimation and Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState and ORs their results, so a non-zero return means one of them is still animating.
evidence: NEW: both callees are named (Actor_SelectAttractAnimation, Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState) and the only caller is the named PlayerSetDefaultAction (0x0015D260), which uses the OR-ed result as 'still animating'. The two slots are the actor manager's +0x1C/+0x20 from FACTS.md; 0.55.

name: maybe_Battle_ReleaseUnitHandle
summary: Drops the battle unit's weak handle at +0x39C: when the generation-tagged handle still resolves and the bound object has the flags 0x20000010, it notifies it through vtable +0xB4, then clears the +0x395 flag and resets +0x39C to the empty sentinel.
evidence: Decompilation contains damaged registers/blocks; The decompilation is damaged - the cleared handle is rebuilt from unaff_r6, so the sentinel * value cannot be verified; the handle decode against 0x007B80C0 and the vtable +0xB4 notification are * clear, but per the project rule a body with unaff_rN stays maybe_ at <= 0.3.

name: Party_Status_ResumeFieldActors
summary: Marks partyStatus->u8_285 = 1, updates primary actor (work+8)->f_54->f_20 via 0x0022CB90 if non-null, and calls Field_Actor_Resume(actor, resumeMode) on every actor in (work+8)->f_54 whose +0x30 flags have 0x40000040 set.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x23A580..0x23A63C: twin of Party_Status_RequestFieldActorRefresh (0x00238CC8); saves 2nd arg mov r6,r1 (missed by Ghidra) and passes it to Field_Actor_Resume (0x3E71A4). Callers Party_Status_SelectPage, PictureCardMoveTarget, Ui_Overlay_CameraFocusTask, Ui_DragScroll_Begin, and Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState all pass (*(osWork->f_08 + 0x48), mode).

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyEntryTag
signature: void maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyEntryTag(UiOverlay* self, u32 id, u32 index)
summary: Pushes a 0x12-byte tag record (text colour and layout fields) to the player's HUD object or to the marker with the given id, and clears it when the index is out of range.
evidence: The body resolves the target through func_0035EB98 and a data-manager row (func_0063EB94), * then applies it with Model_Equip_ApplyAccessoryEffects/func_0031A6AC and maybe_Effect_CreateAttached2. * Whether the copied block is a 'tag' or an effect attachment descriptor is unclear, so keep maybe_ at * 0.4.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_CheckEntryPlacement
summary: Decides whether a marker entry may be placed and where: bails out when the overlay is suppressed, CanShowMarkers fails or entry+0x1C5 is set, resolves the target through Data_ResolveRecordPtrs, then walks candidate anchor offsets (anchor kinds 0/2/4/6) and rejects any that overlaps a field actor (Field_FindActorInRect) or an occupied UI cell, returning 1 only for a free position.
evidence: The early-out chain and the per-anchor clamping are corroborated by named callees (Ui_Overlay_CanShowMarkers, Field_FindActorInRect, Data_ResolveRecordPtrs) and a named caller (Script_RegisterThread_InitContext), but the body still reads uninitialised flag registers (unaff_r11/in_fpscr), so confidence stays below 0.5 and the maybe_ prefix is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_SetStateByteB
summary: Template copy of 0x0023A080: stores the byte at self+0xC1C and broadcasts message 8 to group 0 of the field object manager's object lists.
evidence: Same body as 0x0023A080 (Ghidra swapped the two arguments there); the broadcast callee is now the named Ui_Widget_DispatchToGroupedChildren (0.50), which walks the field object manager's ten child groups. Only one of the two copies can be reached from a given vtable slot and neither has a caller, so the B suffix and maybe_ stay.

name: maybe_Field_FindOverlapIndex
summary: Walks idsA from start, skips ids also present in idsB, resolves the remaining object and, when its flag word matches mask and its condition/group reference is active, applies the attribute hook for shapeHandle; returns start+1 on the first hit.
evidence: The named Field_Condition_HasActiveRef/Field_Object_HasActiveGroupRef/ApplyAttribute callees show the per-candidate test, but the return value is an index advance, so 'overlap' is only the old interpretation.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget(FieldObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 geometry, u32 mask)
summary: Resolves the target under the cursor through the overlay entry list (maybe_Ui_Overlay_FindTargetUnderCursor), then applies the viewport/shape attribute of the matching entry kind to the model part.
evidence: The old Field_ prefix was unsupported: the caller is maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitPartMask, the * callees are the Ui_Overlay_* family (FindTargetUnderCursor, CheckEntryPlacement, * ModelPart_ApplyAttribute) and the function reads the touch flag f_1c5.

name: maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitPartMask
signature: void maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitPartMask(BattleUnit* self, u32 maskIn, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Applies a part/attachment selection to a battle unit: merges the caller mask with the model flag word, probes the primary/secondary attachment tables and forwards the successful transform to the render model, otherwise falls back to the default part update.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateMarkerTrail and the body has FFFF8000 handle-mask damage; kept at 0.30.

name: Party_Status_RemoveMember
summary: Removes a character from the member list: finds it in the global id array, marks that entry 0xff, shifts the following ids down one slot, decrements the count and tears down the member's row.
evidence: Guarded by count heap+0x27218 > 1; func_0066B0E4 reads and func_00612ADC writes entries, with 0xff used as the empty marker (same convention as 0x00235E0C); the shift loop re-reads index i+1 and writes 0xff into i+1; then func_0023A0B0(arg1,charId) removes the 12-byte row and decrements f_274.

name: maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle(BattleUnit* self, u32 handle, u8* other)
summary: Handle/ID match test: masks the argument and self+0x39C with the same constant, compares both the masked index and the shifted generation, then compares the byte at self+0x3A0 with a byte taken from the third argument. The old 'ApplyPartMaskToModel' name came from the caller and does not fit a comparison.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0023B6F4: `push {r4-r8,sb,sl,fp,lr}; sub sp,sp,#0x8c; ldr r8,[pc,#0x34c]; ldrb fp,[sl,#0x95]; and r0,r1,r8,asr #10; ldr r1,[r4,#0x39c]` then at 0x0023B734 `and fp,r1,r8,asr #10; cmp r0,fp; lsreq r0,r5,#0xb; cmpeq r0,r1,lsr #11; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#0` and `ldrb r0,[r4,#0x3a0]; ldrb fp,[r2]; cmp r0,fp`. The 64-byte size in the index is a truncation: the function continues at 0x0023B734.

name: maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle_Cont
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_UnitMatchesHandle_Cont(BattleUnit* self, u32 handle, u8* other)
summary: Continuation of 0x0023B6F4 (no prologue at this address): the masked handle comparison and the +0x3A0 byte comparison, followed by the rest of the match test. It is a separate symbol only because Ghidra split the function here.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0023B734 starts with `and fp,r1,r8,asr #10` - no push - and 0x0023B6F4+0x40 is exactly this address, so it is the second half of the function that starts at 0x0023B6F4. The old 'CompareTargetHandles' guess was close in spirit but named a separate function that does not exist.

name: Party_Status_SetMemberValueByRatio
signature: void Party_Status_SetMemberValueByRatio(PartyStatus* self, u32 charId, float ratio)
summary: Sets a member's value to a fraction of its maximum: takes the maximum from the character record, multiplies it by the incoming float, truncates and clamps it to the maximum, and delegates to Party_Status_SetMemberValue.
evidence: max = vtable+8(rec); vector float->unsigned conversion of max*in_s0 masked with 0xffff and clamped by 'if (max < v) v = max'; then func_00238A48(arg1,arg2,v); only caller 0x002E5198.

name: Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetPartPairForId
signature: void Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetPartPairForId(u32 arg1, u32 key, u32 value)
summary: For every 3-byte entry of the sprite-set table whose key byte matches, sets two parts visible: the first entry byte's part to value and the second's to the opposite, so exactly one of the pair is shown.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0060F824 is the named Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetPartVisible and the table comes from the graphics context (work+0x88 -> +8) through 0x0066AA9C / 0x0062AFBC, so this is a sprite-set part toggle keyed by a table entry, not a generic field flag pair.

name: Gfx_Trail_PushSample
signature: u32 Gfx_Trail_PushSample(GfxTrail* self, const TrailSample* sample, int reset)
summary: Shifts the 56-sample trail history (0x38 entries of 0x30 bytes) one slot, inserts new transform sample into slot 0, and submits vertex strip via 0x006F511C.
evidence: Confirmed by named callers Actor_UpdateModelOnStateChange (0x0022C3F4) at 0x0022C6A4/0x0022C6EC and ActorAction_UpdateMove (0x003ADFAC) at 0x003AE190; manages ribbon motion trail samples for active actors.

name: maybe_Gfx_Trail_BuildRibbon
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Trail_BuildRibbon(void* self, const void* sample, const void* offset, u8 flags)
summary: Builds one ribbon segment: shifts 0xEE-entry history buffer, computes perpendicular camera-facing offset, and inserts new control point.
evidence: Connects with Actor_UpdateFollowTarget and Field_Collision_RaycastScene; ribbon geometry algorithm is clear, but owner class is inferred. Kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Ui_Overlay_CanShowMarkers
summary: Boolean gate for marker drawing: needs self+0x283, a world/UI context whose two header bytes are clear, an active world slot (0x1C or 0x20 depending on self+0x27C) and a mode from 0x00669250 in {1,2,9} or {1,2,4,5}; the optional flag then also requires the current child (slot+0x1C->f_312) to be clear.
evidence: Every branch only narrows a yes/no answer over mode and child state, and all three callers (0x00237868, 0x00238F48, 0x0023AA5C) use it as a guard, so 'can show' is supported by use as well as body.

name: Ui_Menu_ClearMode
summary: Leaves the special display mode: clears the two mode bytes at work+0x2D549 and work+0x2D54A, releases the page-1 state effect of the window's model object and clears bit 1 of the global enabled-element mask.
evidence: The two byte clears, the named Model_ReleaseStatePart(obj, 1) and the '&= ~2' mask clear are explicit, and the named caller maybe_Ui_Menu_EnsureDisplayState (0x003F18F8) uses it to undo the mode it set.

name: Party_Status_RebuildRows
summary: Rebuilds the visible member rows from the global id list in four ordered passes - ordinary members, special members, members carrying the 0x10 flag, and id 0x1C last - emitting one row per id.
evidence: Four loops over heap+0x27218 ids; pass 1 requires func_0062917C(rec)==0 && id != 0x1c, pass 2 requires func_0062917C(rec)!=0, pass 3 tests (rec->f_da & 0x10), pass 4 matches id 0x1c; each hit calls func_00239788(self,id) (row emit, not decompiled); invoked at the end of add/remove/select (0x00238A48, 0x00239510, 0x0023D804).

name: Party_Status_SetEnabled
signature: void Party_Status_SetEnabled(PartyStatus* self, int enabled, int only)

evidence: String constant "OnCalcScenarioProgress" (0x00256068) is the 4th argument of func_00579B64 - the exact same 'load script and bind handler' helper used by the already-named siblings Script_CallBookIdCommand ("TrgBookIDCommand"), Script_CallSelectRuraPattern ("OnSelectRuraPattern"), Script_CallSelectRiremitoUsable and maybe_Script_CallEventHandlers. Same 0x18-stride f_98 record walk, same save/restore of f_6C.

name: Script_CallSelectRiremitoUsable
summary: Asks the OnSelectRiremitoUsable handlers whether the selected travel point is usable and returns 1/0 from the first handler that answers.
evidence: Literal s_OnSelectRiremitoUsable_002564e0 with 0x00579B64; branch on the script result value 1 (usable) and 0 (not usable) handled through 0x007078E4 + 0x006BB0F4/0x006BBD7C; returns 1 when no handler answers

name: Event_ClearActorSlots
summary: Releases the two tagged handles held by every 0x10-byte actor slot of the event (low 6 bits of the handle tag select the record table) through the scene actor release helper, then empties the slot list by setting f_434 = f_430.
evidence: Callers are the named script dispatcher paths (Event_DispatchScriptTrigger, maybe_Script_CallEventHandlers) and the handle-tag release helper func_001C917C is the same one used by the scene code; the two pointers f_430/f_434 are the documented event actor-slot pair.

name: Event_AddCommonHandler
summary: Appends a handler record to the event handler vector at self+0x98, stores the literal name "common" in it and copies the event descriptor handle pair from self+0x30. Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings registers it while applying jump settings.
evidence: The body stores the string literal s_common_0025664c into the new element and binds self+0x30; the only caller is Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings (0.5). That is exactly 'add the common handler', so the old 'select current handler slot' reading was wrong.

name: Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand
signature: u32 Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand(FieldManager* self, u32 commandName, u32 objHandle)
summary: Registers the object handle in the scene gadget list (0x0024B010), stores the resulting entry index in f_948 and then fires the script trigger named 'TrgRCommand' through func_006D4588 with commandName as payload. If the manager is already shut down (f_3ac) nothing happens and 0 is returned.
evidence: `if (self->f_3ac == '\0') { f_948 = func_0024B010(self,arg3); result = func_006D4588(self,0xFF,s_TrgRCommand,arg2); }`. func_006D4588 is the named-event dispatcher: its other callers pass the literals s_OnFieldEnd (0x00249DB4), s_OnCutSceneEnd (0x0024CB38), s_TrgEvent (0x0025466C) and s_TrgCommand (0x00253290), all with the same f_3ac guard and payload; g_0024b010 is the gadget-entry appender. 52 callers spread over the actor/battle/menu spawn code.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_UpdateFadeAndJobs
summary: Per-frame scene-flow update: polls and cancels the asynchronous jobs stored in the 0x14-byte list at +0x3F0, removes completed entries, and advances the screen-fade timer at +0x20, pushing the resulting brightness to device+0x1284 or device+0x1220 depending on the configured fade target.
evidence: Entry stride 0x14, list bounds self+0x3F0/+0x3F4; job calls 0x006BBE08/0x006BDBE4/0x006BD830/0x006BD988/0x006BD10C/0x006BD12C/0x006BA690; fade timer self+0x20 against duration self+0x24; writes device+0x1284 (target<2) or +0x1220 (target==2); callers Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C) and Ui_SceneFlow_SyncState (0x0019F7F4); shares its fade math and constants with ScreenEffect_/0x00284784.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_ReleaseSubObject
summary: Releases one scene-flow sub-object: drops the screen-effect grain/vignette, releases the window's lists and frees the two pack handles it owns.
evidence: All three callees are named release helpers (Ui_ScreenEffect_ReleaseGrainAndVignette, Ui_Window_ReleaseLists, Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry) and the sole caller is Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll; the old Event_SubObject_Destroy name had no event code behind it.

evidence: The two float callees are the named Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio/Battle_Monster_GetMpBarRatio (0x00492520/0x004900A8), and their results are summed into the row fields; the named caller Battle_ActionCommand_ProcessSkillEffect passes affected battle units. The old 'Ui_TextLayout_AddToRowGroup' treated those units as glyphs - there is no glyph metric call in the body.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_AddUnitToRowGroupWithValue(UiTargetRow* rows, BattleUnit* unit, u32 groupId, u16 value)
summary: Twin of 0x00279760 with a second pass over the ten target rows: after inserting the unit into a matching or free row and adding its HP/MP ratios, it also stores a caller-supplied u16 in the row's +0x788 payload field and mirrors the unit's flag into +0x794.
evidence: Disassembly is a byte-for-byte copy of 0x00279760 except for the extra strh to +0x788, and it calls the same named HP/MP ratio getters, so it aggregates battle units rather than glyphs. The only plausible caller signal is the battle skill-effect path; the equipment-function caller association in the old dossier is a symbol-range artefact (no bl to this address exists in 0x0027A118).

name: Item_GetCategoryValue
signature: int Item_GetCategoryValue(unsigned int arg1, unsigned short itemId, int category, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Returns the item record's per-category value: category 1..3 read bytes +0x33/+0x34/+0x35, anything else byte +0x32. -1 when itemId is 0xFF.
evidence: func_0063E05C(manager,itemId) is the item-record accessor (table at data-manager+0x7CC); the four bytes +0x32..+0x35 are the equipment category values that 0x0027A118 compares when placing an item into its category slot.

name: Actor_UnlinkFromParentList2
summary: Same unlink operation for the list at self+0x724; also resets the link id at self+0x738 to 0xffffffff.
evidence: Body mirrors 0x002793C4 with 0x730 -> 0x724, 0x72c -> 0x720; sets f_738 = 0xffffffff, f_8e0 = 0, f_8dc = 0. Named context in the merged C: Model_AdvanceAnimFrames.

name: maybe_Item_FindBagHolderOfTransformTarget
summary: Walks the bag counts and sub-entries and returns the id whose entry lists the requested id as a transform target (type 2), or 0xFFFF when none does.
evidence: No new context: the type-2 test and the 0xFFFF default are explicit, but the 'transform target' meaning of type 2 is an assumption and the underlying table accessor is the message-ish one flagged in FACTS.md. Stays maybe_.

name: Item_CanAddToBag
signature: int Item_CanAddToBag(ItemBag* bag, unsigned short itemId)
summary: One-argument front end for the bag acquisition rules: seeds the out-id with 0xFFFF ('no transform'), calls Item_CheckBagAcquire with resolveTransform=1 and returns whether the item may be put in the bag.
evidence: NEW: the asm at 0x00279D0C is mvn r2,#0; strh r2,[sp]; mov r3,#1; mov r2,sp; bl 0x278374; cmp r0,#0; movne r0,#1 - i.e. exactly Item_CheckBagAcquire(self, itemId, &out, 1) != 0, and Item_CheckBagAcquire is a confident name whose evidence already lists this wrapper. The readable C is truncated by the decompiler transform, so the asm is the evidence here.

name: maybe_Actor_UnlinkFromParentList3
summary: Mirror of 0x002793C4 for the second slot-list family (self+0x714 and the owner's +0x704 list): unlinks the model entry, frees it, recounts active entries and stores a random surviving index in the owner's +0x71C cursor.
evidence: Same call sites as 0x002793C4 (Model_AdvanceAnimFrames, Actor_ResetModelSlots, maybe_Model_SetSlotState) plus Battle_ActionSequence_WaitUnitState; the body is the +0x714/+0x704 mirror of the first helper, so the family is confirmed but the list role (3D vs 2D or by unit kind) is still unknown.

name: Actor_UnlinkFromParentList4
summary: Same unlink operation for the list at self+0x708; resets the link id at self+0x71c to 0xffffffff.
evidence: Mirrors 0x00279B70 with 0x724/0x720 -> 0x708/0x704; single caller Model_AdvanceAnimFrames (0x001CA5DC). Named context in the merged C: Model_AdvanceAnimFrames.

name: maybe_Item_HasAnyWithFlag60
summary: Returns 1 when the bag owns an entry (vtable +0xE8) whose record byte 0x60 is set; scans ids 0..0x120.
evidence: No new context: same 0x121-id / 0x0063E05C pattern as 0x00278604 and the recipe filter, which is not the 0xB3B item table, so the 'item' reading stays unproven even though the flag test itself is exact. Stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Row_ApplyDefaultIconSet
summary: Builds the default seven-entry icon row on the stack (constructor 0x0037EADC: seven equipment-category ids plus 0x38 zeroed state bytes) and applies it to a unit through 0x0037EA64(row, 0, unit, 0), which for each of the seven ids calls unit->vt[0x120](unit, iconId, 1). The row itself is discarded, so the lasting effect is the seven unit notifications.
evidence: NEW: the asm is only push/sub sp,#0x48/bl 0x37EADC/bl 0x37EA64(obj,0,arg,0)/pop, and 0x0037EA64 is a per-icon loop that tests 0x00639954(unit, iconId) and calls unit->vt[0x120](unit, iconId, 1). The single caller (0x003C9ADC) passes a battle unit - the same register is fed to Battle_TestUnitState 0x00639954 - so nothing here dispatches an event and the old 'Event_DispatchActorEvent' name was wrong. What vt[0x120] does is still unverified, hence maybe_.

name: Party_EquipItemIntoCategorySlot
signature: void Party_EquipItemIntoCategorySlot(EquipInventory* self, unsigned short itemId, int category, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Inserts an equipment id into the matching 7-slot category list (+0x5A8 weapon, +0x5B6 armour, +0x5C4 shield, +0x5D2 accessory), keeping each list sorted by the item's category value (record bytes 0x32..0x35) and shifting the weaker entries down.
evidence: The four u16 arrays (7 entries each, 0xE apart) and the item-record category bytes 0x32..0x35 are the same structures read by 0x0027A118's callers: Item_RemoveByLinkedId (0x00278DC4) refreshes them after a removal and maybe_Model_SelectModelIdForActor (0x00277E48) uses them to pick an actor's weapon/armour model. 0xFFFF terminates a list.

name: Svc_ResolveObjectHandle
summary: Resolves the engine handle stored at self+0x110 to its live object and verifies that the object is of the expected class (type descriptor 0x007C33D4) before returning it, else returns NULL. Used by 19 call sites across battle, field and event code.
evidence: Handle decode: g_0027A434=0x1FFFFF (index mask), g_0027A438=0x007B80C0 (table), g_0027A43C=0x007C33D4 (expected type descriptor). Walks the object's RTTI chain (**(code**)*obj)() -> f_c next until it matches, exactly like 0x0026829C/0x00267FD8 use the same table.

name: Actor_StatusBlock_Init
summary: Initialises an actor status/model block: installs vtable g_actorStatusBlockVtable, self-links the intrusive lists, clears the ids to 0xFFFF, builds the model/animation objects, resets the model slots and zeroes the ten 0x24-byte entry records.

name: Ui_WindowManager_DeletingDtor

evidence: Slot +0x04 of vtable 0x0075CE50 (preceding Ui_InitWindowManager at 0x0027A9C8); invokes destructor 0x0027A7F0 then 0x0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_CloseAllPanes
summary: Closes every sub-pane of the battle window: hides or animates out the command panes, closes the message window at +0x81, clears the shared cursor byte and animates out the 0x1D command widgets.

summary: Creates the battle UI's fixed window set: the damage-number window ('win_damage'), the main/bind window and the enemy, command, message, tactics, combo, swap and exchange windows, storing each in its manager slot.

Creates 'win_damage' via func_003E00CC; calls func_0027C5DC (main window), 0x0027CB08 Ui_SetupEnemyWindow, 0x0027CC04 Ui_SetupEquipWindow, 0x0027D108 Ui_SetupMessageWindow, 0x0027D2BC Ui_SetupSakusenWindow, 0x0027DAB0 Ui_SetupRenkeiWindow, 0x0027DF28 Ui_SetupIrekaeWindow and func_003242E0/0x003259B8/0x00391070/0x0043FDC8/0x004EE7A8/0x004EE9FC; stores the singletons at g_0027BC6C..g_0027BC94.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_ShowMessageByIndex
signature: void Ui_BattleWindow_ShowMessageByIndex(void* self, int msgIndex, int styleArg, int showSubPane, int flagArg, void* textProvider)
summary: Displays a battle message in self->f_1BC (and optional sub-pane self->f_228): hides active panes in list self+0x3D4, resolves msgIndex in message table self->f_434 or queries wide text from textProvider, and binds the formatted display record via vtable +0x5C/+0x60.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_IsAnimInactive
summary: Reports that the battle sub-window at +0x228 is hidden or idle: returns 1 when the element's visibility byte +0x14 is 0, or when its state word +0x70 is 0; otherwise 0.

name: Ui_BattleCommandWindow_SwitchActiveSubWindow

signature: void Ui_BattlePopup_Show(BattleWindow* self, u32 text, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u64 num, u32* src)

name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMembers
summary: Refreshes the party strip of the battle UI: for each of the four member slots (+0x40A, -1 = empty) it activates the member once and, for the reserved members R/T/V, fills the next free extra slot; then it refreshes the command candidates and claims free slots for members that need one.

summary: Confirm handler of the battle command window: when the window is flagged ready (self+0x405) and the input word f_130 carries the confirm bits 0x102, it refreshes the member widget (vtable+0x70), reads the highlighted command id (vtable+0x44) and, unless the id is 0x1A (back), pushes it into the downstream command script (f_138 vtable+0x14) and plays the confirm SE.

Its named callers are Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelCmd, Ui_PartyPanel_CheckMembersReady, maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirm and the two party-panel step helpers, all battle command flow. Still maybe_ because 'commit' vs 'execute' cannot be separated from the id-0x1A back special case alone.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ApplyCommandEffect
signature: void maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ApplyCommandEffect(void* commandWindow, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Battle command-window helper: resolves the acting unit from self+0x40C and, for command families 0x34/0x27, calls that unit's vtable+0x64 with another party unit chosen by 0x0063B11C(party+0x4254, 4/0/7); everything else falls through to group 7. Finishes with 0x001CD7C8(unit, 1).
evidence: The address cluster is Ui_BattleCommandWindow_* (ExecuteEscapeOrAuxCommand, ExecuteSelectedCommand), so the class is confirmed, but vtable+0x64 is not identified; 'ApplyCommandEffect' overstates what is known about the call.

name: Ui_SetupIrekaeWindow
summary: Constructs the party exchange (irekae) window: creates win_irekae1..4 and win_sougae1/2 with their captions.
evidence: 0x248 bytes; literal strings win_irekae1..4 and win_sougae1/2 at 0x0027E114..0x0027E160; calls 0x00109DC8/0x001D85EC/0x003259B8/0x003CFCC8/0x00404ECC/0x00405080; handles g_0027e120..g_0027e16c.

name: Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ExecuteSubCommand7
summary: Executes battle sub-command state 7 on sub-window self->f_234 via virtual method +0x60 and commits execution with virtual method +0x70.
evidence: Registered at dispatch slot 0x00728B94; dispatches (**(*f_234 + 0x60))(f_234, 7, 0xFFFFFFFF) and (**(*f_234 + 0x70))().

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_Noop
summary: 44-byte battle-command step helper whose body Ghidra cannot decode (Os_GetGameWork then halt_baddata). Called from three command paths (0x0027FC60, 0x00280CA4, 0x00281C18), so the entry point is real but its behaviour is unknown.
evidence: Body is still damaged (bad instruction data, no control flow after the GetGameWork call), so the placeholder name stays. All four callers are Ui_BattleCmd/Ui_PartyPanel step handlers, which only proves it belongs to the command flow.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandId
signature: void maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandId(void* self, u32 arg2, int commandId)
summary: Maps battle command ids to command groups 0..5 on the battle window manager (0x0063B11C on work+8->+0x5C +0x4254) and re-runs the command handler (vtable +0x100).
evidence: Still damaged: the entry test is decoded as (self * 0x10001) >> 8 and in_OV, and the handler is called through unaff_r4, so the receiver and the dispatch are not trustworthy. The ten 0x0063B11C calls with group ids 0..5 are the only solid anchors.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_HandleMemberSlot
summary: Handles the 'select party member' step of the battle command window: advances the current member slot with Battle_CommandWindow_Update and then sets the command script step to 9, 10 or 0 depending on the slot's step and on party availability.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Battle_CommandWindow_Update is applied to the member slot selected by self[0xF0], and the two helpers Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable / maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_SelectFirstAvailableMember decide the next step. That is the member-slot handler of the name.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirm
summary: Handler-table entry 3 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728B8C): when a command is pending it reads the selected command id from the command list (self+0x234 vt[0x44]) and branches - id 3 shows the battle popup 0x8BA, id 0x13 walks battle units 0x13..0x16 and toggles their state through vt[0x174]/vt[0x70], anything else resets the command selection.
evidence: New context: it is slot 3 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728B8C), next to the confident Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ExecuteSubCommand7 and Ui_BattleCmd_DispatchCommand9, and it dispatches on the command id returned by the command list's vt[0x44] - so 'a confirm handler that branches per command' is supported. The body is still damaged (halt_baddata, unaff_r9, in_stack_0000040c), so it stays below 0.5.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_ConfirmActionState
summary: Continuation branch of maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirm (0x0027E368): validates action target selection via 0x001EBC68 and updates work singleton battle state.
evidence: Direct continuation of 0x0027E368; invokes 0x001EBC68 and queries work singleton manager 0x006F1EEC.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_ConfirmAuxState
summary: Secondary action confirmation continuation branch of 0x0027E368: commits auxiliary command selection via 0x001EBC68.
evidence: Follows 0x0027E610 in confirmation handler; calls 0x001EBC68 and work singleton accessor 0x006F1EEC.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_SetMode11
summary: Transitions battle command window state machine to mode 0x11 via virtual method +0x4C.
evidence: Registered at dispatch slot 0x00728BC4; dispatches (**(*self + 0x4C))(self, 0x11, 1, 1, 0).

name: Ui_BattleCmd_SetMode12
summary: Transitions battle command window state machine to mode 0x12 via virtual method +0x4C.
evidence: Companion to 0x0027E728; dispatches (**(*self + 0x4C))(self, 0x12, 1, 1, 0).

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancel
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancel(BattleWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Handler-table entry 15 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728BEC): when the window is active and a command is pending it tests the enemy-list row under the cursor, rebuilds the command list and moves the sub-window to state 0x12, otherwise it falls through to the shared popup path (messages 0x8BA / 0xC79) and the state-8 request.
evidence: New context: the function is a slot in the battle command window handler table at 0x00728BEC, between the confident Ui_BattleCommandWindow_HideRenkeiSubPane and Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ExecuteEscapeOrAuxCommand, so it is a command handler. The body is still a recovered entry point with halt_baddata and unaff_r7, and it calls maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands plus Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_IsRowSelectable, which fits both a cancel and a target-confirm path - so the 'Cancel' reading stays unproven.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_HandleSlotResult
summary: Processes target/action result node returned from battle command selection: checks status byte at resultNode+5 and stores validated selection into self+0x3FC.
evidence: Calls 0x001EBC68, inspects byte at resultNode+5, and updates command result pointer at self+0x3FC.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandSelect
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandSelect(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Battle command-window select step: refreshes the member widget and window, and when the confirm bit is set checks Battle_Item_CanTargetActor, builds the command for the highlighted slot (byte at self+0x40A+slot*8) with maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands, advances the command script to 0x12 and plays the confirm SE; the cancel bit forwards the stored command id.
evidence: Battle_Item_CanTargetActor and maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands are named and the script state 0x12 is visible, but the three sibling handlers (0x0027E8CC/0x0027FC60/0x00280210) share the same input guard and only differ in the command id they push, so which stage is 'select' vs 'confirm' is still partly guesswork.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SelectOffsetItem
signature: void maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SelectOffsetItem(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 offset)
summary: Tactics (sakusen) window helper: reads the selected member from the pane at self[0x7B], takes that member's stored offset (f_E4), switches the window to state 0x0C, refreshes the list part at self[0x8D] and asks Ui_List_SelectEntryById to select entry (list first id + offset).
evidence: Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId, func_0035EB98 and Ui_List_SelectEntryById are named, and the state 0x0C push is explicit. The sakusen identity still comes from the pane-name evidence (win_sakusen2) recorded in the file header, one step removed.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_CreateSkipWindow
signature: void Ui_BattleWindow_CreateSkipWindow(BattleWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates the 'win_skip' prompt window (the 'press to skip' hint shown while battle messages play) and binds it to the battle window.
evidence: String 'win_skip' (0x0027EB34) passed to func_001D85EC(self, obj, 'win_skip', 0x81); allocation func_00109DC8(0x164,...) + ctor func_004EE7A8(); guarded by the global config byte at work+0x4244; stores the window at self+0x240.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_DispatchCommand9
summary: Dispatches command event opcode 9 to the battle command sub-window controller at self+0x138 via virtual method +0x14.
evidence: Reads controller pointer at self+0x138 and executes (**(*controller + 0x14))(controller, 9).

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands
summary: Rebuilds the battle-command entries: constructs a four-entry 8-byte command array and two 0x68-byte blocks in a 0x480-byte frame, then repopulates the command window; only the prologue survives in readable C.
evidence: Disassembly shows two live arguments (r0 -> r6, r1 -> r7) and a 0x480-byte frame, so the 'void(void)' signature in the old doc was wrong. The only callers (0x0027E8CC, 0x0027FC60) are themselves maybe_ BattleCmd handlers, so the command-rebuild role is supported but the class is not proven.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_ApplyCommandGroup
signature: void Ui_BattleCmd_ApplyCommandGroup(u32 self, int* commandWindow, int commandId)
summary: Maps a battle command id (0x27,0x34,0x39,0x3D,0x43,0x44,0x45,0x47,0x4A,0x4E) to a party group index 0..7 - 0x45 falls back to group 0x1B when group 3 is empty - and applies it through window vtable+0x64(0x0063B11C(party+0x4254, group)).
evidence: The body is a pure id-to-group switch ending in the same vtable+0x64 call in every branch, and the address neighbourhood is the battle command window family. The mechanism is fully visible; only the meaning of the group index is inferred, so 0.5 rather than higher.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_ShowPopupMessage
summary: Shows one of the fixed battle pop-up texts (ids 0x8B4..0x8B7) through Ui_BattlePopup_Show, choosing the variant from a global config byte, then releases the auxiliary message window.
evidence: Callees Ui_BattlePopup_Show, Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout are named and bracket the four text ids, which confirms the show-popup-text-then-close-window reading.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleConfirmA
summary: Handler-table entry 12 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728BD4): on a confirm event it shows the battle popup and then switches on the pending command id at self+0x3FC, advancing the window script to the matching step (0x10, 0x11, 0x13, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16) and hiding the target sub-window.
evidence: New context: it is slot 12 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728BD4), directly before the confident Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ExecuteSelectedCommand, and the body is a clean switch on self+0x3FC with one script-step advance per command id - so 'confirm handler, variant A' is supported. Which command ids 0x10..0x16 are is still unknown, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelB
signature: u32 Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelB(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Cancel branch of the battle command window: on a cancel input it optionally plays the cancel SE, calls the window's own cancel slot (+0x4C with 0,1) and resets the command script to step 0.
evidence: The call to the object's own vtable +0x4C with (0,1) and the reset of the command script via the +0x14 virtual to 0 are exactly a cancel/back action, and the input mask gate (0x106) matches the other cancel paths in this window.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_DispatchCommand2
summary: Dispatches command event opcode 2 to the battle command sub-window controller at self+0x138 via virtual method +0x14.
evidence: Reads controller pointer at self+0x138 and executes (**(*controller + 0x14))(controller, 2).

name: Ui_BattleWindow_OpenCommandList
summary: Opens the battle command-list page: advances the window script to step 0x18, sets the command pane's page to 8 and applies the selected member id and command group.
evidence: The callees are now the confident Battle_CommandListWindow_BuildEntries and Battle_CommandListWindow_SelectEntryById, and the window-script call (vtable +0x4C, step 0x18) matches the other battle-window page openers.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleTargetMove
summary: Target-selection movement step: when the input mask at self+0x4C has the movement bits and the cursor is enabled, plays the move SE, recomputes the screen positions (f_E4/f_E8) of the selected party member and its actor slot, then refreshes the command widget through vtable +0x50.
evidence: The named callees Sound_PlaySeById, Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId and Ui_Widget_CountChildren plus the member-record writes support the target-cursor step, but the +0x4C bit meanings and the owning battle-command window are still unproven, so maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_CloseExtraPane
summary: Closes the auxiliary battle pane selected by the command pane's current page: refreshes the party status rows, asks the command widget for its page (0..0x1C) and invokes that page's close slot with 0.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Ui_PartyStatusWindow_RefreshRows and the 0x1D-entry widget table at self+0x70 confirm that the function walks the same auxiliary-pane table as 0x0027B568 and closes one entry.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandPage
summary: Handler-table entry 0x42 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728D84): with a command pending it shows the battle popup and either closes the command pane (vt[0x4c](self,0,1)) or, when the sub-window reports a live selection, plays the SE and clears the actor UI flag on the battle work.
evidence: New context: it is slot 0x42 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728D84), between the confident Ui_BattleWindow_ShowPopupMessage and Ui_BattleWindow_CloseCommandList, so it is a command handler. Nothing in the body pages a list - it only shows popups and closes/clears - so the 'CommandPage' wording is not supported and the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_SubmitSubWindowState
summary: Commits the updated battle command state to the active sub-window: invokes controller virtual method +0x40 and updates window display parameters.
evidence: Precedes maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleDebugCombo (0x0027FC60); invokes virtual +0x40 on active command controller.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleSecondaryInput
summary: Second input branch of the battle command window: on the confirm bit it plays SE 0 and constructs a 4x8-byte command array with the 0xFF none marker; on the cancel bit it runs the no-op step, refreshes the widget and pushes command id 0x10.
evidence: The body is the same input-guard pattern as its two neighbours and nothing identifies the owning window or the meaning of command 0x10; the earlier 'debug combo' reading was already rejected, so the deliberately vague name stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_ShowMessage17
summary: Handler-table entry 0x43 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728D8C): releases the auxiliary message-window layout, shows battle popup message 0x8C2, moves the window script to step 0x11, then pumps the message window's command list.
evidence: New context: it is slot 0x43 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728D8C), between maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandPage and maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ResetMemberStates, and all three callees are confident (Ui_BattlePopup_Show, Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands, Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout). The '17' in the old name mixes the script step 0x11 with the message id 0x8C2, so the wording is kept but flagged as approximate.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_CloseCommandList
summary: Closes the command list of the battle party window: asks the window script to advance to step 0x12, stores the current page on the command pane, refreshes the party rows and hides the target window.
evidence: Its vtable 0x728CFC lies between Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers and maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_HideTargetWindow, and the named callees maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds, Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshRows and Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Hide make the close path explicit.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_HideTargetWindow
summary: 44-byte forwarder: takes the battle target window at battle work +0x431C and calls its close routine.
evidence: The single call is on the object at (work+8)->f_5C + 0x431C - the same target window 0x0026904C/0x00269130 fill - through the now-named Ui_BattleTargetWindow_CloseIfNotEnemyTurn, so the function is a pure 'close the target window' forwarder.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandConfirm
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandConfirm(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Confirm branch of the battle command window: on the confirm bit it sends the selected member id to the state machine, reads the highlighted command id through vtable +0x44 and, unless it is 0x1A (back), pushes it into the command script and plays the confirm SE; the cancel bit pushes command 0xB.
evidence: Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId and the 0x1A special case are concrete, but as with its siblings no caller identifies which menu stage invokes it, so the stage name remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_AdvancePaneScript
summary: Steps the battle command pane to page 0x17 through the window's +0x4C slot and, when the flag word at self+0x234 is set, refreshes the party name lines and calls the sub-pane's +0x2C slot.
evidence: The body is damaged: Battle_Ui_RefreshPartyNameLines is called with no arguments inside a comma expression and the second call is an unrecovered jump table, so the guard at self+0x234 and the 0x17 page id cannot be tied to a purpose. No caller and no named callee beyond the refresh helper.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_ApplyMemberDisplayByte
summary: Copies the selected battle-window row's display byte (+0x40A) into the matching party unit's f_12E3, when the row has a valid member slot (+0x409 != 0xFF) and the byte is not 0xFF.
evidence: The row is resolved through the battle unit list at +0x4254 (func_002AB698) and the party record through func_0035EB98, which fixes the data flow, but nothing shows the byte is a colour - it is a per-member display byte, so the name no longer claims 'Color'.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelCmd
signature: u32 Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelCmd(int* commandWindow, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Cancel handler: when self+0x405 is set, the game work has f_10, ResetSelection succeeds and (f_4C & 4) is set, it closes the window through vtable+0x4C(self,0,1) and resets the child at self[0x4E] through its vtable+0x14.
evidence: Callee maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ResetSelection plus the close pair identical to 0x00281388 make the cancel role solid; the only unproven detail is the 0x4 flag bit, which does not change the handler name.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ResetMemberStates
summary: Handler-table entry 0x45 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728D9C): when the panel is active it shows the battle popup, and if the sub-window has a live selection it walks the battle party list (battle work +0x4260) resetting every unit's display state (vt[0x5c]=7, vt[0x60]=-1, vt[0x64]=-1) before asking the state controller for state 9.
evidence: New context: it is slot 0x45 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728D9C) and the body walks the battle party list at battle work +0x4260 calling three unit vtable slots per member - it does not close any window, so the old 'CloseAllWindows' wording was wrong and is replaced by what the loop actually does. The class ('party panel' vs 'battle command window') is still not provable from the body, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmMemberSlots
summary: Confirm handler of the party-panel window: validates the current member slot selection with Ui_PartyPanel_HasRequiredMembers, plays the confirm sound, refreshes the four status panels and advances the controller state.
evidence: Named callees Ui_PartyPanel_HasRequiredMembers, Ui_PartyPanel_SelectMemberRow and Ui_BattleTargetWindow_RefreshAllTargets pin the validation-and-refresh step; it is reached only from the window's own state controller, not by a direct call.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers
summary: Performs the party-member swap chosen in the panel: maps the two stored member ids to actor slots in the +0x24A98 id table, calls the swap helper 0x4025BC and Menu_SelectPartyPair, then sets the message args and advances to state 8.
evidence: Named callees Sound_PlaySeById/Ui_BattlePopup_Show plus the 0x1F-entry walk over GameWork+0x24A98 (party/bag storage) and the two stored ids at self[0x7D]/self[0x7E] make the swap role concrete.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_UpdateTargetSubWindow
summary: Updates the target selection sub-window display state when cycling through valid battle targets.
evidence: Invokes virtual methods +0x44 and +0x50 on active target selection widget.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_StepMemberSlot
signature: int maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_StepMemberSlot(void* partyPanel, int arg2, int arg3, void* ctxOut)
summary: Party-panel member-slot handler with two paths: with flag 0x102 it commits the current value (0x004F8C34, now Battle_Ui_RefreshPartyNameLines) into the slot array at self+f_10A*8+0x409; with flag 4 it backs out one slot, decrementing f_10A, or cancels the window at index 0.
evidence: The named callee Battle_Ui_RefreshPartyNameLines confirms the party-panel domain (and that the slot array holds name lines); the handler still mixes commit and back-out, so 'StepMemberSlot' remains a description rather than a single proven role.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_SetStateFromMemberAvailability
summary: Asks Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable whether any usable member is left and pushes controller state 2 (normal advance) or 9 (abort) into the window state controller at self+0x138.
evidence: The only callee is the confident Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable, which fixes the subject (party panel) and the question asked; the old name's 'Advance' was misleading - the function never advances anything itself, it only selects state 2 or 9 - so the wording was corrected.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_CheckMembersReady
summary: Counts the battle party members whose actor object is available and idle and, if the counts allow it, continues the panel with the confirm message args and state 8; otherwise it refreshes the window.
evidence: Callees Menu_CountPartyActors, Sound_PlaySeById and Ui_BattlePopup_Show are named, and the walk over the +0x4254 actor table with vtable+0xF0 validity checks matches the 'members ready' question.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ShowSingleText
summary: Opens the message window on one fixed text: clears the list pane at +0x204, adds id 0x8B8 or 0x8B9 depending on a global flag bit, requests window state 0x11 and finishes the pane setup.
evidence: Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout are its named callees and the state-0x11 request through vtable+0x4C ties it to the message window registered as 'win_message'; it is also listed among the battle popup window entries in Ui_BattlePopup_Show (0x27C2F0), which uses the same +0x204 pane.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmAndAdvance
signature: int maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmAndAdvance(void* self, int arg2, int arg3, void* ctxOut)
summary: Confirm handler of the party panel: when the panel is visible, the game work is live and the confirm flag is set it requests state 0x13 and hides the panel; otherwise it asks the member list whether the selected member is unavailable and commits the selected command.
evidence: The callees are now the named Ui_PartyPanel_IsMemberUnavailable and maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_CommitSelectedCommand, and the state 0x13 request goes through the +0x14 vtable slot, so the confirm/advance reading holds; the flag masks (0x102, 4) are still undecoded, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_CancelIfIdle
summary: When the battle flag at work+0x5C+0x424C is clear it cancels the party panel (vtable+0x4C(self,0,1) and child reset); otherwise it does nothing.
evidence: Uses the same cancel pair as 0x00280410; the +0x424C flag has no other named reader, so 'idle' is still an interpretation of the flag rather than a proven meaning.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_ToggleAutoFlag
summary: Handler-table entry 0x24 of the battle command window (slot 0x00728C94): on a confirm event it shows the battle popup, inverts bit 0 of the global flag byte GameWork+0x2D384 when the sub-window has a live selection, then hides the panel, closes the command pane and asks the state controller for state 0xD.
evidence: New context: it is slot 0x24 of the battle command window handler table (0x00728C94) and the body really does invert bit 0 of Work+0x2D384. That bit is a general story/progress flag, not a dedicated auto-battle flag - 0x00593250 uses the same bit to pick the critical-popup icon - so 'auto flag' remains a guess and the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_CompositeWindow_LayoutRows
signature: void Ui_CompositeWindow_LayoutRows(UiCompositeWindow* self, LayoutMsg* msg, LayoutCtx* ctx, LayoutParam* params)
summary: Composite-window override of the layout pass: runs the children of its two nested lists (+0x3D4/+0x3DC and +0x3F0/+0x3F8) through their layout callbacks in order, then hands the message to the base layout methods (0x0053CDE0 and the window vtable slot +0x20).
evidence: Slot 6 of the composite-window vtable 0x0075CFC8 (whose dtor is Ui_CompositeWindow_Dtor 0x00282578 and slot 4 is Ui_InitWindowManager); same 'fill a message struct then iterate children' shape as Ui_Window_PrepareAndLayoutRows (0x0025E920). Caller: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_SetMode (0x00282660).

name: Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseChildren
summary: Releases the 0x1d child objects stored at self+0x1c0 (stride 4) and then the five named sub-objects at self+0x138/0x1bc/0x238/0x23c/0x240, and drops the refcounted handle at self+0x438.
evidence: for (i = 0; i < 0x1d; i++) release (self + i*4)->f_1c0 via vtable[2] then vtable[1] (release + free); then the five fixed slots; then 0x001241D0 on the refcounted word at self+0x438. Caller 0x00282578 (its own destructor).

name: Ui_Window_IsActive
summary: Predicate used by the window-frame code: true only when the window's own active byte (+0x405) is set and the UI context singleton still has a live root manager (+0x10).
evidence: Thirteen callers, all window-frame logic (0x38C604, 0x38D46C, 0x38D6E0, 0x38D7B4, 0x38DA58, 0x38DE50, 0x38E304, 0x38E5BC, 0x38EF40, 0x38F1A8, 0x38F6C4, 0x38FD80, 0x38FF08) use the result directly as a boolean before calling window methods; body is exactly 'return window->f_405 && ctx->f_10'.

name: Ui_BattleCmd_ResetPendingInput
summary: Clears and resets pending battle command input context at self+0x1BC if an input operation is currently in flight.
evidence: Reads input context pointer at self+0x1BC, tests for non-zero, and cancels active command input.

name: Ui_Window_DeactivateAndClearMembers
summary: Deactivates the window: unlinks both intrusive child lists (f_3D4/f_3F0) calling vtable+0x18(child,0) on each entry, clears f_234, sets f_404=1, handles the optional child at f_23C when world+0x4249 is set, and resets the selection indices f_42C/f_430 to -1.
evidence: Two intrusive-list unhooks, the child deactivate calls and the two -1 selections match the name exactly; no other interpretation fits the body.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable
summary: Returns 0 if the unit at f_42C has f_B128 < 2 or the one at f_430 has f_B148 < 2; otherwise scans the four party units and returns 0 as soon as one both passes maybe_Battle_CheckActorCanAct(world, unit, unit->f_768) and is not skipped by maybe_Actor_ShouldSkipUpdate; only when all four fail does it return 1.

evidence: The 1/30 second step (0x3D088889), the duration comparison, the Sound_PlaySeById with the cue's own id and the two-word descriptor reload are all explicit, and the neighbouring cue helpers (Ui_Cue_Start in maybe_PartyPanel_UpdateHighlight) use the same object.

evidence: NEW: Sound_GetPlayer is the lazy sound-player singleton (353 callers, PlaySE/PrepareBGM/SetVolumeSE), so the bit test is a sound-system state/idle flag rather than a UI flag; the object's identity as a cue still rests on the neighbouring maybe_ names.

The three packed parameters are passed in s1..s3 and are still unnamed.

name: maybe_Actor2D_PlayAnimOnParts

name: maybe_Actor2D_BuildPartSpriteList
signature: void maybe_Actor2D_BuildPartSpriteList(void* self, u32 count, const void* partArray)

name: Actor2D_ShadowNode_Ctor
signature: void Actor2D_ShadowNode_Ctor(Actor2DShadowNode* self, void* arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: maybe_Gfx_RegisterScreenSprite
summary: Once (flag f_29C) and while the player is not blocked, registers this sprite with the GPU context's screen-sprite block (+0xF6C..+0xF82): sprite pointer, draw callback 0x0066FA8C, the sprite's f_11 and the player's screen position shifted left by 3.

name: Actor2D_InitSpanFromRecord

summary: Lightweight initialiser of a 2D field actor that only builds its single sprite span: stores the record at f_298, copies the two ids (f_12/f_14) into f_b0/f_b4, resolves the character record (f_ac = resource->f_2e), applies the ground position from the shorts at +8/+10 and creates the span at f_24C with the record's width/height (f_c/f_e).
evidence: Called from maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType/ByTypeB next to 0x0021BA10 (Actor2D_InitFromPlacement) and 0x0028EFEC; func_00319848 + resource->f_2e for f_ac, func_005F3500(self, short@+8, short@+10) for the ground position, and a fully initialised func_00335A6C span-parameter block whose w/h/x/y come from f_c/f_e and the +8/+10 shorts, created at &self->f_24c - the same span slot and helper as 0x0021BA10.

name: Gfx_ScreenSprite_CheckRectChanged
summary: Returns 1 when the on-screen sprite's cached rectangle is stale: it compares the renderer's f_F74 with the sprite's stored id and the projected glyph cell, and clears the submitted byte f_29C before reporting the change; returns 0 while the cached rect is still valid.

name: maybe_Effect_CreateEightEmitters
signature: void maybe_Effect_CreateEightEmitters(int owner, int arg2, int arg3)

name: Actor2D_CreateSingleSpritePane
signature: void Actor2D_CreateSingleSpritePane(Actor2D* self, const SpriteRecord* rec)
summary: Creates the single fixed-size sprite pane of a 2D actor: calls the base setup func_005F2B54, builds a 200x120 sprite-mesh parameter block with sprite id 0x21 and the record's byte at +0x48, creates the mesh named 'sprite', stores it in f_b8, sets its byte +0x129 to 10 and attaches it to the actor.
evidence: Readable C is a broken fragment; the raw ARM listing shows func_005F2B54(self, rec), the literal size pair {0xc8,0x78} (200x120, identical to the other Actor2D sprite makers), func_0031A48C(&p, 0, 0x21, *(u8*)(arg2+0x48), &size), the global 0x00782234 (the zeroed 'sprite descriptor' also used by 0x0028EFEC) plus self->f_48 as its second word, func_0031A394(..., &p, "sprite" at 0x00290570), self->f_b8 = mesh, mesh->f_129 = 10, func_005E7650(self, mesh). No callers, so it is a factory/type-table entry like its neighbours.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the 2D actor sprite node's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running (0 only at the terminal phase 5).
evidence: NEW: same 28-byte body as 0x001A3C88/0x0021B510/0x003A1CD0, now explained by the disassembly of func_0064C740 (`*(u8*)self == 5`). The class is Actor2D_SpriteNode, not a generic 'Gfx sprite': the sibling getter 0x00290578 is vtable slot 0x0075D908, inside the vtable 0x0075D888 installed by Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor (0x002907D8). The old name 'IsSpriteHidden' had the wrong polarity and no class evidence.

name: Actor2D_CreateEightSpansAlt
signature: void Actor2D_CreateEightSpansAlt(Actor2D* self, const SpanRecord8* rec)
summary: Second copy of Actor2D_CreateEightSpans (0x0021B52C): copies the two ids and the angle from the record, resolves the character, applies the ground position and the rotation, creates the colour animator, then creates the eight 0x48-byte child spans at self+0x298 (each with its own colour block) and finally resets the f_204 span array.
evidence: Instruction-for-instruction identical to 0x0021B52C apart from its private literal pool: f_b4=rec[1], f_b0=rec[2], f_ac=rec[3], func_00319848 + mesh->f_128=func_0029E41C(), func_005F34F0(&rec->f_10), func_005F36E0(rec->f_18,1), func_0031A73C(g_00290754), func_0028E2A0 (Gfx_CreateFColAnimator), func_0047B450/0047B314/0047AF94 per index, 8x func_00335A6C(self,&p,self+0x298+i*0x48,0), func_0047AF5C(&self->f_204,1); the child-name format string is '$%x' (0x0029075c) in both, and the count constant 0x0FFE (0x00290758) in both. Referenced only from the construction vtable at 0x0075D918 with base-adjust -0x22C.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds the 2D actor sprite node's touch record (kind 3) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x4D8..+0x4E0; returns 1.
evidence: NEW: vtable slot 0x0075D904 lies inside the vtable 0x0075D888 installed by Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor (0x002907D8), and the next slot 0x0075D908 = 0x00290578 is the record getter. So the owner is Actor2D_SpriteNode, not the separate Ui_Sprite class the old name claimed; the operation itself is confirmed by the same refresh/get slot pair seen in five sibling classes.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a 2D actor sprite node: installs vtable 0x0075D888, links itself into the 2D actor list and default-constructs the 8 sprite/anim entries (0x48 bytes each) at +0x298.

name: Ui_IconTextWindow_AdjustQuantityByDigit
signature: void Ui_IconTextWindow_AdjustQuantityByDigit(UiIconTextWindow* self, int digitDir, int valueDir)

evidence: Overrides base vtable slot 0x007682A0 (func_003A7E4C, the generic per-frame update); f_a1e++ while < 8; alpha = (u8)(frames*0xff >> 3) written to self->f_a8->f_45 (the byte directly after the +0x44 flag byte modified by 0x002914B0); f_a1c = fade direction; f_94 = 0 ends the element; shared by the parallel vtable at 0x007713E8, i.e. a second class reuses this exact update.

name: Ui_DiveForm_DerivedCtor

name: Container_KeyedListEntry_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a keyed-list entry: stores the supplied vtable at +0x174, runs the base-class destructor 0x003BE544 (which re-installs its own table) and frees the object.

name: Container_KeyedList_SelectAndCommit
signature: unsigned int Container_KeyedList_SelectAndCommit(Container* self, int arg2, int b, int entry)
summary: Marks the container's selection as dirty and commits the currently selected entry of its keyed list; returns 1 when an entry changed.
evidence: 0x5E7598 (per-frame anim tick), self->f_15C=1, then 0x2A891C(self->f_60,0,0,entry) (select) and 0x2A871C(self->f_60) (commit). No external caller: reached through a method table.

name: Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry
summary: Selects and immediately commits the default keyed-list entry; the callers are the field NPC / monster action code paths that need 'pick the entry for the current action'.
evidence: 0x2A891C() then 0x2A871C(self). Called from maybe_Field_NpcUpdateFacing, Field_NpcPlayGesture, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel and six more actor update paths (0x2FB644/0x385EA8/0x3E60F0/0x4E43B8/0x5E7480/0x5F7E88).

name: Container_KeyedList_CommitSelection
summary: Commits a pending list selection: ends the previous entry (vtable slot 0xC on the old entry), begins the new one (vtable slot 8), records it as current and clears the pending index.
evidence: requires f_35!=0 and pending index f_39 < count f_40; optional ordering test uses entry->f_18; then (**(code**)(*old+0xC))(old,pending,new) and (**(code**)(*new+8))(); f_38=pending, f_39=0xFF, f_44=0, f_48=0. Also gates one branch on 0x63AF80 (a list-window predicate).

name: Container_KeyedList_ReleaseEntry
summary: Releases one entry of the keyed list (vtable slot 4) and clears the slot; returns 0 when the index is out of range.
evidence: bounds test arg2 < self->f_40; pointer table at self->f_3C; calls (**(code**)(*entry+4))() and stores 0. Callers are the field NPC/monster action teardown paths (Field_NpcApplyAction, Monster_UpdateBehavior and eight monster behaviour variants).

name: Container_KeyedList_Select

summary: Selects element `index` of a container only if it exists and its sort key (f_18) is not before the currently selected element's key; optionally runs the element's own +0x20/+0x28/+0x24 vtable checks and a `func_0063AF80` notification, then stores the new key pair. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the move is illegal.
evidence: Bounds checks `arg2 < self->f_40` and `self->f_38 < self->f_40`, element pointers at `self->f_3c + arg2*4`, ordering compare on `iVar2->f_18` vs `uVar3->f_18`, vtable slots +0x20/+0x24/+0x28, `func_0063AF80(self,arg2)` then `self->f_39 = local_18` (CONCAT11 of the two keys). Called by 0x002A8698, 0x002A86C0, 0x00377398, 0x005E7828.

name: Ui_RowList_ReleaseAllRows
summary: Releases every row of a list window: calls each row's virtual slot +4, zeroes the slot, frees the pointer array and resets the bookkeeping (count 0, indices 0xFF, value 0).
evidence: NEW: nothing contradicts the first pass; the loop bound is the byte at +0x40, the per-row call is vtable slot +4 and the array free is the same helper the neighbouring UI destructors use, so the 'release all rows' reading is what the body literally does.

name: Container_SlotReplace
signature: u32 Container_SlotReplace(Container* self, u32 index, void* object)
summary: Replaces the object stored in slot `index`: destroys the previous occupant through its vtable slot +4, then stores the new pointer. Used by the field/monster action tables to register a compiled action object in a numbered slot.

signature: void* Battle_ActionAnimEntry_Create(u32 owner, ActionAnimDesc* src, ActionAnimDesc* src2)

summary: Deleting destructor of a row-list window: runs the base destructor 0x002650C4 and tail-calls operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
