The B suffix is needed because Ui_RowList_DeletingDtor already exists at 0x002298E4.

name: Anim_ActionSeq_AdvanceEvents
signature: void Anim_ActionSeq_AdvanceEvents(AnimActionSeq* self, int arg2, int deltaTime)
summary: Advances an action/animation sequence by `deltaTime` and fires every event whose timestamp falls in the newly covered interval. Five parallel event arrays are walked with different record strides (0x14/0x08/0x18/0x3c/0x08), which is why the five cursor fields exist.
evidence: Header `self->f_c` holds counts at +8/+0x10/+0x18/+0x20/+0x28 and relative pointers at +0xc/+0x14/+0x1c/+0x24/+0x2c; events compared against `self->f_10` and `self->f_10+arg3`; per-kind handlers func_0014BB5C, func_0014BBE8, func_0014BCA8, func_0014C150 and func_00220B20(self->f_8, name, arg, 0). Cursors are stored back as shorts at f_14/f_16/f_18/f_1a/f_1c and the end time at f_20/f_24.

name: Anim_ActionSeq_AdvanceTime
signature: void Anim_ActionSeq_AdvanceTime(AnimActionSeq* self, int delta, int runEvents)
summary: Advances the animation action sequence clock: with runEvents=0 it only walks the five per-type event cursors (+0x14/+0x16/+0x18/+0x1A/+0x1C) forward while their timestamps are below the new time; with runEvents!=0 it fires both event streams through 0x2A8CCC and accumulates the time.
evidence: self->f_10 += arg2; five independent cursor arrays in the clip (f_c): counts at clip+8/+0x10/+0x18/+0x20/+0x28 with strides 0x14/8/0x18/0x3C/8 and timestamp at +8; then 0x2A8CCC(self,0/1,arg2) Anim_ActionSeq_AdvanceEvents. Callers 0x2241C4 Actor_StepAnimation and 0x2258A8.

name: Anim_ActionSeq_Reset
signature: void Anim_ActionSeq_Reset(AnimActionSeq* self, void* sequenceData, int playNow)
summary: Prepares the sequence player for a new sequence: stores the header, zeroes the time and all five event cursors, and marks both end times as 'not reached' (0xffffffff); when `playNow` is set it immediately dispatches the events at time 0.
evidence: `self->f_c = arg2; self->f_10 = 0; self->f_14..f_1c = 0; self->f_20 = self->f_24 = 0xffffffff;` then `if (arg3) { func_002A8CCC(self,0); self->f_28 = 1; }`. Callers 0x00223030 and itself. The 0xffffffff sentinels are the same ones 0x002A8CCC compares against.

name: Anim_ActionSeq_StepFrame
summary: Steps the action sequence by exactly one frame, clamps at the clip length (clip+0x34) and resets all five event cursors when the clip wraps.
evidence: if f_c==0 return; on first use fire 0x2A8CCC(self,0) and set f_28=1; if f_10+1 != clip->f_34 advance f_10 to min(cur+1, clip->f_34) else reset f_10/f_14/f_16/f_18/f_1A/f_1C to 0 and f_20/f_24 to -1; then 0x2A8CCC(self,0). Sole caller 0x22405C.

name: Gfx_ObjectTable_LookupByTypeMask
summary: Looks a handle up in the global object table, and when the found object's type mask at +0x30 covers the reference's mask it notifies the reference (vtable+0x14), forwards it to the object's vtable+0x48 and records the handle; returns 1 when a match was handled.
evidence: NEW: the table base is the same 0x007B80C0 20/12-bit handle table used by every other handle lookup in the project, the vtable slot 0x0075E7A8 sits next to maybe_Gfx_HandleTable_Release, and the callers 0x0031B048/0x0031C2E8 are the named Gfx_Actor_Bind* paths - so the type-mask-matched lookup reading holds.

name: Gfx_HandleTable_Release
summary: Releases the packed handle stored at self+0x14: verifies the 11-bit generation tag in the table at 0x007B80C0, sends messages 0x10 and 0x4C to the object and then writes the invalid-handle sentinel back.
evidence: The generation-table layout matches the one used by the now-understood handle refresh 0x00282660, both callers are named Gfx actor code (Gfx_Actor_ApplyAppearance, maybe_Gfx_Actor_FinishMotion), and the body is complete - only the meaning of message 0x10/0x4C is unknown. The single damaged spot (unaff_r7 in the sentinel write) is a decompiler artefact: the disassembly at 0x002A96C8-0x002A96D0 is 'and r0, r7, r1; orr r0, r0, r1; str r0, [r4,#0x14]' with r1 = 0x001FFFFF, i.e. the tag bits forced to all ones - so the only uncertainty there is which register held the old value, not the 'invalidate the handle' meaning.

name: Ui_List_MoveSelectionSkipDisabled
summary: Moves the message/talk list selection one row up or down, skipping rows whose vtable+0x18 predicate reports 'not selectable', and wraps at the ends.
evidence: direction comes from *(char*)(g_002A9920+self); index at self[0xCA0]; count from 0x630D64(); row fetched through vtable+0x10C and tested with vtable+0x18; increments the change counter self[0xCA1]. Called only from 0x2A9F4C (the talk window state machine).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyTalkEntry
summary: Applies the currently selected talk entry: asks 0x2A9E18 for the talk/text id, stores it in the window (+0x3292), builds the entry object through vtable+0xCC and hands the result to vtable+0xF8 so the message text is laid out.
evidence: gate *(char*)(self+0x3244) (already applied); 0x2A9E18 maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_GetTalkId; result stored at self+0x3292 as s16; **(code**)(*self+0xCC)(self,textId,row) into self[0xC9B]; then vtable+0x48(self,0) -> vtable+0xF8. Both callers (0x2A9F4C) are the talk state machine.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_BuildLines
summary: Appends the next visible talk line(s) for the current speaker: resolves the speaker object (window vtable +0x48), looks up its text record, fills the 0x60-byte line record at +0x5d0 (clearing its 18 sub-fields and the 0x38-byte tail), then binds the line's text to the renderer and advances the line index up to 0x47 (71) lines.
evidence: Loop bounded by `local_30 = 3` when the speaker model has flag 0xa0 else 1; `arg1[0xc90]` indexes `arg1[0xc90]*0x18 + 0x5d0` and `*0x60 + 0x1746`; clears bytes up to +0x179d; calls func_00486208 / func_00490994 / func_00497520 (line builders) and func_001FC4FC(self,line,model,record,1); caps the index at 0x47. Line record size and the 0xc90 counter match 0x002ABE74's 10-rows-per-page layout.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_CanShowMessage
summary: Returns 0 when the current speaker is in state 4 or 8 (i.e. hidden/removed) so the message must not be drawn; otherwise refreshes the name/face lookup and returns 1.
evidence: `(**(*arg1+0x48))(arg1,0)` gives the speaker object; `iVar2->f_10 != 0` gates the body; text id read from `iVar2->f_768`; `local_1c->f_29 == 0x08 || == 0x04` returns 0. Same accessors (func_0035EB98 + func_006292F0) as 0x002A99C8.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_GetTalkId
summary: Resolves the message id the talk window should display for its current entry: takes the speaker's party-member index from the sub-object's +0x768, reads the item equipped in hand 0 or 1 (self+0xCA4 selects the hand) and returns that item record's +0xC0, else the talk record's +0xA8, else the 0x212 default; in the second-hand path the two sentinels 0x237/0x239 are remapped to 0x23B.
evidence: NEW: the caller Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyTalkEntry stores the result at self+0x3292 as s16 and passes it to vtable+0xCC(self, id, row) to build the message entry, so the return value is definitely a message id. The two lookups are generic table accessors, not item rows: 0x0063DF9C indexes dm->f_80C with stride 0xE8 and 0x0063FDAC indexes dm->f_794 with stride 0xE0, while the real item lookup 0x0063CDD8 uses dm->f_4 with the 0xB3B bound. What the equipped-hand item contributes to the message id is still unexplained, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState
summary: The talk/message window state machine: on every frame it advances the current state id at +0x3260 (values 0x9C0/0x9C8/0x9EB/0x9F1/...), collects/draws the visible dialogue lines, applies the current text id, handles the pager, plays the per-character voice and finally flushes the window through vtable+0x108.
evidence: state at self[0xC98]; line array at self+0x400 (0x18-byte records, count self[0xC90], current line self+0x3276); text id at +0x3292; calls Ui_MessageWindow_BuildLines 0x2A99C8, CanShowMessage 0x2A9D40, GetTalkId 0x2A9E18, the selection mover 0x2A9790 and the entry applier 0x2A9924, plus 0x398B28/0x3989FC/0x3FC9F0 (text run builder), 0x1FE494/0x1FB4A4/0x1FE804 (field party list), 0x1EBC68 Sound_PlaySeById and Item_LookupRecord 0x61BD4C for the item-name arguments. Reached through vtable 0x75E7CC slot 2, whose other slots are FieldParty_* functions.

name: FieldParty_ResetAllMembers
summary: Empties a field party: calls virtual slot +0x34 with 0, writes the 0xFFFFFFFF 'no party' marker at +0x3260 and clears the ten member-slot bookkeeping fields at +0x3278..+0x3296.

Vtable 0x0075E7B8 has slot +0x1C = Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState (0x2A9F4C, which drives state +0x3260 and flag +0x3246 initialized right here at +0x3260/+0x3244!). name: Model_SetupPartsFromTable

name: Container_List_CollectVisibleIndices
signature: int Container_List_CollectVisibleIndices(Container* self, int offset, int* out, int capacity)

Vtable slot 0x0075E90C in the message-window vtable (0x0031E838 Ui_MessageWindow_AppendLinesFromList at 0x0075E8F0); called from 0x00210690 maybe_FieldScene_Dtor.

name: Ui_TextListWindow_SetVisible

name: Container_NamedMap_Lookup
signature: void* Container_NamedMap_Lookup(Container* self, const char* name)
summary: Looks an object up by name in the name-keyed map rooted at self+0x18. It builds a 32-byte key (name copy + FNV-1a hash), queries the map and returns the stored object pointer or 0.
evidence: FNV-1a constants 0x811C9DC5 (offset basis) and 0x01000193 (prime) at 0x2ACA90/0x2ACA94; the key is a {ptr,len,hash} struct copied with 0x11142C (strncpy) and hashed byte-wise (hash = hash*prime ^ c); lookup through 0x6F2EE4 which returns the map node at &self->f_18; returns *node or 0. The 0x782534 string is the empty-name fallback.

name: Container_NamedMap_Insert
signature: unsigned int Container_NamedMap_Insert(int* self, NamedRecord* rec)
summary: Inserts (or re-keys) a record in the name-keyed map at self+0x18: builds the same FNV-1a name key, removes any existing node with the same sort key, then links the node into the sorted tree ordered by the record's +0x54 key.
evidence: 0x2ACD34 (key helper), key build identical to 0x2AC978, 0x6F2EE4 lookup at &self->f_18, removes nodes while node->f_14 == rec->f_54 by calling 0x115358/0x115390 (tree next) and 0x10EC00/0x10EC14 (tree rebalance); copies the 0x20-byte key into the record at +0x1C and inserts with 0x10EE9C. Callers 0x46B408/0x46B40C/0x591204/0x59121C.

name: Container_NamedMap_EraseEntryForKey
summary: Erases the name-keyed-map entry for one key before it is replaced: looks the node up with the same 9-word hash/name key as the insert path and, if a node exists, destroys the stored key string at +0x30 and unlinks the node from the red-black tree; returns 1 when something was erased.
evidence: Its only caller Container_NamedMap_Insert (0x002ACAA4, confidence 0.50) calls it first and then re-implements the identical FindNodeA + std_RbTree_EraseNode sequence inline, which shows the function is the 'drop the existing entry with this key' half of the insert, not a string update; the key layout (f_54..f_78, hash 0x782534) and the tree at self+0x18 match the insert exactly.

name: Container_NamedMap_Clear
summary: Destroys every object stored in both name-keyed maps of a container (the +0x24 list and the +0x34 list), calling vtable slot 4 on each.
evidence: two list walks rooted at self->f_24/self->f_1C and self->f_34/self->f_30; each node's object is released with (**(code**)(*obj+4))(); tree-next helpers 0x115358/0x115390. Sole caller 0x1D8C80 maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_BindCharacter (window rebind clears the caches first).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepCode3E

evidence: NEW: the dispatcher callee is confidently Ui_MessageWindow_ExecControlCode (0x0030F258) and is called with the literal record byte 0x3E, and the state split 2/4 vs 3/5 plus the timing-table copies are shared with the equally named 0x002B00D4 handler. The constant and the shape are certain, only the meaning of code 0x3E is unknown - which the name deliberately does not claim.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepCode3F42
summary: One message-window task step that executes control code 0x3F in window states 2/4, or code 0x42 in states 3/5 (the two text-speed/auto variants), and then schedules the next step from the corresponding pair of the 0x0072B858 timing table.
evidence: NEW: confidently named callee Ui_MessageWindow_ExecControlCode receives the literal 0x3F/0x42 records, and the pair of state branches matches the 0x002B0044 sibling exactly (same table, same self+0x10/self+0x14 next-step fields). The 'text-speed/auto variant' gloss is NOT proven, so the summary keeps it as the two state variants; name is a structural label, which is exactly what is certain.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepNextQueuedByte
summary: Message-window task step: if the window's 0x1948..0x194C byte queue is empty it finishes the task with step state 1 and the default timing record from 0x0072B888; otherwise it pops the next byte, memmoves the remaining queue down and executes that byte as a control code.
evidence: NEW: Ui_MessageWindow_ExecControlCode is now a confident name and is called with exactly the popped byte plus a zero third argument, and the task-state writes (*(self+8) = 1) plus the timing-table copy at 0x0072B888 match the other named message-window step functions (0x002B0044/0x002B00D4 use the same table). The behaviour is fully described by the old name; only the purpose of control codes in general is unknown.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepCallAndCheckCloseB

evidence: The readable C is truncated by halt_baddata, but the disassembly 0x002B0230..0x002B02C4 is complete and is the same body as 0x002B043C with the callback taken from +0x10/+0x14 instead of +0x0C/+0x10. The vtable slot 0x0075E9E8 sits next to the named Ui_MessageWindow_StepCode3D (0x002B02C8), so the class is certain. The old 'CheckMode' wording was wrong - it checks the same close condition as 0x002B043C.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepCode3D

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepQueuedByteEx

name: Ui_MessageWindow_StepCallAndCheckClose

evidence: The vtable slot 0x0075EA00 is in the message-window step table next to the named Ui_MessageWindow_StepCode3D (0x002B02C8) and maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_StepBranchOnFlag8 (0x002B04D4), and the body is complete. The same close condition is duplicated at 0x002B0230, which confirms the reading.

summary: Constructor of the 'disappear' field-NPC action object (0x2C bytes): runs the shared descriptor ctor and installs vtable 0x0075ED78.
evidence: The only call site (Field_SetupNpcActionScript) allocates 0x2C bytes and passes 'disappear' (s_disappear at 0x00177D2C); the vtable 0x0075ED78 sits directly below the moveSt (0x75EDE0) and movePa (0x75EDAC) vtables, confirming the sibling class ladder.

name: maybe_Field_Npc_DtorDeleteA
summary: Deleting destructor: runs the base destructor 0x00193E40 and tail-calls operator delete 0x0010F6CC. The class is a field NPC only by neighbourhood - the vtable slot 0x0075ED7C's next entry is the still-uncertain maybe_Field_NpcPlayNutAndFaceTarget (0x002B299C).
evidence: The vtable slot 0x0075ED7C has no confident class sibling (0x002B299C is still maybe_), so the NPC label is inherited; the body is the generic bl 0x00193E40 + b 0x0010F6CC.

name: Field_NpcActionRun
summary: Starts the 'run' field-NPC action: clears the action state, asks 0x17A360 for the wander target, stores it, requests the run animation (0x5E7848 with mode 2) and plays either 'Run' or the default idle motion.
evidence: self->f_2C=0, f_30=0.0; 0x17A360 maybe_Field_NpcGetActionAnimId(actor,&flag) returns the target point (f_34/f_38/f_3C); 0x5E7848(actor,2,0) sets the run animation; 0x5E82C4(&out,actor) computes speed (f_40); the motion name is either the literal 'Run' at 0x2B2D84 or the default at 0x2B2D88. Same pattern as the sibling actions 0x2B2ED0/0x2B2F40.

name: Field_NpcActionRunUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the field-NPC run action: retargets when the NPC drifted more than 110 units from its target, moves the NPC along the interpolated path (0x5E8BEC) scaled by the stored speed and re-checks the distance to the player.
evidence: distance test (f_34/f_3C vs actor f_9C/f_A4) against the literal -110.08 at 0x2B2EC0; 0x17A360/0x5E7848 retarget and re-request the run animation; 0x5E8BEC(&dir,actor,&target) gives the step vector, multiplied by f_40 and added to actor f_100/f_104/f_108; 0x177784 Field_NpcCheckPlayerDistance then a jump-table tail (Ghidra lost the switch target).

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveParam
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveParam(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'movePa' field-NPC action object (0x44 bytes, vtable 0x0075EDAC): clears +0xB and +0xC, copies the three-float vector from 0x007E7000 to +0xD..+0xF and stores 2.0 at +0x10.
evidence: Its only caller (Field_NpcApplyAction, 0x0017A8AC) allocates 0x44 bytes and passes 'movePa' (s_movePa at 0x0017ABF0) - a move-parameter action, sibling of the 'moveSt' ctor at 0x002B2F40.

name: Field_NpcAction_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of the field NPC action-state object: runs the base destructor 0x00193E40 and tail-calls operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The vtable slot 0x0075EDB0 shares its table with the confident Field_NpcActionRun (0x002B2CBC) and Field_NpcActionRunUpdate (0x002B2D90), so the class is the NPC action-state object. The B suffix is needed because Field_NpcAction_DeletingDtor already exists at 0x00332D90.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'moveSt' field-NPC action object (0x34 bytes, vtable 0x0075EDE0): runs the shared descriptor ctor, clears the action byte +0xB and the word at +0xC, and installs the vtable.
evidence: Its three call sites all pass the script name 'moveSt' (s_moveSt at 0x0017A6D8 / 0x0017ABE4 / 0x0017813C) together with a freshly allocated 0x34-byte block, so this is a class constructor, not a 'set idle params' mutator; the old name described the caller's intent, not the callee.

name: Field_Npc_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of a field NPC variant: runs the base destructor 0x00193E40 and tail-calls operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The vtable slot 0x0075EDE4 shares its table with the confident Field_NpcCheckPlayerDistance (0x00177784), so the class is a field NPC. The B suffix is needed because Field_Npc_DeletingDtor already exists at 0x004143E8.

name: Ui_FadeWindow_RelocateAndNotifyChildren
signature: u32 Ui_FadeWindow_RelocateAndNotifyChildren(void* params, FadeParams* ctx, PtrCtx* ctx2, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Walks the child list at +0x18 and, for every live child, rebases the pointer in ctx+4 through 0x00507CBC and 0x00507DCC and forwards (ctx, arg4, arg5) to the child's virtual +0x14; returns 1 when at least one child was visited.
evidence: The vtable slot 0x0075EE20 shares its table with the confident Ui_FadeWindow_Dtor (0x0075EE34) and Ui_WidgetGroup_DispatchUpdate (0x0075EE24), so the class is the fade window, not a generic container list; the body is fully readable.

name: Ui_FadeWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the screen-fade window: releases its nested widget at +0x138, restores the two vtables and frees the object.
evidence: the address is slot 0 of vtable 0x75EE34, whose layout slot 4 is Ui_FadeWindow_Setup 0x17BB1C and slot 6 is Ui_Window_LayoutRows; body: func_00291220(self+0x4E*4) Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, then 0x1A6768(self+0x4E*4) on the child, re-installs g_002B30B4, unlinks three list nodes and calls 0x1D8C2C(iVar1-0x138) + 0x10F6CC.

name: Ui_FadeWindow_DtorB
summary: Second fade-window destructor (vtable 0x75EE84, the variant that uses 0x63B698/0x63B6BC as its layout hooks); same teardown as 0x2B3050.
evidence: slot 0 of vtable 0x75EE84, an otherwise identical table to 0x75EE34 except for the two trailing hooks 0x63B698/0x63B6BC (vs 0x63B664/0x63B688) and the vtable word g_002B3120/g_002B3124. Body is the same sequence as 0x2B3050, differing only in the four literal-pool words.

name: maybe_Anim2D_RebindRecordTable
summary: Rebinds a 2D animation player's shared record table: takes a free slot of the 0x7E7250 table (reference swap at self+0x9FC, cached at self+0x9F8) and re-applies the record data through the record-table helpers.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named Pack_ReleaseHandle / Pack_FreeHandleEntry / Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign / Fs_ResourceFindByName, which shows a resource-handle table being rebound rather than an 'anim channel set'; the player still has no caller. 'RecordTable' is the safest description of data the body moves; maybe_ stays because the record format is unknown.

name: Anim2D_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the 2D animation player: releases the reference-counted channel block at +0x9FC (the field the binder 0x002B3128 installs) and then tears down the class at 0x003A8200, which frees its 0x19 x 0x50 animation slots.
evidence: The +0x9FC reference release matches exactly what 0x002B3128 stores there, and the 0x003A8200 teardown is the 0x19*0x50 slot owner - so the class is the same one. The current symbol for 0x003A8200 (maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Dtor) is probably a misnomer from an earlier batch.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion(void* self, int useNut, int seekLastFrame)
summary: Selects the actor's 'Nut' motion when useNut is non-zero (state word +0x288 = -1), otherwise the default 'Open' motion (+0x288 = 0), plays it through the animation owner at +0xB8 and, when seekLastFrame is set, jumps to the clip's last frame.
evidence: NEW: the inline literal at 0x002B342C is 'Nut' and the default name pointer is *0x007283F8, which resolves to the animation-name table entry 'Open' (0x007844C8: dead/Open/Fall_Loop/Sit_Loop/Move...); Ghidra printed 0x0074754E and 0x007283F8 as raw literals. The seek path uses the now-named Anim_Owner_Tick (0x002D19C8). Only the 'Npc' receiver label is inferred, and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CreateSpriteChild
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CreateSpriteChild(int self, void* params, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Creates a mesh/sprite child for a field scene object: resolves the model resource, allocates the 0x178 mesh, applies the transform, registers one child slot and sets the sprite priority.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB and the callee set is sprite-specific (Anim_Instance_CtorSprite/ApplyTemplate, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, Gfx_LookupSpritePriorityByte, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize), so this is scene-object sprite creation, not a generic 'effect emitter'. The product/resource split is still inferred, so maybe_.

name: Field_SceneObject_InvokeModeCallback
summary: Invokes the object's stored callback (self+0x29C) with the two mode words at +0x2A0/+0x2A4 and the object itself, but only when the matching slot of the global mode table 0x007283F8 (+0x0C when +0x2A0 is 0, +0x04 otherwise) is populated.
evidence: NEW: the class is established by the confident Field_SceneObject family (Field_SceneObject_ShowAndSelectEntry 0.50, Field_SceneObject_Delete 0.55, Field_SceneObject_ClearPartFlag 0.55) and the only caller is Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB; the body is complete and the indirect call through self+0x29C with three arguments is unambiguous. The 'Mode' wording is kept because the gate is the global table 0x007283F8, which the named maybe_Field_Npc_SetMotionNut also uses as its default-motion table.

name: Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtorC
summary: Deleting destructor of a field scene object: installs the caller's vtable, unlinks the object's sub-list node, destroys the embedded scene object 0x24C bytes back and frees the block. Same 56-byte template as the 2D sprite destructors.
evidence: NEW: the sibling destructors in this batch are now readable and identical (0x002B423C, 0x001A3BA8/0x001A5AAC, 0x00219938), and all of them end in Field_Object_DtorBase + func_0010F6CC - so this is the family's deleting destructor; 'Dtor' alone hid the fact that it also frees. (Suffix C because the same template is already recorded as Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtor at 0x0044CEB0 and ...B at 0x0044FB8C.)

name: Actor2D_UpdateSpritePositions
summary: Positions the actor's two 2D sprite layers from the owner's screen position and the character height table: the upper layer is offset by -2 and scaled by 0.5, the lower one by +1, each with its own height entry from 0x00728420.
evidence: NEW: the class is established by the confident Actor2D_Update* family (Actor2D_UpdateFacingToTarget 0.60, Actor2D_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy 0.50, Actor2D_UpdateFollowMode 0.50) and the body is complete: it reads the two height-table pairs from 0x00728420, computes two positions and calls the set-position/set-size pair twice. The 'two sprite layers' reading is therefore supported by the structure, not just by the old guess.

name: Font_GlyphQuad_SetUV
signature: void Font_GlyphQuad_SetUV(FontGlyphQuad* self, unsigned int* uv)
summary: Sets one UV/vertex block of a font glyph quad: picks a 2-word render state from the glyph's texture page, updates the quad's UV buffer at +0x204 and stores the 3-word UV record at +0x2D8.
evidence: Callers are the font glyph builders (0x005CA718, maybe_Font_GlyphQuad_CreateFromUVs 0x005CABE4, 0x005CB308); body calls func_0070BBE4(&self->f_204, self->f_3C8, visible) and writes self->f_2D8..f_2E0 from *uv. The sibling 0x002B3AEC does the same for the second/third UV slots.

name: Field_DetachSlotObject
summary: Detaches the object attached through 0x1C75FC from the world's slot table and clears the cached handle at +0x2AC.
evidence: if (self->f_2AC != 0) 0x1C75FC(self->f_2B0); self->f_2AC = 0. 0x1C75FC Field_AttachSlotObject is the matching attach function (used by 0x2B3E44); callers 0x5CA79C and maybe_Gfx_ReleaseNodeHandle 0x5CC878.

name: Font_GlyphQuad_SetUVTriple
signature: void Font_GlyphQuad_SetUVTriple(FontGlyphQuad* self, unsigned int* uv)
summary: Same as Font_GlyphQuad_SetUV but updates the three UV page slots (+0x3C9, and +0x3CA/+0x3CB when they are not -1) and stores the record at +0x2E4.
evidence: Identical callees/fields as 0x002B3A60 (0x0070BBE4, self->f_204, self->f_3C8/3C9/3CA/3CB) with the record moved from +0x2D8 to +0x2E4; same four callers in the font glyph code.

name: Game_SetTwoFlags
signature: void Game_SetTwoFlags(FieldSceneObject* self, unsigned int value)
summary: Writes value to the two game-flag ids cached at +0x3CA and +0x3CB, skipping any that are -1.
evidence: NEW: the caller Field2D_Sprite_CreateTweenMoveDirect and the two -1 guards show this is the 'set the object's two associated game flags' helper; 0x70BBE4 is the global flag writer.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_StopAttachedEffect
summary: Stops and detaches the effect a 2D sprite actor started earlier, but only while the 'effect active' byte f_297 is set: it resolves the effect transform and resource, releases the effect object and clears the flag.
evidence: NEW: the caller Field2D_SpriteNode_Reinit is the sprite node re-initialiser, i.e. the place where a stale effect must be stopped, and the body calls the named Gfx_SpriteActor_StopAnimAndHide at the end. The named effect helpers (0x31A6AC/0x5F4E14/0x5F4DB8) match the described sequence.

name: maybe_Actor2D_DispatchSlotEvent
signature: u32 maybe_Actor2D_DispatchSlotEvent(Actor2D* self, u32 source, int ctx, int ctx2)
summary: Dispatches a 2D actor event to one of two callback pairs: the Z-flag path uses the pair selected by +0x2DC, the other path uses +0x2E8 only when the event source is one of the object's own slots (+0x24C, +0x338, +0x380). The branch condition is an unrecovered flag register, so the two paths cannot be told apart.
evidence: The body still contains in_ZR, i.e. Ghidra lost the flag-producing instruction, so the branch meaning is unreadable; the only solid facts remain the three slot comparisons and the two callback pairs. Confidence is lowered to 0.3 to match the damaged decompilation.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact
signature: FieldSceneObject* maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact(void* heap, int* def, int arg3, int ctx)
summary: Field scene-object constructor: builds the base with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x0075EFDC (+0x98 secondary), caches the actor-manager pointer from work+0x54 twice, sets the 0xFF 'none' ids and chains three 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef members at +0x2EC.
evidence: The named callee Actor_HandleRef_Ctor confirms the three handle references, Os_GetGameWork confirms the two work+0x54 caches, and vtable 0x0075EFDC is the same family as the named Field_SceneObject_CtorC; the class name is still inferred, so kept maybe_.

name: Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtorD
summary: Deleting destructor of a field scene-object variant: installs the caller's vtable, walks three embedded sub-objects to the sprite actor, detaches the two attached slot objects, restores base vtable 0x0075D55C, destroys the scene object and frees the block.
evidence: NEW: the detach call is now named Field_AttachSlotObject and the tail is the familiar Field_Object_DtorBase + func_0010F6CC pair, so this is the family's deleting destructor for the variant that owns two slot objects (unlike 0x002B385C, which owns none). (Suffix D to avoid the existing Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtor/B at 0x0044CEB0/0x0044FB8C.)

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_CreatePlaneSprite
summary: Creates the 200x120 sprite plane used by a field prop: builds the sprite mesh from the object's texture/size table and attaches it as the actor's drawable.
evidence: 0x31A48C(&out, 0, 0x23, def->f_48, {200,120}) builds the 200x120 quad (200/0x78 are the two literals at 0x2B3F5C..0x2B3F60); 0x31A394(&out, self, &quad, 'sprite') Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh creates the drawable, stored at self->f_B8 with f_129=10; 0x5E7650 attaches it. The 'sprite' literal is the same one used by 0x2B4938/0x2B6BCC.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_AdvanceTouchTransition
summary: Advances the object's touch animation one step (Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition) and returns 1 while the state byte at *self is not the terminal value 3, i.e. 'still running'.
evidence: NEW: the asm is push {r4,lr}; mov r4,r0; bl 0x423648; mov r0,r4; bl 0x64DB08; eor r0,r0,#1; pop - and 0x0064DB08 is ldrb r0,[r0]; cmp r0,#3; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#0, i.e. *self == 3. So the function steps the touch state machine and returns 'not finished'; nothing here reads a game or battle state flag, so the old 'Game_IsStateFlagClear' name was wrong. The 'touch' wording is inherited from Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition (0.50), hence maybe_.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateEightParts
summary: Builds the eight sprite parts of a 2D effect actor: copies the descriptor, creates the colour animator, converts the descriptor rectangle into part-space coordinates and adds all eight children (each 0x48 bytes at +0x298 + i*0x48) with their own animated colour.
evidence: `self->f_b4/f_b0/f_ac` copied from arg2+4/+8/+0xc; `func_00319848()` + `func_0029E41C()` provide the animation object stored in `self->f_b8->f_128`; `func_0028E2A0(self,&rect)` (colour animator); loop `i = 0..7` with `func_0047B314(i)` / `func_0047AF94(...)` and `func_00335A6C(self,&part,self+0x298+i*0x48,0)` (AddChild); ends with `func_0047AF5C(&self->f_204,1)`.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_QueryState
summary: Refreshes the object's cached interaction record: builds a type-5 record from the attached actor id (or 0xFF) and the object's position through Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent, then copies its id, three flag bytes and four coordinates into +0x4D8..+0x4F4 and returns 1.
evidence: The callee Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent is confident and its evidence already names this function, so the record shape is verified; what the record means (touch event vs interaction state) rests on that callee's own 0.50 reading, and the actor-id getter 0x0063C7B0 is still unnamed. Kept hedged.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_CtorB
summary: Second constructor variant of the 2D actor sprite node: same 2D-actor base and self-referential list head as 0x002907D8, with 8 x 0x48-byte sprite entries.
evidence: Byte-shape identical to Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor (0x002907D8) apart from its vtable literal (g_002B4234, head +0x9C) and count; caller is the same maybe_Ui_Overlay_CreateSlotWidget (0x00237ADC) which creates UI overlay slots.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_DtorB
summary: Destructor of the 2D actor sprite node built by Actor2D_SpriteNode_CtorB: restores the class's two vtable halves (g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDescB + 0x9C), destroys its eight 0x48-byte sprite entries, installs the base 0x0075D55C vtables, unlinks the embedded scene node, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and frees the block.
evidence: The immediately preceding function 0x002B41F8 is the named Actor2D_SpriteNode_CtorB, which allocates exactly 8 x 0x48 bytes at +0xa6 with the same g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDescB vtable; this body destroys that same array via std_destroy_range(self+0xa6, 8) and then falls into the base destructor. It is the ...B-class twin of the refined maybe_Actor2D_SpriteNode_DtorC (0x0029081C), whose body is identical for g_actor2DSpriteNodeClassDesc. 'Field2D_Actor' guessed the wrong class family.

name: maybe_Field_MarkerWidget_UpdateScreenPos
summary: Converts the widget's local rectangle at +0x2E0 into a screen position by subtracting the field object's camera offsets f_78/f_7C, then resolves the resulting position id (0xFF = none) and applies it through Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation on that object.
evidence: The rectangle/camera-offset subtraction is clear, but the id resolver 0x00319678 is a split symbol inside Ui_PastScenarioWindow_Dtor (0x0031961C), so its meaning is not confirmed; the class name MarkerWidget still comes from the first pass, hence kept maybe_.

name: Field_DragController_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the pointer drag controller: in state 1 it moves the target by the stored delta (one unit per frame, sign preserved), in state 2 it waits for the drag animation to finish; returns 0 when idle.
evidence: state byte f_297: 1 = dragging, 2 = finishing; f_2E4/f_2E8 are the X/Y remainders, decremented toward 0 while the target's f_C4 and +0xC8 fields are nudged by the sign; when the pointer stalls the code compares against the literal g_002B448C pair and switches to state 2; 0x253290(work+0x6C,0x15) plays SE 0x15; 0x636AFC(work+0x6C) tests whether the drag animation ended and sets state 0.

name: maybe_Effect_CreateMeshEmitterPair
summary: Creates mesh emitter pair for effect instance: resolves resources, attaches animation instances, and sets model size.
evidence: Callees Anim_Instance_CtorSprite, Mem_AllocAligned_2, and Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize are confident, but emitter pairing logic is inferred. Kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Field_DragController_OnEvent
signature: unsigned int Field_DragController_OnEvent(FieldDragController* self, int arg2, int eventNode)
summary: Handles the two input events of the drag controller: on the 'drag start' node it records the pointer delta against the actor position and enters state 1; on the 'drag move' node it forwards the rectangle to 0x22CDBC.
evidence: eventNode == self+0x24C: reads work+0x54->+0x20 (current actor), skips when its state byte f_38==0x0B, builds a rect from self->f_2E0 and calls 0x22CDBC(actor,&rect); eventNode == self+0x298: self->f_2E4/f_2E8 = current pointer minus actor position and f_297=1. Event ids are the same +0x24C/+0x298 nodes used by 0x2B4938's drag object.

name: Field_DragController_Ctor
signature: FieldDragController* Field_DragController_Ctor(void* heap, int* def, int arg3, int ctx)
summary: Constructor of the 0x298-byte drag controller object: allocates the base with 0x28E630, installs the class vtable and zeroes the drag state and its parameter block.
evidence: 0x28E630(arg1,&ctx,0x4000000C); *obj = g_002B48B8, obj[0x8B] = vtable+0x98; f_297=0; 0x4AF3F4 builds the parameter block at +0x298 with f_48=0 and the literal triple from g_002B48BC. The matching dtor 0x2B48C4 tears down the same offsets.

name: Field_DragController_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the drag controller: restores both vtable halves, tears down the sprite/actor object and frees the memory.
evidence: arg1[0x8B]=arg2+0x98; 0x17C330(arg1+0xA6) reaches the actor, writes g_002B4914 into it, unlinks and calls 0x335DAC then 0x10F6CC. Mirrors 0x2B4854's layout.

name: maybe_Field_DragController_IsActive
summary: Drag-controller vtable slot: evaluates the field event-scene validity test 0x00636AFC(world+0x6C) and leaves 0/1 in r0.
evidence: The address is inside the Field_DragController class (Ctor 0x002B4854, Dtor 0x002B48C4, OnEvent 0x002B4750), so 'drag controller' was right but 'GetState' was not: there is no state object. Disassembly of the callee shows the body returns a value (0/1) that Ghidra dropped when it typed this function void, which is why a predicate name is justified.

name: Field_SceneObject_CreateSprite
summary: Spawns the sprite/actor part of a field scene object: resolves the sprite type from the record, creates the model through Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, applies the animation template, sets the model size and finally creates and registers the drag controller object.
evidence: rec fields: +0x1A id, +0x1C/+0x1D type pair -> 0x319848 Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable(char,short); allocates the 0x178-byte model with 0x109DC8, builds it through 0x2D1F28, applies 0x2D1304 maybe_Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate, attaches with 0x5E7650, sizes it with 0x5F3500 Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize and sets f_128 from 0x29E41C maybe_Gfx_GetSharedCoreNode; then 'sprite' literal at 0x7BE7CA, 0x31A48C/0x335A6C add the child, and a 0x298-byte object is created with 0x28E630 and linked into work+0x134. Callers 0x352DBC/0x353074 maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType.

name: Field_SceneObject_ReleaseAttachedObject
signature: void Field_SceneObject_ReleaseAttachedObject(FieldSceneObject* self, int arg2, int b, int ctx)
summary: Releases the object attached at +0x29C (detaching its handle through 0x1C7570) and then runs the base release path 0x28E5E0.
evidence: if (self->f_29C != 0) { handle = *(u32*)(self->f_29C+4); 0x1C7570(work+0x54, handle); self->f_29C = 0; } then 0x28E5E0(self,handle,arg3,ctx). 0x28E5E0 is the base destructor/release used by the 0x2B3xxx scene-object family.

name: Field_SceneObject_TriggerGadgetCommand
signature: void Field_SceneObject_TriggerGadgetCommand(FieldSceneObject* self, int arg2, int b, int ctx)
summary: When the object's stored gadget/interaction id resolves to a live gimmick, sends gimmick command 0x16 with the object as argument.
evidence: 0x31A868(self->f_298, self->f_29A) resolves the gimmick; if non-zero calls 0x256678(work+0x6C, 0x16, self->f_4) - 0x256678 is the 'Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand' helper named by an earlier lane, and 0x16 is the command id.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorType7
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorType7(u32 factory, int record, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor variant for a type-7 field scene object (model id 0x9DB): builds it with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x0075F214 (+0x98 secondary), sets the 0xFFFF/0xFF sentinels and writes f_92=7 and f_A5=0x9DB.
evidence: The body calls func_0028E630 once, installs the vtable and writes the type/model ids; there is no child-creation call and no caller, so the old 'CreateTypedChild' name was wrong - it constructs the object itself.

name: Field_SceneObject_DtorC_2B4FE8

name: maybe_Gfx_LoadResourceFromDescriptor
signature: void maybe_Gfx_LoadResourceFromDescriptor(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

evidence: Engine_GetMemoryManager returns the manager singleton in *outPtr, and its layout (FACTS.md / its own doc) puts the global intrusive resource lists at +0x33C..+0x368, so the third argument is a resource list, not a render context. The callee 0x0055A500 is a loader (it stores arg3 at +4, compares a 4-byte magic through the CRT helper 0x001009DC and then walks the source), so 'RegisterRenderObject' described the wrong operation. The loader's own name Gfx_ParseChipFile is unverified, so the new name stays maybe_.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateDeferredSubObject

name: Field_Gimmick_Update

evidence: Callees now named: Field_Gimmick_StepAnimFrame (0x2BDECC), Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, maybe_Field_Gimmick_ClampObjectPosition, maybe_Gfx_ReleaseEffectNodes, plus the Os_GetGameWork -> +0x54/+0x48 UI-overlay reads; the eight-way direction switch feeding PlayAnimation is the per-frame behaviour of an update slot, so 'Update' is the right role name.

It is slot 1 (the begin slot) of the method table 0x0075FC98 whose later slots are the curve-move Update/ApplyPosition pair, matching the old 'move params' guess; the old summary wrongly called +0x2C an animator pointer - it is the state byte compared with 0..4 by 0x002BF298/0x002BF5C4.

summary: Ends the move/landing step: first calls the actor through virtual slot +0x88 (r0 = actor, result discarded - the per-step motion/transform hook), then copies the saved landing position actor+0x3AC/+0x3B0/+0x3B4 back into the live position +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 and marks the transform dirty (+0x118 = 1) so the node is rebuilt next frame.

The neighbouring entry 0x002BFF64 does exactly the same copy/dirty sequence without the virtual call, which isolates the call as the 'apply motion first' half - the old summary already had this reading; the new disassembly only makes it exact, hence confirmed.

name: Actor_Action_Move_UpdateAnimStep0

It is slot 1 of the animator-driver method table 0x0075FD00 together with 0x002C0704 Actor_Action_Detach and 0x002C0654 Move_UpdateAnimation. 'Step0' is the literal argument 0 passed to slot +0x14, which matches the old reading; the exact call chain is new.

name: Svc_Timer_RunDue
summary: Per-frame timer pump: advances the accumulated time by 1/30 s (0x3D088889) and the frame counter, then, if a one-shot callback is armed, fires the callback of the pending timer slot (12 slots of 0x18 bytes at self+0x35C) and finally clears the "timer pending" flag in the engine context.
evidence: Literal 0.0333333 = 1/30 s is added to self->f_364 (elapsed) with self->f_368 (frame count) incremented and self->f_36c set to the step; the 12-entry table is `self + 0x35c + self->f_360*0x18` with self->f_360 = current slot index, and the entry's code pointer at +0x34 (or the adjustor at +0x38 selecting from the table at self+0x37C) is called as `fn(slot, 0)`. Tail: `ctx->f_94 = 0`.

name: Svc_Timer_ClearQueue
summary: Drains the timer queue (keeps pulling entries while the queue reports a positive count) and, when the timer object is in state 2 or 3, resets the corresponding engine subsystem through the global context.
evidence: `while (func_0062F070(self) > 0) func_0010EBD8(self);` is the classic "pop until empty" loop for the queue serviced by 0x002C1D60; `self->f_4a8` is the state byte (2/3) and the tail calls func_002D24BC on `ctx->f_14`, the same subsystem reset used by 0x002B56E8.

name: maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState6
summary: Prepares the display for record 6: attaches the sub-widget at +0x228 unless a modal window is open, hides the element at +0x138, stores the record pointer returned by 0x00642710(self, 6) at +0x250, clears +0x254/+0x258 and resets the sub-widget through its +0x14 slot.
evidence: NEW: 0x00642710 is not a timer start - its asm is ldr r0,[r0,#0x354]; bounds-check against r0->f_60; return base + index*8, i.e. an 8-byte record accessor - so the literal 6 is a table index, not a state number; and 0x0032BD58 is mov r1,#0; add r0,r0,#0x138; b 0x29126C, i.e. the visibility setter on self+0x138. The handler table at 0x007293E0 (23 entries, this one at slot 20) supports the 'state handler' reading, but the class name 'Ui_DateDisplay' is still only from the first pass.

name: maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_Update
summary: Date-label update: ticks the widget tween at self+0x228 against self+0x330 and then hits undecodable data, so the rest of the routine (mark finished, notify the dialog controller with command 0x0B) is known only from the disassembly.
evidence: The decompilation is damaged - the readable body is empty after the declaration block - so per FACTS.md the name stays maybe_ at <= 0.30... kept at 0.35 only because the surviving prologue is the same Ui_Widget_Update(self+0x228, self+0x330) call as its named siblings 0x002C23EC/0x002C24E0/0x002C2540/0x002C2624, which fixes the family but not the step.

name: maybe_Item_BuildCandidateList

name: maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_AdvanceByFlags
summary: Date-display step (entry 10 of the step table 0x007293F0): branches on the screen flag word at +0x344 - with bit 4 set it requests state 10 from the controller at +0x35C, otherwise it asks the step-kind helper on +0x138 and the row helper, requests state 9 or 0x0B, writes label state 3 to +0x4A8 and marks +0x4A9.
evidence: The class is now solid: 0x002C21AC is entry 10 of the rodata step table 0x007293F0, whose named rows are Ui_DateDisplay_AdvanceByLoadState, Ui_DateDisplay_FinishState1, Ui_DateDisplay_FinishState2, Ui_DateDisplay_FinishAndStep and maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState3/7/8/10. The body itself is still damaged (two halt_baddata sites and a bad-instruction warning at 0x002C225E), so the exact meaning of the +0x344 bits and of the two helpers stays open and the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_Panel_SetState5
summary: Step handler of the same template as Ui_Panel_SetState7 (0x00194F00): ticks the widget at self+0x228 with the descriptor at self+0x330, and once the widget reports ready asks the controller at self+0x35C for state 5 through vtable+0x14 and commits it with vtable+0x10. Always returns 1.
evidence: scores.jsonl puts this function and 0x00194F00 in the same vtable (0x0062F680, one sibling each), and the two bodies are the same step-request template with only the state id (5 vs 7) and the field offsets differing - so the 'DateDisplay' class attribution was unsupported and the sibling's established Ui_Panel_SetState<N> convention applies.

name: maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState8
summary: Prepares the display for record 8: hides the element at +0x138, stores the record pointer returned by 0x00642710(self, 8) at +0x250, clears +0x254/+0x258 and resets the sub-widget at +0x228 through its +0x14 slot.

name: Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState4
summary: Date-display step (entry 3 of the step table 0x007293F0): resets the sub-object at +0x138, fetches entry record 4 from the record table at +0x354 through 0x00642710 and installs it into the sub-widget at +0x228, which clears its animation state and restarts it.

The body is byte-identical in shape to the named siblings maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState3/7/8/10 (reset +0x138, fetch record N, install into +0x228), and the disassembly of 0x00642710 shows it is the by-index sibling of Ui_GetEntryRecord (bounds-check self+0x354, return record + index*8), so the '4' is the entry index the family is named after.

name: Ui_DateDisplay_FinishAndStep
summary: Date-label finish step: once the label widget at self+0x228 reports ready, releases the widget at self+0x138 and requests controller state 4 on the object at self+0x35C.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_InstallHandlers
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_InstallHandlers(u32 message, u32 arg2, int arg3)

name: Ui_DateDisplay_FinishState2

name: maybe_Ui_DateDisplay_EnterState3

name: Ui_DiveStartWindowPart_Ctor

name: Ui_DiveStartWindow_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting-destructor thunk of a dive-start window base: stores the incoming vtable, runs the confident Ui_DiveStartWindow_Dtor (0x0032C1AC) and frees the object.

name: Ui_TextWindow_BindRowPanes
summary: Binds the ten numbered text panes of a two-column, five-row text window and primes its animations: walks 'txt_l0'..'txt_l4' and 'txt_r0'..'txt_r4' (incrementing the trailing digit with carry), binds each through Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane, clears the text, looks up 'present' and starts the 'null_bottom' animation.

name: maybe_Ui_Element2D_Ctor_vt76007C
summary: Default constructor of a small 0x130-byte 2D UI element: allocates through 0x001D8B6C, installs vtable 0x0076007C, marks the id at +0x11C as -1 (none), clears two words and installs the shared UI base vtable 0x00759378 at +0x128.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeletingDtorA

name: maybe_Container_InlineVector_PushRecord
signature: void maybe_Container_InlineVector_PushRecord(InlineVector* vector, const TextSlotSource* source, int len, void* arg4, u8 flag)
summary: Appends one record to a vector that keeps its elements inline: when the used size is below 0x580 and the storage still points at the inline area (self+0x14) it copies the source strings in, otherwise it grows through the object's allocator.
evidence: The recovered body is truncated after the inline-storage guard - only the wcslen call at 0x00100B74 survives - so the 0x2C stride and the two string fields are not verified; only the 'end-begin < 0x580' check and the 'begin == self+0x14' inline test are. No caller and no named callee.

name: Text_MessageStack_Pop
summary: Pops the last entry of a message stack: if the vector is non-empty it clears the shown message, rebinds arguments 2/3 for the promoted entry, refreshes the shared message view, compacts the 0x2C-byte records and shrinks the vector.
evidence: 0x2C record stride appears in every pointer step, std_memcpy/std_memmove and Message_SetArg are named, and the visible-message refresh uses already-named func_00707C1C; the 'stack pop' interpretation is fully supported.

name: maybe_Item_BuildCandidateList_A

summary: Resolves a packed resource handle through the object hash (g_2C4EA0/g_2C4EA4), finds the matching object by type id (g_2C4EA8) and attaches it to the resource list with 0x193FA0, then releases the scene entry of self->f_20 (0x14C3EC).

name: Ui_StoryPanel_SetupRecord
signature: void Ui_StoryPanel_SetupRecord(StoryPanel* self, StoryPanelParent* parent, unsigned char mode)

evidence: The named maybe_Ui_RouletteWindow_ResetPanels / maybe_Ui_Screen_InvokeNextCallback calls, the SE id 0xEA7 and the same layout-table restore as the confirmed Ui_JackpotScreen_EndPayout (0x002C7B58) make the jackpot-screen reading consistent.
