name: Ui_JackpotScreen_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the jackpot screen: installs the vtable, releases the two packed handles, unregisters the widgets and frees the UI objects.
evidence: *arg1 = g_002c9cc8 (vtable); releases arg1[0x74] through its vtable+4; the two handles arg1[8]/arg1[9] are validated with the same handle-table test as 0x46E50C and released with 0x1C7570; 0x21F8B8 unregisters; Pack_ReleaseHandle; 0x445D04/0x626A80 release the widget parts.

name: maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure
signature: void maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure(unsigned int vm, unsigned int closure, void* fn, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Large Squirrel VM helper (0x1480 bytes) that prepares a call frame, invokes a closure through the serialized-value helpers and releases the temporary references; only the entry block is recovered.
evidence: Script_ReadSerializedValue / Script_ReadClosureRef / Script_ObjectPtr_Assign are named and confirm Squirrel VM code, and Script_RegisterHook is a named caller, but Ghidra recovered only the entry block of a 5 KB function and hits halt_baddata, so 'RunClosure' remains a guess.

name: maybe_Object_ReleaseRefcountedChildren
summary: Damaged Thumb body that repeatedly decrements a refcount at [obj+4] and calls virtual slot +8 when it reaches zero, for up to four objects: a refcounted teardown releasing child objects.
evidence: NEW: there is no direct bl/b call site (the xref callers came from unrelated Squirrel neighbours); the only recognisable pattern is the refcount-decrement + virtual-dtor sequence repeated four times next to Fs_UnmountByName, and Ghidra reports bad instruction data. 0.2 is all the evidence supports.

name: Container_ReleaseRefHandleArrays
summary: Complete destructor of a handle container: walks all six arrays, drops the reference of every 0x8000000-tagged handle (decrementing the object's refcount and calling its vtable delete at zero), then installs nothing, runs the class destructor and frees the block with the size computed from the counts (counts*8 + records*0x14 + 0x60).
evidence: NEW: the tail is now readable as the standard two-step teardown (call self's vtable entry 0, then sized free via func_00147AEC with the computed byte size), which makes this the *complete* destructor of the object rather than just an array releaser; the six identical refcount-release sequences are unchanged.

name: maybe_Script_Vm_FindBlockByOffset
signature: void* maybe_Script_Vm_FindBlockByOffset(void* self, void* file, int extra, u32 blockIndex, u32 offset)
summary: Finds the block containing an offset in a table of 0x14-byte entries: walks the f_24 entries at f_28, skips blockIndex matches, and for the matching entry positions the file at (entry[+0x10] + extra)*8 and returns entry[+4] + 0x1C (the block payload).
evidence: New context: the caller is now the confident Script_Vm_ResolveStackIndex (0x006BBAC8), which treats the result as a stack-slot block, so this is the Squirrel VM's block lookup rather than a generic container - the old 'Container_' prefix named the wrong subsystem and is replaced. The entry layout and the seek are fully visible, but no other caller confirms the block format, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Container_RefPair_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor for an object holding two reference-counted handles: writes the new vtable tag, releases both handles (refcount decrement, virtual release at zero) and then destroys/frees the object.
evidence: Unchanged: the readable body is truncated at a bad instruction (only `*self = tag` survives) and the function has no callers and no callees in the call graph, so the two release sequences exist only as the earlier disassembly notes. Nothing new to promote it.

name: maybe_Container_NotifyAllAndRegister
summary: Checks completion bit 0x80000000 at self+4, traverses 0x14-byte-stride element array decrementing refcounts, and cleans up storage block.
evidence: Damaged decompilation with register confusion (unaff_r5); destructor/cleanup loop in vtable 0x007602A0 near Sq_Object_Delete.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeleteDtor48
summary: Deleting destructor of a 0x48-byte object: calls the object's own destructor through vtable slot 0 and frees the block with the sized free helper 0x00147AEC.
evidence: Unchanged: the body is the generic two-line deleting destructor (virtual dtor + sized free of 0x48 bytes) and the call graph gives no caller, so neither the owner class nor the subsystem can be settled. The only rodata reference is a teardown table row, which does not name the class.

name: maybe_Script_ThumbStub_2CC714
signature: void maybe_Script_ThumbStub_2CC714(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int* loop, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, int* refcounted)
summary: Unrecovered function in the script/fs block: it walks a 0x14-byte record array, writes one byte and copies two 8-byte halves per record, and releases up to six ref-counted temporaries on exit. Name is a placeholder only.
evidence: Every named callee is Squirrel/FS code (Script_ReadSerializedValue, Script_ObjectPtr_Assign, Script_ReadClosureRef, Fs_UnmountByName), but Ghidra hits bad instruction data and lost all argument registers, so the operation stays unknown; only the placeholder address suffix is honest.

name: Fs_FormatDataPath
signature: int Fs_FormatDataPath(char* self, char* dst, int dstSize, const char* root, ...)
summary: Formats the per-variant asset path "<root>/Data<index>" into the caller's buffer via the vsnprintf wrapper 0x0051BA9C.
evidence: NEW: the inline format string "%s/Data%d" at 0x002CC828 is handed to the same vsnprintf wrapper used by the sibling "%s/mini_%d" formatter, and both alternate in the handler table at 0x0072D788; the format string is decisive for the operation even though the Fs_ prefix is inherited from that table.

name: maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords
signature: u32 maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords(void* save, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Ghidra-damaged save-slot loader: formats two resource names (0x108-byte buffers through format vtable 0x0072D7B0), converts them to wide text with std_mbrlen/std_mbrtowc, splits and opens each archive entry and reads the payloads into the save work (the second into +0xE0E0 with length 0x14). It reads; it does not write.
evidence: The merged callees are the Fs read path (Fs_SplitResourceName, Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadInto, Fs_ClassifyResult) and the save payload is copied into the work object, but the function prologue is lost and no named caller exists, so the exact buffer layout and the 'records' wording stay uncertain.

name: Ui_DataPanel_OpenDefault
signature: void Ui_DataPanel_OpenDefault(DataPanel * self, u8 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Opens a data panel in its default state: clears the busy byte, resets the game window's shared state, re-initialises the panel's party snapshot, stores the requested mode, switches the panel state machine to state 3 and takes the panel's mutex before the caller fills it.
evidence: The callees are now named - Ui_Window_ResetState (0x35F814), Save_InitPartySnapshot (0x10F3E0) and Os_MutexLock - so the body is the 'reset everything, set mode, enter state 3, lock' opening sequence; the panel identity comes from the 0xE400-byte data-panel block the family shares (f_E0F4/f_E110/f_E3C4).

name: Save_WriteSlotStrings
summary: Writes the two variable-length string blocks of one save slot: formats the slot text with the save formatter (g_2CD018), converts it to the on-disk encoding (0x504DB4), writes it (0x505DE0) and validates each step with 0x2CDB84; the second block is the 0x14-byte record at save+0xE0E0.
evidence: format vtable g_002CD018, converters 0x504DB4/0x505DE0, classifier 0x2CDB84, second block at save+0xE0E0 size 0x14, buffer 0x108; caller 0x2CDF54.

name: Save_LoadSlotData
summary: Loads one save slot into the panel object: reads the small 0x14-byte slot header into save+8 and the 0xC8B0-byte party snapshot into save+0x1830, then the trailing 0x1828-byte block into save+0xE0E0, converting the path through the slot's virtual name method and aborting with the Fs status if any read fails.
evidence: The two format helpers are now identified as file loaders (Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPath), and the three destination sizes tile the object exactly - 0x1830 + 0xC8B0 = 0xE0E0, where the named Save_InitPartySnapshot documents the 0xC8B0-byte party snapshot at +0x1830 - so this reads a slot into memory; 'WriteSlotMeta' had the direction and the role wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithStrings
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithStrings(DataPanel* self, u32 mode, char* flags)
summary: Opens the panel with its 31 text strings: copies 0x200 bytes per record into the string block, stamps the time hash, binds the two label panes and switches to state 5.
evidence: The 31x0x200 copy loop and the named Save/Ui_DataPanel callees are clear, but the panel identity (save slot vs. data viewer) and the string-vs-flags split from its sibling stay unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithFlags
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenWithFlags(DataPanel* self, u32 mode, char* flags)
summary: Opens the save/data panel with an option-byte block: optionally resets member triggers and writes a message control tag, initialises the party snapshot, stamps the time hash, copies the 31 member record strings and switches to state 5.
evidence: The named Save_InitPartySnapshot/SaveData_ResetMemberTriggers/Ui_DataPanel_CopyFromWork callees support a save-data panel open, but there is no named caller and the 'flags' contract rests only on the option bytes read from the argument.

name: Save_BuildSlotFilePaths
summary: Builds the two on-disk names of a save slot: formats "%s/Data%d" and "%s/mini_%d" with the slot number and the "data:" mount prefix, converts each narrow name to the engine's UTF-16 form and passes it to the filesystem name helper 0x00504F0C; a negative result is reported through 0x0011ED40.
evidence: The two templates are verified in code.bin: 0x002CC828 = "%s/Data%d" and 0x002CE688 = "%s/mini_%d", formatted with the "data:" prefix at 0x0072D780 (the previous pass misread them as '%s/D%atad'), and the caller is maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords - so these are the save-slot file names, not a delete path.

name: Ui_DataPanel_Reset
signature: void Ui_DataPanel_Reset(DataPanel* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Resets the data panel to an empty state: clears the mode and secondary words, zeroes the 0x24-byte header and the small 0xE-byte field, rebinds the label pane and switches the panel to state 6.
evidence: Callers are the named menu state functions maybe_Ui_Menu_InitModeState (0x3F306C) and maybe_Ui_Menu_StartModeTransition (0x3F3030), and the body ends with the explicit state write self->f_e110 = 6; that is a panel reset on menu mode change.

name: Save_LoadSlotHeader
summary: Loads a save slot's header: memsets a 0x108-byte buffer, formats the resource name for slot through format vtable 0x0072D7A0, converts it to wide text, splits/opens the archive entry and reads 0x1828 bytes into save+8; returns 0 on success and otherwise the Fs error code.
evidence: The callees are now the named Fs read helpers and the caller maybe_Save_MigrateVerify uses the return value as a success code; the direction is into the save work (a header load), which confirms the name. The body has a few unaff_ registers from the lost prologue but the Fs call sequence itself is verified in the disassembly.

name: Fs_ClassifyResult
summary: Classifies a 3DS file-system Result code into the save layer's small status enum: 0 when the call succeeded, 1 for module 0x4400 codes 100..179, 2 for 199..219, 3 for codes at or above g_2CDC40 up to 399, and 5 (after reporting a fatal error through 0x11ED40) for anything else.
evidence: masks 0x80000000/0x3FC00/0x3FF with module 0x4400, range checks 100..180, 199..220 and g_002CDC40..400, fatal 0x11ED40.

name: Os_CalcTimeBasedHash
summary: Builds a 64-bit hash from the console's real-time clock: converts the current date/time with six calendar helpers (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) and mixes them with fixed multipliers into one 64-bit value. Used as a cheap tamper/version fingerprint for stored blocks.
evidence: `func_0050EFA4(&local_90)` (RTC → 8-byte value) then func_00658EB8 / 0x6590E8 / 0x65907C / 0x658F64 / 0x658F0C / 0x659024 / 0x658FCC each extract one field (year/month/day/...); the result is the sum `local_50*10 + uVar4*g + uVar5*g + ... + arg2` with the multipliers from the literal pool at 0x002cde50..0x002cde68. Callers 0x002CD2A0 and 0x002CD498 store it at +0xd418 and +0x2faf8.

name: Fs_ClassifyResultB
summary: Second variant of the save-layer Result classifier: 0 for success, 1 for module 0x4400 codes 0x154..0x167, 2 for everything else after reporting a fatal error through 0x11ED40.
evidence: module 0x4400 with range 0x154..0x168, bounds 0x168..0x185 and g_002CDF50..400, fatal 0x11ED40; callers 0x2CDF54 and 0x2CE494.

name: maybe_Save_MigrateAllSlots
summary: Mounts the save data archive (shared handle 0x72D780, name 'data:') and loops over the four slots: writes each slot's strings with Save_WriteSlotStrings, validates two stored markers and the two 0x5E magic bytes, then copies the slot header fields into the per-slot record and sets the slot state (1/2 ok, 3/4 failure, 6/7 abort).
evidence: The named Save_WriteSlotStrings plus the four-slot loop and 0x5E markers make the slot-initialisation role clear, but nothing in the new names proves this is a version migration rather than first-time slot initialisation, so the 'Migrate' wording stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListState_Reset
summary: Resets a list/scroll state block: clears the counters and flag bytes, zero-fills the 14-byte tail, allocates the 0x1820-byte table at +0x182C, restores the 0x5E cursor, the 0xFF sentinel and the 6-per-page count, and locks the state mutex at +0xE118.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_Menu_SetModeState, which passes *Ui_UiManager_GetInstance() and then stores a mode tag, so the object is the UI manager singleton rather than a standalone list. The 0x5E cursor, the 0xFF sentinel and the 6-per-page count are still the only evidence for 'list state', and the 0x1820-byte allocation is unexplained, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple(void* self, u8 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Minimal data-panel open: rewinds the embedded pane buffer (+0xE3C4 = 0), copies the three pane words from game work +0x2FB18..+0x2FB20, rebinds the pane through 0x0051BB08 with id 0xC, sets the pane state to 9 and locks +0xE118.
evidence: NEW (negative): there is still no caller and none of the three helpers (0x0010F300, 0x0051BB08, mutex lock) carries a name that would identify the panel; only the state word 9 and the +0x2FB18 pane source are certain, so both 'DataPanel' and 'OpenSimple' remain guesses.

name: maybe_Save_MigrateVerify
summary: Verification half of the save-slot setup: mounts the same 'data:' archive, loads the slot header with slot 0xFFFFFFFF, reads the marker at save+0x1820 and compares save->f_1828 and the f_182C checksum with the 0x5E magic; writes result state f_E3C0 = 1 (ok), 4 (already done) or 3 (failed) and sub-state f_E3C4 = 3/4/6/7.
evidence: Its callee is now the named Save_LoadSlotHeader and its caller is the save task resolver maybe_Save_LoadTask_ResolveObject, which confirms it verifies saved slot data; whether the operation is a migration or an ordinary load check is still not proven.

name: Save_VerifyBlock
signature: void Save_VerifyBlock(DataPanel* self, u8 mode, int buffer, u32 size)
summary: Verifies a stored 0xc8b0-byte block: recomputes the time-based hash over the block and compares it with the 64-bit stamp stored in the global state block; on a match the data is copied into the panel's 0x200-byte string block and the state machine advances to 10, otherwise the panel reports error 3.
evidence: `if ((arg4 == 0xc8b0) && (iVar2 = func_0051BB08(arg3,g_002ce658,0xffffffff), *(int*)(g_002ce65c+arg3) == iVar2)) { func_00116C10(&self->f_1830,arg3,0xc8b0); self->f_e110 = 10; ... } self->f_e3c4 = 3;` — the explicit 51376-byte size and the hash compare with the same accessors used by 0x002CDC44 make this a load/verify path; the failure value 3 is the shared error code.

name: Fs_FormatMiniPath
signature: int Fs_FormatMiniPath(char* self, char* dst, int dstSize, const char* root, ...)
summary: Formats the 'mini' variant asset path "<root>/mini_<index>" into the caller's buffer, twin of Fs_FormatDataPath with a different inline format.
evidence: NEW: the inline format "%s/mini_%d" at 0x002CE688 is passed to the same vsnprintf wrapper 0x0051BA9C, and the two formatters alternate in the handler table at 0x0072D788; the format string alone fixes the operation.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_Restore
summary: Writes the panel's current mode and cached strings back to the root object and re-binds the two panes - the restore half of the mode-change path. Walks 0x1F member slots through Party_Member accessor records.
evidence: NEW: the only direct caller is maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords, and the named callee Ui_DataPanel_CopyFromWork shows the panel data is copied; which direction is 'restore' versus 'save' is still inferred from the callee order, so maybe_.

name: std_UInt64Mod256
signature: unsigned int std_UInt64Mod256(unsigned int lo, unsigned int hi, unsigned int value)
summary: Returns `value & 0xff` after calling the 64-bit divide helper, i.e. the remainder of a division by 256 (the compiler emitted a division-by-power-of-two helper call and then kept only the low byte).
evidence: `func_00125E58(); return arg3 & 0xff;` - the arguments to the divide are lost (the call is made with whatever is in r0-r3), but the returned low byte is exactly the remainder modulo 256, the usual shape of a byte-extraction that the optimiser turned into a divide.

name: Ui_KyoukaiWindow_CreatePanes
summary: Builds the "win_kyoukai" window: instantiates the `win_kyoukai_icon` layout (part 0) and the `win_kyoukai_save` layout (part 1) into self+0x2CE and self+0x56, binds the icon/save text widgets from the shared text manager, splices the row list nodes into order and finally calls the widget's own vtable+0x48 to switch it to state 2.
evidence: Two string literals `win_kyoukai_icon` / `win_kyoukai_save` passed to func_001D85EC(layout owner, dest, name, index) - the standard "load BFLYT part into this widget" call; the shared text manager is the 0x98-byte singleton (guard 0x007BE33C, table 0x007BE340, vtable 0x00782A08) and its text objects are configured with 0x001C50BC / 0x001C50E0 (named maybe_Ui_Text_SetArgs); func_001235A4 = intrusive-list insert; final `(**(*arg1+0x48))(arg1, 2)` = set widget state 2.

name: maybe_Ui_KyoukaiWindow_UpdateB
summary: Per-frame update of a second win_kyoukai-class window (vtable 0x0075DF40): pumps its animator, runs the fade update, advances the key animation (Ui_AnimSequence_Update), calls the class tick at vtable+0x4C and, when the close flag is set, clears it and lazily creates/releases the shared UI object.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Ui_AnimSequence_Update confirms the key-animation half; the function still also does a lazy singleton create/clear, so it is not a pure update, and the 'B' suffix only distinguishes it from the timer-pump update 0x0030E810 of the same class. No caller, so maybe_.

name: Text_PushMessageByte
signature: void Text_PushMessageByte(TextBufferOwner* self, unsigned char value)
summary: Appends one byte to the message/command byte vector at self+0xD6C..+0xD74 (begin/cur/cap), growing through the vector's reallocate helper when full. This is the primitive every list-window row-state function uses to build its message bytecode.
evidence: Classic vector push_back shape (cur<cap -> store, cur==cap -> grow via 0x00111378); 22 callers, all message/list-window functions (the Ui_ListWindow_ShowRowState* group 0x002986xx-0x00298Exx, the shop row helpers 0x002858D8/0x00285D24 and the 0x003B3F8C-0x003B4DB4 message-window states). The vector is at +0xD6C/+0xD70/+0xD74, i.e. a byte buffer separate from the row array at +0xD84.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetLeader
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetLeader(UiMessageWindow* self, unsigned int leaderId, unsigned char kind, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Selects the speaking character / message leader for the window: stores the id at +0x138, registers it with the message manager (0x00248D34 with the window's message handler +0x11C) and enables the leader pane (+0xB38).
evidence: Stores self->f_138 = arg2 and calls func_00248D34(&self->f_13C, arg2, self->f_11C, &byteRecord) then func_0029126C(&self->f_B38, 1) (Ui widget show/enable). Callers are the 0x003B3xxx message-window state functions and Ui_ListWindow_ShowRowState08 (0x00298708), which passes self->f_EF0 as the leader id.

name: Text_PushMessageFlags
summary: Appends the control bytes that correspond to a message-flag record: byte 5 set -> 0xB (and stop), otherwise byte 1 -> 0xC, byte 2 -> 0xD, byte 3 -> 0xE, byte 4 -> 0xF.
evidence: Six callers, all in the message/list-window bytecode builders (0x002858D8, 0x00298934, 0x002CEDB0, 0x003B42A8, 0x003B4DB4); the body is a pure switch over bytes 1..5 of the passed record calling Text_PushMessageByte with 0xB..0xF.

name: Ui_ListWindow_ShowRowState10WithFlags
summary: Appends message byte 0x0A followed by the flag-driven bytes of the row record, then runs the shared show-row tail. Recovered entry point that takes the window via a pointer-to-window (arg1+4).
evidence: Body: Text_PushMessageByte(*(arg1+4), 10); Text_PushMessageFlags(*(arg1+4), *(arg1+4)+0x14C); then exactly the shared show-row block of Ui_ListWindow_ShowRowState* (row index +0xD6C, row array +0xD84, maybe_Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord 0x001C5924).

name: Ui_ListWindow_ShowCurrentRow
summary: The shared show-row tail: takes the row record at (self+0xD84, index self+0xD6C, 8-byte entries), applies the row height/style byte when < 0x21, and calls maybe_Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord (0x001C5924) with the assembled record.
evidence: No byte push of its own (unlike the ShowRowState* wrappers) and five callers that build message bytes first (0x00298934, 0x002CEF08, 0x003B42A8, 0x003B4DB4) or supply their own state byte; the identical tail appears in 0x002858D8 and all 0x00298xxx helpers, so this is the common worker.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateFrame
summary: Per-frame refresh of a message-style window: notifies the layout child, runs Ui_MessageText_Update, resolves the pending text id f_131 through the text-sequence manager into f_134 and starts the fade/row transition when f_D6C and f_D70 differ.
evidence: Callee Ui_MessageText_Update is named, but the window class and the fade meaning remain inferred; kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_NotifyComplete
summary: Marks the save operation complete: sets flag +0x12F, optionally runs the completion branch that writes a buffer through 0x0011FE8C/0x0011CFAC, copies the result byte +0x138 into game work +0x2D545 and shows the sub-object at +0xB38.
evidence: Body is damaged: a bad-instruction path truncates it (halt_baddata at 0x002CF1xx), so only two stores and the final Gfx_Node_SetVisible survive. The +0x2D545 result write and the N_082 save-work label still point at save completion, but the name and the class cannot be raised above a low-confidence maybe_.

name: Ui_ListWindow_CtorBase
signature: void Ui_ListWindow_CtorBase(UiListWindow* self, unsigned int* params, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Base constructor of the list window: installs vtable 0x007602E0, copies the 4-word parameter block (+0x11C..+0x128), clears the selection/scroll fields to 0/0xFF, initialises the message manager member at +0x13C and constructs the 3 x 0x330-byte page widgets.
evidence: Called by Ui_ListWindow_Ctor (0x00298F54) and the two other list-window ctors (0x0030F590, 0x003B460C/0x003B52A4); installs vtable 0x007602E0 (same class as 0x0075DF30 - the ShowRowState* owners), and the 0xFF initialisers at +0x12D/+0x12E match the row-selection fields read by Ui_ListWindow_ShowCurrentRow.

name: Ui_Drawable_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the base 2D drawable widget: runs the non-deleting destructor and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: row 0x007602E4 has the confident Ui_Drawable_Dtor at slot 0 and the ToD/transfer virtual at +8 in the same table, so both the class and the deleting-destructor role are now pinned by named code.

name: Ui_Drawable_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the base 2D drawable widget: tears the widget tree down in reverse member order (the 0xD88 refcounted block, the 0x3C intrusive list, three list heads, the 0x54/0x84 list nodes, three 0x50 containers, the 0x330 container array, the 0xD30 reference and the 0x148 sub-object at 0x001D8C2C).
evidence: Shares vtable 0x0075C248 with the already-named Ui_Drawable_DtorDelete (0x002CF634) and with Ui_Drawable_ReleaseMembers (0x002CF9BE), i.e. the same class family, and 0x0030FF0C ends by calling it on the base at -0xE78.

name: Ui_PageList_StepSelectionDown
summary: Moves the paged list's selection down by one and notifies the owner: calls Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects(self+0x54, 0) - which maps 0 to a -1 step - and then the owner's +0x6C slot with the stored index at self+0x64.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects decodes its second argument as a direction (delta == 0 -> -1, otherwise +1) and moves the row index, so the Down/Up split of the first pass is verified; only the 'Counter' wording was wrong - the function steps the selection, not a counter. The class comes from the three vtable rows next to Ui_RowListWindow_LoadPage.

name: Ui_PageList_StepSelectionUp
summary: Upward twin of 0x002CF838: passes 1 (a +1 step) to Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects and then notifies the owner's +0x6C slot with the stored index at self+0x64.
evidence: NEW: the direction argument is verified through the named Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects (delta == 0 -> -1, otherwise +1); the body is byte-identical to 0x002B1A54. Only the 'Counter' wording was wrong - it steps the selection.

name: Ui_Object_DtorThenFree_SetVtable
signature: void Ui_Object_DtorThenFree_SetVtable(unsigned int* self, unsigned int vtable)
summary: Destructor thunk that stores the given vtable and then runs the UI object destructor and the delete.
evidence: Three calls: *arg1 = arg2; 0x1A6768 (Ui_Object_DtorBase); 0x10F6CC (delete).

name: maybe_Ui_BigGrid_Teardown
summary: Flag-gated teardown of a large grid/dive-form screen: when bit 4 of self+0x3770 is clear it either pops the dive-form pane stack at self+0x134 or, for bit 1, releases the pack handles, the layout refs and the embedded UI objects (Pack_ReleaseHandle, Ui_LayoutRef_Release, Ui_Object_DtorBase, std_destroy_range) and finally destroys the object.
evidence: NEW: the old 'HandleInput' name is wrong - the body is a destructor chain (Pack_ReleaseHandle, Ui_LayoutRef_Release x3, Ui_Object_DtorBase x4, std_destroy_range, func_001D8C2C) reached only through the self+0x3770 flag bits. The decompilation is damaged (bad instruction data, overlapping instructions, halt_baddata, `iVar6->f_d88 = iVar6->f_d88 0xFFFFF000 | 0xFFFFF000`), so the name stays maybe_ at 0.3 and the 'BigGrid' part is still only the previous guess.

name: maybe_Ui_GridCursor_ApplySelection
signature: void maybe_Ui_GridCursor_ApplySelection(UiGridController* grid, int allow, u32 delta, u32* out)
summary: Applies a pending grid-cursor selection: reads the current cell/index through the controller's +0x58/+0x5C virtuals, writes the new index and cell count to the caller's output and releases the previous owner.
evidence: Body is only 110 bytes and ends in 'bad instruction data' with a partially lost output contract. The sole named caller is Ui_MemoriesWindow_HandleInput, which only says it belongs to a list/grid cursor.

name: maybe_Ui_Drawable_ReleaseMembers
summary: Member-release half of the drawable widget teardown: releases the 0xD88 reference, the 0x3C list, the list heads and nodes, the 0x50 containers, the 0x330 container array, the 0xD30 reference and the 0x148 sub-object.
evidence: Body is a damaged Thumb decompilation (unaff_r4/r5/r7, dropped argument registers, one removed unreachable block); the exact member set cannot be confirmed even though the tail duplicates 0x002CF644.

name: Ui_Object_CtorSmallB
summary: Second minimal UI object constructor: Ui_Object_CtorBase, install its own vtable and clear the two trailing owner/child words. Same shape as 0x002B1E0C, different vtable.
evidence: Body identical to Ui_Object_CtorSmall (0x002B1E0C): Ui_Object_CtorBase (0x001A66A0), vtable g_002CFAEC, then [0x13]=0 and [0x14]=0. Eight callers, all UI ctors (0x002AC7EC, 0x0041D760, 0x0045F59C, 0x00465978, 0x004782F8, 0x004CE908, 0x004FA5EC).

name: Ui_Object_DtorThenFree_NoVtable
summary: Destructor thunk that runs the UI object destructor and the delete without changing the vtable.
evidence: Two calls: 0x1A6768 (Ui_Object_DtorBase); 0x10F6CC (delete).

name: maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceChildAndSetCharacter
summary: Window virtual that advances the active child page (self+4 +0x748), pushes the pane pair at +0x13C/+0xBFC with the shared layout descriptor, then applies the page's current member id to the status panel at +0xB5C.
evidence: The body is byte-identical to 0x003F0CEC, which is vtable slot 0 of UiJumonWindow (0x76B9B4) and is now confirmed under that class; this copy has no caller or vtable owner, so the effect is clear but the owning class is not - kept maybe_ with the neutral window name.

name: maybe_Ui_Text_FitLineWidth
summary: One copy of the shared member-row update block: resolve the party members at self+0x0A and glyphId, resolve the spell record at self+0x09, and when the member record carries flags 0x0C clamp member+0x16 by the spell record's +0x2EC and re-apply the two row colours; otherwise start transition 0x45/0x47. Ghidra truncates the clamped path with halt_baddata().
evidence: NEW: this is the fourth copy of the block found in 0x002D04EC/0x00381ED8/0x003F0D54 (same func_0035EB98 + 0x0018C184/0x0018C1B8 + Ui_ApplyTextColor pair). The function never measures a text run itself, so 'FitLineWidth' is only the previous author's reading of the clamped value; because that value could equally be a spell cost (the resolver's +0x2EC) and the body ends in halt_baddata, the name stays maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Ui_MessageVoice_SelectBlipPattern
signature: void** Ui_MessageVoice_SelectBlipPattern(int lineIndex, int hasLongRun, void** outDesc)
summary: Selects one of five static message-voice typing-blip pattern descriptors (0x00773DE0..0x00773E10, 0x0076E29C) using weighted random choice based on lineIndex and hasLongRun, writes it to *outDesc, and returns outDesc.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x2CFCC0..0x2CFDC4: takes 3 args (r0=lineIndex, r1=hasLongRun, r2=outDesc), rolls Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng with weights (50,30,20) when hasLongRun!=0 or (70,30,0) when lineIndex>=2, writes descriptor pointer to *r2, returns r2. All 9 callers are Ui_MessageVoice_UpdateLine0..4 and FinishLine0..3 storing result into voice->f_18.

name: maybe_Ui_Sequence_AdvanceTimedStep
signature: unsigned int maybe_Ui_Sequence_AdvanceTimedStep(void* self, int* ctx)
summary: Timed UI sequence step: increments the frame counter at +0x10, plays an SE at steps 0 and 0x49 through Sound_PlaySeCached, and reports done when the sub-object at (*ctx+0xC)+0x1540 has no value or its float at +0x24 equals the constant at 0x00645828.
evidence: CORRECTED: nothing in the body touches a text id — the old 'UpdateTextIdProgression' was unsupported. NEW: only Sound_PlaySeCached is named, and the frame-counter + two SE cues + float completion test describe a timed sequence step whose owner is unknown, so maybe_ 0.35.

name: Ui_DigitRoll_Update
summary: Animates a five-digit rolling counter: plays an SE at step 0 and step 10, scrolls each of the five digit sprites according to the counter and reports completion after 0x2E steps.
evidence: NEW: the loop indexes exactly five digit sprites (0x3942A8(ctx->0xC, i)) and converts a counter-derived value to a float scroll offset, so the digit-roll reading is supported by the arithmetic itself; the SE helper is named.

name: Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerA
signature: void Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerA(UiWidget* self, void* record, void* loader)
summary: Layout-load fix-up: marks loader+0x60C with the pointer being patched, resolves the stored offset through the widget's relocation table and writes the pointer back before clearing the marker.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x002D00AC occupies the immediately preceding row 0x00760498 of the same widget/layout vtable, and both use the 0x60C marker protocol; the operation is fully visible in the body. The twin keeps the 'B' suffix.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_PlayOutcomeAnim
summary: Plays the outcome animation of the smith mini-game: maps outcome 0..3 to the layout panes txt_charge / txt_seikou / txt_daiseikou / txt_shippai, stops the previous animation, starts the named animation through Ui_PlayAnimByName and applies the animation speed via slot +0x54.
evidence: Wording fixed: the function starts a pane animation (Ui_PlayAnimByName) rather than text. The body is damaged (unaff_ registers), so the verdict rests on the disassembly: the four inline pane names at 0x002D0064/0x002D0074/0x002D0080/0x002D009C are passed to Ui_PlayAnimByName (0x53D604) with (self+0x98, name, 0, 1), and those names exist in game_assets/layouts/.../menu_kaji2_text_3d_txt_*.bflan.json, which also confirms the blacksmith menu.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateChargeSlotList
summary: Walks a list of 0x0B-stride timer/effect slots and calls the per-slot updater 0x001EE8B4 on every entry.
evidence: Unchanged and still weak: 0x002D004C is 2 bytes inside the Thumb function that starts at 0x002CFFDC, and the recovered loop depends on unaff_r4/r5/r9, so the body is not trustworthy. The smith-menu attribution is inherited from the earlier disassembly pass and nothing in the call graph (no callers, no named callees) supports it.

name: Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerB
signature: void Ui_Widget_RelocateRecordPointerB(UiWidget* self, void* record, void* loader)
summary: Second emitted copy of the layout-record pointer relocation helper: marks loader+0x60C, re-bases the offset through the widget's table and stores the pointer back.
evidence: NEW: no readable .c exists for this address (the batch path is the function index, so no body can be read - not a damaged decompilation), but it is the vtable row 0x00760498 immediately before the now-confirmed 0x002CFF9C (row 0x0076049C), and that file's header states the two instruction streams are byte-identical. Hence 0.50 and the 'B' suffix.

name: Ui_DigitRoll_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the number-rolling widget: allocates through the UI base constructor 0x001D8B6C, installs vtable 0x00760480 and clears the id word at +0x11C.
evidence: It installs vtable 0x00760480, whose slot +4 is the confident Ui_DigitRoll_DeletingDtor (0x002D010C) and whose own methods are the 0x002CFE5C..0x002D00AC block (Ui_DigitRoll_Update). The twin 0x002C31E0 installs a *different* vtable (0x0076007C), so 'Gfx_Drawable2D' was the wrong family. The caller Ui_FieldScreen_Init creates the field-screen digit roll.

name: Ui_DigitRoll_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the number-rolling widget: runs the shared base destructor and then operator delete.
evidence: Two-instruction deleting-destructor template plus vtable row 0x00760484 sitting directly next to maybe_Ui_DigitRoll_Update (0x002CFE5C), which fixes the class.

name: maybe_Ui_GetTableByteByChild
summary: Returns one byte from a two-word static table at 0x0072B09C, selected by the child index stored in self->f_38->f_C and by the flag self->f_BC.
evidence: Unchanged: the only caller is maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_HandleInputB and the table 0x0072B09C is still unnamed, so the returned byte could be a style, a column or a flag. The body is intact, but nothing in the new names narrows what the byte means.

name: maybe_Ui_SetWidgetEnabled
summary: Widget state vtable slot: when the widget is still uninitialised (+0x14 clear) and the new state is non-zero it raises the UI core's mode word at +0x94, then forwards the flag to the object's state setter.
evidence: Both callers (Ui_DiveWindow_InitPanes, Ui_DiveWindow_ResetSelection) pass a boolean-like flag through this slot, but the tail-called setter 0x0029126C is inside a Ghidra-split function and unnamed, so 'enabled' vs 'visible' is still unverified.

name: Ui_NumberRoll_Update
summary: Drives a slot-machine style digit roll: waits until the digit strings have been laid out, then increments the counter byte group by group with decimal carry (a '9' becomes '0' and carries into the next group), switches between the two panes depending on func_0062A2FC and finally loads the two digit glyph pairs (0x0c/0x0e) into the panes.
evidence: Loop `(**(*arg1+0x34))(arg1,&local_38,digit|page<<16,0)` and `(+0x38)` for the label, then explicit decimal carry code over three 4-byte digit groups (local_34/local_32, local_28/local_2c) on the bytes at local_34/local_32 and local_28 (`'9'` → `'0'` + carry); after `uVar5 > 2` it binds `func_003E00CC(arg1+0x28, ..., s_select3_002d04a8,0)` / `s_select2_002d04b0`, tests `func_0062A2FC(root+0x24a98,1)` and finishes with `func_006406D0(uVar2,0xc)` / `(...,0xe)` passed to `func_001A6680` (set text).

name: Ui_Panel_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a small panel object owning two 0x50-byte panes: installs the vtable, destroys the panes at +0x4C and +0x9C (0x50 apart), destroys the list and frees.
evidence: Mechanism-only name: the body is the generated two-pane teardown (Ui_LayoutRef_Release x2 / Ui_Object_DtorBase / func_0010F6CC) that 0x002C1B9C repeats without the free; no game class is claimed.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplyRowColorState
summary: Applies one menu row's state: queries the overlay cursor-row state (1, 2 or 3), and for each state performs the same row update - resolve the party member at self+0x0A and the skill record at self+0x08, clamp member+0x16 by the record's cost (+0xEE), then push the two row colours (Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt / Ui_ApplyTextColor on pane+0x68C) and start transition 0x2A with tail 0x32/0x33/0x34. With state 0 it runs 0x37/0xFF instead.
evidence: NEW: the three branches are byte-identical apart from the transition id, and the state query is the named maybe_Ui_Overlay_GetCursorRowState, so 'apply the row's colour state' is supported. What member+0x16 / +0x12 and the resolved record's +0xEE actually are (UI width vs MP cost) is still unclear, so it stays maybe_ at 0.42 rather than 0.5.

name: Anim_Clip_ConvertTracks
signature: void Anim_Clip_ConvertTracks(AnimTrack* out, AnimSource* src, void* base, AnimTrack* trackBase, void* stepBase, void* step2Base, int* owner)
summary: Converts one animation track: fills the 0x58-byte output record (source pointer, base/linked track, 6-word keyframe header, 0x14/0x4C step arrays) and, when the owner has a table, resolves the 4-byte step entries through the script int table (0x00193F54) and appends them to the step list.
evidence: Only callers are Anim_Clip_Build (0x0029DE10) and its Thumb loop twin (0x0029E4C6); the record sizes (0x58 track, 0x44 source, 0x4C and 0x14 step) match exactly those functions' allocation arithmetic, and it resolves the per-step value with Script_GetIntTable1 (0x00193F54) using owner+0x40.

name: Ui_SpriteTree_SetRenderMode
summary: Applies a render mode to every sprite in a sprite tree: mode 0 detaches each sprite from its layer, other modes attach it to the layer stored in the entry.
evidence: Iterates self->f_14 entries of 0x14 bytes at *(self+8); writes the mode into entry+0x10 and calls Ui_Sprite_DetachFromLayer (0x0029F2A8) for 0 or Ui_Sprite_AttachToLayer (0x0029F34C) otherwise; caller maybe_Ui_SpriteTree_ApplyLayout (0x0029EF64).

name: Ui_SpriteTree_UpdateLayerAssignments
signature: void Ui_SpriteTree_UpdateLayerAssignments(UiSpriteTree* self, u32 requestedLayer, u8 blend)
summary: Re-assigns every sprite in the tree to a layer, promoting sprites whose source object requests a special blend mode (object+0x50 == 1 or 2) to layer 2, and stores the blend byte for the renderer.
evidence: Entry stride 0x14; reads source object at entry+4 and its +0x50; calls Ui_Sprite_DetachFromLayer/Ui_Sprite_AttachToLayer only when the cached (layer, blend) pair differs; writes entry+0x0F (layer) and entry+0x0E (blend); caller maybe_Ui_SpriteTree_ApplyLayout (0x0029EF64).

name: Anim_SpriteList_SetMode
signature: void Anim_SpriteList_SetMode(int self, unsigned int mode, unsigned char flags)
summary: Applies a playback mode to every sprite-animation entry: resets the 0x58-byte entries, then restarts or reconfigures each 0x14-byte slot through func_0029F34C (mode 0 is promoted to 2 for special entries).
evidence: Iterates self->f_10 entries of 0x58 bytes and self->f_14 slots of 0x14 bytes; calls func_0029F34C and reads per-entry flag byte at +0x50.

name: Anim_SpriteList_Clear
summary: Destroys every 0x58-byte sprite-animation entry in the list (calls the per-entry destructor).
evidence: Loop over self->f_10 calling func_001EE8B4 on *(self+4)+i*0x58.

name: Ui_SpriteList_ApplyFrame
signature: void Ui_SpriteList_ApplyFrame(void* self, int frame, unsigned int arg3)
summary: Applies a frame/argument pair to every sprite in the list (count at +0x14, array at +8, stride 0x14) through Ui_Sprite_BuildQuadFromFrame.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Ui_Sprite_BuildQuadFromFrame, called once per listed sprite with the frame payload at +4, so this is exactly the 'apply this frame to all sprites' helper.

name: Anim_ClipSet_Build
signature: void Anim_ClipSet_Build(AnimClipSet* self, AnimAllocator* alloc, AnimResource* res, unsigned char layer)
summary: Builds the runtime clip set for a resource: allocates res->f_24 clip entries of 0x7C bytes and fills each with Anim_Clip_Build, copying the layer byte into each clip's +0x72 and finally sorting them (0x0029E3B0).
evidence: Allocates i*0x7C+8 with Mem_AllocAligned and calls func_0029DE10 (Anim_Clip_Build) per entry with func_003B37D4(res,i) as the source; callers 0x002D15B4 and 0x002D19F4 are the clip-set play/refresh functions. 0x0029E3B0 then builds the sorted index at self+0x28/self+0x2A.

name: Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams
signature: void Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams(UiSpriteParams* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Copies a compact sprite/text parameter block onto the live render node at self+0x0C (scale, size, character code, colours, blend flags) and then applies the sprite-tree layout so the change becomes visible.
evidence: Writes node fields +0x60/+0x77, +0x6D, +0x73, +0x75, +0x78, +0x7A and calls 0x0029E740 (size), 0x0029EF00 (char code), 0x0029E504 (colour), maybe_Ui_SpriteTree_ApplyLayout (0x0029EF64); caller 0x002D1D34.

name: Anim_Instance_Update
summary: Updates the widget's active animation instance: advances the clip and then re-applies the layout animation to the linked panes.
evidence: If self->f_c != 0 calls FUN_0029E74C then func_0029EC8C(self->f_c, &self->f_24, &self->f_26).

name: Anim_ClipSet_Release
summary: Releases the clip array allocated by Anim_ClipSet_Build (operator delete[] at +8, clear the clip count).
evidence: Calls std_operator_delete_array (0x00100BCC) on *(arg1+8) with the shared heap tag g_002D0FC0, sets +8 = 0 and +0x10 = 0; callers 0x002D15B4 (replacing a clip set) and 0x002D1EA0 (teardown).

name: Anim_ClipSet_PlayById
summary: Starts the animation clip with the given id: walks the clip array from the end, and on a match makes it the active clip, copies its settings, starts it, applies the blend offset and mode, and finally stops every other clip in the set.
evidence: `for (iVar1 = self->f_10 - 1; iVar1 >= 0; iVar1--) { iVar2 = func_0029E59C(*(int*)(self+8) + iVar1*0x7c, arg2); if (iVar2) { self->f_c = ...; ->f_68 = self->f_1c; func_0029E74C(...); func_0029E388(...,(int)self->f_32); func_0029EC8C(...); for (all j != i) { func_0029E388(clip,0); func_0029E6CC(clip); } return 1; } }` — 0x7c-byte clips, 0x29E74C = maybe_Anim_Clip_SpawnAndApply. Callers 0x002D11F4/0x002D1264/0x002D15B4.

name: Anim_Instance_Dtor
summary: Destructor of an animation instance: installs the class vtable, deletes the owned array at +8 through std_operator_delete_array and clears its slot fields.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named std_operator_delete_array and the vtable symbol g_animInstanceVtable is installed first, so the deleting-destructor reading is solid.

name: Anim_PlayByIdForActor
signature: u32 Anim_PlayByIdForActor(Actor* self, int clipId, int force)
summary: Plays a named animation clip on an actor after checking that its model is ready and not hidden; also updates the actor's animation-blend target so the transition is smooth.
evidence: `self->f_b8` virtual +0xc must return non-zero, `f_b8->f_f8 != 0` and `f_b8->f_138 == 0`; if the clip already matches (`func_0010540C(func_0063C774(), arg2) == 0 && arg3 == 0`) it returns 0; otherwise `func_002D0FC4(&iVar1->f_fc,arg2)` and `func_00460138(&iVar1->f_158, iVar1->f_108->f_44)`. Called by Actor2DChangeAnim (0x00153E6C) plus ten other actor/effect initialisers.

name: Anim_PlayById
signature: u32 Anim_PlayById(AnimOwner* self, u32 clipId, int force)
summary: Play helper without the actor-state checks: skips the request when the clip is already current and `force` is 0, otherwise activates it through the clip set and retargets the blend.
evidence: Identical core to 0x002D11F4 (`func_002D0FC4(&self->f_fc,arg2)` + `func_00460138(&self->f_158,self->f_108->f_44)`) but without the `self->f_b8` virtual/`f_f8`/`f_138` guards; the current-clip early-out uses the same `func_0010540C(func_0063C774(),arg2)`.

name: Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate
signature: void Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate(int* self, void* params, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Resets an animation instance (vtable slot 0x10) and copies the large default parameter template g_002D150C into it, overriding selected fields from the caller's parameter block.
evidence: The reset-then-copy-template sequence is explicit and named callers are animation/sprite setup paths (Actor2D_CreateWithAnimInstanceA/B, Field_Actor_InitModelFromRecord, Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance).

name: maybe_Thunk_StateSequenceChangeStateA
summary: Two-instruction trampoline (push {r4,lr}; bl 0x006C8108; pop {r4,pc}) that forwards its three arguments unchanged to the state-sequence transition dispatcher 0x006C8108.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x006C8108 is now readable from the disassembly - it reads the current state index at self+4 (must be < 3), indexes a 3x4 table of {handler, offset} pairs at self+0x34 with the requested new state, resolves the handler against the vtable at self+0x20 when the offset has bit 0 set, and tail-calls it. That is the ChangeState dispatcher of the 3-state sequence class whose tick is std_StateSequence64_Tick (0x006C80BC), so the thunk is a ChangeState forwarder. The three callers (Field_AltarObj_SyncAnimation, Field_Actor_Resume, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateSubObject) place it in the field-actor animation path. The old batch name maybe_Anim_StateDispatch_ThunkA was not supported by anything.

name: Anim_ClipSet_PlayByName
signature: void Anim_ClipSet_PlayByName(AnimClipSet* self, AnimResource* res, AnimPlayRequest* req)
summary: Switches the clip set to another animation: resolves the requested clip id, assigns it to the model (0x003B3650), releases the previous clip set, builds a new one for the resource and plays the requested clip by name or by id (Anim_ClipSet_PlayById), then fills the event fields.
evidence: Calls Anim_ClipSet_Build (0x002D0D20), Anim_ClipSet_Release (0x002D0F94), Anim_ClipSet_PlayById (0x002D0FC4) and the model resolver 0x003B3650; reads the request's clip id from +2/+5/+8 and builds a name buffer via 0x0011142C/0x0011CCA0 when the request carries a string.

name: maybe_Thunk_StateSequenceChangeStateB
summary: Two-instruction trampoline (push {r4,lr}; bl 0x006C8108; pop {r4,pc}) that forwards its three arguments unchanged to the state-sequence transition dispatcher 0x006C8108; same body as 0x002D1588 and 0x002D1F1C.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x006C8108 is the ChangeState dispatcher of the 3-state sequence class (disassembly: current state at self+4 must be < 3, new state indexes a 3x4 {handler, offset} table at self+0x34, handler resolved against the vtable at self+0x20 and tail-called), so the thunk is a ChangeState forwarder rather than an anonymous call. It has 11 callers, all still unnamed, so which class it belongs to stays open - hence maybe_ and the B suffix.

name: Actor_ClassifyDirection4
summary: Classifies a 2D direction delta into four facing sectors (0, 2, 4, 6 = north/east/south/west as used by the 8-way direction set), based on the angle against the reference forward vector and the sign of the cross product.
evidence: dot with -g_002d18c4 (reference forward) compared against the sector limits g_002d18c8/CC/D0; cross product `ref[2]*x - ref[0]*z` picks left/right; angle via 0x00672A14 (acos). Callers Actor2DTurnTarget (0x00153F74) and Actor2DTurnLocator (0x00155728) confirm the facing use.

name: Actor_ClassifyDirection8
summary: Classifies a direction delta into the 8-way facing set (0..7, even = axis aligned, odd = diagonal) by comparing the angle against the reference forward vector with four thresholds and the sign of the cross product for left/right.
evidence: Same structure as 0x002D183C with an extra 0x22.5/0x67.5 degree band (g_002d19b8..c4); 7 callers, all facing/rotation code (Actor2DTurnTarget, Actor2DTurnLocator, 0x00238F48, 0x002399D4, 0x00239D58, 0x0023B2F0, 0x002B5994).

name: Anim_Owner_Tick
summary: Per-frame animation update of an object that owns one animation instance: if a pending transition is set at +0x108 it snaps the player to that frame first, then advances the embedded anim instance at +0xFC.
evidence: Both calls are now named - maybe_Anim_Player_SetFrame on the pending transition and Anim_Instance_Update on the embedded instance - which is exactly 'apply the pending frame, then tick the instance'; only the owning class is generic.

name: Anim_ClipSet_Refresh
summary: Rebuilds the clip set from the current resource when the resource changed (0x003B3650 returns true), then plays the default layer clip and notifies the parent with event 1.
evidence: Calls Anim_ClipSet_Build (0x002D0D20) with the current resource self->f_134, Anim_ClipSet_PlayById-like 0x002D0E5C with the per-object layer byte, then sets self->f_F8 = 1 and posts event 1 through the parent handler at self+0x3C. Called by 0x002D1C98 after a pending request becomes ready.

name: Anim_Instance_Tick
summary: Single-step animation tick: runs the instance update and unconditionally reports success (returns 1).
evidence: Calls FUN_002D0F4C and returns 1; used as a vtable/task callback.

name: Anim_Resource_Bind
signature: int Anim_Resource_Bind(int self, unsigned int* desc, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Binds (or re-uses) the widget's 2D model resource: returns 0 when the same id and alpha are already bound, otherwise destroys the old instance, allocates a 0x6C replacement, loads it through Ui_2dModel_Load and stores the new id/colour block.
evidence: NEW: the loader is the named Ui_2dModel_Load and the allocator Mem_AllocAligned_2, and the reuse test compares the descriptor's id/alpha with the bound slot - all three behaviours are visible in the body.

name: Anim_BindWithDefaultContext
summary: Builds a default 0x30-byte bind context through 0x0011FFD8, zeroes its three trailing fields and passes it to Anim_Resource_Bind. The callers are the actor model rebuild paths, which want the default binding rather than a caller-supplied context.
evidence: The body is fully visible and never reads a context from anywhere: it constructs one with 0x0011FFD8, zeroes local_28/uStack_24/uStack_20 and calls the now-named Anim_Resource_Bind. 'BindFromContext' described the opposite of what happens. The callers Actor_RebuildCharacterModel and maybe_Actor_ApplyModelPartsB both want a fresh default binding.

name: Anim_ClipSet_ApplyPending
summary: When a clip request is pending (self+0x138) and its resource is loaded (0x006488D0), applies it through Anim_ClipSet_PlayByName, resets the request fields and then updates the owner (0x004602B0). Always returns 1.
evidence: Body: if (f_138 && func_006488D0()) { Anim_ClipSet_PlayByName(self, f_138, &self->f_13C); ...clear f_138..f_14C... } func_004602B0(&self->f_158); return 1. The cleared 8-byte request record at +0x13C is the same one Anim_PlayRequest uses in 0x002D15B4.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_UpdateAndReportDone
summary: 16-byte wrapper: runs the pending-dispatch helper 0x0046011C on the object and then returns 1 ('handled'). 0x0046011C itself only does anything when self+0xC is non-zero, in which case it tail-calls 0x0046015C(self, 1, 0).
evidence: Unchanged: the disassembly confirms the whole body is `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x46011c; mov r0,#1; pop {r4,pc}`, and 0x0046011C is a two-branch stub (`ldr r1,[r0,#0xc]; cmp r1,#0; beq return; mov r2,#0; mov r1,#1; b 0x46015c`). No caller, no rodata reference and no named callee, so both the 'screen' owner and the 'done' wording remain guesses.

name: Ui_Sprite_UpdateFromLayout

signature: void Ui_Object_DtorThenFreeEx(unsigned int* self, unsigned int vtable)
summary: Destructor thunk for a UI object with an embedded sub-object at +0x4C: stores the given vtable, destroys the sub-object and frees the memory.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2; 0x3A6E70(arg1+0x13) returns the sub-object base and 0x1A6768 (Ui_Object_DtorBase) is run on base-0x4C, then 0x10F6CC (delete).

name: maybe_Container_SortRangeByKind
summary: Jump-table dispatcher over nine tiny stubs: each stub loads the begin/end pointer pair from self+0/+4 and sorts that 16-byte-element range with a fixed comparator - cases 0..2 pass a comparator function pointer to 0x7230BC, cases 3..8 pass comparator index 0..5 to 0x722EDC.
evidence: CORRECTED: the old 'Ui_Widget_DelegateTrampolines' name is wrong. The disassembly shows `push {r4,lr}; ldrlo pc,[pc,r1,lsl#2]` - a switch on r1 with nine cases - and every case is `ldrd r0,r1,[r0]; mov r2,#k; bl 0x722EDC/0x7230BC; pop {r4,pc}`. Both targets are 16-byte introsort entry points (`cmp r0,r1; bxeq lr; sub r5,r1,r0; asr r2,r5,#4; bl 0x7186E0`), which is why the call graph lists them as std_sort_16B_alt and std_merge_sort_with_buffer. So the block sorts a container range with a selectable comparator, not UI widget delegates. Which container it is stays open, hence maybe_.

name: Container_Vector16_PushRecord
summary: Appends a 16-byte record to a vector of 16-byte elements: builds the default record (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFF, 0x10000, 0xFF...), copies 0xD bytes from the argument over it, then stores it at the write pointer or inserts it via std_vector16_insert.
evidence: Element size 0x10, begin/cur/cap at +4/+8/+0xC and the grow path calling std_vector16_insert (0x0070E494); the default record fields (id -1, 0xFFFF, 0x10000, 0xFF) are the 'empty slot' pattern used by the 0x10-byte UI records elsewhere. Recovered entry point.

name: Ui_ListData_BuildEntries
signature: void Ui_ListData_BuildEntries(UiListData* list, int mode, int limit, int arg4)
summary: Builds the entry list shown by the multi-purpose list window: mode 0 collects the character/actor rows (0x8c-byte records at root+0x24a98), mode 1 the item rows (0x98-byte records at root+0x6b8), 2 both, 3 the third table (f_7bb6/f_7bc0), 4 the fourth and 5 a mixed set; each entry is four words (index, packed id/size, packed flags, kind).
evidence: `func_0066B11C(root+0x24a98)` gives the row count, records at `root+0x24a98 + i*0x8c` with fields f_605e/f_6068/f_6069/f_606c and `func_0066AD94/0x66AF34` for the two sub-ids; the item table is `root+0x6b8` with 0x98-byte records (f_7a, f_90) bounded by `func_006290A8`; entries are appended either in place (`arg1[1] = piVar3+4`) or through `func_0070E494` (vector grow). Called by Ui_DiveManager_Ctor, 0x002FEBB0, 0x00307380, 0x00308A40 and 0x0029AF80.

name: Script_DispatchStateCallback
summary: Dispatches a stored script callback according to the state byte at site+0x11C: states 0..3 call the fixed native function pointers 0x001492BC / 0x00149204 / 0x00147DC4 / 0x00154BE8 through 0x007230BC, and states 4..9 forward to the VM's indexed native call 0x00722FCC with index 0..5.
evidence: The four literal words 0x001492BC, 0x00149204, 0x00147DC4, 0x00154BE8 are all in the 0x0014xxxx Squirrel-native thunk area (0x00147D94 ClearStatus / 0x00154C00 EndTripDoorEffect are named neighbours); 0x007230BC(vm, arg, fnptr) and 0x00722FCC(vm, arg, index) are the two VM call entry points, and site+0x11C is the state (0..9) selecting them. Called from 0x002D8838 and seven other UI/menu entry points.

name: Container_Vector16_EraseAt
signature: unsigned int Container_Vector16_EraseAt(Vector16* self, unsigned int index)
summary: Removes the 16-byte element at the given index from a vector of 16-byte elements (shifting the tail down with 0xD-byte copies), shrinks the size and returns the removed element's first word (-1 when the index is out of range).
evidence: Bounds check against (end-begin)>>4, element copies via 0x00116C10(...,0xD) with 0x10 stride, then end -= 0x10; the same 16-byte element layout as Container_Vector16_PushRecord (0x002D5EC0).

name: Ui_LayoutRequest_Type6
signature: void Ui_LayoutRequest_Type6(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 6 for the scene: builds the stack argument with the low byte forced to 6 and tail-calls the layout loader.
evidence: The tail call is the now-named Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type6 (0x006D9730), and the named caller Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState (0x001A04A4) dispatches it for scene layout kind 7; type byte and target agree, so the wrapper name is supported.

name: Ui_LayoutRequest_Type1
signature: void Ui_LayoutRequest_Type1(void* scene, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int b, unsigned int c)

evidence: NEW: the loader is the named Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type1 (taking the request block whose type byte is 1), and both follow-ups are named (maybe_Ui_Layout_SetCornerGradientColors, Ui_Model2D_LoadResource); its only caller is Ui_Window_OpenScene.

name: Ui_LayoutRequest_Type4
signature: void Ui_LayoutRequest_Type4(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 4 for the scene (type byte 4 in the stack argument, tail-call 0x006DDFA4).

name: Ui_ReleaseHandleBlockB
summary: Releases the eight-handle block at self+0x9E4 (four bytes apart), clearing each handle word and returning it to the handle table.
evidence: NEW: every release is the named Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry and the caller maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_Release2dCommonPack runs it with the other two blocks, so the three functions are the teardown of a scene's 2D resource handles; the name just records which block this one owns.

name: Ui_ReleaseLayoutResources
signature: void Ui_ReleaseLayoutResources(void* scene, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Releases the UI/layout resources owned by a field-scene object: frees the face-icon handle array at scene+0x3E4, clears the resource handle at +0x3E8 and forwards the scene plus resource id to Field_SceneObject_ReleaseResourceHandles. Called from Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll and from the scene-object destructor, i.e. on scene teardown.
evidence: All three callees are now confidently named (Ui_FaceIcon_FreeHandles, Res_HandleClear, Field_SceneObject_ReleaseResourceHandles) and the new named caller Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll is exactly the scene teardown path, so the resources released are the scene's UI/layout resources; the old doubting note was only because two callees used to be maybe_-named.

name: Ui_LayoutRequest_Type5
signature: void Ui_LayoutRequest_Type5(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 5 for the scene (type byte 5, tail-call 0x006E0B28).
evidence: The tail call is the now-named Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type5, and the named caller Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState (0x001A04A4) dispatches it for scene layout kind 1; type byte and loader target agree.

name: Ui_ReleaseHandleBlockC
summary: Releases the large handle block at self+0x834 (the 0x834..0x9E0 run of alternating mark/handle words), clearing each handle and returning it to the handle table.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry and the block is released by the same caller as blocks A and B; the unrolled sequence covers +0x834..+0x9E0 with a few out-of-order fields, which is why the name says 'block' rather than naming each handle.

name: Ui_ReleaseHandleBlockA
summary: Releases the handle block at self+0x784 (0x784..0x830), clearing each handle word and returning it to the handle table.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry and the header's caller (maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_Release2dCommonPack) releases A, B and C together, so the three names are consistent as a set.

name: Ui_LookupMapValueById
signature: unsigned short Ui_LookupMapValueById(void* self, unsigned int key, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int b, int direct)

name: Ui_ListWindow_InitRows
summary: Builds a simple N-row text list using the placeholder pane name null_txt_l1, with the usual incrementing row labels.

name: Ui_Object_DtorThenFree_Variant2

name: maybe_GameMode_IsPlayable
summary: Returns true unless the shared global mode value from 0x00664A80 is 8 or 0xFF, i.e. unless the game is in one of the two loading/transition modes.

name: maybe_Field2D_IsRenderMode400
summary: Returns 1 when the Field2D manager's sub-object at +0x08 holds 0x400 in its +0x14 field. The three callers use the answer as a part-selector / layout switch, so it is a mode test, not a renderer profile.
evidence: FACTS.md identifies (work+8)->f_88 as the Field2D manager, so the object being tested is Field2D and not a Gfx render context; the first-pass 'Gfx' prefix is therefore wrong. The +0x14 field is still only known by its value 0x400, and the named callers (Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup, ActorPart_GetPartIds, maybe_ActorFace_GetExpressionIds) use the answer as a part selector, so the mode meaning stays inferred and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ProbeAdjacentCell
signature: void maybe_Ui_Overlay_ProbeAdjacentCell(u8* self, u32 slot, int* offset)
summary: Builds a small cell descriptor (2/2/2/1 from g_002D7AE4) from the target widget position (core+0x54+0x20, f_78/f_7C) and probes one neighbouring cell: left by 2 + width when offset[0] < 0, right by 2 when offset[0] > 0, or one row up/down when only offset[1] is set, always through Field_Placement_TestAreaC.
evidence: The caller is the equally hypothetical maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateSlotVisibility and the probe goes through the named Field_Placement_TestAreaC, which fixes the 'probe a cell' reading but not that the caller is an overlay.

name: Map_QueryCellRecord
signature: void Map_QueryCellRecord(u32 * out, u32 x, u32 y, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves one map cell by (x,y) and writes {y, cell pointer, record pointer} into the caller's triple, requiring the cell to be walkable (flag +0x38 == 1) and populated (+0x20 > 0); on failure it writes the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel triple.
evidence: The lookup chain is shared verbatim with 0x002D7DDC and 0x002D7F20 (which are now confirmed as the directional cell searches) and its caller Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode reads exactly the cell/record pair this writes, so the 'query the cell record' reading holds.

name: Map_IsCellSolid
signature: unsigned char Map_IsCellSolid(u32 x, u32 y, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns 1 when the map cell at (x,y) exists and its state byte at +0x38 equals 1 - the 2D field's 'static/solid chip' test; missing layer or cell returns 0.
evidence: NEW: the lookup chain is the same func_0062F0E0 -> func_0062C388 -> func_0062C3B0 layer/cell resolver used by the named Field2D_MapChip_CanWalkDirection, and the callers 0x5F41AC/0x5F491A are field scene-object update paths - so the cell-state test is as named.

name: maybe_Map_FindCellInArea
signature: u32 maybe_Map_FindCellInArea(u32 x, u32 y, u32* pos)
summary: Looks up the map cell at (x,y), searches its record list through maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord and then re-checks the hit with the cell hit-test; returns 1 only when the found cell's +0x38 flag is set.
evidence: The callee maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord is now named and the surrounding lookups (0x0062F0E0 map, 0x0062C388 column, 0x0062C3B0 cell) are the same ones Map_FindCellInDirection uses, so the Map attribution holds. The final gate is the cell's +0x38 byte, whose meaning is unknown, so 'InArea' remains vague and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Map_TestCellBlockedFlags
signature: u32 maybe_Map_TestCellBlockedFlags(u32 x, u32 y, u32* pos, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves the Field2D cell at (x,y) and its attribute record for pos, then returns 1 when either attribute 0x20 or 0x40 is present (the pair the trail direction finders treat as impassable).
evidence: Called from the named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode next to the direction finders and uses the same attribute helper with the same two constants; that the flags mean 'blocked' is still an inference from usage, not proven.

name: Map_FindCellInDirection
signature: void Map_FindCellInDirection(u32 * out, int cell, u32 layer, u32 arg4, int * origin, int dir)
summary: Finds the map cell next to `cell` in the requested direction: decides which edge of the cell (+0x30/+0x34 range) faces the origin, and only if that matches the sign of `dir` resolves the neighbour through the layer lookup and hit-test chain; writes {index, cell} or {0xFFFFFFFF, 0} when there is none.
evidence: The direction/edge arithmetic is self-contained and the tail now calls the named maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord and Ui_HitTestRows on the same layer object, i.e. 'resolve the neighbouring cell in this direction' - exactly what the first pass proposed.

name: Map_FindCellInDirectionEx
signature: void Map_FindCellInDirectionEx(u32 * out, u32 x, u32 y, int * origin, int dir)
summary: Coordinate form of the directional cell search: resolves the cell at (x,y), requires it to be a walkable, populated cell (flag +0x38 == 1, count +0x20 > 0), tests the direction against its edge range, and then writes {cell, cellPtr, containedActor} when the neighbour check passes.
evidence: Its only caller is now named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode (0x5F3AF0, 0.55), which walks a trail follower to the next walkable cell; the resolved cell/actor triple it returns is what that walker consumes, and it shares maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord and Ui_HitTestRows with 0x002D7DDC, so 'find the neighbouring cell in direction' is the right role.

name: maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt
signature: void maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt(u32* out, int cell, u32 x, u32 y, int* origin, int dir)
summary: Third directional cell search: picks the dominant axis of the cell rectangle around the origin, then walks the Field2D cell layers with the same attribute queries as the other finders and writes the hit cell or -1.
evidence: Called from the named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode together with the other direction finders, so the family is right; the 0xF/0x10 attribute lookups and the short at cell+0x1C still decide the layer and are not explained, so it stays maybe_.

name: Map_SearchCellRecord
signature: int Map_SearchCellRecord(u32 map, int cell, u32* pos, int mode)
summary: Searches one map cell's record list for the entry at the given position: it resolves the index with 0x0062CB64, then applies the 0x20/0x40 neighbour-mode masks and the 0xF/0x10 short reads from the cell's extra block. Returns the index, the short value, or -1.
evidence: Four of the five callers are now named Map_FindCellInDirection, Map_FindCellInDirectionEx and maybe_Map_FindCellInArea, and the two Gfx_Trail path walkers use it to test the next path cell, so the Map attribution is supported by the call sites. The body is a flag-masked search of a single cell's record list returning an index or -1.

name: Ui_List_HandleInputIfActive
signature: void Ui_List_HandleInputIfActive(u32 list, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d)
summary: Gate that forwards an input event to the list window only when the list controller reports it is active (0x62AF84 != 0).
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Ui_ListWindow_MoveSelection and the four arguments are passed through unchanged, so the function is exactly an 'if active, forward the input' wrapper.

name: Ui_SpriteList_LoadPage
summary: Loads one page of 14 sprite rows: for every slot it takes the record at `page*14 + i` from the row table and binds its text, or blanks the slot when the page is short; then recomputes the scrollbar position.
evidence: `iVar5 = arg2*0xe + i` compared with `self->f_4c`; rows at `self + i*0xc` with fields f_70/f_74/f_78; `func_006308EC(iVar1->f_34 + iVar5*0x10)` fetches the text, `func_001A6680(row->f_70,row->f_74)` binds it, `*(int*)(...+0x78) = iVar5` (or -1); `self->f_50 = rows % 14` via a reciprocal multiply by g_002e3b94; then `func_001D809C(self->f_38, pos-1 | self->f_28<<16)`.

name: maybe_Ui_ActivateScriptedElement
summary: Starts a script-driven UI element: marks its controller (self+0x3570) active, advances the controller state byte through 0x00636C48, dispatches the matching script state callback (Script_DispatchStateCallback on controller+0x34), sets the started flag self+0x356C, rebuilds the element container (Container_SetCountFromByteSize on +0x2DC/+0x2D4) and selects the current grid entry through Ui_List_SelectEntryById.
evidence: NEW: every non-trivial callee is now confidently named (Script_DispatchStateCallback, Container_SetCountFromByteSize, Ui_List_SelectEntryById), which exactly matches 'start the script + apply commands + select entry'. There is still no caller and no vtable sibling, so it is not proven whether this is a one-shot activation or a per-frame re-entry; the name keeps maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Ui_List_SelectById
summary: Asks the window for its bound list object (vtable+0x58) and, when present, selects the entry id stored at the u16 self+0x28 (high-half encoding).
evidence: Identity with 0x00214A78/0x00304FC8 (same three operations) proves it is a select-by-id helper, but which window owns it and whether +0x28 is really an id is still inferred from the 0x001D809C calling convention.

name: maybe_Ui_List_GetPendingCode
summary: Returns 14 (0x0E) when the signed byte at self+0x1C is set, otherwise -1 - a small status/result selector.

name: Ui_ListView_SetItemCount
summary: Recomputes the list view's item count from a begin/end range, resizes the child list accordingly, refreshes the selection and enables/disables the empty-list indicator.
evidence: `iVar1 = arg2[1] - *arg2 >> 4; arg1[0x13] = iVar1; func_00622038(arg1+0x15,iVar1,0); (**(code**)(*arg1+0x6c))(arg1,arg1[0x19]); *(u8*)(arg1[0x1fc]+0x44) = arg1[0x13] < 1 | ... & 0xfe; (**(code**)(*arg1+0x40))(arg1, 0 < arg1[0x13]);` — the 16-byte stride and the +0x44 visible flag match 0x002E3B98, which is the same function without the visibility update.

name: maybe_Ui_TriplePane_SetActive
signature: void maybe_Ui_TriplePane_SetActive(void* self, const u8* indices)

summary: Binds the list view to a new source range: sets the item count, resizes the child list, refreshes the selection and toggles the empty indicator, but leaves the pane visibility untouched.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x002D88EC except that the final `*(u8*)(arg1[0x1fc]+0x44)` write is missing; same `(arg2[1]-*arg2)>>4` count, `func_00622038(arg1+0x15,count,0)` resize and `vtable+0x6c` / `vtable+0x40` calls.

name: Ui_ItemListWindow_InitBase
summary: Constructor/base-initialiser of the item list window: it is a pure tail call into the shared initialiser 0x001A6460, which installs the window's vtable, sets its initial flag and binds its background texture.

name: Ui_ItemListWindow_InitRows
signature: void Ui_ItemListWindow_InitRows(int* self, int* layout, int arg3, int arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_Composite_DtorDelete

name: Ui_ScrollBarObject_Create

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetCurrentText

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyCommand
signature: u32 Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyCommand(UiMessageWindow* self, int commandId, int arg3, int* payload)
summary: Applies one queued message-window command: command 0xFFFF ends the current message (closes the three sub-layouts and calls vfunc +0x10), command 0 selects the string at (arg) from the layout table and dispatches it through the callback stored in arg4.
evidence: Reads the layout table at self+0x1D0->f_58->f_24 + command*4 (offset table idiom), handles 0xFFFF and 0, calls vfuncs +0x18/+0x10 of self->f_AC; invoked from 0x2E09BC which walks the command list at self+0x1C4.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetLayoutByState
signature: u32 Ui_MessageWindow_SetLayoutByState(UiMessageWindow* self, int choiceMode, int force)
summary: Selects the message-window layout: force sets layout 5, choiceMode==0 selects layout 3 (plain message) and clears the two choice sprites, otherwise layout 4 (message with choices).
evidence: Switches on arg2 and calls 0x2E08DC (next-icon) + 0x2E07AC with 3/4/5; 0x4C0C2C/0x4C0B58 clear the two choice sprites at self+0xB0/self+0xFC; self->f_170 stores the layout id.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetLayoutMode
summary: Switches the active message layout to mode 3 (self+0xB0), 4 (self+0xFC) or 5 (self+0x148) by resetting the two choice slots and pointing self->f_AC at the selected layout; returns 0 when the mode is already active.
evidence: if (self->f_170 == mode) return 0; 0x4C0C2C clears two slots; self->f_AC = self+0xB0/+0xFC/+0x148; self->f_170=mode.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetChoiceCursor
summary: Moves the message window's choice cursor to slot 0/1/2: hides the three choice sprites, shows the selected one and notifies the parent window when leaving the two-choice state.
evidence: Clears sprites self+0x1D/0x21/0x24 via 0x2E0288, stores the selected pointer in self[0x1C], vfunc +0xC on it, and calls vfunc +0x40(self,1) when the previous mode was 2; self->f_2A keeps the cursor.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNextIcon

evidence: Strings s_icon_next_002e09b0 and s__icon_messagei_3d_002e099b; flag update `sprite->f_44 & 0xFE | visible`; called when the layout changes and from 0x2E09BC.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands

name: Container_NameHash_Ctor
