evidence: Copies the name with 0x11142C (bounded by 0x1F), initialises three circular list heads at self+4/0x44, computes `h = h*mult ^ c` over the name and stores it at self+0x54; the same idiom as 0x2E4A70 and 0x2E758C.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListA
summary: Deleting destructor of a pooled object: installs the vtable passed in, unlinks the intrusive list at +0x48/+0x4C, destroys the list at +4 when the ownership flag at +0x14 is set, and frees the block through func_0010F6CC. Byte-identical to 0x002E4BD4, 0x0046B5C0 and 0x0046BDEC.
evidence: The +4 teardown is the intrusive-list destroy idiom (0x0010EC00 finds the last node, std_RbTree_EraseNode erases it, now 0.65) and func_0010F6CC is the pool deallocator; the class is still unidentified, so the A suffix stays.

name: Anim_Interp_EvaluateEx
summary: Second interpolation evaluator: applies the easing mode stored at self+8 to the value in s0/t (used for UI scaling) using the sine helper.
evidence: Mode byte *(self+8) selects branch 0/1/2; mode 2 clamps with 0x3F800001 and scales by g_002e4600; calls 0x673468 (sin/cos).

name: Anim_UpdatePoseBlend
summary: Advances a keyframe blend by step (the parameter arrives in s0), rebuilds the 10-float pose from the two endpoint poses at +0x40 and +0x04 and writes the blended pose to the target node (self+0x68).
evidence: self->f_3c += step (blend timer); calls 0x002E465C to interpolate; result fed to 0x001CEE24 (node pose setter). Callers 0x00405398 and 0x0049F728 are motion/camera update paths.

name: Anim_InterpolatePose
signature: void Anim_InterpolatePose(float* out, BlendState* self, float* poseA, float* poseB)
summary: Interpolates two 10-float keyframe poses (three float3 blocks plus a scalar) at the blend factor self+0x3C, using angular interpolation for the orientation block and lerp for positions; copies pose B when the blend weight is below the epsilon.
evidence: 0x005753BC = vector lerp, 0x00575864 = quaternion slerp/nlerp; 0x002E44D4 reads the blend weight; 0x001CEDA4 initialises the output pose; the 0x002E4934/38/3C constants are the epsilon/unit values.

name: Ui_AnimWindow_SelectFrame
summary: Selects which animation frame set the window uses: copies the start/end values of slot 1, 0 or 0xB out of the animation template at self->f_2C into the window fields and rebinds the frame pair (0x1CEE24).
evidence: arg2 1 -> template+0x84/0x88/0x8C, 0 -> +0xA0/0xA4/0xA8, 0xB -> constants g_002e49d8, else +0x74/0x78/0x7C; then func_001CEE24(&self->f_40,&template->f_B0).

name: Ui_AnimWindow_ApplyFrame
signature: void Ui_AnimWindow_ApplyFrame(UiAnimWindow* self, u32 slot, int frameRef)
summary: Applies a frame selection to the anim window: runs Ui_AnimWindow_SelectFrame and, when a frame reference is supplied, copies it from frameRef+0x68, otherwise syncs the window's own frame pointer.
evidence: Slot +8 of vtable 0x007610EC (class with Anim_UpdatePoseBlend at +0x14); body: 0x2E4940(self,slot) then self->f_3C=self->f_30 or 0x1CEE24(self+4,frameRef+0x68).

name: Ui_CompositeObject_Ctor
signature: int Ui_CompositeObject_Ctor(unsigned int* obj, unsigned int owner)
summary: Constructor of a multi-base composite UI object: installs vtable 0x007610EC, initialises the two embedded sub-objects and returns the adjusted base pointer (-0x68).
evidence: Seven named constructors call it first (Ui_ArcListWindow_CtorParts, Ui_MotionPath_Ctor, Ui_ScreenChild_GaugeObject_Ctor, Ui_ScreenController_InitChildren, Model_BlendAttachment_Ctor, ...), which fixes the base-constructor role.

name: Container_NameHash_CtorB
summary: Second name-hash container constructor, identical to 0x2E4324 but with its own hash seed/multiplier globals; used by the second half of the UI list objects.
evidence: Same field layout and 0x11142C copy as 0x2E4324; multiplier g_002e4bcc, seed g_002e4bc4; hash stored at self+0x54.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListB
summary: Deleting destructor of a pooled object: installs the vtable passed in, unlinks the intrusive list at +0x48/+0x4C, destroys the list at +4 when the ownership flag at +0x14 is set, and frees the block. Byte-identical to 0x002E4488, 0x0046B5C0 and 0x0046BDEC - only the vtable the caller passes differs.
evidence: Confirmed byte-identical to the named sibling 0x002E4488 by re-reading both bodies; the intrusive-list destroy (std_RbTree_EraseNode, 0.65) and the pool free are the same. No caller and no vtable constant, so the class stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListC
summary: Non-deleting destructor variant: installs the hard-coded vtable g_002E4C6C, unlinks the intrusive list at +0x48/+0x4C, destroys the list at +4 when the ownership flag at +0x14 is set, and returns self. Same body as 0x002E4488 minus the trailing pool free, so it is the base-destructor half of that pair.
evidence: Re-read against the now-confident std_RbTree_EraseNode (0.65): the +4 teardown is the intrusive-list destroy idiom (0x0010EC00 finds the last node, std_RbTree_EraseNode erases it), and the only difference from 0x002E4488/0x002E4BD4 is the missing func_0010F6CC pool free. The class is still unidentified, so the letter suffix stays.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_BindMessagePairs
summary: Binds the two message-pair texts of the window: resolves the two panes, pairs them with Ui_MessagePair_Bind and stores the pair at self+0x1E18.
evidence: Calls 0x1D85EC=Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify on self+0x11C and self+0x1DC8 with g_002e4ccc/cd0, then 0x1DACFC=Ui_MessagePair_Bind(self+0x1E18,...) and links it with 0x123594.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the message window: destroys the message page at +0x1E18, restores the remaining sub-object vtables, destroys the two 0x414-byte containers and the list node, releases the layout references and frees the window.
evidence: The named Ui_MessagePage_Dtor/Ui_LayoutRef_Release/Ui_Object_DtorBase calls and the final operator delete make this the deleting destructor, but the name Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor is already taken by the earlier 0x001C57E4 window, so the deleting variant gets the distinct name.

name: Ui_Message_SetNameArg
summary: Binds the object's display name to message arguments 2 and 5 so a message like "%s obtained" can be shown.
evidence: `func_0061BD4C(auStack_18,self->f_20a); iVar2 = func_0035EB98(root,self->f_208); func_006D3EA0(2,g_002e4e3c,iVar2+0xca); func_006D3EA0(5,g_002e4e3c,func_0066C99C(str,1));`. The +0xca offset is the name-string field of the name-table entry, used identically by 0x002AF9AC/0x00306A9C.

name: Ui_Message_SetNameAndNumberArgs
summary: Binds both a name and a number to one message: argument 5 gets the name (or the formatted number when the name flag is clear) and arguments 2/3 get the two numbers, with the formatted/name variants selected by f_218/f_219.
evidence: `if (self->f_218 == 0) { func_005E5B98(&buf, self->f_20c & 0xffff, self->f_214); iVar5 = func_0063FD24(root, self->f_208 & 0xffff); ... }` else name path with `func_00707C1C(&buf,&g_002e4fd4,entry+0xca)`; then `func_006D3EA0(5,g_002e4fe0,iVar4)` plus the second block `func_006D3EA0(2,...,local_234)` and `(3,...,local_130)`.

name: Ui_Message_SetNameAndCodeArgs
summary: Binds a name (argument 2) and a code/level value (argument 5) to a message, resolving the code through func_00629034 and falling back to the default pool value when it is not found.
evidence: `func_0018C1B8(auStack_20,self->f_208); iVar1 = func_00629034(auStack_20);` then the same formatted-vs-name split as 0x002AF9AC, `func_006D3EA0(2,g_002e50ac,...)` and `func_006D3EA0(5,g_002e50ac,iVar1 == 0 ? g_002e50b0 : iVar1)`.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_EncodeSelectionCode
signature: void maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_EncodeSelectionCode(int self, u8* out, int kind)
summary: Eight-way dispatcher that fills a caller record {u8 code, u8 arg, u32 value} for kind 0..7 with codes 0x13/0x14/0x26/0x15/0x16/0x1F/0x27; for kind 2 the value comes from the object's vtable slot +0x18.
evidence: Unchanged: the only context is the vtable 0x007611E0 this function is slot 0 of, whose other rows are Ui_ShopWindow_ResetToIdle, maybe_Ui_CreateSpriteByName and the rounding helper 0x002E5170 - enough to keep the Ui_ShopWindow prefix but not to say what the codes select. The neighbouring Ui_Message_SetName* functions are a different family (they fill message argument slots), so the codes are not message argument types.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateSpriteByName
summary: Lazily creates a shared sprite object from the UI heap and applies the name in *name to it.
evidence: NEW: there is no direct bl/b call site; the callee currently named Party_Status_SetMemberValueByRatio is clearly misnamed for this path, so it cannot support the name-application reading. The lazy singleton plus the string argument remain the only evidence, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetEntryPayloadById
summary: Looks the id up in the entry pool at self+0x50 and returns the entry's payload word at +0x18, or NULL when the pool or the entry is missing.
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong. The whole 0x002E5xxx-0x002E6xxx block is the 2D sprite scene module - Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1 (0x002E5D0C) reads the very same self+0x50 pool and walks the same entry+8 child chain, and the neighbours are Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge, Gfx_Scene_AllocSpritePoolHandle, Gfx_EntryPool_Init and Gfx_Scene_FindSpriteByHandle. The lookup helper 0x007141A8 is an inner entry of the misnamed Field_Path_GetPosition (0x00714008), so it cannot name the operation; which of the two pools +0x50/+0x58 is sprites and which is nodes stays open.

name: Gfx_EntryPool_Init
signature: void Gfx_EntryPool_Init(void* pool, uint32_t heapTag, uint32_t heapTag2)
summary: Initialises a gfx scene entry pool: stores the heap tag at +8, allocates the two 8-byte allocator wrappers at +0xC/+0x10, a 0x14-byte occupancy header at +0x18 and 16 entries of 0x34 bytes plus a sentinel, then hands every entry to Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry and clears the occupancy bitmask.
evidence: The sibling Gfx_EntryPool_Clear (0x002E6428, caller Field_DestroyScene) frees exactly these 16 x 0x34 entries through the +0x18 occupancy bitmask, and all three callers here are field-scene code (Field_InitSceneObjects, Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer, maybe_Field_QuerySceneRect). The old 'Battle_PopupPool' prefix came only from the shared allocator-wrapper vtable, which 0x00627404 also installs in a field handle list.

name: Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite
signature: void Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 spriteId, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Submits one sprite to the scene renderer: passes the sprite id, the object's vertex/param block at self+0x1C and the caller parameters to 0x58E770 (scene draw entry).
evidence: Body: 0x588430(&self->f_1C) then func_0058E770(self->f_14, spriteId, &self->f_1C, 0, param, 0, flags); 0x58E770 is in the Gfx scene draw family (0x58A354/0x58C580).

name: Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32* posBlock, u32* colorBlock, int flag)
summary: Allocates a large draw entry (handle tag 0x20000) from the scene's fixed slot pool, stores the 3+10 dwords of geometry/colour data and returns the slot handle.
evidence: Slot pool self->f_50 (capacity +0xC, data +4, bitmap +8); handle = (slot & 0xFFFF) | 0x20000; writes puVar1[0..0xF] from arg3/arg2; mirror of 0x2E59B8 which uses tag 0x10000.

name: Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntrySmall
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntrySmall(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32* posBlock, u32* colorBlock, int flag)
summary: Allocates a small draw entry (handle tag 0x10000) from the same slot pool and fills the 3+4 dwords of colour/geometry data.
evidence: Identical frame to 0x2E5934 but tag 0x10000 and only puVar1[0..9]; pool self->f_50 with bitmap at +8 and capacity at +0xC.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetTaggedEntryPayload
summary: Tagged id lookup: ids carrying 0x0F0000 tag bits resolve through the pool at self+0x50, untagged ids through the pool at self+0x58; both return the entry's payload at +0x0C, or NULL.
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong - this is the same 2D sprite scene module as Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1 (0x002E5D0C), which uses the identical `(id & 0xf0000) != 0` tag test on the self+0x50 pool. The recovered body still depends on the damaged-decompilation flag register in_ZR, so which branch is which is only known from the tag test, and the payload offset +0x0C differs from the +0x18 of the untagged siblings.

name: Gfx_Scene_RemoveSpriteEntries
summary: Removes the object's draw entries from the scene: for each of the four entry lists detaches the list heads (0x58EE0C/0x58EFEC/0x588C38/0x588F68) and frees the corresponding bit in the slot bitmap.
evidence: Calls 0x58EE0C, 0x58EFEC, 0x588C38, 0x588F68 on self->f_14->f_2C and clears bit `1 << (index & 0x1F)` in the bitmap at self->f_18; decrements the live count at f_18+0x10.

name: Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteEx
signature: void Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteEx(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 spriteId, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Second sprite submission variant (0x58E918 instead of 0x58E770); used for the alternate sprite shader/primitive.
evidence: Body: 0x588430(&self->f_1C) then func_0058E918(self->f_14, spriteId, &self->f_1C, 0, param, 0, flags); twin of 0x2E58E0.

name: Gfx_Scene_AllocSpritePoolHandle
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AllocSpritePoolHandle(void* sceneSpriteCtx, u32 frameId, const void* srcRect, void* outInfo)
summary: Forwards (sceneSpriteCtx->f_5C, frameId, srcRect, outInfo) to Gfx_SpritePool_Alloc (0x005F24A4) to allocate and initialize a 0x70-byte sprite pool entry, returning its handle word at entry->u32_68 (or 0 if f_5C is NULL or allocation fails).
evidence: Ghidra dropped r1, r2, and r3 because 0x2E5C38 loads r0 = self->f_5C and forwards r1..r3 untouched to bl 0x5F24A4 (which checks frameId < pool->u32_24, claims a free bit in pool->bitmap_18, initializes the 0x70-byte entry, and returns it), then loads entry->u32_68. All 3 callers (Gfx_SpriteObject_UpdateFrame, Gfx_SpriteObject_InitFromDesc, Ui3D_InitEffectEntryFromRecord) pass (ctx, frameId, &rect, outInfo) and store the returned handle.

name: Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType2
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType2(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 handle, u32* data)
summary: Attaches a type-2 node record to the entry addressed by the handle: allocates a 13-dword record from 0x707E98, links it into the entry's chain (0x7141A8) and copies the 10-dword payload.
evidence: Requires (handle & 0xF0000)!=0 and handle<<7 >= 0; slot lookup 0x7141A8(self->f_50, handle & 0xFFFF); new node from 0x707E98(self->f_54); byte +4 set to 2.

name: Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 handle, u32* data)
summary: Attaches a type-1 node record (6 dwords) to the entry addressed by the handle.
evidence: Same gate as 0x2E5C60 but node tag 1 and only puVar2[2..5] copied; uses 0x707E98 + 0x7141A8.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetChildPayloadById
signature: void* maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetChildPayloadById(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 id, int index)
summary: Resolves the entry for a tagged id in the pool at self+0x50 and walks <index> links down its child chain (entry+8 -> node[0]), returning the child's payload word (+4).
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong. Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1 (0x002E5D0C) builds exactly this chain - it appends a new node to entry+8 of the self+0x50 pool and writes the payload at node+4 - so this is the matching read side of the 2D sprite scene node list. The lookup helper is still an inner entry of the misnamed Field_Path_GetPosition, so the class name stays a guess.

name: Gfx_Scene_AllocSpriteSlot
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AllocSpriteSlot(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32* posBlock, u32* colorBlock, int flag)
summary: Finds the first free slot in the sprite bitmap, reserves it, writes the entry header (tag 0x1040000 | slot) and the 3+3 data dwords, and returns the new entry handle.
evidence: Walks the inverted bitmap at self->f_58 (capacity +0xC, data +4, bitmap +8), computes slot*0x24, sets bit, writes header `(slot&0xFFFF)|0x1040000`, then 3+3 payload dwords; 0x1000000 flag bit honoured.

name: Field_HandleSet_ClearBits
summary: Releases a packed object handle: looks it up in one of two handle tables (0x7141A8 for bit 0x1000000, 0x714160 otherwise), clears the occupancy bit for the record and for every entry in its child list, and decrements the live counter. Used when a field 2D object or scene entry is destroyed.
evidence: two handle tables f_50/f_58, bitmaps f_C/f_10, bit index from the pointer delta scaled by g_002E614C/g_002E6150, callers Field_Object2D_ReleaseSceneEntry/ResetAttachedNodes (N_060) and the sprite destructors.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetEntryPayloadByIdB
summary: Same id->entry+0x18 lookup as 0x002E5270 but against the second entry pool at self+0x58.
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong - the only caller is maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncAttachedNodes and the whole neighbourhood is Gfx_Scene_* 2D sprite scene code. The body is byte-identical to 0x002E5270 apart from the pool offset (+0x58 instead of +0x50), so the B suffix marks the second pool rather than a different operation.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetEntryPayloadByIdC
summary: Third emitted copy of the id->entry+0x18 lookup against the pool at self+0x50, instruction-identical to 0x002E5270.
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong - this is the same 2D sprite scene module (Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1 and Field_HandleSet_ClearBits use the same self+0x50 pool). The body is instruction-identical to 0x002E5270, so the C suffix only records that the compiler emitted a third copy; it is not a different operation.

name: Gfx_Scene_SetNodeParams
signature: void Gfx_Scene_SetNodeParams(GfxSceneSprite* self, int arg2, int* values)
summary: Pushes up to four changed parameters (x/y/z + extra) into the sprite instance found by 0x5F1BFC, recomputing the derived fields and copying the matching 0x88-byte records.
evidence: Compares iVar1->f_54/f_58/f_5C/f_60 against arg3[0..3], builds a change mask, then copies 0x28/0x14-byte sub-blocks with 0x1235A4; 0x5F1BFC is the scene sprite instance lookup.

name: Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries
summary: Frees all draw entries of the object: runs std_destroy_range over the 0x70-byte records, releases the two owned sub-objects and frees the container itself.
evidence: Calls 0x100BE0=std_destroy_range(data, g_002e6314, 0x14, 4) over piVar2[7] entries, vfunc +0x14 on the two holders, then 0x10F6CC; clears self->f_5C.

name: Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag
signature: void Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 handle, int enable)
summary: Sets or clears the 0x1000000 'disabled' flag of the entry referenced by the handle, selecting the large or small pool from the handle tag.
evidence: handle & 0x1000000 selects pool self->f_58 (0x714160) vs self->f_50 (0x7141A8); flag word at +4 |= 0x1000000 or &= 0xFEFFFFFF; called by Field_Object_Enable/DisableSound.

name: Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType4
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType4(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 handle, u32* data)
summary: Attaches a type-4 node record (5 dwords) to the entry addressed by a 0x1000000-tagged handle.
evidence: Requires handle & 0x1000000; slot lookup 0x714160(self->f_58, handle & 0xFFFF); node from 0x707E98(self->f_54); byte +4 = 4; copies puVar3[2..4].

name: Gfx_EntryPool_Clear
summary: Empties a gfx scene entry pool: walks the occupancy bitmask at +0x18 and for every live 0x34-byte entry unlinks and frees its sprite list, node list and the two list heads through the named Gfx_Scene_Delete*/Destroy* helpers, clearing the bit as it goes. Called from Field_DestroyScene.
evidence: The caller is Field_DestroyScene and all five callees are the named Gfx_Scene_DeleteSpriteEntryList/DeleteNodeEntryList/DestroySpriteList/DestroyNodeList helpers, so the pool belongs to the gfx scene rather than battle popups; the only damage left is one unaff_r9 temporary (damaged decompilation), the bitmask/unlink/free flow is intact.

name: Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInArea
signature: int Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInArea(GfxSceneSprite* self, float* point, int maxResults, u32* outHandles)
summary: Spatial query: walks the 0x40-byte entry table, tests each entry's region (type 1 = sphere distance, 2 = cone via 0x6652C4, 3 = axis-aligned box) against the point, applies the extra predicate 0x2E68C8 and writes the handles of the hits into outHandles.
evidence: Type field `(*entry & 0xFFFFF) >> 0x10` with cases 1/2/3; distance test against entry[9], box test entry[6..0xB], callback func_002E68C8; bitmap-indexed table at self->f_10; returns the number of hits (<= arg3).

name: Gfx_SpriteObject_ReleaseChildHandle
summary: When the object owns a child handle at +0x5C, the caller passes a non-zero flag and the child reports itself active through 0x005F1BFC, releases that handle through Svc_HandlePool_Release. Otherwise does nothing.
evidence: The named callers Gfx_SpriteObject_UpdateFrame and Gfx_SceneSprite_Dtor fix the class, and the named callee Svc_HandlePool_Release fixes the operation. The second argument's meaning is not visible in the body, so the first pass's 'pause' reading is dropped from the name and only the release is named.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_CountChildEntries
summary: Resolves the entry for a tagged id in the pool at self+0x50 and counts the nodes of its child chain (entry+8 -> node[0]); returns 0 when the id is untagged or the entry is missing.
evidence: CORRECTED: the 'Fs_GetResource' prefix is wrong - the only caller is Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState and the neighbourhood is Gfx_Scene_* 2D sprite scene code. It is the counting mirror of maybe_Gfx_Scene_GetChildPayloadById (0x002E5DB4), which walks the same entry+8 chain that Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1 builds.

name: Gfx_Scene_IsPointInRegion
summary: Tests a point against a linked list of region records: type 1 sphere (distance <= radius), type 2 cone (projection with sin/cos helper), type 3 box (min/max on all axes).
evidence: Node byte +4 selects 1/2/3; sphere test `(p-c)^2 <= r^2`, cone uses 0x574548/0x574440 with g_002e6b0c seed, box compares against fields 2..7; walks until next==0.

name: maybe_Ui_ListEntry_SetChild
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListEntry_SetChild(UiListEntry* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Replaces the optional 0x40-byte child block of a list entry: when self+0x0C and both arguments are non-zero it releases the old child through Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries, allocates and zeroes a 0x40-byte block, stores it at self+0x5C and initialises it with 0x005F1F08(child, self+0x0C, arg3, arg2).
evidence: NEW: the single caller is the named Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateSlots and the release side is the named Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries. The initialiser 0x005F1F08 is called on a plain 0x40-byte block but its current name (Save_SlotTable_Init) does not fit, so what the child block really is remains unclear - keep maybe_ 0.45.

name: Gfx_Scene_TransformPoint
signature: void Gfx_Scene_TransformPoint(float* out, GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 matrixId, u32 p1, u32 p2, u32 p3)
summary: Transforms a point through the sprite's current matrix: builds a temporary transform (0x58C40C/0x58C370), calls Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance (0x2E74FC) and releases the temporary.
evidence: Calls 0x58C40C, 0x58C370, 0x2E74FC, 0x58C4A0; guards on self->f_14/f_C; writes the two result dwords to arg1.

name: Gfx_SpritePool_SetHandleVisible
signature: void Gfx_SpritePool_SetHandleVisible(void* mgr, int handle, int isVisible)
summary: Looks up a 0x74-byte sprite/render pool entry in mgr->f_14 by handle (0x00589124) and clears (isVisible != 0) or sets (isVisible == 0) hidden flag bit 0x80000000 on entry->u32_10.
evidence: ARM 0x2E6C68: guards handle >= 0 and mgr->f_14 != NULL, resolves entry via 0x00589124(mgr->f_14, handle); if isVisible != 0 tail-calls 0x00589038(mgr->f_14, entry, 0x80000000) (bic entry->u32_10, 0x80000000), else executes orr entry->u32_10, 0x80000000. Called by Show/Hide (0x4C6640/0x4C6680) and Activate/Deactivate (0x4C6A44/0x4C6ADC) passing (u8_10 && u8_3D).

name: Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInRect
signature: int Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInRect(GfxSceneSprite* self, int entryId, int x, int y, int w, int h, int maxResults, u32* outHandles)
summary: Rectangle query over the 0x24-byte entry table: collects entries of the requested id whose screen rectangle overlaps the given rectangle (and optionally walks their child chains).
evidence: Entry stride 0x24, header id at entry[6], rect at +0x1E/+0x20 and +0x22/+0x24; child chain at entry[2] with 0xE/0xC fields; returns hits and stores *puVar7 handles in arg8.

name: Font_CacheGlyphsForText
signature: u32 Font_CacheGlyphsForText(FontCache* self, char* text, FontResource* font, u32 flags)
summary: Ensures every glyph needed by `text` is present in the font cache: it walks the cache's dirty bitmap (one bit per 0x34-byte glyph slot), allocates a slot for each missing code point, hashes the character name to pick the atlas page, and uploads the glyph geometry/UVs (0x0058D2xx / 0x00589Dxx / 0x0058EAxx) into the page. Returns 1 when all glyphs could be installed, 0 when a slot or upload failed.
evidence: The 0x34-byte stride together with the bitmap walk (`~word`, bit per glyph, slot index `i*0x34 + bit*0x34`) is a glyph-cache slot table; the hash loop over the string with the four 32-bit multipliers at 0x002E7260..0x002E726C is a character-name hash; the 0x0058xxxx callees belong to the font/atlas module (0x0058D2B0 build page request, 0x005885A8/0x00588AB0 create glyph, 0x0058EABC/0x0058ED28 upload glyph, 0x0058D00C release request); 0x0011CCA0 is strlen.

name: Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine
signature: int Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine(GfxSceneSprite* self, float* start, int count, u32 p4, u32 p5)
summary: Line/segment query: steps from the start point along the object's direction vector (self+0x38..0x40) and submits each intermediate point to 0x58E770, counting how many succeeded.
evidence: Loop adds self->f_38/0x3C/0x40 * self->f_24 to the point and calls 0x58E770(self->f_14,&pt,&self->f_1C,0,p4,0,p5); normalises the final delta with sqrt.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance
signature: void Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance(u32* out, GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 matrix, u32 arg4, int arg5)
summary: Creates a sprite instance from the scene resource (0x588AB0) and either copies it (0x58EF24) or clones it with a template (0x58EE64); returns the new instance in out.
evidence: Calls 0x588AB0(self->f_14,...), then 0x58EF24/0x58EE64 depending on arg5, fallback release 0x588D08; result written to arg1[0]/arg1[1].

name: Gfx_Scene_FindSpriteByName
summary: Hash lookup of a scene sprite by name: hashes the name with the multiplier at g_002e76a0 and scans the 0x34-byte name records of the sprite table for a matching hash.
evidence: String hash loop `h = h*mult + c` over pairs of characters, then `h = h % g_002e76a4 * g_002e76a8 + h`; compares *result == hash; table at self->f_18 (+0xC count, +4 data, +8 bitmap); 0x11CCA0=strlen.

name: Gfx_Scene_SetSpriteFlag
signature: void Gfx_Scene_SetSpriteFlag(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 arg2, u32 enable)
summary: Sets or clears bit 0 of the sprite instance's +0x67 flag (scene sprite lookup 0x5F1BFC).
evidence: Reads iVar1->f_67, toggles bit 0 when `(~flag & 1) != enable`, writes it back; guard self->f_5C != 0.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart14
signature: void Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart14(u32 * out, GfxSceneSprite * self, u32 nameId, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Creates a scene sprite whose part list is built from the part added by maybe_Gfx_SpriteParts_Add14: bails out when the sprite has no scene object, otherwise builds the parts record with the name id, creates the sprite instance through Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance and clears the temporary parts record.
evidence: The two 'variants' are now distinguishable: this one calls maybe_Gfx_SpriteParts_Add14 while 0x002E77CC calls maybe_Gfx_SpriteParts_Add40, and both share the named Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance / Gfx_SpriteParts_Clear, so naming them after the part they add is more useful than A/B.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_SetIndexPair
summary: Applies a two-word index pair to the Gfx scene stored at self+0x14: it removes the node at indices[1] through Gfx_Scene_RemoveNode and passes indices[0] to a second scene helper (Ghidra split the callee).
evidence: CORRECTED: the first callee is the named (and destructive) Gfx_Scene_RemoveNode, so the old 'SetUV' reading is unsupported; the two ints are plainly two scene indices. What the second, split helper does is still unknown, so maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart40
signature: void Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart40(u32 * out, GfxSceneSprite * self, u32 nameId, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Same sprite creation as 0x002E76F8 but the parts record is built with maybe_Gfx_SpriteParts_Add40, i.e. the second part layout (the '40' part table) used by the other sprite flavour.
evidence: Identical body to 0x002E76F8 except the part-adder call (maybe_Gfx_SpriteParts_Add40 vs Add14) and its name-table constant; the named Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance / Gfx_SpriteParts_Clear calls confirm the rest.

signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteFromBounds(u32* out, GfxSceneSprite* sprite, int bounds, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Creates a scene sprite sized from a bounds record: computes the three scaled extents of the record's +0x64/+0x68, +0x74/+0x78 and +0x84/+0x88 pairs, and only when their sum is non-zero stores the caller's value at record+4 and creates the sprite instance; otherwise it clears out[0]/out[1].

evidence: 0x58D2B0/0x58D00C lock the resource, 0x665E7C counts chunks, 0x58D300/0x58D328 get name/object, 0x10540C applies the filter, 0x5885A8 creates the sprite; the template is assembled from g_002e7a94/a98/a9c.

name: Field_Collision_RaycastScene
signature: u32 Field_Collision_RaycastScene(void* collisionCtx, const void* raySegment, u32 hitMask, u32 flags)
summary: Resets the raycast hit record at collisionCtx+0x1C and, if collision scene collisionCtx->f_14 is loaded, performs a 3D world raycast via 0x0058E3F4, returning non-zero on collision hit or 0 when unobstructed.

All 18 named callers (Field_NpcMoveTowardTarget, Field_IsPointInActorViewCone, Camera_UpdateWorkPath, Actor_UpdateFollowTarget, Field_Action_ApplyMove) branch on r0 == 0 for unobstructed movement/LOS/camera rays; unrelated to sprite drawing.

name: Battle_TextWindow_CtorPane

name: Ui_DungeonWindow_DeletingDtor

name: Field_ActorMotion_Ctor
signature: void* Field_ActorMotion_Ctor(void* self, u32 owner, u32 name, u32 resource, u8 flag)
summary: Generic constructor of the field actor motion/action helper: forwards to the shared object descriptor initialiser (0x00193D84) with flag 0x20000000, installs vtable 0x7614C4 and stores the owner argument at +0x28. Every field-actor motion and action subclass starts here.

The eight callers are deleting destructors of widgets that own an equip row (Ui_TalkSubWidget, Field_ActorMotion, maybe_Battle_DamagePopup, ...), which is why the old name guessed a shared panel base.

name: Ui_Dive_ReloadTextResources
summary: Reloads the diving-minigame text bundle into an existing holder: it fetches `dive_text.bxon` (entry 0x35), `dive_sortie_msg.bxon` (0x0B), `dive_blend_color_text.bxon` (0x25), `spirit_skill_text.bxon` (0x1D) and `dive_msg.bxon` (0x0F) and stores each handle plus a reference-counted copy in the 10-word slot array.

Ghidra loses the frame here (`arg1 >> 1`, unaff_r*), which is why the self pointer is reconstructed rather than read - treat the offsets +2/+4/+6/+8/+10 relative to the 8-byte record as the slot array.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyValueToChildren

name: Ui_Dive_LoadTextResources
summary: Opens every text table the diving minigame needs - `dive_text.bxon` (0x35), `dive_sortie_msg.bxon` (0x0B), `dive_blend_color_text.bxon` (0x25), `spirit_skill_text.bxon` (0x1D), `dive_msg.bxon` (0x0F) - and fills the ten-word slot array at self+0/+4.. with the handles and their reference-counted copies.
evidence: Five copies of the same block, each with a distinct string literal in the pool (`s_dive_text_bxon`, `s_dive_sortie_msg_bxon`, `s_dive_blend_color_text_bxon`, `s_spirit_skill_text_bxon`, `s_dive_msg_bxon`), opened with func_00124E5C(ctx, 5, name), type-checked against 0x007E7250, entry id compared (0x35/0x0B/0x25/0x1D/0x0F) and stored with the refcount helpers 0x00124F60 / 0x0012416C. Called from 0x00213578 together with 0x002E8C68.

name: Gfx_SpritePairArray_Clear
summary: Releases and clears the five (owner, handle) pair slots of the sprite-pair array: each owner word is zeroed and each generation-tagged handle is released through Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry, leaving the array ready for reuse.
evidence: The callee is the named Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry, so the routine releases handles rather than just zeroing memory as 'Init' implied; it is the first half of 0x002EB340 and is used to reset the array.

name: Gfx_SpritePairArray_ClearAndGetBase
summary: Clears all five (owner, handle) pair slots of the sprite-pair array - releasing each handle entry - then releases the five handles once more through the chain of Pack_ReleaseHandle calls and returns the buffer base (the address just before the first pair) so the caller can free it.
evidence: Both helper functions are now named (Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry and Pack_ReleaseHandle), which shows this is not a plain zero-fill but a handle release for all five slots, and the -4 return is the enclosing-buffer idiom used by Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles.

name: Ui_EquipRow_Update
summary: Refreshes one row of the equipment list: walks the 0x1A-byte row records, filters out rows whose item is not in the bag/party (Item_GetStoragePointer) or whose party flag in work+0x27508 is unset, pushes the pane and sets the row's state id.
evidence: Slot +4 of vtable 0x00761500 whose neighbours are maybe_Ui_EquipRow_UpdateCompareText / UpdateEquipMark / Ui_EquipmentWindow_HandleInput; calls Item_GetStoragePointer (0x643324), Ui_Window_PushPane (0x6D7508) and 0x617D7C with states 0x13/0x2E/0x2F; row stride 0x1A u16.

name: Fs_FileJob_Update
summary: State machine of an asynchronous file read job: state 0 opens/queries the file (0x1CFFCC, 0x503264), state 1 acquires the read buffer (0x1D0378), state 2 polls and then closes the pending resource (svc 0x24 wait, svc 0x23 close), state 3 queues the read (0x503A7C, 0x655398), states 4/5 handle retries and the error results (0x6552AC/0x6552BC/0x655304) before signalling completion; returns 1 while the job still runs.
evidence: switch on job+8 with 6 states, 0x1CFFCC/0x503264/0x1D0218/0x1D033C/0x1D0378 (open/read), 0x655xxx async-IO helpers, error codes 9/8/3/4/2 in job+0xC, caller Gfx resource loading.

name: maybe_Container_AddToFirstFreeSlot

name: maybe_Ui_EquipRow_RangeCheck

The Ui_EquipRow family is now confirmed by the named Ui_EquipRow_Update (0x002EB3B4) and Ui_EquipRow_DeletingDtor (0x002EA468), which supports the prefix, but the operation itself is still unreadable.

Everything above still comes from the earlier disassembly notes.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_InitArcMotion
summary: Configures the clip slot for the arcing variant: runs the shared clip-slot init, reads the actor/monster record for the id stored in its sprite object, seeds the start/step/end fields (+0x3C, +0x40, +0x4C), sets the speed constant g_002EBCAC at +0x48, and finally plays the clip named "Run" on the sprite pane.
evidence: Calls 0x0028B3AC (shared clip-slot base) and 0x005E88D4 / 0x005E80A4 / 0x005E88F0 (data-table accessors, the latter keyed by the u16 at sprite+0x258); stores float g_002EBCAC into +0x48; tail call (*(sprite->vtable+0x84))(sprite, 0x002EBCB0) where 0x002EBCB0 holds the literal "Run"; sibling 0x002EBCB4 is the matching per-frame update.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateArcMotion
summary: Per-frame update of the arcing variant: advances +0x48 by dt (backwards while the +0x2C flag is clear), checks it against the owner's +0x44 and the stored end limit +0x4C, and either stops the clip (mode 8) or applies an incremental rotation derived from the sprite's sin/cos components to the sprite basis fields +0x100/+0x104/+0x108 before refreshing the sprite actor.
evidence: Uses the same fields as the neighbouring maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_UpdateBillboardScale (0x0028B3D8, called last): f_24/f_28/f_2c/f_3c/f_40/f_44/f_48/f_4c; trig accumulation of f_8C/f_90/f_94/f_98 into f_100/f_104/f_108 with constant g_002EBDD4; calls 0x005E7848(sprite,8,0) and 0x005E7FA8 for the frame data; the +0x48 progress field is what 0x002EBC5C seeds.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEnemyAiArcAnim
summary: Constructs the eight-slot enemy-AI clip-slot object: base Gfx_BillboardObjectCtorBase, then slot count 8, the arc parameters (0x40A00000 = 5.0, 0xBE4CCCCD = -0.2, 0.5) and the g_animClipSlotArcVtable.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorArc
summary: Deleting destructor of the clip-slot variant that drives an arc motion: shared clip-slot base destructor 0x0028B708 then operator delete.
evidence: NEW: row 0x007615A8 is immediately followed by the confident Anim_ClipSlot_InitArcMotion and Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateArcMotion, so both the class and the 'arc' variant are pinned; only the base-dtor address is an inner entry.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion
summary: Initialises the non-arcing clip-slot variant: runs the shared slot init 0x0028B3AC, stores the amount at +0x3C and starts the clip named "Nut" on the sprite pane at +0x28.
evidence: NEW: the variant is confirmed by the vtable 0x007615E0 this function is slot 0 of - its +0x08 row is the confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion (0x002EBE78), so the 'LinearMotion' label no longer depends on the clip string. The class is the same one whose base sub-object vtable 0x00761610 holds maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorBase.

summary: Per-frame update of one animation clip slot: while the slot is inactive or its progress has not passed the owner's limit it clears the sprite animation, then steers the sprite toward its target and refreshes the move/stuck check.
evidence: vtable 0x007615DC places it at slot +0x0C between maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion (+0x04) and the class dtor, so the Anim_ClipSlot class is proven by its siblings. The body calls the named Field_Actor_SteerTowardTarget and Field_NpcAction_UpdateMoveAndStuckCheck, i.e. a per-frame movement update. 'Linear' is the family marker shared with the init sibling and is kept.

name: Anim_ClipSlot_DeletingDtorLinear
summary: Deleting destructor of the non-arcing clip-slot variant: installs the base vtable 0x00758AE0 (shared 0x00193E40 block) and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: 0x002EBEEC is slot 0 of the vtable 0x007615DC, whose +0x04 row is Anim_ClipSlot_InitLinearMotion and whose +0x0C row is the confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion (0x002EBE78) - so this really is the deleting destructor of the LinearMotion variant, not just a guess from the neighbouring Init/Update pair.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEnemyAiTwoSlotAnim
summary: Constructs the two-slot enemy-AI clip-slot object: base Gfx_BillboardObjectCtorBase, slot count 2, parameter 0x40400000 (3.0) / 0x3E4CCCCD (0.2) and the base g_animClipSlotBaseVtable.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Field_SetupEnemyAi and the vtable is g_animClipSlotBaseVtable, so it is the two-slot sibling of 0x002EBDD8; 'SetTwo' described only the slot count. The object's exact role in the enemy-AI setup is still inferred, so maybe_ stays.

summary: Deleting destructor of the base clip-slot sub-object (the one with no motion driver of its own): installs the base vtable 0x00758AE0 and frees the object.
evidence: NEW: 0x002EBF3C is slot 0 of the vtable 0x00761610, which is the table of the sub-object embedded at +0x30 of the LinearMotion clip-slot class (0x007615E0); its other rows are the plain slot methods 0x0028B3AC/0x0028B6AC/0x0028B3D4, i.e. no motion driver - which is exactly the 'base' reading. The confident Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateLinearMotion sibling fixes the family.

name: Battle_AnimWindow_Ctor
signature: BattleAnimWindow* Battle_AnimWindow_Ctor(u32 heapTag, u32* ownerParams, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: Field_CreateActionRun
summary: Constructor of the running field action: installs g_fieldActionRunVtable (0x00762AFC), zeroes the default words and seeds the run parameters at +0x50..+0x5C.
evidence: NEW: the caller Ui_FieldActionListWindow_InitPanes creates this object for row 2 with the packed name 0x68736164 ("dash"), and the installed vtable is the named g_fieldActionRunVtable (ToggleRun, StopMoveEffect, UpdateMove, UpdateTurnDirection, Run_CheckCanContinue) - the run/dash action, not an animation object.

name: Field_Action_Run_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the run/move action: stores the class vtable into the embedded sub-object at +0x50 (0x001CF7F8), then runs the shared action destructor and frees the block. The real entry point is the 4-byte thunk at 0x00302C8C, which loads the vtable and falls through here.
evidence: NEW: vtable word 0x00762B00 holds 0x00302C8C (the ldr/fall-through thunk), and that vtable's other slots are the confident maybe_Field_Action_ToggleRun, Field_Action_UpdateMove and maybe_Field_Action_StopMoveEffect, so the class is the run action. Confirmed with the thunk documented.

name: Field_Action_HorseStart
summary: Starts horse riding: resolves the mount's rotation, converts it into the rider's yaw/pitch, applies the orientation, clamps the run speed and starts the run animation/UI mode.
evidence: Sibling method of Field_Action_HorseStart_DeletingDtor (0x00303470) and Field_Action_HorseStart_End (0x003033DC) in vtable 0x00762B44; starts horse riding by resolving mount rotation (+0x2D0), aligning rider yaw/pitch, and configuring riding movement.

name: Field_Action_HorseJump
summary: Horse jump: switches to state 1, plays the 'Horse_Jump' animation and starts the vertical velocity.
evidence: String symbol s_Horse_Jump_00302f5c is passed to actor vtable+0x84, state f_2C = 1, vertical velocity f_3C = *g_00302F68, horizontal f_40 = *g_00302F6C * actor->f_26C, then FUN_00366CE8 (mount jump helper) and actor->f_2F4 = 0.

name: Field_Action_HorseLand
summary: Horse landing: switches to state 2, plays the 'Horse_Land' animation, releases the run mode and restores the ground flag.
evidence: String symbol s_Horse_Land_00302ff0 passed to actor vtable+0x84, f_2C = 2, actor vtable+0x54(4), the UI input mode is set with func_004101B4(camera->f_30+0xE0, 1, 0), actor->f_2F4 = 1 and FUN_00367B1C(actor) restores the mount pose.

name: Field_Action_HorseUpdate
summary: Per-frame horse movement: integrates the horse velocity in the rider's frame, applies gravity while airborne, and switches to the landing state when the horse touches the ground or runs into an obstacle.
evidence: func_00414570(self) first (the common move-update tail), then the quaternion f_8C..f_98 is converted into a forward vector and scaled by actor->f_26C * dt; state 1 applies the vertical velocity f_40 -= f_3C*dt; state 0 rotates the remaining distance by the mount quaternion (the manual quaternion multiply block) and compares it with the thresholds f_30C/f_310/f_314 to trigger the jump; state 1 -> state 2 when height < g_003033D4 with the land animation g_003033D8 and FUN_00367B1C; state 2 uses func_00669DD4 + func_005E7848(actor, 1 or 2, 0) to finish.

name: Field_Action_HorseStart_End
summary: Ends horse riding: clears the action's local flag at +0x44, tells the actor to leave state 4 through actor vtable+0x54 and then runs the actor's vtable+0x88 (drop the rider animation link).
evidence: Slot 2 of Field_Action_HorseStart vtable 0x00762B44, alongside slot 0 (0x00303470 Field_Action_HorseStart_DeletingDtor) and slot 3 (0x00302FFC Field_Action_HorseUpdate). Clears action local flag at self+0x44, calls actor vtable+0x54 with state 4 and vtable+0x88.

name: Field_CreateActionHorseStart
summary: Constructor of the horse-start field action: installs g_fieldActionHorseStartVtable (0x00762B40), clears the state byte at +0x2C and copies the default parameter words.
evidence: NEW: the caller Ui_FieldActionListWindow_InitPanes creates this object for row 3 with the packed name 0x706D756A ("jump"), and the installed vtable is the named g_fieldActionHorseStartVtable (HorseStart, HorseStart_End, HorseUpdate) - the mounted jump/start action. The first-pass 'Anim_CreateVariantE' was a generic bucket name.

name: Field_Action_HorseStart_DeletingDtor

evidence: vtable 0x00762B44 slot 0; body bl 0x00193E44 + tail 0x0010F6CC.

name: Field_Action_EvaluateTurnDirection
signature: void Field_Action_EvaluateTurnDirection(float* arg1, const HorseAction* self, float* out, void* ctx)
summary: Computes the desired heading for the run/horse action: rotates the actor's current 2x2 basis by the input yaw (self->f_44), orthonormalises it, hands it to Field_Action_HorseTurn for the turn-rate clamp/lerp and copies the result to out.
evidence: It is a slot of both the run action (vtable 0x762B2C) and the horse action (0x762BA4, next to Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue), and the disassembly shows the direct `bl 0x3038CC` at 0x303714 with (sp, self, out, ctx); that fixes it as the turn-direction evaluator called from the action vtable.

name: Field_Action_InitHorseParams
summary: Start step shared by both horse actions: copies the five speed constants (0x007A6EA4..0x007A6EB4), asks the actor for its animation id via vtable+0x2C, applies it through actor vtable+0x84 and writes the speed into actor+0x138; then derives the ground normal from the actor's quaternion (f_8C..f_98) and clears the gravity word.
evidence: NEW: this address is slot 1 (the start slot) of two action vtables, 0x00762AC0 (horse input action, update = confident Field_Action_MoveInput) and 0x00762B7C (horse step action, update = maybe_Field_Action_MoveStep), which confirms it is the shared start routine of the mounted movement rather than a one-off init. The name is kept because 'InitHorseParams' states what it computes; 0.5 because the exact physical meaning of the five floats is not proven.

name: Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue
summary: Continuation test shared by the two horse actions: returns 2 while the rider is steering/accelerating, 3 when the actor may run on, and -1 when the action is finished.
evidence: It appears as slot 13 (offset 0x34) of both horse vtables 0x00762ABC and 0x00762B78, the same slot 0x0030271C fills for the run action; the return values 2/3/-1 are directly visible.

name: Field_Action_HorseTurn
signature: void Field_Action_HorseTurn(float* out, const HorseAction* self, const float* inputDir, float speed)
summary: Turn step of the horse/run action: below the speed threshold it rotates the current reference heading (camera forward, or self f_2C..f_34) toward inputDir by at most f_40 degrees and writes the result; above it, it lerps the heading toward inputDir and renormalises.
evidence: It belongs to the class whose vtable 0x762B78 also holds maybe_Field_Action_InitHorseParams, maybe_Field_Action_MoveStep and Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue, and is entered from that class's 0x303480 vtable slot (`bl 0x3038CC` at 0x303714). The signature gains the turn-scale float that the ABI passes in s0 and Ghidra dropped.

name: maybe_Field_Action_MoveStep
summary: Per-frame movement step for field actions: samples analog move/look sticks, applies collision movement, and handles wall bumps.

summary: Applies a movement delta to the actor with collision: casts the actor position against the map collision, clamps the delta to the first hit and then moves the actor node.

name: Field_CreateActionMoveStep

name: maybe_Ui_TextLinePool_Init
summary: Step 0 of the small-window step table at 0x00729398 (entry 0; the sibling entry 0x00304D70 is Ui_SmallWindow_InputToState1). When the global 'pool dirty' byte is set it rebuilds the shared pool of 0x1C-byte records (zeroed, class descriptor 0x007F52B8 installed, stored through *0x007BE300) and clears the flag; it then reads the input state and the save bytes at bag+0x985C / bag+0x2CFD and pushes the next sub-state ids (6, 0xB, 0xC..0x18) onto the state vector at self+0x3B8.

The disassembly (0x00304900..0x00304D44) shows the lazy 0x1C-byte-record pool rebuild behind a global flag byte and the std_InlinedVector16_PushByte calls on self+0x3B8. What the 0x1C-byte records are (text lines or something else) is still unverified, so the name keeps maybe_. The 0x24A98 in the disassembly is only the save-work base the function reads two flag bytes from (bag+0x985C and bag+0x2CFD); there is no Item_LookupRecord call and no item-id range anywhere in it, so this is not item code despite the 'Text' in the name.

The named caller maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx uses the return value as the number of items gained, which matches the purchase role.

name: Shop_SellItem
signature: u32 Shop_SellItem(u32* screen, int itemId, int count, int inventorySlot, int memberIndex)
summary: Sell path: looks the item up, removes the units from a party member's inventory (memberIndex < 0x1F) or from the bag, and credits the party gold with record field +0x1C x count. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the item is unknown or the count is invalid.
evidence: CORRECTED: its twin Shop_BuyItemForMember (0x0031120C) passes -price*count to the same ItemBag gold helper 0x00613FC0, while this function passes +record[+0x1C]*count (the sell-price field, not the buy price +0x18) and calls Member_RemoveItemAtSlot / the bag removal helper 0x006115BC - so the old 'BuyItemToBag' had the transaction direction backwards. Named callers include Ui_ShopItemList_BeginBuy / Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx.

name: Ui_ActivateScreenMessageAndModel
summary: Activates a screen's message window and model: sets the message window's active byte, binds the screen's 0x88 sub-object into the message page and re-binds the screen's model.
evidence: NEW: the two callees are now named (maybe_Ui_Slot_BindControl for the message page at +0x1E18 and maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_DetachChild for the model) and twelve screens call it, so the 'activate message and model' reading is confirmed.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_ShowItemInfo
summary: Refreshes the item screen's detail pane for one item: resolves the item row, writes the item name into the label at owner+0x28+0x1DA0 and toggles the pane at owner+0x28+0x1C80 depending on whether the id falls in the equipment ranges 0xA4..0x9BF / 0xB19..0xB1C.
evidence: Both callers are now named Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput and maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_OpenList, so this is the item screen's detail refresh and not a debug label. The body resolves the row with Item_LookupRecord, writes the name through maybe_Ui_MedalPrizeWindow_SetItemText and branches on the equipment id ranges from FACTS.md.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemIcon_PlaceInLine
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemIcon_PlaceInLine(TextLine* line, u32 itemId, u32 column, int glyphSlot)
summary: Places an inline item icon into a text line: when glyphSlot is negative it looks the item up and, if the id is equipment (0xA4..0x9BF or 0xB19..0xB1C), resolves its icon category with func_0066C724 and writes it into the line at column; otherwise it maps the equipment slot through the party member's record before writing.
evidence: CORRECTED: the parameters are a text line plus column/glyph slot, and the body writes through func_002F6ACC on the line object, so 'PlaceItemInMemberSlot' described the lookup, not the operation. The body does resolve item rows, so this is item-icon placement code (not a text-measurement function); the exact line API is unnamed, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_TextBuild_Start
summary: Starts a multi-part text build: lays out part 0 and, when the record has more than 1/2 lines, parts 1 and 2 with their style ids; plays SE 0xE70 when part 3 begins and reports completion after 50 frames.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named maybe_Text_LayoutKernParts and the line count is read from the record's +0x44, so the function is the start/step of the multi-part text layout; the 50-frame wait is the caller-visible completion delay.

name: maybe_Text_LayoutEmitStyleRuns
signature: u32 maybe_Text_LayoutEmitStyleRuns(TextBuilder* self, TextRecord* rec, int part, int extraOffset)
summary: Walks the text record's characters from the end and, for every run of three or more characters that share the same style byte (0x06 = inherit), emits the run as one glyph draw through 0x0044641C; returns 1 when anything was emitted. The `part` argument selects which byte of the 24-bit style word is compared.
evidence: The body compares `*(char*)(&style + part)` between consecutive glyphs (func_0064ACEC style lookup) and only emits when the run length is greater than 2, so it groups runs by style; there is no kerning anywhere in it, so 'KernParts' was misleading. The caller is Ui_TextBuild_Start (0x00311898).

name: maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_SetStyleResource
signature: void maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_SetStyleResource(TextBuilder* self, u32 layout, int styleId, u32 extra)
summary: Binds style/font resource: releases previous handle in table 0x007B4D68 with Ui_Object_DestroyChildren and stores new resource from maybe_Gfx_Effect_CreateByIdFromObject at +0x8C (or +0x90 for style 0x697).
evidence: Not an item table. Called by maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_StepLayout (0x0031258C); manages resource handle destruction via Ui_Object_DestroyChildren (0x0017C51C).

name: maybe_Ui_Object_ReleaseHandles
summary: Clears four state words (+0x04, +0x08, +0x28, +0x94) and releases the two tagged handles at +0x8C and +0x90 through the shared 0x007B4D68 handle table (22-bit index / 10-bit tag check), destroying each resolved object via 0x0017C51C.
evidence: NEW: the release pattern is exactly the shared tagged handle table (index masked with 0x3FFFFF, tag compared with >>10), so 'release handles' is right, but the destroy callee 0x0017C51C is only the maybe_ 'Ui_DestroyChildList' and one caller is itself maybe_. The 0x8C/0x90 pair is on a UI-part/resource object rather than a generic Ui_Object, so the wording keeps maybe_ 0.40.

name: Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout
signature: void Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout(TextBuilder* self, u32 textObj, const u32* styleMask)
summary: Initialises a text builder from a text object: resolves the font metrics and layout box, clamps the origin, selects the active part styles from a bit mask (or from the metrics for multi-style fonts) and computes the per-part baseline/height entries (up to four 0x18-byte descriptors at +0x30).
evidence: The named caller Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntry (0x006258B0) invokes it for multi-line rows after the row lookup and count, and the body calls the named Ui_TextBuilder_SetNumericValues plus the text/layout helpers; initialising the row's text layout is the only reading that fits both sides.

name: maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_StepLayout
summary: Per-frame driver of a timed text/effect layout: interpolates the text origin over a 0x10-frame window, at frame 0 binds the style resource and plays the part sound, at frames 5 and 15 spawns effects 0x69E/0x69F (or plays sounds 0xECC/0xEEA) depending on each part's position, and updates each of the four parts' 0x18-byte entry at self+0x18*i.
evidence: The style binder maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_SetStyleResource and the effect/sound helpers are named, and the frame/part arithmetic is explicit; the owning class is still inferred from 0x00311898 and the neighbour names around 0x0038xx are contested, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_BuildGlyphBuffers
summary: Fills the message widget's two per-line character buffers (full-width at +0xE0 and half-width at +0xF4, 32 chars each) from the message records of lineCount lines, stopping at each 0xFF end marker, and copies the per-line box metrics into +0xB8..+0xDC.
evidence: Ghidra lost a register (unaff_r10 is used as the half-width buffer base), so the buffer choice is only visible through the font-record +0x21 test; the named caller Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById and Ui_Message_SetItemNameArg support the glyph-buffer reading, and no item lookup is involved (not item code).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_BuildGlyphMetrics
summary: Loads the layout metrics for a message text id: line height and base advance into +0x118/+0x119, then fills the eight 0x30-byte glyph slots (+0x130 advance, +0x134/+0x138/+0x13C offsets) from the record's 8-byte glyph list, marking unused slots with glyph id 0xFF.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the now-named Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById (0x003139EC), which calls it right after resolving the text record, and the record fields (font id +0x20, base +0x22, glyph count +0x10, list +0x14) are read at the offsets the summary gives. No item/inventory access, so the glyph wording is not an item misread.

name: Ui_TextObject_CreateMessageGlyph
signature: void Ui_TextObject_CreateMessageGlyph(TextObject* self, u32 recordId, u32 styleId)
summary: Allocates and configures the glyph object for one message character: looks up the character record, fills the 0x3B8-byte glyph descriptor (colour, size, layer, font), registers it in the glyph list and binds its animation timing.
evidence: Called from Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById and the body performs the record lookup, descriptor fill and glyph-list append; the class is anchored by that named caller.

name: maybe_Ui_StartIntroModelSequence
summary: Starts a scripted model sequence for a UI screen: creates the 0x1EB0 model/effect helper with id 0x15, binds the screen model, sets the UI mode word and copies the current view rectangle.
evidence: No confident caller; the body calls Ui_GetCore and Ui_SlotTable_BuildEntriesFromRecords, but the screen class is not proven; kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_EnsureSubObject34
summary: Lazily creates the type-0x34 sub-object (0x37C-byte class, ctor 0x2D5A08) at self+0x6B8 unless the UI flag says the window is busy; returns 1 when created.
evidence: The 0x66B004(sys,0x34) gate, Mem_AllocAligned, Ui_SubObjectHost_Ctor and the 0x2D5A08 ctor are visible and identical in shape to 0x3143C8 (type 0x2C), but the owning window is unnamed.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyPlacementTransform
summary: Builds the message window's 3D placement from a UI row's three rotation angles (row+0x10/+0x14/+0x18) plus a scale/offset pair, then pushes the resulting orientation and the camera matrix onto the 2D-model node of the scene (work+8 -> +0x74).
evidence: Its caller maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_Update (0x00314620) resolves the current message row and calls it with row+8 when a window move finishes, and the body contains no glyph access at all - it builds quaternions and calls Ui_ScreenLayer_SetCameraMatrix on the 2D-model node, so the placement-transform reading fits.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById(MessageText* self, u32 textId, u32 glyphSource, int mode)
summary: Points the message-text widget at a new text id: copies the 0xc2-byte character template, records the text id and mode byte, then rebuilds the glyph buffers and metrics and copies the three base offsets from the font record.
evidence: Callers 0x313B78 and 0x381020 (both 'set text then push pane' wrappers); memcpy 0xc2 into +0x4d4 (32 char codes); +0x5a0 mode byte; calls 0x312EA4/0x312D04/0x312970; f_10c/f_110/f_114 from font record +0x24.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextByIdAnimated
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextByIdAnimated(UiWindow* self, u32 textId, u32 glyphSource)
summary: Same text swap as the Plain variant but with animation enabled (mode 1): sets the text on the widget at self+0x1C, copies the pane rectangle, clears the glyph count and refreshes the linked records at +0x67C.

name: maybe_Ui_ProgressEntry_RecalcPercent
summary: Calculates a 0..110 percentage rating for one of eight 0x30-byte progress/achievement entries based on current, threshold, and max values.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyText
summary: Pushes the current character codes into the 3DS text renderer: picks the glyph range for every code in the 32-slot code array, inserts/removes characters in the text object, sets the colour/scale of the message, and selects one of 30 message-window key-window colours based on the character style byte.
evidence: Calls 0x381B94 (icon-flash ctor), 0x380BE8, 0x6444F4, 0x63E998, 0x1901F4/0x1902B4/0x1902CC (Text_InsertLineChar / font record), 0x19201C Text_ApplyFontRecord; 30-way switch over font style emitting control ids 0x17..0x31; direct callers are none (installed in a vtable).

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenFromByte

evidence: The 0x62564C(&f_5A4) release, the global counter increment and maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple for values below 4 match the reading, and the shape matches Ui_Window_EnsureSubObject34 with type 0x2C, but the owner class is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateMovement
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateMovement(MessageWindow * self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Per-frame message-window tick: with no active move object it commits the queued BGM/voice id, updates the glyph transforms and text callback and clears the eight sub-widget states; while a move object at +0x6B8 is active it drives and releases it.

name: Ui_FieldScreen_Init
summary: Constructor of the large field/menu screen object: allocates and attaches its five parts (smith menu 0x12BC, smith sub-window 0x127C, talk window 0x3984, 0x120-byte 2D drawable, 0x26C-byte panel), then initialises the part handle tags, the two 14-byte 0xFF index tables and the 24 x 0x18 timer/slot block at +0x11C.

Inside, the first three allocations are made by the already-named Ui_SmithMenu_Ctor, Ui_SmithMenu_SubWindow_Ctor and Ui_TalkWindow_Ctor, and Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable performs the attach; that fixes the composite-constructor role, although the screen own menu name stays generic.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseResources
summary: The composite UI window release body: it drops the move object, releases model/pack/sound handles and destroys the embedded lists.
evidence: Four teardown callers (Ui_Window_ReleaseChildLists, ShopWindow_Dtor, ShopWindow_ReleaseObject, Field_ResizeObject) and the body's ten Pack_ReleaseHandle calls plus two GameWork model-handle releases identify a window resource-release routine, not a generic destructor.

name: Fs_IsSndqPath

name: Ui_DiveForm_ListPanel_DeletingDestructor

name: Pb1
signature: void Pb1(int arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: Ui_Window_ApplyState
summary: Applies a window state id: resets the pending child list, re-links the two sub-panes at +0x3E0/+0x4A4, dispatches their visibility, then looks the state up in the table at self+0x52C and binds the record through 0x001DAB30. State ids below 0x10 are remapped by +0x10 when the class flag at +0x388 is set.
evidence: The readable C stops at the first broadcast; asm 0x003161A0..0x0031620C shows the argument being remapped (state<0x10 && f_388==1 -> state+0x10), range-checked against self->f_52C->f_60 and bound to self->f_52C->f_58 + state*8 via 0x001DAB30. The 7 callers are literally the Ui_Window_GotoState0/4/5/6/7/0x21/0x22 wrappers passing constant ids, so the "release pending actions" reading was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FinishIfBusy
summary: If the widget at self+0x11C reports busy (vtable+0x14) it is told to finish (vtable+0x10); 64 bytes, same two-call idiom as 0x00316568 and 0x003175E0.

name: Svc_TimerSub_RunDue_24
summary: Timer pump for the 24-slot timer sub-system: runs the base update, advances the 1/30 s clock at +0x124/+0x128, fires the armed callback of slot self->f_120 (0x18-byte entries at self+0x11C, adjustor table at +0x13C) and clears the UI mode word when the stop byte +0x540 is set.
evidence: The 1/30 s literal (0x3D088889), the 24-slot limit and the 0x18-byte entry layout with code pointer +0x34 / adjustor +0x38 are explicit; the same template appears with 0x0B and 5 slots at 0x0029A920 / 0x002E9614, and this one is vtable 0x00763034 slot 1 (slot 0 is the registered native Pb1).

name: maybe_Ui_EnableViewIfSet
summary: When the screen's view slot at self+0x541 is not -1, enables the view object (child-screen sub-object +0x1C, virtual +0xC with 1).

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_DivePanel_SelectTargetState
summary: Evaluates system and UI modes to select the dive panel target state id (0x0B, 0x0D, 0x13, 0x0A, or -1).
evidence: Called by state transitions 0x003170D0 (Ui_WindowState_Goto15OrMenuState) and 0x003178D0 (Ui_WindowState_Goto5Or16); selects next target state id; returns a value; kept maybe at 0.45.

summary: Interior continuation of dive panel state selector 0x00316388; evaluates mode checks and party string.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_DivePanel_UpdateAvailability
summary: Updates dive panel widget availability and entry name based on Ui_IsMode(3) and pending list at +0x534.
evidence: Operates on DivePanel widget at +0x38C and list at +0x534; covered entry in Ghidra; kept maybe at 0.45.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ResetChildrenA
summary: Window reset step: flushes the pending callbacks (0x00316410), drains the child ring to zero, re-links the two embedded panes at +0x3E0 and +0x4A4 and broadcasts visibility flag 1 to the first.
evidence: NEW: the shared callees are now identified from the disassembly, and none of them frees anything - func_0062F070 (0x0062F070) counts the children of the intrusive ring at self+0x110, func_0010EBD8 (0x0010EBD8) detaches one child from that ring and re-initialises its node, func_00123594 (0x00123594) splices an embedded pane node back into the ring, and Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren (0x001A5F9C) only calls virtual +0x1C on each child. So the old 'DestroyChildren' wording was wrong: the function resets the ring to the class's fixed set of embedded panes and then sets their visibility. The class is still unknown (no caller and no vtable identity), so the maybe_ stays and the letter only distinguishes the six copies.

name: Ui_Window_UpdateInputMode
summary: Applies an input-mode change: starts the +0x38C tween with the new mode, refreshes the window layout, then picks the matching cursor/help animation id (1, 0x14 or 0x15) by asking which of the three input sources is active (Ui_IsMode 0/1/2) and commits it on the animator.
evidence: NEW: the input-source queries are now the named Ui_IsMode and the three-way id mapping is fully readable, so the function really is the 'input mode changed -> select cursor/help animation' update.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_DivePanel_HandleInput
summary: Handles dive panel input events; routes sub-widget selections at +0x38C, toggles pending flag at +0x53C, and drives tween transitions on self->f_11c.
evidence: Slot 0 in dive panel state table 0x00729860 alongside handlers 0x00316B44 and 0x00317188; kept maybe at 0.45.

name: Ui_Window_GotoState0x21
summary: Applies window state 0x21 (Ui_Window_ApplyState), runs the +0x38C member step 0x00316410 and releases the +0x38C tween/list with 0x0029126C(...,1).
evidence: NEW: Ui_Window_ApplyState (0x00316140) is now a confident name and the state id 0x21 is the literal first argument, so 'GotoState0x21' is exactly what the function does; the table word 0x00729968 puts it in the dive-panel state table next to the other confirmed handlers. Confirmed at 0.5 (the meaning of state 0x21 is not needed for the name).

name: Ui_Window_UpdateCursorKind
summary: Chooses the cursor kind (0..4) for the input-state object from the current tween/page value and the active input source, marking the state dirty before changing it.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetRecordHandle
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetRecordHandle(UiMessageWindow* self, unsigned int record_handle, unsigned char flag)
summary: Stores the flag byte at self+0x500, resolves the tagged record component selected by the window state (+0x388 picks the +0x60 state value 2 or 3) and copies the subject/speaker string into the window's text buffer at +0x4A4.
evidence: Its vtable sibling 0x0032BD88 has the same body for its own window class (self+0x2D4) and was named Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetRecordHandle by another pass, so the 'set record handle plus copy name' reading is shared; it stays vtable-only, hence 0.50.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FinishIconLoad
summary: State handler that completes the asynchronous icon/catalogue load: gets the UI root singleton through 0x006F2224 and calls the named Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad on it.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x00383C18 is the confident Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad and the table word at 0x007298A8 places the function among Ui_Window_GotoState5/9/6Or4 handlers; that table uses the generic Ui_Window state names, so the old 'DiveForm' class attribution is no longer supported and the class prefix is reduced to Ui_Window. The body is a one-call state step.

name: Ui_Window_GotoState0
signature: void Ui_Window_GotoState0(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies window state 0 and, unless the global byte work+0x2D1E5 is set, points the tween at +0x4A4 at animation entry 0x0F (0x1F when +0x388 is set) from the window's animation table.

summary: Window state process: updates the layout tween, and once it is idle asks the controller for state 0x17 and commits the transition. Always returns 1 (frame consumed).
evidence: NEW: the state id 0x17 is literal and the guards use the now-understood idle test 0x0062F680; the same body appears 17 times in this block and two copies (0x00317760, 0x00317864) add a fade-page store, which confirms that this is the plain state-0x17 process. Confirmed.

name: Ui_DiveForm_DivePanel_StartIfNotBusy
summary: Starts the panel transition (tween state 3) only while the busy byte +0x528 is clear, then commits it; always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the table word 0x00729940 places it in the dive-panel state table (the neighbouring entries are the named 0x0031611C start, 0x00316BF0 and 0x003176A0 handlers), and the body is a single guarded tween request 3. Confirmed.

name: Ui_WindowState_Goto3

summary: Window state process: updates the layout tween and, once it is idle, requests controller state 3 and commits it. Always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: same body as the confirmed 0x00316BF4 with the literal state changed to 3; the duplicate at 0x003176AC proves the two-class copy pattern. Confirmed.

summary: Prepares the window for state 7: stores mode 5 at +0x524, starts the shared icon-cache load on the UI root singleton, drains the window's action queue and finally applies state 7.
evidence: It is entry 0x00729878 of the same dive-panel state table as Ui_Window_GotoState0/5/9 and ends with the now-named Ui_Window_ApplyState(self, 7), so the state number is proven. The body additionally stores mode 5 at +0x524, calls maybe_Ui_IconCache_BeginLoad on the root singleton and drains the queue through 0x0010EBD8 before the state change.

name: Ui_Window_GotoState9

evidence: NEW: the five callers are now named placement/input helpers (Field_FindFreePlacementCell2D, maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaA/B/C), so the function is the shared 'does this rect hit an object with this owner id' test rather than a UI cursor helper; the record owner compare and the rect math are unchanged.

name: Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh
signature: int Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh(int parent, int spriteRes, unsigned int arg3)

name: maybe_Field_FindPlacementCellWithDelta

name: maybe_Field_CreateActorRuntimeState
summary: Creates and registers the large (~0x298-byte) field state/actor object from a static descriptor, resolves its derived class through the global handle table and returns it with three fields cleared.

name: maybe_Field_GetStateId
summary: Returns field state id 0x27 or 0x28 depending on boolean check 0x005A6168.
evidence: Called across field state and actor initialisers; returns a value; returns state constant 0x27 or 0x28; kept maybe at 0.45.
