name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtorE
summary: Deleting destructor in the 0x31Axxx actor/sprite-actor block: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the object's embedded base node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Body is the standard template (same 56 bytes as 0x0021BC50 etc.) and the block holds maybe_Field_CreateActorRuntimeState (0x0031A8C0) and Gfx_SpriteActor_SetPosAndScale (0x0031AF44); the inherited 'DestroySubObjectAt24C' was wrong because the +0x24C node is the object's own embedded base, not a sub-object it owns.

name: Field2D_TestAreaPassable
signature: u32 Field2D_TestAreaPassable(void* self, const int* point)
summary: Tests a 2x2 sample of map cells starting at point+self offsets with Map_IsCellPassable; if all four are passable it asks Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer whether the box is clear and returns 1 for a clear area, 0 otherwise.
evidence: CORRECTED: the callers are the named Actor2D movement/turn functions (Actor2DMoveEx, Actor2DTurnTarget, Actor2DRunNotSyncDir, Actor2DSlowWalkNotSyncDir) plus Ui_Overlay_TryTouchSelect, and the callees are Map_IsCellPassable / Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer - this is 2D field/map collision, not UI hit testing, so the old Ui_ prefix was wrong.

name: Gfx_Actor_ApplyModelSize
summary: Applies the actor's configured model size and/or scale to its scene object; mode picks which of the two values to push (0 resets nothing, 1 pushes size, 2/3 push scale).
evidence: Switch on mode calling Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize (0x005F3500) with self+0x24/0x28 and 0x005F36E0 with self+0x2C; default branch converts and applies both; caller 0x0016216C = maybe_Actor_SetEnabledBoth.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_SetPosAndScale
signature: void Gfx_SpriteActor_SetPosAndScale(SpriteActor* self, const float* pos, u32 scale)
summary: Moves the sprite node to pos (x,y) and applies scale when the actor has a live scene node.
evidence: Guard on self+0x20 (scene node); 0x5F3500 sets node position, 0x5F36E0 sets scale; identical pair used by 0x31AF8C.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_SetModelAndPos
signature: void Gfx_SpriteActor_SetModelAndPos(SpriteActor* self, const void* params, u32 modelId, u32 variant)
summary: Applies the sprite model selected by (modelId, variant) to a 2D actor: creates the table entry, stores its anim id and the ids on the scene node, applies the priority byte, sets the model size from the locator param block and starts the idle animation.
evidence: Both callers are the warp locators Actor2DWarpLocator and ActorWarpToMapJumpLocatorID, which pass a locator param block plus the model/variant fields of the destination entry; the named callees (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation) confirm the 'apply model + placement/animation' role.

name: Gfx_Actor_BindModelHandle
summary: Resolves the model handle stored in f_14 through the global handle table and caches the pointed object plus its derived values (object+0x78/+0x7C, position ptr +0x20, a byte from object[0x2E]+0x128, and object[0x75]) into the actor.
evidence: func_002A95B4 is the handle-table acquire (global buckets 0x2A9640/0x2A9644, key = f_14>>11); vtable 0x7631C8 also holds 0x31B628/0x31AE0C/0x31B114 (Gfx_Actor_ApplyAppearance*).

name: Gfx_Actor_ApplyAppearance
summary: The actor appearance applier: it stores the model id/variant and hides the default model when the actor is in a special mode.
evidence: The body guards with 0x002A9648, writes f_20->f_1D4 and f_B8->f_128, tests Field_GetActorModelSetIndex and the ctx+0x27F mode byte, then calls 0x62EF8C(...,0)/0x2D0E84 and returns 1 when handled.

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_ApplyAppearanceB
summary: Probably the post-model-change appearance variant, but the body only proves a visibility/release path on f_14 and the +0xB8 sub-object.
evidence: It tests the handle-table entry on self->f_14, queries virtual +0x50, checks * Field_GetActorModelSetIndex and the mode byte, then hides/releases the old model. The companion * relationship to 0x31B114 is plausible, but the B variant is not independently identified.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_ShowForModelSet
summary: The model-set show path: it validates the model-set index and, outside the four menu modes, enables model visibility and re-applies the scale.
evidence: The body calls Field_GetActorModelSetIndex on node+0x36, compares the mode byte at ctx+0x48+0x27F with 1..4, calls 0x62EF8C(...,1) and 0x2D0E84(&node->f_B8->f_FC); three run/walk callers use it.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_HideForModelSet
summary: The model-set hide mirror: it is byte-identical to 0x31B328 except that the visibility call passes 0.
evidence: Six walk/run movement callers (Actor2DMoveEx, Actor2DWalk, Actor2DSlowWalk and their NotSyncDir variants) invoke it, and the body matches the show variant except for 0x62EF8C(...,0), so the hide role is directly demonstrated.

name: Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_Create
summary: Allocates a sprite-animation bank (64-byte rows out of a shared 50-slot pool), stamps it with a rotating slot id, initialises the clip table and returns it. One clip only, unlike 0x31CD88 which adds the TurnL/TurnR clips.
evidence: Caller maybe_Gfx_ResourceHandle_AcquireType1; allocation helper 0x2A96F0(ownerId,0x40000000); 50-entry slot table (mod 0x32); result[7] = slot id, vtable g_0031b61c; clip bookkeeping fields 8..0xe.

name: Gfx_Actor_ReleaseModelHandle
summary: Releases the actor's entry from the global handle table (slot selected by f_1C & 0x3F is cleared to {0, 0x3FFFFFF}) and then frees the actor.
evidence: Clears an 8-byte (ptr,tag) bucket slot; tag 0x3FFFFFF is the 'empty' key used by the 0x2A9640 handle table; followed by func_002A9748 and operator delete 0x10F6CC; vtable 0x7631BC.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_ApplyColourAnim
summary: Applies a sprite actor's colour/animation state: pushes the stored colour when the +0x18 bit 0 is clear, otherwise resolves the animation id at +0x49, sets colour+alpha and falls back to the virtual update.
evidence: The named ActorSetActionSeq caller and the colour setters plus the f_49 animation lookup support the combined colour+animation reading, but the exact bit meanings are still guesses.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClass
summary: Walks the node's RTTI chain and releases it with the routine matching its base class (0x182AC4 for class 0x007C4D9C, 0x232248 for 0x007C4E50).
evidence: NEW: the callers are named ActorRideCSVehicle and the release helpers are now named (Field_Object_ReleaseSpriteResource, maybe_ModelPreview_ResetTransform), so this is confirmed to be the class-dispatched release path.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseChildResource
summary: When the object at +0x20 has a child at +0x160 whose virtual +0xC reports busy, releases the child's handle at +0x11C through 0x0030AC50, which itself tail-calls 0x00562FD0 with the child's +0xA8 value.
evidence: The disassembly shows the child pointer is loaded from self->f_20->f_160 (Ghidra lost it into unaff_r4, so the readable C is damaged), the child's virtual +0xC is tested, and 0x0030AC50 is called on child+0x11C; 0x0030AC50 is `ldr r0,[r0,#0xa8]; cmp r0,#0; beq; b 0x562FD0`, i.e. release one handle. The class prefix is still unproven because the only callers are the two Field_GadgetList helpers, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_ApplyMotion
summary: Commits the actor's stored motion to its scene object according to a mode: mode 0/1 copy position and direction (0 also notifies the effect owner), mode 2 copies and hands the offset target to the sprite mover, mode 3 normalises the direction, builds the rotation from the scene facing and moves the sprite toward the rotated point.
evidence: The mode switch writes the scene object's +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 and ends in the named Gfx_EffectPart_SetTargetPoint / Gfx_SpriteActor_MoveTowardPoint, which shows it applies a motion rather than ticking one; the caller 0x0016216C is still only a maybe_ name, so it stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClassB
summary: Second class-dispatch releaser: walks the node's RTTI chain and calls 0x183918 or 0x235378 for the matching base class (0x007C4D9C / 0x007C4E50).
evidence: NEW: same two class ids and the same caller (ActorRideCSVehicle) as the confirmed 0x0031B978, and the release helpers are named (maybe_Field_Object_ReleaseSpriteResourceB, maybe_Ui_Overlay_SyncSlotFromHandle).

name: Field_Actor_SetWorldPosition
signature: void Field_Actor_SetWorldPosition(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 flags, float* pos)
summary: Writes a new x/y/z world position into the actor's transform (+0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4), marks the transform dirty (+0x118 = 1) and notifies the owner through func_005F5F54; if the actor's parent object still resolves through vtable slot +0xC, the attached sub-object at index 0x47 is refreshed as well.
evidence: Body stores arg4[0], arg4[1], arg4[2] to f_9c/f_a0/f_a4, sets f_118 = 1, then calls func_005F5F54(actor, arg3, 1) and finally func_0030AC50(arg1[0x47]) after the vtable +0xC check. f_9C/f_A0/f_A4 + f_118 is the same transform layout used by 0x003228E8/0x00322A08, and the function sits inside the Gfx_SpriteActor_* block (neighbours maybe_Gfx_Actor_FinishMotion 0x0031C3F4, Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_CreateWithTurns 0x0031CD88).

name: Gfx_Actor_BindTransformFromHandle
summary: Resolves the handle in f_14 and copies the source object's position/rotation (f_9C/f_A0/f_A4), composes the world transform (0x669D88), and caches size/scale fields (f_138/f_13C) plus two bytes from the model slot at f_160.
evidence: Same handle lookup as 0x31B048; func_00669D88 is the vector transform helper used by Field/Battle actor code; writes self+0x24..0x48 and marks source f_15D=1; vtable 0x7631E8 next to Gfx_SpriteActor_UpdateMotion.

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_FinishMotion
summary: Finishes the actor's current motion: takes a handle-table release, applies the final transform (scene +0x21C, +0x138/+0x13C), copies the stored rotation, toggles the scene flag +0x160->f_599 from +0x48, re-finalises the actor (0x005F5DA8), clears the motion handle and returns 1 when a motion was active.
evidence: Gfx_HandleTable_Release is now a confident callee and the surrounding module is the Gfx actor-motion code, which supports the reading; the individual scene writes are still only described and there is no caller, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_UpdateMotion
summary: Per-frame movement integrator for a sprite actor: advances the node along its stored direction with damping, recomputes the normalised direction when it changes, stops at the target distance and derives the alpha/offset from the view direction.
evidence: The position/direction fields and the acos/sqrt helpers match the sprite-actor motion family; without a caller the body itself is self-contained and consistent with the neighbouring SpriteActor helpers.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_MoveTowardPoint
summary: Turns a sprite actor toward a target point and advances it, choosing between two rotation states depending on whether the target is in front of or behind the current facing.
evidence: Caller is now confidently maybe_Gfx_Actor_UpdateMotion and both branches end in the same named transform apply; the virtual +0x84 selection is unexplained but the steering role is clear.

name: Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_CreateWithTurns
summary: Same pool-backed animation bank as 0x31B4F0 but pre-populates five extra clip slots, including the named clips "TurnL" and "TurnR", and the follow-up idle clips.

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_ReleaseHandleSlot

name: Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory

summary: Generic FieldParty event dispatch: always calls vtable+0x3C, then routes event id 0 to vtable+0x138 and any other id to vtable+0x13C.

summary: Iterates member slots (stride 0x60, offset +0x1740) up to count at +0x3240 and invokes per-slot function 0x001FA9D4.

evidence: Loop identical to 0x0031D688 in FieldParty vtable calling alternate per-slot routine 0x001FD2CC; not an item loop; flag does not apply; kept maybe at 0.45.

name: Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache
summary: Shared base constructor for a family of large UI screens: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs base vtable g_0031efcc, clears the flag byte at g_0031efd0, initialises a text-line cache at +0x498 (twice-nested sub-object) and constructs 72 (0x48) 0x60-byte layout entries at +0x48. Concrete screens call it and immediately overwrite the vtable with their own.
evidence: Six callers are themselves screen constructors (0x002AB2B0 maybe_Ui_LargeStateObjectCtor, 0x004C04F4, 0x004F579C, 0x0059DE54, 0x0059F10C `Ui_ScreenObject_Ctor_*`), and 0x004C04F4 shows the pattern `puVar2 = func_0031EECC(); *puVar2 = g_004c056c;` i.e. base ctor plus subclass vtable. Callees are 0x0020002C (Ui_Screen_CtorBase), 0x00398B28 (maybe_Ui_TextLineCache_InitAndReturn), 0x002BB828 and std_ConstructArray(...,0x60,0x48).

name: FieldParty_DeletingDestructor

name: maybe_Ui_TextFade_Update

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_HandleIdle

name: maybe_FieldParty_SubObjectDtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a FieldParty sub-object: installs the base vtable g_fieldPartyVtable, destroys the sixteen 0x58-byte entries at +0xB464 with std_destroy_range, runs the base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_StepUpdate
summary: Frame update of one battle action step: runs the state machine 0xE7D/0xE92/0xE9B/0xEA1/0xEA7/0xEB7, plays SE/popup 0x62, sets the effect direction, resolves the action row through Game_GetDataManager and returns 1 once the +0xD2 done flag is set.
evidence: States 0xE7D..0xEB7 and the +0xD2 completion flag; calls Ui_PopupEntry_PlayById(...,0x62,0), func_005E7848, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, func_0063FC70 (action-row lookup) and func_00630BB8. Renamed from Battle_ActionSequence_Update because 0x004F7320 already merged with that name (the whole-director frame update); this is the per-action step machine that its 0x31Fxxx InitStep/WaitStep/HandleIdle siblings belong to.

summary: Constructor of the second 2D variant of the field object class: runs the base constructor, installs vtable 0x007634AC and initialises the same three trailing words (-1, 0, 0xFFFFFC00).

name: maybe_Battle_ActionObject_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the action-sequence object: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x125C through Pack_Handle_Dtor, runs the shared base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object. Its non-deleting twin is 0x0031F9F0.

summary: In-place destructor companion of 0x0031F9C4: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x125C and runs the base destructor 0x00200220, without freeing the memory.

summary: Deleting destructor of the small slot sub-object: runs the base destructor and frees it.
evidence: Ui_SlotSub_Ctor (0x00326838) constructs it 0x20 bytes earlier, and Casino_Slot_DetectWinLines (0x00326870) follows in the same casino-slot block; renamed from '_Delete' to the engine's dtor vocabulary.

name: Casino_Slot_DetectWinLines
summary: Reads the five reel symbols and detects winning lines: it scans the three visible rows for runs of three or more equal symbols (treating symbol 6 as wild) and calls the payout calculator for each run.
evidence: Reads 5 glyph codes with 0x0064ACEC into a 5x3 table, then for each of three rows counts runs and calls 0x00326B8C(self, symbol, row, runLength) when runLength>1; the 3-row loop and symbol table are exactly the slot result layout; named parent Ui_SlotWindow_Ctor at 0x00328EC0.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_ClearPatternLists
summary: Empties the 22 pattern/line lists of the slot window, destroying every node, and re-initialises the head pointer at +0x460.
evidence: Loops i<0x16 over a stride-0xC array of {begin,end} pairs at self+0x464/f_468, unlinks each node and calls its virtual destructor, then sets self->f_460 = self+99 & ~3. Called by the slot window destructor 0x3297CC; used together with the 22-list construction in 0x328EC0.

name: Os_LogDebugString
summary: Hands the text stored in a debug-string record to the engine log: formats s->f_8 straight into the log object's 0x80-byte message buffer (0x7AC834->+0x848), resets the write pointer, then compacts the record (memmove the 0x20-byte payload at +0xC over the header at +4, clear the +0x24 count) and returns the previous +4 value.
evidence: New: the callee 0x707C1C was disassembled - it is a fixed-size log formatter (push r0-r3, vsnprintf(buf+4, 0x80, fmt=arg2, ap), pop) and this function passes s->f_8 as that format, so this really is 'emit this record's string to the log'. Returns a value (the saved f_4), so a predicate name would be wrong; the body is undamaged.

name: Casino_Slot_CalcPatternPayout
signature: void Casino_Slot_CalcPatternPayout(SlotWindow* self, u32 symbol, int row, int runLength)
summary: Calculates the payout of one winning slot line: multiplies the symbol's payout by the bet level and the run length, adds it to the round's credit/jackpot counters, and appends the corresponding HUD/event nodes to the window's payout list.
evidence: Switch over symbol and runLength, payout multipliers g_003271EC/g_003271F0, calls 0x00642344 (bet level) and 0x00642494 (symbol value); updates self->f_40/f_3C counters with a 99 cap, builds list nodes with tags g_003271F4/0x003271F8/0x00327204/0x00445C2C and registers them via 0x001235A4 at +0x524/+0x530/+0x53C; the callers 0x00326870/0x0032792C/0x003283B4 are the slot window itself.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackA
signature: void Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackA(UiSlotWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg4)
summary: One of the slot window's per-animation callbacks: binds the anim object at self+0x588 to the layout's animation table, copies the start/end frame pair into f_18/f_1c and advances the animation to frame 1.
evidence: func_001DAD58(self+0x588, layout+0x16C) then func_0062F680 (get current anim) and g_00327270->f_70/f_74 stored into self->f_18/f_1c, then vtable+0xC(obj,1). The identical shape recurs at 0x327280/0x3273AC/0x327ECC and all use rodata 0x72ABF8, the slot window's type descriptor.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackB
signature: void Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackB(UiSlotWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Slot window callback that branches on the animation's sub-index: on index 1 it resets the reel animation and, when rows exist, plays the 'stop' transition (row 0xD) and rebinds the message pair; otherwise it just restarts the reel animation.
evidence: Same func_001DAD58/func_0062F680/func_0062F694 prologue as 0x32720C; index==1 path calls func_00328E58 (reset), func_003280C0(self,0xd,0) and func_001DAC34(self+0x588,self+0x5d0), the other path func_003275E4. f_18/f_1c again come from a frame table.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackF
summary: Slot-window animation callback that, when the reel tween at +0x588 finishes, copies the animation's final position into the window's transform fields.
evidence: 0x001DAD58(self+0x588, frame+0x16C), 0x0062F680 (tween end), copies g_003273A4->f_18/f_1C into self+0x18/+0x1C; same pattern as the other SlotWindow_AnimCallback* functions (0x32720C, 0x327280, 0x3273AC, 0x327448, 0x327ECC).

name: Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackC
signature: void Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackC(UiSlotWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Slot window callback for the reel spin/stretch animation: resets the window and applies one of two frame ranges depending on the animation sub-index.
evidence: Identical prologue to 0x32720C and the same two-table selection, but the index branch only picks g_0032743C->f_70/f_74 versus f_38/f_3C; no message-pair rebind.

name: maybe_Ui_StoreRectPairIfViewReady
signature: void maybe_Ui_StoreRectPairIfViewReady(UiSlotWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateIdleState
summary: Chooses the slot window's idle/ready animation: plays the lever/coin sound, requests state 0xB or 0xC depending on whether the bet is ready, and binds the corresponding animation to the reel object.
evidence: Calls 0x001EC1D0 (Snd_RequestBgmPlay) with 0x20, 0x003280C0(self, 0xC/0xB, 0), 0x001DAC34(self+0x588, self+0x5D0), reads g_003275DC->f_20/f_24 and f_58/f_5C, and checks the game-work value 0x0066B2CC(work+0x24A98,0) against g_003275E0.

name: Casino_Slot_ApplyBetAndPayout
signature: void Casino_Slot_ApplyBetAndPayout(SlotWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: The slot bet/payout handler: it maps bet level 0/1/2 to 1/10/100, compares the coin counter and switches the win/lose animation rows.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_SetReelState
summary: Slot-window state handler for the reel spin: when the tween finishes it either rebuilds the payout patterns (on the 'spin' input flag) or selects one of the four idle/stop animations 0xE..0x11 and binds it.
evidence: 0x001DAD58(self+0x588, frame+0x16C), 0x0062F680, tests self->f_580 bits 4/0x102, calls 0x00328E58 (reset payout anim) and 0x003283B4 (payout sequence), selects states 0xE/0xF/0x10/0x11 from flags +0x48/+0x49, then 0x001DAC34 to bind; follows 0x0032748C.

name: Casino_Slot_StepReel
signature: void Casino_Slot_StepReel(SlotMachine* self, u32 arg2, u32 frame)
summary: Slot-machine reel step: clamps the reel index f_44 from the signed direction byte f_582 and advances the wheel through the shared step routine func_004C2C60(self->f_10, 1, frame, frame>>3), then bumps the frame counter f_600.
evidence: self->f_582 sign selects f_44 = 9 / 0; func_004C2C60(self->f_10,1,arg3,arg3>>3); f_600++. Follows the named Casino_Slot_DetectWinLines 0x326870 / Casino_Slot_CalcPatternPayout 0x326B8C and Ui_SlotWindow_* methods from N_015/N_052.

name: Casino_Slot_StopReel
signature: void Casino_Slot_StopReel(SlotMachine* self, u32 reel, u32 arg3)

name: Ui_SlotWindow_ProcessPatterns

evidence: Loop i<0x16 over self+i*0xC with heads f_464/f_468, node virtual call (**(code**)(*node+8))(node,&self); destroyed nodes are unlinked exactly like 0x326AA8. On completion self->f_18/f_1c = g_00327DFC->f_50/f_54, falling back to it only if nothing was removed (bVar1). No direct callers -> vtable slot.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateReelTimer
summary: Slot machine reel timer: increments frame counter at self+0x600; on multiples of 5, executes step sequence (cases 5..10 call func_004C2C60 with descending arg 5..0; case 0xB updates float pair from 0x0072ABF8).
evidence: Entry 0x0072AC08 in slot window dispatch table; neighbours include Ui_SlotWindow_ProcessPatterns (0x00327D20) and Ui_SlotWindow_ResetPayoutAnim (0x00328E58).

name: Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackE
signature: void Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackE(UiSlotWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Slot window callback mirroring Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackB but for the second reel: on sub-index 1 it either stops the reel (row 0xD) when rows exist or falls back to the idle animation.
evidence: func_001DAD58(self+0x588,layout+0x16C), func_0062F680/func_0062F694, func_00328E58, then either func_003280C0(self,0xd,0)+func_001DAC34(self+0x588,self+0x5d0) or func_003275E4; frame pair from g_00327FA4.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateSubWidget
summary: Slot-window refresh entry: forwards the tick at self+0x56C to the embedded widget at +0x588 (Ui_Widget_Update), then drives the payout state machine - resets the payout animation, requests state 0x10/0x11 depending on the +0x48 flag, notifies the widget at self->f_14 and restores the default float pair.
evidence: NEW: all 11 callers are now named and all belong to the slot machine (Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackB/E, Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateIdleState, Ui_SlotWindow_SetReelState, Ui_SlotWindow_PayoutSequence, Casino_Slot_ApplyBetAndPayout/StopReel/ExecCommand, Ui_SlotMachine_UpdateInput), so the class is settled. The method role is not: the readable body is only halt_baddata and the disassembly shows widget update + payout reset + two state requests, so 'UpdateSubWidget' names only the first third of it. Kept maybe_.

name: Sound_PlaySeCached
summary: Plays a sound effect with de-duplication: keeps the last SE id/handle per object, stops the previous handle when a different SE is requested, skips ids in the ignored range 0xE00..0xE62, and caches the new handle.
evidence: Compares against the small ignore list g_003282A8 and the range 0xE00..0xE62, calls 0x001EBC68 (Sound_PlaySeById), 0x0063060C (is playing?) and 0x001EDF88 (stop by handle), stores f_606/f_608; called from 22 UI/sound sites (0x00311898, 0x003B65EC, 0x006D4EDC ...).

name: Sound_PlaySeCachedB
signature: void Sound_PlaySeCachedB(SlotWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)

name: Casino_Slot_BuildPayoutSequence
summary: Builds the whole payout result sequence of the slot machine: clears the pattern lists, debits the bet, then appends the chain of HUD/credit/jackpot/win animations (including the jackpot and coin-get popups) to the window's pending-action list.
evidence: Calls Ui_SlotWindow_ClearPatternLists (0x00326AA8), decrements the bet counters +0x40/+0x3C, appends 18+ tagged list nodes with tags g_00328A98..g_00328E54, calls maybe_Casino_AddJackpotPayout (0x00601320) and maybe_Casino_SpendJackpotCoin (0x00601B44), 0x00642344/0x0064B448/0x00672318; caller 0x0032792C.

summary: Stops the slot window's two payout animations and clears the ten payout interpolation values.
evidence: Virtual +0x18(0) on self->f_14->f_138 and self->f_14->f_1DE4, then zeroes self+0x5D4..+0x5F8; called by the payout/anim callbacks 0x00327280/0x003273AC/0x003275E4/0x00327ECC and by 0x0032792C.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_Ctor
signature: UiSlotWindow* Ui_SlotWindow_Ctor(UiSlotWindow* self, unsigned char mode)
summary: Constructor of the casino slot machine window: allocates the four helper objects (layout animator 0x37C, 0x1A40 reel object, effect pack 0xE84/0x130, list widget 0x1E84), zeroes the 22 pattern lists and the 0x18-slot message table.
evidence: Allocates 0x37C bytes (func_001064D4), 0x1A40 (func_0039467C) and g_00329480 bytes (func_00393B28), 0x1E84 (func_003F3650), then func_00406778 + func_00100050(&obj+0x418, g_0032948C, 0xC, 0x16) = 22 entries of 12 bytes, matching the 22 lists cleared by 0x326AA8/0x327D20. Nearby strings: 'slot_common.bxon', 'slot_pattern.bxon', 'slot_msg.bxon' (0x3291B8-0x3293E8) identify the casino slot mini-game; the same names are the table keys in game_assets/tables/packs/ui/casino_slot_3d/ (slot_msg.json, slot_common.json, slot_pattern.json).

name: Ui_SlotWindow_Destroy
summary: Deleting-destructor wrapper of the slot window: runs Ui_SlotWindow_Dtor and then frees the storage.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_Dtor
signature: UiSlotWindow* Ui_SlotWindow_Dtor(UiSlotWindow* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)

name: Ui_SpriteSpan_SetFromFlags
signature: void Ui_SpriteSpan_SetFromFlags(SpriteSpanWidget* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Rebuilds a sprite-span widget from the flag word at +0x208: selects the sprite span, then renders the numeric/text value held at +0x20c.

name: Ui_TwoListWindow_UpdateChildSelection
summary: Propagates the window's selected id (signed byte at self+0x64) to its two child widgets at self+0x130/self+0x134: each child's vtable+0x1C reports its id, and the child's vtable+0x0C receives whether it is the selected one.
evidence: The readable C is truncated to a single call, so I read the disassembly: it calls 0x0029126C(self), then loops i<2 over the children at self+0x130/self+0x134, asks each child's vtable+0x1C for its id, compares it with the signed byte self+0x64 and passes the boolean to the child's vtable+0x0C. The vtable slot 0x00763E80 sits next to Ui_TwoListWindow_Init (0x00329AFC), so the class is Ui_TwoListWindow, not a generic window.

name: Ui_TwoListWindow_Init
summary: Window initialiser that adopts the two embedded list widgets at self+0x80 and self+0xD8: stores both pointers at f_130/f_134 and, for each, calls virtual +8 to attach the owner and +0xC to reset the list.
evidence: The twice-repeated attach(+8)/reset(+0xC) pair on the two embedded widgets is fully visible in the body and the vtable 0x00763E68 slot +8 is the window init slot; the class has no pane strings, so 'two list widgets' is as specific as the evidence goes.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_UpdatePlacement
summary: Positions a screen-space effect relative to the camera: builds the effect world offset, scales the offset by the distance to the camera (clamped to a near/far range), projects it with Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen and lets the owner apply it (virtual +0x2C).
evidence: The projection callee is the now-named Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen and the distance source is the object at work+0x74, which supports the placement reading, but the owning class is still only inferred from the layout and no real caller was found (the reverse hit is Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen's evidence text, not a call); maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoListPanel_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of a two-list window variant: runs the window header constructor (0x1D08D8), installs the class vtable 0x763E68 plus the secondary table at +0x4C, then constructs the two embedded sub-objects (vtables 0x767258 and 0x75ECE0) and clears their state words.
evidence: NEW: the literal at 0x329D54 is 0x00763E68, and that vtable carries the named Ui_TwoListWindow_Init (0x329AFC, slot 0x20) and Ui_TwoListWindow_UpdateChildSelection (0x329A8C, slot 0x18), so the class is a two-list window variant - the old 'Panel' wording is at least in the right family. It is a subclass though (slots 0/1 are its own dtor 0x329DB4 / 0x329D60), and the two embedded objects use the emotion-balloon (0x767258) and pane-group (0x75ECE0) vtables, so the exact subclass name is still open. Kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_HandleDeadTag
summary: Looks the 4-byte tag "dead" (0x64616564) up on the model at self+0x28 and, when present, re-applies it through the model's vtable+0x84; then runs the state slot at self+0x2C and starts the attached effect.

name: Dive_Effect_InitFromActor

evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7254B8 holds this function next to the already-named Dive_SpawnDropEffect (0x32AC88) and maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShake (0x32ABE0), so the Dive_ class prefix is no longer a guess; the body's only work is the id -> f_E2 lookup and the scaled store into f_A0, which is exactly 'init from actor'.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveEffect_Update
summary: Timer-driven effect-slot sequencer: after the first timer expires it plays the impact SE once, and after the second it walks the effect slots at +0x2C (state 1/2) and attaches the impact effect/model data from the object at +0x28; always returns 1 while waiting.
evidence: The body uses model attach slots (Model_AttachSlot_InitResource), Sound_PlaySeById and a 0x12-byte transform copy, so it is effect/model sequencing; the 'Ui' prefix is unsupported (no UI callee) and 'dive' is only a guess from the nearby Ui_DiveStartWindow (0x0032BCB8). The class remains unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: Dive_SpawnDropEffect
summary: Spawns the dive mini-game's drop/impact effect: plays the 'diveDrop' animation on the effect object, offsets it by the window position, checks the item that was hit and creates the attached impact effect / plays SE 0x1F.

name: Dive_Effect_UpdateStartDelay
summary: Per-frame start-delay check of the dive effect: while the frame counter f_38 is not yet 0x3C (60) it does nothing; on frame 60 it asks the tween controller at +0x2C for state 2 and commits it, i.e. the effect starts. Always returns 1 so the caller keeps ticking.
evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7254F0 holds it next to maybe_Ui_DiveEffect_Update (0x32A850), so the class is the dive effect. The old name 'UpdateTimer' was wrong: the body never increments anything - it only tests `self->f_38 == 0x3C` and then runs the request/commit pair (vtable+0x14(2) then vtable+0x10), so the function is the delayed-start gate, not a timer update.

name: maybe_Dive_Effect_SpawnOriented

evidence: NEW: nothing changed the verdict - there is still no readable C for this address (only the instruction-listing pseudo-C in decomp/functions/maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShakeAlt.c), and the address is not referenced from any rodata table. The R_062 disassembly reading (vsqrt/vdiv basis maths, vneg mirror fixes, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance with effect id 0x45C from the literal at 0x32B3D8, single caller the dive-effect spawner at 0x32B04C) is the only evidence, and it fixes the behaviour but not the class name. Kept maybe_.

name: Gfx_Sprite_InitParams
signature: GfxSprite* Gfx_Sprite_InitParams(GfxSpriteManager* mgr, ResDesc* desc, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Allocates a sprite/effect slot through the manager and installs the default parameter block: vtable 0x7642D4, zero origin, alpha 0xFF, two 0xFFFF limits and the -1/-8 sentinels.
evidence: The named sprite-slot allocator (0x005F8174) and the fixed default block make this an initialiser; the argument-derived word at desc+4 is the only caller-supplied value.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field actor/scene-node class: releases the base object (0x5F8528) and frees it (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x7642DC has this function in slot 0 and its other slots are Field_Actor_ReleaseAttachedEffect (0x32DA9C), maybe_Field_SceneNode_ResetChildren (0x32D264) and Field_Actor_RestartActionSequence (0x32D998) plus the 0x5F7xxx Gfx node methods - so the old 'Gfx_Sprite' class was wrong, this is a field actor. Which of Field_Actor / Field_SceneNode owns the vtable is not settled (both names appear as siblings), so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_BeginEffectState
summary: Switches an actor's effect state: if the byte at +0x238 is not 0xFF it clears +0x221, builds an effect transform at the actor position and spawns effect 0x45C through the 2D effect manager, then sets f_8C=1 and stops the sub-animation; otherwise it plays animation 0x0032DD6C and clears f_8C.
evidence: The spawner is now named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and the two branches are readable, but no caller confirms the 'begin effect state' semantics.

name: Field_Actor_TickEffectState
summary: Per-frame effect-state tick: once the accumulated timer at actor->f_4C+8 passes 0.3 (0x3E99999A) it spawns the state effect once (0x32DE54, guarded by f_230) and then asks the sub-state at f_4C for state 2. Always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764454 has this function in slot 0 with maybe_Field_Actor_BeginEffectState (0x32DBEC) as the preceding entry, so the Field_Actor class is confirmed by its own vtable; the body's two steps (spawn once, then request state 2) are visible in the readable C.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_StartAnim
summary: Starts the node animation: installs the per-frame callback &LAB_0032de44 through vtable+0x84, starts an animation of length 0x3C through 0x5F7784, sets the running byte f_8C and clears the byte at +0x221.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x5F7784 belongs to the same 0x5F7xxx family as the named Gfx_Node_DrawModel (0x5F7578), so the class is a Gfx node, not specifically a sprite - the old 'Gfx_Sprite' wording is dropped. The function is not referenced from any rodata table and has no static caller, so the exact node class and the meaning of the 0x3C length are still open. Kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SpawnStateEffect
summary: Spawns a 0x240-byte effect/model object for a field actor: when the actor has a held item id (f_232 != -1) it looks the item record up, chooses between two effect variants by the item's id range (0xAA3..0xB3A / 0xA82..0xAA2) and calls maybe_Gfx_EffectObject_Replace with the actor position; when f_232 is -1 it instead builds the object from record 0x2DE and loads it through Ui_ItemModel_Load.
evidence: NEW: the item path is now explicit - Item_LookupRecord on actor->f_232 and a range test `(id - * 0xAA3 < 0x98) || (id - 0xA82 < 0x21)` selecting the effect variant, with Ui_ItemModel_Load / * maybe_Gfx_EffectObject_Replace as the sinks. That matches FACTS.md's item id space and shows this is * per-actor model/effect spawning, not a generic state effect. Still maybe_ because the trigger (f_232 * held item vs f_234 sprite path) and the two id ranges' meaning are inferred; the body is also full of * CONCAT/uint3 decompiler artefacts.

name: Gfx_Sprite_InitParamsAlt
summary: Second sprite initialiser: allocates the slot, installs vtable 0x76438C and writes the alternate default block (zero origin then 1.5 scale, 0xFFFF/0xFF limits and the +0x221 flag byte set to 1).
evidence: Same allocation call as 0x0032DB00 but a different vtable and default block, so this is the second variant of the same sprite constructor.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of a second field scene-node class: releases the base object (0x5F8528) and frees it (0x10F6CC) - same body as 0x32DBD0.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764394 has this function in slot 0 and its other slots are maybe_Field_SceneNode_CreateChild_75AEB8 (0x3D5E58) and Field_Actor_UpdateVisibility (0x3D6064) plus the 0x5F7xxx Gfx node methods, so the old 'Gfx_Sprite' class was wrong. The vtable mixes Field_SceneNode_* and Field_Actor_* siblings, so which of the two owns it is not settled; kept maybe_ and named after the scene-node side to stay distinct from 0x32DBD0.

name: Ui_TitleWindow_InitPanes
summary: Cursor window that attaches only the 'txt_title' pane, with a 0x10-byte layout parameter.
evidence: drN; func_002BCFF4(0x10) then virtual +0x34 with the literal 'txt_title' (0x0032E584); vtable slot 7 of 0x00764470; no other panes.

name: Ui_TitleWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the title window: runs the UI object base destructor and releases the block.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x00764470 whose slot +0x1C is the confident Ui_TitleWindow_InitPanes; the body is `Ui_Object_DtorBase(); release`. The 'A' suffix is no longer needed because the other maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_Dtor (0x0032E6E4) is a different 172-byte function that is not in this vtable.

name: Ui_TitleTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Attaches the 'txt_title' pane and a second one-character 'txt' pane to the window at the base layout id.
evidence: Both literals resolve in the retail image: 0x0032E604 = 'txt_title' and 0x0032E610 = 'txt'. With vtable 0x007644D4 slot +7 this is exactly a two-pane title window initialiser.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextFromTable
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextFromTable(UiMessageWindow* self, char table_index, unsigned int text_id, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Sets a text id on the message window using a string from the shared text table (index is offset by 0x22), tagging the write with the window's own id.
evidence: func_00633560(*(singleton+0x10), arg2-0x22) returns the string for the table index, then func_001A6680(self, self->f_28<<0x10 | 1, str) writes it. Callers 0x199F6C, 0x19AB98, 0x1EAB30, 0x3EFD64, 0x3EFF44 are all message/UI callers. The same func_001A6680 idiom is used 13x in the skill-panel row builder 0x364CC0.

name: Ui_TitleTextWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the title-text window: runs the UI object base destructor and releases the block.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x007644D4 whose slot +0x1C is the confident Ui_TitleTextWindow_InitPanes; the body is `Ui_Object_DtorBase(); release`.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_SetAnimFrame
signature: void maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_SetAnimFrame(UiTitleWindow* self, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Window step handler: plays step 0x36 through 0x617D7C, binds the detail widget at owner+0x1084 to owner+0x111C and pushes the pane descriptor 0x729A7C+0x48 onto the window at owner+0x120.
evidence: New evidence: the named callees Ui_Window_PushPane and Ui_Slot_BindControl show a pane-push action, and the object at self+4 is the owning window. The step player 0x617D7C and the meaning of step id 0x36 are still unnamed, so 'SetAnimFrame' is a description rather than a proven operation; maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small window object: detaches the child sprite, removes the node from its owner's ring, releases the tween/layout members and frees.
evidence: No named ctor or vtable sibling references a title window; the teardown mechanism matches the other deleting dtors in this batch but the class label is unverified, so maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNextIcon
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNextIcon(UiMessageWindow* self, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Per-frame update of the message text window: decrements the typewriter countdown, moves/blinks the 'icon_next' marker under the last line, plays the 'stop1' page-end animation and re-positions the text panes 'txt'/'txt1'.
evidence: Loads the literal pane names 'txt1' (0x32E800), 'txt' (0x32E824), 'stop1' (0x32E8F0) and 'icon_next' (0x32EA4C); decrements arg1[10] then moves the icon object by the text height (unaff_r8->f_a8->f_1c/f_20/f_24) and calls func_003E00CC(&f_11C,&f_98,'stop1',0) + func_003DFF34 (snap). Also maps message type ids 0x11/0x25/0x39 (line-break/page types) to hiding the icon and uses float constants 0.1/0.5/0.6/1.0 for the scroll timing.

name: Field_Actor_InitActionSequencer
summary: Hooks a field actor's action/sequencer object together: stores the address of the object's +0x18 block into owner+0x10CC, lazily constructs the shared sequencer table, pulls the actor record with 0x0063D960 and constructs the four 0xC-byte action entries that drive the actor's motion/effect steps.
evidence: Body: `*(int*)(*(int*)(arg1+4) + 0x10cc) = arg1 + 0x18;` then the usual lazy-static build (guard g_0032f1a4, func_0011FE8C/func_0011CFAC, func_00116AE0, vtable PTR_DAT_0032f1b4 cached in g_0032f1a8), func_0063D960() and std_ConstructArray(local_98, PTR_LAB_0032f1b8, 4, 0xc) — a 4-entry, 0xC-stride table. The literal pool also holds `icon1`/`icon_next`, which more likely belongs to the neighbouring message-window icon code (Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNextIcon 0x0032E790) than to this initialiser.

name: Field_Actor_AdvanceModeState
summary: Advances the actor's scene-mode byte (+4): if the current mode matches the scene's mode it first detaches the mode's effect (Ui_ChildSprite_Detach, removes it from the intrusive list, clears f_16C), and at the end it increments the mode byte and runs the extra step 0x002BBB44 when leaving mode 1.
evidence: The body's last statements are the mode switch (actor+4 += 1) with the mode-1 special case, and the effect release (Ui_ChildSprite_Detach + intrusive-list unlink + f_16C = 0) only runs when the current mode matches the scene's mode; the named callees Object_IsHandleAlive and Ui_ChildSprite_Detach confirm the effect teardown.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DtorB
signature: UiMessageWindow* maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DtorB(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Destructor of a message-window variant: installs vtable 0x00764534 and runs the shared message-window teardown chain.
evidence: NEW: still no callers; the two named siblings maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DtorBody (0x004E650C) and DtorBodyB (0x004E6A34) run the same chain, which supports the message-window class but not the exact variant.

name: Fs_FileRequest_Update
signature: u32 Fs_FileRequest_Update(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 high)
summary: Drives one asynchronous file request through its phases (0 = start, 1 = wait for sync, 2 = prepare, 3 = poll, 4 = finish): publishes the request, builds the request header, waits on the event flag/semaphore, releases the command buffer and records a status code in +0xC. Returns 1 while the request may continue and 0 when it has completed or failed.
evidence: Callees are the Fs/Os API family: 0x005031CC (Fs_PublishRequest), 0x00503B78 (maybe_Fs_BuildRequestHeader), 0x001D033C (maybe_Fs_Request_Prepare), 0x001D0134 (maybe_Os_SyncObject_Init), 0x00118170 (Os_InitEventFlag), 0x00503264 (maybe_Svc_Object_InvokeWithArg), 0x0010EA00 (Gfx_CommandBuffer_Release) and 0x00503F58/0x00503F8C. The body is a phase machine on `self->f_8` (0..4) with `self->f_c` set to result codes 1..9 and repeated `return 0`/`return 1` steps.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateMotionScale
signature: void Field_Actor_UpdateMotionScale(FieldActor* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Computes the actor's motion speed/scale from its action parameters (f_2c4/f_2c8) and random jitter, stores them in f_1b4/f_1b8, then runs the normal anim update.
evidence: reads actor->f_28 f_2c4/f_2c8 and 0x0051B1FC random; writes f_1b4/f_1b8; calls 0x0028B02C; f_2c4->f_10/f_20/f_2b are animation params

name: Field_NpcAction_UpdateTimeline
summary: Per-frame NPC-action timeline: accumulates the delta into f_68/f_6C and then runs the callback of the current keyframe (0..11) from the 0x18-byte descriptor array at +0x60, resolving the (fn & 1) thunk convention against the object at +0x80.
evidence: NEW: the callback table at 0x764838 holds this function together with Field_NpcAction_AdvanceTweenState (0x330F08), and the vtable right after it (0x76484C) is the Field_NpcAction_RunToLink class with RunToLinkSetup/RunToLinkUpdate - so the Field_NpcAction base class is confirmed by named siblings. The timeline body is unchanged; only the jump table inside it is unrecovered.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_ComputeOffsetFromHandle
summary: Resolves the target object through Container_FindObjectByTypeIdH, copies its position (+0x9C..+0xA4) and asks 0x005E8BEC to compute the actor's local offset into a stack buffer; returns 1 unconditionally.
evidence: The offset helper writes to a *local* 12-byte buffer and nothing stores it back into the actor, so 'SetPosition' overstates the effect; the store-back is either missing from the decompilation or happens through a pointer Ghidra dropped, hence maybe_.

name: Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffset
summary: Moves the NPC along a small offset stored in its action record: if the action animation has ended it plays sequence 2, otherwise it adds the record offset to the actor position.
evidence: calls Field_NpcGetActionAnimId 0x0017A360 with a flag+Vec3 descriptor; on finish 0x005E7848(actor,2,0); writes f_44/f_48/f_4c from f_1bc/f_1c0/f_1c4

name: Field_NpcAction_StartMoveToTarget
summary: Starts an NPC walk/run action toward a target: copies the target actor's position and the follow point from the owner block (+0x2D8/+0x2E0 and +0x2E4..+0x2EC) into the action's start/goal vectors, initialises the movement helper with them, selects walk or run playback depending on the owner's state and stores the duration in +0x50.
evidence: Body copies f_2d8/f_2dc/f_2e0 to f_44/f_48/f_4c and f_2e4/f_2e8/f_2ec to f_38/f_3c/f_40, sets f_1ac from g_0032fe6c and f_1b0 = 0, calls func_0028AFF4(self, &self->f_44), dispatches `(**(code**)(*self->f_28 + 0x84))(self->f_28, ...)` and finally calls func_005E80A4 / func_005E7F84 with `*(u16*)(self->f_28 + 600)` before writing f_50. It sits directly after Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffset (0x0032FCC4) and before maybe_Field_NpcAction_TurnToActor (0x0033026C).

name: Field_NpcAction_WalkToStoredTarget
summary: Per-frame update of an NPC movement action: after the entry delay in +0x1B4 it latches the position stored on the actor at +0x2D8 and the facing stored at +0x2E4 into the action, picks the Walk/Run animation (or idle 'Nut' when it is already on the spot), steers the actor to that point, then makes it face the stored direction and signals completion through 0x0028C42C before returning 1.
evidence: No static callers - it is a table-driven virtual update (pointer stored at 0x00725774). dt is read from self+0x70; the animation names passed to actor vfunc +0x84 are the literals at 0x0032FE74 'Nut', 0x0032FE78 'Run', 0x0032FE7C 'Walk'; the goal fields +0x2D8..+0x2EC are exactly the ones Monster_SetupEcology (0x00178B08) fills from the ecology spawn record; direction/translation use 0x005E8BEC / 0x005E890C, and the finish path calls 0x0028C42C(self+0x5C, actor+0x2C8) and sets self+0x35 = 1.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteSlot_SetParams
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpriteSlot_SetParams(u32 index, u8 flagA, u8 flagB)
summary: Fills one 0x40-byte entry of a global sprite/effect parameter array: copies three words of the default basis vector into +0x48/+0x4C/+0x50 and stores the caller's flags in the trailing bytes +0x54..+0x58.
evidence: NEW: nothing new - the address is not referenced from any rodata table and has no static caller, and Ghidra's body is still damaged (coprocessor_function, 'index' used as a pointer), so the base register and the array owner remain guesses. Only the 0x40 stride and the three-word copy are confirmed by the instruction listing. A confident name here would be inventing.

name: Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffsetStart
summary: One-shot setup for the 'move by offset' action: it derives the offset from the actor's stored origin (+0x2CC) to its stored goal (+0x2D8), stores it in +0x1BC/+0x1C0/+0x1C4, clears the actor's +0x2A4 field, executes one step of the movement helper 0x0032FCC4, then takes the model's ground speed from 0x005E82C4 and plays 'Run' or 'Walk' depending on the flag that helper returns.
evidence: Callee Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffset (0x0032FCC4), which consumes exactly the +0x1BC offset written here. Animation literals g_00330250 -> 0x0032FE78 'Run' and g_00330254 -> 0x0032FE7C 'Walk' selected by local_c, the byte 0x005E82C4 returns at +8; actor+0x2A4 = -1; self+0x50 = the speed float 0x005E82C4 returns.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_TurnToActor
summary: Starts an NPC action step: takes the target actor id from the action owner (or the object found by Container_FindObjectByTypeId), applies the move speed from Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById, installs step 0x0032FE7C and feeds a random value when the target has the rotation flag.
evidence: Container_FindObjectByTypeId and Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById are named, but the speed arrives in in_s0 and the rotation flag/random use is damaged, so the 'turn to actor' semantic is not proven.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_PlayScaledActionAnim
summary: Fetches action animation id and model scale, chooses animation name by scale flag, and plays it on owner actor.
evidence: Callees Field_NpcGetActionAnimId and Field_Actor_GetMoveSpeedAndFlag confirm scaled action animation selection, but action state context is unverified. Kept maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_IdleB
summary: Twin of 0x0033026C without the target lookup: applies the actor's move speed (from in_s0), installs step 0x0032FE7C, and when the actor animation is ready converts the system speed and applies it through 0x005F5A50.
evidence: The callee set matches 0x0033026C (Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById, 0x0032FE7C, Os_GetGameWork) but the state word and float conversion use in_s0/in_fpscr, so 'Idle' is only an interpretation of the installed callback; the B suffix merely avoids the name of 0x0039BE90.

name: Field_NpcAction_WalkToPlayer
summary: Walk-toward-player action: checks line of sight, measures the squared distance to the player, steers the movement direction and adds velocity each frame; plays sequence 4 when the player is out of sight.
evidence: calls Field_NpcCheckSight 0x0017843C, 0x005E8BEC (steer/step vector), adds to actor f_100/f_104/f_108; 0x005E7848(...,4,0) on failure

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToActor
summary: Run/chase action: gets the target actor, computes a steering direction through 0x005E890C, accelerates the actor and switches to sequence 4 when the target is lost.
evidence: 0x0017843C sight, 0x00619B20 target, 0x00669D88 position, Actor_SteerMoveDirection 0x005E890C; writes actor f_100..f_108

name: Field_NpcAction_StartAnimAndFlagStep
summary: Starts the action's animation through the actor's vtable+0x84 (callback 0x3308E8) and, when the action counter f_2C8 is below 4, sets the matching 'step done' byte in the array at self->f_5C (+0x271 + counter).
evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7257DC holds this function next to the named Field_NpcAction_WaitForLinkEnd (0x330DF0), so the Field_NpcAction class is confirmed by named siblings; the body's two steps (vtable+0x84 animation start, then the guarded step-done byte) are visible in the recovered fragment.

name: Field_NpcAction_WalkToPoint
summary: Walks toward the stored point (f_48) at the action speed, optionally offset toward a target actor; when the timer expires it switches to the next action.
evidence: 0x0017843C, 0x00669D88 current pos, 0x00619B20 target, 0x0028AFF4 applies the point, 0x005E8BEC step; calls 0x0033033C on timeout

name: Field_NpcAction_WalkToActor
summary: Like WalkToPoint but the destination is the target actor's position plus a fixed offset; on timeout it changes the sequence and speed.
evidence: same shape as 0x003308F4 but adds target actor f_9c.. and calls 0x005E7F84 + vtable +0x84 with uRam_00330C8C

name: Field_NpcAction_WalkToActorStep
summary: Movement step for 'walk to actor': each frame it checks line of sight, computes the target position (own actor position plus the target's offset, or the current walk target), and adds the resulting motion to the actor's position; when the step budget runs out it finishes with flag 4.
evidence: Covered entry inside 0x330A84 (Field_NpcAction_WalkToActor, named by N_053); calls that same function, Field_NpcCheckSight 0x17843C, Container_FindObjectByTypeId 0x619B20, Os_GetGameWork 0x6F1EEC, and writes actor->f_100..f_108 with f_1B8 timer.

name: Field_NpcAction_WaitForLinkEnd
summary: Wait action that ends when the timer f_54 runs out or when the NPC action reports the 'LinkEnd' event; then triggers sequence 4.
evidence: string s_LinkEnd_00330EF8; calls 0x00627EE4/0x00669DD4; vtable +0x84 with s_LinkEnd

name: Field_NpcAction_AdvanceTweenState
summary: Asks the action's tween controller at +0x60 whether the current step finished (vtable+0x14 with no id) and, if it did, commits the next state through vtable+0x10.
evidence: NEW: the callback table at 0x764838 pairs this function with Field_NpcAction_UpdateTimeline (0x32FBB4), which drives the same +0x60 controller, and the neighbouring vtable 0x76484C is the named Field_NpcAction_RunToLink class - so the Field_NpcAction base class is confirmed. The request/commit pair is the same two-slot protocol as the named message-window tween code (0x30E3CC).

name: Monster_EcologyCoSubCtor
signature: void* Monster_EcologyCoSubCtor(void* mem, void* owner, void* actor, const char* name, int flag)
summary: Placement constructor for the 'ecoCoSub' monster-ecology sub-behaviour object: it runs the base constructor, installs vtable 0x0076480C on the object and 0x0075AC9C on the member pair at +0x60, back-links the owner at +0x60+0x20, and default-constructs the following 12-entry table of 0x18-byte elements.
evidence: Monster_SetupEcology (0x00178B08) calls it as (mem, self, actor, 'ecoCoSub', 1) and afterwards attaches the result to actor action slot 0xB via 0x002A8BA4; the sibling cases of the same switch call 0x00331748 'ecoRn', 0x004D6F24 'ecoCh' and 0x0039C070 'ecoCoMain'. Callees: 0x0028B160 (base ctor returning the object), Ui_Object_InitMemberPair 0x0021C2DC, std_ConstructArray with 0x18-byte elements and count 0xC; vtables g_00331338/g_0033133C.

name: Field_NpcAction_DeletingDestructorA
summary: Deleting destructor variant for an NPC-action class: installs the vtable argument at the object base, runs the shared base-action destructor 0x00193E40 and frees the block with 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: NEW: the address sits inside the confident Field_NpcAction_* cluster (Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkSetup at 0x003314B0, Field_NpcAction_DeletingDtor at 0x00332D90) and the disassembly shows the standard vptr store + base destructor + free sequence of that family, so the class is no longer a guess.

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkSetup
summary: Setup of an NPC run action: it computes the run direction either toward the object resolved from the action's link (0x00619B20) or, when there is no link, out of the actor's own rotation (+0x8C..+0x98); it then stores direction, delay (actor+0x2C4->+0x1C or 1.0s), speed (a global from 0x0063E650) and finally starts a turn request (0x001798D0) plus the idle 'Nut' animation.
evidence: Paired with 0x0033164C by the adjacent vtable entries 0x00764850 / 0x00764858. Direction written to +0x34/+0x38/+0x3C, +0x40 = 0, delay +0x44 = actor->f_2C4->f_1C else the constant 1.0f (g_00331640), speed +0x48 = *0x0063E650(gameWork); ends with 0x001798D0(actor, 0) (writes a turn request into actor+0x31C) and actor vfunc +0x84 with 'Nut' (g_00331648 = 0x0032FE74).

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the run-to-link action: while the elapsed time (self+0x24->+0x44) is still below the stored delay (+0x44) it merely re-aims the actor at the linked object; once the delay has elapsed it plays 'Run' once, and every frame turns the actor toward the stored direction (0x005F5F54) and translates it by direction * speed(+0x48) * dt.
evidence: Compares self+0x24->f_44 with self+0x44; plays the literal g_00331744 = 'Run' only when the flag +0x40 is still 0 (then sets it); 0x005E8BEC(out, actor, position of the 0x00619B20 link) re-aims; 0x005F5F54(actor, &self->f_34, 0); actor+0x100/0x104/0x108 += f_34/f_38/f_3C * (self+0x48 * dt).

name: Monster_EcologyBehaviorCtor
summary: Allocates and initialises the monster ecology behaviour object: runs the shared AI-behaviour constructor, installs the ecology vtable 0x764848 and copies the three default parameter words.
evidence: The only caller is the named Monster_SetupEcology, the vtable 0x764848 is installed over the shared AI ctor result and the three constants are copied at +0x34..+0x3C.

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToLink_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the 'run to link' NPC action: destroys the string member (0x193E40) and frees the object (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x76484C has this function in slot 0 and the named Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkSetup (0x3314B0, slot 1) and Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkUpdate (0x33164C, slot 3) as its other entries, so the class is the run-to-link action - the old name 'DeletingDestructorB' did not identify the class at all.

name: Field_NpcJumpAction_Setup
summary: Prepares a jump: records the take-off position/rotation (or a target point from the NPC record) and asks the jump planner to build the trajectory.

name: Party_FindNextEntryForCharacter
summary: Advances a party character-entry cursor to the next matching 0x14-byte row of the data-manager table: row charaId 0xFF or equal to cursor->u8_00, story-flag bit set in GameWork+0x2A444, map-visited byte at +0x27508, quest state 9 and party condition opcodes 0x19..0x22; sets the cursor index to 0x7FFFFFFF when exhausted.
evidence: All three confident callers are Party_* helpers (Party_GetFirstActorForCharacter, Party_GetActorNoForCharacter, Party_BuildUsedCharacterList) and they use the returned cursor protocol; the table row fields (+0x08 story flag, +0x0A map flag, +0x0C quest, +0x10 charaId) are the same ones maybe_Party_FindEntryByType reads. It walks party character entries, not live Actor objects, so the Actor_ prefix was wrong.

name: Data_FindNextRowMatchingConditions
summary: Advances the cursor to the next row of the 0x14-byte condition table: skips rows whose type byte does not match *cursor, requires the row flag bit in the save work and the per-row flag byte, then walks the row's compact condition list (opcodes 0x19..0x22) against the selected party member's fields (+0x664, +0x668, +0x66C, +0x3EC and +0x370+0x2F5..0x2FB). On a match it stores the row index in cursor+4; otherwise it writes the FF FF FF 7F end marker.
evidence: The whole body is the evaluator: data-manager/work getters, the 0x14-byte stride, the 0x19..0x22 switch against the member record and the explicit cursor[4..7] end marker. No caller-specific data is used, so the neutral Data_ prefix and the row-scan verb describe exactly what it does for every caller.

name: maybe_Actor_ClassifyTableId

evidence: No new context: the named neighbours only give Game_GetWork/Game_GetDataManager and 0x0066AF08 (the quest-flag reader), so the two compared bytes stay 'the row's two id columns' rather than a known pair of ids, and there is no caller (runtime table). Stays maybe_.

name: Ui_Row_SetIndex

evidence: The body only touches the row's own index/value/child-pane fields and ends in the named Ui_Row_Render through the named maybe_Ui_Result_AdvanceToValidRow, so 'set index and re-render' is confirmed.

name: Ui_Row_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the scrolling-list row base: allocates through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x003B65D4, sets the -1 index sentinel at +0x4A and zeroes the 0x7C-byte inline buffer.
evidence: The -1 sentinel, the zeroed row buffer and the vtable are a row-constructor signature, and named callers Ui_TwoColumnRow_InitPanes, Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects and Ui_SmithMenu_Ctor build list rows.

name: Ui_TwoColumnListWindow_Dtor

name: Ui_SlotWindow_PayoutSequence
summary: Frame-timed payout sequence of the slot window: frame 0 starts the payout animation and plays SE 0xE71, frame 0x14 flips the machine into the payout display state, frame 0x50 plays win/lose cue 3/4 and rebinds the slot control, and after 0x50 it polls the slot widget until the payout animation ends (returning 1).
evidence: NEW: the win/lose branch and the widget poll use the now-named Sound_PlaySeCached, Ui_SlotWindow_ResetPayoutAnim, Ui_Widget_Update and maybe_Ui_Slot_BindControl, and the stage frames are literal comparisons - the sequence is fully readable; its twin 0x00380398 in this batch starts the transition right after.

name: Ui_SlotWindow_ReelStopSequence
summary: Frame-driven reel-stop sequence of the slot-machine window: writes the reel result, plays the stop SE, and after 0x29 frames marks the winning line by creating a result object in one of six per-reel slots (case 0..4 selects the line).
evidence: NEW: the six line vtables are the named g_slotWinTextLine4Vtable / g_slotWinLineDNodeVtable family and the stop SE is 0xE87, so the reel-stop reading is now backed by data symbols as well as the 0x29 frame counter.

name: Casino_Slot_ExecCommand
summary: Executes one slot-machine presentation command: refreshes the payout/value display, resets the five rows, hides the symbols, stores the requested configuration bytes, and when the pending flag is clear and its timer expired starts the win presentation, applies the row state and moves the machine to state 5 or 8.
evidence: All named callees are Casino_Slot_* helpers (ResetRows, HideSymbols, StopAllReels, ApplyRowState) and the state setter 0x003280C0 is called with step 5; the Game_GetWork bag lookup supplies the displayed value, so this is the slot-machine command executor rather than a generic UI handler.

name: maybe_Container_HandleList_ReleaseByType
summary: Releases every handle in the list at self+0x10 whose object reports the given type: handles are 11-bit index + 21-bit generation packed into a word, resolved through the global handle table at 0x007B80C0 (entry size 8, generation at +4), then the object's virtual slot +0x40 is called with 4 (unregister/release) and the list is reset to the empty token.
evidence: Previous evidence: Handle decode `(h & 0x7FF)*8 + table` with `entry[1] == h>>0xB` and the * constant 0x001FFFFF / 0x007B80C0 / 0x0072863C literals at 0x003B6E80..0x003B6E8C; loop count self+0x24, * handles at self+0x10; `(*(*obj))(obj)` returns a link chain compared against g_003B6E88 and the object's * slot +0x40 is called with 4. Finishes by copying the global empty-list token into self+4/+8. 0x003B71C8 * is the lookup variant (calls slot +0x34 and returns early).. Kept as maybe_ with low context score (0) * and pending direct caller resolution.

name: Ui_Smith_UpdateHitEffect
summary: Frame timer of the blacksmith mini-game: plays the hammer SE 0xEE8 on frame 2, spawns the spark effect (id from the table at 0x003B7090) at the anvil on frame 0x2D and plays its SE, and after frame 0x40 copies the two result words from the mini-game descriptor into the result object.
evidence: The frame checkpoints 2/0x2D/0x40, the two literal SE ids, the named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call and the result copies from 0x003B709C are all explicit; the 'Smith' identity comes from the sibling animation table ("SmithStart") in the same block.

name: Ui_Smith_StartSequence
summary: Starts the blacksmith mini-game presentation: resets every actor in the window's id list to its smith animation and tells the smith actor to play "SmithStart", then publishes the two result words.
evidence: Blacksmith mini-game sequence start: resets actor animations in list, dispatches 'SmithStart' motion to smith actor, and publishes forge results.

name: Ui_Smith_WaitForActorsFinished
summary: State callback in the Fun-Size Forge (Smith) presentation sequence (g_smithSequenceStateCallbacks 0x0072863C, G_009.json): iterates the actor handle list at self+0x10, resolves each actor through 0x007B80C0, checks g_actorBaseClass, and tests if motion is finished via virtual slot +0x34. If any actor is not ready, returns early to continue waiting; once all actors finish, advances self+4/self+8 to the next sequence callback.
evidence: State callback entry in g_smithSequenceStateCallbacks (0x0072863C, G_009.json) alongside confirmed Ui_Smith_StartSequence (0x003B70A0, conf 0.55) and Ui_Smith_UpdateHitEffect (0x003B6E90, conf 0.50). Uses the exact same SmithWindow layout (handle array at self+0x10, count self+0x24, state step pointers at self+0x04/0x08). The old Container_HandleList_FindByType guess misread the forge state machine.

name: maybe_Data_CollectLinkedRecords

Changed to confirmed at 0.5 rather than 0.6 because the id semantics stay open.

summary: Puts a parameter row back into its empty state: clears the selection index f_4A and the cursor fields f_1E0/f_1E4, turns off the two icon panes at +0x1D4/+0x1DC while turning on +0x1D8, re-measures the empty caption and re-applies the row.
evidence: The caller is now the confident Ui_TsuyosaWindow_UpdateSelection and the tail is the named maybe_Ui_Row_Apply (0x003B8B88), so 'reset one row' is well supported; the tri-state pane toggle at +0x1D4/+0x1D8/+0x1DC (icon left/middle/right) is still inferred from the bit-0 writes.

name: Ui_TsuyosaWindow_FillRowsB
summary: Second filler of the parameter window's grid: takes the character's id list (func_00629214 count / func_006298F0 getter), sorts it by the display-name field of each entry (comparator reading record+0xC2), writes the ids 17 per row into the 0x30-byte grid at +0x54, then refreshes the caption text and calls Ui_Row_Apply.
evidence: NEW: the callers are the confident Ui_TsuyosaWindow_Update / Ui_TsuyosaWindow_UpdateSelection, the tail is the named maybe_Ui_Row_Apply + Ui_List_SelectEntryById, and the twin 0x003BAA00 proves the family writes the same +0x54 grid. The only novelty here is the sort (maybe_Ui_SortEntriesByGlyphMetric + func_00717CB0 insertion sort by record+0xC2) and the 17-per-row packing. What the ids mean is not proven, so the summary says 'id list', not 'skills'.

name: Ui_TsuyosaWindow_CreateRow
summary: Creates one row object of the tsuyosa (strength) window: UI object base plus vtable 0x00768F10, stores the row index at +0x49, the 0xFF sentinel at +0x4A, clears the six words at +0x1D4..+0x1E8 and fills the 8-byte id array at +0x4B and the 0x180-byte scratch buffer with 0xFF.
evidence: NEW: its constructor Ui_TsuyosaWindow_Ctor (0x002A0E14) is the only caller and its deleting destructor sits at 0x003BB1D4 (slot 0 of the same vtable), so the class and the row role are anchored at both ends.

name: maybe_Ui_TsuyosaWindow_DeleteRow
summary: Deleting destructor of one tsuyosa (strength) row object: runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees. The table's row updater is still a maybe_ name, so the row-class attribution stays tentative.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x00768F14 slot 0 is this function; +0x1C is maybe_Ui_TsuyosaWindow_UpdateRowText and +0x3C maybe_Ui_ListGrid_MoveCursor. The row-text updater supports the tsuyosa-row reading, but it is itself below 0.5, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_Overlay_BindEntries
signature: void Ui_Overlay_BindEntries(UiOverlay* self, u32 owner, u32 actorA, u32 actorB)
summary: Binds the eight overlay sub-objects to the actors they follow: caches the player id, the two actor pointers and the cursor mode, then calls vtable+8 on each of the eight entries.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now the confident Ui_Overlay_RefreshSlots, which passes its own overlay pointer plus the owner and the two actor handles - exactly the argument list this body consumes. That fixes both the class (Ui_Overlay) and the role (bind the eight sub-objects) that the first pass could only guess from the shape of the loop.

name: Ui_Overlay_ApplyVisibility
summary: Decides which overlay elements are visible from the referenced record's flags (data-manager record f_49: +0x17/+0x18) and the current mode (work+8->+0x48 +0x281 == 8), toggling element objects through vtable +0x24.
evidence: Its caller is now the named maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateEntries, the record/flag reads are explicit, and the element toggles go through the named Field_Actor_HasTileFlag* helpers, so the apply-visibility role is supported.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateEntries
summary: Per-frame overlay update: detects movement of the followed actor (3D distance or 2D screen delta), applies the visibility pass and steps each of the eight sub-objects' size/timer, hiding the ones that shrink past the threshold.
evidence: The named callees Ui_Overlay_ApplyVisibility (0x003BB314) and Model_SwitchAttachmentsByState_Hide (0x0022F55C) support the overlay reading, but there is still no named caller (the first pass cited 0x0023DEB0, which is unnamed), so the class stays provisional.

name: maybe_Container_NodeList_Init
summary: Initialises a container object: installs its vtable, clears the eight intrusive node-list heads, allocates the 0x8C/0x14-byte helper nodes with their own vtables and stores them at self[2..9].
evidence: NEW: still no callers, and the recovered body is truncated by bad instruction data (Ghidra lost the tail after the seventh node), so the eight-list layout is the only solid fact. Kept at 0.30.

name: Ui_Overlay_ReleaseSubObjects
summary: Releases the eight sub-objects of the overlay widget: for each of the eight pointers at self+i*4+8 it calls the sub-object's vtable+4 and clears the slot, then returns self.
evidence: The only caller is now the named Ui_Overlay_Dtor (0x0023EC8C), and the body releases the eight sub-objects at self+i*4+8 through their vtable+4 and zeroes each slot, so the class is confirmed; 'Entries' was the wrong noun for sub-objects.

name: Ui_Pane_SetVisibleAndForward
summary: Two-step visibility setter shared by the layout-child classes: calls Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self, visible) and then unconditionally tail-calls the object's vtable +0x5C with the same visible value.
evidence: Disassembly shows both calls (bl 0x001A6460 with r1, then ldr r2,[vtable+0x5c]; bx r2 with r1 = visible). The pointer is slot +0x18 of two vtables (0x0075E4B8, 0x0075E544) whose +0x1C slots are maybe_Ui_SetOwnerAndDispatch and Ui_LayoutChild_InitDispatch, so the generic Ui_Pane_ prefix is the honest one.

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform
signature: void Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform(UiOverlay* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4, float scale)
summary: Positions the active overlay slot: computes the distance scale from the slot's world anchor, tests whether it is ahead of the camera (stored as the slot visibility byte), projects it, refreshes the slot record and then applies the widget screen transform.
evidence: Named callees now cover every step (maybe_Camera_ComputeDistanceScale, Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen, maybe_Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform), and the slot index/stride match the rest of the overlay family.

name: Ui_PartySelectWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructs the party-selection window: base 0x001D8B6C, vtable 0x77404C (party-select row binding) and six 0x14-byte member rows, one per party member.
evidence: vtable uRam003BBFFC = 0x77404C with maybe_Ui_PartySelectWindow_BindSelectedRow and maybe_Ui_Window_ReleaseSlotIcon; 0x00100050(self+0x11c, ctor, 0x14, 6) = 6 rows of 0x14 bytes. Six matches the DQXI party size.

name: maybe_Ui_PartySelect_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: stores the vtable argument, runs the scene-node base teardown 0x001D8C2C and releases the block.
evidence: Same three-instruction template as 0x002C321C and 0x003E37D0 with the vtable passed in; nothing in the body or the call graph names a party-select object, so the class label stays a guess.

name: Ui_Marker_FollowActor
summary: Lazily allocates the 0x98-byte marker and keeps it on its actor: copies the actor position, hides the sprite when the actor is hidden/far (distance limit actor+0x320), and refreshes attachment visibility.
evidence: The body has a unique combination (lazy 0x98 allocation, actor position f_9C/A0/A4, distance compare against actor+0x320, Model_Actor_UpdateAttachmentVisibility) that matches "marker follows actor" and not a generic object update; named neighbours in the same vtable are marker methods.

name: Ui_Window_SetState
summary: Sets a window's state through its holder: marks the window dirty, resets its sub-object lists for the new state (maybe_Ui_Window_ResetSubObjectLists), commits the sub-objects, records the state and clears the retry counter; when there is no window it raises the holder's 'unavailable' byte.
evidence: NEW: the reset callee is now named (maybe_Ui_Window_ResetSubObjectLists) and the three callers are message/status window updaters, so the holder really is a window slot and the value really is its state.

name: maybe_Ui_Marker_RetryBindTarget
summary: Throttled rebind step of a UI marker: counts up the retry counter at +0x08, then samples an id through 0x00649050 (0xff = not ready), stores it on the target object and commits it.
evidence: Body is damaged - Ghidra emits coprocessor_movefromRt and halt_baddata right after the counter branch - so per FACTS.md it stays maybe_ at <= 0.3. Only the 'if (self+8 < 10) self+8 += 1' throttle is readable; the rest of the summary restates the disassembly notes in the header and is not independently verified.

name: maybe_Ui_Marker_RetryBindTarget_Label
summary: Unaligned Thumb entry artefact located two bytes inside 0x003BC428 instruction; not an independent function.
evidence: Sits at 0x003BC42E inside 0x003BC418; Ghidra decompilation is halt_baddata(). Kept maybe_ at 0.20 per FACTS.md.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateSubObject
signature: void* Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateSubObject(void* slot, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates and registers the 0x200-byte sub-object of the tactics (sakusen) window: allocates from the UI heap, constructs it with the sakusen sub-object ctor, registers it through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, stores it in the slot and clears the slot's ready byte at +0x94.

summary: Releases the sub-object referenced by slot word [1] through the UI core's heap and clears the slot, returning the slot so callers can chain; a template copy of the same body lives at 0x003D2DFC.
evidence: The free is the UI heap release used elsewhere for UI children and the slot word is cleared immediately; the only unknown is which class owns the slot, which does not matter for this generic release helper.

name: maybe_Ui_SpriteActor_CreateEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_SpriteActor_CreateEntry(void* self, const void* params)
summary: Creates a 3D sprite-actor entry for the UI: allocates the 0x298-byte actor object, initialises its parameter block, creates the sprite from the table and links it into the list.
evidence: The allocation/ctor/vtable sequence (0x00109DC8 + 0x003DE3E0 + vtable 0x003BC7E8) and the list * link 0x001235A4 are clear; 'for the UI' rests on the surrounding 0x003Bxxxx UI block.

name: maybe_Ui_SpriteActor_SetSprite
summary: Resolves sprite id through 0x002D1810 and assigns the resulting handle to the sprite actor via tail call to 0x002B6B24.
evidence: Two-call setter: bl 0x002D1810 then tail b 0x002B6B24. No named callers or callees to confirm class; kept maybe_.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a sprite actor: stores the caller-supplied vtable and its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the render node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
