name: Field_FindPlacementCellByDelta
signature: void Field_FindPlacementCellByDelta(u32* out, int* dx, int* dy, u32 record, u32 record2, u32* extra)
summary: Searches for a placement cell one step away from the current one: reads the field object manager's grid at (work+8)->f_54->f_20, resolves the record pointers, offsets the current cell index by dx/dy and tests the candidate through maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaB.
evidence: Both named callers are placement code (Ui_PlaceWidgetInFreeCell 0x004231B4, Field_FindFreePlacementCell2D 0x00651A24) and the body reads the field grid at (work+8)->f_54->f_20, offsets the current cell (f_78) by dx/dy and tests the candidate; 'Ui_List_MoveCursorByDelta' described a menu cursor, which the callers contradict.

name: maybe_Ui_List_CanMoveCursor
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_List_CanMoveCursor(u32 cursor, u32 target, u32 arg3, u32 direction)
summary: Cursor-move gate: when Field2D_MapChip_CanWalkDirection reports that the map chip cannot be walked it asks maybe_Ui_List_CellMatchesAtPoint about the {cursor, target} pair in the given direction, otherwise the move is allowed and it returns 1.
evidence: Both callees are now readable: the gate is the named Field2D_MapChip_CanWalkDirection (0x005A34E4) and the real test is maybe_Ui_List_CellMatchesAtPoint (0x00642248), called with a three-word {cursor, target, 0} record. That combination belongs to the 2D field screen rather than a plain menu list, and the callers (maybe_Ui_List_IsCursorCellFree / _Empty) are themselves maybe_ names, so the 'Ui_List_' prefix stays a maybe_.

name: Map_IsCellPassable
summary: Returns true when the map cell is walkable: false if the interaction/blocking test 0x005A3604() reports busy or if the terrain/collision id returned by 0x00664A80(cell) equals 9. Called for every cell in an area footprint by hit-test and placement code.
evidence: Callers maybe_Ui_HitTestGrid (0x0031AD20) and maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaC (0x006E4C68) loop over 2x2 / rect footprints accumulating this result; sentinel id 9 plus 0x005A3604 busy check.

name: maybe_Ui_List_MoveCursorToFreeCell
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_MoveCursorToFreeCell(u32* out, int* offsetRect, int* gridSize, u32 group, u32 key, u32* owner)
summary: Scans a gridSize[0] x gridSize[1] rectangle of cells anchored at the current field object's position (work->f_54->f_20 + f_78/f_7c), returns in out the first cell that the geometric cell hit-test accepts, or the empty record when none does; the not-found path instead tests the area around the actor through 0x006E4900. The caller 0x003BD008 uses the empty record as 'no free cell', so 'free' is still only the caller's interpretation: the accept test itself is a pure hit-test.
evidence: NEW (negative): its only caller is the still-tentative maybe_Ui_List_FindFirstFreeSlot (0x003BD008, 0.45), and the accept callee is the geometric maybe_Ui_List_CellMatchesAtPoint (0x00642248, refined at 0.49 in R3_071). Both the 'cursor' and 'free' wording therefore remain the caller's semantics; only the grid scan and the CellMatchesAtPoint test are proven.

name: maybe_Ui_List_FindFirstFreeSlot
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_FindFirstFreeSlot(char* out, u32 record, u32 grid, u32 group, u64 packed)
summary: Searches a list/grid for the first free slot in one of three scan orders (forward, backward or rotated, chosen by the current layout mode 0/2/4) and returns the first hit, or the empty record.
evidence: The caller Ui_PlaceWidgetInFreeCell supports the 'free cell' reading, but the accept test itself is the hit-test maybe_Ui_List_MoveCursorToFreeCell (0.40) and the three scan orders come from the layout mode via 0x002D1810, so 'free' is still the caller's interpretation.

name: Ui_Object_SelectEmbeddedNode
summary: Broadcasts the selection flag to the children of the embedded node at self+0x3430: passes 1 only when that node equals the element pointer given in r1, so the node shows when it is the current selection and hides otherwise.
evidence: The body is a single tail call to the now-named Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(object+0x3430, object+0x3430 == arg2), the same shape as Ui_SelectElement 0x00259928 with +0x3430 instead of +0x838; the five callers are pane push/pop and bind paths that pass a node pointer.

name: Ui_ListWindow_AddRowToView
summary: Action step that copies one data row into the list window's view: tail-calls 0x00612848(bagWork, rowId), which rejects rows whose name is 7+ characters or whose id/key is empty, finds the first free slot of the 20-entry view table at bagWork+0x7b3c and copies the 0x84-byte row plus its flags and owner key into it; returns 1 on success, 0 when the row is unusable or the view is full.
evidence: Disassembly of the callee settles it: 0x00612848 computes bag + rowId*0x8c + 0x5fe4, calls wcslen on it and bails when the length is >= 7, then scans the 20 entries at bag+0x7b3c for a free slot and memcpys 0x84 bytes. So the merged name Ui_DataPanel_GetRowNameLength is a misnomer - the length test is only a guard - and the wrapper really adds a row to the view. The caller is the named Ui_Window_StartActionBOr2.

name: Ui_ListWindow_RemoveRowByKey
signature: u32 Ui_ListWindow_RemoveRowByKey(void* self, const u32* key)
summary: Action step that removes one row from the list window's view: loads the owner key and calls 0x00612fc8(bagWork, &key), which finds the row of the 20-entry view table at bagWork+0x7b3c whose +0x88 key matches, shifts the following rows down one 0x8c record and clears the last row (key = -1).
evidence: The callee is the already-named Ui_DataPanel_RemoveRowByOwner (0x00612FC8), which matches the reading exactly, and both callers are named window action handlers (Ui_Window_StartAction8Or18, Ui_Window_StartAction8Or2) that pass a record field as the key. The wrapper itself is a 56-byte load-and-call, so there is nothing left to doubt.

name: Ui_DiveForm_InitPanes
summary: Binds every pane of the dive/profile window: the normal and VIP backgrounds, the title and the five list panes, then all the sub-windows (people list, list2, album, keyboard, name entry, talk, yes/no, call list, gold, accessory, operation).
evidence: The literal pane-name table is exhaustive: "bg_normal", "bg_vip", "title", "list_4", "bg_list_normal2", "list2", "list1", "list_5", "list_6", "bg_list_normal", "bg_list_vip", "btn_set1", "menu_dive_peaple", "menu_dive_list", "menu_dive_list2", "menu_dive_album", "win_load_keyboard", "win_load_name", "win_talk", "win_yesno", "menu_dive_calllist", "win_gold", "menu_dive_gold", "menu_dive_accessory", "menu_dive_operation". Slot 3 of five different window vtables (0x758C74, 0x75E6DC, 0x7627C8, 0x762DCC, 0x768FC8), so it is the shared InitPanes of the dive-family windows; Ui_MessagePair_Bind (0x001DACFC) pairs win_talk/win_yesno.

name: Ui_DiveForm_BindControl
summary: Unlinks the window's control node and rebinds the shared control slot used by all five dive-family windows.
evidence: Slot 11 of all five dive vtables (0x00758CA0, 0x0075E708, 0x007627F4, 0x00762DF8, 0x00768FF8). Rebinds shared control slot via confident Ui_Slot_BindControl(self+0x34D8, control).

name: Ui_BaseWindow_Release
summary: Shared release/destructor tail for base windows: calls the base teardown 0x0029F9E0, the class hook at vtable +0x4C, clears the per-object 'pool owner' flag at self+0x356C while clearing the shared pooled UI object, then runs the vtable +0x60 hook and rebinds the child pane.
evidence: It occupies the release slot of four window vtables (0x758C74, 0x75E6DC, 0x7627C8, 0x762DCC) and slot 5 of 0x768FC8, and the body calls the base teardown then only release hooks; the single ambiguous part is the 0x98-byte pooled object, which is a shared scratch object rather than a per-window allocation.

name: Ui_Window_SelectRowFromRef
signature: void Ui_Window_SelectRowFromRef(void* self, const UiItemRef* ref)
summary: Makes the display row named by a {index, kind} list-item reference the current row: resolves the reference with Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRowSimple and copies the row into the data panel's current-row block through Ui_DataPanel_CopyRowIntoCurrent.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body does not use the window's own row array - it resolves a ref and copies the row into the savedata/data-panel current block at work+0x24A98, which is why the callee is Ui_DataPanel_CopyRowIntoCurrent; the old 'Ui_ListWindow' class label overstated what the call site proves.

name: ActorActionSeq_RunNode
signature: void ActorActionSeq_RunNode(ActorSeqRunner* self, int nodeIndex, int step)
summary: Runs one node of the actor action sequence: resets the command list at runner+0x4C8, marks the runner busy (+0x4C4), pushes the 0x10-byte node at array[index] with the step number, and when the node has neither +3 nor +6 set it marks +6 = 1 and the per-actor state byte (work + actorId*0x8C + 0x2AB00) so the step runs only once.
evidence: Twelve callers, all named *ActionSeq_Run* steps (plus the field NPC-event dispatch), all passing a node index into the same f_34/f_38 0x10-byte array that maybe_ActorActionSeq_CollectPendingNodes scans; the once-only marking explains the +6 flag. The old guess needed no wording change.

name: Ui_ListWindow_RemoveSourceRowAt
summary: Deletes row `index` from the 50-entry, 0x8C-byte row table at (work+0x24A98)+0x5FE4: the rows behind it shift down one slot and the freed last row is zeroed with a 0xFFFFFFFF key.
evidence: Named caller Ui_Window_StartAction4Or2 dispatches it as a list action, and 0x00612F5C's disassembly is a memmove of (0x31-index)*0x8C bytes upward over the row at index followed by clearing entry 49 - an index-based row delete, not a flag setter.

name: maybe_Actor_SubObject_ResetAndActivate
summary: Reset-and-activate handler of an actor sub-object (sole slot of vtable 0x0072BD8C): resets the base state, re-shows every child of the +0x180 list, drains the pending-animation counter, re-links the embedded node and sets the sub-widget state to 1.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body starts with Actor_SubObject_Reset and then re-links and activates, so 'Finish' described the wrong end of the transition; it is the same template as the 0x002FDxxx/0x00307xxx family. The class is only known from the vtable literal, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ActorRow_Refresh
summary: Refreshes an actor list row from field/bag state: reads gold and storage values from bag work (+0x24A98) through 0x0066B11C and 0x0066B19C, stores them into sub-objects at +0x160/+0x184, then formats the row message from work record +0x6B8.
evidence: Disassembly 0x003BDAD8..0x003BDB4C reads game work + 0x24800 + 0x298 (ItemBag / Storage work at 0x24A98, per FACTS.md) and passes returned values to 0x00316024(self+0x160), 0x004603F8(self+0x184), 0x00315F98(self+0x160), and 0x003B7DAC(self+0x1C0) via 0x006290A8. Covered by container in functions_index.json; kept maybe_ with corrected bag work evidence.

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderObject_ReleaseBindings
summary: Conditionally releases the three resource bindings held by a render object: the texture binding at +0x68 (when +0x90 is clear), the material binding at +0x94 (when +0x28 is set and +0x30 clear) and the material set at +0x98.
evidence: The three release callees are named in the readable doc, but the decompiled body is damaged (all accesses go through unaff_r4, the argument register was lost), so the exact owner/field mapping cannot be verified - keep maybe_ at <=0.3 per the damaged-body rule.

name: std_LoadU64
signature: u64 std_LoadU64(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u64* p)
summary: Trivial 64-bit load: returns *p unchanged (used as a callback where the container passes two context words that the accessor ignores).

name: Actor_SubObject_Reset
summary: Shared reset of an actor sub-object: resets the ten embedded lists/flags (+0x138, +0x140, +0x17C, +0x1A4, +0x1C4, +0x1F4, +0x1FC, +0x208 ...), marks it busy at +0x14C, starts animation track 15 on the pane at +0x1A4 and moves the state machine at +0x23C back to 0.
evidence: Sixteen destructors call it (maybe_Actor_SubObject_Release*, maybe_Text_Block_Dtor*, 0x003BD9F4, 0x003BDCCC) as their first step, and its own callee 0x002D214C is maybe_Ui_Pane_StartAnimFrame15 (N_023), so this is the common 'detach everything and rewind' routine of the actor sub-object class.

name: Ui_DiveForm_Close
summary: Shuts the dive window down: drains the pending message queue, releases the two control blocks, resets the actor sub-objects, sets the label state and hands over to the shared UI reset helper at +0xBC8.
evidence: NEW: the header's table entry 0x0072C08C places it in the Ui_DiveForm vtable (0x003BD260) next to Ui_DiveForm_DeletingDestructor, and the release calls are field/UI reset helpers used by the other dive-window teardown paths - the 'close this window' reading holds.

name: Data_SetIndexedLabel
signature: void Data_SetIndexedLabel(int unusedCtx, int index, const u16* label)
summary: Stores a 7-character UTF-16 label in the indexed 0x8C-stride label table in GameWork: clears the four leading words of the row and copies the fixed-length string with zero padding.
evidence: The body is fully unambiguous (base + index*0x8C, four cleared words, std_wcsncpy of 7 wide chars) and both named callees (Game_GetWork, std_wcsncpy) confirm it; only what the table is used for remains unknown, which the generic 'Data_' prefix admits.

name: Party_AppendBlankMemberRecords
summary: Calls Party_List_InsertBlankRecord(bagWork) `count` times: that helper shifts the 0x2A0-byte party-record array at bagWork+0x9400 up one slot and installs a freshly blanked record at the front, so this appends `count` empty party members.
evidence: The callee is the already-named Party_List_InsertBlankRecord (0x00193018), and the loop runs exactly `count` times on work+0x24A98; the old 'UI party list insert' reading of 0x00193018 is superseded by the 0x2A0-stride record shift.

name: maybe_ActorActionSeq_CollectPendingNodes
summary: Collects into a 50-entry buffer the ids (first word of each 0x10-byte node) of the action-sequence nodes that are enabled (+9 non-zero) but not started (+3 zero), then blanks the matching rows of the 50-entry work table at bagWork+0x5fe4 through Ui_DataPanel_ResetRowsByIndexList, and returns how many nodes were collected.
evidence: The body is fully readable and the callees are named (std_memmove, Ui_DataPanel_ResetRowsByIndexList, Game_GetWork), so the collect-then-blank behaviour is certain. What stays open is whether the collected words are node ids or row ids, and the runner object at self+0x3570 is only identified by the sibling 0x003BD908, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Actor_SetStateWord
signature: void maybe_Actor_SetStateWord(void* self, int actorId, u16 value)
summary: Plain setter that stores a u16 at work + actorId*0x8C + 0x2AAF8, in the same per-record array whose neighbouring +0x2AB00 byte is the record's state.

name: maybe_Party_CollectMemberIds

name: Model_BindIndexedResource
signature: u32 Model_BindIndexedResource(Model* self, int index, Resource* res)

name: Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain

evidence: NEW: same caller set as 0x003C0BCC (three field steppers plus Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateActorStep), so the 'Field_' prefix is wrong; the fully readable body bumps +0x9A6/+0x87D and returns 1 only when the limit was reached, which matches 'advance the action cursor'.

evidence: The caller Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain and the named Battle_AddStateFlags / Sound_PlaySeById callees make the command-apply reading explicit; the 'M' type test, index wrap by func_00630D64 and the +0x16BA SE id are all visible in the body.

evidence: NEW: all four dispatch targets are named (maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_RunExtraEntry, Field_ActorActionSeq_StepEntryA, Field_ActorActionSeq_AppendEntries) and the three wait branches share the exact 'set wait id, check +0x11/+0x0E, check Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty' pattern with concrete ids. That is the actor step dispatcher, not a single action. 0.55 because the actor state byte at +0x168D is still unnamed and states 6/7 share state 0's path.

name: Battle_Ui_UpdateMemberActionDisplay

summary: Walks the intrusive list (head sentinel at +0, resume node at +0xC) and invokes each node's member-function pointer at node+0x1A4; when a node reports busy it remembers the next node and stops, and it sets the done byte +0x6A once the list is empty or a node stays busy.
evidence: The body is a plain intrusive-list walk with a done byte, and all seven callers are still unnamed screen-close / SE helpers (maybe_Ui_CloseScreenIfFlag, maybe_Menu_PlaySelectSe, ...), so only the 'drain pending list' wording is supported - the 'Menu' subsystem is a guess.

name: maybe_PendingList_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the intrusive list that 0x003D1454 drains: makes the three head words at +0..+8 point at the object, clears the bookkeeping, copies the two sentinel counters from 0x003D15BC/0x003D15C0 into +0x6C/+0x88/+0x8C and zeroes the 0x59-byte node array at +0x10.
evidence: New: the fields match the drainer exactly - this ctor sets the done byte +0x6A to 0 and the resume node +0xC to 0, which are precisely the two fields 0x003D1454 reads and writes. That drainer is called only from UI screen-close / SE helpers, so the old 'Gfx_ResourceHandleList' subsystem was wrong; the list itself is a pending-work list, hence the vaguer name.

name: maybe_Gfx_ResourceHandle_Init
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_ResourceHandle_Init(void* handle, u32 allocator, ResourceDesc* desc)
summary: Creates the resource object for a handle: allocates the 0xC0-byte structure and copies the default block, or builds the 0x50-byte fallback through 0x005ABEB4; returns 1/0.

name: maybe_Event_Packet_ReleaseResource
summary: Releases/detaches one resource handle of an event packet: resolves it through 0x5F5818, calls the resource vtable +0x98/+0x9C when not loaded, otherwise releases it from the render manager.

name: Event_Packet_SetAnimationVariant
summary: The event-packet animation-variant setter: it attaches cbhm_tcs_mant and selects a ccg392_v0xx variant.
evidence: The body contains the literals cbhm_tcs_mant and ccg392_v010/v011/v012/v020/v021/v030/v031, calls 0x002248FC attach and 0x003D1B54 play-named, and is invoked from Event_AnyUnitFlagSet.

name: Event_Packet_GetResourcePair
signature: bool Event_Packet_GetResourcePair(EventPacket* packet, u32 arg2, u32 key, int* outA, int* outB)
summary: Resolves two resource values for a packet key through Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueD and Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueA on the packet's resource descriptor and returns them through outA/outB; returns false unless both resolve.
evidence: NEW: both getters are named Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueD/_A and operate on packet->f_4->f_14, so the pair is a resource-descriptor query; it is a one-slot vtable entry (0x00769850 slot 6), which fits the 'provide two related values' contract.

name: Event_Packet_GetResourcePayload
summary: Resolves the resource handle at +4 (Container_FindEntryByTagAndType) and returns a pointer 0x60 bytes into the resolved block, i.e. the payload of the event-packet resource; returns false when the resource is absent.

name: Script_LookupIntTableValueC
signature: u32 Script_LookupIntTableValueC(ScriptContext* self, u32 packetId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 key, int* out)
summary: Looks a key up in the packet/actor entry chain (packet, then +0x160, then +0x11C, then Model_FindEntryById) and returns entry+0x20, falling back to Script_GetIntTable2 on the context table when the entry or the value is missing. Returns 0 when both paths miss.
evidence: New context: the chain callees are now named (Model_FindEntryById, Script_GetIntTable2), so the lookup-with-int-table-fallback reading is supported; the C suffix only distinguishes it from its sibling 0x003D1C50.

name: Script_LookupIntTableValueD
signature: bool Script_LookupIntTableValueD(ScriptContext* self, u32 key, int* out)
summary: Context-table variant of the script integer lookup: calls Script_GetIntTable3 on *(self+4)+0x14, writes the found value to *out and returns whether a non-zero value was found.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x003D1B2C loads the two arguments from the incoming stack at +8, confirming that the in_stack_00000000/4 words in the damaged C are the real key and out parameters; it then calls the confident Script_GetIntTable3 and returns 1 exactly when the result is non-zero. Its C and E siblings (0x003D1AB8 / 0x003D1C50) already carry the same lookup name at 0.50.

name: maybe_Gfx_BindMaterialSet
signature: void maybe_Gfx_BindMaterialSet(void* self, u32 packetId, u32 variantId)
summary: Binds a material/resource set: resolves the packet/model handle at packetId (0x005F5818), asks the context for the variant through virtual slot +0x14, builds the material set with Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant on the render target at self[2]+0x9C, submits it through 0x0065C1F8 and releases it with Gfx_MaterialSet_Release. No caller, so the owner class (previously guessed ScriptContext) is still unproven.
evidence: NEW: every callee is now named and consistent with a one-shot material-set bind/submit/release (Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant, Gfx_MaterialSet_Release, Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault), and the packet resolve 0x005F5818 is the same handle resolver used by Battle2DUnit_Dtor. But the function has neither a caller nor a vtable slot, so the 'self' class stays unknown; kept below 0.5.

name: Script_LookupIntTableValueE
signature: u32 Script_LookupIntTableValueE(ScriptContext* self, u32 packetId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 key, int* out)
summary: Same packet/actor lookup as 0x003D1AB8 but reads entry+0x28 and falls back to 0x001943B8 (Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueB) on the context table; returns 0 when both paths miss.
evidence: New context: identical now-named chain to 0x003D1AB8 with a different record field and fallback, so it is the sibling lookup rather than a different operation.

name: maybe_Event_Packet_ReleaseChildren
summary: Releases the packet's child list (0x14 entries of two words), detaches it and frees it; used by the scene teardown paths.

name: Event_Packet_AttachModel
signature: void Event_Packet_AttachModel(EventPacket* packet, u32 handle, u32 modelId, int slot, * u32 arg5, u8 variant)

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_InitSubWindows

name: maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetA
signature: void maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetA(void* flagId, int flagId2, int slot)
summary: Icon-stack builder (variant A): while fewer than three icons are placed it tests one of three global flags (0x0066B088 accepts only flagId < 4 through 0x0066B8B0); a clear flag hides the pane at self+slot*4+0x7C, otherwise the next entry's position (self+count*4+0x70, fields +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24) is copied into that pane, the pane is shown and the count at +0x88 is incremented.
evidence: Both callees are now readable as small flag helpers (0x0066B8B0 combines three byte arrays into bits 0..2 and 0x0066AF34's blob tests one bit), so flagId is a 0..3 category index rather than a map id. No caller and no vtable slot tells which icon class this copy serves.

name: Ui_IconRowWindow_InitPanes

summary: Variant of 0x003D2084 that initialises the same three sub-windows through builder 0x003D2300 (indices 0/2/3), clears the selection byte and selects entry 1 through virtual +0x18.

name: maybe_Ui_MapIcon_AddIfFlagSetB

The two embedded sub-objects are re-stamped with vtable 0x00774F68, which is exactly the Ui_CursorWidget vtable of 0x00485D70 in this same batch - the two-cursor layout that initialiser describes. name: maybe_Ui_Element_UpdateChildLayers
summary: Slot 0 of the Ui_Element vtable: when the layout object at +0x11C reports a screen-size class other than 40.0f it (re)creates child layer 1, when it reports 45.0f it creates child layer 3, and it finally ticks the widget's own virtual +0x2C.

name: Ui_Element_ResolveResourceRefC
signature: void Ui_Element_ResolveResourceRefC(int self, int* stream, int* reader)

name: Ui_Widget_CreateChildLayer

name: maybe_Ui_AmountSpinner_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: class destructor 0x001D8C2C (vptr reset plus unlink of the +0x114 list) followed by operator delete 0x0010F6CC. It heads vtable 0x00769AA8, whose slots 4-6 are the range-check / update methods 0x003D273C, 0x003D2810 and 0x003D27CC.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x00769AA8, whose slot 4 (0x003D273C) does a range check on self+0x11C and whose slots 5/6 are the paired update methods - so the deleting-destructor role is solid. The 'AmountSpinner' class name still comes only from the neighbouring resolver stubs.

name: Ui_AmountSpinner_Step
signature: void Ui_AmountSpinner_Step(UiAmountSpinner* self, int digitDelta, int amountDelta)
summary: Steps a money/quantity spinner: moves the digit place (+0x54, clamped 1..7), adds or subtracts 10^(place-1) to the amount (+0x58), keeps it >= 1, clamps it so amount + wallet stays <= 9,999,999, clamps amount * unit price (+0x5C) against the cap at work+0x24AC0 and refreshes both number panes.
evidence: New: the wallet read is 0x0066B2CC(bagWork, 0) and the constant it is clamped against is 0x0098967F, the documented gold cap (FACTS: gold, cap 9,999,999); the per-unit multiplication by +0x5C is a price, so 'amount spinner' is no longer just a guess. Pane refresh goes through the named number-pane setter.

name: Ui_SetNumberText
signature: void Ui_SetNumberText(UiObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Writes the widget's two number panes: formats f_58 as the main amount into pane 0 with font id 0x21 and the product f_5C*f_58 into pane 1 with font id 0x15, through the shared '%d' argument setter and func_001A6680.

name: Gfx_Resource_MarkLoaded
summary: Marks a resource reference as loaded: when the runtime handle at +4 exists and 0x00645848 confirms it, sets the flag byte at +0. Called from Gfx_Resources_Release while walking the resource list.

name: Ui_TitleMessage_CreateChild
signature: void * Ui_TitleMessage_CreateChild(void * slot, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

evidence: Byte-for-byte the same body as the confirmed Ui_ReleaseSubObject (0x003BC520), and its callers are generic teardown paths (Gfx_Resources_Release, Gfx_Resource_Recreate34, Ui_Screen_ReleaseMembers), not title-message code. The old 'Ui_TitleMessage_ReleaseChild' attributed the slot to a class the body never touches; the 'B' suffix marks the template copy.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLine_Reset
summary: Resets one text-line record: id byte 0xFF, float animation/alpha 0.0f, state bytes 0/1, u16 at +0x0A = 0, then clears the 7-wchar text buffer at +0x10 to an empty wide string. The readable C is truncated only because Ghidra mis-marks the wcslen blx 0x00100B74 as noreturn.
evidence: Both named callers are text-layout code (Text_LayoutLines and Ui_Pager_InitTextLayers), which reset their per-line records before filling them, and the twin 0x003D2EE4 has the identical reset prefix and is also called from Text_LayoutLines. No character-status or HP field is read, so 'CharStatusTag' (which came from the wide name buffer) was the wrong reading.

name: maybe_Text_LayoutState_Init
summary: Initialises a text-layout state record: writes a 0x1E-byte descriptor (type 0xFF, float size at +4, flags 0/1, 7-wchar style name at +0x10), then allocates and constructs the 0x18-byte arrays in the save-work area and runs a popcount-based probe; called from Text_LayoutLines.
evidence: The tail call is wcslen (0x00100B74), not a noreturn abort, so the body is not truncated and 'Os_StaticCtor' was wrong; the disassembly shows `strb #0xFF`, `vstr s0,[r4,#4]`, wcsncpy of a 6-wchar literal into +0x10, then std_ConstructArray(...,0x18,0xFF) on work+0x24A94 and the 0x55555555/0x33333333/0x0F0F0F0F popcount sequence. The exact role is still unclear, so maybe_ at 0.30.

name: Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchors

evidence: Callees maybe_Battle_Ui_GetBalloonAnchor (0x001F6EC4), maybe_Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons (0x001F5F5C), maybe_Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor (0x001F89CC); caller 0x003D3A38 (balloon state machine); writes anchor slots self[0x3d..0x42].

evidence: Callees GetMemberAnchorScreen (0x001F9F88), 0x003CA408 (member pose update), 0x001F9B58, math 0x005736A0, sound 0x005E7848(id 0x36); caller 0x003D3A38; fields self[0x3b55..] hold anchor state.

name: Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateState
summary: State machine for a battle balloon/gauge sequence: states 0xE30..0xE50 drive fade-in, anchor move, rotation, sound and completion, calling 0x003D32B4 and 0x003D35C0 and reading the tracked model's flags.
evidence: Switch over self->f_ed40 values -1/0xE30/0xE3F/0xE46/0xE4B/0xE50; calls 0x003D32B4, 0x003D35C0, 0x004D5228, 0x004D5608, 0x005E7848; returns self->f_ed3c.

name: Ui_TargetMarker_ObjectDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of one battle target-marker object: destroys the sixteen 0xE4-byte effect entries at +0xC8, releases the effect link sub-object at +0x70, installs the base vtable, destroys the inherited sixteen 0x58-byte entries and frees the outer block.

name: Battle_Ui_Balloon_GetGroupCenter
summary: Writes the balloon group centre: normally FieldParty_CalcGroupCenterPosition, but when the group-follow flag is set it tracks the model of the unit matching the current leader id and applies its facing offset.
evidence: Caller Ui_BattleTargetMarker_Manager_Update (0x003D427C); callee FieldParty_CalcGroupCenterPosition (0x001FAC10); flag at arg1+0x22af, leader id at arg1[0x8a9].

name: Ui_SmithMenu_DetailStack_PopPush

name: Ui_StatComparePanel_Fill

evidence: The nine row calls with the record's u16 fields (+0x12, +0x1A, +0x26, +0x2A and the vtable+8 accessor) and the temporary func_001902A4(record,8) clear/restore pair make the comparison direction explicit; 0x003FBC78 is the row emitter in this batch.

name: Ui_StatComparePanel_SetRow

name: Ui_TwoColumnTextWindow_InitPanes

evidence: drN then virtual +0x34 with 'txt_text' (0x003FBE18); a nine-iteration loop formats 'txt_r1_%d' (0x003FBE24) with i+1 and 'txt_r2_%d' (0x003FBE30) with i+1, attaching them at layout ids i+1 and i+10, and finally calls virtual +0x18(self,0) (the select/index reset).

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorList

evidence: arg2[0x10] count and vtable+0xD4 per actor; ids 0x25/0x26/0x28/0x29 and g_003fc608 (0xC76); allocates 0x218 and fills +0x208/+0x20C/+0x210/+0x214/+0x215/+0x218; 34 callers incl. 0x1FB4A4 FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine, 0x31FDB8/0x320868 Battle_ActionSequence, 0x388A38 Battle_Ui_InitPartyLayout, 0x3C123C Field_ActorActionSeq_AppendEntries.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_ClearAll
summary: Clears/hides all current popup/display entries: fetches the battle context and posts the reserved id 0xFFFF with a null entry and the given fade flag, which makes the popup manager drop the active entries. Called before every batch of new popups.
evidence: Posts 0x20A9B8(ctx,0xFFFF,0xFFFFFFFF,0, is2D, fadeMode); 0x2DFDE8 handles id 0xFFFF as the special clear case; 61 callers across battle UI (0x38FF08, 0x3F463C...), field (0x1FB4A4) and menu code - the common first action of every popup spawner.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnValue

evidence: The small entry layout and the fixed 0x4C post id are explicit, and the only caller is Battle_Equip_UpdateArmourSlot, which needs a plain value message.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair(u32 ctx, u32* desc, int fadeMode)

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForStatus
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForStatus(u32 ctx, u8* desc, int fadeMode)

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList(u32 ctx, void* valueList, int fadeStep)
summary: Builds the numeric popup entry for one actor: if the record has several 12-byte rows it averages their signed values and picks the multi-number animation (0x1A-0x1F / 0x1C/0x20 / 0x33 family); for a single value it picks the small/big variant, then posts the 0x21C-byte entry through 0x20A9B8. This is the damage/heal number popup used by the action sequences.
evidence: Reads arg2->f_480 count and signed shorts with stride 0xC, averages via 0.5f (g_003fcd70) and posts ids 0x1A..0x1F/0x1C/0x20/0x30..0x33/0xDB; fills +0x208/+0x20C/+0x210/+0x214/+0x218/+0x219; 34 callers incl. 0x31FDB8/0x320868/0x322130 Battle_ActionSequence and 0x3F6530/0x3F8C48.
