evidence: Body is exactly two calls: func_001A6768 (named Ui_Object_DtorBase by N_0xx) and func_0010F6CC, the free helper that closes every destructor in this range. No field is read or written.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyCharacterParam
summary: Applies one character-display parameter to the model: resolves the party member with 0x0035EB98(work, self->f_3C), bails out when the member's +0xDA bit 0x10 is set, resolves the portrait index (f_3D, or the first valid one), reads the 0x10-byte portrait entry and binds the resulting transform/resource.
evidence: NEW: the callers now include Gfx_CreateEquipObjectForNode, and the callee Party_ResolveAppearanceVariantIndex shows this is appearance/portrait parameter application; the body has several removed unreachable blocks, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SecondaryDeletingDtorA
summary: Deleting destructor in the secondary (multiple-inheritance) vtable 0x0076D6A8: runs the 0x002650C4 Ui window base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: Vtable 0x0076D6A8 re-read: every slot is a 0x002650xx Ui window base method plus the adjustor 0x0040A370, so the class is a Ui window subclass with multiple inheritance; 'PanelPart' was a placeholder and no slot identifies the concrete class.

name: Model_Equip_CreateWeaponMeshes
summary: Creates the four equipment meshes of a character model: slots 0 and 1 get a 'meshWeaponEquip' node, slots 2 and 3 get a 'meshSheathEquip' node; each node is attached to the owner, given a layout config and stored at self+0x40+8*slot.
evidence: Loops slots 0..3, allocating 0x6EC-byte scene nodes (g_0040A65C) and creating them with func_00225D90(size, params, name, self->f_38) using the literal names 'meshWeaponEquip' (0x0040A660) for slots 0/1 and 'meshSheathEquip' (0x0040A670) for slots 2/3; stores the node at self+slot*8+0x40, keeps self->f_2C as its owner, applies a config block through func_00221AA8 (maybe_Ui_ApplyLayoutConfig) and registers it with func_005E7650. Callers are the battle action-anim window 0x002EC50C, the equip window 0x003D4834 and the generic UI sub-window 0x003E6110, i.e. every screen that shows an equipped character.

name: Model_Equip_ApplyCommand
signature: void Model_Equip_ApplyCommand(CharacterModel* self, const u8* cmd, int updateCompare)
summary: Applies one equipment command to a character model: commands 0/1 set the weapon or off-hand item, commands 2..5 clear all attached items, and when updateCompare is set it recomputes the equipment compare code and notifies the panel if it changed.
evidence: Dispatches to the three model helpers named in this batch (0x0040B174 slot 0, 0x0040B02C slot 1, 0x0040B364 clear); callers 0x00377420 and 0x0066DAD0 are the equipment-change paths, and the compare code comes from 0x0031D178 - the same function the equip text window uses at the start of this batch.

name: Model_Equip_AttachItemNode
signature: void Model_Equip_AttachItemNode(CharacterModel* self, int slot, int itemId, const float* transform)
summary: Attaches the mesh node of an item to the model: builds the attachment record (node name 'N_ALL', the item's transform block), for slot 1 rotates it by pi/2 using the sin/cos helpers so the off-hand item is oriented correctly, then creates the node through 0x0040A980 and stores the item id in the slot; on failure it releases the node and stores 0xFFFF.
evidence: The two rotation constants in the pool are pi and 2*pi (0x40490FDB and 0x40C90FDB) and 0x3F000000 is 0.5, so the 'cos/sin (angle-0.5)*2pi' block is a half-turn offset; 'N_ALL' is the node-name literal and the 0xFFFF sentinel is the shared 'no item' value.

name: Model_Equip_CommitNodeChanges
summary: Commits a pending node change: when the node exists it intersects the model's visibility mask with the character's +0x12E4 byte and, if the node should be shown, applies the model state and re-binds the node; then marks the reference as committed (byte +6).
evidence: Nineteen callers across the model/effect code (including 0x0040B674 and the field NPC/actor code); the mask test 'self->f_62 & actor->f_12E4' is the same pair that 0x0040AB04 uses to show/hide the four nodes.

name: Model_CreateAttachedEffect
signature: u32 Model_CreateAttachedEffect(CharacterModel* self, ItemRecord* item, const void* nodeDesc)
summary: Builds the effect node that visualises an equipped item: copies the item's 0x12-byte effect parameter block plus its colour/scale fields, creates the attached effect (0x2239F4) and binds it to the model at the descriptor's node via Model_AttachSlot_Setup.
evidence: The callee set is now named (Item_LookupRecord, Model_AttachSlot_Setup, maybe_Effect_CreateAttached2) and the caller 0x40A758 passes the item record plus the transform block, so the effect-from-item role is supported.

name: Model_Equip_UpdateNodeVisibility
summary: Shows or hides the model's four equipment nodes (f_40 every 8 bytes): a node is shown only when the model's visibility byte, the character's +0x12E4 mask and the node's own +6 flag all agree, otherwise it is detached.
evidence: The loop bound 4, the 8-byte node stride with the pointer at +0x40 and the flag at +0x46 match the node slots used by 0x0040A8C4/0x0040B674; g_0040abe4 (4836 = 0x12E4) is the literal offset of the character record's visibility mask.

name: Model_AttachSlot_Release
summary: Releases an equipment/model attach slot: if the slot still holds a model it hides every attach slot of that model and clears the 'occupied' byte at +6. Called from model creation, equipment update, model release and NPC balloon setup, i.e. every place that tears a character model down.
evidence: if (*slot != 0) { func_0022225C(); *(u8*)(slot+6) = 0; } and func_0022225C is already named Model_AttachSlot_HideAll. Callers: Model_Equip_UpdateActorEquipment, Model_CreateCharacterModelWithEquipment, Gfx_Model_Release, Field_Npc_InitEmoteBalloon.

name: Model_Equip_GetBoneTransformDescriptor
signature: int Model_Equip_GetBoneTransformDescriptor(void* modelEquip, u32 equipCategory, int index, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the bone-transform descriptor for one equipment category: resolves the CharacterRecord through the data manager and 0x0063eb94, then returns the per-category sub-record (0x160/0x1b0 for category 0, 0x200, 0x250, 0x2a0, 0x2f0, 0x340, 0x368+index*0x28, 0x3b8, 0x3e0, 0x408) that holds the bone name and Euler angles the item model is attached with.
evidence: Corrected: the old name put this in the UI text-label subsystem, but FACTS.md and the caller both place it in Model_Equip - the only caller is the confident Model_Equip_AttachItemSlot (0x0040B7A8, 0.72), which calls it as 0x0040AC1C(modelEquip, itemRec->u8_29) and then builds a 3x4 matrix from the returned Euler angles, defaulting to bone "N_ALL". The body matches: it resolves the CharacterRecord with 0x0063EB94(dm, self->f_65) and returns record + a per-equip-category offset.

name: Model_Equip_ApplyCharacterEquipment
summary: Binds a character to the model and applies its equipment: stores the id (+0x65) and the character's shape byte (+0x3C), reads the two equipped item ids from the character record, applies them to slot 0 and 1, clears the remaining attachments and refreshes the node visibility.
evidence: Calls the three model helpers named in this batch in exactly the order 'slot0, slot1, clear, update'; the callers include Gfx_Model_Release (N_025) and Battle_ActionAnimTable_Build (N_004), the two places that rebuild a character model.

name: Model_Equip_ApplyAccessorySlots
signature: void Model_Equip_ApplyAccessorySlots(CharacterModel* self, int slotA, int slotB)
summary: Handles the two accessory slots of the model: when they change it either detaches both accessory nodes or, when both are cleared, re-applies the character's default items to them, updating the node ids and grip state.
evidence: The two slot bytes +0x68/+0x69 and their item ids +0x44/+0x4C are the same fields 0x0040B02C/0x0040B174 manipulate, and the 0xFFFF sentinel is the shared 'no item' value from the pool.

name: Model_Equip_ApplySlotFromCharacter
signature: void Model_Equip_ApplySlotFromCharacter(CharacterModel* self, int slot, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Re-applies one equipment slot of the model from the bound character's record: reads the item id for the slot, dispatches to the slot-0/slot-1 setter or clears everything for the accessory slots, then refreshes the compare display.
evidence: Same dispatch table as 0x0040A680 but the item id comes from the character record via func_006292F0; caller 0x0023761C is in the model/effect code.

name: Model_Equip_SetSlot1Item
summary: Sets the off-hand (slot 1) item of the model: validates the item, picks the attachment transform for the item's class (shield vs. other, with a per-shape variant at +0x3C), attaches the node through 0x0040A758(slot 1) and updates the accessory node accordingly; an invalid or empty item detaches the node.
evidence: Uses the same 0xFFFF sentinel, 0x0061BD4C record lookup and 0x0066C344/0x0066CCEC item-class tests as 0x0040B174 (slot 0), and the two pool transform blocks differ only by the character shape byte.

name: Model_Equip_SetSlot0Item
summary: Sets the main-hand (slot 0) weapon of the model: attaches the weapon node with the shape-dependent transform, updates the paired accessory node, and for two-handed items also sets the off-hand node; an empty id detaches both nodes.
evidence: Sibling of 0x0040B02C with the transform tables swapped; the 0x0066C344/0x0066C5CC tests decide whether the weapon uses the second hand, which is what makes the 'two-handed' reading safe.

name: Model_Equip_ApplyAccessoryEffects
summary: Applies the accessory effect of the bound character to the model: takes the character's effect index (0x0023D078), looks the effect record up in the 0x10-byte table from 0x0063EB94 and creates the attached effect, then updates the two accessory node slots and the node visibility.
evidence: The effect creation uses maybe_Effect_CreateAttached2 (0x002239F4) with the same parameter block as 0x0040A980, and the tail calls 0x0040AE18/0x0040AB04 are the accessory-slot and visibility updates of this batch.

name: Model_Equip_SetGripNode
signature: void Model_Equip_SetGripNode(CharacterModel* self, int gripState, int hand)
summary: Switches the weapon grip of the model: for gripState 0 it detaches the paired hand node and attaches the 'wbhm_grip_on' node of the selected hand, for gripState 1 it attaches the node and swaps to 'wbhm_grip_off', committing each change through 0x0040A8C4.
evidence: The two literal node names s_wbhm_grip_on_0040b738 / s_wbhm_grip_off_0040b728 are read directly from the readable C and are the same 'wbhm' weapon-hand rig as 0x003F3B08; eight callers, all model setup paths.

name: Model_Equip_UpdateGripState
signature: void Model_Equip_UpdateGripState(CharacterModel* self, int gripState, int force)
summary: Applies a grip-state change unless the off-hand item is a shield and force is clear, in which case the grip must stay unchanged; stores the new state at +0x61.
evidence: Reads the slot-1 item id (+0x4C) and tests it with 0x0066CCEC (the shield/class predicate used by 0x0040B02C), then calls Model_Equip_SetGripNode (0x0040B674); nine callers including Gfx_Model_Release (N_025) and maybe_Ui_SubWindow_Init (N_004).

name: Model_Equip_AttachItemSlot
signature: void Model_Equip_AttachItemSlot(void* modelEquip, u32 slotIndex, int itemId)
summary: Releases any existing attachment on equipment slotIndex, resolves itemId's equip category (ItemRecord->u8_29) and bone transform descriptor (0x0040AC1C, default bone "N_ALL", converting Euler degrees to a 3x4 matrix), and attaches the 3D item model via Model_CreateAttachedEffect (0x0040A980).
evidence: Classic Item_LookupRecord 'Text_*' poison — zero UI labels or rotated text! All 3 callers are Model_Equip_ApplyAccessorySlots, Model_Equip_SetSlot1Item, and Model_Equip_SetSlot0Item (passing slot 2 or 3 and itemId). Releases slot entry (self + slotIndex*0x10)->f_40 via Model_AttachSlot_ReleaseAll (0x222B54), looks up Item_LookupRecord(&desc, itemId), queries bone offset/angles via 0x40AC1C(..., itemRec->u8_29, slotIndex == 3), builds 3x4 transform on stack, calls Model_CreateAttachedEffect (0x40A980), and stores u16_44 = itemId.

name: Model_Equip_SetGripSlot
summary: Sets which grip node a model uses: forwards (self, slotId, 1) to Model_Equip_SetGripNode and remembers the slot id in the byte at +0x60. Used by the equipment and model-creation paths.
evidence: Calls func_0040B674 (already named Model_Equip_SetGripNode) with a fixed extra argument 1, then stores arg2 into self->f_60. Callers: Model_Equip_UpdateActorEquipment, Model_CreateCharacterModelWithEquipment, Field_Npc_InitEmoteBalloon, maybe_Ui_SubWindow_Init.

name: Ui_TextLabel_SetTextGroup
signature: void Ui_TextLabel_SetTextGroup(UiTextLabel* label, u32 groupId, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: The text-label group setter: it assigns the group id, records the line count and rebuilds the label's slot objects.
evidence: The body writes self->f_65=groupId and f_66=dirty, resolves func_0035EB98(ctx,groupId)/func_0062943C, clears byte +99 and calls func_0040B364(self,1) plus func_0040AB04; two UI model/status callers use it.

name: Field_Object2D_CreateSceneEntry
signature: SceneEntry* Field_Object2D_CreateSceneEntry(u32 factory, SceneEntryDef* def, SceneRef* ref)
summary: Creates a 2D-field scene entry object: copies a 5-word descriptor, calls the scene-node base constructor 0x002D97E8, installs vtable 0x76D724 (Field_Object2D_ReleaseSceneEntry/UpdateSceneNodes) and constructs a 4-element 8-byte array.
evidence: Vtable g_0040BB9C = 0x76D724 with named Field_Object2D_* slots; callers Model_CreateCharacterModelWithEquipment, Battle_ActionAnimWindow_Init, Ui_EquipWindow_Init; base 0x002D97E8.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SecondaryDeletingDtorB
summary: Sibling of 0x0040A374: deleting destructor in the secondary vtable 0x0076D6E8, which has the identical 0x002650xx base-method layout and adjustor 0x0040BAE8.
evidence: Vtable 0x0076D6E8 re-read: same slot layout as 0x0076D6A8 (all 0x002650xx base methods, adjustor 0x0040BAE8), no class-specific method and no caller; 'PanelPart' was a placeholder.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateSceneNodes
summary: Recomputes a 2D field object's screen rectangles: offsets its stored rect by the parent transform, writes the node position/size for every type-4 node in the handle list and swaps width/height when the display mode (0/2/6) mirrors the screen.
evidence: The body only touches the object's rect fields (f_1F8..f_234) and the type-4 scene nodes reached through the named Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext; the mirror modes come from func_002D1814, exactly as the name says.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_AddQuadChild
summary: Adds one textured quad child to a sprite actor: runs the base prepare virtual, copies the source/destination rects and the size into the per-child tables, allocates the draw slot through Gfx_Scene_AllocSpriteSlot and increments the child index (max 8).
evidence: NEW: the sprite creation is the named Gfx_Scene_AllocSpriteSlot on the scene sprite context and the caller is the named Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild (0x00335A6C); the two-rect + uv layout and the per-child index byte are literal.

name: Field_Object2D_ShowSceneEntryA
signature: void Field_Object2D_ShowSceneEntryA(FieldObject2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Latch-on 'show' method for one of the object's two 2D scene entries: if the entry is currently hidden it marks it visible (byte +0x10) and, when the object is active (+0x42), tells the scene manager to enable the entry (Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(...,1)).
evidence: if (self->f_10 == 0) { self->f_10 = 1; if (self->f_42) Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(ctx, self->f_5c, 1); } - Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag is func_002E6318 from an earlier batch. Sibling of 0x0040C2C0/0x0040C920/0x0040CB78.

name: Field_Object2D_ReleaseSceneEntry
summary: Detaches the object from the 2D scene: releases the scene entry (Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries), clears the handle at +0x5c and resets the parameters of every attached node (8-byte stride at +0x16c) to the default 'visible, no flip, no offset' values, then zeroes the node count.
evidence: func_002E5F50(ctx, self->f_5c) is Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries (0x2E5F50), then self->f_5c = 0 and a loop over self->f_1ec calling func_0011FFFC(self+i*8+0x16c, {1,1,0,0}).

name: Field_Object2D_HideSceneEntryA
signature: void Field_Object2D_HideSceneEntryA(FieldObject2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Latch-off counterpart of 0x0040C200: when the entry is visible it clears the visible byte and disables the corresponding scene entry (Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(...,0)).
evidence: if (self->f_10 != 0) { self->f_10 = 0; Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(ctx, self->f_5c, 0); }

name: Field_Object2D_CreateSpriteEntry
signature: SceneEntry* Field_Object2D_CreateSpriteEntry(u32 factory, SceneEntryDef* def, SceneRef* ref)
summary: Creates the sprite variant of a 2D-field scene entry: base 0x002D9744, then a child node via 0x003DFB10 with vtable 0x76D724 and an 0x8 x 0x10 array. Called when a sprite actor adds a child.
evidence: Caller maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild (0x00335A6C); base 0x002D9744 then 0x003DFB10; vtable g_0040C3BC = 0x76D724 (Field_Object2D scene entry).

name: maybe_Ui_PanelPart_DeletingDtorC
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelPart_DeletingDtorC(void* self, unsigned int flags)
summary: Deleting destructor variant that first stores the third register argument at +0x3C, then runs the 0x002650C4 base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x0040CCC4 and no rodata reference survives, so even the +0x3C store may be a decompiler artefact of the freed `this`; nothing changed since the first pass.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncAttachedNodes
summary: Per-frame positioner for the 2D nodes/light attached to an object: computes the owner transform (or rotates the local offset by the owner quaternion when self+0x16A is set), writes the node position only when it actually changed, and repeats for every child node (type 1 position, type 2 position plus quaternion).
evidence: No new context: the quaternion helpers (0x00574548/0x005744DC) and the child accessors (0x002E685C/0x002E5DA8) are still unnamed and the function is reached only through a vtable, so the 'attached nodes' reading remains structural. The epsilon comparison is still the only constant.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_AddRotationChild
summary: Adds one child quad to a sprite actor: copies the child's six transform floats into the actor's per-child table, rotates them by the parent matrix and submits either a rotated (type 2, Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge) or billboard (type 1, AddSpriteEntrySmall) sprite; the handle lands in self[0x17].
evidence: Both draw helpers are named now and the branch on def+0x14 == 1/2 is the billboard/rotated distinction, exactly as the first pass read it.

name: Field_Object2D_ShowSceneEntryB
signature: void Field_Object2D_ShowSceneEntryB(Field_Object2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Second 'show' entry of the same class as 0x0040C200 (two independent scene handles are used, for example body and shadow sprites); identical semantics with the flag store ordered after the scene call.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same logic as 0x0040C200 with the f_10 store moved after the Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(...,1) call. Both exist because two different vtable slots use it.

name: Gfx_Trail_AddSegment
summary: Appends one segment to a 16-segment trail: stores the six floats, transforms them by the parent matrix and submits a rotated (Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType2) or billboard (AddNodeType1) quad; returns 0 when the ring is full.
evidence: The draw helpers are named and the 0x10 cap / 0x18 stride match the earlier reading; the returned 1/0 is the 'added' flag.

name: Field_Object2D_ResetAttachedNodes
signature: void Field_Object2D_ResetAttachedNodes(Field_Object2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Teardown for the attached-node list: releases the scene entry, clears the handle at +0x5c and restores every one of the +0x2f8 node transforms (0x18 bytes each, two vec3s at +0x178) to the default orientation constant, then zeroes the node count.
evidence: func_002E5F50(ctx, self->f_5c) then a loop over self->f_2f8 writing the six dwords of g_0040cb74 (0x7e7000, a .data block holding the identity orientation) into f_178..f_18c.

name: Field_Object2D_HideSceneEntryB
signature: void Field_Object2D_HideSceneEntryB(Field_Object2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Second 'hide' entry: disables the object's scene entry and clears the visible latch.
evidence: if (self->f_10 != 0) { Gfx_Scene_SetEntryFlag(ctx, self->f_5c, 0); self->f_10 = 0; } - the counterpart of 0x0040C920.

name: Field_Object2D_CreateSpriteEntryB
signature: SceneEntry* Field_Object2D_CreateSpriteEntryB(u32 factory, SceneEntryDef* def, SceneRef* ref)
summary: Second sprite-entry constructor: base 0x002D97E8, child via 0x003DFB10 with vtable 0x76D77C (Field_Object2D_ResetAttachedNodes/SyncAttachedNodes), plus three copied vector components and an 0x18 x 0x10 array.
evidence: Callers maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildB/C/D; vtable g_0040CCA8 = 0x76D77C with named Field_Object2D_* slots; copies g_0040CCAC triple into child+0x134.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelPart_DeletingDtorD
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelPart_DeletingDtorD(void* self, unsigned int flags)
summary: Fourth sibling of the 0x0040A374 group: writes +0x3C, destroys the 0x002650C4 base object and frees it.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x0040C3C8 and no rodata reference for this address; the class remains unidentified.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_IsEventSlotFree
summary: Returns 1 when the game work and its event state exist and the shared field/event gate reports ready. Slot 1 of the Field_Object2D vtable 0x76D7D8.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x76D7D8 = [0] Field_Object2D_Dtor, [1] this, ... [6] Field_Object2D_ApplyResultFlag. The body is byte-identical to the confident Actor2D_IsEventSlotFree, which returns 1 when the gate is non-zero; the old name 'IsBusy' asserted the opposite polarity of the only confident reading of this body, so it is corrected rather than confirmed.

name: Field_Object2D_ApplyResultFlag
summary: Issues the object's interaction command (Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent with the three argument bytes f_46/f_45/f_48) and, when it succeeds and a flag id is stored at +0x49, sets that bit in the game-work flag word via 0x006135D8(work+0x24A98, id); returns the command result.
evidence: New context: the command callee is the now-named Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent and the flag setter is called with the documented bag/flag block (work+0x24A98), which is exactly 'run the interaction then record the visited flag'.

name: Field_Object2D_CtorC
summary: Third constructor of the 2D field-object class: runs the base initialiser 0x0017C1C8, installs vtable 0x0076D7D4 and seeds the id/layer fields with the 'none' sentinels (id byte 0xFF, u16 0xFFFF, word 0, byte 0xFF) so the object reads as unplaced.
evidence: It installs vtable 0x0076D7D4, whose slot +4 is the confident Field_Object2D_Dtor (0x0040CF40) and whose other slots are Field_Object2D methods (maybe_Field_Object2D_IsEventSlotFree, Field_Object2D_ApplyResultFlag); Field_Object2D_CtorA/CtorB already exist at 0x00265878/0x0031F968, so this is the third constructor of that class.

name: Field_Object2D_Dtor
summary: Destructor for the 2D field-object class: releases the embedded drawable object (0x17C334, named maybe_Ui_DestroyObject earlier) and frees the instance.
evidence: Calls func_0017C334 then func_0010F6CC; 0x0017C334 is the 'destroy embedded drawable' helper that also appears in 0x0040D32C and 0x00410124.

name: Field_Object2D_CommitPendingFlag
signature: int Field_Object2D_CommitPendingFlag(Field_Object2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Commits a pending interaction: when the command manager is idle it sends the stored triple (f_2CE, f_2CD, event 1) through Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent and clears the pending byte f_2CC.
evidence: New context: the body is exactly 'if idle: raise event, clear pending flag' and the callee is the named Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent; the triple f_2CC/f_2CD/f_2CE is filled from the placement record by 0x0040D050, which is consistent with a per-object pending flag.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_AttachToActor
summary: Binds the object's sprite to a live field actor: resolves the handle in the actor table, accepts only actors of type 0x20000001 and asks the actor for the world transform to attach to.
evidence: Standard handle decode (handle>>11 index, generation compare) and type mask (actor->f_30 & * 0x20000041) == 0x20000001; the identical prologue appears in 0x0040D1B8, so both belong to the same * class.

name: Field_Object2D_ApplyPlacementRecord
summary: Initialises a field object from its placement record: copies the record id, position/scale (scale 0.5), rotation quaternion, the two sprite ids, the flag bytes and the action ids, builds the model transform (0x39FA90) and applies the model scale. This is the bridge between the level3d object table and the runtime 2D sprite object.
evidence: Called from maybe_Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable, i.e. the routine that walks the map object table. Field-for-field copies arg2[0xf..0x1a] into f_48..f_60, doubles as -arg2[4] into f_68, scales arg2[0x15..0x17] by 0.5 (g_0040d16c) and sets the size word at the offset g_0040d174 (0x2ce).

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateInteraction
summary: Per-frame interaction step: when the object has a hold mode or a live actor it either keeps the sprite attached to the actor transform or sends command 0xB with the mask 0xFFFFF800.
evidence: The actor-table prologue is identical to 0x0040CFCC and the other branch calls * func_00256678(work->f_6C, 0xB, 0xFFFFF800|...) through Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand, but the * command's meaning is unknown.

name: Field_ObjectCtor_vt76D7FC
summary: Constructor of a field object from the shared object pool: installs vtable 0x76D7FC, seeds the two inverted default vectors, the id/flip/alpha defaults (0, 3, 0xFF), then constructs the embedded sprite at +0x1C and its default fields; returns the object base 0x70 bytes before the sprite.
evidence: The embedded constructor is now named Field_ObjectSprite_CtorBase, so this is an object ctor that owns a field sprite (the old 'CreateNode' suggested a leaf node); which object kind it is, is expressed by the vtable suffix.

name: Field_Object2D_DestroyNode
summary: Destructor of the object created by 0x0040D29C: stamps the base vtable, destroys the embedded sprite at +0x70 and the Ui_Object part, then frees the node.
evidence: NEW: the ctor/dtor pair is visible in the numbers (0x0040D29C constructs exactly this 0x70-offset sprite layout, and the body's chain subtracts back to it), and the callees are named (Gfx_Sprite_DtorAlt, Ui_Object_DtorBody); the class still has no data-table entry, so the subsystem name is inferred from the vtable family.

name: Ui_TextFormat_SetMemberNameAndItemText
summary: Sets message argument slot 2 to the member name (+0xCA, padded/truncated to 0x7F wchars) and slot 5 to the display text of the id at self+0x210 (Item_LookupRecord then Text_FormatMessageArg), i.e. a 'member got item' message.
evidence: The disassembly calls Item_LookupRecord on self+0x210 and Text_FormatMessageArg before repointing slot 5, and slot 2 is written like its confirmed sibling 0x003D8FF0. The Item_LookupRecord call only supplies the item's display name: this is text formatting, not item/inventory logic.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_IsEventSlotFreeB
summary: Returns the shared field/event gate value (0 when the game work is absent). Slot 2 of the Field_Object2D notification vtable 0x76D8F0.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x76D8F0 = [0] Ui_Window_CloseAndHide, [1] maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncTaskChain, [2] this, [3] Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventB - the four-slot notification interface whose slot 2 is the gate in every other class. 'QueryChannel' named a 'channel' that does not exist anywhere in the body; the only call is the shared gate.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot
summary: Per-frame update of a 2D field object's attached effect: runs the standard prelude, restarts the effect through 0x40D7E0 when the object is active, then pushes the object's world position into the 2D effect manager (0x6224F8).
evidence: The restart callee 0x40D7E0 is now maybe_Field_Object2D_RestartStateEffect and the neighbour 0x4E667C pushes positions to the same manager, so 'update the object's effect slot' is supported.

name: maybe_Effect_QuadEmitter_SetupA
summary: A-variant setup of a sprite emitter: copies layer/colour/position/rotation from the definition, builds one type-2 sprite child descriptor, attaches it at f_278, stores the definition origin at +0x2C8 and loads effect pack 0x4B5.
evidence: The body is the twin of 0x0040D620 and the Gfx emitter callees are named, but the 'quad' wording still rests only on the opaque type-2 descriptor.

name: maybe_Effect_QuadEmitter_SetupB
summary: B-variant of the sprite-emitter setup: reads its layer byte from def+0x18, stores f_2D8 = 1 and sub-id f_2DC = def[0x17], otherwise performing the same child-descriptor build, attach and effect-pack load as 0x0040D4F8.
evidence: Field-for-field identical to the A variant apart from the variant flag/sub-id, which matches a two-variant emitter class; 'quad' remains unproven.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect
signature: void maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect(Field_Object2D* self, int state, u32 arg3, float arg4)
summary: Starts the effect that belongs to a given object state: for states 10/11 it stops the previous effect, builds the spawn transform from the object position and requests effect id 0x4B5, also notifying the model interface through vtable +0x38.
evidence: The literal 0x4B5 and the state switch are clear and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance/Effect_ReleaseHandle are named, but nothing calls it yet, so the class attribution stays tentative.

name: Field_Object2D_RestartStateEffect
summary: Stops the object's current state effect (Effect_ReleaseHandle on self->f_2E8), rebuilds the effect transform from the object position at f_9C..f_A4 (mirroring the global at 0x007E7024 when f_2D8 is clear) and recreates effect id 0x4B5 via Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, storing the new handle back in f_2E8. Called by Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot when the object's state effect has to be restarted.
evidence: The body explicitly releases f_2E8, builds the transform and recreates effect 0x4B5 into f_2E8; its caller is the named Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot. The only inference left is the 'restart' framing, which the release-then-recreate order supports.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncTaskChain
summary: Attaches or detaches the object's task chain (self+0x2C8) to match the actor state byte f_312 (state 7 uses the detach helper 0x002337CC, other states the attach helper Actor_CreateTaskChainB) and returns whether it changed anything.
evidence: The disassembly confirms the actor state is only read, never written (the older SwapActorState reading was inverted), and the only writes go to &self->f_2c8. The two branch helpers 0x002337CC and Actor_CreateTaskChainB still lack confident names, so what the chain controls remains inferred.

name: Field_Object2D_DtorWithSubObject
summary: Multiple-inheritance destructor of the 2D field-object class: installs the primary vtable (from the literal g_0040d9f8) and the secondary one 0xd4 bytes later, destroys the embedded sub-object at +0x2e0 and frees the instance.
evidence: Pattern *self = g_0040d9f8; self[0x96] = g_0040d9f8 + 0xd4; is the standard two-vtable dtor. g_0040d9f8 resolves to the vtable at 0x76d83c whose slots are 0x5F6xxx/0x669xxx/0x40D900 methods, and slot 2 of that table is this very function. Then func_0030C3F0(self+0xb8), func_00124154, func_0028EFB4(iVar-0x2e0) and func_0010F6CC.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState
summary: Touch/click state machine for interactive field objects: phase 1 drags the object by the delta between the current and previous touch point, phase 2 feeds the touch point into the game's cursor handler and starts the press animation, phase 3 waits for the animation to end, phase 4 sends the release and advances the event. Phases are written back into ev[0].
evidence: Phases are the literal bytes 1..5 in arg1[0]; coordinates are compared against the work object's cursor at +0x78/+0x7c (piVar2[0x1e]/[0x1f]); calls func_0023A580(work->f_48,0), func_00239A94(work->f_48,&pair), func_002387E0, func_002394D8. Callers: the whole 2D-sprite/touch family (maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_IsReady, maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_CheckAndDraw, maybe_Field_Gadget_IsTouchOutside, func_00423648) - a touch event handler, not a renderer.

name: Field_Object2D_BuildTouchEvent
signature: TouchEvent* Field_Object2D_BuildTouchEvent(TouchEvent* out, u8 phase, u8 phase2, u32* point)
summary: Fills a touch event (type 1, kind, phase, x, y) and immediately hands control to the game's input handler with slot 4, i.e. it synthesises a press/move/release for a 2D object.
evidence: *out = 1; out[1] = arg2; out[2] = arg3; out[4..11] = point; then (**(code**)(*uiObject + 0x58))(uiObject, 4) where uiObject = work->f_54->f_20. Callers: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_ReadGeometryA/B, maybe_Ui_Widget_LoadSpriteFrame, maybe_Field_Gadget_GetTouchPoint.

name: Field_Object2D_RunStateSequence
summary: Four-step sequence that opens a scripted view around the object: request the overlay (0x2D24BC), wait for it (vtable +0x30), then move a camera/effect anchor either to the object position or to the stored anchor (+0x324) and play the overlay element animations; the last step waits for the anchor to finish and closes the overlay. Always returns true (it is polled until the state machine reaches 4).
evidence: State byte f_2c8 is compared against 0,1,2,3 and set to 1..4; the calls are the UI overlay ones already named by earlier batches (maybe_Ui_Overlay_TriggerElementAnimation, maybe_Ui_Overlay_ResetElementAnimation, Party_Status_SelectPage, func_005F5F54 with an actor and a transform, func_00238CC8/func_00236B50/func_00237198 on work->f_48). f_9c/f_a0/f_a4 copied into the anchor at +0x9c proves the sequence is anchored on this object.

name: Field_Object2D_SetDrawPass
summary: Switches a field 2D object between its two sprite draw passes: calls the remove/insert vtable slots (+0x40/+0x58 or +0x3C/+0x54) with layer 4 in opposite order, sets the two draw ids at +0x2B4/+0x310 to 0/-1 accordingly and records the mode byte at +0xC8.
evidence: NEW: three callers are named and all are draw-order paths (Field_Object2D_RunStateSequence, Field_Object2D_OnSetDrawPass, Effect_MeshEmitter_Setup), which confirms the 'move between draw passes' reading; the vtable-slot pairs and the 0/-1 ids are literal.

name: Effect_MeshEmitter_Setup
summary: Configures a mesh-based effect emitter from its definition: loads effect pack 0x4A1, sets the rotation from the definition quaternion, adds two sprite children, a colour animator and the mesh object (mesh id at def+0x9A), and copies the definition's offsets/scale into the emitter fields.
evidence: Named callees Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams, Gfx_AddFColAnimator, Gfx_EffectPack_LoadById and maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC cover every build step, so the 'mesh emitter setup' reading is supported by the actual calls, not just the constants.

name: Field_Object2D_CtorWithAttachedEffect
signature: Field_Object2D* Field_Object2D_CtorWithAttachedEffect(Field_Object2D_Desc* desc, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Constructor for a Field::Object2D subclass that also creates an attached effect/node sub-object: installs the primary and secondary vtables, invalidates the handle field and copies a global 3-vector pair into the sub-object.
evidence: Sets `*obj = vtable(0x0076D934)` and `obj[0x96] = vtable + 0xd4` (secondary vtable), zeroes f_b2, then fills f_50/f_54/f_58 and f_5c/f_60/100 from two global vectors and returns sub-0x2d4; vtable 0x0076D934 holds Field_Object2D_OnDeactivate / PlaceEffectInFrontOfCamera / PlayIdleEffect. Allocates via 0x0028EE8C.

name: maybe_Actor2D_HandleObject_DeletingDtorWithPack
summary: Deleting destructor of an Actor2D-derived object with three sub-objects: it stamps the primary vtable at +0 and the secondary one at +0x258, runs the Actor_HandleRefEx base body at +0x2D4, destroys the Pack_Handle at +0x2CC, runs the Actor2D_EffectNode body on self and frees.
evidence: New evidence from disassembly: the calls are 0x4AF56C (Actor_HandleRefEx non-deleting body) on self+0x2D4, 0x124154 (Pack_Handle_Dtor) on self+0x2CC and 0x28EFB4 (Actor2D_EffectNode non-deleting body) on self. The old 'Ui_Object' prefix was wrong: no UI object is involved, the class is an Actor2D object owning a handle. The exact class vtable (passed in r1) is unknown, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_IsEventSlotFreeC
summary: Returns the shared field/event gate value. Slot 2 of the Field_Object2D notification vtable 0x76DAE0.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x76DAE0 = [0] Ui_Window_CloseAndHide, [2] this, [3] Field_Object2D_SetStateEffect. The disassembly is `push {r3,lr}; bl Os_GetGameWork; ldr r0,[r0]; ldr r0,[r0,#8]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x6c]; bl func_00636AFC; pop {r3,pc}` - r0 survives the pop, so this returns a value (a getter); Ghidra typed it void and dropped the return, which is why the old name guessed a side-effect-only 'PollChannel'.

name: Field_Object2D_PlaceEffectInFrontOfCamera
summary: Places the object (typically a 'look at me' effect sprite) on the line from the camera to its target: computes the squared distance to the reference position, applies an exponential distance factor (0.1 step) and offsets the object from the camera position along the camera orientation, then marks the transform dirty.
evidence: Reference position comes from work->f_74 (the camera object) f_b0..f_b8, orientation from work->f_74->f_130..f_13c rotated by func_00574548 with g_0040e974 (0x7e7024), the smoothing constants are g_0040e760 = 0.1 and g_0040e768 = 0.0, and the result is written to f_9c/f_a0/f_a4 with f_118 = 1 (transform dirty) followed by func_005F6018(self) - the 'mark transform changed' slot of this class' vtable.

name: Field_Object2D_PlayIdleEffect
summary: Spawns the object's default effect (id 0x4B0) at the object position and stores the handle at +0x2D8.
evidence: The body is a single, complete effect spawn with a fixed id and a stored handle; the name describes exactly that.

name: Field_Object2D_SetStateEffect
summary: Swaps the object's effect when its state changes: states 4/5 stop the old handle and spawn 0x4af or 0x4b0, states 2/3 toggle a boolean on the sub-object (vtable slot 0x14) and in all cases the model interface (f_270, slot 0x84) is told about the new state.
evidence: Handle validity is checked with the standard handle table g_0040eb88 / mask g_0040eb84 = 0x3fffff, the spawn ids are 0x4af (g_0040eb8c) and 0x4b0; the sub-object call is (**(int**)(*self->f_4c + 0x14))(self->f_4c, state==2).

name: Effect_BillboardEmitter_Setup
summary: Configures a single billboard (descriptor type 1) effect part: layer byte, the two sub-ids and the colour, one non-rotated sprite child whose scale is the definition's radius times the shared basis vector, and the colour mirrored into +0x2C8..+0x2D0.
evidence: New context: the spawn block maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectBillboardEmitter calls it, and the body builds exactly one child with descriptor type 1 - the same type byte the other effect setups use for the billboard path.

name: Field_Object2D_OnDeactivate
signature: void Field_Object2D_OnDeactivate(Field_Object2D* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 ctx)
summary: Deactivation path: when the object was active it notifies the embedded scene object (0x336938), unregisters itself from the field scene (0x1C9110(work->f_54, self)) and releases the state effect handle.
evidence: Guard is self->f_41 != 0; func_00336938(self) is the scene-object notifier, then func_001C9110(work->f_54, self) only when f_26c != -1, then the effect handle check against g_0040ed0c (0x3fffff) and func_0035FC84 stop.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_NotifyCommand16
signature: void maybe_Field_Object2D_NotifyCommand16(Field_Object2D* self, int offset, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Sends field-gadget command 0x16 with the object id when the u16 at self+offset is not 0xFFFF and the object's u16 f_2D4 is not 0xFF.
evidence: The old OnTouchConfirm guessed a touch-screen entry point, but the body only reads two u16 fields and emits the same command-0x16 gadget notification; no input or touch API appears. The two u16 fields are still unexplained, so maybe_ stays.

name: Field_Object2D_DeletingDtor
summary: Scalar deleting destructor of a Field::Object2D node: destroys the Actor2D effect-node base (0x28EFB4) and frees the object.
evidence: Vtable 0x76DA34 holds the confidently named Field_Object2D_OnDeactivate, Field_Object2D_PlaceEffectInFrontOfCamera and Field_Object2D_PlayIdleEffect, so the class is fixed; the base destructor 0x28EFB4 is the Actor2D::EffectNode one. Vtable 0x76DA34 re-read: slots 2/6/10 are Field_Object2D_OnDeactivate (0x0040EC7C), Field_Object2D_PlaceEffectInFrontOfCamera (0x0040E320) and Field_Object2D_PlayIdleEffect (0x0040E978), all confident names from M1.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateBattleTrigger
summary: Per-frame poll of an object's battle trigger: when the per-map byte at work+0x2A4E6+self->f_298 is 1 or 4 it returns the channel busy state; otherwise it starts the trigger once (flag f_29A, trigger object f_29C) and on later frames calls Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle.
evidence: NEW: the completion call is the confident Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle and the started flag is f_29A on the trigger object at f_29C, so this is the trigger's per-frame poll; the per-map byte table at work+0x2A4E6 is still only inferred.

name: Field_Object2D_SetConfirmMessage
signature: void Field_Object2D_SetConfirmMessage(FieldObject2D* self, int which, u32 textId)
summary: Builds the message arguments for the object's confirm prompt: selects the primary or secondary message record, sets args 8/9, resolves the text id to a message line and registers it for display.
evidence: Caller maybe_Field_Object2D_ConfirmInteraction (0x0040F730); Message_SetArg(8,...) / (9,...); table 0x0063F1E0 and Text_CopyMessageLine (0x0063A46C); descriptor registers via 0x00707C1C.

name: Field_SceneNode_UpdateTalkText
summary: Per-frame update of a field scene node with a message slot: when the node is not yet talking (0x309 clear) but has text pending (0x308 set) it forces the slot's message-state byte to 0xFF; when that state is 1 or 4 and the node has a model it plays the talk animation (0x002D1258) and freezes the animator on the last frame.
evidence: The per-slot byte at work+node->f_298+0x2A4E6 is the same one the sibling maybe_Field_SceneNode_UpdateMessageAction (0x0040FAE4) reads as talk state 1/4, and the tail callee is the named Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame (0x005F4F5C). Verified this address is the first word of vtable 0x0076DB54, grouping it with the field-node update slots.

name: Field_Object2D_InitModel
summary: Builds the 3D representation of a field object from its placement record: copies the record fields, looks the monster/NPC model definition up by (kind, id) and, when found, allocates a 0x178 anim instance, applies the anim template, attaches the colour animator, sets the model size from the record and registers the resulting sprite in the scene.
evidence: func_0066A7B8(work->f_b4) -> model table; func_0062C388/0062C3B0 select the definition; func_00109DC8(0x178, self->f_48, 4) + func_002D1F28 allocate/init the anim instance; func_0031A73C builds the sprite params and func_00335A6C registers it. g_0040f3ac/0x6e65704f is the literal 'Open' plus its length, i.e. an anim template name.

name: Field_Object2D_InitModelVariant
summary: Byte-for-byte twin of 0x0040F0F0 (model/animator construction from a placement record) except that the object is flagged variant 1 (f_2f0 = 1) and a different anim template name is used, so the two spawning paths build the normal and the alternate appearance of the same object.
evidence: Same call set as 0x0040F0F0; only self->f_2f0 (0 vs 1), the template literals (g_0040f66c/0x6e65704f, g_0040f678) and the record offsets of two shorts differ.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishTalkText
summary: End-of-talk step: if the node's talk slot +0x298 is set, it may write 0xFF into the shared state byte at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E+slot, then if that byte is 1 or 4 and node->f_B8 is live it refreshes the talk target through 0x002D1258.
evidence: The byte index resolves to the shared pastword/quest block at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E (FACTS.md), so this is not a scene-object-local flag; the exact owner semantics are still unclear, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Field_Object2D_ConfirmInteraction
summary: Player-confirm branch of a field 2D object: clears the latch byte +0x29A; if the per-map byte is 1 or 4 it posts script command 0x19/0x1A via Event_OnTriggerCommand, otherwise it plays the confirm SE, stops the stored animation and sends command 0x18 through Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand.
evidence: Event_OnTriggerCommand, Sound_PlaySeById, Field_Object2D_SetConfirmMessage and Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand are all named and form the two halves of the confirm path; the function is a vtable override, so the absence of a direct caller is expected. (The earlier evidence sentence about a confirm-message setter described the neighbouring setter, not this body.)

name: Field_Object2D_CtorSprite
signature: Field_Object2D* Field_Object2D_CtorSprite(Field_Object2D_Desc* desc, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Constructor for the sprite variant of Field::Object2D: installs the sprite vtable, sets the object handle to 0xFFFF ("none") and initialises the embedded sprite slot.
evidence: New via 0x0028E630(...,0x4000000c); `*obj = vtable(0x0076DB24)`, `obj[0x8b] = vtable + 0x98`; obj->f_a6 = 0xffff; byte at +0x29a cleared; vtable 0x0076DB24 contains Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance, Field_SceneNode_UpdateTalkText and Field_SceneObject_Hide.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SpriteDeletingDtor
summary: Destructor counterpart of Field_Object2D_CtorSprite (0x0040F898): reinstalls the primary vtable and the +0x98 secondary one, tears the sprite slot down through 0x0059AA7C/0x0028E6C4 and frees the object.
evidence: No rodata table references this address and the two teardown callees are still unnamed (0x0059AA7C is only known through Field_BattleTrigger_Delete, 0x0028E6C4 is unnamed), so 'Sprite' rests on the ctor neighbour alone.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateDeferredSubObject
summary: Third copy of the same deferred start: flag +0x2CA, sub-object +0x2CC. Waits for the event state to report idle, latches the flag, starts the sub-object through its virtual +0x1C slot, then polls it through 0x0046E50C.
evidence: vtable 0x0076DC94 places it at slot +0x08 next to the named Field_Object2D_CancelInteraction (+0x04), which supports the Field_Object2D class. The body is the 0x002BDAC8 template with +0x2CA/+0x2CC, so 'WaitThenStartEffect' was right about the two phases but invented the 'effect' part; the name now says what is actually started and polled.

name: Field_Object2D_SetCancelMessage
signature: void Field_Object2D_SetCancelMessage(FieldObject2D* self, int which, u32 textId)
summary: Cancel-prompt twin of 0x0040EEE8: sets message args 8/9 and registers the resolved text for the object's cancel interaction.
evidence: Caller maybe_Field_Object2D_CancelInteraction (0x0040FFD4); identical body to 0x0040EEE8 with a different global message slot (g_0040FAE0).

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_UpdateMessageAction
summary: Per-frame talk/message state machine of a field scene node: it resolves the attached object handle, fires the node's +0x84 handler with 0x6E4F when the +0xC6 byte is 1, and when the per-node message state at work+0x2A4E6+index is 1 or 4 it fires +0x84 with the node's +0xC8 block, starts a 60-frame action through 0x005F7784 and clears the pending byte at +0xAD.
evidence: The body is fully visible and the per-node message state byte at work+0x2A4E6 is read and written, which supports the 'message action' reading; the callees Ui_ResolveObjectHandle and Game_GetWork are named. But the two +0x84 dispatches and 0x005F7784 are still unnamed and the function has no callers, so the class and the exact action stay unproven and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupB
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant B: stores the emitter record fields, sets the effect node name to the fixed string "Open" at +0x320, applies the placement position/rotation, adds a sprite child with a colour descriptor, registers an fCol animator and creates the mesh from def->+0x42 and variant byte f_11.
evidence: Re-checked against its spawner: maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterB (0x0034D0B8) allocates the emitter and calls this with the on-stack definition, and the fixed string 0x6E65704F = "Open" is confirmed in the body. 'MeshEmitter' is still inferred from the sibling family rather than a named constructor, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupC
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant C: same sprite child + fCol animator + mesh creation as 0x0040FBB8 but stores the fixed string "Off" at +0x320, sets the variant flag f_318 = 1, takes the mesh id from def->f_F and writes it to +0x312 instead of +0x2C8.
evidence: Re-checked against its spawner: maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterC (0x0034D454) allocates the emitter and calls this with the on-stack definition, and the fixed string 0x0066664F = "Off" is the counterpart of "Open" in 0x0040FBB8. The class prefix is still a family inference, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction(void* node, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Variant of the talk-action completion: clears the same shared state byte at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E+id to 0xFF when the node is flagged idle, and when the byte is 1 or 4 it plays the talk animation through virtual +0x84, calls 0x005F7784(node,0x3C,0) and clears node[0xAD].

name: Field_Object2D_CancelInteraction
summary: Cancel branch of a 2D field-object interaction: clears the interaction latch, then depending on the object variant either calls the vtable stop slot (+0x84) or plays the cancel SE, and finally sets the cancel message and pushes event command 0x18 for the object.
evidence: Named callees Field_Object2D_SetCancelMessage and Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand (with command 0x18 on work->f_6C) plus the mirror-image accept path at 0x0040F730 confirm this is the cancel side of the same interaction, not a generic effect.

name: Field_Object2D_CtorMesh

summary: Constructor for the mesh variant of Field::Object2D: installs the mesh-node vtable, resets the 0xFFFF handle and initialises the attached mesh/scene-node slot.
evidence: New via 0x0028EE8C; `*obj = vtable(0x0076DBE0)`, `obj[0x96] = vtable + 0xd4`; f_b2 = 0xffff; vtable 0x0076DBE0 contains Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName and Field_SceneNode_UpdateMessageAction; returns result-0x2cc.

summary: Variant destructor for the same 2D field-object class: installs the given vtable plus the secondary one 0xd4 bytes later, destroys the embedded drawable at +0x2cc and frees the instance.
evidence: *self = arg2; self[0x96] = arg2 + 0xd4;  the same two-vtable layout as 0x0040D9C0 but with the vtable passed in, then func_0017C334(self+0xb3), func_0028EFB4(iVar-0x2cc), func_0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_BindLayoutAnimation
signature: void maybe_Ui_Screen_BindLayoutAnimation(Ui_Screen* self, int layoutId, int arg3)
summary: Registers a (table, context) pair with the Ui core singleton: calls 0x00707C1C(core+0x848, 0x007BFBD4, self->f_20C) and then rebinds core+0x844 to core+0x84C.
evidence: The address is slot 8 of vtable 0x0076DCC0, whose slot 0 is Field_Object_SetMode and slot 3 Field_Object_OnEvent, so the owning class is a Field_Object subclass, not a Ui_Screen; the callers are the horse-riding actions (Field_Action_HorseStart/Land/Update) and the jockey panels, i.e. a shared 'tell the Ui core about this layout' helper. 0x00707C1C is still unnamed, so the exact registration stays unproven.

name: Gfx_ScreenFade_Update
summary: Advances a screen fade/blend: counts the progress value up to the duration, lerps three RGB triples (start->end colours for the three screen regions) by the resulting 0..1 factor and hands the factor to the blend routine. name: maybe_Ui_Tween_ClampValue

evidence: switch(self->f_11c): 0 = start 'ten_out'? -> func_003E043C(&f_19c,0) + func_003E021C(&f_1ec,0); 1 = wait for the animation at f_1ec to finish (func_00649B80) then f_141=1 and start f_19c; 2 = when f_264 is set, play 'ten_in' (f_14c) and advance; 3 = wait for f_14c, stop it; 4 = reset f_120=0xffff, f_124=0, f_11c=0. When f_120 equals the idle marker g_00469cf4 it calls 0x469D84 (next queued number) instead. Tail calls the widget update through self->f_98->f_2c.

name: Battle_Popup_PlayQueuedNumber
summary: Pops the next pending number out of the widget's 4-entry queue, makes it current and starts its text/number animation; does nothing when the queue is empty.
evidence: Scans the 4 entries at self+0x23c (stride 8: {id, value}) for the first one whose id differs from the 0xffff empty marker, moves it into self->f_120/f_124 and clears the slot. Then resolves the text record for that id from the 'battle_Text.bxon' table at self->f_144 (offset table at f_58->f_24, stride 4, as in 0x4445A4) and hands it to the record's vtable slot +8; when no record exists it falls into func_00100B74 (fatal error), i.e. the id must exist. Finally resets f_120 to the idle marker and f_11c to 0.

name: Text_CountBackwardSameClassRun
signature: u32 Text_CountBackwardSameClassRun(void* messagePtr, u32 propByteIndex, int startCharIndex)

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_Begin
summary: Start method of the Dragon Jump action: stops the actor animation, sets frame 4, clears the jump flags (+0x14c..+0x14e) and requests the state (0, 2 or 5) that matches the actor's jump variant byte (+0x3f0), committing the request if accepted.
evidence: Slot 1 of vtable 0x773AB4 whose slot 0 is the action's deleting dtor and whose slot 3 (0x476C88) is its per-frame update; body calls actor vtable+0x80/+0x58(self,4), switches on `actor->f_3f0` 1/2/3 and uses the state-machine pair vtable+0x14(request)/+0x10(commit) on self+0x2c that all DragonJump states use.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_DragonJumpBaseUpdate
summary: Common update of an actor jump action: derives the horizontal displacement from the actor's position delta, scales it by the action's speed factor (self+0x140 = 1/3) and applies the delta matrix to the actor node.
evidence: Re-read: the delta/scale math is readable and the 1/3 speed factor at self+0x140 is real, but the 'Dragon_Jump' attribution still comes only from the neighbouring function band - nothing inside the function names the action. The name stays maybe_.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_OnEvent
summary: Animation-event hook of the Dragon Jump action: event 13 (0xD, the end of the 'JumpM_Up_Loop' animation) raises the loop-finished flag read by the up-loop update.
evidence: Slot 6 of vtable 0x773AB4; body is only `if (arg2 == 0xd) self->f_14c = 1;` and f_14c is the flag guarded by Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpLoopUpdate (0x475CE4).

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpLoopUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_Loop' segment: plays the loop animation, moves the actor along the stored velocity for the frame delta, and when the animation time budget is used up requests jump state 4.
evidence: Plays the literal string at 0x475DB8 = "Dragon_JumpM_Up_Loop"; the sibling state Actor_Action_DragonJumpMDownLoopUpdate (0x475DD4) does exactly the same with "Dragon_JumpM_Down_Loop", and both use velocity block +0x130..+0x140 and request state 4/7.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMDownLoopUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the Dragon-Jump 'M down loop' element: sets the model's anim name to Dragon_JumpM_Down_Loop, scales the fall speed (halved when the actor's +0x3F1 flag is set) and applies the frame displacement to the actor node.
evidence: String 'Dragon_JumpM_Down_Loop' at 0x475E88 through model vtable+0x84; factor 0x475EA0/0x475EA4; computes f_3E0-f_3C8 / f_3E8-f_3D0 and applies via 0x5736A0 + 0x5F5F54; part of the same block as the other Dragon_Jump updates.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpAirDriftUpdate
summary: Airborne hold state: keeps adding a constant drift vector to the actor position each frame; when the remaining height (+0x3d8 - +0xa0) drops below zero it requests jump state 7.
evidence: Adds the float triple at 0x7E7024 to actor->f_100/104/108 scaled by self->f_140 (delta time) and compares `0.0 <= actor->f_3d8 - actor->f_a0` - the same height test used by the other DragonJump segments; uses state-machine request 7.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpSStartUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the Dragon-Jump 'S start' element: sets the anim name, computes the jump arc (horizontal distance vs. gravity constants) and derives the vertical speed factor, scale and duration stored in f_13C..f_148.
evidence: String 'Dragon_JumpS_Start' at 0x47610C; constants 0x476120..0x476144; SQRT of the x/z delta; writes f_13C/f_140/f_144/f_148 then f_130..f_138 and clears f_14C/f_14D.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpStartUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the Dragon-Jump 'M up start' element: names the model animation 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_StartSE' and applies the frame displacement/rotation to the actor node.
evidence: String 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_StartSE' at 0x4761F4 through model vtable+0x84; takes the actor's local position 0x9C/0xA0/0xA4, adds the frame delta and applies via 0x5736A0/0x5F5F54; clears f_14C/f_14D.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpEnd_Start
summary: Prepares the 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_End' segment: plays the end animation, converts the remaining horizontal distance and height into per-frame speeds over (animationFrames-2) ticks and stores the half-frame vertical step.
evidence: Plays the literal "Dragon_JumpM_Up_End" (0x47629C); divides the 2D distance by the tick count into self->f_13c and sets self->f_144 = -(dt / (ticks/2)) - exactly the fields the follow-up updates integrate.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpSEnd_Update
summary: Update for the short jump's landing segment: switches from 'Dragon_JumpS_End' to 'Dragon_JumpS_Loop' when the animation runs past frame 14, clamps the vertical speed so the actor cannot overshoot the ground, and requests state 8 when the tick budget runs out.
evidence: Plays literal strings "Dragon_JumpS_End" (0x47644C) and "Dragon_JumpS_Loop" (0x476460), gates the loop on func_00669DD4 (animation finished) and uses the same f_13c/f_138/f_134 velocity + f_140 delta-time integration as the other jump states.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_LerpToStartPose
summary: Eases the actor position and height toward the stored jump start pose at 0.15 per frame and then requests state 3; used as the recovery/return segment after a jump.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpEnd_Update
summary: Continuation of the 'M Up End' segment: counts the ticks down, keeps the vertical speed inside the remaining height, moves the actor along the horizontal velocity plus the vertical component, and requests state 8 when the timer expires.
evidence: Continuation of dragon jump M Up End state; moves actor and transitions to state 8 on timer expiry.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMDownEndUpdate

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMDownStartUpdate

evidence: The record-based branch (f_295, f_2E8 bits 0/1) and the work-row ladder are both explicit, and the fallback goes through the now-named Item_LookupRecord plus 0x66C5F4 on the equipped item, i.e. a state/icon selector by construction.

name: Battle_Actor_GetStateIcon
summary: Party-actor twin of Battle_Monster_GetStateIcon: returns f_DD when set, otherwise uses the f_FF flag bits with the battle work's action rows 0x62/99/100/0x65/0x66/0x67 to pick icon 0..6, falling back to the equipped item's state.
evidence: The body is the same ladder as the monster variant with party-record offsets (f_DD/f_FF), and the item fallback again uses the named Item_LookupRecord; the caller context (battle message row building) is unchanged.

name: maybe_Battle_RollUnitVisibilityChance
summary: Probability gate used when syncing battle unit models: for kinds 2/8/10/11/12/0x90 it succeeds outright when the model record's +0x108 flag is set, otherwise it rolls the battle RNG against 25%; kinds 3/9 roll against 12.5% or 67.5% depending on the same flag. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: The caller Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility uses the result to decide whether to call the action model's vtable +0x128 for a unit id, and the record it reads is the per-model one from 0x0063E5C8 (byte +0x108), so this is a unit-visibility roll, not an 'action chance'. The kind switch itself is still unexplained, hence maybe_.

name: Text_IsRowVisible
signature: u32 Text_IsRowVisible(int * self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Visibility gate shared by the battle row builders: true when the object carries flag 0x85 or the game is in battle mode (+0x4208 == 0x0B).
evidence: vtable 0xE8(0x85) else reads *(char*)(gamework+0x4208)!=0x0B -> return 0; called by 10+ row builders of this batch and Ui_TextLayout functions

name: maybe_Battle_RollActionStatusChance
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_RollActionStatusChance(u32 actionId, u32 unitArg, void* target, void* result, int variant)
summary: Rolls an action's status-effect chance against a target: resolves the action row (or the SkillRecord it points at), computes the chance with Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers, compares a 1..100 battle-RNG roll, then calls maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc and tests the target's immunity; sets result->f_54 and returns 1 when the status lands.
evidence: The named SkillRecord wrapper func_0018C1B8 (f_CE variance, f_DE/f_E2/f_CC) and Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers, plus maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc and the vtable +0xF8 check, show a status-application roll; the only caller Battle_Ui_ShowActionEffectMessage consumes the result as 'status applied'. The old 'RollActionRowSuccess' name described text rows, not this.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcSkillEffectValue
signature: int maybe_Battle_CalcSkillEffectValue(void* skillRef, void* unit, int varianceMode)
summary: Computes a skill effect value from the skill record's min/max/threshold/curve fields: picks the unit stat selected by record+0xDF (unit+0x24 or +0x26), interpolates between record+0xC4/+0xC6 using the +0xC8 threshold and +0xCA cap, then adds a battle-RNG variance from record+0xCE (forced to -value for mode 1 or +value for mode 2).
evidence: func_0018C1B8 is the SkillRecord accessor per FACTS, and the body reads the record's +0xC4/+0xC6/+0xC8/+0xCA/+0xCE/+0xDF fields and calls the battle RNG 0x001CA474; there is no accuracy, dodge or hit test anywhere. The old 'CalcEvasionChance' name had no supporting operation. The field meanings are still inferred from the math, so maybe_ stays.

name: Text_CalcRowHeightEx
signature: int Text_CalcRowHeightEx(int arg1, int row, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int arg5, int arg6)
summary: Computes the height of a text row including the 1.0/1.2 line scaling and the row padding, storing the result in the row at +0x52.
evidence: Now known to be called from Text_ApplyRowStyle (0x488638) next to Text_CalcRowBox/Text_MeasureElement, i.e. the row-style pass; the 1.0/1.2 literals and the +0x52 store match the height computation.

name: Text_UpdateBlinkStateA
summary: Blink-state updater for the row flag family 0x2C..0x2F/0xA5: resolves the currently set flag, scales it and refreshes the layout.
evidence: explicit checks vtable 0xE8(0x2C/0x2D/0xA5/0x2E/0x2F); calls 0x491270 then 0x487FC0; float 100.0/0.01; caller 0x4903CC

name: Text_UpdateBlinkStateB

name: Battle_MonsterUi_CheckStatusIcons
summary: Asks the monster UI whether status keys 0x6A/0x6B are active and returns 0xFFFFFFED (-19) or 0xFFFFFFEC (-20), or 0 when neither is set - the row code uses these as 'display the status icon' result codes.
evidence: Two calls to vtable+0xE8(self, 0x6A) / (self, 0x6B) returning -0x13 and -0x14; the same vtable+0xE8 'has key' query is used by the Text/Monster row code around it.

name: Party_Member_GetAttackCount
summary: Returns the member's number of attack instances: 2 when the equipped slot-0 item kind is 0x11 (falcon, two hits) or the member has an off-hand weapon, otherwise 1.
evidence: The body uses the established func_0035EB98 (party member) + func_006292F0(member,0) (slot-0 item) and the named Party_Member_HasOffhandWeapon, and treats item kind 0x11 (the FACTS falcon 2-hit subtype) exactly like an off-hand weapon. Callers use the result as a loop count in Battle_Message_BuildActorRowBig (0 < local_ac; i < local_ac) and in AI action evaluation, so it is an attack/row count, not an 'equipment category'.

name: Text_FindMarkerRow
summary: Scans the layout rows of a message id and returns the index of the first marker row (characters 0x3E..0x47 in byte +0x58).

name: Battle_Monster_UpdateStatBar

name: Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue

evidence: The body calls 0x48CA0C with style 3 and 0x48B278 for the display slot, then returns f_2A; three battle-row helpers use it, and 0xFF is handled as the no-effect sentinel.

name: maybe_Battle_Row_UpdateIfKindMatches
signature: void maybe_Battle_Row_UpdateIfKindMatches(char* self, void* unit, int arg3)

evidence: The caller is now the named Battle_Row_SumHpBar and the record comes from 0x0063DCA4, which fixes the 'compare row ids with the unit record' reading; but the func_001CA3E4 result is unused, so what the match is supposed to do is still unknown.

name: Battle_Action_GetEffectValue
summary: Returns the action's effect value as a float: special units (+0x10 set) go through Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue, ordinary units convert the action record's u16 fields +0x13C/+0x13E/+0x140/+0x142 to float, each guarded by the flag bytes +0x189/+0x187/+0x185/+0x184.
evidence: NEW: the special-unit branch calls the confident Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue, so the general branch is the same query for ordinary units; the four VectorUnsignedToFloat calls write s0, i.e. the function returns a float, which the old 'GetRowValue' name did not say.

name: Text_MeasureRowByTemplate

Not item code: the function only measures a row.

name: Battle_CalcSkillDefenseReduction

name: maybe_Monster_GetAttackStat

name: Battle_Monster_GetHpBarAnchor

name: Text_GetRowAdvance

name: maybe_Party_GetMemberCombatStats
summary: Returns two float combat stats for a party member: reads the member record through 0x0035EB98 and the triple +0x740 / +0xEC0 + +0xB00, with an extra slot lookup and float scaling when the member flag +0xDA bit 7 is set.

name: Battle_Monster_UpdateMpBar
summary: The monster MP-bar update: it scales the current MP and refreshes the bar rectangle, falling back to the stat formatter for an invalid actor.

name: Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio
summary: Computes the HP-bar fill of a battle monster: takes the record max at f_26, compares the current ratio with 1% and marks the layout dirty on a change; the value is returned in s0.

name: Battle_CalcSpellEffectTotal
signature: int Battle_CalcSpellEffectTotal(u32 spellId, void* row, u32 target, float scale, u32 arg5, int applyLayout, int arg7)
summary: Evaluates a spell's eight 0x2C-byte effect entries (row kind 5) against a target, sums their values with the RNG variance, and when the spell's +0x296 flag is clear instead lays out the eight default rows; writes the resulting short to row+4.
evidence: The function starts with the spell-record resolver 0x0018C184 (SpellRecord per FACTS) and the callees Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch / Battle_MonsterUi_ResolveRowType resolve the effect rows; its position in 0x00485D90..0x00497900 (Battle Combat Math) and the old 'Text_' prefix was wrong.

name: Battle_Message_BuildRowForMonster

evidence: id compares 0x18/0xA4/0xA5 and row kinds 0x0E/0x16/0x1C; float 1.0/100.0/0.01/0.00001/2.0/0.9; calls maybe_Battle_Actor_GetStateIcon, 0x48FC6C, 0x490F20, 0x486B84, 0x48D894, 0x48EAA8, 0x48EBE0, 0x48D768

name: Battle_ApplyEquipCategoryDamageModifier
summary: Scales a battle damage value by the equipment category of the unit's slot-0 item: resolves the party member and its equipped item, reads ItemRecord+0x29 and picks one of four coefficients (f_114/f_118/f_11C, default f_120) from the data-manager record returned by 0x0063D178, then clamps the scaled value.
evidence: CORRECTED: the only caller is the named Battle_CalcActorDamageModifier, which stores the short result back into the unit record and passes it to func_00486B84; ItemRecord+0x29 is the documented equip category, so this is a battle damage coefficient chosen by equip category, not a text 'row metric' (the old name described the table offset, not the meaning).

name: Text_BuildRowForActor
signature: int Text_BuildRowForActor(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, int arg6, u32 arg7)
summary: Builds a generic actor message row: resolves the actor, measures the row through the layout engine, applies the 0x10/0x20 width flags and stores the result.
evidence: calls 0x20D08C, 0x4882F4, 0x49ACF8, 0x49AA0C, 0x48D894, 0x48748C (maybe_Monster_GetResistValue), maybe_Field_FindActorEntryByModel; called by Battle_BuildTargetSlots, Ui_MessageWindow_BuildLines etc.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetActionRow

The row-specific values are written by calls Ghidra shows without arguments.

The dropped call arguments (push {r3,...} prologue trap) keep it at maybe_.

name: Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect

name: Battle_ActionRecord_GetPower

summary: Looks up an action record by action ID through Game_GetDataManager and func_0063FD24, returning the signed 16-bit action power / HP delta field at +0xD0.

name: maybe_Battle_RollHitRateByTemplate

name: maybe_Text_Row_GetScaleFactorA
summary: Returns a per-row-type float multiplier for a battle text/bar row: probes the row type through virtual +0xE8 for the id group 0x1E, 0x1F, 0xA2, 0xAB, 0xAE, 0x20, 0x21, 0x101, 0x114 and 0x11C, reads a value for that type through 0x00491270 (default 100.0), scales it by 0.01f and marks the layout dirty when the result is non-zero. Callers multiply a row value by the returned s0 float.

The two verified callers (0x004937C4 and 0x004948B0, bl sites checked in asm) multiply by in_s0, so the getter role is solid. NOTE for follow-up: the merged name of 0x00491270, Battle_CalcRandomDamageVariance, does not fit a one-argument row-type call; it behaves like a shared table-row float helper and should be re-examined.

name: maybe_Text_Row_ApplySpacingPresetB

evidence: The same fallback ladder as the A preset at 0x00497FD4 with a different id group; its callers are battle stat-bar code (Battle_Monster_UpdateStatBar), so these are battle message rows rather than generic text spacing, and 'SpacingPreset' is still an inference.

name: maybe_Text_Row_GetScaleFactorC
summary: Second per-row-type float multiplier for a battle text/bar row: probes the row type through virtual +0xE8 for the id group beginning 0x23, 0x24, 0xA3, 0xAC, 0xAF, 0x25, 0x26 (then 0x115, 0x107, 0x102 and a computed +8 id), reads a value for that type through 0x00491270 (default 100.0), scales it by 0.01f and marks the layout dirty when the result is non-zero. Callers multiply a row value by the returned s0 float.
evidence: Same shape as 0x00497FD4: one row-type argument to 0x00491270, float result in s0 (Ghidra drops it), and the callers 0x00494AC0 and 0x00495B2C have bl sites inside their bodies (0x00494AF0/0x494B58 and 0x00495C34/0x495C50, checked in asm) and consume the float as a multiplier. name: maybe_Battle_GetMemberScaledStat
summary: Looks up the party member behind actor+0x768 and folds the two float tables at member+0xD78 and member+0x1138 for the given stat index, scales by 0.01 and passes the result through the float scaler at 0x00487FC0; returns the battle-work pointer at +0x4238.
evidence: FACTS.md puts this address range in battle combat math, func_0035EB98 makes the actor's +0x768 a party-member index, and 0x00487FC0 is a float scaling/rounding helper (it takes/returns a float in s0), not 'Text_MarkLayoutDirty'; 'Row_CalcActorMetric' therefore described neither a row nor a metric.

name: Battle_Row_DispatchForActor

evidence: NEW: both the template builder (Ui_LayoutParams_Init) and the dispatcher (maybe_Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch) are named, and the sibling maybe_Battle_Row_SumActorValuesB in the call set uses the same template layout - so the per-actor row dispatch is readable; the 4x4 search loops are literal.

name: Text_Row_ApplySpacingByCategory

name: Text_GetActorFieldByIndex

evidence: New context: the record resolver is now Monster_LookupRecord and the neighbour is Battle_Row_SumHpBar, so the caller side is the battle text-row builder; the subsystem prefix Text_ is therefore the usage, not the data (it is monster data, not item data).

name: Battle_Row_SumHpBar
summary: Builds the summed-HP battle row for a party group: adds the HP-derived values of up to four matched actor slots, converts the total into a bar fill, applies the hit flash and writes the three label segments.
evidence: The same named caller Battle_Message_BuildRowForMonsterEx dispatches to it in the other row branch (local_35c == 0) as the alternative to Battle_MonsterPanel_Build, and the body sums the row's actor slots before calling the named Battle_Monster_CalcHpBarFill/CalcHpBarOrigin; 'Sum' therefore describes the summed party HP bar, not turn priority.

name: maybe_Battle_Row_SumActorValuesB

summary: Variant of the row value summer that takes an explicit row index, re-dispatches the row through 0x004989DC and writes the accumulated value plus two companion segments into the row's text element.
evidence: Re-read: same named neighbour set as 0x00498A88 and the same three-segment writer, so it is the indexed twin of that function. The re-dispatch target 0x004989DC is still unnamed, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Battle_Row_UpdateFromActorSlot

Caller Text_MeasureRowByType uses it while re-measuring rows.

summary: Builds a monster battle-row panel: resolves the monster record, measures the name, computes the HP-bar origin/fill/span and writes the numeric label segments plus the blink animation.

name: maybe_Battle_MessageRow_RollVariance
summary: Rolls a symmetric battle-RNG value in [-f_14, f_14] and returns it together with the battle-work message-row base at +0x4238; all five callers are battle message-row builders, so this is most likely the row's random variance, not a group-attack proc roll.
evidence: CORRECTED: the caller set is entirely battle message-row code (Battle_MessageRow_BuildLayout, Text_Row_MeasureIconRowWidth, maybe_Battle_Row_SumActorValues/UpdateFromActorSlot), and the object's +0x14 is used as a symmetric range around zero; 'multi-target proc' described a use no caller supports. The return is a two-word CONCAT that Ghidra mixed up, so confidence stays low.

name: maybe_Battle_RollSignedRange
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_RollSignedRange(void* record, int unusedA, int unusedB)
summary: Rolls a random integer in [-record->f_14, record->f_14] over the battle work array at +0x4218 and converts it to float. The 64-bit return the decompiler shows is a decode artefact.

name: Anim_InstanceList_UpdateTiming

name: maybe_Party_UpdateMemberHpDisplay
summary: Per-frame party status pass: walks the alive party members, derives a per-member offset from the status bits at member+0xDA and pushes (HP - offset, clamped to 1) into the member's display object, then lazily creates the two 0x98-byte status widgets and sets their colour from the same mode bits (0xFF440000 / 0xC7158500 / 0xEEEE6600 / 0xEEEEEE00).
evidence: NEW: the old name is wrong. The body walks Party_CountAliveMembers / Party_GetActiveMemberDataByIndex, reads the status word at member+0xDA (bits 0x10 and 0x02) and the HP at member+0x14, calls the member's vt[+4] with the resulting value, and then picks one of four RGBA colour constants for the lazily created 0x98-byte widgets. Nothing here is an animation instance list. Kept maybe_ because the exact meaning of the vt[+4] call and of the two widgets is still inferred.

name: maybe_Anim_InstanceList_ApplyModeByte
summary: Reads the current state byte at (work+8)->+0x48->+0x281 and, when it is non-zero, looks it up through 0x0063D6B8. The return value is unused, so the only visible effect is the callee's side effect.
evidence: No caller was found in the readable tree and the lookup result is discarded, so neither the 'Anim_InstanceList' receiver nor 'Apply' can be confirmed; the only new anchor is that the byte is the documented UI overlay mode byte at +0x281.

name: Anim_FormatEnemyAnimationPath

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_InitFromTriggerRecord

What the gadget then does with them is still unknown, hence maybe_.

evidence: All three literals resolve (0x004FBFEC/FF8/004FC004) and the body binds exactly those panes; this is the plainest example of the title+pager pattern, so confidence is at the top of the allowed range.

name: Ui_TextBuilder_SetNumericValues
signature: void Ui_TextBuilder_SetNumericValues(int self, u32 builder, u32 record)
summary: Fills the two numeric text entries of a text builder from a record: formats the record's value pair into decimal strings and stores them as the two sub-elements of the element at +0x300. Called by Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout; the two 0x6F0F1C conversions and the pair of 0x1A6680 element setters are the number-formatting path.
evidence: func_003813B0(arg3), func_00644A9C(arg3,arg2), then func_006F0F1C(...,iVar2)+func_001A6680(self+0x300, index|1/2, str+4); caller 0x00311CB8 maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout

name: Ui_SmithMenu_SetDetailPair
signature: void Ui_SmithMenu_SetDetailPair(UiWidget* self, int value1, int value2)
