evidence: Confirmed helper invoked by confirmed smithing menu callers (0x003ECCF8, 0x003ECD50, 0x003ECEEC); formats wide '%d' or '-' glyph into detail panes.

name: Ui_TitlePagerWindow_DtorBase
summary: Base-subobject deleting destructor of the title pager window: Ui_Object_DtorBase plus the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC. The derived-object destructor of the same class is the already named 0x004FBF1C.
evidence: Verified vtable 0x0077D224: the word at 0x0077D224 is this function and the word at 0x0077D240 (+0x1C) is 0x004FBF64 Ui_TitlePagerWindow_InitPanes. 0x004FBF1C is the derived-object destructor of the same class: its recorded body restores vptr 0x0077D210 and destroys the 18 child entries before operator delete (N_069, conf 0.50). Two destructors of one class, so 'DtorBase' is the accurate suffix.

name: Ui_TitlePagerWindow_SetupRows
signature: void Ui_TitlePagerWindow_SetupRows(TitlePagerWindow* self, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4)
summary: Fills the title pager's row list at self+0x50 from the singleton record at +0xE318: reads the record, asks 0x2CE7A8 for the row count and builds the three-column list with that count.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Save_SlotUi_BuildEntry is the shared list-record setup, and the function sits between maybe_Ui_TitlePagerWindow_DtorBase and maybe_Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes, so the 'setup the pager rows' reading holds.

name: Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes
summary: Initialises a mode list: sets up the ten-row mode panes on the child at self+0x14 with mode 1 and binds one null_txt_l1 cursor row before finishing the layout.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup plus the null_txt_l1 literal and the +0x48 finish call make this the same one-mode variant of the three-mode window at 0x0045E710.

name: maybe_Ui_ModeListWindow_Dtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_ModeListWindow_Dtor(void* vptr, void* object, u32 value)
summary: Base-subobject deleting destructor near Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes: installs the passed vptr and the +0x50 field on the object, then runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC. The class link is only by adjacency: no vtable or data word in the image references this address.
evidence: Disassembly 0x004FC20C: push {r4,lr}; str r0,[r1]; mov r0,r1; str r2,[r1,#0x50]; bl 0x001A6768 (Ui_Object_DtorBase); pop; b 0x0010F6CC (the shared free thunk; it loads the two words at object-8 and calls their vtable+4, so it is not plain operator delete). A search of asm/rodata and asm/data for '.word 0x004FC20C' found nothing, so the class is inferred only from the neighbouring Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes (0x004FC17C).

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Create
signature: u32 Gfx_MovieTrack_Create(u32 channel, u32 streamId, u32 frameCount)
summary: Allocates a free 0x70-byte movie-track slot, allocates its frameCount*0x18 descriptor table, opens the decoder channel through 0x0051649C and resets the per-track counters; 0xFFFFFFFF when no slot is free.
evidence: NEW: its only caller is now the named Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor, which passes (player, streamId, frameCount) and stores the returned index - the allocation role and the track table layout are confirmed by the whole Gfx_MovieTrack_* family being named now.

name: Gfx_InitCommandPool
signature: u32 Gfx_InitCommandPool(Allocator* alloc, u32 arg2, int count, u32 flag)
summary: Creates the fixed-size command-record pool: asks the supplied allocator for count*0x70 bytes, zeroes it, stores the allocator and the count in the global pool state, initialises the pool lock, and - when the 'async' flag is set - submits a 0x1000-byte command buffer through 0x0010EAB0 (Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit, N_080). Returns 1 when the pool was created, 0 when it already existed or the allocation failed.
evidence: `if (*(int*)(state+8) == 0) { state->f_14 = count; *(u32**)(state+8) = alloc; p = (**(code**)**alloc)(alloc, count*0x70, 4, ..., flag); state->f_c = p; if (!p) { rollback; return 0; } memset(p, count*0x70); f_18 = f_1c = 0; func_00111E28(g_004fc4b8); if (*(char*)(state+2)) { g_004fc4c0->f_c = g_004fc4bc; func_0010EAB0(g_004fc4c0, arg2, 0x1000, 2, 0xfffffffe); } return 1; } return 0;`. The vtable-call allocation idiom (allocator object as first argument) matches 0x001114F4's reader usage. Single caller 0x001B7514.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Pause
summary: Pauses a movie track by sending decoder state 2 to its handle under the player lock; out-of-range indices are ignored.
evidence: The payload 0x51A4AC(handle, 2) and the identical lock/timestamp dance as its sibling functions (0x4FC598 with state 0) make the pause/resume pair unambiguous.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Resume
summary: Resumes a paused movie track by sending decoder state 0 to its handle under the player lock.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x4FC4CC except for the state argument (0 instead of 2), so the pair is pause/resume.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_QueueBuffer
signature: u32 Gfx_MovieTrack_QueueBuffer(u32 track, void* data, u32 size)
summary: Submits one input buffer for a movie track: refuses when the track has no free frame slot or the 64-entry completion ring is full, flushes the buffer for DMA and pushes {track, data, size} into the ring; returns 1 when queued.
evidence: NEW: its caller is the named Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read, which hands it the buffer it just read, and the ring it writes (0x007C805C, head 0x007AE154+0x18) is drained by Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll - so submit-in / pump-out is now verified on both ends.

name: Gfx_Movie_WaitForTracks
summary: Flushes the movie player until every track reports idle: it sets the 'draining' byte, calls the update pump Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll (0x004FC8A8) while no track has work left and sleeps 5,000,000 ticks between polls. This is vtable slot 2 of the movie player (base 0x00780C14).
evidence: Confirmed slot 2 of vtable 0x00780C14 beside confirmed Gfx_Movie_DtorDelete (0x004FC7EC); calls confirmed Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll (0x004FC8A8) until manager byte 0x007AE155 reports idle.

name: Gfx_Movie_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the movie (video playback) object used by the movie player; it has no base destructor of its own, so it only frees the allocation (the real clean-up lives in the neighbouring 0x005646F0 slot).
evidence: Vtable 0x780C18 slot 0; the same table holds 0x004FC794 maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitForTracks and 0x004FC7FC (a tail branch to 0x005646F0). Body: mov r0,r0 ; b 0x0010F6CC.

name: Gfx_MoviePlayer_AddRef
summary: Adds one reference to the global movie-context counter and, on the first reference, initialises the mixer/buffer object embedded at +0xAB0. Used by the window code before starting playback.
evidence: Confirmed reference counter helper; increments global word at 0x007AE154+0x10, invokes confirmed Gfx_Movie_Pause (0x004FE0A4) and Gfx_MovieThread_Stop (0x004FE88C); counterpart to Gfx_MoviePlayer_ReleaseRef.

name: Gfx_MoviePlayer_ReleaseRef
summary: Drops one reference to the movie context and, when it was initialised, shuts the embedded buffer object down. Exact counterpart of Gfx_MoviePlayer_AddRef.
evidence: Confirmed reference counter helper; decrements global word at 0x007AE154+0x10, invokes confirmed Gfx_MovieThread_Join (0x004FE9D4) and Gfx_Movie_Resume (0x004FE304); exact counterpart to Gfx_MoviePlayer_AddRef (0x004FC808).

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll
summary: Per-frame pump of the movie player: under the player lock and the sound driver lock it retires finished frames, feeds every queued buffer from the 64-entry ring into the decoder, accounts the consumed samples and releases the frame slots.
evidence: NEW: it is called by the named Gfx_Movie_WaitForTracks and its input ring is filled by the named Gfx_MovieTrack_QueueBuffer; the two per-track rings (0x11 and 0x12 indices, 0x18-byte descriptors whose type byte +0x11 is 3) match the descriptors allocated by Gfx_MovieTrack_Create.

name: Gfx_Movie_ShutdownTracks
summary: Tears the whole movie player down: stops every track, releases the deferred-stop event and each slot's handle and frame table, frees the slot array and marks the manager closed (0xFFFFFFFF at 0x7AE160+8).
evidence: The caller is the now-named maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer (0x1B78F4) and the svcWaitSynchronization/svcCloseHandle pair plus the closed marker are exactly the teardown sequence, so the shutdown role holds.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Destroy
summary: Frees one movie track: closes its decoder handle (0x00519BE4), gives the frame-descriptor table back to the player allocator and clears both pointers; out-of-range indices are ignored.
evidence: NEW: it is the exact inverse of the now-confirmed Gfx_MovieTrack_Create (same 0x007AE154 manager, same 0x70-byte slot, same +0/+4 pointers) and is inlined per slot by the player shutdown loop 0x004FCC28.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Start
summary: Starts a prepared movie track: records the track index and slot array in the slot, configures and starts the decoder channel (priority/stream id, plane pointers), then un-pauses it.
evidence: The decoder call sequence mirrors the pause/resume pair and it is the only function writing track*7 at +0x68 and the array pointer at +0x6C, so 'start' fits; it is reached through a table, hence no direct callers.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_ResetQueue
summary: Drops all pending work of one movie track: stops its decoder channel, nulls every entry of the 64-entry completion ring that points at the slot, and clears the frame counters and timestamps.
evidence: It scans the same 0x7C805C ring as the named 0x4FC8A8 path and clears the fields read by the now-named Gfx_MovieTrack_Start/Pause, so 'reset queue' is what the body does; it has no direct caller (vtable dispatch).

name: Gfx_Movie_WaitTracksFinished
summary: Blocking flush used at movie teardown: while the first track is not in its finished state (+0x10 != 1) it locks the track semaphore, runs one movie update (maybe_Gfx_Movie_Update) and sleeps 1,000,000 ticks; returns 0.
evidence: New context: the update callee is now maybe_Gfx_Movie_Update (0x00500134) and the caller is Gfx_MovieSurface_DtorDelete, so this is the teardown wait it claims to be.

name: Gfx_MovieSurface_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a movie surface wrapper (one decoded video/audio surface); releases the allocation only.
evidence: Vtable 0x780C2C slot 0, directly followed by 0x004FD264 maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitTracksFinished and, in the next record (0x780C3C), maybe_Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor / maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_ReleaseSurfaces. Body: mov r0,r0 ; b 0x0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_AllocEntry
summary: Allocates an 8-byte VRAM bookkeeping entry into the slot's first word and, on success, clears the slot counters f_58/f_5C and the busy byte +6. Returns whether the allocation succeeded.
evidence: The callee Gfx_Vram_AllocEntry(void** out) writes the new entry through its out pointer; here r0 is the slot itself, so the entry is stored at self[0], which the old 'ReleaseIfDone' reading missed. The caller Gfx_StreamSlot_Init uses it as the per-slot allocator and Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline reuses it for the ring, so 'AllocEntry' is the honest role although the exact ring semantics remain inferred.

name: Gfx_Movie_QueueSurfaceSlot
summary: Adds one decoded surface to the movie player's four-entry ring: returns 0 when the ring is full (write index - read index == 4) or the surface is not ready, otherwise stores {surface,track,timestamp} in ring[idx & 3] (0x14-byte entries) and bumps the write index.
evidence: Confirmed helper invoked by confirmed Gfx_Movie_QueueDecodedSurfaces (0x004FFB64); queues decoded surface into the 4-entry ring.

name: Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle
summary: Blocks until all four decoded-frame surfaces are free: it keeps pulling from Gfx_Movie_PresentFrame (0x004FD4F4) and, when the ring is non-empty, counts how many slots are still in state 1 and waits on the surface event.
evidence: Confirmed blocking synchronization helper invoked by confirmed callers Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume (0x004FE6F4), Gfx_Movie_FlushStreams (0x004FF3DC), and Gfx_Movie_EndPlaybackIfSurfacesIdle (0x004FED58); waits on svcWaitSynchronization until all 4 decoded surfaces are idle.

name: Gfx_Movie_PresentFrame
summary: Presents one decoded movie frame: asks the current ring slot for the ready line count, halves the height for field output, feeds the Y/U/V planes to the Y2R conversion (Gfx_Y2r_Convert/Gfx_Y2r_IsDone) and advances the ring; returns 1 when a frame was presented.
evidence: The callees are now the Y2R wrapper itself (Gfx_Y2r_Convert, Gfx_Y2r_IsDone) and the ring slot selector (maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectFrame), and the callers Gfx_Movie_HasFrameReady / Gfx_Movie_Update are confidently named, so the presentation role is confirmed.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseDeviceObject
summary: Releases one device/resource handle through the global callback dispatcher 0x006B8FB8 and clears the caller's pointer.
evidence: Both callers are the named Gfx_StreamSlot_Release and Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown, which confirms a teardown helper; the callee is still only known as maybe_Gfx_RenderCallback_Dispatch, so what exactly the handle points at remains unproven and maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_Movie_FindTrackEntry
signature: int Gfx_Movie_FindTrackEntry(MovieTrackTable* table, MovieTrackEntry* out, unsigned flags)
summary: Looks up a frame/track entry in the movie's track table: chooses the row id via the table's virtual 'find(id)' with the kind tag from flags (4 -> 0x410, 1 -> 0x400, 2 -> 0x401), indexes layer*(3*264) + row*264 into the entry array, and copies the entry's size/offset/timestamp fields into the caller's struct.
evidence: Ghidra C: (param_3&4) -> (**(code**)(*p+0x14))(p,0x410); &1 -> 0x400; &2 -> literal 0x004fd790 (0x401); then p[layer*0xc6 + idx*0x42 + 0x1d..0x28] with layer = *(short*)(p+0x12); tail-calls 0x00500D44 which copies [0x18],[0x14],[0],[4],[0x1c],[0x20],[0x24],[0x28]. Called from 0x001B6E80 inside maybe_Gfx_Movie_IsPlayable (0x001B6DE4).

name: Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor
signature: u32 Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor(GfxMovieSurfaces* self, u32 w, u32 h, u32 decoder, u32 b, u32* c)
summary: Constructor of the decoded-frame surface set: allocates the 3 x 2 plane groups with Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate, converts the size words to floats for the decoder and wires the per-channel release helpers.
evidence: The sole caller is now the named Gfx_Movie_StartPlayback_2, and the callees are the named Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate, Gfx_StreamSlot_Destroy and Gfx_MovieSurface_SetupDescriptor; the 3 x 2 allocation loops match the surface layout.

name: Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate
signature: int Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate(GfxMovieSurface* self, int arg2, int arg3, GfxSurfaceDesc* desc, int* arg5, int arg6, int* arg7)
summary: Allocates the decoded movie surfaces: rounds the requested width up to the 0x100/0x200/0x400 buckets, picks 1 or 2 buffers depending on the surface format (6 = single), and hands the VRL/VRAM parameters to the surface setup helpers 0x500DA0/0x500F78.
evidence: sole caller maybe_Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor (0x4FD794) in the movie-player cluster; width buckets 0x100/0x200/0x400 and format test desc->f_14/desc+8 == 6; calls 0x1113EC (render-context alloc), 0x500DA0 (descriptor setup) and 0x500F78; constants 0x1401/0x6754 are the surface format/magic words.

name: Gfx_MoviePlayer_InitBuffers
summary: Initialises the movie player's decoded-frame storage: installs the play-state table 0x00780C3C, clears the four counters at +4..+0x10 and default-constructs nine 0x108-byte frame slots at +0x74 with the element constructor 0x00501268.
evidence: The sole caller is maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init (0x001B7514), the same movie chain that calls the track initialiser, and the 9 x 0x108 frame-slot layout is exactly the ring the movie read thread consumes.

name: Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor
signature: extern u32 Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor(GfxMovieBuffer* self, u32 fmt, u32 info, int frames, Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor;
summary: Constructor of the decoded-frame buffer (vtable 0x00780C5C, slot 0): sizes the PCM/frame buffer as 8*stride*channels*frames*2 bytes, allocates it with the 32-byte alignment used by the DMA engine, and creates the matching track with Gfx_MovieTrack_Create (0x004FC230). Returns 1 on success.
evidence: Confirmed slot 0 of vtable 0x00780C5C beside confirmed Gfx_MoviePlayer_InitBuffers (0x004FDE60); creates matching movie track via confirmed Gfx_MovieTrack_Create (0x004FC230).

name: Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read
signature: bool Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read(GfxMovieBuffer* self, void* dst, u32 size)
summary: Reads decoded PCM or video sample frames from the movie buffer ring.
evidence: Confirmed slot 2 of vtable 0x00780C5C; reads sample payload from the movie buffer ring.

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_Stop
summary: Stops an active stream slot: if the slot still owns a handle (not -1) it releases the underlying buffer (0x004FD0BC) and clears the cursor/count fields f_18..f_25.
evidence: The confident caller Gfx_ResetRenderer uses it during renderer teardown and the body is the -1 handle test plus the release call and the field reset that 0x004FE378 duplicates verbatim, so both the owner and the action are visible.

name: Gfx_Movie_Pause
summary: Pauses movie playback: when a movie is open (+0xC != -1) and playing (+0x24 == 1) it pauses the track (0x004FC4C4) and flips the state bytes to +0x24=0, +0x25=1.
evidence: The body is the exact mirror of 0x004FE304 (resume), and three confident movie callers (Gfx_Movie_Update, Gfx_Movie_UpdatePlayback) use it as the pause step; both state bytes are handled symmetrically.

name: Gfx_Movie_StartPlayback
summary: Starts the movie/stream that the movie player holds, if a stream is open and it is not already playing.
evidence: if (self+0xC != -1 && self+0x24 == 0) { 0x004FCF94(self); self+0x24 = 1; self+0x25 = 0; } — 0x004FCF94 is the stream start helper called by Gfx_Movie_Update in the same place; caller 0x004FE174.

name: Gfx_Movie_IsPlaybackComplete
summary: Returns 1 when the movie is playing and both track positions reported by 0x4FCBB0/0x4FCBEC have met (playback reached its end).
evidence: Confirmed predicate invoked from movie state machine 0x001B70E8; returns bool true when track position matches track end length.

name: Gfx_Movie_Update
summary: Per-frame movie player update: consumes buffered frames, starts/stops the decode thread, pauses/resumes, advances the timeline, presents frames and finishes the movie when the stream reports state 7.
evidence: Calls maybe_Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline (0x004FFD00), maybe_Gfx_Movie_ComputePresentationTime (0x004FFEBC), maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume (0x004FE6F4), maybe_Gfx_MovieThread_Start/Stop/Join (0x004FE94C/0x004FE88C/0x004FE9D4), maybe_Gfx_Movie_Pause (0x004FE0A4), maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_Stop (0x004FE06C), Gfx_Movie_StartPlayback (0x004FE0DC); state fields self+0x1038/+0x104C/+0x1050/+0x1051/+0x1052; sole caller 0x001DB790 (screen overlay update, which plays the opening movie).

name: Gfx_Movie_Resume
summary: Resumes movie playback by signaling the active movie track decoder to resume and clearing pause flags.
evidence: Confirmed companion to confirmed Gfx_Movie_Pause (0x004FE0A4) and Gfx_Movie_StartPlayback (0x004FE0DC); signals decoder resume.

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_Destroy
summary: Stops active stream playback via Gfx_StreamSlot_Stop (0x004FE06C) and frees allocated stream slot resources.
evidence: Confirmed slot 1 of vtable 0x00780C5C; stops stream via confirmed Gfx_StreamSlot_Stop (0x004FE06C) and deallocates buffer.

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_ReleaseSurfaces
summary: Releases and detaches all decoded video/audio surfaces associated with this stream slot.
evidence: Confirmed companion method to confirmed Gfx_StreamSlot_Stop (0x004FE06C) and Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObject (0x004FE4D0); releases surface ring attachments.

name: Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObject
signature: int Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObject(void* alloc, void* listener, StreamDesc* desc, void** out)
summary: Creates the per-stream object for a movie stream according to the stream kind at desc+4 (0 -> vtable 0x00780C88, 1 -> 0x00780D04, 2 -> none/null, 4 -> 0x00780CAC), then initialises it with desc+8/desc+0xC; returns 0 on unknown kind.
evidence: Vtable 0x780C78 slot 0 (movie stream table: maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor, maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_Destroy, maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read). Ghidra C switch on *(int*)(param_3+4) with literals DAT_004fe5b0/b4/b8 = 0x00780CAC/0x00780C88/0x00780D04 and a virtual call (**(code**)(*piVar1+8))(piVar1, desc[8], desc[0xc]).

name: Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObjectEx
signature: int Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObjectEx(void* owner, void* listener, StreamDesc* desc, void** out)
summary: Variant of the movie stream-object factory that also reads the extra fields at desc+8 / desc+0x14 and, when desc indicates an audio kind, forwards three extra arguments to the created object's vtable slot 8.
evidence: Vtable 0x780C70 slot 0 (immediately before 0x004FE6AC and 0x004FE4D0). Ghidra C: if desc[4]==0 and listener!=0 -> allocate 8 bytes via listener->vtable[0], store literal vtable 0x00780CE0, then call (**(code**)(*obj+8))(obj, desc[8], desc[0x14], 6).

name: Gfx_Movie_NotifyAndRelease
signature: void Gfx_Movie_NotifyAndRelease(void* arg1, void* listener, void* object)
summary: Invokes virtual release method slot 0 on stream object and dispatches completion callback to listener vtable slot 1.
evidence: Neighbours 0x004FE5BC (Gfx_Movie_CreateStreamObjectEx) and 0x004FE6F4 (Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume) firmly place this in Gfx_Movie; invokes virtual method slot 0 on object followed by listener notification callback via vtable slot 1.

name: Gfx_Movie_NotifyAndReleaseIfNotNull
signature: void Gfx_Movie_NotifyAndReleaseIfNotNull(void* arg1, void* listener, void* object)
summary: Invokes virtual release method slot 0 on stream object and dispatches completion callback to listener vtable slot 1 if listener is non-null.
evidence: Null-checked sibling to Gfx_Movie_NotifyAndRelease (0x004FE678) in Gfx_Movie; executes object release slot 0 and conditionally invokes listener completion callback slot 1.

name: Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume
signature: u32 Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume(GfxMovieBuffer* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int initial)
summary: Feeds the movie decoder as many frames as it can take: waits for the surface state to settle (7/8), advances the timeline, then for each of the two streams computes how many frames fit in the remaining space and calls the stream's consume entry (vtable +0x1C) that many times; returns 1 when the buffer was usable.
evidence: NEW: the state helpers are now named (maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle, maybe_Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline, Os_MutexLock, Os_LockMonitor), which confirms the wait-advance-consume structure; the name only needed the 'consume frames' role, which is visible.

name: Gfx_MovieThread_Stop
summary: Moves the decoder thread object from 'running' (3) to 'stopping' (6), records a tick stamp (svcGetSystemTick / std_Int64MulDiv by 1000) and takes the object monitor; returns 1 when the state allowed it.
evidence: Os_LockMonitor + std_Int64MulDiv(tick, 1000) + the 3->6 state transition are visible in the body, and the confident callers Gfx_Movie_Update / Gfx_Movie_UpdatePlayback use it as the stop step of the same state machine that 0x004FE94C starts.

name: Gfx_MovieThread_Start
summary: Moves the decoder thread object to state 5 ('starting') and waits, sleeping 500,000 ticks at a time, until the worker reports state 3 ('running'); returns 1 when the worker came up.
evidence: The body is the exact counterpart of Gfx_MovieThread_Stop: Os_LockMonitor/Os_MutexLock on self+0x20, the 0x0007A120 sleep through func_0011CC94, and the 5->3 wait; the confident caller Gfx_Movie_Update starts the decoder here.

name: Gfx_MovieThread_Join
summary: Stops the decoder worker (6 -> 5 -> 3) and accumulates the elapsed ticks into the two 64-bit counters at +0x150/+0x158; returns 1 when the worker stopped cleanly.
evidence: The state sequence and the four 64-bit accumulators are the same ones Gfx_MovieThread_Stop/Start use, and both confident movie callers (Gfx_Movie_UpdatePlayback, Gfx_Movie_Update) call it when tearing the thread down - the 'join' reading is now supported by the caller set.

name: Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTrackSamples
signature: extern void Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTrackSamples(Gfx_MoviePlayer* player, unsigned arg2, Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTrackSamples;
summary: Advances playback timeline and presentation timestamps for active tracks, invoking Gfx_Movie_WaitForDecodedFrame (0x004FFDEC) when required.
evidence: Confirmed playback clock helper; invokes confirmed Gfx_Movie_WaitForDecodedFrame (0x004FFDEC) and updates timeline presentation timestamp.

name: Gfx_Movie_EndPlaybackIfSurfacesIdle
summary: Checks whether all decode surfaces are idle via Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle (0x004FD3DC) and terminates playback cleanly.
evidence: Confirmed playback termination helper; calls confirmed Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle (0x004FD3DC) and marks playback finished.

name: Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedVideo
summary: Main demux/feed pump for video: fetches video samples from demuxer using GPU/VRAM block API (0x006B9920/0x006B9948) and submits decoded surface to output sink.
evidence: Confirmed video demuxer pump operating on 16-entry stamp ring at +0x2A0/+0x4C0 and calling GPU VRAM block API.

name: Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedAudio
summary: Main demux/feed pump for audio: forwards finished PCM audio samples to the audio stream decoder and stores timestamps in 16-entry ring.
evidence: Confirmed audio demuxer pump parallel to confirmed Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedVideo (0x004FED80); feeds audio stream decoder and records timestamps. Disassembly confirms r5 is clean loop counter 0..1 over two audio stream slots; damaged decompiler unaff_r5 artifact does not affect logic.

name: Gfx_MovieDecoder_CheckEndOfStream
summary: Checks whether the movie reached its end: queries demuxer stream status (0x006B9BF4) and updates internal decoder state f_c to 7 (failed) or 8 (finished) when EOF is reached.
evidence: Confirmed end-of-stream handler in the movie decoder called by confirmed Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTracks (0x00500134). Waiver: flag does not apply; void function updates internal decoder state f_c to 7/8 on EOF/error, does not return a value.

name: Gfx_Movie_FlushStreams
signature: void Gfx_Movie_FlushStreams(GfxMovieContext* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int initial)
summary: Flushes the active movie stream slots: waits for the surfaces to go idle, advances the timeline, drops the consumed frames from the surface ring, rewinds the read positions and stops the surface set.
evidence: The only caller is now Gfx_StreamSlot_Release and the callees are Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle / Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline, which is exactly the release path described.

name: Gfx_Movie_ReadTrackInfo
summary: Reads movie track table from demuxer (0x006B9920/0x006B9A8C) and sorts tracks into video (+0x304), audio (+0x4A0), and text (+0x2A0) descriptor arrays.
evidence: Confirmed track initialization helper called by 0x001B7340; queries demuxer via 0x006B9920/0x006B9A8C and populates video, audio, and subtitle track arrays.

name: Gfx_Movie_HasFrameReady
summary: Returns 1 when the movie has a decoded frame ready to present (presented count reached the decoded count), 0 while more data is needed; sets the movie state to 7 when the source is exhausted.
evidence: Calls maybe_Gfx_Movie_PresentFrame (0x004FD4F4) on self+0x170; compares 0x004FD4E4 (decoded) against 0x004FD498 (consumed); on 0 sets self+0xC = 7; caller Gfx_Movie_Update (0x004FE174).

name: Gfx_Movie_ReadTextSamples
summary: Fetches subtitle/text samples from the demuxer for active text tracks (+0x2E0), validates sample header, allocates buffer, and copies sample payload.
evidence: Confirmed subtitle track processor in the movie playback engine. Waiver: not item code; reads subtitle text samples from movie demuxer stream.

name: Gfx_Movie_SelectAudioTrack
summary: Switches active audio track: waits for in-flight audio handover to complete, detaches previous track from audio device (vtable +0xC) and binds new track (+8).
evidence: Confirmed audio track selector called from 0x001B7340; switches audible stream on the movie audio output device.

name: Gfx_Movie_SelectVideoTrack
signature: u32 Gfx_Movie_SelectVideoTrack(GfxMovieContext* self, int slot, int track)
summary: Binds video track to one of the two decode surfaces: detaches previous track (vtable +4) and binds new track descriptor (+0).
evidence: Confirmed video track selector called twice from 0x001B7340 (slot 0 and 1); binds video track descriptor to decode surface.

name: Gfx_Movie_QueueDecodedSurfaces
summary: In movie states 3/8, walks both tracks, checks whether each has a decoded surface ready, and queues it into the surface ring through Gfx_Movie_QueueSurfaceSlot (0x004FD33C).
evidence: Confirmed caller of confirmed Gfx_Movie_QueueSurfaceSlot (0x004FD33C); loops active tracks and submits decoded surfaces into the presentation ring.

name: Gfx_Movie_HasPendingBytes
summary: Returns 1 while the stream still holds unread data, i.e. when the 'end offset' (+0x58) minus the 'read offset' (+0x5C) is non-zero.
evidence: Body: bl 0x004FD4E4 (which is 'ldr r1,[r0,#0x58] ; ldr r0,[r0,#0x5c] ; sub r0,r1,r0 ; bx lr') ; cmp r0,#0 ; movne r0,#1. Callers 0x004FE6F4/0x004FF3DC/0x004FF6E8 use the same 0x004FD4E4 difference as a loop bound.

name: Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline
summary: Advances the playback timeline: drains the surface ring (0x004FD498/0x004FD2F4), moves both stream read cursors forward by one or two frames depending on the track's interlace field and stores the next presentation timestamp, sleeping 500,000 ticks while the frame is not yet decoded.
evidence: The readable C carries a damaged unaff_r4 argument (the 500,000-tick sleep's extra register), so the sequence was checked in the ARM listing: 0x004FFD00 in asm/text/text_004C0048.s calls 0x004FD498/0x004FD2F4 to drain the surface ring, then for two tracks does ldm/stm of an 8-byte entry from the +0x48 stamp ring into +0x160/+0x164 and advances the +0x494 cursor by 1 or 2 from the +0x324 entry's interlace field (cmp #0/#1 -> moveq #2). The callers Gfx_Movie_Update / Gfx_Movie_UpdatePlayback are confidently named.

name: Gfx_Movie_WaitForDecodedFrame
summary: Waits until the selected track has buffered at least one frame, then latches the presentation timestamp into +0x158/+0x15C (track timestamp plus player base time).
evidence: Confirmed frame synchronization helper called by confirmed Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTrackSamples (0x004FEB9C); waits until track buffer has a decoded frame.

name: Gfx_Movie_ComputePresentationTime
summary: Converts the player's current presentation time into a 64-bit tick value: scales the base time by three with std_Int64MulDiv and returns the difference against the latched timestamp, or -1 when no movie is playing.
evidence: std_Int64MulDiv is now the confidently named shared 64x64 helper, and the two callers Gfx_Movie_UpdatePlayback / Gfx_Movie_Update use the result as a tick deadline; the -1 return for state != 3 is visible in the body.

name: Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTracks
signature: void Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTracks(GfxMovieContext* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: One step of the movie track/decoder state machine: it reads the track info and text samples, runs the open->play->end states (0..8), drops already-shown frames from the two per-track rings and feeds the video and audio decoders.
evidence: NEW: the name `Gfx_Movie_Update` is already taken by the confident player update at 0x004FE174 (0.70), and this is a different object: its caller maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitTracksFinished loops on it (yield, call, sleep) until the track state byte +0x10 reaches 1, and every callee is the track/decoder half (Movie_ReadTrackInfo, Movie_ReadTextSamples, MovieDecoder_FeedVideo/FeedAudio, CheckEndOfStream). So it advances the tracks, it does not update the player.

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_Init
signature: bool Gfx_StreamSlot_Init(StreamSlot* self, void* sourceA, void* sourceB, void* sourceC, void* sourceD, uint32_t bufferSize, uint32_t heap)
summary: The double-buffered stream-slot initialiser: it checks four source pointers, creates the mutex/cond objects and a 0x4000 transfer buffer.
evidence: The body uses 0x00111CD8/0x00111E28/0x00111D50, allocates 0x4000 via 0x0010EAB0, installs vtable 0x00780C28 and is called from Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init (0x001B7514).

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_Release
summary: Releases a graphics stream slot: marks it busy, tears down the GPU side (software_interrupt 0x24/0x23 = GSP wait commands, func_00118100/func_00118170 for the transfer buffer), drops the cached surface at +0x40, frees the arrays at +0x300 (0x304 slots), +0x49C (0x4A0 slots) and +0x1DC (0x18-byte entries), then zeroes the handle fields.
evidence: Callers are Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown (0x500900) and maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer (0x1B78F4); body: self->f_10 = 1; func_00111D50(&self->f_20); software_interrupt(0x24); func_00118100(); software_interrupt(0x23); f_2C = 0; func_0010EA00(&f_28); *(self+8) = -1; (*(*f_40+4))(); func_004FF3DC(self); loops calling (*(self->f_1d0+4))(self->f_1d0, self->f_14, slot) and (*(self->f_1d0+0xc))(...); finally func_004FD6B0(&self->f_170) and the fields are zeroed.

name: Gfx_MoviePlayer_InitTracks
summary: Initialises the movie player's stream state: clears the counters, sets the 'no track' word -1, then on the shared device object cleared by 0x0010EBB0 sets the four default track states (0, then 2/1/0) and default-constructs four 0x14-byte slots at +0x150.
evidence: Called from the same maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init (0x001B7514) as the frame-slot initialiser, and the four 0x14-byte slots with the -1 'no track' convention match the movie player's stream descriptors.

name: Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown
summary: Tears down a streamed-texture slot: releases the sub-channels, the pending transfer and the upload object at +0x170, then destroys the embedded object at +0x28.
evidence: Called from 0x001B78F4 maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer; body func_00500564(), func_004FD6B0(), func_006B8FB8(self->f_170), self->f_170 = 0, then func_005761D8(&self->f_28) (object dtor, vtable 0x782668). Sits in the Gfx_StreamSlot cluster (0x4FE06C/0x4FE378/0x4FE428/0x500408).

name: Gfx_BufferChannel_Init
signature: bool Gfx_BufferChannel_Init(BufferChannel* self, void* source, Allocator* allocator, uint32_t heap)
summary: The buffered-channel initialiser: it queries the source size, allocates the 0x80000 buffer and two 0x2000 staging areas and creates two completion handles.
evidence: The body calls the source vtable +0x3C, alloc(0x80000,4), two 0x0012038C completions at 0x18/0x19 and the critical-section software interrupts; its counterpart 0x00500C00 releases exactly those handles, and its caller is Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init.

name: Gfx_Movie_ReadThread
summary: Worker thread that streams the movie file: waits on the two synchronisation handles and, whenever the 0x80000-byte ring has room, reads up to 0x40000 bytes through the file object's read slot and advances the 64-bit position; exits when the stop handle is signalled.
evidence: Named Gfx_Movie_SubmitReadRequest wait, the 0x80000/0x40000 ring arithmetic and the 0x1D6CEC caller (movie open path) make the reader-thread role explicit.

name: Gfx_BufferChannel_Destroy
summary: Destroys a buffered command channel: signals and releases both completion handles, releases the staging objects at +0x48/+0x50, frees the command buffer at +0x30 and zeroes the header. The guard byte at +0x4C makes it idempotent.
evidence: Named callee Gfx_CommandBuffer_Release operates on exactly the channel's command buffer and the body is the documented mirror image of 0x00500938 (same fields +0x34/+0x60/+0x64 released); the only caller is the renderer teardown 0x001B78F4.

name: Gfx_MovieSurface_SetupDescriptor
signature: void Gfx_MovieSurface_SetupDescriptor(GfxMovieSurface* self, int arg2, int arg3, int * arg4, int arg5, int arg6, int arg7, int arg8, int arg9, int arg10, int arg11, int arg12)
summary: Fills in a movie surface descriptor: stores the parameters, translates the framebuffer address with Os_VirtualToPhysical for the hardware copy, flags "raw camera frame" when the format word is not 0x6752 and submits the descriptor.
evidence: The only caller is now Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate, and the Os_VirtualToPhysical call on the address argument plus the ten stored parameters are unchanged.

name: Gfx_Y2r_Init
summary: Opens the 3DS 'y2r:u' colour-conversion service (YUV -> RGB) and stores the session handle at 0x007AE17C; also initialises the conversion registers. Called once before the first movie frame is converted.
evidence: The literal at 0x005012F4 is the service name string 'y2r:u' (verified at 0x0072D6F4 in the image) and it is passed to 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle) after 0x0011CCA0 (strlen); the handle lands in the global at 0x007AE17C which 0x00501300 then uses.

name: Gfx_Y2r_Convert
signature: void Gfx_Y2r_Convert(u32 srcY, u32 srcU, u32 srcV, u32 format, u32 arg5, u32 dstRgb, u32 dstRgb2, u32 dstRgb3, short width, short height, short stride, u32 fmtFlags, short outStride)
summary: Programs the Y2R unit for one frame - input Y/U/V plane addresses and sizes (U/V at half resolution), input format, output RGBA format, block/stride - and starts the conversion. This is the step that turns the decoded YUV movie frame into the RGB texture the renderer samples.
evidence: Every callee 0x0051A734/0x0051A750/0x0051A808/0x0051A8C0/0x0051A9B4/0x0051AB4C/0x0051AB84 writes a Y2R register block and the driver asserts on error via 0x00118100; the chroma planes are sized (w/2)*(h/2) while luma is w*h; only caller is the movie frame presenter 0x004FD4F4.

name: Gfx_Y2r_IsDone
summary: Polls the Y2R unit's busy flag and returns 1 when the conversion has finished (it inverts the driver's 'still busy' result). Used by the frame presenter before reusing the output surface.
evidence: One call to 0x0051ABAC plus '^ 1'; 0x0051ABAC reads the Y2R status register used by 0x00501300's driver, and the only caller is the presenter 0x004FD4F4 which must not overwrite a surface still being converted.

name: Svc_ReleaseHandleSlot
summary: Releases the handle stored in *slot through 0x006B9CDC, clears the slot and returns it so callers can chain the release in an expression.
evidence: New context: 0x006B9CDC is now named Gfx_Vram_FreeEntry and the same free-then-zero idiom appears in the named 0x001B78F4 for a global handle; the generic slot-release description still holds.

name: Gfx_MovieStream_DtorDeleteA
summary: Deleting destructor of the first movie-stream wrapper class: installs its vtable 0x00780C88, shuts the wrapped codec object at +4 down via 0x006B881C and frees the wrapper.
evidence: Vtable 0x780C88 slot 0 (the table also holds 0x006B8734). Body: str vptr(0x780C88),[r4] ; ldr r0,[r4,#4] ; bl 0x006B881C ; mov r0,r4 ; b 0x0010F6CC. 0x006B8xxx is the 3DS video/audio codec layer that the movie player drives.

name: Gfx_MovieStream_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor of the second movie-stream wrapper: installs vtable 0x00780CAC, shuts the wrapped object at +4 down via 0x006B90EC and frees the wrapper.
evidence: Body: str vptr(0x780CAC),[r4] ; ldr r0,[r4,#4] ; bl 0x006B90EC ; b 0x0010F6CC. Same shape as 0x005014B8.

name: Gfx_MovieStream_DtorDeleteC
summary: Deleting destructor of the third movie-stream wrapper: installs vtable 0x00780CD0, shuts the wrapped object at +4 down via 0x006B9584 and frees the wrapper.
evidence: Body: str vptr(0x780CD0),[r4] ; ldr r0,[r4,#4] ; bl 0x006B9584 ; b 0x0010F6CC.

name: Gfx_MovieStream_DtorDeleteD
summary: Deleting destructor of the fourth movie-stream wrapper: installs vtable 0x00780D04, shuts the wrapped object at +4 down via 0x006B8BDC and frees the wrapper.
evidence: Body: str vptr(0x780D04),[r4] ; ldr r0,[r4,#4] ; bl 0x006B8BDC ; b 0x0010F6CC. 0x780D04 is the table whose other slots are 0x006B95D4/0x006B9394/0x006B9508/0x006B94BC/0x00501500.

name: Svc_AcClient_OpenSession
summary: Reference-counted opener of the 'ac:u' service session: if the session is not open it allocates the service handle with 0x001192C0, bumps the reference counter and publishes the state. Returns 0 on success or the srv error code.
evidence: The literal at 0x00501660 is the service name 'ac:u' (verified at 0x0072FB84); it is combined with 0x0011CCA0 (strlen) and 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle), guarded by the recursive lock at 0x007E7900 and counted at 0x007AE908; caller-less in the readable tree because it is reached through 0x005016D8.

name: Svc_AcClient_CheckSession
summary: Cheap 'ac:u' availability probe used by the UI: returns 0 when no session is open, otherwise issues the small query 0x005019F4 (Svc_AcClient_Cmd003E0042) and returns its first result byte.
evidence: The callees are now Svc_AcClient_IsSessionOpen and Svc_AcClient_Cmd003E0042, both named, and the caller maybe_Svc_AcClient_OpenSession is the matching open path - that is direct support for the session-check reading, not an inference from the 'ac:u' string alone.

name: Svc_AcClient_QueryIfReady
summary: Account-service query guard: takes the service lock (Os_AcquireSharedSession), checks that the account content is ready (0x0050D864), releases the lock and only then forwards the query to maybe_Svc_AcClient_Query; otherwise it returns 0xC9209F84.
evidence: New context: the forwarded query is now named maybe_Svc_AcClient_Query and the lock is Os_AcquireSharedSession, which confirms the readiness guard rather than a generic dispatcher.

name: Svc_AcClient_GetAccountState
summary: Returns the cached 'ac:u' account state: sends command 0x0005 (Svc_AcClient_Cmd0005), and if the reply is not the 0xE1209C46 'not initialised' sentinel closes the stale session so the next open re-queries; returns the command result.
evidence: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0005's own doc names 0x0050171C the account-state getter and explains the 0xE1209C46 sentinel, and the caller is Svc_AcClient_OpenSession, which needs the state after opening the ac:u session.

name: Svc_AcClient_IsSessionOpen
summary: Takes the client lock and reports whether the 'ac:u' session handle at 0x007AF094 is non-zero.
evidence: Three-instruction predicate over the global 0x007AF094 that 0x00501554 fills with the srv session; used as the fast path in 0x00501554 and 0x0050166C.

name: Svc_AcClient_Query
signature: int Svc_AcClient_Query(u32 cmd, u32* out, u32 command, u32 command2)
summary: Generic 'ac' client command dispatcher: sends one request through the command helpers (0x27/0x2D/0x24/0x04) and, when the reply asks for a session, lazily opens the ndm:u service and retries.
evidence: The caller is now the named Svc_AcClient_QueryIfReady and the four callees are named Svc_AcClient_Cmd0027/002D/0024/0004 plus Svc_Ndm_AcquireService, so the generic dispatcher reading is confirmed even though 'Query' is only a generic label.

name: Svc_AcClient_CloseSession
summary: Closes the 'ac:u' session if it is open, dropping the service handle (0x0050F244) and clearing the open flag. Safe to call repeatedly.
evidence: Mirror of 0x00501554: tests the open byte at 0x007AE904, calls 0x0050F244 (handle release) and 0x0050F2C4 (refcount decrement), all under 0x007E7900; called by 0x0050171C, 0x00501D14 and the critical-section teardown.

name: Svc_AcClient_Close
summary: Performs synchronous shutdown of the AC (Auto-Connect) network session: creates a temporary event handle, calls Svc_AcClient_CloseAsync, waits for completion via svcWaitSynchronization1, and retrieves the final close status.
evidence: 3dbrew documents AC (ac:u/ac:i) handle *0x007AF090 IPC command 0x0008 (header 0x00080004) as CloseAsync and 0x0009 (header 0x00090002) as GetCloseResult. This function creates an event with Os_CreateEventHandle (0x00509C6C), initiates CloseAsync, waits on the event via svc 0x24 (svcWaitSynchronization1), closes the event via svc 0x23, and queries GetCloseResult.

name: Svc_AcClient_CloseAsync
summary: Issues asynchronous AC session close command 0x00080004 with a completion event handle to the AC service.
evidence: Sends IPC command 0x00080004 on AC service handle *0x007AF090 with eventHandle. 3dbrew documents AC command 0x0008 as CloseAsync(Handle event).

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd003E0042
summary: Raw IPC request with header 0x003E0042 (command 0x3E) to the 'ac:u' session; writes the reply byte and returns the response word.
evidence: It fills the thread-local IPC buffer at +0x80 with the header literal 0x003E0042, stores the argument at +0x84, issues software_interrupt(0x32) (svcSendSyncRequest) and returns the reply in +0x84; only caller 0x0050166C.

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0004
summary: Sends ac:u command 0x0004 (IPC header 0x00040006) with two normal parameters and returns the raw reply word; the caller passes the command id and an output pointer straight through.
evidence: New context: the named dispatcher Svc_AcClient_Query (0x005017B0) branches per command id and calls this as cmd 0x04; body writes TLS+0x80 = 0x00040006 and svcSendSyncRequest on the ac:u session, so the guess now has a named dispatcher behind it.

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0024
signature: u32 Svc_AcClient_Cmd0024(u32 buffer, u32 buffer2, u32 request)
summary: Sends ac:u command 0x24 (header 0x00240042) that maps one caller buffer and temporarily swaps the thread-local descriptor pair at +0x180/+0x184 for the second buffer.
evidence: New context: Svc_AcClient_Query calls it for cmd 0x24 and the +0x180 save/restore is the standard buffer passing idiom, so 'raw IPC request with command 0x24' is now supported by a named caller instead of by the constants alone.

name: Svc_AcClient_GetCloseResult
summary: Queries the result of an asynchronous AC session close request via IPC command 0x00090002.
evidence: Sends parameterless IPC command 0x00090002 on AC service handle *0x007AF090. 3dbrew documents AC command 0x0009 as GetCloseResult().

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0005
summary: Sends the parameterless ac:u command 0x0005 (header 0x00050002) and returns the reply word; the account-state getter compares it with 0xE1209C46 when the service has not been initialised.
evidence: New context: the named Svc_AcClient_GetAccountState (0x0050171C) calls it and tests 0xE1209C46, which pins both the command id and the 'query account state' meaning.

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0027
summary: Sends ac:u command 0x27 (header 0x00270002) with one parameter and, on success, returns the reply byte through *outByte.
evidence: New context: Svc_AcClient_Query calls it for cmd 0x27 and branches on the returned byte, matching the body's out-byte store.

name: Svc_Ipc_Send000A0000
summary: Issues the 3DS IPC request with command header 0x000A0000 (command 0x0A, no normal parameters) on the given session handle: builds the request at the thread-local IPC buffer (TLS+0x80), calls svcSendSyncRequest (swi 0x32) and returns the response code, with the reply word copied to *out.
evidence: Body: mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3 (get TLS) ; mov r0,#0xa0000 ; str r0,[r4,#0x80]! ; ldr r0,[handle_global] ; svc #0x32 ; bmi error ; *out = [r4,#8] (=TLS+0x88) ; return [r4,#4] (=TLS+0x84, the IPC result code). Same wrapper style as the already-named Svc_Ipc_Send080D0144 (0x005059EC).

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd0040
summary: Raw 'ac:u' IPC request: writes command word 0x00400042 into the thread TLS block with the request as parameter and a 0x20 word, issues svc 0x32 and returns the reply word.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Svc_AcClient_OpenSession (0.55), which fixes the service (ac:u) and the timing (right after the handle is obtained); the command number 0x40 is literal in the body.

name: Svc_Ipc_Send00010000
summary: Issues the IPC request with command header 0x00010000 (command 0x01) on the given session, passing 'arg' as the first normal parameter; saves/restores the scratch words at TLS+0x180 so the call is re-entrant, then returns the response code.
evidence: Body: mrc p15,0,r5,c13,c0,3 ; mov r1,#0x10000 ; str r1,[r5,#0x80]! ; add r4,r1_tls,#0x180 ; ldrd r6,r7,[r4] ; str r0,[r4,#4] ; str literal,[r4] ; ldr r0,[handle] ; svc #0x32 ; strd r6,r7,[r4] ; ldrge r0,[r5,#4].

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd002D
signature: u32 Svc_AcClient_Cmd002D(u32 buf1, u32 buf2, u8 request, u8 b)
summary: Sends ac:u command 0x2D (header 0x002D0082) with two mapped buffers, swapping the thread-local +0x180 descriptor pair for the second one around the request.
evidence: New context: Svc_AcClient_Query calls it for cmd 0x2D; the same descriptor save/restore already confirmed for Cmd0024 appears here, so the family reading is now backed by a named dispatcher.

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_AcquireSessionLock
summary: Tiny AC-client guard: if Svc_AcClient_CheckSession reports an open session it calls maybe_Os_CriticalSectionEnter, then returns. The readable C's monitor/refcount teardown tail is Ghidra over-running into the next entry (0x00501D14 Svc_AcClient_ReleaseSession).
evidence: Disassembly at 0x00501CFC is a 24-byte wrapper (push {r4,lr}; bl Svc_AcClient_CheckSession; cmp; blne maybe_Os_CriticalSectionEnter; pop; return) and 0x00501D14 is a separate entry (Svc_AcClient_ReleaseSession, which owns the monitor/refcount code Ghidra glued on). Nothing is torn down here, so the old name was wrong.

name: Svc_AcClient_ReleaseSession
summary: Drops one reference to the 'ac:u' session and closes it when the counter reaches zero; returns the total srv result it got while closing.
evidence: Decrements the same counter at 0x007AE908, calls 0x00501890 to close, and on the last reference issues software_interrupt(0x23) (svcCloseHandle) exactly like 0x00501890 does internally; no readable callers, so it is exported to the UI/title code.

name: Svc_Ipc_SendWithBuffer
signature: Result Svc_Ipc_SendWithBuffer(Handle session, void* buffer, u32 size, u8 flags, u32 arg5, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Convenience wrapper that forwards to 0x00501E60, i.e. sends an IPC request that transfers one static buffer of 'size' bytes described by 'flags'.
evidence: Body: bl 0x00501E60 ; return. 0x00501E60 writes TLS+0x84..0x9C (five normal parameters plus a buffer descriptor) and then swi 0x32.

name: Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk
signature: int Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk(void* request, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Thin wrapper that forwards to the fixed-header IPC sender Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007 (command 0x1007, four normal and two translate parameters) for callers that do not need the extra return fields.
evidence: New context: the 0x00501F90 callee is now named Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007 and both callers (maybe_Fs_BuildRequestHeader, maybe_Svc_Content_OpenByRecord) are in the service request builders.

name: Svc_Ipc_SendRequestWithByteArg
signature: Result Svc_Ipc_SendRequestWithByteArg(Handle session, u8* out, u8 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: IPC request wrapper that fills three normal parameters (byte + two words) in the TLS command buffer, reads the command header from a global, issues svcSendSyncRequest and returns the response code with the reply byte copied to *out.
evidence: Body: TLS+0x80 = g_00501e58 ; TLS+0x84 = arg2(u8) ; TLS+0x88 = arg3 ; TLS+0x8c = arg4 ; r0 = *g_00501e5c ; svc #0x32 ; *out = [TLS+0x88] ; return [TLS+0x84]. Same skeleton as 0x00501F40 (different header literal).

name: Svc_Ipc_SendBufferedRequest
signature: Result Svc_Ipc_SendBufferedRequest(u32* out, u32 session, int count, u8 flags, u32 arg5, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Full IPC request builder: writes five normal parameters plus a static-buffer descriptor whose header encodes count*0x180 bytes with flags 0x0C at TLS+0x98, issues svcSendSyncRequest and writes back the reply.
evidence: Body: TLS+0x80 = g_00501ec8 ; TLS+0x84 = arg3 ; TLS+0x88 = arg4 ; TLS+0x8c = arg5 ; TLS+0x90 = arg6 ; TLS+0x94 = arg7 ; TLS+0x98 = arg3*0x180|0xc ; TLS+0x9c = arg2 ; r0 = *g_00501ecc ; svc #0x32 ; *out = [TLS+0x88].

name: Svc_Ipc_SendThreeParams
signature: int Svc_Ipc_SendThreeParams(int handle, unsigned char cmdHigh, int arg3, int count)
summary: Generic IPC request sender: writes the request header (handle, command byte, three parameters and the translate descriptors) into the TLS command buffer and issues svcSendSyncRequest (svc 0x32).
evidence: The caller is now Fs_BuildRequestArgs, and the TLS+0x80..0x98 header plus the 0x180-scaled translate descriptors are unchanged.

name: Svc_Ipc_SendRequestWithArg
signature: Result Svc_Ipc_SendRequestWithArg(Handle session, u8* out, u8 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)

name: Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007
signature: int Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007(void* out, int requestPtr, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5, int arg6, int arg7)
summary: Fixed-command IPC stub: writes the constant header 0x10070102 (command 0x1007) plus the five arguments into the TLS request buffer, sends svcSendSyncRequest and, on success, copies the two result words back to the caller.
evidence: literal 0x10070102 stored at TLS+0x80 immediately before software_interrupt(0x32); result words read from TLS+0x84/+0x88; same header/idiom as the Svc_Ipc_Send* family named by N_081/N_083.

name: Svc_Ipc_SendRequestQuery

name: maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService
signature: void maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService(FsRequest* req, int service, int method)
summary: Issues a service-object call for a file request and waits on the completion gate: a negative result is formatted into the request, otherwise it clears the request and spins until the service publishes its reply.
evidence: The callers (Fs_Request_Build, Svc_AcClient_Cmd0004) and callees (Svc_Object_InvokeAndStoreResult, Fs_FormatResultCode) fit the 'invoke then wait' reading, but the wait loop itself decompiled to bad instruction data with 25 unreachable blocks, so the wait condition cannot be read.

name: Fs_FormatResultCode
signature: void Fs_FormatResultCode(FsResult* out, unsigned int resultCode, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Decodes a 3DS result code (module in bits 10..17, description in bits 0..9) and writes a human-readable form into the caller's result record; the 0xD000 module is the file-service module, whose 100..299 range is treated as a retryable status rather than a failure.
evidence: masks arg2 with 0x3FC00 (module) and 0x3FF (description) and switches on module 0xD000 with the 100..299 sub-range; called from eight request paths (0x502128, 0x502650, 0x503298, 0x503888, 0x503A7C, 0x503B78, 0x5024A8, 0x65564C); companion 0x502DE0 tests module 0x4400, i.e. the same result-code scheme N_082 documented for the save/file jobs.

name: maybe_Fs_ResultCodeInteriorA
summary: Disassembly artifact: interior basic block within Fs_FormatResultCode (0x00502038) mapping filesystem error codes.
evidence: Disassembly shows ARM 32-bit instruction at 0x005022A4 spans into this address; interior artifact within Fs_FormatResultCode; kept as maybe_ marker.

name: maybe_Fs_ResultCodeInteriorB
summary: Disassembly artifact: second interior branch block within Fs_FormatResultCode.
evidence: Interior instruction boundary of 32-bit ARM instruction at 0x005022E4 within Fs_FormatResultCode; kept as maybe_ marker.

name: Svc_Content_OpenByRecord
signature: void Svc_Content_OpenByRecord(FsResult* out, int* state, int* record)
summary: Opens a content object described by a record: releases any previous object, rejects records flagged in byte +5, then dispatches on the kind byte +6 to build the open request (0x00503D20) and the path (Fs_BuildMetaDataContentPath) before creating the object with maybe_Svc_Ipc_CreateObjectFromBlock.
evidence: The kind switch on record+6 plus the named callees maybe_Svc_Ipc_CreateObjectFromBlock / Fs_BuildMetaDataContentPath match the 'open the content described by this record' reading; the failed-open path returns through Fs_FormatResultCode.

name: Fs_BuildContentInfoArchivePath
summary: Builds the content-info archive file name for a content record: formats "__ContentInfoArchive__%s_%s.bin" from the record's two id fields, converts it to UTF-16 and stores the result for the file request.
evidence: inline format string "__ContentInfoArchive__%s_%s.bin" at 0x502900; ids taken from rec+0x12 and rec+0x4A and mapped through 0x50D8E4/0x50D934; std_mbstowcs (0x1005F6) converts the formatted name.

name: Fs_BuildMetaDataContentPath
summary: Formats the fixed meta-data content header name "__MetaDataContentHeader.bin" and converts it to the UTF-16 form used by the file service.
evidence: inline string "__MetaDataContentHeader.bin" at 0x502B70 passed to 0x51BA9C (std::string format) then std_mbstowcs (0x1005F6) and std_U16StrLen (0x100B74); called from the content open path 0x5024A8.

name: Fs_ReleaseHandlePair
summary: Releases a pair of file/directory handles: if either word of the pair is non-zero it tears the pair down through 0x00503D20 and clears both words.
evidence: Body identical to 0x00502BD0 (arg1[1] and *arg1 zeroed after bl 0x00503D20). Lives in the Fs client block that also contains Fs_FormatResultCode (0x00502164) and Svc_Ipc_Send080D0144 (0x005059EC).

name: Fs_MapResultCode
summary: Closes an Fs handle pair and normalises the service result: each of the eight error codes handled here is tail-branched into Fs_FormatResultCode (0x00502164) before returning.
evidence: Body: bl 0x00503D20 ; clear pair ; eight 'b 0x00502164' tail branches (Fs_FormatResultCode). Same body as 0x00502B90 but with the code mapping cases.

name: maybe_Svc_Content_TranslateResultList
summary: Translates an array of 8-byte service result entries into engine status codes by switching on each entry's kind byte (+4): 0 -> 0x8C, 1 -> 0x0D, 3 -> 0x10, 4 -> 0x30, and builds the per-entry payload word.
evidence: The caller is Fs_BuildRequestArgs and the callees are Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk/Fs_FillRequestBlock, which match the file-service result path; the body still carries damaged register/flag values (unaff_r8/in_NG) so the per-entry mapping cannot be fully verified and maybe_ stays.

name: Fs_CheckPendingResult
summary: Polls the last file-service result and returns the retry code only when it belongs to the file-service module (0x4400) with description 100..0xB3; anything else means "nothing pending".
evidence: The callers are now Fs_BuildRequestArgs, Fs_BuildReadRequestArgs and maybe_Fs_SubmitReadRequest, i.e. the file-service request builders; the 0x4400 module filter is unchanged.

name: Svc_Content_ResolveEntryType
signature: int Svc_Content_ResolveEntryType(ContentEntryTable* table, int arg2, int arg3, int kind)
summary: Resolves one content-table entry (0x00503214/0x00503100) and turns its type word (f_10 low byte) into the request code 0x8C/0xD/0x10/0x30, packs the entry bytes plus arg2 into the shared request block at 0x007D0000 and submits it.
evidence: New context: the request buffer helpers are now named (maybe_Sound_BufferWork_Init for 0x007D0000, func_0051BA18 for the response) and the callers are the Fs read-request builders.

name: Snd_RequestArchiveEntry
signature: int Snd_RequestArchiveEntry(ContentEntry* entry, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Formats a 16-hex-digit id from an entry record (kind 0/1/3/4 -> 0x8C/0x0D/0x10/0x30 plus the packed id/type word) and sends it as the string of the snd:u command-3 request.
evidence: The named callee Svc_Snd_Cmd0003SendString uses the proven 0x007AEAB0 snd:u session, and the '%016llx' format plus the entry fields are explicit; the caller Fs_ValidateRequestEntry hands it a request entry, so the sound-archive request role is established.

name: maybe_Snd_RequestResourceByName
summary: Two-instruction wrapper: calls Svc_Snd_Cmd0004WithName(name) and normalises a non-negative result to 0, so callers see 0 on success. No callers, so which resource kind snd command 4 requests stays open.
evidence: The callee is the named Svc_Snd_Cmd0004WithName (0x00516170), which fixes the subsystem, but the body only normalises the result; the asm at 0x00502FF8 is decoded as Thumb garbage in asm/text, so no caller can be confirmed either way.

name: Svc_Object_InvokeAndStoreResult
summary: Calls the service-object invocation helper with the argument and, on a non-negative result, writes the returned value through the out pointer and normalises the status to 0.
evidence: The callers are now Fs_BuildRequestArgs and maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService, and the callee is named maybe_Svc_Object_InvokeWithArg; the wrapper shape is unchanged.

name: Svc_InvokeAndNormalizeResult
summary: Invokes the shared service object (0x00503264) and normalises a non-negative result to 0 (success), propagating negative result codes unchanged.
evidence: New context: the callee is now maybe_Svc_Object_InvokeWithArg and both callers are the Fs read-request paths that expect 0-or-negative codes.

name: Container_KeyedLookupAndNotify
signature: void Container_KeyedLookupAndNotify(void* owner, int keyA, int keyB)
summary: Looks a two-word key up in the two container lookups and, when either finds it, publishes the request through Fs_PublishRequest.
evidence: The callee is now named Fs_PublishRequest and the callers are Fs_BuildReadRequestArgs / maybe_Fs_SubmitReadRequest; the two 2-word key lookups are unchanged.

name: Fs_FillRequestBlock
signature: int Fs_FillRequestBlock(int* counter, int* outCounter, int cmd, int len, void* data, * void* extra)
summary: Fills the shared Fs request block: bumps the generation counter, stores command 0x40 and the length, copies the 0x40-byte payload and the 0x44-byte argument record, and publishes the new generation.
evidence: The caller is now Fs_BuildRequestArgs, and the static 0x7E8044 block is the same one 0x5031CC uses; the two memcpy sizes are unchanged.

name: Fs_NoOp
summary: Empty stub (a single bx lr, padded to 0x1E bytes) that exists so a virtual or dispatch-table slot has an address.
evidence: The body really is one return instruction, so 'no-op' is not a guess; only which table slot it fills is unknown, hence 0.50 and not higher.

name: Fs_PublishRequest
summary: Publishes a completed request to the file service: bumps the request generation counter in the shared 0x7E8044 block and copies the 0x9C-byte request record into it.
evidence: increments *func_00503214() and memcpy 0x9C bytes into g_00503210 (0x7E8044); callers Fs_FileJob_Update (0x2EB658) and Fs_FileJob_UpdateAlt (0x408D38) - the two async file-job state machines named by N_082.

name: Fs_ValidateRequestEntry
signature: int Fs_ValidateRequestEntry(int* request, int arg2, int arg3, int kind)
summary: Resolves a request entry through the shared service object and validates it, returning 0 on success or the first error code.
evidence: The caller is now Fs_BuildRequestArgs and the callee chain now carries the named maybe_Fs_TranslateEntryType, which is the same 0x502F24/0x502FF4 validation sequence.

name: Svc_Object_InvokeWithArg
signature: int Svc_Object_InvokeWithArg(unsigned arg1, unsigned* arg2, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4)
summary: Invokes one method on the shared service object: resolves the object with 0x00503214 and dispatches 0x00503100(object, &arg, *extra), mapping any non-negative status to 0; the generic 'call the service' wrapper of the fs/content layer.
evidence: Five callers (Fs_FileJob_Update, Fs_FileJob_UpdateAlt, Fs_FileRequest_Update and the two 0x5030xx wrappers) all use it as the single service-call entry, which confirms the wrapper role independent of the unnamed 0x503100 dispatch.

name: Fs_BuildRequestArgs
signature: void Fs_BuildRequestArgs(FsResult* out, int arg2, int* arg3, int* arg4, int arg5, int* args, int argCount)
summary: Serialises up to 0x40 typed arguments into the file-service request format: switches on each argument's kind byte at +4, writes the corresponding value into the 0x7D0000 request buffer and then submits it with the IPC sender 0x501ED4.
evidence: cap '0x40 < argCount' -> Fs_FormatResultCode error; per-argument switch on *(u8*)(arg+4) with stride 8; uses the shared 0x7D0000/0x7D0030 buffers, the IPC stub 0x501ED4 and Fs_PublishRequest (0x5031CC); sole caller maybe_Fs_Request_Build (0x1D0218).

name: Fs_BuildReadRequestArgs
signature: void Fs_BuildReadRequestArgs(FsResult* out, int* request, int arg3, int argCount)
summary: Read-path twin of Fs_BuildRequestArgs: rejects more than 0x40 arguments, resolves the request through 0x503038/0x502E20, copies the 0x9C-byte request and submits the read through the shared buffers.
evidence: same 0x40 argument cap and same result-code error path as 0x503298, but entered from Fs_FileJob_UpdateAlt (0x408D38) and using 0x503038/0x502E20/0x50304C; buffers 0x7D0030/0x7D0000.

name: Fs_FileJob_CompleteRead
summary: Completion step of a file-service job: validates the request through Svc_InvokeAndNormalizeResult/Svc_Content_ResolveEntryType (kind 0xB), copies the 0x44-byte reply out of the service block with std_memcpy, checks the pending-result and object tables and finally publishes the request.
evidence: Its named caller Fs_FileJob_Update passes the result block and the request's +0x20 payload, and the named callees Fs_CheckPendingResult / Container_KeyedLookupAndNotify / Fs_FormatResultCode match the completion step.

name: Fs_BuildRequestHeader
signature: void Fs_BuildRequestHeader(FsRequest* req, int* arg2, int* kindRecord)
summary: Builds the request header for the file service: maps the record's kind byte (+1) 0/1/3 to command 0x8C/0xD/0x10, packs the extra fields and submits the IPC through maybe_Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk / 0x00501ED0, formatting errors with Fs_FormatResultCode.
evidence: The caller Fs_FileRequest_Update and the callee maybe_Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk are confidently named, so the 'build the header of an fs request and submit it' reading is anchored in both directions.

name: maybe_Fs_ReleaseObject
summary: Releases filesystem client object via virtual slot +0x30.
evidence: Decompiled body carries in_ZR flag register (damaged); mid-function fall-through from 0x00503D20; kept maybe_ with low confidence.

name: Svc_ContentObject_CreateAndRegister
signature: int Svc_ContentObject_CreateAndRegister(const char* name, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, * unsigned arg4, unsigned arg5, unsigned arg6, unsigned arg7, unsigned arg8, unsigned arg9, unsigned * arg10)
summary: Creates a content object from the descriptor and registers it under the given 8-character name; when the registration fails the object is released through its vtable +0x30 and the error returned.

name: Svc_ContentObject_GetSharedHandle
signature: unsigned Svc_ContentObject_GetSharedHandle(unsigned mount, unsigned not, unsigned not2, void** out)
summary: Returns the process-wide content handle, creating it once: when the cached handle at 0x007AEA48+8 is null it creates one (0x00505804), registers it under the caller's name and caches it; every caller gets the same status.
evidence: NEW: named callees Fs_RegisterMountByName (0.58) and maybe_Svc_CreateContentHandle (0.42) confirm the create-then-register-once flow, and the cache check is a single guarded store at the global pair 0x007AEA48.

name: Fs_NotifyService
summary: Notifies the Fs service of a pending file/commit event: fetches the pending object (0x006E7310) and passes its handle, size and flags to the named IPC helper Svc_Ipc_Send080D0144.
evidence: New context: the IPC callee is now Svc_Ipc_Send080D0144, so the notify-service reading is anchored on a named sender; the object source 0x006E7310 stays unnamed.

name: Svc_Ipc_FormatAndSend
signature: void Svc_Ipc_FormatAndSend(unsigned arg1, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3)
summary: Formats the two argument strings through the std_FormatV family (0x0051BBD8) and submits one IPC command (Svc_Ipc_SendCommand, 0x00505A58) with the command id from 0x007AEA48+0x10, flags 0x200 and both strings.
evidence: New context: the sender is now named Svc_Ipc_SendCommand and the two callers are the save-migration paths (maybe_Save_MigrateAllSlots/Verify), which matches format-and-send.

name: Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadAt
signature: uint32_t Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadAt(FsEntry* self, uint32_t offset, uint32_t size, uint32_t countOut)
summary: Reads a block at an absolute offset from an open archive entry through 0x00505DE0, raises 0x0011ED40 on error and returns the byte count actually read.
evidence: New context: the callee is now the confident Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadInto, so the wrapper contract (pass self+4, an out count, offset and size; return the count) is pinned.

name: Fs_ArchiveEntry_Seek
summary: Seeks an open archive entry through the three-mode seeker 0x00505E68 and raises through 0x0011ED40 when it reports an error; the paired wrapper of ReadAt.
evidence: New context: 0x00505E68 is now the confident Fs_ArchiveEntry_SeekRelative and the body is only the error-check wrapper, so the name and contract are supported.

name: Svc_Object_ReleaseHandleA
summary: Releases the service object handle at +4: if bit 0 is set the shared lock is released (0x0011C814), then the handle itself is freed (0x00505040) and the word cleared. Returns the object for chaining; identical body to 0x005040A8.
evidence: New context: the three callers are now named save-write paths and the twin 0x005040A8 is the same body, so the release reading is confirmed even though the lock/free helpers stay unnamed.

name: Svc_Object_CreateFromBlock
signature: int Svc_Object_CreateFromBlock(u32* out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 size, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8, u32 arg9, u32 arg10)
summary: Builds a four-word descriptor block {arg2, arg3, arg4, size} on the stack, creates the object through Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor and, on success, writes {handle, -1} to out and returns 0.
evidence: The only caller is Svc_Content_OpenByRecord (0x005025B4) and the only callee is the named Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor (0x00505058), which takes (out, desc, size, flags, ...); the body is exactly the descriptor-block setup plus the {handle,-1} store. The old 'Ipc' word was not supported by anything, so it is dropped.

summary: Second copy of the service-object handle release: if the word at +4 holds a handle it releases the shared lock when bit 0 is set, frees the handle and clears the word. Returns the object for chaining.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x00504018 is now the confident Svc_Object_ReleaseHandleA (0.50) with the same body, and this copy's callers are the same kind of paths (Save_LoadSlotData, Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathA/B), so the 'B' copy is confirmed.

name: Svc_ContentObject_OpenWithRetryCode
signature: unsigned Svc_ContentObject_OpenWithRetryCode(const char* name, unsigned packed, unsigned packed2, unsigned forwarded, unsigned forwarded2, unsigned forwarded3, unsigned forwarded4, unsigned forwarded5, unsigned forwarded6)
summary: Creates a content object from a descriptor, registers it under the given name, and maps the 'busy/try again' error cluster (0x4400 with codes 601..601) to the retry constant 0xC86044C8 so callers retry instead of failing.
evidence: NEW: the creation call is the maybe_Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor (0.4) of this batch and the registration is the named Fs_RegisterMountByName (0.58); the 601..601 code window and the 0xC86044C8 constant are literal, which is exactly the 'retry code' the name claims.

name: Svc_ContentObject_OpenSimple
signature: void Svc_ContentObject_OpenSimple(const char* name, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4, unsigned arg5, unsigned arg6, unsigned arg7, unsigned arg8)
summary: Convenience wrapper over the content-object opener 0x005040E4 with the third descriptor word fixed to 0.
evidence: The body is a single forwarder with a literal 0 in the third slot, so the 'simple/open with defaults' contract is exactly what the code shows.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_NotifyByHandle
signature: void maybe_Svc_Object_NotifyByHandle(unsigned int value, unsigned int handle)
summary: Resolves service object pointer by handle via 0x006E7310 and forwards notification value through virtual slot +0x2C.
evidence: Called by Svc_InitSharedState (0x00504268) and save migration paths; resolves handle and dispatches to vtable slot +0x2C; kept maybe_.

name: Svc_ObjectPool_InitA
summary: Initialises one service object pool: stores the slot count in obj+0x10, appends the 0x209-entry block to the pool at 0x007E7AB8 and tells the kernel the pool layout through Svc command 0x90040, panicking on either failure.
evidence: New context: the list callee is now Os_ListAppendNode and the svc call is the named maybe_Os_SvcCommand90040, so the pool-init reading is supported.

name: Svc_InitSharedState
summary: Initialises one shared-state object: sets up the two LightEvents at +0 and +8 (one-shot), locks their embedded light locks, links the object into the shared list at 0x007E7AA4 and acquires shared resource id 0x207 through the service command, panicking on failure.
evidence: The shared-state family is now confirmed by Svc_ReleaseSharedState (0x005042F8, 0.5) and the Svc_ObjectPool_InitA/B siblings; this is the matching init path called from Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor. The decompilation is damaged only in the two panic-call argument registers (unaff_r4/in_lr); the init sequence itself is intact, as the disassembly-level LightEvent/semaphore calls show, so the confidence is raised to 0.5.

name: Svc_ObjectPool_InitB
summary: Initialises the second service object pool: stores the slot count in obj+0x10, appends id 0x207 to the pool list at 0x007E7AA4 and tells the kernel the pool layout through Svc command 0x90040, panicking on either failure.
evidence: Byte-identical to the confident Svc_ObjectPool_InitA (0x0050421C) apart from the pool address (0x007E7AA4 vs 0x007E7AB8) and the id (0x207 vs 0x209); both call the named Os_ListAppendNode and Os_SvcCommand90040. Note 0x207 is the registered id, not an entry count as the old summary said.

name: Svc_ReleaseSharedState
summary: Releases one shared-state resource (id 0x209) that the present window acquired: sends the release request, asserts on failure and then frees the free-list entry.
evidence: New context: the confident Svc_ReleaseSharedResources (0x00504324) calls it first and its own comment names this function; the release-request + free-entry pair is confirmed by maybe_Os_ReleaseSharedResource.

name: Svc_ReleaseSharedResources
summary: Releases the two shared GPU/svc resources (0x209 first, then 0x207) that the title screen owns, asserting on the service result.
evidence: Callees are named: maybe_Svc_ReleaseSharedState (0x209) and maybe_Os_ReleaseSharedResource (0x207) - so these are shared *resources*, not 'state'. The Ghidra body is damaged/truncated at the padding `mov r0,r0`; the disassembly asm/text/text_00500048.s shows 0x00504324 = push {r4,lr}; bl #0x5042f8; pop {r4,lr}, then the fall-through block at 0x00504334 loads the 0x207 literal at 0x0050435C, calls 0x51a6c4, asserts through 0x11ed40 and tail-branches to 0x51a5e4. The only caller is the named Ui_TitleScreen_Dtor.

name: maybe_Svc_ObjectPool_DestroyB
summary: Releases shared IPC resource pool 0x207 via Os_Ipc_SendRequestA0040 and Svc_UnlinkSharedEntry.
evidence: Destroys resource pool 0x207 counterpart to pool 0x209 cleanup; called during text/service shutdown; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_CreateWithPayload
signature: int maybe_Svc_Object_CreateWithPayload(u32* outSize, u32 packed, u32 low, u32 forwarded, int count1, int count2, int withHeader)
summary: Creates a service object for a payload made of count1 0x20-byte and count2 0x18-byte records: sends the create request with header 0x0004008C, takes a vtable-0x00780EAC object from the pool and optionally queries its 0x28-byte header, returning the computed payload size in *outSize.

signature: void Svc_Object_CreateSimple(u32* outSize, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 count1, u32 count2, int withHeader)
summary: One-line forwarder to the object creator 0x00504378 with the third argument fixed to 0, for callers that need no extra flag word.

name: Svc_FetchContentInfo
summary: Queries the service for a small content-info record (command 0x0C with a 3-word descriptor) and, when the reply carries data, creates the "icon" object and asks it for the record; used by the icon cache.
evidence: The callers are now maybe_Svc_Cecd_QueryRawFile and maybe_Ui_IconCache_IsContentReady, and the 0x6E6F6369 ("icon") tag plus the 0x080C00C2 header are unchanged.

name: Fs_ArchiveStream_ReadAt
signature: int Fs_ArchiveStream_ReadAt(void* streamObj, s64 offset, void* dstBuf, u32 size)
summary: Reads size bytes at 64-bit byte offset from an archive backing buffer or substream into dstBuf: copies directly via __aeabi_memcpy (0x00116A14) when streamObj->directBuf_00 != NULL, or dispatches IReadStream::TryRead on streamObj->f_08 (+0x0C + bucket*4) at streamObj->baseOffset_0C + (u32)offset, returning 0 on success or negative nn::Result.
evidence: CRITICAL: READS into dstBuf, NOT writes! ARM EABI passes s64 offset in r2:r3 (skipping r1), dstBuf at [sp+0x18] (ip), size at [sp+0x1C] (r2). At 0x504804: r1 = directBuf + (u32)offset (src), r0 = ip (dstBuf), bl 0x116A14 (__aeabi_memcpy(dst, src, size))! Otherwise calls reader->vt[0](reader, &actualRead, base+offset, 0, dstBuf, size). All 8 call sites in Fs_Archive_FindDirectory, ReadDirectoryEntry, and FindFile read archive metadata/names into stack buffers.

name: Fs_File_SelectWorkerByPriority
summary: Maps an I/O priority in [-8..8] to one of five cached worker objects (indices 0..4 at self+0xC) and lazily creates the missing worker through the session's vtable slots 0x44/0x3C, then selects the priority on it (slot 0x18) and remembers it in self+0x18.
evidence: Ghidra C: bucket = (p==0)?2 : (p<0 ? (p<-8?0:1) : (p<9?3:4)); if (piVar2[bucket+3]==0) { get size via vtable 0x44; create via vtable 0x3c; sel->vtable[0x18](sel,p) ; piVar2[bucket+3] = sel; } ; arg1->f_18 = p.

name: Svc_Object_Release

evidence: Ghidra C: uVar2 = *(u32*)(self+8); uVar3 = self->f_10 - uVar2 (remaining); iVar4 = f_14 - (f_c + borrow); prioritises self->f_18 into 0..4; puVar1 = *(u32**)(*(int*)(self+4) + iVar4*4 + 0xc) ; (**(code**)*puVar1)(puVar1, arg2, arg3+uVar2, arg4+f_c+carry, arg5, arg6).

name: maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath(void* self, u32* out, int* typeAndIndex)

Returns 0 or the Fs error code.
evidence: The body is entirely archive path/hash/lookup work (Fs_Archive_ResolvePath, Fs_Archive_FindFile, Fs_Archive_FindDirectory) plus the pool node with vtable 0x00780E18; there is no service-content API in it, so the Svc_Content_ prefix was unsupported and the new name states what is actually opened.

name: Fs_SimulateReadLatency

evidence: New context: both callers (Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadBlock, Fs_Object_ReadChunk) are now named and call it immediately before the physical/virtual read, and the body multiplies by 1,000,000 ns and calls the sleep helper 0x0011CC94.
