signature: void Gfx_VertexStream_WriteQuantizedColors(int self, u32 channelShift, float* values, u32 flags)
summary: Quantises 256 float channel values into saturated 8-bit samples, inserts each byte into one lane of two 0x82-word vertex blocks and marks the block dirty; used to bake per-vertex colour data into the GPU stream.
evidence: Its named caller maybe_Gfx_VertexStream_BuildColorDeltas (0x00508740) first builds the 256-entry delta table and then calls it with a channel shift, and the body performs the 2 x 0x80-sample loop with the 1.0/255.0 saturation constants - the colour quantisation contract is now supported by both sides.

name: Gfx_Lighting_BuildLutDeltas
signature: void Gfx_Lighting_BuildLutDeltas(u32 self, u32 channelShift, float* values, u32 forwarded)
summary: Constructs 256 consecutive difference/derivative samples from a floating-point table and passes them to Gfx_VertexStream_WriteQuantizedColors to configure PICA200 lighting lookup tables.
evidence: Callee Gfx_VertexStream_WriteQuantizedColors (0x0050857C) writes PICA200 GPU registers 0x00AF (GPUREG_LIGHTING_LUT_INDEX) and 0x00B0 (GPUREG_LIGHTING_LUT_DATA). PICA200 hardware encodes 256-sample lighting LUTs as difference/slope deltas between successive samples (values[i+1] - values[i]). Called by Gfx_MaterialState_WriteConstants (0x00659C24).

name: Gfx_BuildVertexFormatDescriptor
summary: Builds the PICA200 vertex-attribute block: attribute-buffer headers at 0x0201/0x0203, a 0x98-byte cleared region, twelve FIXEDATTRIB_INDEX entries (register 0x0232, index 0..11) and the chained sub-descriptors, returning the final descriptor.
evidence: The command words write registers 0x0201/0x0203 and 0x0232 with mask 0x3F - the PICA200 vertex-attribute command set listed in FACTS.md - and there are exactly 12 attribute entries. The four builder helpers and 15 draw-path callers are named.

name: Gfx_CommandBuffer_AppendBlock
signature: void Gfx_CommandBuffer_AppendBlock(GfxCommandBuffer* buf, int size, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Appends a block to the growing GPU command buffer: grows the buffer with 0x508B9C (keeping the 0x18-byte header aligned to 4), writes the payload with 0x508BE8, then patches the relative pointer of the previous block and optionally emits the flush record.
evidence: nine callers, all in the 0x65Axxx-0x65Cxxx Gfx command builders; (iVar1 - arg1[2] & 0xFFFFFFFC) + 0x18 is the alignment+header size; *(u32*)arg1[3] = (new - base) >> 3 is the GPU relative-pointer encoding used by the PICA200 command lists.

name: Gfx_CommandBuffer_InitPair
signature: unsigned int* Gfx_CommandBuffer_InitPair(GfxCommandBuffer* buf, unsigned int** out, int address, int arg4)
summary: Initialises a two-address GPU descriptor: stores the caller's words, translates the source address and the following record to physical addresses, shifts them right by 3 (PICA200 address encoding) and marks the pair valid.
evidence: Two Os_VirtualToPhysical calls followed by >>3 stores at +0xC/+0x10 is the standard PICA200 command encoding; no direct callers because it is invoked through a function table.

name: maybe_Gfx_DrawState_InitDefaults
summary: Default-initialises a 0x40-byte GPU draw-state block: runs the 12-element fixed-array default init at +4 (empty element ctor 0x006E7B38) and zero-fills the block so draw passes only override the fields they use.
evidence: The real entry is 0x005090F0 and this address is 0x10 bytes inside it, so the name is an alias of the range; the readable body is empty. The three named textured-draw passes (0x00567638/0x00568C90/0x00569450) call 0x005090F0 with a local 0x40-byte state, which still supports the default-init role.

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_ApplyFormat
signature: void Gfx_ResourceSet_ApplyFormat(GfxResourceSet* self, int* record, int arg3, int kind)
summary: Maps a resource kind (0/1/2/3/4/5/6) to the element size used when registering the resource in the set (through 0x508FE4) and stores the count byte at record+2.
evidence: The callers are now named (Gfx_ModelResource_Parse, Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource) and the kind-to-size switch feeds the same registry helper as the sibling loaders, so the format-application reading holds.

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_SetSlot
signature: void Gfx_ResourceSet_SetSlot(GfxResourceSet* self, int* record, int value, unsigned int* src)
summary: Stores one resource slot: marks the present byte at +0x154+index, writes the five-word descriptor at +0x1A8+index*5 (from src or the default descriptor 0x0072FC2C) and registers the slot through 0x00508FE4.
evidence: The caller Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource is confident and the body's present-byte + 5-word descriptor write is exactly a per-slot store; the default descriptor at 0x72FC2C is used when src is null.

name: Gfx_Material_BindTextureSlots
signature: void Gfx_Material_BindTextureSlots(Gfx_Material* material, const TextureSetRecord* set, unsigned pageId)
summary: Fills a material's twelve texture slots from a texture-set record: finds the first free 0x1C-byte slot, binds each texture, records its type code and converts the format byte to a texel size (1/2/3/4/6/8/0xC/0x10).
evidence: Corrected to say it binds the material's slots (the object is the material; the loop finds a free slot at material[i*0x1c+0x58] and marks material+0x154+index). Callers are now six: the model-instance draw paths, Gfx_CmdBuf_AppendCommandList and the overlay sprite draw, so a generic 'bind texture set' name was misleading. Named context in the merged C: Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureAndDraw.

name: maybe_Gfx_Object_CtorFlags12
summary: Stores the owner word at +0 and default-constructs twelve one-byte flags at +4 with the empty element stub 0x006E7B38.
evidence: No caller; 0x006E7B38 is the empty `bx lr` stub also used by the draw-state default init, which is the only Gfx link. The 12-flag shape is certain, the class is not.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_ConstructPassSlots
summary: Default-constructs the twelve 0x70-byte per-pass slots of a model instance at +0x160 via std_ConstructArray.
evidence: Body is a single std_ConstructArray call; renamed from 'CtorPassSlots' to the verb form used elsewhere in the project. Callers are the draw paths that lazily initialise a pass slot. Named context in the merged C: Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureAndDraw, std_ConstructArray.

name: Gfx_CommandNode_BuildChain4
summary: Builds a chain of four GPU state nodes from the pool: marks the head with command 5, links each node to its predecessor and stores the caller's pointer in the tail node, returning the head.
evidence: Four 0x5095E4 pool allocations with f_1C=5, f_20=parent, f_24=next; twenty callers, all the Gfx_ModelInstance draw passes. Named context in the merged C: Gfx_CharShadowPass_BuildCommands, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteBlendingRegisters, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteTextureSamplerConfig, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteUniformFloats, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteVertexAttributes.

name: maybe_Container_DefaultInit3x3
summary: Default-constructs three consecutive three-element byte arrays (at offsets 0, +3 and +6) with the empty element stubs and returns the object base.
evidence: Disassembly (0x005096C8) shows three consecutive std_ConstructArray calls with stride 1/count 3 at offsets 0, +3 and +6, followed by the base adjustment and pop {r4,pc}. No caller and no element behaviour (the ctors are empty stubs), so only the 3x3 shape is proven; the doc header’s claim that the real entry is 0x10 bytes earlier is not visible in this listing.

name: Gfx_CommandNode_InitSixSlots
summary: Default-constructs six 0x18-byte GPU state nodes in place (element ctor 0x5096B8); companion of 0x509638, which builds the same nodes as a chain.
evidence: Exactly six std_ConstructArray elements of 0x18 bytes with ctor 0x5096B8, and 27 callers, all named Gfx_ModelInstance draw/bind passes that also use the chain builder 0x509638.

name: Gfx_Movie_SubmitReadRequest
signature: void Gfx_Movie_SubmitReadRequest(u32 bufHi, u32 bufLo, int size, u8 flag)
summary: Assembles the four-word movie read request (buffer, buffer high word, size, flag) and submits it to the async archive read helper 0x00125614 with the completion callback 0x00125D84; sizes below 0xB take the stack-array path whose continuation was lost.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Gfx_Movie_ReadThread (0x00500ABC), which waits on the two handles at self+0x68 and consumes exactly this request; the request/callback pair 0x00125614/0x00125D84 is complete and visible.

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyA
summary: Destructor: unlinks the object through Os_CloseHandleAndUnlink(self), then closes the kernel handle at +0x14 (svcCloseHandle) and clears it, returning the object.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00509A20-0x00509A48: bl 0x111e44 with r0=self, ldr r0,[r4,#0x14]!, svc #0x23, str #0, sub r0,r4,#0x14. The close-and-clear shape is certain, but nothing in the body identifies the primitive as a sync object, so the old hypothesis stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Fs_StartAsyncRead
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_StartAsyncRead(int self, u32 handle, u32 length, u32 destination, u32 flags)
summary: Starts a read on an already-open handle: requires a 0x1000-aligned length and an idle object, stores the handle, sets the wait flag from bit 1 of flags, issues svc 0x1F on the handle and marks the request done on success.
evidence: The only caller is the thunk Fs_StartAsyncReadThunk, so the name is circular, and the body issues svc 0x1F (the blocking-wait slot of the CTR SVC table, between svcClearEvent 0x1E and svcWaitSynchronizationN 0x20) on the stored handle - so 'start async' may overclaim. The 0x1000 length alignment and the done flag at +0x18 are the hard facts.

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyB
summary: Destroys the second kind of synchronisation object: closes its kernel handle with Os_CloseHandle, then closes the remaining handle with svcCloseHandle and clears the stored handle field; returns the object.
evidence: The sibling 0x00509A20 has the same shape with a different close helper and both are waited on together by the content-cache code at 0x0050A714; which primitive each object kind represents (event vs condition) is still unknown.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_ReleaseHandles
summary: Destroys two kernel handles held in self via svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) and restores default vtable 0x00741A74.
evidence: Closes kernel handles via svc 0x23 and resets vtable; owner class remains unnamed; kept maybe_.

name: Svc_HandleSlot_CloseA
summary: Closes the handle in *slot through svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23) and stores 0; returns the slot for chaining.
evidence: if (*arg1 != 0) { software_interrupt(0x23); *arg1 = 0; } return arg1; identical in shape to 0x00509BFC and 0x0050F1A0.

name: Svc_HandleSlot_CloseB
summary: Second, byte-identical close-and-clear helper used for a different handle slot; kept separate by the original code layout.
evidence: Same 0x28-byte body as 0x00509BD4 (svc #0x23 + clear + return arg1); separate entry point at 0x00509BFC.

name: Svc_CloseHandleSlot
summary: Closes the kernel handle stored in *handleSlot when it is non-zero (pre-close sync helper then svcCloseHandle) and clears the slot; returns the slot so callers can chain.
evidence: The two-line shape is the SDK close-handle idiom confirmed at 0x00517E10 (two identical blocks) and used by the named Os close-handle helpers; svc #0x23 is svcCloseHandle, so both the verb and the handle-slot layout are corroborated.

name: Os_CreateEventHandle
summary: Creates an anonymous kernel event handle if *cachedHandle is 0, storing the resulting handle in *cachedHandle.
evidence: Caller 0x005018E8 (Svc_AcClient_Close) creates an event with this helper, passes it to Svc_AcClient_CloseAsync (0x005019AC), waits on it with svc 0x24 (svcWaitSynchronization1), and closes it with svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle). Thread IDs cannot be waited on or closed with svcCloseHandle; the handle is a synchronization event initialized via callee 0x0012038C.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_Load
summary: Loads the shared icon atlas once: guards on the global loaded byte, runs the texture-open sequence (0x0050C22C/0x0050C520/0x0050C4E4), reads the atlas format byte and marks the global state as loaded.
evidence: Only caller is 0x00383764 (Ui_LoadIconTextures, named in an earlier batch); g_00509D3C is a small state record (*g==0 'not loaded', [1] 'opening', [4] atlas format); 0x0010C694/0x0010BDF8/0x0010BE20 are the CTR texture-load calls; neighbouring functions 0x0050C11C/0x0050C4E4 handle the same state record.

name: Ui_IconCache_OpenService
summary: Starts the icon/atlas service once: skips when already started, opens 'cecd:u', waits for the atlas load, acquires the shared atlas context/session, records the cache mode byte and marks the global state started.
evidence: Four named callees now pin it: Svc_Cecd_OpenService, Ui_IconAtlas_WaitForLoad, maybe_Ui_AcquireAtlasContext and Os_AcquireSharedSession - the once-only guard on g_00509D3C is the only extra state.

name: Svc_Cecd_EnsureReady
summary: Makes sure the cecd content session is up before a create/read/write: starts the service (0x0050F2A4), sleeps 16 ms, then either sends the 0x0B/0x0C request once or polls up to 60 times while the change-state event is pending.
evidence: All nine callers are the cecd wrappers Svc_Cecd_*WithRetry plus maybe_Ui_IconCache_OpenWithRetry, each calling Svc_Cecd_EnsureReady(1,0) immediately before its service request.

name: Ui_IconCache_ReleaseService
summary: Releases the icon-cache service: takes the monitor lock 0x007E7948, sends the stop command 0x0E when `force` is set, releases the service object (0x0050F284) and clears the 'started' byte when it was running, and always unlocks. Returns the state/error word it observed.
evidence: Six named callers use it symmetrically with the acquire side - Ui_IconAtlas_Close, Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread, and the icon-cache open/close/create functions - which pins the class (icon cache) and the role (stop/release the shared service). Only the exact return-value meaning is unclear.

name: Svc_Cecd_GetChangeStateEvent
summary: Retrieves the CECD state change notification event handle into *out by dispatching through Svc_Cecd session selector 0x0050C5C4.
evidence: Callee 0x0050C5C4 checks active CECD handles (*0x007B005C / *0x007B0058) and calls either Svc_Cecd_GetChangeStateEventHandle (0x0050C888) or secondary handler Svc_Cecd_GetChangeStateEventHandleB (0x0050CDC0), returning the event handle to the caller.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_StartService
summary: Starts the icon-cache service once: when the state block 0x007AE9E0 says 'opened but not started' it takes the 0x007E7948 lock, calls 0x0050F2A4(0), waits 16,000,000 ticks (~60 ms), marks 0x007AE9E0+2 started and unlocks. It never polls for readiness.
evidence: The surrounding family is confidently Ui_IconCache_* (Ui_IconCache_OpenService/StopService/Open/Close/RequestPage) and this function only starts and marks the service; 'Deferred' implied a later poll that does not exist.

name: Ui_IconCache_StopService
summary: Stops the icon-cache service: drops the start reference (Svc_RefCount_Release), clears the started bytes, asks the protocol layer to close (0x0050C4C0), resets the mailbox (Svc_Cecd_ResetMailbox) and clears the global 'opened' byte at 0x007AE9E0.
evidence: It is the exact counterpart of the named maybe_Ui_IconCache_StartService (0x0050A010): same state block 0x007AE9E0, same lock, and it clears the +1/+2 bytes that StartService sets before clearing the +0 opened byte; the caller Gfx_ShutdownRenderServices (0x00383EC8) is the render-service shutdown path that owns the icon atlas.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries
signature: int maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries(UiIconCache* self, UiIconPage* page, int* outPtrs, u32 size, int pageIndex)
summary: Reads one icon-cache page: queries the size for page index 0/1 through the object's +8 vtable, allocates/locks the matching page buffer (self[0xEA] or self[0x156]), copies the 0x20-byte page header into page, validates the 0x6060 entry tag and the object id, and writes the pointers of the 0x70-byte entries into outPtrs.
evidence: All callers are now named Ui_IconCache_Open/RequestPage/WriteEntry and the body's page-index-0/1 state block (0x007AE9E5+3/+4) matches the same cache subsystem; it reads a page and validates its entries rather than only 'headers', but the page layout itself is still inferred.

name: maybe_Fs_InvokeReadEntryPoint
signature: int maybe_Fs_InvokeReadEntryPoint(int* self, u32 forwarded, u32 forwarded2, int mode)
summary: Invokes virtual slot +0x14 on self and returns error code 0xC8810BEF.
evidence: Both mode branches perform the identical virtual dispatch; no callers exist in the codebase; kept maybe_.

name: Ui_IconCache_WriteEntry
signature: int Ui_IconCache_WriteEntry(UiIconCache* self, void* out, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5, int arg6)
summary: Serialises one icon-cache entry: prepares/validates it with 0x50A520 and, when that succeeds, writes the raw block through maybe_Ui_IconCache_WriteRawBlock.
evidence: The guard on the prepare result and the single named writer call at the tail leave no other plausible role, and the caller is in the icon-cache consumer range.

name: Ui_IconCache_RequestPage
signature: int Ui_IconCache_RequestPage(UiIconCache* self, int pageIndex, u32 size)
summary: Issues the read request for one of the two icon-cache pages (command 0x14 with page flag 3 or 4) and then parses the reply into the page's entry-header arrays, clearing the page's 'dirty/valid' byte.
evidence: New context: the confident Ui_IconCache_Close, Ui_IconCache_SetPage and Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry all call it per page and ignore the result, exactly as a page-refresh helper should.

name: Ui_IconCache_CommitEntryThunk
summary: Tiny thunk that jumps straight to Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry (0x0050A714); exists only so a vtable/table slot can point at a distinct address.
evidence: Body is a single call to 0x0050A714, which N_007 named Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry.

name: Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry
signature: int Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry(void * self, void * entry, u32 slot, u32 flags, int arg5)
summary: Commits one icon-cache entry: takes the monitor lock, resolves the entry's timestamp, writes the entry record and its page through the service helpers, then unlocks and notifies the waiting worker.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntryThunk is now confident and the callees include the confident Os_LockMonitor, Field_Clock_ConvertTimestamp and std_String_InitEmpty; the surrounding cluster is a fully named icon-cache service (RequestIcon, FetchIcon, ReadEntryTable).

name: Ui_IconCache_Open
signature: int Ui_IconCache_Open(UiIconCache* self, u32 recordId, int expectedCount)
summary: Opens the icon cache for one content record: starts the worker service, looks the record up, rejects a count mismatch, reads both entry-header tables and the entry table, stores the current timestamp and returns 0 (or the lookup error/0xC8810BEA on mismatch).
evidence: Every failure path now goes through named helpers (maybe_Ui_IconCache_Close, maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReleaseService, maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryHeaders/Table), and the two named callers are the icon-texture loaders; the error-return contract makes the 'open' role explicit.

name: Ui_IconCache_Close
summary: Closes the icon cache: writes back both pages (0x18C bytes each), drops the record handle, wipes the page structures and the two temporary buffers, and - when the argument is 0 - also releases the service reference and clears the global state flags.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Ui_IconCache_RequestPage and maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReleaseService are the two halves of the body, and the 0x18C/0x318 buffer sizes plus the 0x6262/0x6767 empty-page magic match the page loader 0x0050A100. The argument only selects "flush and release" vs. "flush only".

name: Svc_Cecd_OpenRawWithRetry
signature: void Svc_Cecd_OpenRawWithRetry(u32 self, u32 id, u32 size, void* buffer, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Opens a raw CECD file through Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile and, on 0xC8A10BF0 'not started', starts the service, sets the retry byte at 0x007AE9E6 and retries the open once.
evidence: The callee is the named Cecd command-0x03 open wrapper (0x0050C328), so the previous Ui_IconCache prefix was wrong. The disassembly shows r0 is a discarded vtable self and the seven following register/stack values are forwarded unchanged.

name: Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryTable
summary: Reads the small index block (service command 0x05): asks for its size, allocates 800 bytes, verifies the 0x6767 magic and the declared count, converts the 8-byte entries into pointers at +0x159 and returns the number of entries.
evidence: Its four callers are the icon-cache cluster (Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry, Ui_IconCache_Open, Ui_IconCache_Create, Ui_IconCache_SetPage), which pins the service even though those caller names are themselves still low-confidence; the 0x6767 magic and the (size-8)>>3 count check in the body are exactly an entry-table reader.

name: Ui_IconCache_Create
signature: int Ui_IconCache_Create(UiIconCache* self, u32 recordId, int stored, int must, u32 size1, u32 size2, u32 count1, u32 count2, u32 max1, u32 max2, u32 max3, u32 max4, u32 max5)
summary: Creates the two icon pages of a record: validates the size/count limits (0x100000 bytes, 99 entries, 0x19000), sends commands 0x0B/0x0C/0x0D through the object's vtable, reads the two page headers and the entry table, then stores the record id and the current timestamp. Returns 0 on success.
evidence: NEW: five named callees of the same class (Ui_IconCache_Close 0.55, Ui_IconCache_Commit 0.5, Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryTable 0.55, maybe_Ui_IconCache_RequestPage 0.42, maybe_Ui_IconCache_CountMatchingEntries) and the named Svc_Time_GetCurrentTimestamp / Field_Clock_ConvertTimestamp pair make the class and the create-then-commit flow reliable; the 'Ui_' prefix is kept because the whole family carries it.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_LoadEntries
summary: Loads the atlas entry table: issues command 0x0B with the entry count, commits the request and closes the object; returns the protocol result. This is the single call the UI screen uses after Ui_IconAtlas_Init.
evidence: The only caller is 0x00383C18 (the icon load stage 2) which pairs it with Ui_IconAtlas_Init (0x0050C11C) and Ui_IconAtlas_Release (0x0050C208); the body is the compact 'vtable +0x24 / 0x0050BD60 / 0x0050AEE4' sequence.

name: Ui_IconCache_CountMatchingEntries
summary: Walks the icon-cache entries (self[6] of them), reads each 0x60-byte record through the vtable read slot (+0x34) and counts the records whose flag byte intersects flagMask (bit 0x80 ignored); a mask of 0 counts every readable record.
evidence: Both call sites are inside Ui_IconCache_Create (0x0050B45C and 0x0050B4DC) with masks 0 and 1, and the body is a pure count loop over self[6] records with the flag test 'bStack_7c & flagMask & 0xFFFFFF7F'; the family (Ui_IconCache_ReadHeader/SetPage/Commit) is already confident.

name: Ui_IconCache_SetPage
summary: Selects and re-reads one of the icon cache's two pages: sends command 0x0D for page 1 or 0x0C for page 0, reads the page header, requests the page block (+0xF3/0x87) and, for page 1, refreshes the entry table.
evidence: The two branches differ only in the command byte and the page pointers, and the trailing calls are the now-named maybe_Ui_IconCache_RequestPage / maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryTable, matching a page switch.

name: Ui_IconCache_StoreRecordByCommand
signature: void Ui_IconCache_StoreRecordByCommand(int* self, int command, u8* data, u32 size)
summary: Handles one cached-record write command: 0x8C..0x8F store a single saved flag byte (+0x77/+0x1DD/+0x1DE/+0x1DF), 0x65..0xC7 forward the payload through the vtable write slot (+0x30, or +0x24 when there is no data), and the 0x60-byte header is then flushed back to the backing handle.
evidence: Both call sites are inside Ui_IconCache_Create (0x0050B724 with blls and 0x0050B78C) and the body dispatches on the command byte exactly as the old summary said; the sibling Ui_IconCache_Commit (0x0050BD60) uses the same vtable slots.

name: Ui_IconCache_ReadHeader
summary: Reads the 0x18C-byte icon-cache header through the object's vtable read slot, validates the 0x6868 magic and every per-entry tag (command 0x0B), then commits the cache and returns the read status.
evidence: NEW: the body reads 0x18C bytes via vtable+0x34, checks the 0x6868 magic at +0x10, walks self[6] entries calling vtable+8 with command 0x0B, and finishes with Ui_IconCache_Commit; the sibling entry points Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry/CountMatchingEntries are already confident names for the same object.

name: Ui_IconCache_Commit
summary: Commits a pending icon-page operation: reads the 8-byte status (command 0x0A), writes the whole 0x18C page buffer with command 0x01 and reads the status back.
evidence: Both the status read (vtable +8, command 0x0A) and the write (vtable +0x30/+0x34 pair with command 0x01 over 0x18C bytes) appear in the caller set 0x0050B3CC/0x0050B824/0x0050BBD8, i.e. every page operation ends with this; "Commit" describes exactly that.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_IsPresent
summary: Probes the cache service through self->vtable+0x2C with two flags, returning the service's status and using maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize to latch whether the requested content is present.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry and the named maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize callee support the cache-presence reading, but the function returns a service status word (not a clean bool) and the two vtable queries are unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: Svc_Cecd_ReadRawWithRetry
signature: void Svc_Cecd_ReadRawWithRetry(u32 self, u32 id, u32 size, u32 destination, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Reads a raw CECD file through Svc_Cecd_ReadRawFile and retries once after starting the service when it returns 0xC8A10BF0.
evidence: The callee is the named command-0x07 raw-read wrapper (0x0050C55C). The disassembly matches the 0x0050BF64 dispatch read retry one-for-one but calls ReadRawFile instead of ReadDispatch, so the distinct Raw name is required (ReadWithRetry already belongs to 0x0050BF64).

name: Svc_Cecd_ReadWithRetry
signature: void Svc_Cecd_ReadWithRetry(u32 self, u32 id, u32 size, u32 destination, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Protocol entry 1 of the CECD service: reads a raw CECD file through Svc_Cecd_ReadDispatch and, when it fails with 0xC8A10BF0, starts the service (0x0050D864 path), sets the retry byte and dispatches once more.
evidence: New context: the dispatcher is now named Svc_Cecd_ReadDispatch and the error/retry pair is visible in the body, confirming the read-with-retry reading.

name: maybe_Svc_Cecd_Cmd0009WithRetry
signature: void maybe_Svc_Cecd_Cmd0009WithRetry(u32 self, u32 value, u32 buffer, int size, u32 flags)
summary: Retry wrapper for CECD command 0x0009: dispatches through 0x0050D050, and on 0xC8A10BF0 starts the service, sets the retry byte and dispatches once more.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x0050D050 shows the callee is the Cmd0009/Cmd0009B session dispatcher (header 0x000900C2 with value, size, flags and buffer), not the delete dispatcher. CECD delete is command 0x11 (Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawFile) and 0x0A (DeleteDispatch), so the old DeleteWithRetry wording was not supported by the command number.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_Close
summary: Closes an icon atlas object: releases the two page buffers, closes the pages, drops the service reference and clears the 'open' byte. Safe on an already closed object.
evidence: Called by Ui_IconAtlas_Release (0x0050C208) and Ui_IconAtlas_Dtor (0x0050C1E0); it calls 0x0050AEE4 and frees the buffers at +0x3A8/+0x558 through 0x0050D634, guarded by the byte flags at 0x007AE9E8/0x007AE9E9.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_Init
summary: Initialises the icon-atlas descriptor: installs vtable 0x00780FC4, clears the atlas state bytes and the 0x21F..0x22E slot array, seeds the two glyph/style constants 0x6262/0x6767 and marks the atlas usable.
evidence: Called from Ui_LoadIconTextures and 0x00383C18; vtable 0x00780FC4; writes the packed constants 0x00006262 and 0x00006767 at +0x7F/+0xEB/+0x157 (two-character codes 'bb'/'gg'); 0x0050C23C decides the 'valid' byte at +9.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the icon atlas: installs the class vtable (0x00780FC4), closes the object and frees the allocation.
evidence: Writes vtable 0x00780FC4 = [0x0050C208, 0x0050C1E0, 0x00658928, 0] then 0x0050C060 + func_0010F6CC (operator delete); it is vtable slot 1 of that class.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_Release
summary: Non-deleting destructor / release of the icon atlas: installs the class vtable and closes the object, returning the same pointer.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x00780FC4 = [0x0050C208, 0x0050C1E0, 0x00658928, 0]; it is the function 0x00383C18 calls after reading the entry table.

name: maybe_Svc_Cecd_ResetMailbox
summary: Resets the CECD state block at 0x007EF020, writing state bytes, clearing message markers, and releasing owned sub-object.
evidence: Manipulates CECD state block 0x007EF020 and flag *0x007AF0E0; mailbox semantics are inferred from 0xFFFFFFFF marker; kept as maybe_.

name: Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile
summary: Opens the raw CECD file: dispatches CECD command 0x03 to whichever of the two session slots is active (Cmd0003 or the B variant) and returns.
evidence: NEW: CECD command numbering (0x03 = Open, 0x07 = Read) plus the confident siblings Svc_Cecd_WriteRawFile (0x50C3CC), Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawFile (0x50C474) and Svc_Cecd_OpenService (0x50C520) put this wrapper in the raw file open/read/write/delete set; its caller is the open-retry wrapper. The two-slot dispatch is only session bookkeeping, not a different operation.

name: Svc_Cecd_WriteRawFile
summary: Wraps CECD command 0x12 (header 0x00120104) for whichever of the two session slots is active.
evidence: The only caller is now maybe_Svc_Cecd_WriteWithRetry, which agrees with the write label, and the 0x12 dispatch is unchanged.

name: Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawFile
summary: Wraps CECD command 0x11 (header 0x00110104) for whichever of the two session slots is active.
evidence: The only caller is now maybe_Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawWithRetry, which agrees with the delete label.

name: Ui_IconAtlas_WaitForLoad
summary: Spin-waits for the icon atlas completion flag (g_007B0058) to become non-zero, sleeping 10 ms (0x00989680 ns) per iteration.
evidence: while (*g_0050C518 == 0) 0x0011CC94(0x00989680, 0); called from Ui_IconAtlas_Load right before the texture-open step; the 10 ms sleep constant is the only immediate.

name: Svc_Cecd_OpenService
summary: Opens the CECD service session ('cecd:u') used by the icon/content cache and stores the handle in the global session slot 0x007B0058.
evidence: The literal at 0x0050C554 is the string 'cecd:u' (verified at 0x007418AC in the image); it is passed through 0x0011CCA0 (strlen) to 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle) after 0x00113430 (GetThreadId guard); callers are Ui_IconAtlas_Load (0x00509CD0) and 0x00509CE0.

name: Svc_Cecd_ReadRawFile
summary: Reads the raw CECD file: dispatches CECD command 0x07 to the active session slot (Cmd0007 or the B variant).
evidence: NEW: CECD command 0x07 = Read, the wrapper sits in the same raw-file block as Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile/WriteRawFile/DeleteRawFile, and its caller is Svc_Cecd_ReadWithRetry (0x50BF64). Only the session-slot selection is unresolved detail.

CECD 0x000E and 0x000F are the two documented event-handle getters; which of the two is which follows libctru order (0x000E = CecInfo, 0x000F = ChangeState) and is NOT independently verified here.

name: Ui_IconCache_FlushEntries
signature: int Ui_IconCache_FlushEntries(UiIconCache* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Flushes the dirty icon-cache slots: builds the header strings, checks the cache file with 0x00658BFC and commits every 0x70-byte entry via 0x0050D530 up to self->f_130.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread carries the same class prefix and the 0x70-byte entry loop with the commit helper is visible, so both the class and the flush role are confirmed.

name: Ui_IconCache_WriteRawBlock
signature: unsigned int Ui_IconCache_WriteRawBlock(UiIconCache* self, short* header, unsigned int size)
summary: Writes a raw block into the icon cache: validates the 0x6060 magic and the 0x70..0x19000 size range, memcpy's the payload and marks the cache entry written.
evidence: The magic compare, both size guards, the payload copy and the self->f_131 = 1 written-flag are explicit, and its twin 0x50D3B4 performs the same validation for the read direction, so the read/write pair is established.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_BeginWrite
signature: unsigned int maybe_Ui_IconCache_BeginWrite(void* self, int arg2, unsigned int size)
summary: Begins a cache-block write: validates a 4-byte-aligned size in 0x70..0x18000, opens/validates the cache index through 0x00658BFC, records the size at f_134 and arg2 at f_138, and computes the total block size from the self->f_130 directory entries (0xC stride) into self+4/self+8. Returns an nn::Result code (0 on success).
evidence: NEW: the caller Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest (named, 0.50) also calls Ui_IconCache_ResetHeader (0x0050D4CC) in the same block, and the callee 0x0050D864 is now maybe_Svc_ContentInfo_IsCacheCurrent, so the function is part of the same content-cache writer. Whether that cache holds UI icons or Cecd content is still open (both labels appear in the cluster), so the module prefix keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_IconCache_ResetHeader
summary: Clears the cache header: zeroes the two words of every 6-word record, resets the record count at +0x98, memsets the 0x70-byte header and restores the 0x6060 magic.
evidence: New context: the confident Ui_IconCache_WriteRawBlock and Ui_IconCache_ResetEntry call it before writing a new header, and the 0x6060 magic it restores is the one WriteRawBlock validates.

name: Ui_IconCache_ResetEntry
summary: Clears the twelve icon-cache state fields at +0x130..+0x160 and resets the shared block header, leaving the object itself intact.
evidence: Twelve explicit field clears followed by the now-named maybe_Ui_IconCache_ResetHeader; there is no allocation or I/O, so this is a state reset.

name: Str_AssignIfNotNull
signature: int Str_AssignIfNotNull(int dest, int src, int present)
summary: Assigns a string member when the source is present, using the empty-string constructor 0x006722EC for the empty case or the copy helper 0x0011FFFC otherwise.
evidence: The body is the two-way std_String_InitFrom/func_006722EC branch and the caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry uses it for an optional cache key; there is no other effect to name.

name: std_String_InitFrom
signature: unsigned int* std_String_InitFrom(unsigned int* self, int src)
summary: Small-string construct/copy helper: initialises an empty string when the source pointer is null, otherwise copies the source string into the destination.
evidence: if (src == 0) 0x6722EC() else 0x11FFFC(src); six callers all in string-assignment contexts (0x50D14C, 0x50D3B4, 0x6584F0, 0x65854C, maybe_Svc_CacheIndex_WriteTable, 0x50D660).

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_CopyTimestamp
summary: Writes one 8-byte icon-index field into the caller's buffer: a non-null source is copied by 0x0011FFFC, a null source takes the initialiser 0x006722EC; returns the out pointer.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable uses it for the 'ERROR   ' literal when an entry is missing and for the entry name otherwise, so it is an 8-byte record-field writer rather than a timestamp converter. The exact source type is still unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: std_String_InitEmpty
summary: Initialises an empty small string by calling the shared empty-string constructor 0x6722EC and returning the same buffer.
evidence: body is 0x6722EC() then return self; called wherever a string member must be reset (0x4121B4, 0x50D14C, 0x50D3B4, maybe_Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry).

name: maybe_Font_MapCharToLanguageFallback
signature: u32 maybe_Font_MapCharToLanguageFallback(u8* charPtr, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 high)
summary: Queries system language configuration block 0x000A0002 and checks language bit tables to map character code to font fallback index.
evidence: Not item code: queries system configuration block 0x000A0002 (system language) and checks language bitmask tables against language code returned by Svc_Cfg_GetSystemLanguageCode. Called by Ui_WindowState_Goto15OrMenuState and Ui_TalkWindow_HandleEvent7; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_ContentInfo_IsCacheCurrent
summary: Returns whether the cached content info is at least as new as the system's content version: reads the 0xD0000 system word, fetches the content info under the global monitor and compares the stored halfword at +0x2C with the low half of the system word.
evidence: The named Svc_FetchContentInfo and the monitor lock/unlock are clear, but its callers are only the tentatively named icon-cache loaders and the corrupted Fs_BuildContentInfoArchivePath body, so neither 'Ui_IconCache' nor 'Cecd' is proven; the operation itself is a content-version comparison.

name: maybe_Svc_Cfg_GetRegionInfo

evidence: The session and command shape are certain, but no caller and no data symbol name 0x007AF0F8; the only anchor is that the sibling 0x0050D9BC uses the same session for the system-language query, so 'region' remains a guess.

name: Svc_Cfg_GetSystemLanguage

evidence: Confirmed against Nintendo 3DS CTR SDK and libctru CFGU_GetSystemLanguage: issues IPC command header 0x00020000 on cfg:u handle *0x007AF0F8 and stores the returned language enum in *outByte. Called by Fs_BuildMetaDataContentPath and Text_ClassifyInput.

name: Svc_Cfg_GetSystemLanguageCode

evidence: Direct wrapper around confirmed Svc_Cfg_GetSystemLanguage (0x0050D9BC); calls it with a stack buffer and masks the resulting language enum byte. Called by Gfx_MovieTrack_StartPlayback_2 (0x001B7340) and font fallback mapper.

name: Os_InvokeCallbacksVariant
summary: Second copy of the OS pending-callback dispatcher: when (pending & ~handled) is set, invokes up to eight registered callbacks, drains the runtime event, sends the close request and clears the pending flags; unlike Os_InvokeCallbacks (0x00118814) it also writes the handled state (0/1) into block[0] before returning it.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x00118814 is now named Os_InvokeCallbacks (0.50) and the two bodies are identical except for the final handled-byte store in this copy (disassembly writes 0/1 to 0x007AEA00), so the variant relationship is proven; only the suffix 'Variant' remains purely descriptive.

evidence: When write==0 it returns the size (2 for CRLF, 1 for CR/LF); otherwise func_001113EC(buffer, index-1) then stores 0x0d/0x0a at buffer+index-1 (and a second unit for CRLF) and returns 1 or 2. Called from both text converters 0x0050DECC and 0x0050E264.

name: Str_Utf16ToUtf8
signature: int Str_Utf16ToUtf8(char* out, int* out_written, const unsigned short* in, int* in_read, int crlf)
summary: Converts UTF-16 text to UTF-8 with optional CRLF translation and output-size clamping, returning an error code when the output buffer is too small.
evidence: Decodes 1/2/3/4-byte UTF-8 sequences from the wide input (surrogate pair -> 4 bytes, 0xD800..0xDFFF), honours the output limit from func_0050DE40 (local_2c/local_38), emits '\r\n' through func_0050DDAC when arg5 != 0, and returns g_0050E25C (0xD8E14403) / g_0050E260 (0xD9014401) error codes. Companion of Str_Utf8ToUtf16 (0x0050E264).

name: Str_Utf8ToUtf16
signature: int Str_Utf8ToUtf16(unsigned short* out, int* out_written, const unsigned char* in, int* in_read, int crlf)
summary: Converts UTF-8 text to UTF-16 with CRLF translation, skipping a leading UTF-8 BOM and clamping to the destination size.
evidence: Strips the EF BB BF BOM, decodes 1-4 byte sequences (including surrogate pairs via 0xDC00/0xD7C0), writes '\r\n' through func_0050DDAC when arg5 != 0, uses the size probe func_0050DE40 and returns g_0050E57C/0x0050E580 error codes. Called from 0x0050DD70 (debug log) and 0x0050E264 itself.

summary: Cleans up embedded sub-object at +0x18 and decrements reference count at self+0x54.
