summary: Verifies sound system initialization flag at stateWord, aborting via std_RunTerminateHandler if uninitialized, and returns sound system pointer 0x007F09C8.
evidence: Direct accessor body called by Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC); returns global sound system instance 0x007F09C8; kept maybe_.

name: Snd_WaitAudioTransfer
signature: int Snd_WaitAudioTransfer(SndTransfer* self, u64* elapsed, u32 arg3, int size1, int size2, u32 dataPtr, int waitMode)
summary: Submits or waits for one audio buffer transfer. On the first call it reads the millisecond clock, builds the five-word transfer request and posts it with the async transfer helper 0x00111F60; afterwards it compares the hardware tick pairs (0x005191B4/0x00519224 around the memory barrier) to report how long the transfer took in *elapsed, and either drops the user count of the owning slot or sleeps on the wait handle.
evidence: Branch 1: `t = func_001139B0(); if (t && waitMode == 1) dataPtr = default; func_00111E28(&self->f_34); local_38 = 4; ...; uVar3 = func_00111F60(&self->f_10, &local_38, g_00517994, auStack_28, size1+size2, dataPtr, waitMode, 0);` then error checks against module 0x6. Branch 2 uses 0x005191B4/0x00519224 (tick snapshots) and `func_0011CC94(g_0051800c, 0)` (sleep) and adjusts the atomic counter at +0x14. Callers: 0x005179A8 and 0x00517A70 in the same sound block.

name: maybe_Sound_MixerThread_MainThumb
signature: void maybe_Sound_MixerThread_MainThumb(u32 thread, u32 thread2, int thread3, u32 thread4, int frame)
summary: Thumb-mode mixer thread body (twin of the ARM copy at 0x00517B6C): waits for the DSP display event, runs the per-frame audio update through the callback slots at +0x20/+0x28/+0x30, advances the 64-bit frame clock with svc 0x28 and loops while the run flag is set.
evidence: Re-read: the callback slots match the named maybe_Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate and maybe_Sound_WaitForDisplayTime, which supports the mixer-thread reading, but the decompilation is damaged (unaff_r4/r7, in_lr and a bogus CONCAT44 of the first argument), so the register roles can only be settled from the disassembly. Stays maybe_.

name: Snd_StartVoicePlayback
signature: int Snd_StartVoicePlayback(SndVoice* self, u32* src, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32* arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Starts playback of one voice: waits/submits the buffer through Snd_WaitAudioTransfer, records the two caller parameters at +0x20/+0x24, and optionally applies a three-word loop/rate parameter block with 0x00517CF0. If that second step fails the voice is torn down again with 0x00517A70.
evidence: `result = func_00517884(self, arg6, arg7, src[0], src[1], src[2], arg8); if (result >= 0) { self->f_20 = arg3; self->f_24 = arg4; if (arg5 == 0 || (result = func_00517CF0(self, arg5[0], arg5[1], arg5[2])) >= 0) return 0; func_00517A70(self); } return result;`. No direct callers - it is a vtable entry of the sound voice class (0x00517884/0x005179A8/0x00517A70 form the start/stop trio).

name: Sound_GetSystemHeader
summary: Copies the first two words of the sound-system object into the caller's buffer (an 8-byte header getter); the 'does not return' note is a Ghidra artifact.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00517A38..0x00517A5C is push/mov r4,r0/bl 0x005177DC (Sound_GetSystem)/mov r1,r0/mov r0,r4/pop/ldm {r1,r2}/stm {r1,r2}/bx lr, exactly an 8-byte copy out of the system object. Its caller is the named Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling.

name: Sound_GetSystemThunk
summary: 16-byte thunk: 'push {r4,lr}; bl 0x005177DC; pop {r4,lr}' returns the sound-system pointer from maybe_Sound_GetSystemIfInitialized (0x005177DC, which loads the global and tests its bit 0).
evidence: Disassembly 0x00517A60-0x00517A6C is exactly push/bl 0x5177dc/pop, and 0x005177DC is the real entry of maybe_Sound_GetSystemIfInitialized (ldr r0,[pc]; push {r4,lr}; ldr r0,[r0]; tst r0,#1) - Ghidra split that function at 0x005177E0. Both callers (Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks, maybe_Sound_Driver_StopTimer) use it as a getter.

name: Svc_Gpu_CleanupCommandBuffers
summary: Tears down the two GPU command/transfer buffers of a slot: for each in-use buffer it waits for GSP (software_interrupt 0x24), finishes the pending transfer (func_00118100/func_00118170, software_interrupt 0x23), issues a data-synchronisation barrier, invalidates the cache range (func_00111D50) and resets the bookkeeping words (f_3C = -1, global 0x7F09C4 = 1).
evidence: Two symmetric blocks with `software_interrupt(0x24); ... func_00118100(); ... func_00118170(&self->f_18); software_interrupt(0x23); ... coproc_moveto_Data_Synchronization(0); func_00111D50(&self->f_48);` - the same GSP-wait idiom as Gfx_StreamSlot_Release (0x500564). Writes the global flag at 0x7F09C4.

name: maybe_Sound_GetSystemThunkArg
summary: Thunk invoking sound system instance accessor 0x005177DC.
evidence: Short thunk invoking sound system accessor 0x005177DC; callee is Sound_RingBuffer_Write (0x0051779C); kept maybe_.

name: Sound_MixerThread_Main
summary: The mixer thread: loops while the run flag is set, sleeps until the next frame (svcSleepThread via 0x518010 or the tick helper 0x517E7C), polls the two DSP event counters (0x51756C), calls the registered frame callback +0x28/0x2c and the per-frame update 0x51867C, and advances the 64-bit frame clock.
evidence: Same structure as the Thumb twin 0x517942; the callback slots +0x28/+0x2c and the mutex at +0x48 are the ones 0x5184AC/0x518550 register; 0x51867C is the frame update.

name: Snd_StartChannelTransferThread
signature: unsigned Snd_StartChannelTransferThread(Sound_DspChannel* self, unsigned buffer, unsigned size, unsigned* timeout)
summary: Starts the DSP transfer thread of a sound channel: it resets the two light events, fills the thread attribute block and calls Os_CreateThreadWithStack with entry 0x00518768 and the buffer/size/timeout arguments, then stores the sign of the result at f_E.
evidence: NEW: the body calls the confident Os_CreateThreadWithStack with entry 0x00518768 and never waits, so the old 'WaitForDspFrame' name described the wrong half; the only caller is the named Snd_StartVoicePlayback.

name: maybe_Sound_SetPendingState
summary: Thunk: gets the sound system (0x005177DC) and stores the argument byte at system+8, but only when the system's +0x30 flag is zero. The +0x30 gate and the +8 field are unnamed, so 'pending state' is a guess.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00517DE8-0x00517E08: push {r4,lr}; mov r4,r0; bl 0x5177dc; mov r1,r4; pop {r4,lr}; ldrb r2,[r0,#0x30]; cmp r2,#0; strbeq r1,[r0,#8]. The conditional setter is certain; the meaning of +0x30/+8 is not.

name: maybe_Sound_CloseObjectHandles
summary: Closes and clears the two kernel handles an object owns (+0x18 first, then +0x10) and returns the object; the handle-release step of a sound-subsystem teardown.
evidence: Disassembly is two copies of `bl 0x00118170; if ([p]) { svc 0x23; [p] = 0; }` applied to +0x18 and +0x10, then `return self`. The only named neighbour is Sound_Decoder_InitChannelTable (0x0054F18C), which is sound-subsystem code, so 'Sound' holds; 'Dsp' was unsupported and is dropped. No direct `bl` to this address exists in asm/text, so the caller edge is indirect and the object type stays open.

name: Sound_GetDisplayTime
summary: Samples the DSP display timestamp under the sound lock counter (0x5191B4/0x518BE0), computes the 64-bit delta and returns it through the caller's pair, retrying after a timeout when the DSP is not ready.
evidence: The callers are the named mixer-thread functions (Sound_MixerThread_Main, Sound_Frame_PublishChannelTable) and the lock helpers Os_LockSemaphore/Os_TryLockSemaphore are named, so the timing-sample role holds.

name: Sound_WaitForDisplayTime
summary: Locking counterpart of 0x517E7C used by the frame update: samples the DSP timestamp and sleeps before retrying while the display is not ready; returns no timestamp.
evidence: Same caller set as 0x517E7C plus the movie playback frame path (0x4FC8A8) and the same lock/timestamp sequence minus the output pair, so it is the wait-only variant.

name: maybe_Sound_SubmitAdpcmFrame
signature: unsigned maybe_Sound_SubmitAdpcmFrame(unsigned char* samples, unsigned arg2, int params, int channel, int count)
summary: Packs one ADPCM frame for the DSP: splits eight sample bytes into sixteen nibbles, combines them with the channel's predictor/step values from the parameter block and writes the result, then waits for the DSP event.
evidence: The packing loop is readable, but the body is damaged (unaff_r5, bad instruction data, a bogus func_0x005d1f7a target and an Os_CreateThreadWithStack call that cannot belong here), so the frame layout cannot be re-verified; the named caller Sound_SubmitAdpcmBlocks carries the same role name.

name: maybe_Sound_DspWriteChannelConfig
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_DspWriteChannelConfig(u32 value, u32 forwarded, u32 forwarded2, u32 forwarded3)
summary: Writes DSP channel register configuration word with flag bit 0x10 and forwards to 0x0011E9A8.
evidence: Decompiled body carries unaff_r4/unaff_r5 (damaged decompilation); writes channel register configuration; kept maybe_ with low confidence.

name: Sound_Channel_WriteParamBlock
signature: void Sound_Channel_WriteParamBlock(u32 driver, int channel, u16* block)
summary: Copies a masked 0x14-byte DSP channel parameter block into the driver's per-channel table: mask bit0 = one halfword, bit1 = one word, bit2 = five words (filter/loop data), then marks the channel dirty and flushes the DSP cache.
evidence: Writes `func_001129F4() + channel*0x14` (the same table maybe_Snd_SetChannelFilterInfo 0x118E58 writes) and calls 0x118E58 to publish the dirty flags; the mask/field layout is identical to 0x118E58's.

name: Sound_Channel_ApplyParamBlock
signature: void Sound_Channel_ApplyParamBlock(int manager, int channel, u16 * block)
summary: Applies a command block to one sound channel: stores the block's flags/parameters into the channel state (enable, wave-buffer id, sample format, loop, ADPCM coefficients) and notifies the DSP service. Its neighbours in symbols.json already name the matching writer Sound_Channel_WriteParamBlock (0x5182CC); this is the immediate-mode counterpart used by both wave setters.
evidence: writes manager+channel+6, manager+channel*0x34+0x2A, +0x2E, +0x30..+0x40, +0x44..+0x5A per block bits 1/2/4; func_001129F4() gets the channel table; func_00118FD4(0x7EF414) signals the DSP; callers 0x516900/0x516A58/0x51698C

name: Sound_ForwardToVoicePlayback
signature: void Sound_ForwardToVoicePlayback(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Gathers six register/stack arguments, fetches the sound system (0x005177DC) and tail-forwards everything to the named Snd_StartVoicePlayback (0x005179A8).
evidence: Disassembly 0x0051846C-0x0051848C: push {r4-r8,sb,sl,lr}; sub sp,#0x10; mov r8,r0; add r0,sp,#0x30; ldm r0,{r5,r6,r7}; mov sl,r2; mov r4,r3; bl 0x5177dc, then bl 0x5179a8 (Snd_StartVoicePlayback). The decompiler's 'does not return' claim was wrong.

name: Sound_Channel_InvokeCallback
signature: void Sound_Channel_InvokeCallback(SoundChannel* self, u32 sub, u32 buf)
summary: Calls the decode/mix hook registered for one of the channel's two slots with the four 0x280-byte chunk pointers, a length of 0xA0 and the hook's argument, under the channel's own monitor.
evidence: NEW: the hook table and argument table are read as self+sub*4+0x14 / +0x1c and the four chunk offsets (0, 0x280, 0x500, 0x780) match the buffer layout used by the confirmed Sound_Channel_ApplyCommand / CancelBuffer siblings.

name: Sound_Channel_SetDecodeHook
signature: void Sound_Channel_SetDecodeHook(SoundChannel* self, u32 sub, int hook, u32 callback)
summary: Installs or removes the decode/mix hook of one channel slot and tells the driver whether the slot is active (0x118BAC).
evidence: Stores hook/arg at +0x14/+0x1c of the slot and calls maybe_Snd_SetUnitAdpcmWord (0x118BAC) with 0/1 - the same activation helper 0x5185E4 uses.

name: Sound_Channel_SetActive
signature: void Sound_Channel_SetActive(SoundChannel* self, u32 slot, u8 active)
summary: Sets the per-slot active byte and publishes it to the driver through 0x118BAC(bank, slot).
evidence: `*(u8*)(self + sub + 0x30) = active; 0x118BAC(0x518644, sub)` - the flag byte read by 0x518550 and the driver helper 0x118BAC.

name: maybe_Sound_GetQueueRoot
summary: Returns func_00117ED0(&soundSystem->f_34) as a tail call: it hands the sound system's +0x34 member to the kernel wait helper, and all movie-track paths call it before touching their track queue.
evidence: Disassembly is 'bl Sound_GetSystem; add r0,r0,#0x34; b 0x00117ED0', so the getter shape is certain, but whether +0x34 is a queue root is not; its nine callers are Gfx_MovieTrack_Create/Destroy/Pause/Resume/Start/ResetQueue.

name: Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate
summary: Starts one sound frame: atomically bumps the frame counter, waits for the display time, and when the driver is idle processes the pending start request and the per-frame channel table update.
evidence: The callers are now Sound_MixerThread_Main / maybe_Sound_MixerThread_MainThumb / maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll, and the callees are Sound_WaitForDisplayTime and Sound_Frame_UpdateChannels.

name: maybe_Sound_ResetChannelState
summary: Entry fragment of sound channel state reset invoking sound accessor 0x005177DC.
evidence: Split fragment with truncated decompiled body; calls sound system accessor; kept maybe_.

name: Sound_Channel_InitSlot
summary: Initialises a channel slot: state byte = 2, default timing/list/callback fields cleared, the DSP volume/frequency defaults installed, and the slot's wave-buffer descriptor reset (0x519C1C).
evidence: Writes the same field block 0x518A7C/0x518BE0 later read (state +4, times +0x18/+0x1c, callbacks +0x2c/+0x30, descriptor +0x68) and calls maybe_Sound_WaveBuffer_Reset (0x519C1C); called by 0x516F1C.

name: maybe_Sound_CalcDspAdpcmStep
summary: Fixed-point helper that turns a scale/step pair into two 16-bit coefficients (including a square-root term), stores them at +8/+10 of the object and copies them into the DSP register block with dirty flag 8.
evidence: Two callees (0x0051B6B0, 0x0011E9A8) remain unnamed and the constants (0x40000000/0x3F800000/0x47000000) fit both an ADPCM step and a filter coefficient; 'ADPCM step' is still a hypothesis and there is no caller, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Sound_Frame_UpdateChannels
summary: Per-frame channel update: reads the system tick, computes the frame delta (0x517478/0x516E58), mixes both sub-channels of the current half (0x5174F8), runs the channel scheduler (0x5171B0) with the remaining time and switches the published buffer half.
evidence: Reads the 24-entry channel pointer tables at +0x109c/+0x10ac/+0x1174 (0x60-byte halves) and calls 0x5174F8, 0x5171B0, 0x51717C, 0x517328; wrapped in the 0x11E99C/0x11E9B4/0x11E9A8 critical section.

name: Sound_Frame_PublishChannelTable
summary: Publishes the next frame's channel table: reads the free-running frame counter, copies the 24 channel descriptors of the new half (0x519DCC), copies the 0x260-byte DSP parameter block (0x116C10) and advances the buffer index.
evidence: 0x18-iteration copy of `self + half*0x60 + ch*4 + 0x1174`, a 0x260-byte 0x116C10 copy from +0x1314/+0x1328 and 0x51779C for the sample ring; the half index is `counter & 1` as in 0x518A7C.

name: Sound_DspChannel_Start
summary: Starts a DSP channel: clears the low byte of its status word and raises command bit 0x10000 in the channel's DSP command word (the 'key on' bit).
evidence: `puVar2->f_28 = (u16)puVar2[0x28] & 0xff00; *puVar2 |= 0x10000;` on `driver + (half&1)*0x60 + channel*4 + 0x10b4`; called by 0x51A4AC/0x51A4D8 when a channel enters state 1.

name: Sound_DspChannel_Stop
summary: Stops a DSP channel: sets its status word to 1 and raises the same 0x10000 command bit.
evidence: Same access pattern as 0x518D04 with `puVar2->f_28 = 1`; used by the pause path 0x51A45C.

name: maybe_Sound_DspChannel_SetLoopCount
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_DspChannel_SetLoopCount(u32 driver, int channel, u16 count)
summary: Writes 16-bit count at channel DSP state offset +0xA2 and sets command bit 0x10000000.
evidence: Sole caller maybe_Sound_Channel_FlushPriority (0x00519D90) passes priority expired node data; exact field semantics remain unconfirmed so kept maybe_.

name: Sound_DspChannel_GetPlayPosition
summary: Returns the current playback position (16-bit counter at +2 of the DSP channel state selected by the frame half), or 0xFFFFFFFF when the DSP is not running.
evidence: Reads `*(u16*)(*(int*)(driver + (half)*4 + 0x10ac) + 2)`; the same 'position' value is added to the channel clock by 0x517624 and used by the frame update 0x518A7C.

name: Sound_DspChannel_Pause
summary: Sets bit 0x10 (the DSP channel pause/hold command bit) in the channel's command word while the driver lock is held, and returns 1; returns 0 when the driver is not ready.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Sound_Channel_Refill (0.5), which calls it for a starved channel; the lock/unlock pair and the single OR of 0x10 are the whole body.

name: Sound_DspChannel_SetWaveBuffer
signature: u32 Sound_DspChannel_SetWaveBuffer(u32 driver, int channel, u32* wave, u32 sub)
summary: Programs one of the four sub-wave buffers of a DSP channel: converts the sample count to bytes for the channel format bits, byte-swaps the address/length, stores the loop point, sets the sub-wave valid bit at +0x4A and raises command bit 0x80000.
evidence: NEW: caller Sound_Channel_Refill (0.5) plus the identical format decoding and the 0x14-byte stride shared with the sibling 0x0051927C; the +0x4A bitfield is indexed by the sub-wave number.

name: Sound_DspChannel_UpdateSampleInfo
signature: u32 Sound_DspChannel_UpdateSampleInfo(u32 driver, int channel, u32* wave)
summary: Refreshes a DSP channel's sample info when the queued wave id matches the channel's current sample id: copies the id, the loop flag and the byte-swapped address and raises command bit 8.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Sound_Channel_Refill (0.5) and the compare-then-command-bit-8 shape matches the other three channel helpers in this batch.

name: Sound_DspChannel_Flush
summary: Sets the 0x20000000 command bit in one DSP channel's command word under the sound monitor and returns 1, or 0 when the sound system is not initialised.
evidence: The body is a single read-modify-write of the channel word selected by the driver's active-bank bit, wrapped in the sound monitor; the only uncertainty is what the 0x20000000 bit means (flush/key-off), which the callers after a key-on support.

name: Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter
summary: Polls one audio-transfer slot: it waits on the slot's sync handle (svcWaitSynchronization1) and, when a full frame period has elapsed, cancels the wait, bumps the slot's frame byte at +0x131D and reports true; otherwise it reports false and leaves the slot alone.
evidence: NEW: the two named callers Sound_GetDisplayTime and Sound_WaitForDisplayTime are exactly the per-transfer frame tick users, and the body's svc 0x24 (svcWaitSynchronization1, per FACTS.md) plus the +0x131D increment show it advances the transfer frame, not a graphics frame.

name: Snd_ForceAdvanceFrameCounter
summary: Unconditional twin of Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter: waits on the slot's sync handle (svcWaitSynchronization1), re-arbitrates it (svc 0x19) and bumps the transfer frame byte at +0x131D without testing whether a frame period elapsed. Sound_GetDisplayTime and Sound_WaitForDisplayTime call it when they must advance the transfer frame immediately.
evidence: The sibling 0x005191B4 is now the confirmed Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter (0.50, R3_025) and its body is this one plus the 0x400000 frame-period test; both share the same two named callers (Sound_GetDisplayTime, Sound_WaitForDisplayTime) and the same svc 0x24 / svc 0x19 / +0x131D increment. So the function advances the frame counter unconditionally and never resets anything, which is what the old ResetFrameCounter name claimed.

name: Sound_DspChannel_SetupSample
signature: u32 Sound_DspChannel_SetupSample(u32 driver, int channel, u32* wave, u32 flags)
summary: Full DSP channel sample setup: converts the sample count to bytes for the format bits (8/16/32-bit, mono/stereo with the 0xD/8 rounding), translates the address to DSP space, stores the sample and loop addresses, copies up to two loop halfwords and raises the 0x40200000 command bits.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the confident Sound_Channel_Refill (0.5) and the sibling setters of this batch (0x00518EA8/0x00518F10/0x0051908C) all do the same channel-state program-and-lock dance, which confirms the DSP channel role.

name: maybe_Sound_ReleaseStreamObject
summary: Resets stream index at self+0x10 to -1 and closes two owned kernel handles via svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle).
evidence: Closes two kernel handles with svc 0x23 and marks index -1; stream wrapper owner unverified so kept maybe_.

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_Init
summary: Initialises a wave buffer: lays out the 0x280-byte sample chunks after the aligned buffer base, zero-fills the buffer (0x1113EC) and resets the per-chunk write offsets; returns 1 the first time and 0 if already initialised.
evidence: `*(u32*)(self + i*4 + 0x1c) = i*0x280*self->f_3c + (base+0x1f & ~0x1f)` for i < count, then 0x1113EC memset and the per-chunk zero loop; the 0x280-byte DSP frame stride is also used by 0x519674/0x5174F8.

name: maybe_Sound_MixTwoChannels
summary: Mixes 0xA0-sample audio channel buffers into ring buffer slots using fixed-point coefficient arithmetic and advances buffer write index.
evidence: Called by Sound_Channel_ReleaseBuffers (0x00517418), Sound_Channel_SetWaveBufferMain (0x0051765C), and Sound_Channel_SetWaveBufferAux (0x00517700); channel routing details inferred; kept maybe_.

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_ComputeLayout
summary: Derives a wave buffer's chunk pointers from its counts: converts the two float-derived counts with VectorFloatToUnsigned(...,3), spaces the chunks 0x280 bytes apart and fills the four mix-buffer pointers, then hands the result to Sound_WaveBuffer_BuildChannelParams.
evidence: The callee Sound_WaveBuffer_BuildChannelParams is a confirmed name now, and the callers are Sound_Channel_SetWaveBufferAux and Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB - both take a wave buffer and need its chunk pointers, which is exactly what this body computes.

name: maybe_Sound_MixFourChannels
summary: Multi-channel audio mixer: computes fixed-point weighted samples across six ring buffers and updates stream channel positions.
evidence: Surround/effects mixer companion to 0x00519544; channel assignments inferred so kept maybe_.

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_BuildChannelParams
summary: Builds the per-channel fixed-point playback parameters (sample-rate steps at +0x9C/+0xA4, loop counters and six volume/pan coefficients) from a wave-buffer layout record, clamping each field and scaling by 0xA0. Called from Sound_WaveBuffer_ComputeLayout (0x519674); the 0xA0 fixed-point scale, 6 coefficient slots and the pan mirror based on f_24 are the channel-parameter conversion.
evidence: reads self+4/+8/+0xC, fields f_30..f_38, f_10/f_1C/f_20/f_24; clamps with 4.888/0.2046/128/0.95/1.0 constants; writes f_9C..f_EC; func_00673468 and func_001113EC(self->f_28,self->f_2C); caller 0x00519674 maybe_Sound_WaveBuffer_ComputeLayout

name: Sound_WaveBuffer_Reset
summary: Resets a wave-buffer descriptor to its default state (state byte 2, default command word, cleared counters and list head) and re-initialises its embedded sync primitive.
evidence: Its only caller is the confident Sound_Channel_InitSlot, which allocates a channel and resets its wave buffer before use; the body is a straight field-reset routine, so nothing about the guess was in conflict.

name: maybe_Sound_Channel_ApplyPendingLoopCount
summary: When the channel node's u16 at +0x6C has bit 0x8000 set, pushes the node's pending value (s16 at +4) into the DSP channel state through 0x00518DE8 (driver 0x007EF414, channel = node[0] & 0xFF) and clears the bit.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00519D90-0x00519DB8: ldrh r0,[r0,#0x6C]; tst r0,#0x8000; beq end; ldr r0,[r4]; ldrsh r2,[r4,#4]; and r1,r0,#0xff; bl 0x518de8; then clears 0x8000. The old 'FlushPriority' name claimed a priority flush that the body does not do; the callee (maybe_Sound_DspChannel_SetLoopCount) is itself only a maybe_, so the 'loop count' wording stays provisional.

name: Sound_Channel_ApplyCommand
summary: Applies a command packet to a channel: if the packet's stream id matches it stores the byte-swapped word, drops the buffers up to the packet's start id (marking them state 3) and derives the running flag from the packet's low byte.
evidence: NEW: the buffer states 1/2/3 and the +0x70 monitor are shared with the confirmed Sound_Channel_CancelBuffer / Reinsert siblings in this batch, and the 0xA0-byte audio-unit protocol matches InvokeCallback; the 'apply command' reading is directly supported by the packet fields it consumes.

name: Sound_SetChannelParamBlock
summary: Copies a 0x20-byte parameter block into channel offset self+0x7C and sets parameter dirty flag bit 0x40 at self+0x6C.
evidence: Called by Sound_Voice_ApplyPendingParams (0x0054CFA8) and Gfx_MovieTrack_Start (0x004FCF9C); copies 0x20-byte parameter block into channel state at offset +0x7C and marks parameter update flag bit 0x40 at +0x6C.

name: Sound_Channel_Refill
summary: Refills a channel's wave buffers: releases exhausted buffers, starts up to five queued buffers (0x518F10/0x51908C) and advances the packet cursor; when the queue is empty it pauses the channel (0x518EA8) and stops it.
evidence: Walks the buffer list, calls 0x518EA8/0x51908C/0x518F10/0x51927C, uses the 5-slot limit at +0x34 and the DMB before state changes; called from the frame update.

name: Sound_Channel_QueueBuffer
summary: Queues a wave buffer on a channel: rejects buffers without data, unlinks it from any other list, marks it state 1, appends it to the channel's buffer list and gives it the next sequence id.
evidence: `if (*(int*)(buf+4) == 0) { buf->f_11 = 3; return; }`, then list append at self->f_30 and `buf->f_12 = self[6]++`; same node layout as 0x51A2BC/0x519FCC.

name: Sound_Channel_CancelBuffer
summary: Walks the channel's buffer list and, when the buffer is still queued (state != 3), raises the channel's cancel flag (+0x6F bit 1) so the refill path drops it.
evidence: NEW: the list walk (+0x30 head, +0x14 next) and the state byte +0x11 are the same ones Sound_Channel_ApplyCommand marks with state 3, so the two together are the cancel protocol; no further inference is needed for this 96-byte function.

name: Sound_Channel_FlushBuffers
summary: Flushes the channel: marks every queued buffer state 3, clears the queue head/pointers, sets the lock-out bit 0x8000, bumps the stream id and clears the buffer list.
evidence: Loop `buf->f_11 = 3` over self->f_30, then zeroes +0x30/+0x34/+0x36, sets `self->f_6c |= 0x8000` and increments *(short*)(self+4); called by 0x51A4AC on start.

name: Sound_Channel_Pause
summary: Pauses a channel by sending the DSP pause command for its channel index and setting the paused byte.
evidence: `0x518D78(driver, *self & 0xff); *(u8*)(self+0xc) = 1;`; called by the scheduler 0x5171B0 and by 0x51A4AC.

name: Sound_Channel_SetState
summary: Sets a channel's playback state: writes the state byte, and for play/pause sends the matching DSP key-on (0x518D04) / flush (0x51914C) command for the channel index stored in the descriptor, mirroring the state there.
evidence: `*(u8*)(self+4) = state; if (state == 1) 0x51A31C(self->f_68); *(u8*)(f68+0xd) = state; ... 0x518D04/0x51914C(driver, *f68 & 0xff)`; called by the movie/audio track start-pause-resume helpers and the scheduler.

name: Sound_Channel_SetPlayState
summary: Applies a three-value play state to one DSP channel: stores the state byte at +0xD, and for state 1 issues Sound_DspChannel_Start, clears the pending byte at +3 and issues Sound_DspChannel_Flush (a restart), while state 2 only issues Start. All five callers are sound or movie-track paths, so this is the single place that turns a logical play state into DSP commands.
evidence: All five callers are now named sound paths (Sound_Channel_Allocate, Sound_Voice_ApplyPendingParams, Sound_Voice_UpdatePlayState, Gfx_MovieTrack_Start, Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll) and the two callees are the confirmed Sound_DspChannel_Start / Sound_DspChannel_Flush. The body is a plain switch on the state value, so SetStateSimple was vague rather than wrong; the name now says which state it sets.

name: Snd_InitVoice
summary: Initialises one DSP voice: stores the voice index, sets the twelve data/state pointers to the -1 sentinel, resets the three counters, initialises the voice lock, sets the reference count to 1 and raises the 'active' bit 0x8000 in the flags.
evidence: `*self = index; self[0x16]=self[0x12]=self[0xe]=self[0x17]=self[0x13]=self[0xf]=self[0x18]=self[0x14]=self[0x10]=self[0x19]=self[0x15]=self[0x11]=0xffffffff; self[0x1c]=self[0x1d]=0; self[0x1e]=0xffffffff; func_00111E28(&self->f_1c); *(u16*)(self+1) = 1; self->f_1b |= 0x8000;`. Called by 0x00696E10, which builds the 24-voice channel table.

name: Svc_UnlinkSharedEntry
summary: Looks the handle up in the global shared-resource list at 0x007F2358 under its monitor, unlinks the matching entry from the intrusive prev/next list and returns it (NULL when absent). It frees nothing itself: both callers release the returned entry afterwards.
evidence: The body is a complete intrusive doubly-linked-list unlink: Os_LockMonitor/Os_UnlockMonitor around the sentinel at 0x007F2358+0x18, prev/next at entry+4/+8, the handle compared against entry+0xC, and the sentinel repaired when the removed entry was the tail. Both named callers (Svc_ReleaseSharedState, maybe_Svc_ObjectPool_DestroyB) free the returned pointer, which confirms the unlink-only reading.

name: Os_Ipc_SendRequestA0040
summary: Sends the fixed IPC command 0x000A0040 with one parameter: writes the header and the resource id into the calling thread's TLS command buffer (TLS+0x80 / TLS+0x84), issues svcSendSyncRequest (svc 0x32) on the session handle at 0x007AF900 and returns the response word on success. The shared-resource release paths use it before freeing an entry.
evidence: Disassembly-level reading of the body: coproc_movefrom_User_R_Thread_and_Process_ID is the mrc p15 TLS read, TLS+0x80 is the IPC command buffer, software_interrupt(0x32) is svcSendSyncRequest and the handle comes from the global 0x007AF900. The old mechanical SvcCommandA0040 name described the constant, not the operation; the callers (Svc_ReleaseSharedState, Svc_ReleaseSharedResources, maybe_Svc_ObjectPool_DestroyB) are all teardown paths.

name: Os_SvcCommand90040
summary: Issues the one-parameter SVC request 0x00090040 with a shared-resource id through software interrupt 0x32 and returns the kernel's result word.
evidence: The body explicitly stores command 0x00090040 and the resource id in the thread block, executes svc 0x32 and returns the result; the named callers Svc_ObjectPool_InitA/InitB call it to acquire the shared resource, so the mechanical SVC-wrapper name is accurate.

name: std_FastSinCos
signature: void std_FastSinCos(float angle, float* outSin, float* outCos)
summary: Table-driven sin/cos pair: takes |angle|, splits it into an integer index and fraction (table of 16-byte entries at 0x72FC50), linearly interpolates the sine and cosine entries and restores the sign for negative input. Used everywhere a rotation is needed instead of the soft-float library.
evidence: `aBS = ABS(angle); if (65536.0f <= (int)aBS) func_00673288()` (range reduction clamp); index = VectorFloatToUnsigned(aBS); `*arg1 = tbl[0] + (aBS - (float)index) * tbl[2]` and `*arg2 = tbl[1] + (aBS - (float)index) * tbl[3]` with sign flip from the FPSCR record; the table base is 0x72FC50 and 0x47800000 = 65536.0f. Callers include the UI transform code (0x452348, 0x5331CC, 0x537EEC, 0x53F62C, 0x540AAC, 0x65D534).

name: maybe_Sound_GetDefaultTemplate
summary: Asserts sound module initialized via stateWord and returns default data template pointer 0x008386FC.
evidence: Called by Sound_Channel_Allocate (0x00516F1C); returns constant template data pointer 0x008386FC; template owner unverified so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Math_WrapFloatToU16
summary: Wraps a float into [0, limit) with fmodf, then truncates to an unsigned 16-bit value with the current FPSCR rounding mode and converts the result back to float. The name describes the arithmetic only; the owner (CRT helper vs. sound driver) is unknown.
evidence: No caller can be trusted: the six reported callers (Fs_CheckPendingResult, four Fx_Billboard_* routines and Math_Vector3_DistanceSquared) do not share a float-to-u16 wrap step, which points at a shared CRT/compiler helper in the std_FastSinCos/std_Fmodf block rather than at those call sites. The body still drops the result register, so even the return type is inferred.

name: Fs_WorkBuffer_Init
summary: Zeroes an 0xE30-byte file-service request/work buffer and stamps its first word with type 5.
evidence: All three callers are now named file-service paths (Fs_BuildRequestArgs, Svc_Content_ResolveEntryType, and the debug-label init that reuses the same buffer) and the size/type constants are explicit; nothing in the body is sound-specific, so 'Fs_WorkBuffer_Init' replaces the old Sound_ guess.

name: Err_WaitForAppletReady

evidence: Loops checking nn::err status result 0xC8A0CFFC; established in FACTS.md.

name: Sound_Driver_Init
signature: unsigned int Sound_Driver_Init(unsigned char* config, unsigned int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Starts the sound driver: negotiates the display mode, maps the shared DSP region (page-aligned), opens/closes the driver handles, sets the 0x00989680 (100 ms in ticks) and 0.01/0.1 timing constants and hands control to the driver start helper 0x51C38C.
evidence: callees maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode (0x10CF50), maybe_Os_MapSharedMemory (0x11E80C), Os_CloseHandle (0x11E8A0) and maybe_Sound_QueryDriverStateB (0x51C900); constants 0x00989680/0x004C4B40 (= 10M/5M ticks = 100/50 ms at 67 MHz) and 0.01/0.1 floats; immediately precedes the sound driver shutdown 0x51C38C.

name: maybe_Err_WaitForIpcIdleOrFatal
summary: Retries Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle(0) while it reports a negative non-fatal result, sleeping 10 ms on 0xE0A0CC08 and stopping on success or on the err:f sentinel 0xC8A0CFFC.
evidence: The loop constants are the err:f family values (FACTS.md: 0xC8A0CFFC) and the callee is the named Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle, so this waits rather than checking a returned value; the previous '1 ms' wording was wrong (0x00989680 ns = 10 ms).

name: std_FormatV

name: Gfx_EnsureGpuSession

name: maybe_Sound_NotifyServiceThread

evidence: Disassembly 0x0051BD7C-0x0051BDA4: ldr r5,[r0]; bl 0x11f730; mov r3,r6; mov r2,r4; mov r1,r5; pop {r4,r5,r6,lr}; b 0x51bdac. The argument order is certain, but neither 0x0011F730 nor the global is named, so 'NotifyServiceThread' remains a reading of the two arguments.

name: Err_WaitForStatusFlags
summary: Wait helper of the CTR SDK nn::err (err:f) client: clears the one-byte state at 0x007AE954, runs the two state hooks 0x00113A40(3)/0x001143C8(0), then polls the status query until the returned status word shares a set bit with both of the two flag bytes it also returns (sleeping 10,000,000 ticks per poll), and restores the saved state at 0x007AE954 afterwards.
evidence: NEW: FACTS.md records 0x0051BA34..0x0051CD40 as the CTR SDK nn::err (err:f) fatal-error applet library, and this address sits inside that range; both callers are the err paths 0x0051BA38 (fatal-result check) and 0x0051CCFC (throw). The old Sound_ prefix came from the equally poisoned Sound_* labels in the same range - 0x007AE954 lies in the OS IPC state block next to the 0x007AE910 session state used by Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, not in a sound object.

name: Sound_Driver_Shutdown
signature: int Sound_Driver_Shutdown(unsigned int arg1, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Stops the sound driver: signals and closes the driver events, releases the scheduler/GPU lock, tears down the two runtime objects and (for the sound path) re-runs the client shutdown with the 1000000-tick timeout.
evidence: calls maybe_Os_SignalAndClose (0x113814), Os_UnlockScheduler (0x119E1C), 0x114284/0x114298, 0x11391C/0x113964/0x113980/0x1139B0 and the fatal reporter 0x11ED40; constants 0x000F4240 (1e6) and 0x7AE910 flag; called from Sound_Driver_Init (0x51B7C4) and 0x51CC68.

name: Sound_QueryDriverState
summary: Polls the sound DSP driver state (Sound_Dsp_QueryState / 0x0051CB10) under the sound lock until it leaves the retry codes, then restores the thread priority and returns the final status.
evidence: The callee Sound_Dsp_QueryState and the confident callers Sound_Driver_Init / Sound_WaitForDriverCommand make it the state-polling primitive; the retry-constant loop and the thread-priority restore (0x00113980/0x0011391C) are visible in the body.

name: Gfx_Y2r_ConvertFrame
signature: void Gfx_Y2r_ConvertFrame(int base, int* srcDesc, int* planeInfo)
summary: Converts one YUV frame into the Y/U/V destination planes: picks the row converter for the pixel format, walks 400 rows x 240 pixels (8 pixels per step) and finally converts the second plane.
evidence: New context: the Y2R family (Gfx_Y2r_Init/Convert/IsDone, Gfx_Y2r_GetSessionHandle) is confident, and this body only wraps the row converter 0x0051C678 with the plane pointers from the descriptor; the 400x240 bounds match the top screen.

name: Gfx_Y2r_ConvertPlane
signature: void Gfx_Y2r_ConvertPlane(u32* dst, u32* planeDesc, int planeIndex, int secondPlane)
summary: Converts one plane of a YUV frame into the RGB destination: picks the row converter from the descriptor's pixel format and runs 240 pixels per row for 320 or 400 rows. Gfx_Y2r_ConvertFrame calls it once per plane.
evidence: The named caller Gfx_Y2r_ConvertFrame (0x0051C5F0) calls it three times with plane index 1, 0 and (0, secondPlane=1), so it converts one plane of the frame; the disassembly at 0x0051C684 is 'movne ip,#0x140 / moveq ip,#0x190' (320/400 rows), which is the conditional Ghidra lost as in_ZR - the body is damaged but the disassembly settles the row count.

name: Fs_StartAsyncReadThunk

name: Sound_Dsp_GetStatus

name: Sound_Dsp_WriteWaveBuffer

name: Sound_Dsp_QueryState

name: Err_FatalErrInfo_Init
summary: Initialises a 0xF80-byte CTR SDK nn::err::FatalErrInfo: zeroes the header and the 0xED8-byte body, sets +0xEE4 = 1, zeroes 0x89 bytes at +0xEE7, sets the timeout word at +0xF70 to -1 and constructs the object at +0xF76.
evidence: FACTS.md records that 0x0051CBF8 builds the 0xF80-byte FatalErrInfo, and the confident caller Fs_ReportFatalError (0x001D033C, 0.72) documents it: it allocates 0xF90 stack bytes, calls this, writes the nn::Result to errInfo+0x04 and submits through Err_LaunchFatalErrorApplet. The second caller 0x0033598C does the same with word 0 = 2. The old 'Sound_ChannelWork_Ctor' name came from the poisoned Sound_Driver_* range.

name: Err_LaunchFatalErrorApplet
summary: Launches the nn::err fatal-error applet for an already filled FatalErrInfo: queries the err service (tolerating the 'already configured' code 0xC8A0CFFC), stops the previous session, runs the err driver setup with the 0xF80 struct and the current display timing, and writes the returned state byte.
evidence: The caller is the named Fs_ReportFatalError, whose body builds the 0xF80-byte nn::err::FatalErrInfo via 0x0051CBF8 and passes it here; FACTS.md records 0x51BA34..0x51CD40 as CTR SDK nn::err (result 0xC8A0CFFC), so the previous 'Sound_Driver_Reconfigure' named the wrong library entirely.

name: Err_ThrowFatalError
summary: Final step of the nn::err fatal-error path: queries the error state (0x0051C508 with argument 0x406) and, unless the result is success or the tolerated 0xC8A0CFFC, aborts through 0x0011C814.
evidence: NEW: the only two bl sites in the whole image are the fatal-error construction paths - 0x001D035C inside Fs_ReportFatalError, right after 0x0051CBF8 builds the FatalErrInfo, and 0x003359A8 which builds the same structure - so this is the throw/abort step of nn::err, as FACTS.md places the whole 0x0051BA34..0x0051CD40 range. Note: 0x0051CCFC is a mid-function split symbol; the real entry is 0x0051CCF8, whose 'ldr r0,[pc,#0x20]' loads the 0x406 argument that the decompiled body is missing.

name: Container_ByteBuffer_Append
signature: void Container_ByteBuffer_Append(ContainerByteBuffer* buf, void* data, int size)
summary: Appends size bytes to a byte buffer: memcpy to buf->data + buf->used and advance the used counter.
evidence: func_00116A14(*arg1 + arg1[1], data, size) = memcpy, then arg1[1] += size; sole caller 0x5593E4 in the model/resource packing area.

name: Container_ByteBuffer_AlignTo
summary: Rounds the buffer's used size up to the given power-of-two alignment and zero-fills the padding.
evidence: used = (used + alignment - 1) & ~(alignment - 1); func_001113EC(*arg1 + oldUsed, aligned - oldUsed) zero-fills the gap; sole caller 0x5593E4 (same packer as Container_ByteBuffer_Append).

name: maybe_std_StringSubstrClamped
signature: void maybe_std_StringSubstrClamped(u32 str, u32 length, int pos, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Five-argument thunk (real entry 0x0051D03C, which pushes r0-r3): clamps arg2 to arg3+1 and tail-calls the range helper 0x001001C4 with (arg1, clamped, arg4, &arg5). Whether that helper builds a string range or throws is still open, so the substring reading is unproven.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0051D03C-0x0051D064 is 'push {r0-r3}; push {r4,lr}; add r4,r2,#1; cmp r1,r4; movhi r1,r4; blx 0x1001c4' - a clamp-and-forward thunk, not the 540-byte function the doc claims; no bl/b to it exists in asm/text, so the xref callers (Model_Instance_UpdateFromParams, Anim_IsInstanceBusy) are stale.

name: Fx_ChannelGroup_UpdateUnits
summary: Steps every unit of an FX channel group for count sub-steps: for each unit whose f_24 matches the group's channel id it calls the unit vtable slots +8/+0x18 (and +0x1C when the template flag bit 0 is set), then releases the finished units through 0x005306CC.
evidence: Its only caller is the named Fx_System_UpdateChannelGroups (0x0052F988), which walks the channel-list table at self+0x120 and passes one group node plus a sub-step count; the body walks group[4..group[2]] and calls the unit vtables, so nothing here is sound code - the old 'Sound_UpdateVoiceGroup' name was wrong.

name: Fx_System_InitRandomVectorTables
summary: Allocates the two 512-entry vec3 tables (0x1800 bytes each) used by the particle emitter: the first is filled with xorshift128 random vectors in [-1,1), the second holds the same vectors normalised to unit length, and both are published through the globals at 0x7B0034.
evidence: Its only caller is the confident Fx_System_Init, and the sibling table builder Math_InitSinTable128 (0x5230B4) is called from the same init; both allocate from the same 512-entry pool, so 'init-time table setup' is now certain.

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_ReleaseTwo
summary: Releases both resources held by the global slot pair at 0x7B0034 by calling the object's virtual release slot (vtable+0xC) once per word, then clears the pair. Same idiom as the single-slot releasers.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Fx_System_Shutdown, which tears down the tables 0x51D3E8/0x5230B4 allocate; releasing both published pointers there is the only consistent reading.

name: Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad
summary: Main per-particle render-data builder: advances the LCG at +0x8C, samples the RNG tables, decides whether the particle uses the object-local or the world transform, and writes the quad's position, size and colour fields. Called from every emission variant and from the emitter update paths.
evidence: Reads self+0x8C LCG (multiply by g_0051D920, add 0x3039), iVar14->f_2E0/f_314 scale terms, arg2[0x4F]/[0x50] point at +0x28/+0x58 or at transformed copies, RNG table g_0051D930 indexed by the u16 at self+0x8A. Four callers in this batch (0x51E834/0x51F5B8/0x51F93C/0x51FFE8) plus the 0x52xxxx update functions.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesFromGlobalVelocity
summary: Particle spawn loop that takes each particle's velocity from the global constant vector g_0051EB18 instead of the emitter's random table, clamps the spawn count with g_0051EB00/g_0051EB04 and hands each particle to the shared quad builder.
evidence: The shared builder is the confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad and the node allocator 0x00530798 is named too, so the spawn-loop reading holds; the emitter type that selects this variant is still inferred, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Fx_InitSpawnedParticle
summary: Initialises one freshly allocated particle: stores the emitter back-pointer, builds its transform copy, draws the spawn velocity/size/lifetime values from the emitter RNG ranges, applies the spawn-direction flags and links it into the emitter's active list.
evidence: All fifteen maybe_Fx_EmitParticles* variants call it immediately after taking a particle from the pool (in the render-path else branch), and the body fills particle[0x54]/[0x56], the RNG-driven velocity and the active-list links - that is particle initialisation, not a quad build.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomRadius
summary: Emission variant that randomises the spawn radius (one RNG draw, then the square root of the squared radius) before handing each particle to the shared quad builder.
evidence: The shared builder Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad is now confidently named, which supports the emit-variant reading, but the radius distribution is still derived from the arithmetic alone and the function has no direct caller; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOriented
summary: Emission variant that draws three random angles and multiplies them into a rotation matrix (0x12551C) so each spawned particle gets its own orientation before the quad is built.
evidence: The shared Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee plus the 0x12551C matrix multiply support the oriented emission, but the orientation reading is still an inference from the three angle draws and there is no caller; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialSpread
summary: Emission variant that spreads particles radially around the emitter axis: two square roots per particle (one for the radial offset, one for the height) before the quad build.
evidence: The shared builder is a confident name; the radial reading still comes only from the pair of square roots and the axis constants, and there is no direct caller to corroborate it, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRing
summary: Ring/disc emission: takes a random radius factor, scales it by (1 - distance/radius) and a square root, orients the offset with the 16-byte RNG table at g_005209A8 and writes the quad.
evidence: The shared quad builder is confidently named; the ring/disc shape is inferred from the radial factor and the RNG-table orientation, not from a caller, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists
summary: Removes a particle node from the emitter's active or pending doubly-linked list (selected by particle->f_158), decrements the list counter, clears the 'linked' word at +0x144 and releases the render data when +0x154 is set.
evidence: Pointer swaps on emitter->f_E0/f_E4/f_E8/f_EC and neighbours' +0x148/+0x14C; decrements f_10 or f_14; 'self->f_144 = 0'; if (f_154) func_0052F664(*self->f_150->f_1c). Six callers in this batch (all the list-update functions).

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesBox
summary: Box/axis emission: splits the spawn count between the X and Z axes with the LCG, offsets each particle along the chosen axis and leaves the other component on the centre line (no square root is used).
evidence: The shared builder is a confident name; the box shape is still read off the two-axis split in the body, with no named caller to confirm the emitter type, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesSphere
summary: Spherical-shell emission: computes the radius as sqrt((1 - r) + r^2*(1 - r)) so particles land on the emitter's sphere surface, then builds the quad.
evidence: The shared Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad callee is confident; the sphere formula is a body reading only and no caller confirms the emitter type, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesOriented
summary: Fully oriented emission: builds a 4x4 basis from the three stored angles, optionally rotates the particle direction with 0x12551C and writes the quad; supports an alternate orientation source.
evidence: The shared quad builder and the 0x12551C multiply are visible, but the 'oriented' reading is an inference from the matrix build and there is no caller that names the emitter type; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesCone
summary: Cone emission: the radial factor is r + (1-r)*(1 - distance^2), giving a density that falls off towards the cone base, then each particle goes through the shared quad builder.
evidence: The shared Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad builder is confident, but the cone shape is still read from the falloff formula only and no direct caller names the emitter type; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleTarget
signature: float* Fx_UpdateParticleTarget(int self, int particle, float* keyframe)
summary: Applies one keyframe of the particle's steering target: each enabled axis (mask in keyframe[4]) eases the velocity towards the target position, either in object space or (when the emitter has a transform at f_CC) in world space after matrix multiply/inverse.
evidence: Mask tests 'fVar1 & 1/2/4'; 'arg2->f_24 = arg2->f_24 + *arg3 * ((target - arg2->f_c) - arg2->f_24) * in_s0'; func_001252E8/func_0012551C used for the transformed branch; returns arg3+6. Five callers in this batch.

name: Fx_AddParticleOffset
signature: u32* Fx_AddParticleOffset(int self, int particle, u32* data)
summary: Adds a table-driven offset to the particle's position: reads the next entry of the 12-byte offset table at g_005222FC (index at self+0x88) and scales it by the three values in the parameter block.
evidence: func_0011CD80 (a pointer/key test on arg2+4/*arg3); index 'f88 = self->f_88++' & 0xFFFF01FF into (g_005222FC + idx*0xC); arg2->f_24 += v0*arg3[1] etc.; returns arg3+4. Five callers in this batch.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesArc
summary: Arc emission: spaces particles evenly along an arc by stepping the angle with 1/(count-1) and emits them along the rotating axis; a single particle falls back to the base angle.
evidence: The shared quad builder is confident and the even-angle stepping is visible in the body, but nothing external confirms the emitter type and there is no caller; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_Release
summary: Releases one global resource slot (the 0x7B0030 table allocated by Math_InitSinTable128) through its virtual release slot and clears the published pointer.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Shutdown immediately next to 0x51D5B4, and it clears the pointer that Math_InitSinTable128 publishes; the single-release variant of the same idiom.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleScaleFromKeyframe
signature: short* maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleScaleFromKeyframe(FxParticle* self, u32* particle, short* keyframe)
summary: Applies one 6-word keyframe record to a particle: tracks the running maximum in particle[4], copies the base size into particle[1]/particle[0], and when the record's transform flag is set rotates the velocity triple particle[9..0xB] through the emitter basis and negates one component by the record's factor. Returns the next record.
evidence: The four per-particle updaters that call it (0x5237C4/0x524390/0x5257E8/0x526F38) call 0x00523184 immediately after, so the pair is the keyframe stepper; the record is 6 words (returns keyframe+6) and the fields written are size and velocity, so 'ScaleFromKeyframe' covers only half of what it does.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomB
summary: Emission variant combining one RNG draw, a square root and the shared quad builder; differs from 0x51F5B8 in the field set it initialises (it uses the 0x5227C4 distance bias).
evidence: Only the shared builder is a confident name; the B suffix exists because the body is a close copy of another variant, and no caller or constant proves the difference, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedB
summary: Second random-orientation emission variant: one RNG draw plus a 0x12551C matrix multiply and two square roots; writes orientation-related fields on the particle before the quad build.
evidence: The shared builder is confirmed, but the B/C variants differ only in which emitter fields they inherit, which no caller or constant proves; maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Math_InitSinTable128
summary: Builds the effect system's 128-entry sine table: for i in 0..0x7F it stores sin(i/128 * 2*pi) * 0.5 + 0.5, interpolating from the existing 256-entry sine table at 0x741AFC with 24-bit fraction, and publishes the table through 0x007B0030.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Init together with 0x51D3E8 (the random-vector tables); the 0x741AFC table it reads is the shared 256-entry sine table used by 0x125034, so the build-from-sine role of this loop is confirmed.

name: Fx_UpdateParticlePosition
signature: int* Fx_UpdateParticlePosition(FxParticle* self, FxParticleState* particle, int* keyframe)
summary: Eases the particle position (f_C/f_10/f_14) toward the keyframe target by rate*dt, optionally transforming the target through the emitter basis first; returns the next keyframe record (keyframe+5).
evidence: The body is unambiguous: particle->f_C += keyframe[4]*(keyframe[1]-particle->f_C)*dt for all three components, and the four per-particle updaters (0x5237C4/0x524390/0x5257E8/0x526F38) call it right after the scale step. The dt arrives in s0, which Ghidra dropped as in_s0 (VFP argument trap, not damage).

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedC
summary: Third random-orientation emission variant (one RNG draw, one matrix multiply, two square roots); differs from 0x522BA8 in which particle fields it inherits from the emitter.
evidence: Same body family as 0x522BA8 with a different inherited-field set; no external evidence distinguishes the two, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleA
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type A: looks up the emitter's transform/keyframes and advances position, steering and scale for the single particle.
evidence: The named callers maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR (0x0052D010) and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListU (0x0052DF78) pass one particle per iteration, and the callee set is the named Fx_AddParticleOffset/Fx_UpdateParticleTarget plus the keyframe appliers - so it is per-particle; the A letter only records the type ordinal, maybe_ 0.45.

summary: Per-particle update that integrates position, dispatches the three per-emitter update tables at 0x007B2CAC/0x007B2CCC/0x007B2CE8 and applies the scale/rotation/lifetime curves.
evidence: Two named list updaters (0x0052BBC4, 0x0052BE8C) call it once per particle, and the three global function tables explain the indirect calls; the old 'ListB' implied a list walk, so the name is corrected but the B letter still only records the ordinal - maybe_ at 0.45.

summary: Per-particle update that re-caches the emitter transform (0x005254FC), integrates velocity, applies the fade factors and writes the world position into the render node.
evidence: The named list updaters 0x0052C58C and 0x0052C6AC call it once per particle; the transform-cache call and four fade factors are clear, but the variant letter cannot be resolved, so the old 'ListC' is corrected to per-particle and kept maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleD
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type D through the shared per-particle frame/keyframe pipeline (offset, target, scale, position, extra block) with this type's flag set.
evidence: The named callers maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListQ (0x0052CD5C) and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListT (0x0052DC28) call it once per particle, and the body has the same structure and callee set as 0x005257E8/0x005237C4; the list wording came from the batch grouping, not from the code, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Fx_ApplyParticleStateThunk
summary: 16-byte thunk: 'push {r4,lr}; bl 0x0052E08C; pop {r4,pc}' forwards both arguments unchanged to Fx_ApplyParticleState.
evidence: Disassembly 0x005248B0-0x005248B8 is exactly push/bl 0x52e08c/pop with no argument shuffling, so it is a pure thunk; the R_T01 batch already renamed it Fx_ApplyParticleStateThunk, which the disassembly confirms. The batch's old 'UpdateParticleFlagsA' name described the callee's effect, not this function.

name: Fx_ApplyParticleStateThunk2

evidence: Disassembly 0x005248C0-0x005248C8 is 'push {r4,lr}; bl 0x52e08c; pop {r4,pc}', byte-identical to 0x005248B0; the R_T01 batch already renamed it Fx_ApplyParticleStateThunk2, which the disassembly confirms.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleColorA
summary: Interpolates the emitter template's f_368/f_36C pair by the particle's lifetime fraction into the particle's f_78/f_7C. The pair is a two-component ramp (colour or UV offset); nothing in the body proves which.
