summary: Same template interpolation as 0x00524900 plus five '+= coefficient*dt' accumulators (f_74/f_80/f_84/f_88/f_8C), so a fading particle keeps drifting its colour/UV channels.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same interpolation as 0x00524900 followed by five accumulators; no caller and no named callee, so the channel meaning stays inferred.

name: Fx_ApplyAllParticleStates
summary: Applies both particle render-state groups: calls Fx_ApplyParticleState once with mode 0 and once with mode 1, so the particle's two packed state words are refreshed together.
evidence: The callee Fx_ApplyParticleState is now confident (0.50) and documented as 'applies one group of particle render flags'; this wrapper is exactly two calls with modes 0 and 1, i.e. both groups. The old name 'SetParticleFlags' described it as writing a flag word, which the body never does.

name: Fx_IntegrateParticleVelocity
summary: Simple Euler integration of the particle position from its velocity using the frame delta (float register s0), then applies the particle state flags.
evidence: self->f_48/4C/50 += self->f_54/58/5C * in_s0; then func_0052E08C(self, 1).

name: Fx_CopyEmitterBaseTransform
summary: Refreshes the emitter (0x005254FC) and copies its two strided transform triples (f_34/f_44/f_54 and f_64/f_74/f_84) into the particle's cached slots (f_E8/f_F8/f_108 and f_118/f_128/f_138).
evidence: The neighbouring updater 0x00523184 reads the same f_34/f_44/f_54 triple as the emitter basis before transforming a target, and this function copies exactly that triple (plus the f_64/f_74/f_84 one) into the particle's cache; the six stores are certain.

name: maybe_Fx_CopyEmitterBaseTransformScaled
summary: Same transform copy as 0x00524C68 but first multiplies the particle scale by f_300 + (1 - f_300)*(1 - dt), so a fading particle inherits a shrunk base transform.
evidence: The fade re-scaling is clear (a 0.5-style lerp with in_s0) and the copy matches its pair 0x00524C68, but the field meaning is inferred and there is no caller, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialC
summary: Radial emission variant driven by the emitter's lifetime accumulator: computes a random radius and writes the particle quad, returning an integer status instead of the usual float.
evidence: The shared builder is confidently named, but the public wrapper 0x005307E0 that dispatches the float-returning variants was not followed for this one, so the u32 return is unexplained and the name stays provisional at 0.35.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialD
summary: Another radial emission variant: one square root per particle and a different RNG table, used by an emitter type whose distribution is a flat disc.
evidence: The shared builder is confirmed; the flat-disc reading comes only from the arithmetic and no caller corroborates it, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Gfx_TryConvertBuffer
signature: int Gfx_TryConvertBuffer(int handle, int arg2, int arg3, int src, int dst)
summary: Boolean guard around the buffer conversion at 0x00505FD8: rejects a -1 handle or a null source/destination and returns 1 only when the conversion does not report the high-bit error flag. The disassembly shows the whole function is 0x44 bytes, so the 632-byte size is Ghidra merging the following routine.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00525494..0x005254D4 is only 0x44 bytes (a new function starts at 0x005254D8), and it is a pure success/failure wrapper: cmn r0,#1 / cmpne r3,#0 / cmpne ip,#0 then bl 0x505FD8 and tst r0,#0x80000000. So it reports whether the conversion succeeded rather than copying a buffer, which is what CopyBufferChecked implied.

name: Fx_CommitParticleStream
summary: Flushes the pending particle vertices into the global stream at 0x007AFF18: copies the node's f_28 block (count = pending*6) and then its f_10 block, advances the write cursor and returns it. Four list updaters tail-call it after filling the records.
evidence: Four named list updaters (0x52BBC4/0x52C58C/0x52CD5C/0x52D010) end with a b/bl to it, and the body is two memcpys into 0x007AFF18[0] followed by 'return advanced pointer' - a stream commit, not an RNG seed.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleE
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type E: applies the emitter's speed/gravity/steering flags, advances the keyframe/scale/rotation tracks, writes the resulting vertex position into the effect command buffer and bumps the particle age.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR (0x0052D010) dispatches to it per particle next to maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleA, and the body writes the PICA command block plus per-particle vertex fields through the named Fx_AddParticleOffset/Fx_UpdateParticleTarget - so it updates one particle; the type letter stays because five sibling variants exist, maybe_ 0.45.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleF
summary: Per-particle integration for emitter type F: transforms the velocity through the emitter basis, updates the sprite/scale accumulators, recomputes the two normal pairs through Fx_ComputeParticleNormal and applies the colour/state step through 0x0052E4AC.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListL (0x0052BBC4) calls it once per particle in its else branch, and the body is one particle's whole frame update, not a list walk; the old 'ListF' was a batch artifact, so the name is corrected but the F type letter still only records the ordinal - maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleG
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type G through the shared per-particle frame/keyframe pipeline with this type's flag set.
evidence: Four named particle-list dispatchers (L/N/Q/R) call it per particle before choosing the concrete list writer, and the body has the same structure and named helpers as the E/H variants; the G letter still only records the emitter-type ordinal, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticlesInline
summary: Interior address, not a function entry: the disassembly at 0x00526814 is 'ldr fp,[r2,#0x548]' in the middle of the particle update loop, so Ghidra's halt_baddata body is an artefact. Kept as a marker.
evidence: asm/text/text_00500048.s shows unbroken ARM instructions across 0x00526814 (0x00526810 vldmia sl!,{s14}; 0x00526814 ldr fp,[r2,#0x548]); no bl/b to it exists, so it is a mid-function split symbol.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleH
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type H: same per-particle frame/keyframe pipeline as the other Fx_UpdateParticle variants (offset, target, scale, position, extra block) with this type's flag set.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListQ (0x0052CD5C) dispatches to it per particle alongside Fx_UpdateParticleG/D, and the body has the same structure and callee set (Fx_AddParticleOffset, Fx_UpdateParticleTarget, keyframe appliers) as the H sibling - it is a per-particle integrator, but 'H' still only records the emitter-type ordinal, so maybe_ 0.45.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleTransform
summary: Copies a caller-supplied 3-float vector into the particle's render-transform block: values[2] to +0x60, values[1] to +0x64, values[0] to +0x68 (the engine stores the triple in reverse component order), then notifies the batch (0x52E3C8) and advances the emitter frame.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00527758: ldm r2,{r2,r3,ip}; ldr r1,[r1]; str ip,[r1,#0x60]!; str r3,[r1,#4]; str r2,[r1,#8] - a plain 3-word store, no matrix. The sibling 0x00528780 writes the same three floats from self+0x3C..0x44 into the shared render record, so the triple is a vector, but nothing names which vector; all four callers are maybe_ UpdateParticleList* walkers.

name: maybe_Fx_ResetParticleTransform
summary: Clears only the particle's +0x6C word (the fourth word of the render-transform block) and notifies the batch; it does not touch the three floats at +0x60/+0x64/+0x68, so 'Reset' means 'drop the marker', not 'zero the transform'.
evidence: Body is a single store of 0 to *particle+0x6C plus the batch notify and Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame; the same word is cleared by 0x00528750 and left untouched by 0x00527758, so it is a marker word, but no caller or vtable sibling says what it marks.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI
signature: int maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI(int self, int particle, int keyframe, int flags)
summary: Per-particle update that walks the particle's child chain, emits sprite quads through Fx_UpdateParticleSprite and advances the shared vertex-stream pointer 0x007AFF18 in 0x12-entry batches.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListQ (0x0052CD5C), which dispatches it for emitter kind 5; the emission mechanics are clear, but the batch size (0x12) and child-chain offsets are decompiler inferences, so maybe_ at 0.38.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleRotation
summary: Same three-float store as 0x00527758 (values[0] to +0x68, values[1] to +0x64, values[2] to +0x60) plus an explicit clear of the +0x6C marker word, then the batch notify and frame advance.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00528750 is 0x00527758 plus 'mov r2,#0; str r2,[r1,#0xc]' - identical stores, one extra clear. That makes the 'Rotation' half of the name unverifiable: the two functions write the same vector and differ only in the marker word.

name: maybe_Fx_ApplyParticleRotation
summary: Writes the particle's f_3C/f_40/f_44 triple into the current vertex record (+0x60/+0x64/+0x68), flushes the node block (0x0052E3C8) and tail-jumps to the vertex flush 0x0052E784. The triple is a 3-component vector; rotation is only one candidate.
evidence: Disassembly 0x005287B4-0x005287E8: ldm r1,{r1,r2,r3} from self+0x3C, three stores at [r0,#0x60]!/[r0,#4]/[r0,#8], bl 0x52e3c8, b 0x52e784. Its sibling 0x00529A60 writes the same three words and additionally clears +0x6C, so the triple is a record field, not proven to be a rotation.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ
signature: float maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ(int self, float dt, float* particle, float* extra)
summary: Largest per-particle update variant: integrates the particle, resolves the parent transform, emits its sprite quads and links the particle into the active/free lists.
evidence: The body is 0xAA0 bytes of heavy FP control flow (in_fpscr/NAN/SQRT) and its only caller is the maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListQ dispatcher, which calls it for emitter kind 6; no field or helper is named enough to pin the variant, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSprite
signature: u32* maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSprite(u32 self, u32* out, void* particle, float* colour, int flag, int flag2, int flag3)
summary: Emits one particle sprite's draw record: scales the template colour by the frame colour, writes the 0x28-word PICA vertex/UV/colour block and returns the advanced write pointer.
evidence: The body appends the command words 0x8000004C/0x000F02C0/0x023F02C1 and returns the advanced pointer, so it emits rather than updating stored state; the four calls per particle from maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI confirm the emit role.

name: maybe_Fx_ResetParticleSprite
signature: void maybe_Fx_ResetParticleSprite(u32 self, u32 arg2, int* particleRef)
summary: Clears the +0x6C word of the current vertex record and flushes it (0x0052E3C8, then tail-jump to 0x0052E784). The +0x6C word is a per-record flag; 'sprite' is a guess.
evidence: Disassembly is three statements: str #0 into [*particleRef+0x6C], bl 0x52e3c8, b 0x52e784. Its siblings 0x005287B4/0x00529A60 write the same record and 0x00529A60 also clears +0x6C, so the clear is certain but the flag's meaning is not.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSpriteB
signature: u32* maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSpriteB(u32 self, u32* out, void* particle, float* colour, int flag, int flag2, int flag3)
summary: Second particle-sprite emit path: same 0x28-word draw record, but the UV/position terms come from the emitter template at +0xDC instead of the keyframe copy.
evidence: Same field set and command words as 0x0052943C with the template base, so it is a variant emitter rather than a new operation; its caller maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ keeps both sides below 0.5.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleSpriteFromNode
summary: Variant of 0x005287B4: writes the f_3C/f_40/f_44 triple into the current vertex record (+0x60/+0x64/+0x68), clears the record's +0x6C flag, flushes the node block and tail-jumps to 0x0052E784.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00529A60-0x00529A9C is the same store sequence as 0x005287B4 plus 'str #0,[r0,#0xc]' (record +0x6C); no bl/b to it exists in asm/text, so the five named callers in the old xref (Fx_System_Init, Fx_DestroyEmitter, ...) are stale.

name: Gfx_ModelResource_Release
signature: int Gfx_ModelResource_Release(GfxModelResource* self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Releases a parsed model resource: frees the two owned blocks at +0xC and +0x954 with the graphics allocator and issues the GPU teardown commands for the remaining sub-resources.
evidence: The sole caller is now the named Gfx_ModelResource_Parse (0x529DC0), the frees use Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock (0x532388) and the queue calls are the named Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntry* helpers, so the release role is confirmed.

name: Gfx_ModelResource_Parse
signature: int Gfx_ModelResource_Parse(GfxModelResource* self, void* owner, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Parses a complete model resource: allocates a 0x2B0 work block from the owner's allocator, recognises the resource-set header through Gfx_ResourceSet_Parse, converts the referenced buffers to physical GPU addresses and builds the sub-resources (resource sets, vertex streams, materials) for the model instance.
evidence: 0xCC0-byte body; (*(owner_vtable+8))(owner,0x2B0,0x80) allocation, Os_VirtualToPhysical on the payload addresses, calls Gfx_ResourceSet_Parse (0x5064CC), 0x509160/0x50949C (resource-set format/slot), 0x529BD0 (release on failure); sole caller Fx_System_Init (0x52E9C8).

name: Fx_System_ReleaseAllParts
summary: Releases every part of the effect system: the named sub-objects at +0x18/+0x24/+0x30/+0x600/+0x96C/+0x978, the 30 texture/anim slots at +0x3C, and the two large buffers at +0x8/+0x954, then clears the "initialised" flag. Called from the Fx system shutdown 0x5308AC; the 30-entry x 12-byte table and the six list heads are the effect-system part table.
evidence: loops i<0x1E over arg1[i*3+0xF] freeing via vtable+0xC; func_00532388 on arg1[3]/arg1[0x255]; g_0052ac64=0x102; called by 0x005308AC (Fx_System_Shutdown)

name: Fx_EmitterInitFromTemplate
summary: Initialises an emitter instance from its template at +0xDC: copies the spawn box, scale, colour and curve parameters, then builds the module pointer list from the module array at +0x100 and sets the per-module capability flags.
evidence: Its caller is the confident Fx_SpawnEmitter, which is the only thing that would clone a template into a live emitter; the field block it copies matches the template layout used by that spawner.

name: Fx_Emitter_SelectUpdateModes
summary: Turns the emitter template's flag word (bits 2/8/9/0xD and the 0x10/0x40/0x80 group) into the six small mode bytes at +0x290..+0x295 that the per-particle updaters switch on.
evidence: NEW: its only caller is the confident Fx_EmitterReset (0x0052B7F4), and the body contains no calls and no module list at all - it only tests template bits and writes the six selector bytes, which is exactly what the name claims.

name: Fx_EmitterRandomizeSpawn
summary: Computes the emitter's random spawn orientation: advances the LCG (seed*0x41C64E6D+0x3039) three times per axis, maps each value through the 8-byte range table at 0x00741AFC and builds the two 3x3 spawn matrices at +0x200 and +0x1D0.
evidence: New context: it is called by the confident Fx_EmitterReset and by the two emitter frame updates, and the range table + LCG + matrix construction match the template's angle ranges, so 'randomise spawn' is supported; kept at 0.50 rather than higher because the template fields are still unnamed.

name: Fx_EmitterReset
summary: Resets a live emitter: clears the state words, stores the owner id at +0xDC, installs the default parameter block from g_0052B9BC and re-runs the module and spawn-transform updates.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_SpawnEmitter right after the template init, and it re-runs Fx_EmitterUpdateModules (0x52Bxxx family); a reset/rebind step is the only consistent reading.

name: maybe_Fx_InterpolateParticlePair
signature: void maybe_Fx_InterpolateParticlePair(float* outA, float* outB, FxParticle* self, int templateRec)
summary: Scales the template's f_30/f_34 pair by the particle's lifetime fraction and writes the two results to self+0x1E/+0x1F. The sprite emitters use those as the quad centre (self[0x1E]+self[0x20], self[0x1F]-self[0x21]), so the old 'normal' reading is not supported; the pair's exact meaning is still open.
evidence: Both call sites (0x00525E70 line 169 and 0x00526F38 line 184) pass (self+0x1E, self+0x1F, self, self[0x51]+0x338) and the second pair (self+0x26, self+0x27, self[0x51]+0x3B0), and the body is the same lifetime-fraction interpolation as the colour pair 0x00524900/0x00524A10 - a two-component template ramp, not a normal vector.

name: Fx_SampleKeyframeCurve
summary: Samples a keyframe curve at a time: binary-searches the (time, value) pairs starting at +0x14, interpolates between the two bracketing keys and wraps the time with fmodf when the curve loops.
evidence: The caller is now Fx_BuildEmitterTransformMatrices, which is exactly where an emitter curve gets sampled; the 2-floats-per-key layout and std_Fmodf are unchanged.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListL
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListL(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Walks the particle's active sub-particle list (head at particle+0xE0, next at +0x14C): live entries get the per-particle update plus a vtable call, dead ones are unlinked with Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists, and the processed count lands in particle+0x284 before Fx_CommitParticleStream.
evidence: Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists is now confident (0.50) and is called by every member of this family at exactly the 'entry is dead' branch; the walk shape (f_E0 head, f_14C next, f_284 counter) is identical across L/M/N/O/Q/T, so only the letter disambiguates the per-particle helper each one uses.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterTarget
signature: void maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterTarget(FxEmitter* self, int arg2, int target)
summary: Interpolates the emitter's position from (f_34,f_44,f_54) toward the target (f_98,f_A0) in fixed-size steps, calling the emitter's per-step callback from the table at 0x007AEB6C for every intermediate position.
evidence: Both emitter update variants (0x0052C26C and 0x0052F10C) call it when their step condition is met, and the distance clamp/step loop is visible, but the callback table and target fields are unnamed, so 'update emitter target' is a description rather than a proven contract - maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListM
summary: Short active-list updater: walks particle+0xE0 applying maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleB to live entries and unlinking dead ones, but when the emitter flag 0x400 is set it walks the alternate list at particle+0xE8 (next at +0x148) instead.
evidence: Same walker shape as its five siblings (f_E0/f_14C, f_284 counter) with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) on the dead branch; the 0x400 flag selects the second list head at +0xE8, which is the only structural difference from L.

name: Fx_BuildEmitterTransformMatrices
summary: Rebuilds the two 3x4 orientation matrices an emitter uses while spawning (the local basis at +0x1D0 and the world basis at +0x200): converts the emitter's three rotation angles to sine/cosine through the shared fixed-point trig table, expands them into a scaled orthonormal basis, stamps the two 32-bit spawn values (+0x18C/+0x194) into the matrix and copies the emitter's current frame number into every live particle module so newly spawned particles start on the right frame.
evidence: Only caller 0x0052F10C (Fx_UpdateEmitterTransform) calls it right before copying both matrices to the template at +0x1D0/+0x1A0 through 0x0012515C. Matrix pair written at emitter+0x1D0 (indices 0x74..0x7F) and emitter+0x200 (0x80..0x8B); g_0052C260 scales the euler angles into table units, 0x00125034 is the fixed-point sincos table lookup (index in the top 8 bits, Q24 fraction below), g_0052C264 converts the Q24 fraction and g_0052C268 is the sin/cos table base. First loop walks emitter[0x41] live particle pointers and writes the frame stamp through the module pointer at particle+8.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterFrame
summary: Frame update of an emitter driven by another object: reads the owner clock at +0x53C, advances the emitter timeline and calls the target, curve and transform updates.
evidence: There is no caller and the body is nearly identical to 0x0052F10C (same Fx_DestroyEmitter/Fx_EmitterRandomizeSpawn callees), so the split between 'frame' and 'transform' is still an interpretation; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListN
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListN(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Active-list updater that pairs maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleC (dead entries) with 0x526B98 plus the vtable call (live entries), counts them in particle+0x284 and commits the stream through maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream.
evidence: Identical control flow to Fx_UpdateParticleListL with a different per-particle helper pair; the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) and maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream appear at the same two points, which fixes the 'walk and update the active list' role.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListO
summary: Minimal active-list updater: walks particle+0xE0 calling maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleC for each live entry, unlinks dead entries with Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists and counts the processed entries in particle+0x284.
evidence: The smallest member of the family (24 lines) and the clearest: one list head, one per-particle helper, the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) on the dead branch and the shared f_284 counter.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleTrail
signature: void maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleTrail(int self, float* particle, int update)
summary: Maintains a particle's 0x58-byte-stride trail history: smooths with 0.7, advances the ring write indices and appends the current position/rotation segments.
evidence: The body works on the 0x584C..0x586C ring of 0x58-byte segments with the 0x3F333333 (0.7) smoothing and calls std_FastSinCos/std_Expf, which is a trail/ribbon update rather than a generic list walk. The 0x58 segment layout is still inferred from offsets and the caller is a maybe_ dispatcher.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListQ
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListQ(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Full active-list updater: resets the list through 0x527738, walks particle+0xE0 with maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleH plus the vtable call for live entries and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleD for dead ones, re-applies maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListP per entry and commits the stream.
evidence: Same walker skeleton as L/M/N/O/T (f_E0 head, f_14C next, f_284 counter) with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) and maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream at the same points; it is the richest variant, not a dispatcher - the four 'sibling' calls are the per-entry helpers, not a type switch.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR
signature: u32 maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR(FxEmitter* self, u32 list, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 forwarded2)
summary: Active-list updater for one emitter type: walks the live children, advances each particle (0x5237C4/0x5257E8/0x526554), copies the vertex record and tail-jumps to Fx_CommitParticleStream. The R suffix is a positional label.
evidence: Real callees are maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleA/E/G, 0x00527738/0x00527780 and a tail-jump to Fx_CommitParticleStream; no caller exists, so which emitter type uses it stays unknown and the letter remains positional.

name: maybe_Fx_SpawnParticleBatch
summary: Spawn routine: for each of the emitter's remaining f_560 particles it takes a block from the particle pool (0x00530798), initialises position/velocity/colour/scale from the template and its RNG ranges, and links it into the active and free lists.
evidence: Its only caller is maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListP (0x0052C728), which invokes it when a particle's spawn timer elapses, and the body fills exactly the fields the per-particle updaters consume - the old 'UpdateParticleListS' implied a per-particle update, but this really spawns the batch; maybe_ at 0.40 because f_560 and the template block are inferred.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListT
summary: Active-list updater that applies maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleD and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListP to every live entry and, for dead ones, advances the owning emitter's frame counter (f_154) before unlinking; the 0x400 emitter flag selects the alternate list at +0xE8.
evidence: Same walker skeleton as its five siblings with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50); the extra block on the dead branch copies the emitter's f_5C..f_74 words into the render node, which is the same copy Fx_UpdateParticleListR/U perform.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListU
summary: Minimal active-list updater: walks the child list, calls maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleA for the live entries, unlinks expired ones and keeps the particle counter in sync. The U suffix is a positional label.
evidence: Its only real callee is maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleA (0x005237C4) and it has no caller, so it duplicates the non-forwarded path of 0x0052D010 without the variant selector; the emitter type stays unknown.

name: Fx_ApplyParticleState
summary: Applies one group of particle render flags: refreshes the cached transform and writes the packed state words selected by the mode.
evidence: The callers are now Fx_IntegrateParticleVelocity, Fx_SetParticleFlags, maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleFlagsA/B and the tKR wrapper, i.e. the particle-state setters. Some integer inputs are damaged (extraout_r1), hence 0.5.

name: Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame
summary: Advances the global emitter frame counter at 0x0052E3C0 (increment, reset every 8 steps) and refreshes the shared transform cache.

name: maybe_Fx_ApplyParticleStateAlt
summary: Interpolates particle state attributes across lifetime fraction and writes channels into +0xBC/+0xC0/+0xC4.
evidence: Shares interpolation structure with Fx_ApplyParticleState (0x0052E08C); called by unconfirmed particle updaters 0x00525E70 and 0x00526F38; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Fx_FlushParticleNodeBlock
summary: 0x18-byte thunk: calls the shared flush tail 0x0052E3C8 (which copies the current node's f_1C/f_20 block into the stream at 0x007AFF18 and resets the pending count) and returns its argument. It is not a batch begin.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0052E76C-0x0052E780 is 'push {r4,lr}; mov r4,r0; bl 0x52e3c8; mov r0,r4; pop {r4,lr}' - a pure thunk; Ghidra merged the following function's body into it, which is where the 'begin batch' reading came from. 0x0052E3C8 is the flush tail of Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame (0x0052E35C).

name: maybe_Fx_EndParticleBatch
summary: Shared tail of the seven vertex-record writers: clears the pending count, copies the emitter node's f_810 block (f_814 words) to the stream cursor at 0x007AFF18, advances the cursor and increments the batch counter.
evidence: Seven functions tail-jump here (0x00527758, 0x00528750, 0x005287B4, 0x0052943C, 0x00529714, 0x0052973C, 0x00529A60) right after writing a record, and the body is one memcpy of node->f_810 plus a counter bump; 'end batch' describes the flush+count but the buffer roles are still inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_SkeletalAnim_InitFrame
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SkeletalAnim_InitFrame(int self, unsigned char* frame)
summary: Initialises per-frame skeletal-animation work: copies the 0x120-byte default table and selects the offset/size of each node group by the frame kind byte (5/6) and its flags.
evidence: NEW: still no caller (the function is reached through the animation vtable), and the only named callee is std_memcpy; 'skeletal animation' is inferred from the neighbouring animation vtable, so maybe_.

name: Fx_AppendNodeData
summary: Appends a node's data block to the stream: if node[1] (data) and node[2] (word count) are both set, copies node[2] words and returns the advanced pointer; otherwise returns the pointer unchanged.
evidence: Three real callers (0x00526554, 0x005280A8, 0x0052899C) pass one node and use the returned pointer as the next write position, and the body is memcpy(stream, node[1], node[2]<<2) + 'return stream + node[2]*4' - an append, never a list head.

name: Fx_System_Init
signature: void Fx_System_Init(FxSystem* self, int arg2, FxSystemDesc* desc)
summary: Initialises the effect system: stores the pool sizes and geometry descriptions from the descriptor, builds the particle tables (0x51D3E8/0x5230B4), parses the effect model resources (0x529DC0) and constructs the emitter arrays.
evidence: caller maybe_Mem_PoolBlock_Init (0x53082C) passes the Fx work block; calls 0x51D3E8/0x5230B4 (particle tables), 0x529DC0 (model resource) and 0x530AE8; the sibling names in the same range are Fx_System_Dtor (0x53089C), Fx_System_Shutdown (0x5308AC), Fx_System_ReleaseAllParts (0x52AA80), and the descriptor fields 0x448/0x44C/0x324 match the Fx pool layout.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterTransform
summary: Emitter frame update that also rebuilds the emitter transform: reads the owner clock, then runs the target/curve/transform updates and the draw-list calls.
evidence: There is no caller, and the named callees (Fx_DestroyEmitter, Fx_BuildEmitterTransformMatrices, maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterTarget) are shared with the near-identical 0x0052C26C, so which of the two is the transform update is not settled; maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Fx_DestroyEmitter
summary: Destroys one live emitter instance: drains its two child-object lists, drops the emitter's animation link, clears the active flag, decrements the template reference counter (and the manager's template count when it reaches zero) and unlinks the instance from the manager's per-type doubly-linked list, fixing the head/tail pointers. Called by the emitter update paths as soon as the remaining lifetime or the last particle reaches zero.
evidence: Callees 0x005209D8 (destroy/unlink a child node; looped while emitter+0xE0/+0xE4 are non-null) and 0x00529B50 (clear the 2-entry animation link at +0x18); the shared template pointer emitter->f_1C has its +4 word decremented (refcount), manager+0x474 the live-template count and manager+0x328 the released counter; list unlink uses emitter+0xD0/+0xD4 and the per-type head at `manager + emitter->f_18*4 + 0x20`. Callers 0x0052C26C and 0x0052F10C (both emitter frame updates) call it on lifetime <= 0 or when no particles remain.

name: Gfx_ModelSlot_Release
signature: void Gfx_ModelSlot_Release(void* self, void* owner, int slotIndex)
summary: Releases one model-resource slot: takes the object from the table at self->f_C[slotIndex], releases its parts (0x00531D58) and calls the owner's virtual release (vtable +0xC), then clears the table entry.
evidence: Its only caller maybe_Gfx_BindResourceSlot (0x0055DBB8) calls it when the slot is occupied and then binds the replacement through the confident Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace, so this is the release half of that pair; the body clears self->f_C[slotIndex] after the vtable release.

name: Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace
signature: int Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace(void* self, void* owner, u32 arg3, int slotIndex, u32 arg5)
summary: Replaces one model-resource slot: releases the old slot exactly like 0x0052F6D0, allocates a fresh 0x3C-byte 0x80-aligned slot from the owner and initialises it through Gfx_ModelResource_Reset.
evidence: Corrected and confirmed: the release half is identical to the slot release, and the new half calls the confident Gfx_ModelResource_Reset with (owner, arg3, slotIndex, self, arg5); the caller is Gfx_BindResourceSlot, so this is model-resource bookkeeping, not an emitter operation.

name: Fx_Group_DestroyEmitters
summary: Destroys all active emitters in an emitter group: releases their child nodes and animation links, decrements template refcounts on the FX manager, unlinks them from manager lists, and unlinks the group via 0x005306CC.
evidence: Matches Fx_DestroyEmitter (0x0052F4D4) inline loop over group->f_10 emitters with tag check iVar2->f_24 == group->f_c; frees child nodes with 0x005209D8, animation link via 0x00529B50, updates template refcount at iVar2->f_1c+4, and unlinks group via 0x005306CC.

name: Fx_System_UpdateChannelGroups
signature: unsigned int Fx_System_UpdateChannelGroups(Fx_System* self, unsigned int list, int channel, int flag)
summary: Advances the FX system clock and updates all active emitter groups attached to a given channel list, ticking sub-steps via 0x0051D25C and updating emitter nodes through Fx_Group_UpdateEmitters (0x005304AC).
evidence: Belongs to Fx_System (offsets +0x488/+0x48C 64-bit clock, +0x120 channel list table, +0x460/+0x464 stats in callee 0x005304AC); walks group->f_27c links and ticks active emitter groups instead of scene units.

name: Fx_SpawnEmitter
signature: void Fx_SpawnEmitter(FxManager* manager, FxEmitterInstance* emitter, FxSpawnRequest* request, int slot, int entry, u32 seed, int useOwnerClock)
summary: Instantiates one emitter from a spawn request: chooses the particle seed (fixed / drawn from the shared 32-bit LCG / explicit), optionally starts the emitter clock from the owner, resets the instance, copies the spawn position, colour and curve parameters of the requested entry into the emitter, attaches the request's animation references and resolves the two optional child nodes from the owner model's node table.
evidence: Callees Fx_EmitterReset 0x0052B7F4 and Fx_EmitterInitFromTemplate 0x0052AC80; request+8 selects the seed mode (-1 fixed, 0 LCG, else explicit), the LCG state is fetched with 0x0051D5A8; manager->f_c[slot] is the per-slot table, `entry*0x3C` indexes into it (spawn/curve block at +0x18); 0x005321F4 builds the spawn parameter block from request+0x18, 0x00529AB0/0x00529B3C attach the animation links, 0x0052BBB8 applies the owner-node pointer at request+0x190. No direct C callers: reached through the effect-manager function table, so the argument roles come from the body and from the sibling calls in 0x0052C26C/0x0052F10C.

name: maybe_Mem_PoolSlot_Allocate
signature: void* maybe_Mem_PoolSlot_Allocate(PoolOwner* owner, ObjectSlotDesc* desc, uint32_t kind, uint32_t index, uint32_t sub, uint32_t arg6)
summary: Allocates a 0x5880-byte slot from the fixed object pool, links it into the owner's slot list and fills the slot header (kind, owner, descriptor id, zeroed counters); returns null when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: The callers Gfx_ModelInstance_Init/InitWithTransform and the fixed 0x5880 stride support the pool-slot reading, but the body is damaged (SBORROW4/unaff values around the pool index), so the exact field semantics cannot be verified and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Thumb_MisidentifiedEntry
summary: Not a function entry: 0x00530054 is the ARM instruction 'bl 0x00504F30' (word 0xEBFF53B5) inside maybe_Mem_PoolSlot_Allocate (0x00530014), misdecoded as a Thumb push. Kept as a marker.
evidence: asm/text/text_00500048.s decodes 0x00530054 as 'push {r0,r1,r4,r6,lr}' followed by '.short 0xEBFF', i.e. the Thumb decoder lost sync inside an ARM function; no bl/b to it exists.

name: Fx_AllocParticleNode
signature: u32* Fx_AllocParticleNode(FxParticlePool* self, FxParticleType* type, u32 flags)
summary: Hands out one 0x5880-byte block from the fixed pool at self+0x33C using the round-robin cursor self+0x444 masked by self+0x45C, links it into the per-type list at self+type*4+0x340 through the free-list word at +0x5870, stamps the flags/type words and returns it; returns 0 after self+0x450 failed probes.
evidence: The only real caller is the confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad (0.50), which fixes the 'allocate a render block for the quad builder' role; the block is 0x5880 bytes with its list link at +0x5870, so 'node' means a pool node, not a single particle.

name: Fx_Group_UpdateEmitters
signature: int Fx_Group_UpdateEmitters(Fx_System* self, int arg2, Fx_EmitterGroup* group, int skipStart, unsigned int* params)
summary: Updates each active emitter in an effect emitter group: calls emitter lifecycle methods (+8 start, +0x10 update, +0x14 sub-step), accumulates particle and quad stats onto the FX system, and unlinks the group via 0x005306CC when empty.
evidence: Caller 0x0052F988 passes Fx_System and channel group; iterates group->f_10 emitter entries, checking emitter->f_24 == group->f_c and updating FX manager stat fields +0x460/+0x464/+0x46C/+0x480/+0x4D8.

name: Fx_System_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the FX system block: installs vtable 0x0078122C, clears the state byte at +1 and, when the descriptor reports a non-zero element count, lays the element storage out with Fx_System_Init.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0052E9C8 is now named Fx_System_Init, and the constant-level neighbours are Fx_System_Init/Fx_System_Shutdown/Gfx_Texture_InitDescriptor - so the block is an FX system object, not a generic memory pool block. The descriptor call and the +0x4E8 allocation size are unchanged.

name: Fx_System_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the effect system singleton: runs the shutdown and frees the system block. Paired wrapper around 0x5308AC (the shutdown body) + operator delete.
evidence: func_005308AC(); func_0010F6CC=operator delete; pointer at 0x781230 next to 0x78122C (the vtable installed by 0x5308AC)

name: Fx_System_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the effect system down: installs vtable 0x78122C, frees the cached Fx buffers and the 30-part table, releases the global effect context, and destroys the 0x1E x 0xC slot array. The routine walks the fixed Fx slot offsets (+0x338/+0x4A0/+0x3A8/+0x4A4/+0x4AC/+0x4B0/+0x320/+0x338...), which matches the effect-system pool layout used by 0x52AA80.
evidence: stores g_00530ad8=0x78122C; frees arg1[0x128], [0x129], [0xCF], [0x12A], [299], [300], [200] (0x298-stride parts via 0x529B50); calls 0x51D5B4,0x5225B8,0x52AA80; std_destroy_range(...,0x530AFC,0xC,0x1E); caller 0x53089C

name: Gfx_ResourceSlot_ReleaseArrayEntry
summary: Releases one three-word resource slot (destroy through vtable+0xC, clear owner and handle) and returns the slot. Used as the element destructor of the Fx system's 30-slot resource array.
evidence: Called from the confident Fx_System_Shutdown, which walks the same 30-slot array, and it uses the identical vtable+0xC release idiom as the two siblings above.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource(GfxModelInstance* self, void* owner, GfxResourceSet* res, unsigned int arg4, int arg5, unsigned char* extra)
summary: Builds a drawable model instance from a parsed resource set: fixes the header-relative pointers, registers the resource slots (0x509160/0x509290), converts the vertex/index buffers to physical addresses, allocates the 0x448-byte part blocks and sets up the per-pass draw state.
evidence: 0x121C-byte initialiser; self->f_10 = res->f_10 + res and self->f_14 = res->f_14 + res are relative-pointer fixups; calls 0x509160/0x509290 (resource-set format/slot), 0x525494 (buffer conversion), 0x52E7E8, Os_VirtualToPhysical and std_ConstructArray; sole caller 0x532340.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ReleaseAll
summary: Releases every 0x3C-byte part record of a part list (count from self->f_C+8, records at self->f_18): frees each part's GPU blocks through Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock, optionally keeping the caller's part, and drops the tracked resources.
evidence: The callers are now Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace and Fx_SpawnEmitter, i.e. model-slot replacement/emitter setup, and the named Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock/Gfx_UnregisterResources calls confirm the release pass; the body still has unaff_r4 and the list owner is not fully proven, so maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_ModelResource_Reset
summary: Resets a model resource in place (clears +0xC, the flag byte +0x31 and +0x34) and immediately rebuilds it through Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource.
evidence: The body is the field clear followed by the single confidently named Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource call on the same object, so 'reset and rebuild' is exactly what it does.

name: Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock
signature: void Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock(unsigned int address, unsigned int tag)
summary: Frees a graphics-memory block: classifies the address against the 0x20000/0x30000 allocation regions and returns the block to the matching GPU allocator.
evidence: two region tests against the 0x20000/0x30000 markers via 0x1109D8/0x11099C and then 0x6BA1DC/0x6BA210 (GPU memory allocator); callers Fx_System_ReleaseAllParts (0x52AA80) and 0x529BD0/0x531D58 (model resource release).

name: maybe_Gfx_AllocGraphicsBlockByRegion
signature: int maybe_Gfx_AllocGraphicsBlockByRegion(int address, int block, int regionType, unsigned int arg4, int cmdBuf, int force)
summary: Selects a graphics memory region by kind (1 -> the 0x20000-byte region, 2 -> the 0x30000-byte region), asks that region's allocator (the function pair returned by 0x006BA1DC) for a block and, when a block came back or force is set, submits the resulting transfer through Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntry or SubmitEntryDirect; returns the block pointer. The old Free verb was wrong: the only caller stores the returned pointer.
evidence: The body never releases anything: it calls the region allocator through the function pointer from 0x006BA1DC with the region size (0x20000 / 0x30000) and returns its result, and Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource (the only caller) zeroes the block field, calls this and stores the returned pointer. The region kind is the only thing the two branches change, so the name now says alloc-by-region instead of free-by-type.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks(GfxModelInstance* self, int base, int* desc)
summary: Lays out the model instance's sub-blocks inside the resource buffer: for each sub-block it computes the 0x448-byte slot address, default-constructs the vertex-stream and command-node arrays and records the block offsets in the descriptor.
evidence: The caller Gfx_CharShadow_AllocMeshes and the named callees maybe_Gfx_VertexStream_Ctor / Gfx_CommandNode_InitSixSlots / Gfx_CommandBuffer_PadTo16 / maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots describe exactly the per-sub-block layout work; the 0x448 stride is shared with 0x00533008.

name: maybe_Fx_RenderBatch_Init
summary: Constructor of a render-batch object: zeroes the header, builds three intrusive lists through 0x001252C8 with the same 0x008386FC list template, sets the default depth/near-far values 240.0/400.0 and returns the object at offset -0xD4 of the last allocation.
evidence: The body is a one-shot constructor (0x1D8 bytes of fields zeroed and defaulted, three list heads built, pointer at -0xD4 returned) and not a begin/end batch pair; there is no caller, so the render-batch owner is still inferred - maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupIndices
signature: u32 Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupIndices(int * out, int set, int metadata)
summary: Maps every resource name of a resource set to its u16 index in the metadata table (+0x38), marks missing entries 0xFFFF and returns a status word telling whether all/some/none were found. Called by Gfx_BindIndexedResourceSet; the 0xFFFF sentinel and the 0x80008000/0x4000 return flags are the resource-binding protocol used by the model renderer.
evidence: iterates set->f_10 entries, reads *(u32*)set->f_c[i] as the resource key, func_00659668(metadata+0x38,key), writes u16 to *out[i], pads 0xFFFF, returns 0x80008000 / 0x4000 / 0; caller 0x0055E2A8 Gfx_BindIndexedResourceSet

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupSingleIndex
signature: u32 Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupSingleIndex(int * out, int set, int metadata)
summary: Single-table variant of 0x532BB8: maps the resource names of a set to indices in metadata+0x74 (shader/texture slot table) with the same 0xFFFF/missing handling. Identical control flow to 0x532BB8, only the metadata sub-table offset differs (0x74 instead of 0x38); called by Gfx_BindSingleResource.
evidence: same loop with func_00659668(arg3+0x74,key); g_00532de0=0xFFFF, g_00532de4=0x80008000; caller 0x0055E484 Gfx_BindSingleResource

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupVariantIndices
signature: u32 Gfx_ResourceSet_LookupVariantIndices(int * out, int set, int metadata)
summary: Variant of the resource-set mapper that first tries the metadata table at +0x88 and falls back to the 0xFFFF "missing" index per entry. Same loop and return flags as 0x532BB8/0x532CD0, but with the optional table +0x88 and an explicit per-entry fallback; called by Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant.
evidence: if metadata->f_88!=0: func_00659668(&metadata->f_88,key) else 0xFFFF; writes 0xFFFF for misses; g_00532f08=0xFFFF; caller 0x00564130 Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant

name: Fx_Billboard_EmitList
signature: void Fx_Billboard_EmitList(int self, u32 count, u32 flags)
summary: Walks the batch's entry array and appends each transformed particle/billboard quad through the shared emit helper; called from the scene draw path.
evidence: The callers are now Gfx_SceneObject_CullAndDrawParts and Gfx_ModelInstance_ApplyEnvParams, and the per-entry maybe_Fx_Billboard_BuildTransform + 0x533DCC emit is unchanged.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots(GfxModelPart* part, u32 base, u32 count, u32 size, u8 mode)
summary: Carves a model instance's per-part slot arrays out of the resource buffer at base: 16-byte-aligns size, reserves count 0x448-byte and 0xD0-byte per-slot tables, then default-constructs the 0x20-byte elements of every 0x100-byte block. The caller passes a null destination, so the first parameter is damaged.
evidence: The only caller is now Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks (0.50), which passes the same count/size/base it uses for its 0x448-byte sub-block layout. That call passes 0 for the destination while the body writes self+0x14, so the decompiled first parameter (and therefore the 'model part' class identity) is not proven; kept at 0.45.

name: Fx_BuildEmitterTransforms
signature: u32 Fx_BuildEmitterTransforms(FxEmitterSet* self, u16* flags, FxContext* ctx)
summary: Builds the 4x3 transform of each emitter instance from its kind: iterates the 0x18-byte emitter records, decides visibility from the enable mask and the context kind/flag bits, then for orientation modes 0/1/2 fills the matrix with std_FastSinCos rotation, scale from the packed f_98 word and translation/offset from f_A4.
evidence: Loop over `self + i*0x18`: f_94 flags (`f_94 & 1`), f_96 kind (3/4 test ctx->f_40/f_48), enable test `(*flags & *(u16*)(0x533550 + i*2))`; then mode byte f_95 selects one of three matrix builders, all using func_0051B158 (std_FastSinCos) and constants 0x3F000000/0x3F800000/0; the packed 64-bit f_98/f_A4 words are split into two floats by shifting. Neighbours in the same module: Fx_SpawnEmitter (0x52FA9C) and Fx_BuildDistributionTable (0x5342D8).

name: Fx_Billboard_TransformPoint
signature: void Fx_Billboard_TransformPoint(float* out, float* point, int matrix)
summary: Transforms one point by the matrix and writes the result into out[0..2] (plus a fourth component), using 0x0051B70C for the per-component multiply-add and 0x0053427C for the projection.
evidence: 'local_24 = *arg2*fVar2 + arg2[1]*fVar3 + arg2[2]*fVar4' with fVar2/3/4 = matrix+4/+0x14/+0x24; calls 0x0051B70C and 0x0053427C.

name: Fx_Billboard_TransformVector
signature: void Fx_Billboard_TransformVector(float* destination, float* direction, int matrix)
summary: Direction-only variant of 0x0053390C: same matrix multiply but the translation column is skipped, so it transforms a vector rather than a point.
evidence: Identical matrix field pattern (+0x04/+0x14/+0x24) as 0x0053390C; uses 0x0051B70C/0x0053427C; called only from 0x00533DCC.

name: Fx_Billboard_TransformNormal
summary: Normal transformation for the billboard basis: negates the incoming normal, multiplies by the matrix's upper-left 3x3 and normalises so the sprite faces the camera.
evidence: 'local_20 = -arg1[0xB]' plus matrix reads +0x04/+0x14; constant g_00533DC4; called only from 0x00533DCC.

name: Fx_Billboard_BuildTransform
signature: void Fx_Billboard_BuildTransform(u32 flags, float* out, float* scale, float* matrix, u32 arg5)
summary: Builds a camera-facing billboard matrix from the source matrix: normalises its three axes with square roots, applies the scale and emits the transformed point/vector/normal through Fx_Billboard_TransformPoint/Vector/Normal.
evidence: Three of its callees are the named Fx_Billboard_TransformPoint/Vector/Normal (plus maybe_Fx_Billboard_TransformPointProjected), so the billboard transform role is confirmed by the callee set; only the flag masking (arg1 & 0x70000) is unexplained.

name: Fx_Billboard_CalcBasisMatrix
signature: void Fx_Billboard_CalcBasisMatrix(float* outMatrix, const float* inAxes, const float* viewMatrix)
summary: Calculates an orthonormal billboard 3x3 orientation matrix from input axes and view matrix: normalizes the forward axis via 0x0053427C and computes the cross product with 0x0051B70C.
evidence: Destination receives three 3-float basis vectors at offsets 0, +4, +8 (stride 4 floats), not a single point; uses vector normalization (0x0053427C) and cross product (0x0051B70C) to produce an orthonormal billboard orientation matrix.

name: Gfx_CommandBuffer_PadTo16
summary: Pads the command buffer to a 16-byte boundary with zero words so the following block starts at the GPU's required alignment, and reports the padded size.
evidence: computes ((end - start) & ~3) + 8 and the 4 - ((size & 0xF) >> 2) guard, then writes zero words up to the aligned end; callers 0x5324F4 and 0x5346DC (both GPU command assembly).

name: Fx_BuildDistributionTable
signature: void Fx_BuildDistributionTable(float* table, int mode, FxCurveCoefficients* curve, float outLo, float outHi, float exponent, float inLo, float inHi)
summary: Fills a 128-entry lookup table that describes how a random emitter parameter is distributed over its input domain: the input is normalised from [inLo,inHi] to 0..1, passed through a rational curve (curve+0x28/0x2C/0x38/0x3C) and then shaped by the selected mode (0 = rational/linear, 1 = exponential decay, 2 = gaussian exp(-x^2), 3/4 = mirrored exponential variants) and mapped onto [outLo,outHi]. The caller then packs the floats to 13-bit fixed point for the runtime random sampler.
evidence: Sole caller 0x0065973C stores the 512-byte table into a 0x218-byte per-spawn FX record and marks it valid; 0x00508C40 then converts it to packed 13-bit fixed-point pairs (`orr r2, r3, r2, lsl #13`). All five branches share the same normalisation by (inHi-inLo) and clamp to [outLo,outHi]; only the final transform differs and uses std_Expf (0x00672FBC) for modes 1-4. Loop bound 0x7F = 128 entries.

name: Fx_InitQuadSlotIndices
summary: Initializes an array of four slot or index words to 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) via 0x0051CF40 and returns the slots pointer.
evidence: Callee 0x0051CF40 is 'mvn r1, #0; str r1, [r0]; bx lr', which writes 0xFFFFFFFF into *r0. 0x005346B4 calls it four times with r0, r0+4, r0+8, r0+0xC, subtracts 0xC to restore the pointer, and returns r0. It initializes four index/slot words, not measuring a batch.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureDescriptors
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureDescriptors(GfxModelInstance* self, int* descriptor, int* material)
summary: Emits the PICA200 texture descriptor block for one material: writes the size/param words, encodes the material's format, mip and border flags into the descriptor and appends it to the model instance's command buffer through Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureDescriptor.
evidence: sole caller Gfx_ModelInstance_BindResources (0x5348D0); explicit 0x00200080/0x000F0080 descriptor words and the flag packing from material->f_1C/f_58; calls Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureDescriptor (0x6579C8) plus 0x657C60/0x657E28/0x657E68/0x658030.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_BindResources
signature: u32 Gfx_ModelInstance_BindResources(int self, int model, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Binds the resources of one model/animation group: for each of the group's 0xB-word descriptors it resolves the texture/material names against the model's metadata tables, fills the three sub-structures and dispatches the per-part setup. The 0x80000008/0x80000010/0x80000020 error bits and the repeated func_00659668 name lookups are the model resource binding used by the renderer.
evidence: self->f_34 array of 0xB-word records; func_00659668 on model+0x1C, +0x34, +0x28; error bits 0x80000008/0x10/0x20; func_005346DC per part; caller 0x00564750

name: Gfx_Bch_BuildMaterials
signature: void Gfx_Bch_BuildMaterials(GfxModel* self, int* materials, int* state, int arg4, int arg5)
summary: Builds the material/primitive list of a BCH model: walks the material records, aligns each block to 4 bytes, parses the embedded resource sets (Gfx_ResourceSet_Parse) and emits the draw state for each material.
evidence: caller 0x535168 (Gfx_BchHeader_Validate) -> 0x53531C; uses Gfx_ResourceSet_Parse (0x5064CC), the 4-byte alignment (*arg2+3 & ~3) and 0x6557D8/0x655AA4/0x655C0C/0x655D68 (PICA200 state writers) - the same material pipeline as Gfx_ModelInstance_BindMaterials.

name: Gfx_Bch_LoadModel
signature: unsigned int Gfx_Bch_LoadModel(GfxBchModel* out, int* header, unsigned int* info)
summary: Loads a BCH (Binary Castle) model from a memory buffer: validates the 'BCH\0' magic, the version (<= 0x22) and the reserved/alignment bits, collects the decoded error bits into the return value, then fills the caller's model descriptor and builds the materials (0x534D4C) and mesh data (0x53531C) from the header's tables.
evidence: compares *header with 0x00484342 = 'BCH\0' (error 0x80000040), rejects version > 0x22 (0x80000002) and bad reserved bits (0x80000020/0x80000008/0x80000004); on success copies the 10-word descriptor into out, sets out[0xB]=header, out[0xC]=info[0] and tail-calls Gfx_Bch_LoadMeshData plus Gfx_Bch_BuildMaterials; callers 0x56DE24 Gfx_Resource_CreateFromDescriptor and 0x56EF30 Gfx_ModelResource_Init.

name: Gfx_Bch_LoadMeshData
signature: void Gfx_Bch_LoadMeshData(unsigned int* self, unsigned int arg2, int vertexData, unsigned int arg4, int arg5, int arg6, unsigned int* counts)
summary: Copies the BCH mesh payload into GPU memory: translates the source address, checks which allocation region it belongs to (0x20000), then copies the vertex/index arrays and writes their physical addresses into the draw records.
evidence: Os_VirtualToPhysical + 0x1109D8(0x20000) region test, per-entry copy loop over counts and the material flag test (~(arg6->f_40 >> 2) & 1); callers 0x535168 (BCH header path) and the mesh-building chain.

name: maybe_Ui_Animator_ReleaseBindings
summary: Walks layout animation binding array, clears pane cached transform fields (+0x8C..+0xA0), and unbinds animation resources.
evidence: Iterates through binding records clearing layout pane transforms; callers 0x0056DD6C and 0x0056EEB8 are unconfirmed destructors; kept maybe_.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_BindSecondaryResources
summary: Resolves the two secondary resource names of a model part (+0x5C/+0x60 and +0x64/+0x68) through the model metadata, storing the matched entries at +0x4C/+0x50. Same metadata lookup helper and 0x80000020 error bit as 0x5348D0 but for only two named slots; called from the same resource-list attach.
evidence: func_00659668(model+0x34, self->f_5C/f_64) with f_60/f_68; on miss returns 0x80000020; writes f_4C and f_50; caller 0x00564750

name: Ui_System_SetSlotPoolParam
signature: void Ui_System_SetSlotPoolParam(unsigned int self, unsigned int value)
summary: Configures UI layout slot pool allocator by registering self with tag 0x0400010F via 0x0053D160 and storing parameter into global *0x007AE894.
evidence: Directly invoked by confirmed Ui_System_InitSlotPool (0x0021E6B8) during UI core system allocation to configure layout allocator global state (*0x007AE894).

name: Gfx_Flim_Parse
signature: unsigned int Gfx_Flim_Parse(unsigned int* self, int data, int size)
summary: Parses a FLIM texture image: finds the 'FLIM' magic at the end of the block, reads the 0x07020100 header fields (format/size/mip count) and builds the texture object used by the material binder.

Compares [fat+4]==0xc and ldrh [fat+6] < 0x4000 (SFAT node count), computes data block address from the archive and node offset, then memcmp against 0x0072FABC ('SFNT') and checks [block+4]==8.
