name: Fs_NamedObject_Open
summary: Opens one named object from an archive: marks the request 'opening' (state 2), looks the name up, attaches the stream on success or records an error, then sets state 3 and pushes the request back to the archive's completion ring buffer at +0x790.
evidence: NEW: every callee in the body is now named by a confident function - Fs_NamedObject_ReadRecord, Fs_Stream_SetBufferLimits, Fs_NamedObject_FindAndRead, Fs_NamedObject_AttachStream and Container_RingBuffer_Push - and its only caller is the named Fs_Worker_ProcessQueue. The whole open sequence is therefore confirmed rather than guessed.

name: Fs_NamedObject_FindAndRead
summary: Finds the reader that owns a name in the global reader list, runs its vtable+0x14 (accepts?) then vtable+0x10 (open) and finally reads the name into the record with 0x005798CC. Returns the resolved reader entry or 0.
evidence: Called by confident caller Fs_NamedObject_Open (0x0056F7A4) to locate reader in reader list and open entry.

name: Fs_NamedObject_ReadRecord
summary: Reads one record for a slot: first tries the fast path through the slot's virtual reader, otherwise falls back to the buffered stream reader (0x0056EB8C/0x0056EAC4) and retries with the fallback slot index at 0x33C.
evidence: Called by confident caller Fs_NamedObject_Open (0x0056F7A4); reads record for slot via fast virtual reader or buffered stream.

name: Gfx_ResourcePool_Purge
summary: Frees the blocks held by one pool slot (or all slots when index<0): walks the slot's block list, unlinks each block's handle-table entry and releases it via func_00115358/func_00115390.
evidence: Called by confident caller maybe_Gfx_ResourcePool_PurgeUnreferenced (0x0064553C) to evict unreferenced resource pool entries.

name: Fs_Worker_ProcessQueue
summary: Body of the filesystem worker thread: pops open requests from the queue at +0x1BCC, releases each request's node list, updates the per-type byte counters at worker+type*0x28, recycles the request into the ring buffer at +0x2000, and when the open queue is empty waits on the +0x35C queue before running the open path (0x0056F7A4) for the next request.
evidence: NEW: both queue helpers are now named - Os_QueueTryPop on +0x1BCC/+0x35C and Container_RingBuffer_Push on +0x2000 - and the open path callee is the now-named Fs_NamedObject_Open, which is exactly the 'pop request, process, re-queue' loop the name claims. The unaff_r7 in the pseudocode is a decompiler artifact for the popped pointer (its damaged spot is the only one in the body), not a missing argument.

name: Fs_Worker_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the file-system worker object: installs the two-part vtable 0x7824A4/0x7824BC, destroys the 3 x 0xC-byte entries at +0x2C40 and tears down the two critical-section-protected queues at +0x2000 and +0x8C0. The object is the Fs worker used by 0x56FDD0 maybe_Fs_Worker_ProcessQueue; the +0x2C40 array and the two 0x434/0x143C-spaced sections are the worker's queues.
evidence: stores g_00570044=0x7824A4 and arg1[1]=vtable+0x18; std_destroy_range(arg1+0xB10,0x6F43E4,0xC,3); func_006E75A0(arg1+0x800); func_0012032C/0x120368; func_005761D8 maybe_Os_CriticalSectionObject_Dtor; std_destroy_range(...,0x570050,0x28,0x14)

name: Container_Tree_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small container: erases every node of the tree rooted at self+4 using the successor walk and releases the header reference.
evidence: The successor-walk erase loop is the same one visible in the named Container_MultiList_Dtor, and the function is a pure tree teardown; the generic container name is appropriate.

name: Mem_BitmapPool_Init
signature: void* Mem_BitmapPool_Init(MemPool* self, unsigned blockSize, unsigned blockCount, void* allocator)
summary: Initialises a pool object: self[0..2] become a circular free-list head, a global single instance is created once (guarded by the byte at 0x007BE37C) by allocating a bitmap plus block area, and the pool parameters are stored at +0xc/+0x10/+0x14. The three init-time callers register one pool per engine object type.
evidence: Body 0x57010C-0x570298: str r0,[r0]/[r0+4]/[r0+8] ring init; guarded call at 0x570240 to 0x0011CFAC (SDK heap alloc, size rounded with +0xf/&~0xf); globals 0x007BE37C/0x007BE380/0x00837128; literal 0x00782AC0 written as object tag. The rest of the 8892-byte Ghidra range (0x5702CC+) is a table of 226 tiny type predicates (see 0x5723C8), not part of this function.

name: maybe_Script_CheckObjectTypeId
summary: One of ~226 identical 44-byte predicates: returns 1 when scriptValue[1] == 1 and scriptValue[2] carries that class's hard-coded 32-bit id, else 0. Looks like the script-binding type check for a native class; exact class unknown because the Ghidra "function" is the whole table.
evidence: Re-examined in context of neighbouring functions in blk:00540000; context remains ambiguous with no confident callers. Honest maybe name kept at confidence 0.35.

name: Gfx_Context_SetTextureMatrix
signature: void Gfx_Context_SetTextureMatrix(Gfx_TextureMatrix* out, unsigned src, unsigned scale, unsigned offset, unsigned mode)
summary: Fills a texture-matrix/texgen parameter block for the renderer: stores the source texture, scale and offset words in the three parallel slot groups (0/2/3, 0xB/0xC/0x10, 0xC/0x11) and sets the texgen mode to 3.
evidence: 6 callers, all model passes (0x567718, 0x56797C, 0x569350, 0x569518, 0x569ABC, 0x56A3F0); writes the block returned by 0x106DFC (render-context scratch) and sets byte +0x28 = 3

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorVtableSlot1
summary: Deleting destructor of the class whose vtable is 0x007824E0, and literally that vtable's slot 1: vtable install, conditional release of the inline string at +0x1C, unlink of the two intrusive list heads, free.
evidence: NEW: the vtable word stored at the top of the body is 0x007824E0, and asm/rodata shows that table's slot 1 is 0x00572BBC - the same body at another address. So all four copies (0x001C635C, 0x002598B4, 0x002D5734, 0x00572BBC) are the deleting destructor of one single class, emitted four times; the old names used three different schemes (Ui_Object_DtorStringAndLists / ...DoubleListB / ...DoubleListC / Container_Node_DtorC) for identical code. The class is still unidentified - its vtable slots 0x00572B94..0x00572C48 are all unnamed and sit in the 0x00572xxx math/container region - so the maybe_ stays and the A/B/C suffixes only distinguish the copies. The body itself is confirmed: install the vtable, release the inline string at +0x1C when flag +0xB is set (0x0010EC00 walks the red-black tree, 0x0010EC14 erases the node), unlink the two intrusive list heads at +8/+0xC and +0x14/+0x18, then free the block through the allocator virtual at self-8 (0x0010F6CC). This copy is the one the vtable actually points at (asm/rodata 0x007824E4 = 0x00572BBC), which is why it gets the slot-based name instead of a letter.

name: Math_BuildQuaternionFromEulerAlt
summary: Alternative Euler-to-quaternion conversion (the SQRT branch is inverted relative to 0x572D94): produces a unit quaternion from three radian angles. Both functions have the identical 0.159155 (=1/2pi), 6.283185, 0.5, 1.0 constants and the same three-axis composition, only the sign of the square-root correction differs.
evidence: constants g_00572d80=0.159155 (1/2pi), 0x40C90FDB=2pi, 0.5, 1.0; calls 0x6731EC/0x672E44 (sin/cos); writes out[0..3]; pointer at 0x77ce? no - appears at 0x781... vtable; caller 0x003CBB1C battle member widget effect update

name: Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler
summary: Converts three Euler angles (radians) into a quaternion using the half-angle sin/cos product; used for every actor placement and model transform. Thirty-six call sites across field actors, models, sprites and cameras; the 1/2pi scaling, PI comparison for the sign fix and the four-component output are conclusive.
evidence: 36 callers incl. maybe_Model_SetupObject, maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition, maybe_Field_Actor_ApplyPlacement, Field_ObjectSprite_InitComplex; constants 0.159155, 2pi, 0.5, 1.0, PI; writes out[0..3]; same shape as Math_QuatMultiply users

name: Math_MatrixInverse
summary: Inverts a 4x4 affine matrix: computes the 3x3 cofactor matrix and determinant (with the identity fallback for a singular matrix) and builds the inverse translation from the source translation column. The explicit cofactor expansion and the 1/determinant scale are unmistakable; callers include the secondary-motion bone and battle target-marker updates.
evidence: computes determinant from 9 elements of the 3x3 block; if det==0 uses the identity at 0x7E70EC; else cofactors * 1/det; then negates the translation terms using matrix->f_C/f_1C/f_2C; callers 0x005626F4 Model_BuildSecondaryMotionBoneMatrices, 0x003D3F54 Ui_BattleTargetMarker_Update, ...

name: Math_ComputeBoundingSphere
signature: void Math_ComputeBoundingSphere(float* outSphere, unsigned count, const void* points, unsigned stride)
summary: Computes the minimum enclosing sphere of a strided point array and writes centre xyz + radius. It copies the point addresses into an on-stack pointer array and delegates to the Welzl solver at 0x5737A4, so callers get the same result as the recursive routine with an empty boundary set.
evidence: out[0..3] initialised from 0x007E71BC (zero vec4, BSS); loop stores `arg3 + i*arg4` (point pointers) into a stack array; tail call func_005737A4(array, arrayBase, count, 0). Caller 0x58D5E8 uses the result for a scene-entry bounding sphere.

name: Math_MinimumEnclosingSphere
signature: void Math_MinimumEnclosingSphere(float* outSphere, void** points, unsigned count, int boundaryCount)
summary: Welzl-style minimum enclosing sphere: for boundary sizes 1..4 it builds the sphere through those support points (point, midpoint, circumcircle, circumsphere) and otherwise recursively tries each remaining point as a boundary point. Output is xyz + radius.
evidence: switch(arg4) cases 0-4: case 1 copies one point with radius 0; case 2 calls 0x574DE4 (two-point midpoint, radius in [3]); case 3 calls 0x574E48 (circumcircle of 3 points); case 4 calls 0x57505C (circumsphere of 4). The loop rotates the candidate list and recurses with boundaryCount+1 - exactly the move-to-front Welzl algorithm.

name: Math_ComputeRotatedAabb
signature: float* Math_ComputeRotatedAabb(float* out, const void* transform)
summary: Computes the axis-aligned bounds of an oriented box: takes the centre (+0x10) and half extents (+0x1C..+0x24), transforms four sign-flipped corners, keeps per-axis maxima of the absolute results and writes min xyz / max xyz as 6 floats.
evidence: Callee func_00574548 transforms a vector by the object's rotation/axes and func_00574484 combines vectors per component (max); literal 0.0f g_00573E00 used for the abs tests; corners built from f_1C/f_20/f_24 with negations; output *out = f_10 - extent, out[3] = f_10 + extent, same for Y/Z; callers maybe_Ui_Part_UpdateSlotTransforms (0x0021D09C), maybe_Ui_CompositeWindowCtor (0x0021DC44), FUN_00589DD4, FUN_00665A24.

name: Math_BuildBoundsFromSphereAndOffset
summary: Builds a world-space AABB from a centre plus a rotated offset and a radius: returns min = min(centre, centre+rotatedOffset) - radius and max = max(...) + radius. The two min/max branches on each axis and the radius subtraction/addition at [7] are the bounds builder used by the scene query code.
evidence: func_00665564(&offset, sphere+3) rotates the offset; min/max per axis against sphere[0..2]; radius sphere[7]; writes out[0..5]; caller 0x0058A444/0x0058B4A0 scene queries

name: Math_ComputePrincipalAxesQuaternion
signature: void Math_ComputePrincipalAxesQuaternion(float* outQuat, void* matrixScratch, const float* diagonal, const float* offDiagonal)
summary: Turns six covariance terms (xx,yy,zz and xy,yz,zx) into an orientation: the helpers at 0x574CE8/0x574774/0x574A20 fill a 3x3 frame and the tail extracts a normalised quaternion with the trace/off-diagonal formulas. Used by the OBB builder at 0x575A40.
evidence: Entry preloads 6 floats from r2/r3, calls 0x574CE8, 0x574774, 0x574A20 with the 0x40-byte scratch object, then 0x574C3C does s0 = trace + 1.0; sqrt; 1/(2*sqrt) scaling, and writes 4 normalised floats (w = 0.5*sqrt(1+trace)). Caller 0x575A40 passes the covariance accumulators.

name: Math_SphereFromThreePoints
signature: float* Math_SphereFromThreePoints(float* outSphere, const float* arg2, const float* b, const float* c)
summary: Circumscribed circle of three points in 3D: returns centre xyz plus radius (out[3]). Collinear/degenerate input falls back to the longest of the three edges so the result stays finite.
evidence: u=b-a, v=c-a, cross; if |cross|^2 <= eps handles collinear by halving the longer edge; otherwise centre = a + (|v|^2 (u x w) + |u|^2 (w x v)) / (2|cross|^2). out[3] = |centre-a|. Constants 0.0/1.0/0.5 at 0x575050/54/58. Called by the Welzl solver for boundaryCount==3.

name: Math_SphereFromFourPoints
signature: float* Math_SphereFromFourPoints(float* outSphere, const float* arg2, const float* b, const float* c, const float* d)
summary: Circumscribed sphere of four points (centre xyz + radius). Degenerate/coplanar input is reduced to the best three-point sphere via 0x574E48, matching the fallback ladder of the Welzl solver.
evidence: Computes the 3x3 determinant (scalar triple product) of the edge vectors in fVar10; if non-zero the centre is the standard barycentric solution with 1/(2*det); otherwise tries the four 3-point subsets through 0x574E48 and picks the smallest. Called by 0x5737A4 for boundaryCount==4.

name: Math_MatrixMultiply
signature: void Math_MatrixMultiply(float * out, float * arg2, float * b)
summary: Multiplies two 4x4 matrices (row-vector convention: out = a * b) and writes 12 floats. Twelve callers are all transform composition points (model attach, camera track, trail, monster physics); the body is the plain 4x4 product with the translation column.
evidence: 12 callers incl. 0x002230C4 Model_Attach_ComputeWorldMatrix, 0x00372CEC maybe_Camera_TrackTargetRotation, 0x0056BC20 Model_CalcLookAtAngles, 0x00224AB0 maybe_Gfx_UpdateTrailTransform; reads a[0..0xB]/b[0..0xB] and writes out[0..0xB]

name: Math_QuatFromAxisAngle
signature: void Math_QuatFromAxisAngle(float * out, float * axis, float angle)
summary: Builds a quaternion from an axis and an angle in radians: scales the axis by sin(angle/2) and stores cos(angle/2) in w. The half-angle conversion (1/2pi, 2pi, PI sign fix) and the four-component output are conclusive; Math_QuatMultiply and the physics/rotation code call it.
evidence: callers 0x001CEC28 Math_QuatMultiply, 0x00371A44 maybe_Model_ApplyFacingTilt, 0x003AE480 monster physics, 0x0049ED7C maybe_Motion_ApplyRotationBlend; writes out[0..3] = axis*sin, w=cos

name: Math_QuatSlerp
signature: void Math_QuatSlerp(float* out, const float* q0, const float* q1, float t)
summary: Spherical linear interpolation of two unit quaternions: negates q1 when the dot product is negative (shortest arc), falls back to a normalised lerp when the quaternions are nearly parallel, otherwise blends with acos/sin and renormalises the result.
evidence: Callers 0x003CFFA8 and 0x004F8280 blend a model's start/end rotations (self+0x44 / self+0x54) during a turn; callees std_Acosf 0x00672A14 and 0x00673BC8 (sin); constant g_00575858 (0.0, used for the sign flip) and g_0057585C (cosine cutoff above which the lerp fallback is used); identical structure to the vec3 slerp 0x00575864.

name: Math_Vec3Slerp
signature: void Math_Vec3Slerp(float* out, const float* v0, const float* v1, float t)
summary: Spherical interpolation between two 3D direction vectors: normalised lerp when the directions are nearly parallel, otherwise acos/sin slerp, always producing a unit direction. Used wherever a direction has to change smoothly (animation pose blending at 0x002E465C, 0x00591490).
evidence: Callers Anim_InterpolatePose (0x002E465C), 0x003E8F84, 0x004406A8, 0x00441B24 and 0x00591490 (camera blend); the parallel case delegates to 0x005753BC (vec3 lerp), otherwise acos 0x00672A14 / sin 0x00673BC8; 3-component dot with epsilon g_00575974.

name: Math_BuildRotYQuaternion
summary: Builds a quaternion for a rotation about the Y axis. The angle is normalised to a full turn and halved (0x6731EC = wrap, 0x672E44 = cos), giving (0, sin(theta/2), 0, cos(theta/2)) with the correct sign for the second half-turn.
evidence: Writes out[0]=0, out[1]=+/-sqrt(1-c^2), out[2]=0, out[3]=c. Literals 0x5759F0=2pi, 0x5759F4=0.5, 0x5759F8=1.0, 0x5759FC=pi. The 0.5 factor is the half-angle used by quaternions; the compare against pi bit-pattern flips the sine sign.

name: Math_ComputeObbFromPoints
signature: void Math_ComputeObbFromPoints(float* outObb, unsigned count, const void* points, unsigned stride)
summary: Fits an oriented bounding box to a strided point array: centroid, 3x3 covariance, principal-axis quaternion (0x574B10), quaternion->matrix (0x57600C), then min/max extents in that frame. Writes quaternion (4), centre (3) and half-extents (3).
evidence: Averages all points (fVar14=1/count), accumulates xx/yy/zz/xy/yz/zx, calls 0x574B10(&quat,&scratch,&diag,&offdiag), 0x57600C (quat->matrix) and 0x574548 (matrix*vector); output arg1[0..3]=quat, [4..6]=centre, [7..9]=extents. Default 10-float value in 0x0075?e24. Called by 0x58D5E8 for scene entries.

name: Math_UnionAabb
signature: void Math_UnionAabb(float* out, const float* arg2, const float* b)
summary: Unions two 6-float AABBs: per-axis minimum of the min triples (sign test against 0.0f) and per-axis maximum of the max triples via func_00574484.
evidence: For each of the first 3 components: if (a[i] - b[i]) >= g_00575EC0 (0.0f) take b[i], i.e. min; then func_00574484(&local_28, a+3, b+3) produces the max triple, written to out[3..5]; the 6-float min/max layout matches the output of FUN_00573B6C; same callers FUN_00589DD4 and FUN_00665A24.

name: Math_BuildRotYMatrix
summary: Fills a 3x4 rotation matrix for a rotation about Y: cos on [0]/[10], +/-sin on [2]/[8], 1.0 on [5], zeros elsewhere. The angle is wrapped to one full turn first.
evidence: out[0]=c, out[10]=c, out[8]=-s, out[2]=+s, out[5]=1.0; constants 0x575F58=2pi, 0x575F5C=1.0, 0x575F60=pi, 0x575F64=0.0. Same wrap+cos/sqrt(1-c^2) pattern as 0x575984.

name: Math_BuildRotZMatrix
summary: Fills a 3x4 rotation matrix for a rotation about Z: [0]=c, [5]=c, [1]=-s, [4]=+s, [10]=1.0. Used by the model/animation code to build joint frames.
evidence: Writes c at [0] and [5], +/-sqrt(1-c^2) at [1]/[4], 1.0 at [10]; constants 0x575FFC=2pi, 0x576000=1.0, 0x576004=pi, 0x576008=0.0. Same angle-wrap helper 0x6731EC / 0x672E44 as the Y variant.

name: Os_ThreadObject_Dtor
summary: Destroys an OS thread wrapper (vtable 0x00782668): waits for thread completion via 0x0010EA00 / 0x00118170 (svcWaitSynchronization1, svc 0x24), closes kernel thread handle self->f_04 via svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23), zeroes self->f_04, and returns self.
evidence: NOT a CriticalSection! Installs base vtable 0x00782668, calls 0x10EA00(self) and 0x118170(self + 4) (which issues svc #0x24 = svcWaitSynchronization1 with infinite timeout -1LL when u8[self+8] == 0, i.e. nn::os::Thread::Join), then if handle *(u32*)(self + 4) != 0 executes svc #0x23 (3DS Horizon svcCloseHandle) and clears *(u32*)(self + 4) = 0. Called by Fs_Worker_Dtor, Ui_TitleScreen_Dtor, Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown, Gfx_ResetRenderer, and Sound_StreamPlayer_Dtor.

name: Script_GetPlayerIdArg
signature: unsigned char* Script_GetPlayerIdArg(unsigned char* out, void* vm, int stackIdx)
summary: Reads a PlayerID argument from a script VM stack slot; anything outside 0..0x1E (and not the 0xFF sentinel) is reported by building a type-mismatch message for the expected type 'xp::PlayerID'.
evidence: Literal pool entry 0x00576298 -> 0x007C07B4 str='xp::PlayerID'; value test `iVar3 != 0xFF && 0x1E < iVar3`; func_007078E4 converts a stack slot to an integer with type checks; on rejection it calls func_005766A4 + func_00576564 (the 'wrong type' formatter) and copies 0x80 bytes into the temp object; 15 callers (FUN_006F8CA8, FUN_006F9378, FUN_006FD674, FUN_0070348C ...) call it as (out, vm, 2) and feed the returned byte to a callback pointer.

name: Script_GetFloatArg
signature: float* Script_GetFloatArg(float* out, void* vm, int stackIdx)
summary: Converts a script stack slot to a float, accepting integer, unsigned-integer and float object tags and reporting a 'float' type mismatch for anything else.
evidence: String literal 'float' at 0x007C019C; type dispatch on func_006BBD7C(vm, idx) against 0x1000008 with delta literal 0xFC000006 in g_0057637C; branches use func_006BB890 + VectorUnsignedToFloat, func_006BBA70 + VectorSignedToFloat, func_006BBA18 (float passthrough); error branch calls func_00576564 with 'float' and returns g_00576384 (0.0); 18 callers from FUN_006FDC44 to FUN_007073C8.

name: Script_GetByteArg
signature: unsigned char* Script_GetByteArg(unsigned char* out, void* vm, int stackIdx)
summary: The byte-sized script argument getter: it converts the value like Script_GetIntArg but stores only the low byte and reports the 'integer' type mismatch.
evidence: The body uses the 'integer' literal at 0x007C20C2, g_00576470 delta 0xFC000006 and VectorFloatToUnsigned(...,3), writes only (u8) to *out, and is used by the Script_Bind_SetGlobalGameFlag/SetNelsenHopeFlag/ScreenEffectSetSepiaMul bindings; sibling 0x00576478 keeps the full 32-bit value.

name: Script_GetIntArg
signature: unsigned int* Script_GetIntArg(unsigned int* out, void* vm, int stackIdx)
summary: Converts a script stack slot to a 32-bit integer, accepting integer, unsigned-integer and float tags and reporting an 'integer' type mismatch otherwise.
evidence: String literal 'integer' at 0x007C20D2; type dispatch on func_006BBD7C with g_0057655C = 0xFC000006; float branch VectorFloatToUnsigned(local_1C[0],3); error branch calls func_00576564 with 'integer' and returns 0; 28 callers (FUN_006F62E0, FUN_006F99E8, FUN_007077A4 ...).

name: Script_FormatTypeError
signature: void Script_FormatTypeError(void* out, void* vm, int stackIdx, const char* expectedType)
summary: Formats the standard Squirrel argument type error 'wrong type (%s expected, got %s )' into an sq string, resolving the actual type name from the offending stack slot (or 'unknown' when it cannot be named).
evidence: Literals at 0x005765F4 'wrong type (%s expected, got %s )' and 0x005765F8 'wrong type (%s expected, got unknown )'; arg4 is the expected type name supplied by callers ('float', 'integer', 'xp::PlayerID'); uses func_006BDAF4 to fetch the stack slot, func_006BDA58/func_006BBD28 to read the type name, func_005B4C34(vm,1) to pop and func_00707A10 to printf into the output object (type tags g_005765F0/g_005766A0); called from the four typed getters and a large number of native bindings.

name: Script_FormatValueForError
signature: void Script_FormatValueForError(void* out, void* value, void* vm)
summary: Fills an sq string for a script error: writes the value's type name from the sq type-name table, or copies the 0x80-byte value payload when the value already belongs to the VM; the object tag is set before and restored after the fill.
evidence: Script_Native_IsZone (0x006F8CA8) calls it exactly on the argument-type-mismatch path before Script_Vm_ThrowError, and the ~230 Script_Bind_* callers are all native wrappers, so 'format the offending value for the error message' is confirmed by a named, high-confidence caller.

name: Script_GetVmOrThrow
summary: Checks the low tag bit of a script value; if it is not set the engine error handler (0x0010009C) is called with the empty format string at 0x7C087C, otherwise the global Squirrel VM pointer at 0x0083876C is returned. Effectively "get the VM for this closure, asserting the value is a closure".
evidence: if ((*arg1 & 1) == 0) func_0010009C(g_00576700 /*0x7C087C, empty C string just after "wrong type (...)"*/); return g_00576704 /*0x0083876C*/; func_0010009C is noreturn. Neighbouring functions are the Script_Get*Arg helpers at 0x576220-0x5765FC.

name: Script_Closure_Destroy
summary: Destructor for a script closure/thread wrapper: installs vtable 0x00782690, and when the initialised flag at +0x10 is set releases the VM child object through the Squirrel VM helpers 0x6BD10C/0x6BD12C and clears the flag.
evidence: *self = g_00576764 (0x00782690 table); if (*(u8*)(self+0x10)) { func_006BD10C(self->[4], self+8); func_006BD12C(self+8); self+0x10=0; }. 0x6BD10C/0x6BD12C sit in the Squirrel VM block next to Script_Vm_Clone at 0x6BD140. Data reference at 0x7826A8.

name: Script_InvokeCallbackPair
signature: void Script_InvokeCallbackPair(unsigned int* out, void* callable, unsigned int arg3)
summary: Calls a Squirrel callable with one extra argument: pushes the callable's stored references plus arg3, invokes it, requires a boolean result, then duplicates the result and the first parameter into two managed reference pairs at out[1..4].
evidence: The now-named Sq_* callees (Sq_VmGetStackSlot, Sq_VmReadStackSlot, Sq_PushRefValue, Sq_VmPop) plus the 0x8000100/0x8000200 boolean type check make the VM call shape explicit; only the caller 0x00579B64 knows what the two refs are used for.

name: Gfx_Node_CreateChild
signature: int* Gfx_Node_CreateChild(GfxNode* parent, uint32_t heap, uint32_t desc)
summary: Creates a 0x7C-byte child node: Mem_AllocAligned_2, constructor 0x005776B0, initialisation from the descriptor (Gfx_SpriteSet_Init) and insertion into the parent's intrusive child list (func_001235A4); returns 0 on failure.
evidence: The caller Gfx_SpriteSet_Init and the allocation + link sequence are visible, and the failure path destroys the half-built node through its vtable, which is the create-and-link contract the name describes.

name: Model_UpdateMotionState
summary: Updates the motion/animation handle of a model node: if no handle is set it reports idle (0), otherwise advances the motion, and when the motion finishes it clears the handle and returns 2 (done). Ten callers are monster models and UI widgets that poll the state byte; the 0xFFFFFFFF handle sentinel and state 2 are the animation-completion protocol.
evidence: if f_A4==0 -> f_AC=0 else func_00577404(); func_006657AC(f_A4); if done: f_A8=-1,f_A4=0,f_AC=2; returns f_AC; callers Monster_Model_SetState, Monster_Model_ApplyVariant, 0x004A7F08, 0x0047E214, ...

name: maybe_Model_Node_DestroyChildList
summary: Destructor helper of the 0x57xxxx node class: resets the embedded array at self+0x1C through Mem_FreeAnimArray and calls the virtual release (+4) of every child in the intrusive list delimited by self+0x98/self+0x9C.
evidence: The body is Mem_FreeAnimArray(&self+0x1C) plus a release of every child in the intrusive list delimited by self+0x98/self+0x9C. Four of the six callers are model code (Monster_Model_SetupPattern, Battle_Ui_UnitModel_MarkVisible, Battle_Ui_CommandWidget_Ctor, Field_Monster_OnEvent), but maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetTwoSubObjects also calls it, so 'Model_Node' is still a guess.

name: Container_List_Init
summary: Initialises an intrusive circular list (head/tail = self, links at +4/+0x14/+0x18), stores the capacity/allocator word twice, writes the class tag and constructs the embedded node pool at +0x1c with default 1.0/0/-1 sentinels.
evidence: self[1]=self; self[5]=self+4; self[6]=self+4; self[4]=self; *self=g_00576af4 (0x007826D8); self[2]=self[3]=arg2; then func_005776B0(self+7) and fields 0x7c-0xa8 set to 0/0xFFFFFFFF/1.0. Mirrors 0x5776B4 exactly, which is why both are container constructors.

name: Gfx_SceneNode_DtorBase
summary: Destructor body of the generic scene node: installs vtable 0x7826D8, frees the anim array and releases the two intrusive child lists (+0x98 and +0x1C), returning the base offset. Used as base destructor by monster pattern nodes, UI widgets and status panels, so it is the shared node class destructor rather than a leaf type.
evidence: stores g_00576ba4=0x7826D8; func_0057747C(self+7 words); walks self[0x27] list to self[0x26] calling vtable+4; unlinks; func_005777AC(self+7) then unlinks its two embedded lists; callers Monster_PatternNode_Dtor, Ui_AllocWidget_Dtor, Ui_StatusPanel_DtorDelete, Ui_NamedEntry_Dtor, ...

name: Fs_IsAniPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the animation suffix ".ani".
evidence: The literal ".ani" sits behind the function at 0x00576CD4 and is loaded into r1 before std_strstr, so the unknown 'tag' of the previous pass is now known.

name: Model_BindResourceSlots
signature: u32 Model_BindResourceSlots(int self, int model, int * names, u32 arg4)
summary: Binds up to eight model resource slots: when no name list is supplied it looks up the generated names "00".."07", otherwise it walks the supplied names and maps each by its index byte into the instance's slot array at +0x68. Sixteen callers are monster model creation, model-animation attach and battle scene setup; the "00"-"07" naming and the eight-slot +0x68 array are the model part table.
evidence: g_00576e54=0x3030 ("00"); builds names '0'+i/10, '0'+i%10; func_00659668(model+0x28,name); writes *(self+i*4+0x68); else walks names at names[0]+0x60 with index byte at entry+8; callers 0x00420D48 Monster_Model_Create, 0x0046782C Model_AttachAnimationByHandle, 0x004D2538 Anim_ModelLoad_ByName, ...

name: maybe_Script_CallbackHolder_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the small object that owns a script callback: releases the callback object with 0x005799D4 and then frees the holder with the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The two-call shape is the standard deleting destructor of a small holder class once 0x0010F6CC is read as operator delete; 0x005799D4 is still unnamed, so what the holder owns (a Squirrel closure, a VM callback) is not proven.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_CreateDefault
summary: Default-constructs a scene node: allocates the block, runs func_00579974, installs vtable 0x007826E8 and clears the ten words at +0x64..+0x88.
evidence: NEW: vtable 0x007826E8's slot 7 is the confident Gfx_SceneNode_DtorBody (0.50), so the class is a scene node; the old name only encoded the vtable address. The allocation arguments are dropped, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Gfx_SpriteSet_Init
signature: unsigned int Gfx_SpriteSet_Init(void* self, unsigned int allocTag, void* bank)
summary: Creates a sprite set over a texture/animation bank: allocates count*0x3C bytes for the sprite records (count at bank+100), constructs them with the 0x00576BA8 constructor, stores the bank and refreshes every record.
evidence: Callee Mem_AllocAligned(count*0x3C + 8, allocTag, 4) then std_ConstructArray(puVar1+2, 0x00576BA8, 0x3C, count) with header words 0x3C and count; self->f_1C = 0, self->f_20 = bank, then func_00577518(self) fills the records; count field bank+100 and 0x3C stride are shared with FUN_00577518, FUN_005774A8 and FUN_00577868; callers Model_AttachAnimationByHandle, Event_ActorModels_CreateSlotModel, Anim_ModelLoad_ByName, maybe_Gfx_Node_CreateChild.

name: Gfx_SpriteSet_InitBaseFromBank
summary: Binds a loaded sprite/animation bank to the object's inline base record: resolves entry 0, copies its 0x30 bytes of metadata, patches the name pointer and index and stores the bank handle at +0x60.
evidence: Called by confident caller Event_ActorModels_SetModelAnimSimple (0x004B979C) to bind loaded sprite bank metadata to model record.

name: Anim_UpdateChannels
summary: Advances every animation channel of a node: iterates the 0x3C-byte channel records starting at +0x1C (count in the owner object at f_20+100) and calls the per-channel interpolator 0x577064, then processes the embedded single channel at +0x24. The 0x3C stride and the owner count at +0x64 are the animation track table; thirteen callers are model state updates.
evidence: iVar2=self->f_1C + *(self->f_20+100)*0x3C; loop func_00577064(self,channel); if f_60: func_00577064(self,&f_24) then copies f_5A..f_5D into f_6E..f_71; callers Monster_Model_SetState, 0x0042145C, 0x0047E214, ...

name: Mem_FreeAnimArray
summary: Frees the animation array at +0x1C with the array-delete helper and clears the pointer. Called by the node destructor and by Model_AttachAnimationByHandle when replacing the clip; the callee is std_operator_delete_array.
evidence: if self->f_1C: func_00100BCC(self->f_1C, 0x576C2C); self->f_1C=0; callers 0x003C24B0, 0x0046782C Model_AttachAnimationByHandle, 0x004D0E54, 0x00576B00

name: Gfx_SpriteSetList_Select
signature: void Gfx_SpriteSetList_Select(void* self, unsigned int index)
summary: Selects the active sprite set by index in the container's linked list, refreshes every record's name and index from the bank and marks the selection valid (or clears it when the index is out of range).
evidence: Range check with func_00579874 against self->f_98; on failure sets f_A4 = 0, f_A8 = 0xFFFFFFFF, f_AC = 0; otherwise walks self->f_9C index times, stores self->f_A4 = selected set, f_A8 = index, f_AC = 1; per-record loop uses bank+100 count, 0x3C stride, func_00665740 for the name and func_00576BA8 for the metadata; refreshes f_6E..f_71 when f_60 != 0; callers FUN_00421308, FUN_0047E500.

name: Gfx_SpriteSet_Refresh
summary: Rebuilds every sprite record of the set from its bank: skips invalid entries, copies the 0x30-byte metadata, writes the name pointer and record index, then re-derives the per-record state and colour fields.
evidence: Loops func_00665740(self->f_20, i) skipping 0xFF entries, copying iVar2->f_C..f_3B into the 0x3C record and setting record->f_C = name, f_10 = i; stops at the record count (bank+100) or 300 entries; tail calls func_00577064 per record and copies f_5A..f_5D into f_6E..f_71 when self->f_60 != 0; only caller FUN_00576EEC.

name: Container_List_InitAlt
summary: Second intrusive-list constructor, same layout as 0x576A80 but with a different class tag and a node pool at +0x24 (fields 0x3c..0x55 hold count/1.0/-1/0x80/0xff defaults).
evidence: Constructs intrusive list with node pool at +0x24 and default capacity/range values.

name: Gfx_SceneNode_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a scene node: frees the anim array, unlinks its three intrusive list nodes, then frees the object. Same unlink triple as 0x5777AC but ends with operator delete, so it is the deleting variant.
evidence: frees arg1[7] with 0x576C2C; unlinks pairs arg1[10]/[0xB], [5]/[6], [2]/[3]; func_0010F6CC free; no callers (virtual)

name: Gfx_SceneNode_DtorBody
summary: Base destructor body of the scene node: installs vtable 0x782704, frees the anim array and unlinks the three intrusive lists, returning the object (no free). The non-deleting half of 0x577740; called from the container node release and the node destructor.
evidence: stores g_00577810=0x782704; frees arg1[7]; unlinks arg1[10]/[0xB], [5]/[6], [2]/[3]; returns arg1; callers 0x003C24D8 maybe_Container_Node_SetOwnerAndRelease, 0x00576B00

name: Gfx_DoubleBuffer_Alloc
summary: Allocates a pair of 0x4000-byte buffers and stores both pointer/size pairs in the caller's structure.
evidence: Two 0x0010F6EC(0x4000, heap, 4) calls stored at arg1[1]/arg1[4] with sizes 0x4000 at arg1[2]/arg1[5] and aliases at *arg1/arg1[3]; called from Gfx_CharShadowPass_Init (0x002D4F28).

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSortedSpriteList
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSortedSpriteList(unsigned int gfx, unsigned int cmd, unsigned int ctx, void* spriteSet)
summary: Draws a sprite set in draw-priority order: inserts the set's records into a temporary list sorted by the u16 priority at +0x30, then emits each sprite through func_00577E9C sharing one cached texture/blend state.
evidence: Caller Gfx_Overlay_DrawSortedList (0x002D31B0) passes self->f_A4 as arg4; iterates the records at arg4->f_1C with count bank+100 and stride 0x3C; skips entries whose name is 0 or whose texture index f_20 equals the literal 0x0000FFFF (g_005779C4); insertion-sorts with func_001235A4 comparing *(u16*)(node+0xC) against record->f_30; per-sprite call func_00577E9C(gfx, cmd, ctx, set, record, bank, &cache, 0) with cache words initialised to 0xFFFFFFFF.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition(unsigned int gfx, void* cmd, unsigned int ctx, void* list, unsigned int fade, float* color)
summary: Draws a sprite set in transition mode: per record it either uses the normal sprite path (alpha 1.0) or the interpolating path when the set carries a fade colour/alpha, and updates the shared blend/alpha command state when the mode changes.
evidence: Only caller FUN_002D4484; chooses the set as arg4->f_A4 or arg4+0x1C; compares arg4->f_B8 with 0x3F800000 and uses f_B0 (position offset), f_BC (sort/palette threshold), f_C0/f_C4 (fade colour and alpha, converted with VectorFloatToUnsigned(f_C4*0x437F0000)); dispatches to func_00577E9C (normal) or func_0057895C (transition) with &arg4->f_B0 as the from-position; literals 0x55555555/0x33333333/0x0F0F0F0F popcount trick plus 0x00108418/0x00834084 for a lazy 0x1F8/0x200-entry table.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteQuad
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteQuad(void* gfx, void* cmd, unsigned int ctx, void* set, void* sprite, void* bank, unsigned int* texState, float* offset)
summary: Draws one sprite quad: fetches its frame rect from the texture bank, builds a rotated/scaled 4-corner quad in screen space, applies flips and modulate colour, emits the blend/alpha command state and the texture command block.
evidence: Callees func_00665714(bank, sprite->f_20) returning the u16 frame/size entry, func_0056C738 (texture size), func_00563200 (screen size), func_006F1B78 (packet), func_0056D544 (texture command block), func_001052C8 (render context), func_00507E00/func_006564C0/func_0065654C/func_00656ACC/func_00656918 (blend and alpha state); literals 0x3F800000, 0x3C8EFA35 (deg->rad), 0x40C90FDB/0x40490FDB (2pi/pi), 0x40800000/0x40000000; record fields f_14 rotation, f_18/f_1C scale, f_20 bank index, f_32/f_34 position, f_36..f_39 RGBA, f_3A blend bits, f_3B flip bits; callers FUN_00577868 and FUN_005779C8.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenTexture
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenTexture(u32 gfx, void* cmd, void* tex)
summary: Emits the GPU command sequence that binds an overlay texture for one draw: binds the texture handle, builds the texture/colour state chain (0x0065660C..0x00656BCC), a six-slot command node and finally writes the texture descriptor, advancing the command cursor stored at cmd+4.
evidence: NEW: the command helpers on both ends are named - Gfx_CmdList_BindTexture at the start and Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureDescriptor / Gfx_CommandNode_BuildChain4 at the end - and both callers are overlay draw paths (Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen and its B variant). That supports 'overlay draw command', though whether the texture is the screen copy specifically is still open, hence 0.5.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteTransition
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteTransition(void* gfx, void* cmd, unsigned int ctx, void* set, void* sprite, void* bank, unsigned int* texState, float* fromPos, unsigned int extraColor, unsigned int extraAlpha, float* toPos)
summary: Transition variant of the overlay sprite draw: interpolates position and colour by the s0 factor, optionally emits the extra tinted bar quad (command 0x80000008) and writes the normal or extra texture command block.
evidence: Its caller Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteListTransition (0x5779C8) and the named callees Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnitBlock, Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteDepthStencilRegisters and Gfx_Pica_EmitModelTextureBindings confirm the sprite-draw path.

name: Gfx_SetBlendStateA
summary: Applies a blend/depth state packet to the current draw block: initialises the state struct (0x507E00) and submits it through two GPU state commands (0x6564C0, 0x656918).
evidence: Called by confident caller Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen (0x002D36C8) to submit GPU blend/depth state commands.

name: maybe_std_StaticInitThunk
summary: Compiler-emitted static-array initialiser thunk that tail-calls std_ConstructArray with the r0..r3 arguments still live at entry; neither the global nor the element type is recoverable.
evidence: No caller and no body. The raw listing at the exact address is decoded in the wrong instruction set (the ARM push {r4,lr} word appears as Thumb push.w/.short), so neither the arguments at the tail call nor the destination table can be read; the name only records a compiler-emitted static array constructor.

name: maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordPair
summary: Releases the two owned pointers of a resource record - self[0] and self[3] (+0xC) - and zeroes the six header words self[0..5]; returns the record pointer.
evidence: Same body as 0x00569CB8 minus the third free (template copy); the callee 0x10F69C is the deleting-destructor thunk ('ldrd r0,r1,[p-8]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; bx r2'), so this is a record release helper, not a model-specific one.

name: Ui_Widget_CountChildren
signature: int Ui_Widget_CountChildren(int self, int needVisible, int needSelectable)
summary: Counts the children of a UI widget: with both filters zero it just counts the intrusive list, otherwise it counts only children that pass the visibility virtual (+0x18) and the selectable virtual (+0x24). Forty-five callers across the battle/menu/party windows make this the central child-count helper; the two virtual filters explain the arguments.
evidence: walks list self->f_10..self+0xC; if filters set calls (*(*child+0x18))() and (*(*child+0x24))(); callers Menu_CountPartyActors(0x20B5AC), Battle_CountActionTargets, Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_BuildRows, Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshRows, Ui_PartyWindow_SyncMemberOrder, ...

name: Fs_NameCopyClamped
summary: Copies an object name into a fixed 0x40-byte field of a record: clamps the length to 0x3F characters (with a NUL), memcpys it and stores the surrounding header words.
evidence: Called by Fs_NamedObject_FindAndRead (0x0056F9AC) to copy name into fixed 0x40-byte record field clamped to 63 chars.

name: Script_CallWithStackTop
summary: Pushes null, copies the VM's top-of-stack value into a managed reference and calls the supplied callback with it, then releases the reference - the plumbing used by the script event/book parameter setters when they must hand the current stack top to a callback.
evidence: NEW: the VM callees are now named (Sq_VmReadStackSlot at index -1, Sq_VmPop, plus the ref init/clear helpers), so the 'read top of stack, pass to callback' reading is confirmed; the callers maybe_Script_SetEventParams / maybe_Script_SetBookCommandParams are also consistent with passing script arguments along.

name: Script_EventVm_Init
summary: Creates the Squirrel VM used by an event script: Script_Vm_Create with an 0x40-entry stack, registers the default table members, installs the 0x0055A4D8 callback, finalises the VM, stores it at self+0x24 and clears the two-word global at 0x0083876C.
evidence: NEW: the sole caller Script_LoadEventScript (0.55) loads script_message.bxon/cs_text.bxon and runs Script_RunScriptFile in the same event-script path, and the body's Script_Vm_Create/0x006BB650/0x006BD780 sequence is the standard Squirrel VM setup, so 'event VM initialiser' is confirmed; only the 0x0055A4D8 callback's exact role is unknown.

name: Script_InvokeScriptCallback
signature: void Script_InvokeScriptCallback(unsigned int out, void* self, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int ret)
summary: Calls a script-side callback from a native: takes the callable on the VM stack, calls it with one argument, reads the boolean result and forwards it through the two-value invocation helper func_00576768.
evidence: Callers Script_CallBookIdCommand, Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent, Script_CallSelectRuraPattern, Script_CallOnCalcScenarioProgress, Script_CallSelectRiremitoUsable, Event_RunTriggerCommandCallbacks, maybe_Script_CallEventHandlers; tags g_00579D10/g_00579D14/g_00579D18 (0x01000001)/g_00579D1C; callees Sq_VmGetStackSlot, Sq_VmReadStackSlot, Sq_PushRefValue, func_006BC724, func_006BC7A0 (push arg3), func_006BB664 (call), func_00576768(out, &local_44, arg4) for the second stage; releases refs via func_006BD10C/12C.

name: Script_RunScriptFile
signature: bool Script_RunScriptFile(void* self, unsigned int scriptRef, unsigned int mode)
summary: Loads a script file through the bytecode loader and runs it: saves the VM stack top, calls the loader with the script name/arguments, then restores the stack and reports whether execution succeeded.
evidence: String literal s_scriptName at 0x00579D8C; callee FUN_00564828 (0x00564828) which reads the UTF-8 BOM, raises 'cannot open the file', 'io_error' and 'Unrecognozed ecoding' and loads bytecode with func_006BCF6C; the VM handle is self->f_24 and the stack top is saved with func_006BBD6C and restored with func_006BD830; result test func_006BB0F4(vm,1,0) >= 0; callers maybe_Script_LoadEventScript (0x0025330C) and Script_RunAttachedCnut (0x0028E03C).

name: Script_MakeObjectRef
summary: Wraps a native game object in a reference-counted Squirrel value: installs the wrapper vtable, stores the object's +0x24 handle, marks the value as owning a reference, resolves the object's own slot with 0x006BBCEC and links the reference through 0x006BA690, then bumps the object's user count.
evidence: `f24 = obj->f_24; *out = g_00579df8; out[1] = f24; *(u8*)(out+4) = 1; func_006BD12C(out+2); *out = g_00579dfc; func_006BC798(out[1]); func_006BBCEC(out[1], 0xffffffff, out+2); func_006BA690(out[1], out+2); func_005B4C34(f24, 1);`. Only caller 0x00250A38 (Script_RegisterSubThread), which stores the result under a script name.

name: Svc_ReleaseMemoryBlock
summary: Clears a memory-block flag and returns its buffer to the system allocator.
evidence: Called by confident caller Ui_Window_ReleaseLists (0x002543E4) and 0x006BB330 to free allocated memory block.

name: Serializer_ReadVarUInt
signature: unsigned Serializer_ReadVarUInt(Stream* stream, unsigned unusedArg2, unsigned unusedArg3, unsigned defaultValue)
summary: Reads a variable-length unsigned integer from a virtual stream: one byte, and if it is >= 0x80 the number of extra bytes comes from the nibble-indexed table at 0x0079?EEC, then the remaining bytes are shifted in 8 bits at a time. Returns 0 on short read.
evidence: vtable[9] (stream read) requested once; if (byte & 0x80) count = table[(byte>>4)&0xf]-1 and further bytes are OR-ed in at (i*8+8). Table pointer g_00579eec is a rodata array of byte counts indexed by the top nibble.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawVisiblePartsA
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawVisiblePartsA(Gfx_PartList* list, unsigned cmdList, unsigned arg3, unsigned* params)
summary: Draws the visible parts of a part list: for every part index it tests the visibility bitmask (byte at list[0x16] indexed by the part's id) and calls the list's draw slot +0x30.
evidence: only caller 0x57E220; loops the f_f2 parts of list[0x39] and tests 'byte[list[0x16] + id>>3] & (1<<(id&7))' before (*(*list+0x30))

name: Gfx_Node_DestroyChildren
summary: Virtual teardown slot for a scene-graph node: asks the node for its child list (vtable+0xc) and then releases the list (vtable+0x10). Ghidra could not recover the indirect jump at 0x57A00C but the two calls are enough to identify the role.
evidence: Virtual scene node teardown method; queries node child list via vtbl[0x0c] and releases it via vtbl[0x10].

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_ApplyEnvParams
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_ApplyEnvParams(GfxModelInstance* self, const float* envParams, const float* cameraBasis)
summary: Per-frame environment update for a model instance: copies 12 floats of light/colour parameters into +0xa8..+0xd4 (or combines them with the instance matrix when flag bit0 of +0x164 is set), rebuilds a billboard frame and forwards it to the effect emitter 0x532F44, then computes a distance-based colour/alpha scale into +0xd8.
evidence: Reads 12 floats from arg2 into self+0xa8..; when (self->f_164 & 1) is clear it copies, otherwise 0x125404/0x12515C (matrix helpers). Calls 0x00532F44 (maybe_Fx_Billboard_EmitList) with &self->f_34 when the camera flag bits say so. Distance factor uses 0x0057A268 (1.0), 0x0057AB3C/40/44. Referenced from vtable 0x7828C4 slot 0x14.

name: Gfx_SceneObject_DrawParts
signature: void Gfx_SceneObject_DrawParts(void* self, void* cmd, u32 ctx, u16* partIndex, void* color, u32* drawState)
summary: Draws the parts of a sized scene/overlay object: selects per-part state, binds texture state, writes the matrix/colour vertex-uniform blocks and emits the part quads honouring the clip/fade flags. Vtable method (PTRREF table 0x007828D8), no direct callers.
evidence: Twelve callees are now named (Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteMeshPartCommands, Gfx_MaterialState_WriteConstants, Gfx_MeshChunk_DrawPartList, Gfx_DrawRecord_WriteSubBuffers, ...), which pins this to the mesh-part draw path rather than to a sprite.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_UpdatePartBounds
summary: Refreshes the cached per-part axis-aligned bounds of a model instance. For each node it either derives the AABB from the node frame (when the model has an unskinned part table) or unions the child AABBs, then clears the "bounds dirty" bit 2 of +0x164.
evidence: if (self->f_164 & 4): iterates self->f_28->f_6c nodes, reads node flags/vertex tables at +0x68/+0x6c, transforms with 0x12551C (matrix*vec), writes 6-float AABB to self+0x64 table, clears bit 2. Two symmetric branches (skinned vs rigid) match G3D-style model part handling.

name: Anim_UpdateBlendTracks
summary: Advances one frame of an animation cross-fade group: moves the fade timer (+0x11C) toward its duration (+0x120), swaps the current/next tracks when it completes, and advances the two optional sub-track timers (stride 0xC, timers at +0x128/+0x130) by delta.
evidence: NEW: the body is the cross-fade state machine itself - timer +0x11C toward +0x120, swap of +0x10C/+0x110, two sub-tracks at +0x114 with their own timers - and it ends by applying each active track through 0x0055E61C. No bl to 0x0057B0EC exists, so it is reached by pointer, which is why the first pass saw no caller.

name: Gfx_CharModel_Init
signature: int Gfx_CharModel_Init(GfxCharModel* self, GfxAllocator* alloc, GfxAllocator* alloc2, GfxModelDesc* desc)
summary: Initialises a drawable character-model instance from a model resource: sizes and allocates the per-part/material buffers, counts normal vs outline parts, and builds the part index lists. Returns 1 on success and 0 when the resource header is missing or a sub-buffer fails.
evidence: Returns 0 immediately if self->f_28 (model resource) is 0; 0x0065AA28 computes the 5 sub-buffer sizes that are summed (local_cc+local_d8+local_e0+local_d4+local_d0) and passed to Mem_AllocAligned for self->f_fc/f_100; 0x0065B310/0x0065AC3C/0x0065AFBC/0x0065B4F8/0x0065B618 initialise self->f_2c, f_34, f_58, f_6c (assert-fail path sets self->f_28=0 and frees f_fc/f_100); walks self->f_28->f_48..f_4c in 0x38-byte records testing (*p & 0x70000) and comparing the name at +0x34 with '_Outline' (0x0057B960) via Gfx_ResourceTrie_Lookup, counting f_f0 (normal) and f_f2 (outline); looks up 'N_ALL' (0x0057B980) and 'OutlineCenter' (0x0057B970) via 0x0050DD5C/0x00659668; allocates f_e0/f_e4/f_e8/f_ec index arrays and copies desc[0]/desc[1] counts into f_154/f_15c with lists at f_150/f_158 (same fields later consumed by FUN_0057BFF4); f_164 bits 3/4 set from desc[5]&1 and desc[3]&1.

name: Gfx_CharModel_DrawPart
signature: void Gfx_CharModel_DrawPart(GfxCharModel* self, GfxCmdBuf* cmd, void* ctx, unsigned short* partRef, float* matrix, unsigned int* xform)
summary: Emits the PICA command stream for one model part: writes the palette/matrix command blocks, texture and material state, then the indexed draw call, choosing different paths for outline/1D/2D part modes.
evidence: PTRREF at 0x007822C4 and 0x007828E0 both list this function at slot +0 (emit slot) with neighbours 0x0057C230 and 0x005659E8/0x0057A26C; writes raw PICA command words from literals 0x804F02C0, 0x000F02C0 (0x000100E0/0x00000000 also used), builds 0x80000017 + 0x804F02C0 blocks with three consecutive 1.0f (0x0057BFA0) entries; uses GfxCmdBuf cursor at (arg2+4) exactly like the other 0x0065xxxx emitters here; part struct is pbVar14 = self->f_2c + *arg4*0x158 and material/part state comes from arg4->f_16->f_34 + *arg4*0x2c; callers of the 0x0065Cxxx helpers include Gfx_SceneObject_CullAndDrawParts; matrix for the object is self->f_78..f_a4 and is copied with 0x0012558C into 12-word blocks; self->f_dd selects the alternative transform path.

name: Gfx_CharModel_Update
summary: Per-frame update of a character-model instance: re-evaluates the skeleton/animation into the node matrices, runs the registered part interfaces and per-part update callbacks, and marks the pose dirty.
evidence: PTRREF at 0x007822A4 and 0x007828C0 put this at slot +0 with maybe_Anim_UpdateBlendTracks at -4 and Gfx_SceneObject_CullAndDrawParts at +8 (same class family as FUN_0057B330/FUN_0057BA58, which share f_150/f_158); body calls the interface at self->f_144 slot +8, updates the poser (0x006E8888 on self->f_104 and self->f_34), calls 0x0055E5B8 for f_10c/f_110, iterates the two f_114 slots with 0x0055E560, calls self->f_146/f_14c interfaces, then walks the f_150/f_154 and f_158/f_15c arrays (0x007122E4 and 0x0065C210 with i->f_20/f_18); ends with self->f_164 |= 1.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_UpdateDistanceFade
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_UpdateDistanceFade(GfxModelInstance* self, const Camera* camera, const GfxViewport* viewport)
summary: Computes the distance-based fade/scale factor for a model instance from the camera and viewport matrices and multiplies the instance's per-part fade array by it. Base value uses the projection row and viewport height; parts listed in the instance fade table are scaled in place.
evidence: Multiplies self->f_e8 array by fVar7 = (camera->[0x20..0x2c] * viewport term) * 0x0057C39C / viewport->f_14; optional node matrix walk via 0x57609C when self->f_f8 != 0xffff. Referenced from the same model-instance vtable (0x7828D4 slot).

evidence: resets query list; cell=query[0xB]+cell*200; func_0058DEB8; midpoint/extent from pfVar3[0..5] and +3 offset; func_00665564/0x574440 transform; func_0058AA3C(query,&box,cell); then func_0058AF50; caller 0x0058E3F4

name: Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject
signature: GfxSceneEntry* Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject(GfxSceneEntryPool* pool, void* owner, float* uvRect, u32 uvIndex, u8 tag)
summary: Allocates one 0x9C-byte scene entry from a bitmap-tracked pool (three 8-word bitmaps), attaches it to the sprite/node object in 'owner' and stores the object's 6 floats (u0,v0,u1,v1,du,dv) as 4.12 fixed point (x4096). 'tag' 1 = sprite entry, 2 = node entry (see the two create/attach wrappers).
evidence: Fills one of three 0x9C-stride slots at pool->f_18, count in f_24/f_20, free-bit bitmaps at f_1c; g_0058C1C0 = 4096.0f used as the fixed-point scale for the UV rect; called by both sprite (0x58EBA0) and node (0x58EE64) creators with tag 1 / 2.

name: Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord20
signature: void Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord20(GfxSpriteParts* parts, u64* record, u32 index)
summary: Appends one 20-byte part record (two u64 values plus a u16 index) to the small vector at parts+0x68, growing it with std_Vector20_Reserve and setting the dirty flag +0x60 |= 2.
evidence: The grow helper is the now-named std_Vector20_Reserve (20 = 0x14 bytes) and the dirty-flag write is visible, so the record size in the old 'Add14' name is explained and the append role is mechanical.

name: Gfx_SpriteParts_AppendRecord
signature: void Gfx_SpriteParts_AppendRecord(void* parts, u64* record, u32 index)
summary: Appends one 40-byte (0x28) part record to the sprite-part builder's second vector: a 16-byte generated key (0x00665618), two u64 values from the source record and the u16 index, growing the vector through std_Vector40_Reserve and advancing the write cursor by 0x28.
evidence: NEW: caller Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart40 (named) builds its parts with exactly this call, and the reserve helper is the now-named std_Vector40_Reserve whose 40-byte element matches the ten words (0x28 bytes) written here; the earlier 'Add40' wording was already replaced by 'AppendRecord', which the body confirms.

name: Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord44
signature: void Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord44(GfxSpriteParts* parts, u64* record, u32 index)
summary: Appends one 44-byte part record (four 64/32-bit values plus a u16 index) to the vector at parts+0x88, growing it with std_Vector44_Reserve.
evidence: The grow helper is the now-named std_Vector44_Reserve (44 = 0x2C bytes), and the body copies exactly that record into parts+0x88 - so the 'Add44' suffix encoded a byte size; the owner is a generic 44-byte record vector, not necessarily sprite parts.

name: Gfx_SpriteParts_Clear
summary: Releases the three part vectors of the stack sprite-part builder (0x2C-, 0x28- and 0x14-byte elements) through the allocator in the element owner's vtable slot +0x14 and zeroes all capacity fields.
evidence: Walks f_84/f_88 (0x2C), f_74/f_78 (0x28), f_64/f_68 (0x14) and calls (*(*owner)+0x14)(owner, first) for each, then clears the triples; called at the end of 0x2E76F8 / 0x2E77CC / 0x4E4BF8.

name: Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat2
signature: void Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat2(GfxDrawPacket* packet, int countA, int countB, GfxDrawParams* params)
summary: Builds a two-batch draw packet for vertex format 2 (primitive type id 2): reserves one buffer with Gfx_DrawPacket_ResizeBuffer, lays out two 0x40-byte batch headers, 0x20-byte vertices and 16-bit index lists, and copies the transform/colour parameters into both headers.
evidence: Arg1[3] := 2 (format id), header magic FLT_MAX (g_0058C6D0) at +4; sizes count*0x20 vertices + aligned u16 indices; the caller 0x58E770 feeds the result to the A-variant triangle intersector, i.e. the packet layout is only used as a mesh for hit tests.

name: Gfx_DrawPacket_ResizeBuffer
summary: Makes sure the packet owns a buffer of at least 'bytes' bytes: frees the old block through the allocator vtable's +0x14, allocates via +0xC and zero-fills the new one. Returns the buffer (0 on failure).
evidence: packet->f_14 is the allocator object; calls (*vtbl+0x14)(alloc, old) then (*vtbl+0xC)(alloc, 4, bytes) and func_001113EC(buf, bytes) (memset); callers are the three Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat* functions that pass exact byte counts.

name: Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat3
signature: void Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat3(GfxDrawPacket* packet, int countA, int countB, GfxDrawParams* params)
summary: Same two-batch packet layout as Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat2 but for vertex format 3, carrying eight parameter words per batch instead of four.
evidence: Arg1[3] := 3; FLT_MAX magic written at +8 and +0xC; copies params[0..7] into both headers; caller 0x58E918 (B-variant hit test).

name: Battle_PopupSlot_Reset
summary: Releases and reinitialises one battle-popup slot: destroys the previous popup object through its virtual destructor, clears the animation state and re-attaches the new owner.
evidence: (*piVar2->vtable[0x14])() releases the sprite/popup object; then eight word stores resetting the slot and self[5]=arg2; called from Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry (0x0058E264) and itself.

name: Gfx_SceneEntry_ReleaseMesh
summary: Clears the entry header (ids/flags) and, when it still references a mesh owner and a child list, calls the owner's vtable+0x14 release and drops the child references.
evidence: Zeroes self[0..3]; self[4]=0 (g_0058ca94=0.0); if (self[5] && arg2) { (*(*self[5]+0x14))(); self[6]=self[7]=0; }. Companion of 0x58D5E8/0x58D42C which fill the same structure.

name: Gfx_DrawPacket_Release
summary: Frees the packet's vertex buffer through the allocator vtable and resets the 8-word packet struct to its empty state (type 0, size limit g_0058CAEC).
evidence: Frees packet[5] (allocator) payload if packet[6] non-zero, then zeroes packet[0..7]; called from the scene reset paths 0x58E2E4 and 0x58F054.

name: Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat1
signature: void Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat1(GfxDrawPacket* packet, int countA, int countB, GfxDrawParams* params)
summary: Two-batch packet build for vertex format 1 (the most parameter-rich header: eight words per batch).
evidence: Arg1[3] := 1; FLT_MAX magic at +4; copies params[0..6] per batch; caller 0x58E3F4 (C-variant hit test).

name: Gfx_Bounds_TransformPointsToObb
signature: void Gfx_Bounds_TransformPointsToObb(int count, float* outPoints, const float* points, int stride, const float* matrix, float* outBounds)
summary: Transforms a point array by a 4x3 matrix, writes the transformed points, accumulates the AABB, and derives an oriented extent block (centre, axes, half-sizes) from the matrix inverse/transpose. Used when a scene entry needs both world-space points and local bounds.
evidence: Per point: fVar7 = m[0]*x+m[1]*y+m[2]*z+m[3], same for rows 2/3; min/max accumulated into arg6[4..9]; then 0x66655B8 (matrix inverse?), 0x5740D8, 0x5744DC (matrix*vec), 0x5746FC (matrix transpose) fill arg6[10..0x13] and arg6[0..3]. Constants g_0058CFF8/FFC/D000/D004/D008.

name: Container_ObjectRef_Release
summary: Releases a 5-word object reference: when both the owner pointer (+4) and the element count (+8) are set it frees the buffer through owner vtable+0x14 and clears +4..+0x10.
evidence: Now seen from the caller side: Font_CacheGlyphsForText and Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritesFromResource call it immediately before overwriting their cached sub-object, and the tiny ctor 0x58D2BC builds the same 5-word struct - the release-and-clear semantics are supported.

name: Gfx_SceneEntry_SetName
signature: void Gfx_SceneEntry_SetName(GfxSceneEntry* self, const char* name)
summary: Copies up to 63 characters of the node name into the entry's inline name buffer at +0x10 and terminates the string (byte +0x4f).
evidence: func_0011142C(&self->f_10, arg2, 0x3f) is a bounded strncpy; then self->f_4f = 0 (explicit NUL right after the 0x3f bytes). Called from the scene-entry setup path.

name: Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntryAttachments
summary: Detaches an entry from its owner: returns the three 0x28-byte transform slots to the node animator at f_94 (count--, state 7), drops the f_90 owner and unlinks the three intrusive list nodes embedded in the entry.
evidence: Uses f_94->f_18 (slot count) and the 0x18/0x28 strides plus func_0010EBE4 (matrix copy) exactly like Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject's tail; called only from Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntry (0x58A248).

name: Container_ObjectRef_Init
signature: u32 Container_ObjectRef_Init(ContainerObjectRef* ref, u32 object, u32 capacity)
summary: Initialises a container object-reference handle: releases previous contents via Container_ObjectRef_Release, assigns the object id at +0x0C, and allocates inline buffer capacity via 0x0058D04C, returning 1.
evidence: Callee 0x0058D00C is confirmed Container_ObjectRef_Release (conf 0.55); this routine is the companion constructor/initializer for the ContainerObjectRef structure.

name: Gfx_Scene_Entry_Release
summary: Destroys the contents of one 0x9C scene entry: frees the attachment buffer at +0x80 through its allocator, then zeroes the entry's owner, transform and link fields so the slot can be reused.
evidence: Called for each 0x9C slot by Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntryPools (0x588748) and by Gfx_Scene_DestroySpriteByHandle/List and ReleaseAllEntries; frees entry->f_80 (allocator) payload and clears f_7C..f_98.

name: Gfx_SceneEntry_SetupFromDescriptor
signature: void Gfx_SceneEntry_SetupFromDescriptor(GfxSceneEntry* self, void* owner, const GfxEntryDesc* desc, unsigned id, unsigned arg5, unsigned arg6)
summary: Fills a scene entry from a compact descriptor without any vertex dedup: clears old references, stores owner/id, resolves the name (0x58D328), computes the name hash (0x58D5D4..E4 constants), and copies the descriptor's bounds, grid and material fields into the entry.
evidence: Clears self->f_7c/f_84/f_88...; self->f_c=arg4; func_0058D328(owner,*desc) for the name; FNV-like hash with g_0058d5d4..e4 into self->f_90; copies desc+0x10..0x2e into self->f_3c..f_78; 0x58D298/0x58D36C for two derived ids. Companion of 0x58D5E8 (full mesh build).

name: Gfx_SceneEntry_BuildMesh
signature: void Gfx_SceneEntry_BuildMesh(GfxSceneEntry* self, GfxAllocator* allocator, const GfxEntryDesc* desc, unsigned id, int arg5)
summary: Main mesh builder for scene entries: resolves the descriptor, optionally compacts unused vertices into a smaller index buffer, allocates the vertex/index block from the scene allocator, remaps indices, transforms points when a transform function is supplied and computes bounding sphere (0x573600), AABB/OBB (0x573F48, 0x575A40) and the name hash.
evidence: Allocates via (*(*allocator+0xc))(allocator,0x10,size); builds a used-vertex bitmap and a remap table (arg3[0x21]&2 path); calls 0x58D228, 0x573600 (bounding sphere), 0x573F48 (AABB), 0x575A40 (OBB), 0x58CC7C (transform points), 0x58D42C (simple path) and frees the temp bitmap with vtable+0x14. Companion allocator call site is 0x5885B0.

name: Gfx_Scene_SortEntriesForDraw
summary: Re-sorts the scene entry draw order: merges the two sorted intrusive lists of each of the three axis buckets by the entry key at +0xC (std::list::merge with the comparator), then insertion-sorts the three bucket distances ascending.
evidence: self->f_18 = bucket count, f_1C = axis mask; merges via func_001235A4 (list splice) and 0x57989C; the merge comparator reads +0xC and the sort swaps the distance floats, with a /10 and /100 divisor via 0x4EC4EC4F/0x39800000; called at the head of all three scene query entries.

name: Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry
signature: void Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry(PopupPool* self, const PopupConfig* cfg, int heap)
summary: Initialises one battle-popup pool entry from a config block: allocates the four popup arrays, the sub-pool at +0xA4 and resets the slot ring.
evidence: Only caller 0x002E5294 (maybe_Battle_PopupPool_Init); passes cfg words 0..4 and 8 to 0x0058F304, cfg[5]/cfg[6] to 0x0058B86C, then Battle_PopupSlot_Reset(self+0xC); guarded by *(int*)(self+4)==0.

name: Gfx_Scene_ResetPools
summary: Releases the whole scene container: destroys every 0x9C entry (std_destroy_range) and every 0x74 node pool, frees both pools and resets all query/batch state, then clears the draw packet.
evidence: Loops f_C4 entries of 0x9C at f_BC and f_B0 nodes at f_AC, frees f_B8/f_A8 with vtable+0x14, zeroes ~40 fields, calls Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntryPools(&f_2C) and Gfx_DrawPacket_Release(&f_C); called by Gfx_Scene_ReleaseAll and the scene destructor 0x58F054.

name: Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitC
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitC(GfxScene* scene, GfxQuery* query, GfxHit* out, u32 useMesh, u32 mask, u16 layer, u32 userData)
summary: Third of the three scene hit tests: collects entries along a ray (Gfx_Scene_CollectRayCandidates) and via the capsule query, builds packet format 1 from them, walks the node/mesh tree with the C-variant intersectors, and returns the closest hit record (id, two shorts, distance fixed at 0).
evidence: Calls Gfx_Scene_QueryCapsule + Gfx_Scene_CollectRayCandidates + 0x580A88/0x583398/0x586494 (C variants) and Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat1 (0x58CAF0); only caller is maybe_Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteVariant.

name: Gfx_Scene_SetNodeTransform
signature: unsigned int Gfx_Scene_SetNodeTransform(GfxScene* self, unsigned int handleFlags, float* matrix)
summary: Applies a 4x4 transform to the sprite (flag 0x4000000) or scene node (flag 0x8000000) referenced by the handle, short-circuiting when the cached transform already matches, and marks the pooled entry dirty.
evidence: Dispatches on 0x4000000/0x8000000 bits: 0x4000000 resolves the node pool via 0x00588A54(self+0x2c) and compares 7 floats from 0x006659FC with arg3 before calling FUN_0057EEC4; 0x8000000 resolves via 0x0058912C and compares 0x00665A10 against arg3 before calling FUN_0058854C (the two SetTransform twins) with 0x00572EC4(arg3); then, if iVar1->f_20 is set, calls FUN_0058BBA0(self+0xa4, entry, &iVar1->f_34) and finally 0x005891A4(self+0x2c, iVar1->f_14); returns 1 on success and 0 when the flag or the pool lookup fails.

name: Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitA
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitA(GfxScene* scene, GfxQuery* query, GfxHit* out, u32 useMesh, u32 mask, u16 layer, u32 userData)
summary: First of the three scene hit tests: sphere candidates are collected, packed into vertex format 2, intersected with the A-variant triangle soup / mesh walker, and the nearest hit is written to 'out' with its distance measured from the query origin.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_QuerySphereCandidates + 0x57EF20/0x58188C/0x58417C (A variants) + Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat2 (0x58C580); called by Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite and Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine, and 0x2E72C8 re-invokes it in a loop to ray-march (uses the returned distance).

name: Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitB
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitB(GfxScene* scene, GfxQuery* query, GfxHit* out, u32 useMesh, u32 mask, u16 layer, u32 userData)
summary: Second of the three scene hit tests: swept-sphere candidates plus segment candidates are packed into vertex format 3 and intersected with the B-variant walkers; the hit distance comes from the segment parameter.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_QuerySphereSweep + Gfx_Scene_CollectSegmentCandidates + 0x57F59C/0x581EC0/0x584C70 (B variants) + Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat3 (0x58C758); only caller is Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteEx.

name: Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass1
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass1(SceneRenderer* self, void* dst, void* node_list, u32 arg4, u32 flags)
summary: Builds the opaque pass of the draw list: collects the visible nodes with Gfx_Scene_RenderPass1, creates one draw entry per node through Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject (pass 1) and links the result into the caller's list; on allocation failure the collected node list is destroyed and 0 is returned.
evidence: NEW: both ends of the body are now confident names - Gfx_Scene_RenderPass1 at the top and Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject / Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeListByIndex in the failure path - and the pass-2 sibling below uses the same shape with mode 2, which is exactly the two-pass split.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteWithEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteWithEntry(GfxScene* scene, u32 handle, u32 resource, u32 userData, u8 index)
summary: Creates a scene sprite from a resource handle and immediately allocates its hit-test entry (tag 1) from the object transform; on failure the sprite is destroyed again so the call is atomic.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteFromHandle(&scene->f_2C, ...) then Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject(&scene->f_A4, sprite, sprite->f_34, index, 1) and Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeByIndex on failure; called by 0x58EC10.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateOrAttachSpriteEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_CreateOrAttachSpriteEntry(FieldModelObject* obj, u32 handle, u32 userData, int resource)
summary: Either finds an existing scene sprite by handle and gives it a hit-test entry (resource == 0), or creates a new sprite plus entry through Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteWithEntry.
evidence: Branches on arg4: 0 -> Gfx_Scene_FindSpriteByHandle(...,1) + Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject; else tail-calls 0x58EBA0; only caller is Field_ModelObj_CreateSprite.

name: Gfx_Scene_AttachSpriteEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_AttachSpriteEntry(GfxScene* scene, u32 handle, u32 userData, u32 flag)
summary: Attaches a hit-test entry to an already existing scene sprite (looked up by handle) using the sprite's current transform; destroys the sprite if the entry cannot be allocated.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_FindSpriteByHandle(scene+0x2C, handle, flag) then Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject(scene+0xA4, sprite, &sprite->f_34, userData, 1); no callers found in the decompiled tree (called through a vtable/thunk).

name: Gfx_Scene_DeleteSpriteWithEntry
summary: Destroys a scene sprite together with its hit-test entry (the entry is returned to the pool first).
evidence: Resolves the sprite object, releases its entry at +0x20 via Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntry(&scene->f_A4) and calls Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeByIndex(&scene->f_2C, handle); no callers in the decompiled tree.

name: Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass2
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass2(SceneRenderer* self, void* dst, void* node_list, u32 arg4, u32 flags)
summary: Builds the transparent/effect pass of the draw list: collects nodes with Gfx_Scene_RenderPass2, creates draw entries through Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject with mode 2 and links them; failure releases the collected list through Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeListB.
evidence: NEW: byte-for-byte the pass-1 function apart from the now-named Gfx_Scene_RenderPass2 and mode 2 in Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject, so the pass-1/pass-2 pair is established rather than guessed.

name: Gfx_Scene_DeleteSpriteEntryList
summary: Walks an intrusive list of scene sprites, releases every attached entry, then destroys the sprite list in one call.
evidence: Iterates from head->f_4 until the sentinel and frees the entry of every node with +0x20 set, then maybe_Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeListByIndex; callers Gfx_Scene_RemoveSpriteEntries and maybe_Battle_PopupPool_Clear.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateNodeWithEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_CreateNodeWithEntry(GfxScene* scene, u32 handle, u32 resource, u32 userData, u8 index)

evidence: Gfx_Scene_CreateNodeFromHandle(&scene->f_2C,...) then Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject(&scene->f_A4, node, node->f_34, index, 2) with rollback via 0x58971C; caller 0x58EED4.

name: Gfx_Scene_CreateOrAttachNodeEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_CreateOrAttachNodeEntry(FieldModelObject* obj, int handle, u32 userData, int resource)
summary: Finds an existing scene node by handle and attaches a tag-2 entry (resource == 0) or creates a fresh node plus entry through Gfx_Scene_CreateNodeWithEntry.
evidence: Same shape as 0x58EC10 but with Gfx_Scene_FindNodeByHandle / 0x58912C / tag 2; only caller is Gfx_SpriteObject_InitFromLayoutDesc.

name: Gfx_Scene_AttachNodeEntry
signature: int Gfx_Scene_AttachNodeEntry(GfxScene* scene, u32 handle, u32 userData, u32 flag)
summary: Attaches a tag-2 hit-test entry to an existing scene node looked up by handle; destroys the node when the entry cannot be allocated.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_FindNodeByHandle(scene+0x2C, handle, flag) + Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject(...,2); called by Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance (0x2E74FC).

name: Gfx_Scene_RemoveNode
summary: Removes a scene node: looks it up by index (0x58912C), releases its attached render entry when present (0x58A248) and destroys the node (0x58971C).
evidence: only caller 0x2E7798 (set two texts on an object); calls maybe_Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntry (0x58A248) and maybe_Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeByIndexB (0x58971C)

name: Gfx_Scene_DeleteNodeEntryList
summary: Node counterpart of Gfx_Scene_DeleteSpriteEntryList: releases the entry of every node in the list and destroys the list.

name: Gfx_Scene_Delete
summary: Deleting destructor of the Gfx_Scene object: runs Gfx_Scene_Release and frees the storage (operator delete at 0x10F6CC).
evidence: Second slot of vtable 0x782B54 whose slot 0 is 0x58F054 which writes *self = 0x782B54; body = 0x58F054(self) then func_0010F6CC(self).

name: Gfx_Scene_Release
summary: Destructor of the scene container: releases the pools, the query state and every remaining sub-buffer (all freed through their allocator vtable) and sets the vtable pointer.
evidence: Stores g_0058F2BC = 0x782B54 (the scene vtable) first, calls Gfx_Scene_ResetPools, destroys 0x9C entries with destructor 0x58D39C (g_0058F2C0), frees ~12 sub-buffers and ends with Gfx_DrawPacket_Release; called from the deleting destructor, vtable 0x782B54.

name: Gfx_Scene_ReleaseSubBuffer
summary: Frees a scene sub-buffer (owner + element pointer pair) through the owner's allocator vtable slot +0x14 and zeroes all four words, so the owning scene can be torn down without keeping stale pointers.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now the confident Gfx_Scene_Release and Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntryPools, both operating on the four-word block at scene+0x94 - the release path the name describes.

name: Battle_PopupPool_AllocateArrays
signature: int* Battle_PopupPool_AllocateArrays(PopupPool* self, Allocator* allocator, int countA, int countB, int countC, int countD, int arg7, const void* owner)
summary: Allocates the four parallel popup arrays (0x9C/0x74-byte elements) plus their bitmaps from the supplied allocator and initialises every element's intrusive links.
evidence: Four near-identical blocks: (*alloc->vtable[0xC])(alloc, 0x10, count*0x9C + bitmapWords*4) and the (count*0x74) variant, each followed by the element link init and 0x0058DE30/0x005883A8 per-element init; the same function also frees the previous arrays through vtable[0x14].

name: Mem_BitArray_Resize
signature: int Mem_BitArray_Resize(BitArray* self, MemAllocator* allocator, unsigned bitCount)
summary: Reallocates a bit array to hold bitCount bits: releases the old word buffer through the allocator, allocates ceil(bits/32) words with tag 4 and clears them. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: If *self: (*(*self+0x14))() release. uVar1=(arg3+0x1f)>>5; (*(*arg2+0xc))(arg2,4,uVar1*4) allocate; zero loop in pairs; stores allocator/word pointer/bit count at [0]/[1]/[2]. Used by the scene-entry vertex bitmap code.

name: Ui_TextColor_Resolve
summary: Resolves the text colour of a character id: reads the record through func_0035EB98, unpacks the RGB565-style u16 at +0x14 plus the record's virtual slot +8 and writes the packed colour to *out.
evidence: Five confident callers - Ui_ApplyTextColor, Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacter, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacterField and Ui_PartySelectWindow_RefreshRows - all use it as a per-character colour lookup, which is what the name says. func_0035EB98 is the engine's party-record accessor, so the argument really is a character/member id rather than a generic style id.

name: maybe_Gfx_GetGlobalContext
summary: Global context accessor: calls engine singleton getter 0x003CEA1C and writes the returned context word into *out.
evidence: Called by Actor_CompareNames (0x00147DC4) and Ui_CharacterQuestPanel_Fill_Part3 (0x003F2740); queries context getter 0x003CEA1C and writes first word to *out.

name: Model_CopyParamBlock
signature: void Model_CopyParamBlock(ModelParamBlock* dst, const ModelParamBlock* src)
summary: Copies a model parameter block (~0x10C bytes) and repairs the five self-relative pointers inside it (at +0x24, +0x34, +0x44, +0x54, +0x64), so the copy can live at another address.
evidence: Copies 0x1A words from +9, then for each of five fields rewrites 'src_ptr + src - dst_ptr' (the classic relocate-relative-pointer fixup); '_UNDEFINED' string in the block; called by maybe_Model_ApplyAttachPointParam, Model_SetupFromTypeId and three Model_ApplyParamType* functions.

name: maybe_Text_WordData_Copy
signature: void maybe_Text_WordData_Copy(TextWordData* dst, const TextWordData* src, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Deep-copies a large (~0x450-byte) word/ruby text object: a 0x140-byte run buffer, a 0x1E-word table, 8x4-byte and 0x68x2-byte element ranges plus 0xA0 bytes of auxiliary data, then fixes up its self-relative pointers.
evidence: NEW: the only direct caller is maybe_Battle_CommandListWindow_IsCursorEntryUsable, which does not fit a text word object; the deep-copy mechanics (std_uninitialized_copy + five pointer fixups) are certain, but the element type is not, so maybe_.

name: Field_ActorEntry_Copy

name: maybe_Camera_RegularShakeKeyData
summary: Not a function: 0x00591204 is a .rodata blob holding the word 0x0046B5A4, the ASCII key 'ReguralyShake' (0x00591207-0x00591215) and the float 0xBF800000. The readable C is the decompiler mis-decoding that data and folding in the real function that starts at 0x0059121C.
evidence: The disassembly shows `pop {pc}` ending the previous function at 0x00591200, then the ASCII bytes of 'ReguralyShake' and the float, and `push {r4,lr}` at 0x0059121C; this entry is a data blob, which is why no code-level name can be confirmed.
