evidence: Callers maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_SelectRecipe(0x00263B04) and maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_BuildDetailWidget(0x00263BEC); rows of 4 bytes at out+2..out+21 with *out = recipeId and out[1] = -1; u16 half filled from func_00192580(0x00192580); if recipeId != -1 the record from Game_GetDataManager + func_0063F108(id) supplies f_10 (entry count, up to 4) and f_14 (offset base) and byte +2 of each 8-byte sub-entry.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Entry_Ctor
summary: Stores the same byte at +0 and +1 and constructs the trailing four-byte-element array at +2 with element type 0x005A62EC.
evidence: No caller and no named callee; 0x005A62EC is unnamed. The recipe-book attribution still comes only from the position between 0x005A691C and 0x005A6D18; too small to identify its owner.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_InitFromFlags
summary: Fills the horse/uma window state: copies six rows of byte pairs from work+0x24A98+0x57D4 into self, derives the per-row enable bytes, and stores the five global flag bytes (Flag_GetGlobalIndexed 0..4) at self+3/+7/+0xB/+0xF/+0x13.
evidence: Its caller Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor (0x004CCC34) passes the window body, and the body copies from the stable work block and stores Flag_GetGlobalIndexed results, which fixes both the class and the init-from-flags semantics.

name: maybe_std_StaticInitWordArray6
summary: Compiler-emitted static initialiser: calls std_ConstructArray with the r0..r3 arguments live at entry, then clears six 32-bit words at the returned base.
evidence: Disassembly (0x005A6C88) shows `blx std_ConstructArray` before any argument setup, then a loop r2=0..5 storing zero at base + r2*4, then `pop {r4,pc}`. That is a static init/clear of a six-word table, not a UI table initialiser as the old neighbourhood name guessed.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor(u8* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor of a small state block used by the recipe-book / title-demo screens: sets the state byte to 1, the id word to -1 and two 0xFF sentinels, then constructs three 4-byte elements of type 0x00192580 at +0xA.
evidence: NEW: the caller 0x001F1BEC is still only maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor, and the element type 0x00192580 is shared with the party-stat code (0x001924DC Party_Member_RecalcStatsFromCommand), so the block's role is plausible but neither the owning screen nor the element semantics is confirmed; kept below 0.5.

name: Ui_RecipeBook_AddEntry
summary: Adds one byte (a recipe/member id) to the list if it is not already present, growing the buffer when full (the non-returning func_00111378 path is the allocator/copy helper), then re-sorts the list through 0x5A71E8.
evidence: Linear find over [list[0], list[1]); on duplicate nothing happens; growth path compares `list[1] == list[2]` and calls func_00111378; stores `*end = value; list[1] = end+1;` then func_005A71E8(list). Callers: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_HandleDirectionInput (0x2640A4) and 0x5A6EC8.

name: Ui_RecipeBook_FillPartyEntries
summary: Rebuilds the recipe book's member list: clears the list, reads the party member count from the work, resolves the lazily created member table and appends every member's byte id (+0xC8 of the record) with the sorted-insert helper, so the entries stay ordered.
evidence: Callees are named now (Party_CountAliveMembers, Party_GetActiveMemberDataByIndex, Ui_RecipeBook_AddEntry) and the callers are the named recipe-book constructor/selection paths, which fixes the 'fill with one entry per party member' reading.

name: Ui_SortedByteList_EraseValueAndSort
summary: Searches for a byte value in a std::vector<u8>, erases the first matching element using std::memmove, and re-sorts the remaining elements using introsort.
evidence: Caller is maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_HandleDirectionInput (0x002640A4); vector layout (*vector=begin, vector[1]=end); calls std::memmove at 0x00111378 and std::__introsort_loop at 0x0071FBA8; immediately adjacent to Ui_SortedByteList_Sort (0x005A71E8).

name: Ui_SortedByteList_Sort
signature: void Ui_SortedByteList_Sort(ByteList* list, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Sorts the byte list in place with an insertion sort: small lists (< 17 bytes) use a straightforward shift loop, larger ones the same algorithm unrolled by 16, comparing with the comparator func_0071FBA8.
evidence: Classic insertion-sort code with the even/odd pointer-shift idiom and an unrolled tail (`i = begin + 0x10`); comparator call func_0071FBA8(begin, end, len, arg4, arg4). Sole caller 0x5A6D88.

name: Gfx_KeyframeTrack_DispatchHandler
signature: u32 Gfx_KeyframeTrack_DispatchHandler(KeyframeTrack* self, u32 context, int* trackData, u32 flags, int owner, u32 arg6, u32 arg7)

name: Model_EvaluateNodeTransform
summary: Evaluates a model node's local transform for the current frame: builds the base translation/rotation from the node's animation channels (or from the bound weighted clips), composes it with the parent transform and calls the node-type-specific matrix builder; marks the node as evaluated.
evidence: Uses self+0x5C (blend enable), +0x54/+0x50 (weighted scale/direction clips), +0x4C (weighted transform clip), +0x34 (node data) and +0x38 (parent node); calls Model_ComputeWeightedScale (0x005AAE08), Model_ComputeWeightedDirection (0x005AAA50), Model_ComputeWeightedTransform (0x005AB1B0), Math_MatrixMultiply (0x0057609C), 0x00574428, std_Sinf/std_Cosf (0x00672E44/0x006731EC); dispatches through g_005A7834 by node type (self->f_34+8) and sets self+0x5D = 1.

name: std_str_contains

name: Gfx_RenderObject_CreateNamedNode
signature: int* Gfx_RenderObject_CreateNamedNode(NodeArena* arena, const RenderDesc* desc, int kind, int value, const Parser* parser)
summary: Carves a two-word node out of the render-object bump arena, stamps the class tag, asks the descriptor parser for the name, resolves that name to an index in the render object's name table and stores the index in node[1].
evidence: NEW: the sibling handler 0x005A8050 in the same dispatch table (0x007A2DD8) is the confident Gfx_RenderObject_AllocFromArena and uses the identical arena bump pattern, which fixes the family. The function does not search for an existing node - it allocates one and resolves a name to an index - so 'FindNodeByName' was misleading.

name: Gfx_ApplyMaterialAnimKey
signature: void Gfx_ApplyMaterialAnimKey(void* arg1, MaterialAnimState* state, AnimKey* key, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies the current material-colour animation key to the graphics context (device+0x11D8..0x11EC): posts the key's colour values when the material animation is not paused, then advances the state to the next key or ends the animation.
evidence: Reads *key->f_40 (start time, 4 floats) and writes device+0x11EC/+0x11DC/+0x11E0/+0x11E4/+0x11E8/+0x11D8; stores key->f_40+1 into state+0xAC (next key); comparand g_005A7B38; part of the same per-frame key application family as 0x005A7E80; no readable callers.

name: Gfx_ResetMaterialAnimKey
summary: Clears the material-colour animation state on the graphics context (device+0x11EC and device+0x11D8).
evidence: Gfx_GetContext(); device+0x11EC = 0; device+0x11D8 = 0; mirrors the fields written by Gfx_ApplyMaterialAnimKey (0x005A7AAC); no readable callers (called through a vtable).

name: Gfx_ApplyLayerColors
signature: void Gfx_ApplyLayerColors(GfxLayerColorSet* self, byte* entry, AnimKey* key)
summary: Applies per-layer colour multipliers to the three material layers: for each enabled layer it sets the blend colours, the layer fade and the material override from the packed floats in the key, then bumps the draw-group counter.
evidence: Builds three device layer pointers (device+0x8C8/+0x994/+0xA60); converts the key floats to packed RGBA with the 255.0f constant g_005A7DA0; calls 0x0055F590 (material select), 0x0055EB60/0x0055EB00 (blend colours), 0x0055F2A8/0x0055F3A4 (layer fade); increments device+0x1340; only runs when g_005A7D9C < key->f_34->f_34 (the key time).

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderObject_CreateNamedNodeAlt
signature: int* maybe_Gfx_RenderObject_CreateNamedNodeAlt(NodeArena* arena, const RenderDesc* desc, int kind, int value, const Parser* parser)
summary: Same as Gfx_RenderObject_CreateNamedNode but resolves the descriptor's second name offset (+0x04 instead of +0x14), i.e. the other of the two named sub-objects.
evidence: NEW: byte-for-byte the same body as 0x005A79D0 except for the name offset (+0x04 vs +0x14), and it sits in the next slot of the same 0x007A2DD8 handler table next to the confident Gfx_RenderObject_AllocFromArena. Which of the two names is the 'primary' one is still unknown, so the Alt suffix and maybe_ stay.

name: Gfx_ApplyColorFadeKey
signature: void Gfx_ApplyColorFadeKey(void* arg1, ColorFadeState* state, AnimKey* key, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies a full-screen colour fade key to the graphics context: reads the key's fade value, stores it in device+0x1240, sets the fade target from device+0x1224/+0x1228 to g_005A7F00/g_005A7F04 and advances the state to the next key.
evidence: Writes device+0x1240 (value), +0x123C (next key), +0x1224/+0x1228 (g_005A7EFC), +0x122C/+0x1230 (g_005A7F00/04); advances state+0xB0; counterpart of Gfx_ResetColorFadeKey (0x005A7F08).

name: Gfx_ResetColorFadeKey
summary: Resets the full-screen colour fade on the graphics context: clears the active key at device+0x123C and restores the default fade value device+0x1240.
evidence: Gfx_GetContext(); device+0x123C = 0; device+0x1240 = g_005A7F34; complements Gfx_ApplyColorFadeKey (0x005A7E80).

name: Model_Instance_DispatchCallback
signature: void Model_Instance_DispatchCallback(int nodeState, ModelInstance* model, int context)

evidence: Pointer referenced in table at 0x005624850 and 0x007A2EFC; calls 0x0055AAAC; calls indirect callback model->f_a4(nodeState, context + 4); sits adjacent to Model_Instance_UpdateFromParams (0x005A8104).

name: Gfx_RenderObject_AllocFromArena
signature: GfxRenderObject* Gfx_RenderObject_AllocFromArena(Arena* arena, const GfxRenderObjectDesc* desc, unsigned id, GfxRenderObjectUser* user)
summary: Carves a 0x4c-byte render object out of a bump arena (arena base + used size), stamps the class tag, id, default matrix and a -1 sentinel, then records the model resource length in the user structure.

name: Model_Instance_UpdateFromParams
signature: void Model_Instance_UpdateFromParams(ModelInstance* self, ModelRecord* record, AnimState* state)
summary: Updates a model instance from an animation/attachment record: reuses or creates the model via 0x0055DD7C, copies the 4x4 transform and pushes the record's scale onto the instance's 0x23C field.
evidence: Checks rec->f_B4 (model id) >= 0 and state->f_58/f_34->f_34 ranges; 0x00530014/0x0055DD7C create the instance, 0x0051D0D8 and 0x00574428 copy the matrix, and the final store self->f_c->f_23C = state->f_34->f_34 is the visible scale; one-shot allocation via 0x0011CFAC/0x0011FE8C.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSet
signature: u32* Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSet(int* allocState, ModelData* model, int* materialDesc, u32 renderFlags, u32* resourceMgr)
summary: Allocates and initializes a 0x20C-byte render object for a 3D model, installs vtable 0x78348C, and binds its material set and texture descriptors.
evidence: Handler 4 in table 0x7A2DE8; calls Gfx_RenderObject_InitBase (0x005A8F50); installs vtable g_005a84a4 (0x78348C); resolves material textures via resourceMgr callback.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateWithScaleOverride
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateWithScaleOverride(RenderObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Render-object update variant: when the parameter object (self+0x208) is flagged at +0x1A it writes that object's +0xC value into the renderer's scale field at (*(*(self+0x10+4)+0x160))+0x134, runs the prepare hook and the renderer's virtual +0x9C, then tail-calls Gfx_RenderObject_Update.
evidence: The tail callee Gfx_RenderObject_Update is now confident (0.50) and the body stores exactly one float into the renderer's scale field - the same field 0x005A9D58 multiplies by f_20C - so 'WithScaleOverride' is supported and the earlier 'WithMatrix' wording named the wrong parameter.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSetA
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSetA(RenderObject* self, const ResPair* resources, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t b, uint32_t c)
summary: Binds the split material set of a render object: initialises slot 0 from the first resource pair, binds an indexed set into slot 3 and a single texture into slot 2.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_Update
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_Update(RenderObject* self, u32 arg2, RenderContext* ctx)
summary: Per-frame update of a render object: refreshes visibility/attachment flags, binds the material set and feeds the blend/material parameters of the current animation frame into the render packets.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_ReleaseModel
summary: Releases the model attached to a render object: frees the model's skeleton node, resets its material/attach state, clears the render flags and then invokes the object's virtual destructor slot.
evidence: Resolves the model at self+0x10 -> +4 -> +0x160; calls 0x0030AC0C on its +0x11C member, then Gfx_SkeletonNode_ResetMaterials (0x005A8E28); resets node+0x599/+0x59A, node+0x11C->+0xDD = 0; finishes with (**(code**)(*arg2+4))(arg2, self+0xC); caller none readable (vtable path).

name: Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSetFromDesc

name: Gfx_SkeletonNode_ResetMaterials
summary: Resets a model skeleton node's material state: clears the node's shader/material overrides and releases the nine material/texture bindings held at +0x44..+0x1C4.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_InitBase
summary: Initializes common base fields of a 3D render object, installs base vtable 0x7834A0, and configures default blend and render flag words.
evidence: Called by Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSet (0x005A8378) and Gfx_RenderObject_BindBlendMaterialSet (0x005A9C0C); writes vtable g_005a9060 (0x7834A0); initializes color/blend templates and transform vectors.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_DetachFromDevice
summary: Detaches a render object's model from the graphics context: clears its material slots, releases its three bindings, unlinks its node from the device attach-slot list (device+0x2A4 + slot*0xC) and from the layer list (device+0xE6C + layer*0xC).
evidence: Calls 0x0057B9B0/0x0057B988/0x0057BFCC on self[2], Gfx_TextureBinding_Release on self+3, Gfx_MaterialBinding_Release on self+0xE, Gfx_MaterialSet_Release on self+0x1B; 0x0010EBE4(device+0x2A4 + (self[0][1] != 0)*0xC, self[2]+4) and 0x001235A4(device+0xE6C + device->f_e84*0xC, ...); no readable callers.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_CreateForModel
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_CreateForModel(RenderObject* self, ModelInstance* model, ResProvider* provider)

name: Gfx_RenderObject_BuildMaterialSets
signature: uint32_t Gfx_RenderObject_BuildMaterialSets(RenderObject* self, ModelInstance* model, uint32_t heap, ResourceSet* resources)
summary: Builds all material slots of a render object for one model: looks up the texture names in the model's texture tables and binds the single, indexed and variant sets plus their two 0x168-byte material records.
evidence: Three 0x00659668 name lookups against model->f_30 (+0 / +0x64 / +0x70 / +0x7C tables), each followed by 0x0055E484, 0x0055E2A8 or 0x00564130; allocation of the 0x168-byte and 0x80-byte records via 0x00109DC8; 0x00100050 builds the material ring; sentinel 0x0000FFFF means 'not found'.

name: Anim_UpdateLinkedSubBlends
summary: Keeps an animated object's sub-blends in sync with its animation clock: when the clock wraps past zero it re-links the enabled sub-objects into the animator's blend slots and restarts their cross-fades, otherwise it just advances them.
evidence: NEW: the body tests the animation clock (anim->f_58 <= 0 or a large negative value) and then re-links the three optional sub-objects through 0x0057B9B0/0x0057B988, using the same timer fields as the confident 0x0057B0EC. No bl to 0x005A95D0 exists, so it is reached by pointer.

name: Gfx_RenderSlot_BindIndexedSet

name: Gfx_RenderSlot_BindSingleTexture
signature: void Gfx_RenderSlot_BindSingleTexture(RenderObject* self, uint32_t heap, int slot, ResDesc* desc)

name: Gfx_RenderSlot_Init
signature: void Gfx_RenderSlot_Init(RenderObject* self, ModelInstance* instance, ResDesc* desc, uint8_t flags, int16_t arg5, int16_t b)
summary: Initialises a render slot: clears the alpha/UV defaults, binds the texture through 0x0055E484 and converts the wrap/border values into the slot's 1/scale and edge fields.

name: Gfx_RenderSlot_BindTexture
signature: void Gfx_RenderSlot_BindTexture(RenderObject* self, uint32_t heap, ResDesc* desc)

name: Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateBlendSlots
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateBlendSlots(RenderObject* self, u32* packet, int flags)
summary: Interpolates the two material-blend weights (f_1E0/f_1E8) with Anim_AdvanceTimelineValue and writes them, with the texture/colour pointers, into the render packet slots 0x44..0x4F; releases the old texture binding when the slot changes.
evidence: The callee set (Gfx_TextureBinding_Release, Anim_AdvanceTimelineValue, func_0055E61C) and the caller Gfx_RenderObject_BindBlendMaterialSet now show the blend-slot update, so both the interpolation and the slot write are accounted for.

summary: Allocates and initializes a 0x210-byte blended render object, installs vtable 0x7834B4, and binds its blend material descriptors.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateScaled
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateScaled(RenderObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)

name: Gfx_RenderObject_RebindById
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_RebindById(RenderObject* self, uint32_t arg2, ResProvider* provider)

name: Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSetB
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_BindMaterialSetB(RenderObject* self, const ResPair* resources, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t b, uint32_t c)

name: Gfx_Sprite_UpdateDescriptorProjection
signature: void Gfx_Sprite_UpdateDescriptorProjection(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, void* desc)
summary: Ensures the shared sprite context exists, pushes the descriptor's UV pair and, when the descriptor carries a size, projects its four corner words through the scene transform and stores the resulting screen position back into desc+4/+8.
evidence: The body never submits a draw: it writes the computed projection into the descriptor's own f_40[1]/f_40[2] (the field it reads on the next call) and uses the named Gfx_Scene_TransformPoint, so SubmitFromDescriptor described the wrong direction of data flow.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_InitSharedContext
summary: Lazily creates the shared sprite render context singleton at 0x007BE318 (0x60-byte objects, vtable 0x007829A4, built by Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init) and, when the descriptor has a UV/index pair at +8, pushes it through 0x2E7798.
evidence: The singleton creation is the same one 0x005AA038 performs and the callee Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init (0.50) is named, but the function has no caller and the second half is a single UV call, so 'InitSharedContext' still overstates the role.

name: Field_LampGimmick_ApplyParams

name: Ui_ObjectList_ResetSlots
summary: Clears the object list and releases its ten 0xC0-byte slots at +0x88, then marks the list as having no owner (f_808 = 0xFF). It is the reset-to-empty form of the confirmed 0x005D1978 Ui_ObjectList_InitSlotArray, which stores an owner pointer instead, and it is called from both Field_Gimmick_Ctor and Field_UiGimmick_Dtor.
evidence: Identical body to the confirmed 0x005D1978 Ui_ObjectList_InitSlotArray (Ui_ObjectList_Clear plus ten Effect_Instance_ReleaseResources calls at self + i*0xC0 + 0x88), differing only in the f_808 store: 0xFF here versus the owner pointer there. Because it runs from both Field_Gimmick_Ctor and Field_UiGimmick_Dtor it is a reset, not an init, so the name was corrected rather than confirmed.

name: Mem_CalcAlignedBufferRange
signature: void Mem_CalcAlignedBufferRange(u32* out, u32 base, u32 size, u32 elemSize, u32 align)
summary: Computes an aligned buffer description: aligns the base up to `align` (align 0 is treated as 1), rounds the element size up to at least 4 bytes, and writes {0, alignedBase, alignedBase + count*elemSize, elemSize} into out.
evidence: uVar2 = align-1; uVar3 = (base+align-1) & ~uVar2; if (elemSize<4) { align += 3; elemSize = align & ~uVar2 } iVar1 = func_0011CFAC(size-(uVar3-base), elemSize) (division helper); out[1]=uVar3; out[2]=iVar1*elemSize+uVar3; out[3]=elemSize; followed by the Sound subsystem (0x5E94F0 Sound_SequencePlayer_UpdateVoices).

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_UpdateVoices
summary: Refreshes the live voices of a sequence player at a new playback position: if the current voice (f_18) is still inside the range of its 0x18-byte event it retunes/fades it with the sound core (0x1EE018), otherwise drops it; releases the pending stream (f_1C) once 0x63071C says it is done, and walks the 32-slot voice bitmask (f_28/f_24/f_30) updating each slot whose handle matches.
evidence: Called only by 0x5E9824 (the seek); uses Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle(0x1EDF88), sound core from func_006F1DF8 (the same singleton the PlaySE natives use), the 0x18-byte event stride seen in 0x5E9824 (`arg1[1] + i*0x18`), and the voice bitmask at f_24/f_28/f_30 with per-slot {handle, data} at f_3C/f_40.

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_Reset
summary: Releases a sequence player slot: clears the pending event, stops all its active voices through 0x5E9A48 when any are live, resets the read/seek positions to -1 and returns 1 so the caller knows the slot is free.
evidence: `if (*arg1 != 0) { arg1[6] = 0; if (0 < arg1[9]) func_005E9A48(arg1, arg1[10], -1); arg1[0xb] = 0; arg1[0xc] = 0; arg1[3] = -1; arg1[4] = 0; arg1[2] = -1; } return 1;`; caller maybe_Sound_ReleaseFileSlot(0x1EDD7C) releases the file slot of the same player.

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_Init
summary: Binds a freshly allocated sound file to a sequence-player slot: verifies the file is of the expected magic (g_005e9820), clears every position/voice field, zero-fills the 0x100-byte voice table and stores the file pointer plus its data pointer (+7 words).
evidence: `if (*arg2 == g_005e9820) { ... clear arg1[0..10] ... func_00116AE0(arg1+0xf, 0x100); arg1[1] = arg2+7; *arg1 = arg2; return 1; }`; caller maybe_Sound_AllocFileSlot(0x1EE294) is the allocator counterpart of the release slot that calls 0x5E9740.

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_Seek
signature: void Sound_SequencePlayer_Seek(SoundSequencePlayer* self, u32 position, int flags)
summary: Moves a sequence player to a new playback position: keeps the previous position, binary-searches the 0x18-byte event table for the event containing the new position, clamps the slot index, then updates/stops the voices (0x5E94F0, 0x5E9968, 0x5E9A48) and processes the events between old and new position (0x5E9B6C).
evidence: `arg1[2] = arg1[3]; arg1[3] = position;` binary search over `arg1[1] + i*0x18` comparing `*(u32*)(...)` with the position; then calls 0x5E94F0, 0x5E9968, 0x5E9A48 and 0x5E9B6C; caller Snd_RequestBgmStop(0x1EE4F8) - i.e. the BGM seek path.

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_StopVoices
signature: int Sound_SequencePlayer_StopVoices(SoundSequencePlayer* self, u32 voiceMask, int limit)
summary: Stops every voice selected by the bitmask: for each set bit with a live slot it fades/stops the voice through the sound core (0x1EDF88), clears the slot, updates the three bookkeeping masks (f_28 active, f_38 fading, f_24/f_34 counters) and returns how many voices were stopped.
evidence: Loop pops bits of arg2 (`arg2 & 1`, arg2 >>= 1) with slots at self + i*8 (f_3C handle, f_40 data); calls func_001EDF88(sound_core, slot->f_3c) = Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle; clears bits in f_28/f_38 and decrements f_24/f_34; callers 0x5E9740 (reset) and 0x5E9824 (seek).

name: Sound_SequencePlayer_ProcessEvents
signature: int Sound_SequencePlayer_ProcessEvents(SoundSequencePlayer* self, u32 position, int arg3)
summary: The sequence player's event pump: walks the 0x18-byte event records from the current index up to the position, and for every record whose type byte (record+0xC) and timing window match it allocates a voice slot (f_10..), starts the referenced stream with 0x1ECADC, updates the active/fading masks and dispatches the remaining event kinds through 0x5E9C6C/0x5EA194/0x5EA4B0. This is the code that turns a BGM track's event list into actual voices.
evidence: 0x984-byte function called only from 0x5E9824 (seek); event stride 0x18 with `*piVar14` = tick and `(char)piVar14[3]` = type; opcode table reachable through `*(int*)(*arg1+0x14) - 9`; voice allocation via the f_10 bitmask and func_001ECADC(sound_core, *(u16*)(record+0xE)); calls the per-opcode handlers 0x5E9C6C, 0x5EA194, 0x5EA4B0; sound core from func_006F1DF8.

name: Sound_AllocStreamSlot

name: Sound_CommandQueue_Commit
summary: Publishes the queue's write index: under the sound mutex, when the queue is active (flag f_20 bit 0) and a write is pending (f_6A != f_6E), sets f_6E = f_6A and wakes the consumer.
evidence: if ((self->f_20 & 1) && *lock < 0) { svc 0x24; if (self->f_6A != self->f_6E) { self->f_6E = self->f_6A; func_00111D50(&lock) } svc 0x14 }; the read/write indices f_6A/f_6E and 16-entry ring are the same as in 0x5EAF40/0x5EB028; neighbours Sound_StreamPlayer_Shutdown / Sound_Stream_EnsureCapacity.

name: Sound_CommandQueue_Push
signature: u8 Sound_CommandQueue_Push(void* queue, u32 arg2, void* payload, u16 id)
summary: Enqueues one sound command: under the mutex, takes the next write slot (16 entries of 0x44 bytes at queue->f_28), copies the payload (0x1261E8), stores the argument and command id, and advances the write index; returns 1 on success, 0 when the ring is full.
evidence: sVar1 = (f_6A + 1) % 0x10; if (f_6C != sVar1) { iVar4 = f_28 + f_6A*0x44; func_001261E8(iVar4, arg3); iVar4->f_40 = arg2; iVar4->f_42 = arg4; f_6A = sVar1; return 1 } return 0; accompanied by svc 0x24/0x14 lock pairs; neighbours Sound_AllocStreamSlot / Sound_StreamPlayer_Shutdown.

name: Sound_CommandQueue_PushCommand
summary: Enqueues a payload-less sound command (command id only, no argument) using the same 16-slot ring and mutex as Sound_CommandQueue_Push.
evidence: sVar1 = (f_6A + 1) % 0x10; if (f_6C != sVar1) { puVar4 = f_28 + f_6A*0x44; *puVar4 = 0; puVar4->f_40 = arg2; puVar4->f_42 = 0; f_6A = sVar1; return 1 } neighbours 0x5EAE28 Sound_AllocStreamSlot / 0x5EB0E0 Sound_StreamPlayer_Shutdown.

name: Sound_StreamPlayer_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a threaded sound/stream object: installs vtable 0x784218,

name: Sound_Stream_EnsureCapacity
signature: unsigned Sound_Stream_EnsureCapacity(Sound_StreamPool* pool, unsigned requirement, const unsigned* requirements)
summary: Grows the stream pools to satisfy a requirement record: looks the requirement id up among the 5-word records in arg3 and reallocates the node, entry, list and packet pools through the allocator when their capacities are too small, relinking the existing entries.

name: Sound_Stream_PopFreeNode
summary: Takes one free 0x18-byte node from the stream pool: reuses the last node of the preallocated pool or allocates a new one and publishes it as the current node; returns 0 when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: The free-node array at pool[8]/pool[10], the 0x18 allocation and the std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeRelease shrink are visible, and the two callers (MoLive_StreamTable_BeginPackets, MoLive_Reader_ReadEp) consume the node as the next packet.

name: Sound_Stream_BuildChunk
signature: unsigned Sound_Stream_BuildChunk(Sound_Stream* stream, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, int arg4)
summary: Builds the next stream chunk: sums the sizes of the queued nodes (wrapping at the ring size f_34), asks the packet builder for a chunk of that size and copies the queued data into it with std_RingBuffer_CopyWrapped.
evidence: The ring walk (f_30/f_38/f_3C) plus std_RingBuffer_CopyWrapped and std_SlotVector_Append now describe the chunk assembly completely, and the caller MoLive_StreamTable_CommitPackets is the matching consumer.

name: MoLive_Stream_PopPacket
summary: Moves the next pending packet slot into the stream's active packet vector and advances the read cursor; returns 1 when a packet was taken and 0 when none are pending. The 3DS sound driver calls it once per packet to walk a stream's queued packets.
evidence: Readable C decomp/readable/functions/FUN_005EBD2C_005ebd2c.c: if(self->f_38!=0) it calls func_007103E8(&self->f_2c, self->f_30 + self->f_3c*0x10) (std_SlotVector_Append of one 0x10-byte slot taken from the ring at f_30 indexed by f_3c), then advances f_3c (wrapping at f_34), decreases f_38 (pending count) and adds the slot payload size (slot[1]+0xC) to f_14 (bit position), returning 1. Callers are all sound-driver entry points: 0x006B98C0 loops it f_38 times (skip queued packets), 0x006B99C4 (MoLive_Decoder_GetPacket) and 0x006B9BC0 (MoLive_Decoder_NextPacket). Same 0x10-byte {owner,instance,prev,next} slot format as std_SlotVector_* (0x0070FC08/0x007103E8).

name: MoLive_BitReader_ReadBits
summary: MSB-first bit reader: pulls bytes out of the stream until the 64-bit accumulator holds at least 'count' bits, then returns the top 'count' bits and drops them. Used by the MoLive packet/EP parser for its variable-length codes.
evidence: Readable C: asserts count<=0x40 via func_0011C810 (noreturn abort), keeps a 64-bit accumulator in *self/self[1], a bit count in self[2] and a byte cursor in self[3]; while (bits<count) { b=*cursor++; acc = func_00300E18(b,0,0x38-bits) | acc; bits+=8; } then result = func_00126148(acc, count) (64-bit shift) and acc = func_00300E18(acc,count). func_00300E18 is the ARM 64-bit left-shift helper and func_00126148 the right-shift helper. Called from MoLive_Reader_ReadEp (0x005EE58C, where it reads a unary run of zero bits and then a stream id: 'while (func_005EBDF4(&br,1)==0) i++; uVar1 = func_005EBDF4(&br,i)') and from MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket (0x005ED154).

name: MoLive_Decoder_CreateFilter
summary: Allocates one 0x24-byte MoLive decoder/filter node through the factory's virtual allocator and tags it as decoder type 2 with sub-type 6 and the given owner argument.
evidence: puVar2 = (**(code**)*arg1)(arg1, 0x24); if (puVar2) { puVar2[5]=-1; *puVar2=g_005EBFD8; puVar2[1]=2; puVar2[2]=6; puVar2[3]=arg1; puVar2[4]=arg2; }; neighbours 0x5EBD2C MoLive_Stream_PopPacket / 0x5EBDF4 MoLive_BitReader_ReadBits / 0x5EC1A0 MoLive_StreamTable_RegisterDefaultDecoders.

name: MoLive_Decoder_CreateFilterB
summary: Second MoLive decoder factory helper: same 0x24-byte node, decoder type 1 with sub-type 0xC.

name: MoLive_StreamTable_RegisterDefaultDecoders

summary: Populates the MoLive stream-descriptor tree with the built-in stream types (3, 2 and 4) plus the caller-supplied type, each pointing at its static descriptor/callback table. Called once when a reader is constructed.
evidence: Readable C: four calls to func_005EC204(self, key, value, &table) with keys arg3, 3, 2, 4 and static tables g_005EC1F4/1F8/1FC/200. The real entry point is 0x005EC19C which is a 4-byte ARM default-argument stub ('mov r2,#1' then falls through, confirmed by disassembly), which is why MoLive_Reader_Ctor (0x005EEDBC) calls 0x005EC19C. Only caller of 0x005EC1A0 is that ctor path; func_005EC204 is Container_AvlTree_Insert.

Called by MoLive_StreamTable_RegisterDefaultDecoders (0x005EC1A0) and the MoLive stream map code.

name: MoLive_Reader_Process
summary: Main per-call state machine of the MoLive streaming reader: scans the incoming buffer for the next packet, validates/changes the packet size, resets the bit reader, then decodes all Eps in the packet and returns a status code (0 = need more data, 2 = packet done, 0x42/0x43/0x44/0x49/0x80/0x100 = the error/again codes).
evidence: Readable C (0x5E0 bytes): calls the reader-interface vtable at self+0x51E ([0x14] get position/size, [0x18] seek, [0x24] get timestamp, [0x28] is-end), calls func_00155380 repeatedly to parse a frame/packet header out of the buffer (rejects headers shorter than 0x10), then func_005ED154 (DecodePacket) in a loop until it returns 0x100, func_005ECF88 (ParseEpHeader), func_005EE58C (ReadEp) in a loop until it returns g_005ECCDC, and 0x005ECD8C/0x005ECCE0/0x005EE398 for the stream-table housekeeping. Contains the string 'error: reader could not change its packet size' (0x005ECCAC) and the two 'invalid packet size' codes at g_005ECCA4/CCA8. Only caller: 0x006B9BF8 (MoLive_Decoder_Update), which maps the returned code to a driver error code.

name: MoLive_StreamTable_BeginPackets
summary: Walks every stream in the reader's stream map and opens a new packet on it (MoLive_Stream_BeginPacket), marking the stream dirty so its data is re-read. Returns 0 if any stream could not allocate its packet.
evidence: Readable C: in-order walk of the tree at self+0x1430 (root at +0x1430+8, same iteration idiom as the other stream-table functions), body = func_005EBA14(stream) and on success stream->f_48->f_11 = 1; returns 0 as soon as one call fails. Callers: 0x005EC700 (MoLive_Reader_Process) and 0x005EEDBC/0x005EEF10 indirectly via the ctor/dtor reset path. The module is provably MoLive, not the generic sound layer: the sibling allocator paths in this band assert with 'MoLive::Allocator: not enough memory to allocate %d bytes !!!' (0x005EC31C, 0x005ED7B4, 0x00735154). func_005EBA14 (named maybe_Sound_Stream_PopFreeNode by N_083, which had no access to the MoLive strings) allocates a 0x18-byte segment from the stream allocator, stores it at stream+0x48 and links it into the pending list at +0x44.

name: MoLive_StreamTable_FlushSegments
summary: For every stream: appends the segment currently queued at stream+0x44 to the stream's segment vector (std_SlotVector_AppendRange), detaches it from its owner and marks the stream dirty. This hands the freshly parsed packet data to each stream's decoder.
evidence: Readable C: walks the tree at self+0x1430; per stream takes f48 = stream->f_48, and when f48 and f48->f_8 are set calls func_0070FC08(&stream->f_2c, &stream+0x44, &stream+0x54) = std_SlotVector_AppendRange over the 0x10-byte slot at +0x44; then unlinks that slot from the intrusive list and re-initialises the list head at +0x44; finally f48->f_11 = 1. Called from MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700) and the ctor path.

name: MoLive_StreamTable_ReleaseUnused
summary: Erases from the stream map every stream that has finished (no pending packet at +0x68 and no queued bytes at +0x38); streams that are still active just have their pending flag cleared.
evidence: Readable C: walks the tree at self+0x1430; per node takes stream = node->f_18->f_10; if stream->f_68 == 0 && stream->f_38 == 0 it calls func_0070C528(out, &self->f_141c, &iter) = std_RbTree_EraseNodeRebalance, otherwise only clears stream->f_68. Called from MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700) right after decoding a packet.

name: MoLive_Reader_ParseEpHeader
signature: u32 MoLive_Reader_ParseEpHeader(MoLiveReader* self, u8* buffer, u32* offset, u32 size)
summary: Parses the leading EP header of a packet: the flags byte (bit0 = 'first', bit1 = 'last', bits2..7 = stream count), the 64-bit time base and the optional 16-bit packet counter, then advances the reader's time by (new_stream_count - old_stream_count) * stream_size. Returns 0 or a MoLive error code (0x43 truncated, 0x44 decode failed, 0x46 inconsistent stream count, 0x50 bad counter).
evidence: Readable C: reads one byte and stores (b&2)>>1 and b&1 into the two flags at self+0x1491 / g_005ED14C+self, takes the 6-bit field (b>>2) as the packet's frame/stream count (the running value at self+0x1484 starts at 0x40 = 'unset'), then multiplies the count delta by self[2] (stream size) and accumulates it into the 64-bit time at self[0..3], then calls func_005ECCE0 (BeginPackets) and validates the 16-bit counter at g_005ED150+self against self+0x1484 (0x10000 = unset) calling func_005EE398 on mismatch. Returns the same 0x43/0x44/0x46/0x50 code set as the other MoLive packet functions. Called only from MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700).

name: MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket
signature: u32 MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket(MoLiveReader* self, u8* buffer, u32* offset, u32 size)
summary: Decodes one packet body: for each stream id found in the packet it looks the stream up in the reader's stream map, creates a 0x24-byte stream entry (with the MoLive allocator, 'MoLive::Allocator: not enough memory...') when the id is new, binds the per-stream decoder callback and feeds it the packet slice. Returns 0x100 when the packet is exhausted.
evidence: Readable C (0x1244 bytes): uses the bit reader 0x005EBDF4, does two ordered-tree searches over the map at self+0x141C (root) / self+0x1430 (header) for the stream id, allocates a 0x24-byte node through the allocator vtable with the 'MoLive::Allocator: not enough memory to allocate %d bytes !!!' string at 0x005ED7B4 (inside this function), inserts it with func_006172CC (Container_AvlTree_InsertFixup), calls func_00715E68 (std_RbTree_InsertUnique) on the secondary map at self+0x507, func_00669820/006698AC (stream-map find / bind), func_0070F840 and func_007106F0 for slot-list cleanup. Called only from MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700) in the 'while (func_005ED154(...) != 0x100)' loop.

name: MoLive_StreamTable_CommitPackets
summary: Walks every stream in the reader's stream map and commits the packet segments gathered so far into that stream's bit-stream buffer (MoLive_Stream_CommitPacket). Returns 0 if any stream failed.
evidence: Readable C: in-order walk of the tree at self+0x1430, body = func_005EBBA8(stream); result is ANDed (0 on first failure). func_005EBBA8 (maybe_Sound_Stream_BuildChunk in N_083) sums the 0xC sizes of the pending 0x10-byte slots and calls func_007103E8 (std_SlotVector_Append) to append them to the stream's decode buffer. Callers: MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700) before parsing Eps, and the ctor path.

name: MoLive_Reader_SetSource
summary: Attaches a data source to the MoLive reader: detaches the previous one, stores the new interface at self+0x1478, opens it (vtable +0xC) and resets the reader state (time, bit reader, packet counters). Returns 0x41 if the source refuses to open.
evidence: Readable C: calls func_005EE4E0 (DetachSource), stores arg2 at self[0x51E] (=+0x1478), calls (*source->vtable[3])(source) as the open call, then (*source->vtable[1])(source) to read the source type into g_005EE4DC+self, and clears *self..self[3] (64-bit time), self[0x520]=0x40, self[0x521]=0x10000, self+0x148F and self+0x1491. The real entry point is 0x005EE430 (a 12-byte 'if (arg2==0) return 0x40;' guard verified in asm), which is what 0x006B9694 calls. Only caller: 0x006B9694 (MoLive_Decoder_Create).

name: MoLive_Reader_DetachSource
summary: Closes and forgets the attached data source, erases every stream from the reader's stream map, releases the segment vector and resets the time/bit-reader state. Used both by the destructor and when a new source is attached.
evidence: Readable C: if self[0x51E] (source) != 0 it calls (*source->vtable[4])(source) (close), clears the slot, calls func_0070CB90(out, self+0x507, first, last) = std_RbTree_EraseRange over the secondary map at self+0x507, then func_007106F0(self+0x50F, 0, self[0x512]) = std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeDelete and clears self[0x512], time and flags (+0x148D). Called by MoLive_Reader_SetSource (0x005EE43C) and MoLive_Reader_Dtor (0x005EEF10).

name: MoLive_Reader_ReadEp
signature: u32 MoLive_Reader_ReadEp(MoLiveReader* self, u8* buffer, u32* offset, u32 size)
summary: Reads one EP (element) record out of the packet: a unary-coded stream id selects the stream in the reader's stream map, then that stream's data is appended. Emits the diagnostic messages 'ReadEp: cannot find stream %d', 'Ep goes beyond end of packet' and 'ReadEp: stream %d already disabled' through the reader's error callback.
evidence: Readable C: contains the three ReadEp strings at 0x005EEA30 / 0x005EEA54 / 0x005EEA74 (all inside this function's range 0x005EE58C-0x005EEDBC); reads the unary run with func_005EBDF4 (MoLive_BitReader_ReadBits), does a lower_bound/upper_bound pair over the stream map at self+0x286 (=+0x1430), reports 'ReadEp: cannot find stream %d' through the callback at self+0x291 when the id is unknown, and returns g_005EEDB8 (0x100) when the packet is finished. Called only from MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700) in the 'while (func_005EE58C(...) != g_005ECCDC)' loop.

name: MoLive_Reader_Ctor
signature: MoLiveReader* MoLive_Reader_Ctor(MoLiveReader* self, MoLiveAllocator* allocator, u32 flags)
summary: Constructs a MoLive streaming reader: clears the time/packet state, installs the allocator, creates the two ordered maps (stream map at +0x141C and the secondary map at +0x507), the 0x10-byte slot vector at +0x143C and the two AVL trees, then registers the default stream decoders.

Caller: 0x006B9694 (MoLive_Decoder_Create), which allocates the 0x14A0-byte block through the global allocator at g_006B988C and pairs it with 0x005EEF10 as destructor; the chain is entered from 0x001B7514 (maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init, N_082), i.e. this decoder supplies the audio of a movie.

name: MoLive_Reader_Dtor
summary: Destroys a MoLive reader: detaches the source, clears both AVL trees, releases the slot vector and the tree node pool, and frees the map's backing store. Returns self.
evidence: Readable C: func_005EE4E0 (DetachSource); func_0061745C(&self->f_1498) and func_0061745C(&self->f_144C) = Container_AvlTree_Clear on the two trees; func_007106F0(&self->f_143C, 0, self->f_1448) = std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeDelete; (*alloc->vtable[1])(alloc, self->f_1440) frees the map block; func_0070CB90(out, &self->f_141C, ...) = std_RbTree_EraseRange and then walks the free list at self+0x1420 freeing each node with the allocator's vtable[1]. name: Save_CryptoContext_Destroy

name: SaveCode_Decode
signature: void SaveCode_Decode(int arg1, int arg2, u8 * arg3, u32 arg4)

name: SaveCode_EncodeFixed20
signature: u32 SaveCode_EncodeFixed20(const u16* ids, u32 count, u8* out)
summary: Encodes a fixed set of 20 item/flag ids (each must be in 0x3000..0x30FC) into the compact 17-character Spell-of-Restoration record: maps ids through the 64-entry alphabet, delta-encodes the 6-bit indices, scrambles them with the LFSR stream, verifies the checksum and fills the caller's record.
evidence: requires count == 0x14 and every u16 in [0x3000,0x30FC] (0xFC < v-0x3000 -> return 0), alphabet at g_005EF8E8 (64 entries), index deltas masked &0x3F, LFSR with g_005EF8EC and 14 x 8 bits, checksum must be 0, then out[0]=1 and the id fields are written from table g_005EF8F0; calls 0x5F0408 for the trailing digit block; related known names SaveCode_Encode 0x5EF33C / SaveCode_Decode 0x5EF3CC / SaveCode_ValidateChar 0x5EF474.

name: SaveCode_EncodeVariable
signature: u32 SaveCode_EncodeVariable(const u16* ids, u32 count, u8* out)
summary: Variable-length variant of the code encoder: maps `count` ids through the same 64-entry alphabet, packs the 6-bit deltas, appends a CRC-16 (poly 0x1021) and verifies it before filling the caller's record with type 2.
evidence: loop j < arg2 over u16 in [0x3000,0x30FC] with table g_005EFD2C; delta encoding with cVar14 = ((local_b8&7)>>1)+1; CRC loop with 0x1021 and masks 0x1F/0x7FF; out[0]=2; ids from g_005EFD34; calls 0x5F0408; neighbours SaveCode_Encode 0x5EF33C / SaveCode_Decode 0x5EF3CC.

name: SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify
signature: u32 SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify(u32 codeA, u32 count, u32 arg3, u32 b, u8* out)
summary: Validates a Spell-of-Restoration input: checks the character set (0x5EF474), decodes the 13-byte payload with the known SaveCode_Decode, verifies/decodes it (0x5F09A4) and unpacks the 3 output words plus the scrambled index into the caller's structure.
evidence: func_005EF474 (SaveCode_ValidateChar) guard; SaveCode_Decode(arg1,arg2,&local,0xD); func_005F09A4(a,&local,&local_30,b); func_005EFF70(&local_30,6,&local_450,7); out[0]=0, words at out+2/+6/+10, out->f_2C/f_30 from local_2C bits; CRC32 table via func_005F08DC/func_005F0868; known names SaveCode_* at 0x5EF33C-0x5EF474.

name: Str_BitBuffer_ShiftRight
signature: void Str_BitBuffer_ShiftRight(u8* buf, int size, u32 bits)
summary: Shifts a byte buffer right by `bits` bits in place (the 32-bit chunk move is unrolled two bytes at a time), zero-filling the tail; used by the save-code bit packing.
evidence: arg3>>3 byte offset, arg3&7 bit shift; loop copies `pbVar5[1] >> (8-shift) | bVar1 << shift` and then zero-fills from the end to arg2; called by 0x5F09A4 (0x5F01AC(&local_20,3,1)) and by the bit-packed save-code encoder 0x5EF914.

name: SaveCode_GenerateCheckDigits
signature: void SaveCode_GenerateCheckDigits(int data, int len, int* out)
summary: Builds the five check digits stored at the end of the encoded save code: seeds a small PRNG from the CRC-16/CRC-32 of the payload (0x5F08DC/0x5F0868), draws five distinct values, then insertion-sorts them into out[0..4].
evidence: CRC32 over arg1 for arg2*2 bytes -> local_638 = g_005F0758 ^ crc; 100-entry (0x32 x2) table and 6-entry selection table on the stack; func_00723CD8 (random) per round; writes out[j*4] for j<5 and ends with an insertion sort; called from 0x5EF4F0/0x5EF914 as the trailing digit generator.

name: Save_CopyChecksumTable
summary: Copies the static 512-byte save/check-digit table at 0x0072E93C through a stack buffer into the caller's buffer and returns it. Called from the save crypto context init and from both check-digit generation and verification, so the table is part of the save-code checksum path.
evidence: All three callers are now named and all are save-code crypto: Save_Crypto_Context_Init (0x005F0E14), SaveCode_GenerateCheckDigits (0x005F0408) and SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify (0x005EFE3C); the 0x200-byte source at 0x0072E93C and std_memcpy are visible. What exactly the 256 u16 entries encode (polynomial vs lookup) is still not proven, so 0.5.

name: std_Crc32_InitTable
summary: Copies the static 1024-byte (256 x u32) CRC-32 lookup table into the caller's buffer and returns it; the table is then fed to the CRC update helper 0x5F0868.
evidence: std_memcpy(auStack_410, g_005F0920, 0x400) then std_memcpy(arg1, auStack_410, 0x400); callers: 0x5F0408 (func_005F08DC(auStack_468)) and 0x5EFE3C; 0x400 bytes = 256 u32 entries.

name: Save_Crypto_SetKeyFromString
signature: bool Save_Crypto_SetKeyFromString(void* ctx, const char* key)
summary: Sets the save-data cipher key from a NUL-terminated string: resets the context state and runs the Blowfish key schedule (0x5F0E64) over strlen(key) bytes, returning whether the key was accepted.
evidence: func_005EFD38(arg1) resets the context; uVar1 = func_0011CCA0(arg2) = strlen(key); iVar2 = func_005F0E64(arg1+0x10, arg2, uVar1); return iVar2 != 0; 0x5F0E64 is the Blowfish ExpandKey (18-word P-array from g_005F1030, 4x256 S-boxes from g_005F1034), so this is its string-key wrapper; 0x5F0E14 initialises the same context.

name: Save_Crypto_SealBlock
signature: u32 Save_Crypto_SealBlock(void* ctx, u32* block, u32* out, const u8* key)
summary: Encrypts one 8-byte block of save data with the context's Blowfish key schedule, mixes in the key/MAC bytes and verifies the resulting MAC before copying the plaintext to out; returns 1 when the block is authentic.
evidence: Save-style flow: copy block, bit-rotate (0x5F02E0/0x5F02D4), func_005F14EC(ctx+0x10, ..., 8) (Blowfish encrypt), XOR with arg4 bytes, second encrypt at a rotated offset, func_005F07A4 MAC over 0xB bytes, compare two bytes and then func_0011FFFC(arg3,&local_30); the same routine family is used by SaveCode_DecodeAndVerify.

name: Save_Crypto_OpenBlock
signature: u32 Save_Crypto_OpenBlock(void* ctx, u32* block, u32* out, const u8* key)
summary: Inverse of Save_Crypto_SealBlock: decrypts one 8-byte block (0x5F19E8), applies the key bytes and MAC, and writes the 13-byte plaintext record to out when the MAC matches.
evidence: starts with func_005EFDB8(arg1) state and func_005F07A4 MAC, decrypts with func_005F19E8(ctx+0x10,...,8) twice, XORs arg4, then out[0..2] + byte at +0x0C = local_38/local_34/local_30/local_2C; mirrors 0x5F09A4.

name: Save_Crypto_Context_Init
summary: Initialises a save-data crypt context: zeroes the header, clears the 0x48-byte P-array and the 0x1000-byte S-box storage, then copies the default CRC table (0x5F082C) into the context.
evidence: *arg1=0; arg1[1..3]=0; func_00116AE0(arg1+4,0x48); func_00116AE0(arg1+0x16,0x1000); func_005F082C(arg1+0x416); returns arg1-0x1058 (the outer object); 0x48 = 18 Blowfish P words, 0x1000 = 4 x 256 S-box words.

name: Save_Crypto_ExpandKey
signature: u32 Save_Crypto_ExpandKey(void* ctx, const u8* key, u32 keyLen)
summary: Blowfish key schedule for the save data: XORs the key into the 18-word P-array, encrypts the running block with the current schedule nine times to rebuild P, then rekeys all four S-boxes the same way.
evidence: requires 4 <= keyLen < 0x39; copies the default P-array (0x48 bytes from g_005F1030) and the 4 x 0x400-byte S-boxes (g_005F1034); XORs the key cyclically into P (0x12 words / 4 = 18), then 0x12/2 = 9 rounds of func_005F153C to rewrite P, then 4 x 0x100 rounds to rewrite the S-boxes; this is the textbook Blowfish ExpandKey.

name: Save_Crypto_EncryptBlocks

name: Gfx_Screen_ForwardFadeOut
signature: void Gfx_Screen_ForwardFadeOut(int self, u32 screenIndex, u32 arg3)
summary: Tail-call forwarder: picks the per-screen fade window (self+4 for screen 0, self+8 for screen 1) and jumps to its fade-out entry 0x0017BD1C (Ui_Bar_StartFadeOut).

name: Gfx_Screen_ForwardSetAlphaVariant

evidence: asm: the word at 0x0060E7B0 is `b #0x17bdc8`, the last instruction of the thunk at 0x0060E7A0 (`cmp r1,#0; ldreq r0,[r0,#4]; ldrne r0,[r0,#8]; mov r1,r2`), so it is code, not a VFP literal; 0x0017BDC8 is the real entry of Ui_Bar_SetAlphaVariant (0x0017BDD0 is a split symbol).

name: Gfx_Screen_GetClearColor

evidence: Entry is 0x60E7FC (`cmp r1,#0` hoisted before push {r4,lr}); 0x17BC6C reads the screen fade float, then `cmp r4,#7; ldrlo pc,[pc,r4,lsl#2]` switch whose cases each load a global colour and swap bytes (lsl/lsr/orr) before returning.

name: Gfx_Screen_GetClearColorByMode
signature: u32 Gfx_Screen_GetClearColorByMode(int self, u32 screenIndex, u32 mode)

evidence: asm: 0x0060E7FC is the entry (`cmp r1,#0; push {r4,lr}; ldreq r0,[r0,#4]; ldrne r0,[r0,#8]; mov r4,r2`), so this symbol starts at its `bl #0x17bc6c`; then `cmp r4,#7; ldrlo pc,[pc,r4,lsl#2]` with 7 cases that each load a global colour and byte-swap it before `pop {r4,pc}`. It RETURNS a colour, so the old 'SetClearColor' verb was wrong.

name: Item_CompareEntryKey16
signature: u32 Item_CompareEntryKey16(u32 arg1, u16* left, u16* right)

signature: void Bg2D_SetTexturePages(Bg2DScene* self, int mode, Bg2DPageEntry* entries, u32 arg4)

name: Font_BuildGlyphPages
signature: u32 Font_BuildGlyphPages(Font* self, FontResource* res, int isAlt)

name: Gfx_Sky_BindModelAndTexture

name: Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_Create

name: maybe_Code_MisalignedSymbol0062209E

evidence: asm: 0x00622090..0x006220BC decodes as one coherent ARM routine (`add r1,r4,#0x10; ldm r1,{r1,r2}; cmp r1,r2; ldrlt r0,[r4,#0x10]; blt; str r0,[r4,#0x10]; add r2,r0,#1; ldr r1,[pc,#0x38]; mov r0,sp; bl #0x6f0e1c`), so 0x0062209E is not an instruction boundary; the coprocessor_function in the C is the damaged Thumb decode, not a UI flag setter.

summary: Tail of the routine at 0x00623114 that assigns a null Squirrel value to self+0x28: releases the temporary SQObject - if its type word has the refcounted tag 0x08000000 it decrements the refcount at +4 and calls the object's vtable slot +8 when it reaches zero.

The 0x08000000 refcounted tag and the vtable/refcount layout are Squirrel's SQObject, not a container slot array. The readable C is damaged (unaff_/flag registers), so the disassembly quoted above is the ground truth.

name: Script_Object_Dtor

evidence: asm: `ldr r0,[pc,#0xc0]; str r0,[r4]` installs 0x00780258; `tst r1,#0x80000000` guards the 0x00245C40 detach; then four copies of the SQObject release sequence (`tst r0,#0x8000000; ldr r1,[r0,#4]; subs r1,r1,#1; str r1,[r0,#4]; blx [vtable+8]`) walk backwards through the members; finally `str r2,[r4,#-0x18]` installs 0x0075A728 and clears the list links. Not a model part-visibility routine. The readable C is damaged (unaff_/flag registers), so the disassembly quoted above is the ground truth.

name: Party_IsMemberActive
summary: Returns bit 0 of the character record found for the member's id at +0xC8 through func_0063F8F0(dataManager,id) - i.e. whether the character currently belongs to the active party.
evidence: Two named callers settle the meaning: Item_FindInInventory (0x00254C20) only searches the inventory of members where this is non-zero, and Party_Status_RebuildRows (0x0023C588) shows or hides the member row from the same result. Party_CountAliveMembers counts the same bit.

name: Party_CountLearnedSkills
summary: Counts how many of the record's 60 skill ids at +0x122 satisfy the per-id predicate at 0x006C29A0, i.e. how many skills the character has learned. The same count gates every walk of the skill list (Party_GetSkillCountSlot0..7, Text_Layout_Init, Text_SetFormatArgsFromPlayerData).
evidence: NEW: the whole family of callers is now named - Party_GetSkillCountSlot0 (0x0070BF2C, 0.60) documents `func_0035EB98(work,slot)` + 'counts the non-0xFFFF entries of its 60-entry u16 skill-id list at +0x122 (0x006291A8)', and 0x003AA448/0x003AAB38 sum the SP cost of exactly this list through SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill. The old 'MonsterBook_CountRecorded' reading is contradicted: the array is the learned-skill list, not a monster book.

name: maybe_Party_GetCharaFlagBit1
summary: Reads the character id at member+0xC8, looks up a small data-manager row for it and returns bit 1 of that row's flags byte (+4). The meaning of the bit is unknown, but it is a per-character data flag, not a PartyMember field.
evidence: CORRECTED: the named caller Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel (0.55) calls this right after func_0035EB98(member) and combines the result with maybe_Party_IsReserveMember, so it is a character-table flag - but the row comes from a bounded data-manager accessor, NOT the 0x434-stride CharacterRecord documented in FACTS, so 'MemberRecord' in the old name was wrong. The bit's semantics still have no string or user evidence.

name: Party_CountExtraSkillSlots
summary: Counts how many of the two u16 ids at member+0x19A / +0x19C pass the same learned-skill predicate (0x006C29A0) that Party_CountLearnedSkills uses for the 60-entry list at +0x122. The party stat calculation (Party_StatCalc_ApplyBaseStats / SetupMemberContext) consumes the count.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x006291A8 is now named Party_CountLearnedSkills (0.60) and uses the identical predicate over +0x122..+0x19A, which fixes both the predicate and the record; this function is the same count over the two slots immediately before the +0x19E active-state array. What the two slots mean semantically is still unknown, but 'extra skill slots' is a faithful description of the operation.

name: PartyMember_GetCharRecordFlag430
summary: Looks up member->u8_C8 (charaId) in the CharacterRecord table (dm->f_38C, stride 0x434) and returns the boolean byte +0x430. This is a per-character 0/1 flag (e.g. 'is available/visible'), not a 32-bit equipment mask.
evidence: NEW: 13 named UI callers now consume it as a 0/1 test (Ui_CharaStatusWindow_FillPartyMember, Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple, Ui_Row_UpdateFull/Text, Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemPanesB, Ui_CharacterQuestPanel_Fill, Ui_ItemListWindow_Build*), and FACTS.md records the disassembly (6 ARM instructions, charaId at member+0xC8, CharacterRecord +0x430 u8). The 'push {r3,lr}' alignment made Ghidra invent trailing args; the real signature takes only member.

name: Battle_CountTargetsWithStatus2E9
summary: Counts the battle units whose status word at +0x2e9 shares the given mask, used to show valid skill targets.
evidence: Loops 0x28 unit ids at self+0x1274, resolves each via func_0018C184 and tests (unit->f_2e9 & mask); called from Battle_SkillTarget_Update.

name: Battle_CountTargetsWithStatus80
summary: Second target-count helper: counts units whose status byte at +0x80 shares the mask (0x3c entries).
evidence: Loops 0x3c ids at self+0x129c, resolves via func_0018C1B8 and tests (unit->f_80 & mask); called from Battle_SkillTarget_Update.

name: Battle_CheckAbilityAllowedByWeapon
summary: Returns 0 unless the ability id is in the actor's 40-slot spell list at +0x1274, then checks the equipped weapon categories (ItemRecord+0x29 and the spell record's +0x294/+0x2ED) and returns 1 only when the current equipment permits the ability.
evidence: The previous 'CanUseItem' was wrong: the first loop searches the 40-byte spell list at +0x1274 (FACTS.md: PartyMember spells), and the second half compares the spell/weapon category fields, with the named caller Battle_CanActorUseAbility; it returns u32 so the Check predicate name is safe.

name: Battle_IsTargetRestrictedByAbility
summary: Returns true when either of the two selected ability ids is one of the special/reserved abilities (0xf8, 0x120, 0x13c and the g_0062973c/40/44 ids) that use a custom target rule.
evidence: Reads the two ability ids with func_006292F0(self,0/1) and compares them against 0xf8/0x120/0x13c and g_0062973c/g_00629740/g_00629744; called from Battle_AttackTarget_Update and Ui_BattleSpellWindow_Refresh.

name: maybe_Party_IsReserveMember
summary: Returns 1 when the party member's CharacterRecord has bit 0 clear and bit 1 set, i.e. the character is not in the active party but is still usable; returns 0 otherwise.
evidence: The body is the same CharacterRecord flag read as 0x0062917C/0x0062923C and the callers pick menu rows / equipment previews for such characters (Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds, Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel, Menu_CreateEntryObjects), which fits 'reserve member', but the label is an inference from usage.

name: Party_Member_HasDualHandWeapon
summary: Returns 1 when a party member's off-hand equipment slot (slot 1 via 0x006292F0) holds either a one-handed weapon (category 0..4 via 0x0066C5A8, dual-wield) or claws (category 6 at ItemRecord+0x29), enabling two-hand basic attacks/visuals; returns 0 otherwise.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x6297D8..0x629840 + 0x6292F0 + 0x66C5A8 + 0x1905E4: every caller passes PartyMember* from 0x35EB98(*Game_GetWork(), charaId) (not Actor* or Item*). Queries off-hand itemId = 0x6292F0(member, 1), resolves Item_LookupRecord, and tests 0x66C5A8 (u8[rec+0x29] <= 4, 1H weapon) || u8[rec+0x29] == 6 (claws). Callers Battle_BuildTargetSlots (sets hit count 2 vs 1) and Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessDefaultAction use it for dual-hand attacks.

name: Party_Member_HasOffhandWeapon
summary: Returns 1 when a party member's off-hand equipment slot (slot 1 via 0x006292F0) holds a one-handed weapon (ItemRecord->u8_29 <= 4 via 0x0066C5A8, i.e. true dual-wielding with a separate off-hand Attack stat), or 0 otherwise.
evidence: ARM disasm 0x629844..0x62988C + 0x6292F0 + 0x66C5A8 + 0x1905E4: takes PartyMember* (from 0x35EB98), resolves off-hand itemId = 0x6292F0(member, 1) via Item_LookupRecord, and returns 1 iff 0x66C5A8 (u8[rec+0x29] <= 4, 1H weapon) is non-zero. Callers Ui_CharaStatusWindow_FillPartyMember, Ui_EquipTextWindow_Refresh, Ui_Row_UpdateFull, and Ui_TextLayout_BuildRows gate the secondary off-hand ATK display on it.

name: maybe_ItemBag_CountValidSlots
summary: Counts the slots 0..0x59 (90) for which the first accessor 0x0066B534 returns 0 and the second 0x0066AF08 does not return 0xFF. The 90-slot bound matches the DQXI bag size, but the two accessors are mid-function labels inside other routines, so the owner object is not established.
evidence: No new evidence, and the caller set now argues against the bag reading: two of the three callers are Actor2D routines (Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle, maybe_Actor2D_ResetIfRegistered) and only Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats is item-side. Both accessors (0x0066B534, 0x0066AF08) are mid-function labels inside 0x0066B264 and 0x0066AE3C rather than function starts, so neither can be named.

name: maybe_ItemBag_CountItemsOfType
summary: Counts the slots 0..0x59 (90) whose type byte from 0x0066AF08 equals 9, i.e. one specific kind rather than an arbitrary type argument.
evidence: No new evidence: the only callee 0x0066AF08 is a mid-function label inside 0x0066AE3C, so the slot array and the meaning of the constant 9 are still unproven; the callers (Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats, maybe_Ui_PanelGroup_Push) do not settle it either.

name: maybe_HandleRecord_GetNameLength
summary: Returns the length of the wide name at rec+8 when the record's four leading id bytes are all set (none is 0xFF), and 0 otherwise. It is a validity-gated name-length getter, not an assert: nothing aborts.
evidence: 0x00100B74 is wcslen (Thumb loop counting u16 until 0, then bx lr - see asm/text/text_00100048.s), so the tail call returns a value instead of aborting; the four 0xFF comparisons are a 'record is initialised' test. The old 'Assert...Valid' name was wrong on both counts.

name: Battle_Unit_HasStatusEffect
summary: Checks whether battle unit work object has specified status condition active by querying status table via Game_GetDataManager; returns predicate u32.
evidence: Caller 0x00304FFC (maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetupSlotAnims); queries status condition through Game_GetDataManager (0x0011CB38) and evaluates condition bit; returns a value.

name: Actor_HasTimestampInRecentList
summary: Builds timestamp hash via 0x0011FFFC and searches the 32-entry recent stamp list at self+0x975c for a matching record; returns bool.
evidence: Linear search over 32 8-byte entries at self+0x975C comparing generated timestamp against recent entries; returns a value.

name: Ui_StatusWindow_CountActiveSlots
summary: Counts how many slots in the status-window slot range return active status via 0x0066AD5C.
evidence: Loops over slot indices calling 0x0066AD5C(self, index) and returns count of active slots; returns a value.

name: Battle_Targeting_FindNearestCandidate
summary: Searches battle target group for nearest valid target unit based on position distance calculations.
evidence: Evaluates candidates in unit target group, checking liveness and finding minimum distance; returns a value.

name: Item_CountStorableItems
summary: Unless both storage flags +0x2A71 and +0x2B0C are set, walks every item id 0..0xB3A and counts those whose ItemRecord flag +0x20 marks them storable; caps the result at 999 (0x3E7).
evidence: The body was re-read against FACTS.md item fields: the +0x20 flag test and the 0xB3B item walk are explicit, and the caller Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats is named, so the 'count storable item types' role is supported (the 999 cap is a display limit).

name: Item_CountOwnedTypesFromBitmask
summary: Counts the item ids 0..0xB3A whose bit is set in the per-item bitmask at work+0x4B30 (0x168 bytes), filtered by record flag +0x20.
evidence: Bit test (self+0x4B30)[i>>5] & 1<<(i&31) over the 0xB3B item rows, the same 2880-bit table the save clears with memset 0x168.

name: Party_GetMemberRecord
summary: Bounds-checked accessor for the 8-slot party-member table at self+0x944C (stride 0x60); returns null when the index is negative or past the count.
evidence: The count routine 0x62A110 is called by Ui_MemberTable_Init and Ui_PartyList_InsertMember, and the table range 0x944C..0x974C is exactly 8 * 0x60, which supports the member-slot reading; the Ghidra bounds expression itself is partly mangled.

name: maybe_Monster_SumRecordedCounts
summary: Walks all 0x413 (1043) ids, and for each id whose record has a non-zero field +0x22 adds the per-id counter at owner+0x3AE4+id*4; the total is clamped to 0x1869F (99,999) and returned.
evidence: No new evidence: the loop bound 0x413 and the record accessor 0x0063DCA4 are unchanged, and the two callers (Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats, Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands) still do not fit a monster walk. The old Battle_Unit_CalcActionRange reading is definitively wrong (no action id, no distance, no float), but what the counter means is still open.

name: Ui_Message_ResolveSpeakerName
summary: Validates speaker slot at self+0x92F4 and returns speaker name character width measured with wcslen (0x00100B74).
evidence: Inspects speaker header bytes at self+0x92F4 and calls 0x00100B74 (wcslen) on wide speaker name at self+0x92FC; returns a value; not an item.

name: Party_GetMemberCount
summary: Counts the used party-member slots by walking the id bytes at self+0x944C until the 0xFF terminator; returns 8 for an empty table. The decompiler cut the counting loop into a noreturn wcslen call, but the byte scan is visible.
evidence: NEW: five of the six callers are now named (Ui_PartyList_InsertMember, Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats, Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands, Party_GetMemberRecord, Party_HasFreeMemberSlot), all of which need the member count before indexing the party tables; the only helper is the mis-marked wcslen, which only truncates the decompiled loop.

name: Battle_Unit_CheckActionCost
summary: Checks if battle unit has sufficient MP or resources for action by querying cost from data manager and comparing to unit MP; returns predicate u32.
evidence: Queries action MP cost via Game_GetDataManager (0x0011CB38) and compares against current MP at unit+0x48; returns a value.

name: Party_GetFirstNameLength
summary: Returns UTF-16 character length of party/character name stored at self+0x8630 using wcslen (0x00100B74).
evidence: Callers 0x00466350 (maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_UpdateSelection), 0x002A69A0, 0x00308970, 0x00307624; tail-calls 0x00100B74 (wcslen) on name string at self+0x8630; returns a value; not an item.

name: Party_HasFreeMemberSlot
signature: bool Party_HasFreeMemberSlot(WorkData* self, u32 arg2, PartyLimit* limit)
summary: Checks whether the active party has room for additional members by comparing current count to limit object counters; returns bool.
evidence: Compares limit->f_bc0 against limit->f_bc1 and adds current party count from 0x0062A110; returns a value.

name: Party_GetFirstMemberNameLength
summary: Returns UTF-16 character length of the first row name in the table at self+0x5fe4 using wcslen (0x00100B74) when list has entries.
evidence: Caller 0x003087B8 (maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_ShowPage9); checks 0x0066B11C > 0 and tail-calls 0x00100B74 (wcslen) on row name at self+0x5fe4; returns a value; not an item.

name: maybe_NameEntry_IsValid
summary: Shared tail entered from 0x0062A480 with entry = self+0x8668: returns a value (1/0) - 1 when the 7-wchar name at entry+4 is non-empty and shorter than 7 characters, 0 otherwise. 0x0062A320 performs the same check for the entry at self+0x8630.
evidence: asm: 0x0062A480 `add r0,r0,#0x268; adds r0,r0,#0x8400` sets the flags that the `beq` at 0x0062A48C consumes, so this is a fall-through tail, not a standalone measurement; it then does `add r4,r0,#4; blx wcslen; cmp r0,#7; movhs r0,#0; ldrh r0,[r4]; cmp r0,#0; movne r0,#1`. It returns a value (1/0), so the void signature in the old doc is Ghidra's dropped return. Not a speaker-name measurement.

name: maybe_Monster_CountDistinctRecordedKinds
summary: Builds a 65-word bitmask over the record field +0x22 of every id present in owner+0x3AE4 (also setting the bits of the three related ids found through the table at 0x007273A4), popcounts it and returns that number clamped to 999.
evidence: No new evidence: the two callers (Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats, Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands) do not fit a monster walk, and the record accessor 0x0063DCA4 has no readable file, so neither the table identity nor the meaning of field +0x22 is proven. The popcount and the 999 clamp are certain from the body.

name: Party_GetSecondRowNameLength
summary: Template copy of first-member row label length query; checks count via 0x0066B11C and returns length via wcslen (0x00100B74).
evidence: Caller 0x00307380 (maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunList4); identical logic to 0x0062A3CC querying wcslen of self+0x5fe4; returns a value; not an item.

name: maybe_Ui_QueryTransitionBusyInState7
summary: Returns 1 when the object's state word at self+0x578 is 7 and the child screen's +0xC object reports its operation as still running, otherwise 0.
evidence: NEW: still no callers; the state-7 guard and the busy query are certain, the transition wording is not.

name: Ui_ConvertRecordToScreenPosition
summary: Converts a map point record coordinate (rec->f_c) into 2D screen coordinates (out[0], out[1]) via 0x0066747C.
evidence: Caller 0x004ACC00 (Ui_ScreenAnchor_UpdateFromTarget); delegates to 0x0066747C and stores XY screen floats into out.

name: Ui_Object_IsAlive
summary: Tests liveness of a UI object: returns 1 if self+4 is non-zero or if child part at self->f_44 reports active via vtable+0x30; returns predicate u32.
evidence: Checks self+4 and queries child part liveness via virtual slot +0x30 on self->f_44; returns a value.

name: Gfx_TrailMesh_GetSourcePosition
summary: Resolves a trail source handle to its current world position: looks the object up in the global handle table (0x7B80C0 / 0x1FFFFF mask) and copies the three floats at +0x9C..+0xA4, falling back to the global zero vector.
evidence: reads puVar3[0x27..0x29] (= +0x9C..+0xA4) of the object whose type id equals g_0062A904; fallback copies g_0062A908 (0x7E7000, the zero vector also used by 0x5D19B8 and 0x62A90C); all four callers are Gfx_TrailMesh_Build{Sorted,Uniform,Straight,Clamped}.

name: Gfx_TrailMesh_GetSourceDirection
summary: Same lookup as Gfx_TrailMesh_GetSourcePosition but returns the trail source's forward direction, computed from the stored quaternion at +0x8C..+0x98 (x,z swapped, doubled, y from the remaining component). Used to orient trail ribbons.
evidence: reads puVar3[0x23..0x26] (quaternion at +0x8C..+0x98) and builds (x*z + y*w, y*z - x*w, ...) scaled by 2.0 (g_0062A9EC = 0x40000000); same handle-table prologue as 0x62A860; callers Gfx_TrailMesh_BuildSorted/Straight/Clamped.

name: Object_IsHandleAlive
summary: Validates an object handle against the global handle table at 0x007B80C0 and returns true if handle slot is active.
evidence: Caller 0x004C5F48 (Actor_CheckVisibility); inspects handle generation/index in global handle table 0x007B80C0; returns a value.

name: Battle_Unit_UpdateEffectAnchors
summary: Recomputes the world anchor points a battle unit's state/action effects attach to, from the unit's grid position, facing and the field scene camera/map-rect helpers.
evidence: Three confident callers (Battle_SetupUnitFromMonsterData, BattleActor_ShowActionEffect, BattleActor_ShowFixedEffect) and all eight callees are 3D anchor math (Field_SceneNode_GetPosition, Math_QuatToForwardVector, Field_Scene_GetCameraMode, Field_GetMapScreenSize, Field_Actor_GetGridRow/Column/Direction). The old stat-refresh reading is no longer tenable.

name: Map_ResolveJumpLocationId
summary: Resolves the actual map/location ID for a respawn, vehicle embarkation, or script jump event.
evidence: Called by 11 callers including LoadRespawnJump (0x001500E8), SetEmbarkartionInfo (0x00158C28), and Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent (0x00251230). Queries jump table via 0x0063CC1C, checks story flags in Game_GetWork() at +0x27508/+0x27509/+0x27727.

name: maybe_Actor_FillDisplayParams
signature: void maybe_Actor_FillDisplayParams(void* self, void* out, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Fills the caller's display-params struct from the global display block: a header u16 from work+0x27C5C, tag byte 0xFF at out+0x40, then the fields work+0x27224..0x27254 into out+0xC..+0x3C and work+0x27C60 into out+8.
evidence: Both callers (ActorGetRegionBookID and maybe_Ui_MapWindow_RefreshEntry) consume the struct, and every source field comes from the work+0x27218 display block that 0x004A4ADC also counts; the layout is now readable but the struct's real use is still inferred.

name: Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition
summary: Positions a balloon/marker relative to its anchor actor: offsets by the sprite half-size plus an 8-pixel gap on the side selected by f_3c8 (left/right/top/bottom) and asks the actor to draw the balloon there.
evidence: Reads self->f_3c8 (side 0..3), f_29c/f_2a0 sizes via func_0011CD80, target position from func_006F1EEC+0x54, and calls func_0022CF3C Actor_TryPlayActionSeq0F(actor, {f_3ca, mode}).

name: Container_FindNodeByString
signature: void Container_FindNodeByString(u32 out, int list, u32 name, u32 arg4)
summary: Finds a list node whose 0x40-byte name at node+0x14 equals arg3 and returns a handle to node+0xC, or an invalid handle when not found.
evidence: Walks the intrusive list arg2->f_30..f_2c (next at node+4), 0x11CCA0(strlen)+0x123660(node+0x14,arg3,0x40) name compare, 0x563540(&handle,node+0xC) or invalid sentinel 0xfffff000 via g_0062b0e4.

name: Actor_IsHandleAlive
summary: Liveness test for actor: returns true if owner chain f_30->f_94 is intact, +4 is 0, and flag bit 0 of +8 is 0.
evidence: Callers 0x0062FF38 (Actor_IsHandleAliveB), 0x00643744, 0x0064DDF8, 0x00640EC4; tests owner link and actor status flags; returns a value.

name: Actor_IsInRestPose
summary: Checks if actor is fully idle: verifies sprite existence via 0x0062F680 and ensures animation/position accumulators match targets; returns predicate u32.
evidence: 18 named callers in script and window dispatchers (Ui_Window_AdvanceCmd*, etc.); tests sprite liveness and accumulator equality; returns a value.

name: Container_ValidateHandle
signature: u32 Container_ValidateHandle(u32* table, u32 index, int checkVirtual)
summary: Validates a tagged handle: for index < 0x83 it reads table[index*2+0x250], requires the 0xB-bit generation tag to match the global handle table at 0x007B80C0... (indexed by the low bits) and, when requested, the object's virtual +0x34 predicate; on failure it returns the 'stale' sentinel with the caller's tag patched in.
evidence: NEW: it is called by four confident handle users - Event_GetOrAddActorSlot, Field_FindObjectByMode, Field_GadgetList_FindOrAddByHandle and Ui_ResolveObjectHandle - all of which need the 'is this handle still valid' answer, so the name is confirmed. The exact tag arithmetic is decompiler-muddy, hence 0.55.

name: Actor_GetModelHandleById
signature: unsigned int Actor_GetModelHandleById(Actor* self, unsigned int modelId, int validate)
summary: Returns the model-instance handle for a model slot id (< 0x83) from the actor's 0x83-entry handle table, validating it through the handle table when requested.
evidence: Indexes self+0x251*2 words, checks the handle generation against 0x0062b4d4/0x0062b4d8 and optionally calls the object's virtual +0x34; returns 0xfffff800-style null handle on failure. Called from Actor_ApplyModelRecord and Field_Scene_FindObjectValueById.

name: Actor_SlotListHasFreeEntry
summary: Searches one of the four slot lists at actor+0x128+slot*4 for an entry whose vtable+0x34 reports idle; returns predicate u32.
evidence: Iterates linked slot list at actor+0x128+slot*4 calling virtual slot +0x34, returning 1 on first idle entry; returns a value.

name: Field_HasModelSet
summary: The model-set presence predicate: it returns exactly whether Field_GetActorModelSetIndex is not the 0xFF sentinel.
evidence: The whole body is `return func_001C7EA4() != 0xFF;`, and 0x001C7EA4 is already named Field_GetActorModelSetIndex with 0xFF as its no-model-set sentinel. The bool signature returns a real value, so the predicate is valid.

name: Actor_ModelHasSwingOffPart
summary: Returns true when the actor's model set contains the named part '_swingOff' with a non-null object.
evidence: Looks up the literal '_swingOff' (0x0062B614) with func_0011CCA0 (string hash) + func_00659668 (find in model part table) and tests the entry's object pointer; called from Actor_ApplyModelSetByName.

name: Actor_ModelHasCapePart
summary: Returns true when the actor's model set contains the named part '_cape' with a non-null object.
evidence: Same pattern as 0x0062B5A0 with the literal '_cape' (0x0062B694) and self->f_20; called from Actor_ApplyModelSetByName and FUN_00222858.

name: Actor_ModelHasFaceOffPart
summary: Returns true when the actor's model set contains the named part '_faceOff' with a non-null object.
evidence: Same lookup with the literal '_faceOff' (0x0062B710) against self->f_20->f_14 part table; called from Actor_ApplyModelSetByName and FUN_00224394.

name: Battle_SelectPoseGroup
summary: Chooses the animation pose group for a battle actor from its current state/ability: returns 0x1b, 0x1c, 0x28, 0x40, 0x46 or 0 when applicable.
evidence: Calls the actor's virtual +0xe8 (has-state) for ids 2,3,0x90,0x79,0x75,0x76,0x9d,0xf6,0xc2,0xda and func_00639954/func_0062BBF4; each branch maps to a pose id; called by battle unit display and Battle_ActionAnimObject_SetActor.

name: Battle_IsUnitModelVisible
signature: bool Battle_IsUnitModelVisible(void* work, void* obj, unsigned short modelId)
summary: Decides whether a unit's model is shown in the current battle presentation: the model record's +0x3E flag must be set, body id 400 always passes, and a short whitelist (0x13D, 0x13E, 0x13F, 0x28A, 0x358, 0x3A5, 0x3B9) passes only while the battle 3D-mode byte +0x4244 is set.
evidence: The named callers are Actor_NotifyComponentEvent, Actor_ResetComponents, Actor_SetComponentFlag and Model_SetupFromTypeId, i.e. actor component/model setup, and the two inputs are a model id (resolved through 0x0063E05C to a record whose +0x3E flag gates it) and the object's body id - so the predicate is about the model, not about a battle unit. Renamed from IsUnitVisibleInBattle, which said 'unit' twice and hid the model/body-id keying.

name: Actor_HasConfuseStatus
summary: Returns true when the actor has the 'confuse' status effect active.
evidence: Resolves self->f_110 through the class registry (mask 0x0062bc80/table 0x0062bc84) and calls func_00669E58(obj, 'confuse'); string literal 'confuse' at 0x0062BC8C. Called from Battle_SelectPoseGroup.

name: Item_Container_HasKeyItem
signature: u32 Item_Container_HasKeyItem(int * self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Checks whether the inventory container currently holds any key items (category 2).
evidence: Virtual method in 4 item container vtables (0x00759A20, 0x0076C6C8, 0x00774CCC, 0x00774E54). Scans 289 inventory item slots at self+0x49, checks category via 0x0063E05C(id)->f_44 == 2 (key items).

name: Monster_LookupRecord
signature: void Monster_LookupRecord(int unit, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up the monster metadata record from data manager for a given battle unit.
evidence: Called by 0x0020AF04, 0x00486DF0, 0x00497110, 0x004993B8. Queries monster record using 0x0063E5C8 from data manager 0x0011CB38 using unit sub-id unit->f_76c.

name: Monster_LookupByActorId

evidence: The table walk and the desc[2] mask test are literal and the callers are now named camera/object/text paths (Camera_ApplyWorkEntries, Camera_UpdateWorkEntry, Camera_IsCandidateVisible, Object_MarkReleased, Text_LayoutRecord), which confirms it is a shared handle-slot lookup and that callers use the return value. name: Ui_Message_SetArgsFromRecordB
summary: Sets message arguments 2/3/5 from a record and mirrors the record id into the global UI name widget: ids <2 fill all three slots, otherwise only slot 2.

name: Ui_ScreenTransition_IsBlockingDraw
summary: Returns 1 if self->f_DC is non-null and its vt[+0x0C]() returns 0, if any of the five overlay/fade layers (+0xE0, +0xE4, +0x110, +0xF8, +0x10C) has active byte +0x94 != 0, or if self->u32_114 != 0; returns 0 only when all are clear.
evidence: Ten named callers in the field renderer (Field2D_Scene_RenderAll, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects, Field2D_Sprite_UpdateState, Field2D_MapChip_WalkTrace, Battle_TextWindow_UpdateVisibility*) gate drawing on the result, and the disassembly 0x632FC4..0x633060 strictly returns 0/1.

name: Text_FormatNumberControlTag
