name: Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorA
signature: u32 Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorA(SoundSeqParam* self, u32 version, SoundTrackDesc* out)
summary: Decodes a sequence track descriptor: for format versions around g_006610A0/A4 it fetches the track record and fills up to four 0xd-byte slot descriptors (u16 ids, RGBA bytes, key table pointers) plus the track header fields, selecting legacy or extended fields by version. Used by the sequence player to build its voice table.
evidence: reads version thresholds g_006610A0 (0x02030100) and g_006610A4 (0x02030200), fills 4 slots of 0xd bytes at arg3+4, and calls the named SeqParam getters 0x0065FC28/0x0065FC34/0x0065FC50; magic 0x220E is the slot tag.

name: Sound_Seq_GetWaveRefBase
signature: bool Sound_Seq_GetWaveRefBase(SoundSeqData* seqData, unsigned int id, unsigned int* outWaveRef)
summary: Base implementation of wave reference query: extracts wave ID word, type-1 value via maybe_Sound_SeqField_GetValue_Off08, and byte flag from sequence record into out, returning true on success.
evidence: Confirmed by caller Sound_SeqParam_GetWaveRef (0x0065E340, conf 0.50) which queries this base method before merging extension vtable slot +0x2C. Confirmed at 0.55.

name: Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorB
signature: u32 Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorB(SoundSeqParam* self, u32 version, u8* out)
summary: Compact variant of the track descriptor reader: writes the enable byte, a 32-bit value at +4 and a 32-bit value at +8, using the same version threshold g_006611A4 and the same legacy/extended record selection.
evidence: same version constant pattern and the same 0x0065F678/0x0065FC50/0x0065FF20 helpers as 0x00660E20; writes 0xc bytes at arg3.

name: Sound_Seq_FindEventOffset
summary: Resolves a tagged sequence event (high byte 1, 2 or 3) to the byte offset of its payload: variant 2 looks up a sub-record, variant 3 a wave entry, and variant 1 scans the event table for a range containing the id. Returns 0 when not found.
evidence: switches on arg2>>24 (1/2/3); calls 0x0065FABC/0x0065FBBC/0x0065F5D4 and adds either +4 or +8 relative offset; magic 0x2205 tag; same table layout as the descriptor readers.

name: Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase
signature: unsigned int Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase(SoundSeqData* seqData, unsigned int id, unsigned int* outTrackKind)
summary: Base implementation of track kind query: verifies record kind equals 1 via func_0065FF20 and copies record value, size, byte and flag into out, returning 1 on success.
evidence: Confirmed by caller Sound_SeqParam_GetTrackKind (0x0065E3F4, conf 0.50) which queries this base method before merging extension parameters. Confirmed at 0.55.

name: Sound_ArchiveStream_GetTrackHeader
summary: Reads the eight u16 track-header fields for the stream into the caller's array (widened to u32), forcing the last field to 1 when the stream version is below the header version.
evidence: The only caller is now Sound_ArchiveStream_GetTrackInfo, and the 0x65FBA4 header read plus the 0x2030200 version gate are unchanged.

name: Sound_WaveInfo_CopyHeaderFixed
summary: Copies the fixed 0x4C-byte wave-info header to the caller and always reports success.
evidence: uVar1 = func_0065F324(*(self+4)); func_00116C10(out, uVar1, 0x4c); return 1. Caller 0x00553368 (Sound_Track_ExecuteCommand).

name: Sound_Seq_GetEntryPairByIndex
signature: u32 Sound_Seq_GetEntryPairByIndex(SoundParamOwner* self, u32* out, int index)
summary: Copies the first two words of entry `index` from the owner's 0x14-stride table (base at self+8) into out[0..1] and appends the value from 0x00661474 into out[2], returning 1.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the confident Sound_Track_ExecuteCommand, which needs the per-index parameter triple; the 0x14 stride, the two copied words and the third value from an entry point in the same reader are all visible.

name: maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_GetSubBlockPairAlt
signature: bool maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_GetSubBlockPairAlt(SoundParamOwner* owner, void* outBlock, void* outPointer, unsigned int index)
summary: Byte-identical twin of 0x0066092C: copies a 0x26-byte sub-block from the sound parameter object into outA and following pointer into outB; reached from MIDI event dispatch.
evidence: Called by Sound_Track_DispatchMidiEvent (0x005539F8), Sound_Voice_ApplyPendingParams, and Sound_SeqChannel_ApplyMixParams; identical to 0x0066092C; kept maybe at 0.45.

name: maybe_Sound_Stats_SumPending
summary: Sums the integer counter at node-0x14 over an intrusive list, under the sound driver's monitor lock, and returns the total. Callers use it both from the frame profiler and from the sequence-player active-note update, i.e. it counts queued sound work.
evidence: Caller Sound_Profile_RecordFrame (0x0054DAA4) and the lock helpers Os_LockMonitor/Os_UnlockMonitor are named, and maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes also calls it, supporting the queued-work count. The node geometry (-0x58 list node, counter at node-0x14) is still inferred and one caller (Ui_TextBlock_Update) does not fit, so 0.48.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_GetPlaybackInfo
summary: Copies the player's current playback state (byte +0x90 plus the three position/count words +0x8C/+0x94/+0x98) into the caller's record under the driver lock; returns 1 when playing, 0 otherwise.
evidence: NEW: the fields it copies are the same ones the now-named Sound_SeqPlayer_GetPosition reads (+0x74/+0x78) in the same locked block, so the 'read the playback state' role is confirmed; the caller-side types are still inferred.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_GetPosition
summary: Returns one of the player's two playback positions under the driver lock: -1 when the player is not open, 0 when it is open but not playing, otherwise f_78 (which != 0) or f_74.
evidence: NEW: same open/playing flags and lock as the confirmed GetPlaybackInfo sibling, and 0x0054FE18 uses the same two fields as start/duration - the 'position query' reading holds.

name: Sound_Voice_CreateFromSeqRecord
signature: SoundVoice* Sound_Voice_CreateFromSeqRecord(unsigned int owner, unsigned int accessor, SoundParamOwner* seq, unsigned int* args)
summary: Starts a sequence voice: resolves the note row through 0x0065EDE0, looks up the wave/sample header, parses its format with 0x0065EF6C, allocates the voice with 0x00555E38 (top 2 channels) and then sets pitch, volume, pan, priority and sample pointers through the 0x0054xxxx sound-track helpers before starting the note (0x005561BC).
evidence: Calls 0x0065EDE0 (voice descriptor), 0x0066097C, 0x0054944C, 0x0065EF6C (maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat, N_035), 0x00555E38 (Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote area), then writes voice->f_194/f_195/f_19c/f_198/f_17c/f_b0/f_174 and calls 0x00547134/0x005472D8/0x005472F8/0x00547370/0x005561BC. Only caller 0x00545B58 (sound sequence player).

name: Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand
signature: u32 Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand(u32 arg1, int channel, u32 value, u32 volume, u16 arg5)
summary: Executes one sequence command against a channel: a large switch over the command byte (0x80..0xCC and the 0xB0/0xC0 ranges) applies the operands to the channel's volume/pan/tune/envelope fields, calls the var-length reader for operands and the note start/stop helpers for the note commands.
evidence: NEW: the switch is readable enough to see the individual command handlers and the named helpers (Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg, Sound_SeqChannel_KillNotes, maybe_Sound_SeqChannel_StopNotes); several branches still end in halt_baddata, but the dispatch role is certain. The damaged decompilation is limited to the 0xF0-extension cases (halt_baddata); the main command switch, the operand reader and the note helpers decode cleanly.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand_Tail
summary: Continuation fragment inside Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand (0x00661974) resulting from Ghidra disassembling an ARM switch tail as Thumb.
evidence: Function 0x00661974 ends right at 0x00661BEA; disassembly shows 32-bit ARM switch branches misidentified as Thumb code resulting in halt_baddata() and unaff_ registers. Kept maybe_ at confidence 0.30 due to damaged mid-function split symbol.

name: Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk
signature: void Sound_Seq_NoteOnThunk(u32 arg1, SoundSeqChannel* channel, u32 note, u32 velocity, u32 duration, u32 reuse)
summary: Six-argument thunk that drops its first argument and forwards the rest straight to Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote; it exists so the sequencer can call the note starter through a uniform function-pointer signature.
evidence: The body is a single call to Sound_SeqChannel_StartNote, which is now a confident name (N_035), and the function has no direct caller - i.e. it really is a callback-table adapter, exactly as the name says.

name: Sound_Seq_StepVoiceTrack
signature: u32 Sound_Seq_StepVoiceTrack(int* cursor, SeqTrack* track, int mode)
summary: Steps one track of a sequence: reads the next opcode from the track's byte stream (with the 0xA2..0xA5 extended prefixes), decodes its operands with Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg and dispatches note/parameter commands to the player vtable, returning 1 at the 0xFF end-of-track marker.
evidence: NEW: the opcode prefixes, the byte-stream cursor update and the 0xFF terminator are all readable, and the operand helper is the confident Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg, so this is the sequence track stepper.

name: Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg
signature: u32 Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg(u32 arg1, u32* cursor, u32 b, u32 c, u32 kind)
summary: Reads a variable-width operand from a sequence byte stream: kind 1 = u8, 2 = big-endian u16, 3 = 7-bit varint chain (continuation bit 0x80), 4/5 = wider fixed forms. Returns the decoded value and advances the cursor.
evidence: explicit switch with case 3 doing `result = (b & 0x7F) | result << 7` while the 0x80 bit is set - the standard MIDI-style variable-length quantity; case 2 reads two bytes big-endian; g_00662ddc = 0x0000FFFF is the mask constant; called from both sequence interpreters 0x00661974 and 0x00662714.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByteHi_Off04
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByteHi_Off04(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Reads accessor type 4 from the field table at rec+4 and returns the high byte of the 16-bit value (0 when absent).
evidence: NEW: the sole caller is the confident Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor, and this is one of six accessors differing only in table offset (+4) and accessor type (4); the type number and the return shape are visible in the body.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetPointerByTag_Off04
signature: void* Sound_SeqField_GetPointerByTag_Off04(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Chases a relative pointer stored under accessor type 9 in the field table at rec+4: returns rec+offset+*(offset+4), or the shared default at 0x007B003C when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: caller Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor is now confident, and the relative-pointer arithmetic plus the shared default make the name a literal description of the body.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault3C
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault3C(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Byte getter (accessor type 0) on the field table at rec+4, defaulting to 0x3C when the field is absent.
evidence: NEW: the sole caller is the now-confident Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor; accessor type 0, the 0x3C default and the 0xFF mask are all visible in the body.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off04
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off04(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Boolean field (accessor type 4 on rec+4): returns 1 when the field exists and its low byte is non-zero, else 0.
evidence: NEW: caller Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor is now confident; the body's 'exists && (value & 0xFF) != 0' is a flag test, matching the name.

name: m210b
signature: u32 m210b(int arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off04

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault7F
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault7F(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Byte getter (accessor type 1) on the field table at rec+4, defaulting to 0x7F (the usual velocity/volume maximum) when the field is absent.

name: maybe_Anim_Timeline_Advance
summary: Advances an animation/interpolation timeline step; invokes type-indexed callback from table 0x007E8120 when current time reaches limit, returning scaled float in s0.
evidence: Body compares self->f_10 with limit self->f_8 and dispatches through callback table 0x007E8120; apparent sound callers are jump table branch targets; kept maybe_ at confidence 0.45 due to ambiguous external context.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetSlotIntValue
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x0C of the element interface stored at self+0x24 and returns its integer result converted to float. The decompiled body drops the float return; the call and the VectorSignedToFloat conversion are visible.
evidence: Caller Math_Vector_FixedToFloat (0x006F06CC, a UI tween command handler despite its name) calls this only when the tween target's f_2C flag is clear, i.e. it fetches the element's current value; the virtual slot and int->float conversion match. No caller uses it as a specific metric, and the float return was dropped, so the name stays generic.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetMetricA
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x14 of the element interface at self+0x24 and returns the resulting float metric in VFP register s0.
evidence: Pure virtual getter wrapper on interface +0x24 slot +0x14 returning float in s0; only caller Math_Matrix44_Multiply is an xref artifact; kept maybe at 0.40.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetScaledHeight
summary: Returns the element's vertical extent: calls virtual slot +0x10 of the interface at self+0x24 and multiplies the integer result by the holder's vertical scale at self+0x0C. The caller adds the value to the rect's y to form y1, so the result is a height, not an abstract metric.
evidence: NEW: the caller Math_Vector_FloatToFixed (0.80) does inFloat[1]=obj->f_14; h=GetMetricB(obj); inFloat[3]=h+obj->f_14, i.e. it uses the return value as the rect height. Disassembly 0x00663444: ldr r1,[r1,#0x10]; blx r1; vcvt.f32.s32; vldr s1,[r4,#0xc]; vmul.f32 - the slot result is scaled by self+0x0C, while the twin 0x006633EC scales slot +0x0C by self+0x08 (horizontal). The old 'MetricB' said nothing about which metric.

name: std_CopyBlock64
summary: Copies a fixed 64-byte block with the optimised memcpy (0x00116C10) and returns dst+0x40 so callers can chain writes into a packed structure.
evidence: func_00116C10(arg2, arg1, 0x40); return arg2 + 0x40. No callers in the readable corpus (invoked through a table).

name: Font_Atlas_GetGlyphPage
summary: Font atlas virtual slot 0: asks the concrete atlas (virtual +0x40) for the packed glyph record and extracts the page index from bits 16..23. Two atlas implementations share this vtable shape at 0x00781DF0 and 0x00781F54.
evidence: slot 0 of the two font-atlas vtables 0x00781DF0/0x00781F54 whose slots 1/2 are the glyph-cell search and quad builder; result = (value & 0xffffff) >> 16.

name: Font_Atlas_FindGlyphCell
summary: Font atlas virtual slot 1: resolves a character code to a glyph cell by walking the range list at self->f_c->f_10 (ranges of u16 pairs, 3 bytes per glyph). Returns the 3-byte cell record or the atlas default cell when the code is 0xffff.
evidence: slot 1 of vtables 0x00781DF0/0x00781F54; range list nodes {first,last,next} with 3-byte cells; default code 0xffff and default cell at atlas+8.

name: Font_Atlas_BuildGlyphQuad
signature: void Font_Atlas_BuildGlyphQuad(FontAtlas* self, GlyphQuad* out, u32 charCode)
summary: Font atlas virtual slot 2: maps a character code to a cell and fills the 0x14-byte quad descriptor (texture offset, page, glyph width/height, UV scale and pointer to the atlas), including the lookup through the range list. Used by the text renderer for each glyph.
evidence: slot 2 of vtables 0x00781DF0/0x00781F54; computes cell index with 0x0011CFAC, writes +0..+0x13 of out including atlas+0x10 pointer; the direct-code twin is 0x0066374C.

name: Font_Atlas_BuildGlyphQuadDirect
signature: void Font_Atlas_BuildGlyphQuadDirect(FontAtlas* self, GlyphQuad* out, u32 charCode)
summary: Same quad builder as 0x00663714 but without the range-list search: it treats the argument as an already resolved glyph index. Used where the caller has just searched the atlas.
evidence: identical output layout and atlas pointer store as 0x00663714 but skips 0x00663608 and the range walk; 0x00663714 itself falls back to this body after resolving the range.

name: Gfx_AtlasPage_GetSize
summary: Fills a {0, width, height} triple: when the cell source's virtual +0x50 reports layout kind 1, the width and height come from the global atlas page descriptor at 0x0073BAE4 (+0x18/+0x1C); otherwise the triple stays zero.
evidence: Callers are now Font_Atlas_LookupCell, Font_MapCharToGlyph, Font_GetGlyphAdvance, Text_BuildGlyphQuads and Bg2D_FindTexturePageByName, i.e. every consumer is texture-atlas/glyph layout, and the global page descriptor's +0x18/+0x1C are read as the page size. 'Ui_' was too narrow (Bg2D uses it too), so the prefix is corrected.

name: Font_Atlas_GetCellAt
signature: unsigned char Font_Atlas_GetCellAt(AtlasPageSet* set, AtlasPage* page, int layer, unsigned int x, unsigned int y)
summary: Samples one byte of an atlas page grid at pixel (x,y). It computes the cell address from the page's own scale/offset fields (u16 at +0x10..+0x16 divided by the record's +0x2C/+0x2E), bounds-checks it against the page rectangle (u16 at +8/+0xA and +0xC/+0xE) and returns the byte at that cell, or 0xFF when the coordinate is outside.
evidence: div-based index computation with func_0011CD80(u16 * coord, divisor) for both axes; entry = set->f_28 + (dy*f_48 + f_46 + dx)*0x14; cell = *(page->f_10 + (y-origin)*pitch + (x-origin) + index); default result 0xff. Callers 0x00664A80 and 0x0066503C (Font_Atlas_LookupCell, N_076) — i.e. the font/glyph page lookup path.

name: Font_GetGlyphCell
signature: int Font_GetGlyphCell(GlyphPageSet* pages, int page, GlyphLayout* layout, int subPage, int x, int y)
summary: Maps a pixel offset to the 6-byte glyph cell entry of a font atlas page: when the page is already linearised it uses the row stride table, otherwise it computes the sub-cell indices through func_0011CD80 and validates the cell rectangle.
evidence: Returns piVar3[2] + index*6 where piVar3 is a 5-word page record with row/column tables; callers Text_BuildGlyphQuads and Font_CalcGlyphScale-adjacent code; fields +0x10/+0x14 are per-subpage widths and +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20/+0x24 the cell grid.

name: Font_GetGlyphQuadUV
signature: void Font_GetGlyphQuadUV(GlyphPageSet* pages, int page, short* u, short* v, int glyphIndex)
summary: Fills the four U and V texture coordinates of one glyph, applying the eight rotation/flip cases encoded in the glyph entry's bits 9..11.
evidence: Eight-case switch on (entry & 0xFFF) >> 9 permuting the four corners; the glyph entry is found by accumulating per-glyph byte lengths from page+0x18, and the size comes from pages+8 +0x10/+0x14. Caller Text_BuildGlyphQuads.

name: Text_BuildCharTransform
signature: float* Text_BuildCharTransform(TextRenderer* self, u32 charIndex, GlyphEntry* glyph, u32 styleId, float* out, int second, float* uvOut)
summary: Builds the per-character 3x4 transform (and the optional 16-float UV quad) used to draw one glyph, applying the active rotation/scale/skew style and the glyph's 0x14-byte cell from the font table; returns the next free output pointer.
evidence: Its two callers are Text_BuildGlyphQuads and maybe_Text_BuildGlyphQuadsThumb, i.e. the glyph quad emitters, and the body's std_FastSinCos + 12/16-float writes match a per-glyph transform - the role is confirmed by the caller pair.

name: maybe_Text_BuildCharTransform_Tail
summary: Continuation fragment / mid-function tail of Text_BuildCharTransform (0x00663FB8); stores character transform quad registers.
evidence: Direct continuation of 0x00663FB8 (size 0x146 ends at 0x006640FE); Ghidra split ARM character transform stores into a fake Thumb entry with unaff_ registers; not an item function; kept maybe_ at confidence 0.30.

name: Model_Node_ComposeMatrix
signature: void Model_Node_ComposeMatrix(ModelNode* self, float* outMatrix, float* outProjection)
summary: Composes a node's 3x4 world matrix from its rotation data: mode 0 makes a look-at basis from the node's forward vector, mode 1 uses forward plus a reference up vector, mode 2 builds it from Euler angles with sin/cos; also emits the projection matrix when asked.
evidence: self+0x64 selects mode 0/1/2; mode 2 uses std_FastSinCos (0x0051B158) and the sine table g_00664714 with range constants g_0066470C/10; writes a 12-float matrix to arg2 and a second 16-float projection to arg3; constants g_006644C8..DC; callers Model_ComputeWeightedDirection/Transform and 0x005AA7A8.

name: Container_HashMap_FindByKey
signature: void* Container_HashMap_FindByKey(u32* key, u32 keyLen, u32 arg3, u32 seed)
summary: Looks an object up in the global hash map by a 0x40-byte key: hashes the first word, walks the bucket's intrusive list and compares the stored 16-word key with memcmp.
evidence: 0x6647CC reads the global map header (g_006648B0 bucket mask, g_006648B4 table, g_006648BC seed), masks (key>>0xc), walks the list at entry+0x7c and compares 0x40 bytes with 0x123660 (memcmp). 0x7135D4/0x7139AC are byte-identical variants over different registries. Callers maybe_Ui_EntryList_FindByIdList/FindByKeyList.

name: Font_GetGlyphClass
signature: unsigned char Font_GetGlyphClass(TextBlock* block, int x, int y)
summary: Translates a local pixel position inside a text block into the 5-bit glyph class of the character covering it, or 0xFF when the position is outside or ambiguous.
evidence: Resolves the character index via func_006638D8 and then the cell with Font_GetGlyphCell, requiring the class byte at cell+2 to be neither 0 nor 0x1F. Callers: Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup and a screen-sprite rect check.

name: Font_Atlas_GetGlyphCellByte
summary: Returns one byte of the current glyph-atlas page for a glyph code: initialises the 0x1348-byte global page table once, picks the active page (optionally indirected through +0xF84 when +0xFE4 is set), converts the code to a cell and samples the page grid with Font_Atlas_GetCellAt; 0xFF when the page or cell is missing.
evidence: NEW: the callee is now confident (Font_Atlas_GetCellAt, 0x006638E8, 0.50) and documents itself as the page-grid sampler used by '0x00664A80 and Font_Atlas_LookupCell' - i.e. this function is the glyph-code entry point of the font atlas path, which is exactly what the name says.

name: Font_Atlas_LookupCell
signature: unsigned Font_Atlas_LookupCell(FontAtlas* atlas, unsigned x, unsigned y, unsigned unusedD)
summary: Resolves the glyph/character cell value at pixel (x,y) of the current atlas page, returning 0xFF when the atlas has no page or the cell does not exist.
evidence: Picks the page via atlas->f_14 (or the per-index table at +0x34 when f_94 is set), calls func_006638D8 then func_006638E8(page, cell, 0, x, y). Used by ~15 map/font/UI callers, always as a 'what is at this pixel' query.

name: Font_GetGlyphAdvance
summary: Returns the horizontal advance of a glyph (falling back to 0x80) by looking the glyph up in the current atlas page.
evidence: Same page resolution as Font_Atlas_LookupCell, then func_00663FAC(page, glyph, index); 0x80 fallback; callers Font_CalcGlyphScale and Text_BuildGlyphQuads.

name: maybe_Font_Atlas_FindPageForGlyph
signature: void maybe_Font_Atlas_FindPageForGlyph(FontAtlasSet* self, u32 target, char* outPage, u8* outCell)
summary: Selects the page and cell whose stored byte is the nearest value at or below target (ties keep the current best), scanning every page's eleven values; with no pages it returns page 0 / cell 10 untouched.
evidence: No new evidence: the page resolver 0x006638D8 is still unnamed and the two callers (Anim_Clip_Build, Ui_List_FindRowIdAtPoint) do not fit a font atlas, so the glyph reading is an assumption. The body only maps a numeric value to a (page, cell) pair by nearest-value search, which is why the summary says value rather than glyph.

name: Font_MapCharToGlyph
signature: int Font_MapCharToGlyph(FontMap* self, int charCode, u32 style)
summary: Maps a character code to a glyph id through the atlas at self+4: applies the optional remap table at self+0x34 when flag +0x94 is set, then resolves the cell (0x006638D8) and the glyph (0x00663FAC). Returns 0x80 (the fallback glyph) on failure.
evidence: calls the named 0x006638D8 Font_Atlas_GetCellAt-style lookup and 0x00663FAC; remap table at self+0x34 indexed by charCode when self+0x94 is set; fallback constant 0x80; sits inside the Font_/Text_ cluster of N_076/N_097.

name: Math_Obb_ContainsPoint
signature: int Math_Obb_ContainsPoint(const float* obb, const float* point)
summary: Tests a world point against an oriented box: the box stores centre (+0x10), inverted-free quaternion (+0x00) and half extents (+0x1C), so the point is transformed into box space and compared against the extents.
evidence: Normalises the quaternion in arg1[0..3], rotates (point - centre) by its conjugate, then compares the three components with arg1[7..9]; callers Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInArea and the sensor-gadget overlap tests.

name: Math_TransformOffsetPoint
signature: void Math_TransformOffsetPoint(float* out, const float* record)
summary: Rotates the local offset stored at record+0x0C by the record's quaternion and adds it to the record's base position, producing a world point.
evidence: func_00665564(&tmp, record+3) performs the quaternion rotation, then tmp is added to record[0..2]; callers are the sphere-sweep/ray/segment candidate collectors, which need a world-space test point.

name: Math_BuildCombinedBounds
summary: Builds the combined bounding volume of an object by unioning, in order, a set of spheres (centre+radius), oriented boxes (converted with 0x00574484 and offset by their own extents) and axis-aligned boxes (0x00573B6C), then writes the min/max corners, the centre and a radius computed from the half-extent diagonal. When bit 1 of +0x60 is clear it simply forwards to the cached bounds at self+0x10.
evidence: func_00575E38 (Math_UnionAabb, N_093) chained over three arrays; func_00574484 for the oriented-box corners; func_00573B6C (Math_ComputeRotatedAabb, N_093) for the last group; g_00665E44/58 constants (empty bounds), g_00665E5C = 0.5f; SQRT of the half-extent squares written to out[3]. Only caller 0x0058765C.

name: Model_ComputeAttachmentAnchor
signature: void Model_ComputeAttachmentAnchor(ActorView* view, float* outPos, float* outDir)
summary: Computes the world anchor point and facing direction of a model attachment from the camera forward vector, the node matrix, the node offset and the two camera transition targets, clamping the height to the configured band.
evidence: Both callers are now named attachment code: maybe_Model_ComposeAttachmentMatrix (0x005913CC) stores outPos straight into xf+4, and maybe_Model_UpdateBlendedAttachmentMatrix (0x00591490) slerps xf+0x10 toward outDir; that confirms it is the attachment's anchor/direction rather than a camera API.

name: maybe_Field_IsUiMode9
summary: Returns 1 when the field work and the overlay manager both exist and the UI mode byte (overlay+0x281) is 9; otherwise 0.
evidence: NEW: the byte at overlay+0x281 is the UI mode used by 0x0062F7E4 (mode 1) and 0x006342F4 (mode 8/9 checks), so it is a UI mode, not a scene type. The vtable is a model/anim table (slot 3 maybe_Model_UpdateBlendedAttachmentMatrix, [4] Anim_UpdatePoseBlend), and the function ignores self entirely, so only the '9' in the old name was right.

name: Field_CheckCameraOcclusionGate
summary: Combines three gates into one answer: the player-state allow table, the work's two mode bytes and Camera_IsPlayerViewClear(owner); returns non-zero only when all three pass.
evidence: The AND of the state-table gate, the two work bytes (+0x44/+0x45) and the named Camera_IsPlayerViewClear is explicit, and the sibling 0x00654F90 uses the same gate before pushing the projection.

name: maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVectorD
signature: void maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVectorD(void* owner, const float* from, int unusedA, int unusedB)
summary: Duplicate of maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVector: interpolates the owner's +0x48 vector toward `from` with mode 0. Slot 13 of a 24-slot vtable.
evidence: NEW: byte-identical to 0x00651590 and again slot 13 of a 24-slot vtable, so it is the same interface method on another class. The target is the manager at work+8->+0x4C, not a camera.

name: Camera_IsPlayerViewClear
summary: Returns 1 when the player's position is clear for the camera: not inside an occluder, not blocked by the field collision, the camera projection accepts the point and the owner's virtual validator (or the object table) confirms it.
evidence: func_0063451C (player pos) then func_0062E4B8 (point-inside-collider), func_003B1528 (field blocked test), func_001D4828 (camera projection set) with white colour, then vtable+0x5C and func_006542CC. Callers: 0x00654F90 and 0x006660EC.

name: maybe_Node_ComputeAttachedTransform
signature: void maybe_Node_ComputeAttachedTransform(float* out, void* node, float* params)
summary: Computes the transform of an object attached to a scene node: copies the parameter point, rotates the node basis (Math_TransformOffsetPoint), probes along the result with Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine and writes the entry-relative position plus its base translation.
evidence: The copy/rotate/cast/store sequence is fully visible and the callees are named (Math_TransformOffsetPoint, Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine); its callers are Field_SpinAction_Update and maybe_Battle_UpdateSkullRunAnchor, both field-action paths. The owning class and the two node offset groups (f_284..f_29C) remain unproven, so it stays maybe_.

name: Text_Style_IsPlainRecord
signature: unsigned char Text_Style_IsPlainRecord(StyleOwner* self, unsigned int id, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Checks if the text style is plain (style byte == 1 when unlinked, or SkillRecord category byte +0xDC == 0).
evidence: Confirmed by confident caller Text_MessageWindow_ResolveLineStyle (0x004DEBBC, conf 0.50), which tests this predicate to validate line continuation.

name: Text_Style_MatchesId
summary: Style predicate: when the text owner has no record id it compares its stored style id directly; otherwise it maps the record's flag byte (1 -> id 2, 0 -> id 1) and tests the requested id.
evidence: Both callers are now named text windows (Text_Scroll_UpdateStateMachine, Text_TalkWindow_Update) and the data-manager lookup resolves the style record; the two mapping cases are exactly what the name claims.

name: Text_Style_IsSpecialKind
signature: unsigned int Text_Style_IsSpecialKind(StyleOwner* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Checks if the text style belongs to special kinds 8..11 or SkillRecord category +0xDC == 5.
evidence: Confirmed by confident caller Text_MessageWindow_ResolveLineStyle (0x004DEBBC, conf 0.50), which tests this predicate to validate special text styling.

name: Ui_SelectHighestVariantCode
summary: Queries UI object child via vtable+0x48 and tests variant codes 0x89..0x8F via vtable+0xE8, returning the first matching code or 0x88.
evidence: Named caller Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_ResetRows (0x0059B294) calls this function on the party window, writes the returned code into win->f_4C7, and filters unit lists by that exact vtable+0xE8 variant code.

name: Data_IsRecordOrderLess
signature: bool Data_IsRecordOrderLess(unsigned int ignored, unsigned int idA, unsigned int idB, unsigned int manager)
summary: Sort predicate over the data tables: looks both ids up with 0x0063DED4 and compares their sort byte at +0xB, returning true when A sorts before B.
evidence: Two func_0063DED4 lookups through func_0011CB38(.) and return iVar2->f_b < iVar3->f_b. Only caller 0x0071C610 (script binding table).

name: maybe_Data_ValidateGroupSlots
signature: unsigned int maybe_Data_ValidateGroupSlots(char* groups, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int* arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Validates a group table: for every group it checks that none of the declared slots still holds the 0xFF 'unset' sentinel, returning 0 as soon as an unset slot is found (used to decide whether a recipe/party group is complete).
evidence: No new context: the only named callee is Game_GetDataManager and there are no callers, so the 'group slots' reading still rests on the 0xFF sentinel test and the loop shape. Stays maybe_.

name: Data_IsLastGroupIndex
signature: unsigned int Data_IsLastGroupIndex(char* group, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Returns 1 when the slot index stored at group+9 is the last slot of the table referenced by the id at group+8 (both must be set, i.e. not 0xFF).
evidence: cVar1 = *(arg1+8); if != -1 and *(arg1+9) != -1 -> func_0063F108(manager, id)->f_10 - 1 == *(u8*)(arg1+9). Only caller 0x00261DC4.

name: Data_FindIdByName
signature: int Data_FindIdByName(DataOwner* self, const char* name)
summary: Hashes the name (multiply/xor rolling hash) and scans the owner's name table (8-byte entries: hash + u16 id) for a matching hash and equal string, returning the stored 16-bit id or -1.
evidence: Rolling hash with g_00666B68/g_00666B6C multipliers, then loop i<f_12 comparing *(u32*)(f_60+0x34+i*8) and func_0010540C(entry+1, name) == 0 (strcmp); returns *(short*)(f_60+0x34+i*8+4). Only caller 0x00267D18.

name: Anim_IsInstanceBusy
summary: Returns 1 while an animation instance still has work: true when the playhead has not reached the end time, or when any type-1 node still has active sub-animations/tracks.
evidence: Early return 1 when self+0x54 < self+0x5C (current < end time); then scans the 0x60-stride node array at self+0x14 for node type 1 (node->f_34+8 == 1) and checks its sub-animation list via 0x00659318 and 0x0051D068 for any remaining duration; caller maybe_Anim_UpdateAndCheckFinished (0x005B09C8).

name: maybe_Work_GetIdValueIfAtLeast
signature: u8 maybe_Work_GetIdValueIfAtLeast(u32 arg1, u8* query, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Conditional getter over the per-id 0x14-byte records at (work+0x24A98)+0x2D2D: query[0] is the id (0xFF means none), query[1] the minimum and query[2] the value; returns query[2] when record[id].byte0 >= query[1], else 0.
evidence: 0x0066B17C disassembly reads the byte at bag + id*0x14 + 0x2D2D (0xFF for id 0xFF), and the body then compares query[1] and returns query[2]. The 'Party' prefix was unsupported - this is a generic per-id record table.

name: MonsterBook_CompareSortIndex
signature: bool MonsterBook_CompareSortIndex(u32 arg1, u32 lhsId, u32 rhsId, u32 arg4)
summary: Ordering predicate for monster-id sorts: resolves both ids through the monster/data table (0x0063E3C8) and returns lhs->+0x11 < rhs->+0x11 (the record's sort index).
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the confident std_introsort_monsterId8, whose comparator must be this function, and the two lookups plus the byte compare at +0x11 are visible. The 'MonsterBook' label follows from the sorted id type.

name: Skill_CompareSortPriority
signature: int Skill_CompareSortPriority(void* unusedA, void* unusedB, int skillB)
summary: Comparator for skill IDs: resolves SkillRecord for two skills via 0x0018C1B8 and returns 1 if skill A's sort priority key (+0xC2) is less than skill B's.
evidence: Caller 0x0071F514 and body resolve IDs through 0x0018C1B8, which FACTS.md confirms is the SkillRecord lookup wrapper (0x0063D018), not an item or text glyph lookup; compares SkillRecord->u16_c2 for skill sort.

name: Data_IsRecordSortBefore
signature: unsigned int Data_IsRecordSortBefore(unsigned int ignored, unsigned int idA, unsigned int idB, unsigned int manager)
summary: Sort predicate over the data tables: compares the sort key at +0x26 of both records (ties broken by id order), returning 1 when A should be listed before B.
evidence: func_0063E998(manager, idA) and (manager, idB); if A null -> 0; if B non-null then compare f_26 and fall back to idA > idB. Callers 0x0071D06C / 0x007231A0 (script binding tables).

name: maybe_Field2D_Layer_GetField12
summary: Returns byte +0x12 of the layer record at layer->f_04->f_298; the value is compared for equality across the 0x38-byte Field2D layer entries (collision, map build, layer update) and passed to the map-chip code in ResetWalkTrigger.
evidence: Disassembly ldr r0,[r0,#4]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x298]; ldrb r0,[r0,#0x12] is certain, and the four callers are now named Field2D layer/collision functions. Whether the byte is a layer id, a floor index or a tag is still ambiguous (the comparisons do not expose its origin), so the neutral field name is kept.

name: Field2D_Layer_GetKindGroup
summary: Maps the Field2D layer record's type byte (+0x13) to a coarse group: 1 for types 0/1/5, 2 for type 2, 3 for types 3/4/7, 0 otherwise; used by Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers.
evidence: The switch is fully visible and its only caller is the named Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers, which classifies layers for update; the function literally converts a layer kind into a group, so the name is exactly what the body does even though the group meanings are not labelled.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_PushTrailSample
signature: void maybe_Field_Object2D_PushTrailSample(FieldObject2D* self, FieldUnit* unit, TrailHistory** history)
summary: Shifts a 3-entry position/state history down and pushes a new sample from unit->f_4C8 for 2D field object movement trails.
evidence: Reads unit->f_4C8 position pair and state class, shifts three 12-byte history entries, and stores new record; lacks direct named callers, so kept maybe_ at confidence 0.40.

name: Field2D_DecodeChipWallType
signature: void Field2D_DecodeChipWallType(ChipDirection* out, const unsigned* map, const int* cell)
summary: Translates the map chip value (0xB..0x11) at the given cell into a direction/wall descriptor: out[0..1] are cleared and out[2] holds 0..6 for the wall kinds, or 0 for no direction.
evidence: switch on func_0066503C(*map, cell[0]<<3, cell[1]<<3) with cases 0xB..0x11 producing ids 0..6; called by 13 Field2D chip/solid/walk-direction helpers.

name: Data_PureVirtualStub
summary: Unimplemented virtual slot: it builds the trap frame and calls the runtime's fatal handler (0x00100050, marked 'does not return' by Ghidra). Present in the vtable so a missing override fails loudly instead of jumping to garbage.
evidence: Body is only func_00100050(local_68, g_00667660, 8) annotated '/* WARNING: Subroutine does not return */'; the same 68-byte stack frame pattern returns g_00667660 (a message/code pair). Only caller 0x005C3B10.

name: maybe_Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute(u32 ignored, u32 id, u32 arg3, u32 manager)
summary: Resolves the 2D scene object with the given id through the shared scene-sprite context and applies attribute constant 0xC41 to its model part at +0x3C.
evidence: The id lookup (func_002E5A34), Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext and the model-part attribute call with literal 0xC41 are clear, and the named callers Field2D_Actor_StepMoveTargets / Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects fix the 2D object subsystem. What attribute 0xC41 means is unknown, so the maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_Scene_FindFirstEntryInRect
signature: int Gfx_Scene_FindFirstEntryInRect(void* arg1, const int* pos, const unsigned* size, int listBase, int listCount)
summary: Runs a rectangle query over the scene's 0x24-byte entry table and returns the address of the first matching entry (or the end of the list).
evidence: func_002E6CB8 (Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesInRect) with a rect built from arg2/arg3 and func_0031A47C(size[0]), then returns listBase + index*4; callers are the field2D sprite path helpers.

name: Field2D_SpriteBlock_UpdateChipRange
summary: Recomputes the map-chip span covered by a 2D sprite block: sets the block scale, starts the path movement of every 0xE8-stride line entry, converts the left and right edge (centre -2 / +2) into chip ids through Field2D_MapChip_PackLayerChipIds and reports the pair to the block's interface (vtable +0x24).
evidence: Nine named callers are all Field2D_* (Field2D_Step_WaitDistance, Field2D_Step_GetPosition, Field2D_Sprite_UpdateScreenBounds, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects, Field2D_Sprite_StepMove, Field2D_Sprite_CheckGimmickTrigger, Field2D_Scene_AllocLayerList) and every callee is Field2D map/sprite code, so the Field2D reading is settled; the 'TextWindow' parameter type in the old signature was a misnomer.

name: Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffset
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffset(Field2DPosition* out, Field2DObject* obj, u32 offset)
summary: Maps an offset along a 2D map object's walk path to a world position: adds the per-offset pixel delta to the object origin, starts the chip walk, traces one ray step and transforms the result; writes chip id, step result and x/y to out, or zeroes it when the trace fails.
evidence: Its callers are the now-named Field2D_MapChip_QueryCollisionAt and Field2D_MapChip_FindReachablePath, and every callee is a named Field2D helper (BeginChipWalk, TraceRayStep, Actor_TransformPosition, PackLayerChipIds); the fill/zero branches are fully visible.

name: Field2D_MapChip_MapPointToCell
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_MapPointToCell(Cell* out, Field2DActor* self, unsigned int point)
summary: Maps a scene point to a 2D map cell: clamps it with Field2D_MapChip_GetColumnInfo against the actor's +0x78/+0x7C position and, when the point moved, transforms it through Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition; returns the cell or zero when the transform fails.
evidence: Callers now include Field2D_Actor_StepMoveTargets, Field2D_MapChip_CheckPathConnectivity, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects and maybe_Field2D_Sprite_FindPath, and both callees (Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition, Field2D_MapChip_GetColumnInfo) are named. The out-cell is written in both branches, matching a map-point-to-cell mapping.

name: maybe_Field2D_Object_NeedsUpdate
summary: Returns 0 only when self->f_88->vt[+0x08](self->f_88, (char*)self + 8) returns 0 and self->f_08->f_B8 passes both idle checks 0x00669B68 (s8_F8 != 0) and 0x00669B7C (u32_138 == 0); otherwise returns 1.
evidence: The ARM body and the two idle-check callees are decoded and the seven named Field2D_Scene_* callers use it as an active/needs-processing gate on scene->f_4C8 / entry->f_E0, but the exact Field2D container class at +0x4C8 is not yet named.

name: Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffsetAlt
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_ResolvePositionAtOffsetAlt(Field2DPosition* out, Field2DObject* obj, u32 offset)
summary: Maps a chip offset to a world position: takes the object's cell position, checks the neighbouring chip, adds the per-offset pixel delta from 0x005C0A30 and transforms the point through Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition; fills x/y or zeroes the output when the neighbour check fails.
evidence: Both callers are now named Field2D map-chip routines (Field2D_MapChip_QueryCollisionAt, Field2D_MapChip_FindReachablePath) and all three callees are Field2D (Field2D_Sprite_CheckNeighbour, Field2D_Actor_TransformPosition, Field2D_MapChip_PackLayerChipIds), so the subsystem is certain; the body reads the cell position, adds the offset delta and transforms it, writing x/y or zeroing the output.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectA
summary: Computes 2D field object screen-space bounding rectangle using position at (object+8)->+0x78/+0x7C and constant 2x2 extent transformed via func_0031A658.
evidence: Called during 2D collision and movement tasks (maybe_Field2D_MapChip_QueryCollision 0x005BEF04); variant A of screen rect family using object+8 position and 2x2 size; kept maybe_ at confidence 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectB
summary: Computes 2D field object screen bounding rectangle using position at (object+4)->+0x78/+0x7C and constant 2x2 extent transformed via func_0031A658.
evidence: Variant B of the Field_Object2D screen rect calculation family reading coordinates from object+4 instead of object+8; kept maybe_ at confidence 0.45.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_GetStyleByte18
summary: Getter for the byte at +0x18 of the style/theme record reached through self+4 -> +0x298. The value is consumed by the 2D map scene builder and tile renderer.
evidence: Callers are now Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData and Field2D_Scene_RenderTileGrid, i.e. 2D map code, not text layout, so the old 'Text_Style' subsystem was wrong. The record chain and the +0x18 offset are certain, but what the byte encodes is not, so the offset-based name stays at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_IsPointInAreaRect
summary: Directional hit test: takes the area record at (*(self+8))+0x2D4, builds its rectangle from the extents at +0x2BC/+0x2C0 plus the record's four u16 fields (+0x10..+0x16), and tests whether the point at +0x78/+0x7C shifted by -2/+2 in `direction` lies inside it; on a hit it delegates to 0x005CED04 with the same direction.
evidence: NEW: the neighbours are now Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectB (0x00667D78) and Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep (0x00667EA4), so this is 2D field-object code, not a text window; the body is a plain rectangle containment test (rect from +0x2BC/+0x2C0 + record f_10..f_16, point +0x78/+0x7C +/-2). The old 'Text_Window_IsPointInScrollArea' named a subsystem and a scroll area that the code does not show.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep
signature: int maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep(Field2DSprite* sprite, const short* step, int arg3)
summary: Chooses the next path step for a field-2D sprite: tests the target box overlap against the sprite position plus the step vector, then picks a random +/- extent from the sprite's 0x2B4 record and clamps it into the bounds.
evidence: The overlap tests and Math_RandRangeInt(0,2) are visible and five callers use the boolean result to advance, but large parts of the body are unrecoverable (halt_baddata, SBORROW4, a bogus func_0xffda23fe).

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep_Tail
summary: Continuation tail of 0x00667EA4 (maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep); handles path-step branch stores.

name: Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_006B75B8
summary: Outlined cold path of a function-local C++ static: under compiler guard 0x007BE2D0 it zero-initialises the shared 8-byte default value at 0x007BE2D4 and releases the guard through the 0x00101A94 veneer. Same body as the rest of the Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_* family (e.g. 0x0068A520).
evidence: Disassembly is the standard ARM EABI guard helper: push {r4,lr}; ldr r0,=0x007BE2D0; blx 0x0010009C (__cxa_guard_acquire); cmp/beq return; ldr r0,=0x007BE2D4; mov r1,#0; stm r0,{r1,r2} (8 bytes zeroed); ldr r0,=0x007BE2D0; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x00101A94 (__cxa_guard_release). Byte-for-byte the shape of the 30-member Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_* family (0x00689770..0x0069268C), and 0x007BE2D4 is the shared default/zero pair that 81 readable functions use as the 'no value' sentinel. The old name was wrong twice: the guarded object is 0x007BE2D4, not the address the doc quoted (0x007A6874 / 0x007A6A80 / 0x007A6614 / 0x007A662C / 0x007A6620 / 0x007A6638 are literal-pool words belonging to the preceding function, never loaded by this body), and the helper is not Field-specific.

name: std_Scalbn
summary: Multiplies *value by 2^exponent in place with C99 overflow/underflow handling: results that overflow become +/-infinity and results that underflow are flushed to signed zero, both with errno=ERANGE (2); NaN/inf inputs are left untouched. This is the scaling step of the C library's hexadecimal float parser.
evidence: Sole caller 0x001015E0 (std_ParseHexFloat) calls it with the assembled mantissa double and the binary exponent; the body tests the 11 exponent bits against 0x7FF, calls the soft-float scaling core 0x00723F8C, compares the result with the infinity constants g_006B8218/g_006B8220, sets errno through std_SetErrno(2) and builds the overflow value from g_006B8228*g_006B8228 while preserving the sign bit.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_FlushTextureUnits
summary: Emits the pending texture-unit commands: for texture units 0..2 whose 'dirty' bit is set it enqueues the texture setup command (via Gfx_GpuState_SetupTextureUnit or the multi-unit variant) and then appends the two trailing state words to the command buffer.
evidence: Readable C: for i in 0..2, tests bit (i+10) in the dirty mask at arg1, and depending on the per-unit type byte calls func_006BE858(*tex, i) (single unit) or func_006BF800(base, i) (multi unit); afterwards, when something was emitted and (state->f_770 & 7) != 0, writes two (value, command) word pairs into the buffer at g_006B83BC (write pointer, limit g_006B83C0) with command words g_006B83C4 / g_006B83C8. Called only from Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC) for the texture dirty bit.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteScreenScale
signature: void maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteScreenScale(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 width, u32 height)
summary: Emits the screen-scale GPU state: converts the two float arguments and the reciprocal of the requested screen size to PICA 24-bit floats and appends them as (value, command) pairs for registers 0x0041..0x0044 plus a packed 0x0068 write, then caches (arg1, arg2, width, height) in the pipeline-state record at 0x007AF058+0x20..+0x2C and sets its valid byte at +0x30.
evidence: NEW: the same command-buffer idiom and the same pipeline-state global 0x007AF058 as the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC) and maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteMaterialColor (0x006BFE40), which also start with 'uVar = 0x000F0041' and read *0x007AF058 - so this is a Gfx_GpuState_* writer, not a command-list quad builder. The resolution table is ground truth: 0x36000000 for 1024 decodes as PICA float24 (value<<8) 2^-10 = 1/1024, 0x38111111 for 240 = 1/240, so the function derives normalised 1/width and 1/height scale factors from a screen size. The old name claimed a quad and fixed-point coordinates; there is neither. Kept maybe_ because the exact PICA register names for 0x0041..0x0044 and 0x0068 are not verifiable from this repo.

name: Gfx_Texture_DecodeEtc1
signature: u32 Gfx_Texture_DecodeEtc1(GfxTextureDecode* self, u8* src, u32 size)
summary: Decodes an ETC1-compressed texture into 16-bit RGB565 pixels: allocates/reuses the temporary and destination buffers, decodes each 8-byte block with the ETC1 block decoder and de-swizzles the 4x4 blocks into the destination with the requested stride.
evidence: Readable C: block count = func_0011CFAC(size, self[6]) (ceil), capacity from func_00518278(blocks-0x26, 2, 1), buffers grown through the allocator at g_006B8A50; per block it calls func_0011FFD8 (fill a 8-byte ETC1 block descriptor from the stream) and func_00518154 - which is a verified ETC1 block decoder (reads the 64-bit block, the differential bit, the per-subblock colour tables, and writes 16 RGB565 pixels). The inner loop then copies the decoded pixels into the destination with stride self[6], i.e. the swizzle walk.

signature: int Gfx_Movie_ConvertFrameRowsTo16bpp(void* ctx, u32 src, int height)
summary: Same staging-buffer growth as 0x006B8C38, then converts a decoded frame row by row: per row it calls 0x00146C88 on each 8-byte plane descriptor and 0x00146B10 (Gfx_DrawLine2D16) to blit 0x80-byte source strips into the 16bpp destination.
evidence: Growth step is byte-identical to 0x006B8C38, but the conversion loop uses func_00146B10(plane, src, 0x80, planeCount, dst + j*2) and func_00146C88(plane, src) with a 0x80-byte source stride; hook pair 0x007AE5C4.

name: Gfx_Movie_AllocStreamObjectC
signature: int Gfx_Movie_AllocStreamObjectC(void** out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int count)
summary: Allocates the largest codec context (0x3C bytes) plus two count*4 scratch arrays through the hook at 0x007AE5B4 and initialises them through 0x0014ECF8; rejects count <= 5 and unwinds every partial allocation. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: Hook pair 0x007AE5B4; 0x3C bytes then two count*4 buffers, then 0x0014ECF8(obj,arg2,arg3,count,0,1); counterpart 0x006B9584 is used by the movie-stream deleting destructor 0x00501508.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieQueue_Peek
summary: Copies the next queued movie-frame descriptor out of the ring under the global movie monitor 0x007CF360: surface id, two converted addresses, three timestamp words and the per-frame words indexed by the read index, and returns 1; returns 0 when the queue is empty. The read index (f_34) is not advanced, so it is a peek.
evidence: The body writes exactly the frame descriptor fields from f_28/f_2c indexed by f_34 and never updates f_34, confirming a read-only peek; the frame-ring shape matches the movie track code, but no named caller confirms the queue class.

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_GetCount
summary: Returns the number of decoded movie frames currently queued, copied out under the global movie lock.
evidence: lock g_006b94b8 = 0x007CF360, `*arg2 = queue->f_38`, unlock, return 1; f_38 is the same count field 0x006B9518/0x006B95E4 modify.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetGlobalPair
summary: Publishes two words into the global pair at 0x007AE5B4 and re-initialises the critical section at 0x007CF360 with flags 0x04000048.
evidence: CORRECTED subsystem: the caller is Gfx_InitVramBanks and the immediate neighbours are Gfx_ResetGlobalPair (0x6B9060), Gfx_Vram_SetAllocatorWithDefaults (0x6B90A8) and the Gfx_Movie_* block, so neither 'Sq_' nor 'Os_' was right; the pair's contents (probably VRAM allocator state) are still unidentified, hence 0.4.

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_Pop
summary: Consumes one decoded movie frame from the ring: advances the head index (wrapping at capacity) and decrements the queued count, under the global movie lock. Returns 0 when the queue is empty.
evidence: `f_34 = (f_34 + 1) % *(int*)(queue+8)` plus `f_38--` inside the g_006b9580 lock, with the empty test on f_38; the exact inverse of 0x006B95E4.

name: Gfx_Movie_FreeStreamObjectC
summary: Frees the 0x3C-byte codec context from 0x006B9254: shutdown call 0x00155608, then the two scratch arrays at +0x2C/+0x28, then the object, all through the hook at 0x007AE5B4.
evidence: Called from 0x00501508 (Gfx_MovieStream_DtorDeleteC); body calls 0x00155608 then frees object+0x2C, object+0x28 and object via *(hook+4).

name: Gfx_MovieQueue_Push
summary: Adds a freshly decoded surface to the movie frame ring: converts the surface with 0x00152EA8, records the paired value from 0x0015D4A0, advances the tail index (wrapping at capacity) and increments the count. Returns 0 when the ring is full.
evidence: capacity check `f_38 < *(u32*)(queue+8)`, 0x00152EA8(self, surface, 0) then 0x0015D4A0(self) stored at f_28[tail]/f_2C[tail], tail wrap and f_38++ under the g_006b9690 lock; inverse of 0x006B9518.

name: MoLive_Decoder_Create
signature: u32 MoLive_Decoder_Create(MoLiveDecoder** out, u32 value, u32 value2)
summary: Creates a MoLive streaming decoder: allocates the small wrapper and the 0x14A0-byte reader through the global sound allocator (g_006B988C), constructs the reader, installs the callback table at +0x14C0 and attaches the source interface; maps MoLive status codes to the sound driver's error codes.
evidence: Readable C: uses the allocator callbacks (*g_006B988C)(size) / (*g_006B988C)[1](ptr), stores the string-adjacent constant g_006B9890 in the wrapper's first word, allocates g_006B9894 bytes for the reader, calls func_005EEDBC (MoLive_Reader_Ctor), sets decoder+0x14C0 = g_006B9898, +0x14C4 = arg3, +0x14C8 = arg2, then func_005EE430 (MoLive_Reader_SetSource) with (decoder, decoder+0x14C0); on failure calls func_005EEF10 (Dtor) and frees. The big switch maps 0/1/2/3/0x40/0x41..0x49 to driver codes 0/3/0x10/0x11/1/4/5/0xc/0xe/0xf/6/9 - the same mapping as 0x006B9BF8.

name: MoLive_Decoder_SkipPackets
summary: Discards all packets currently queued on the decoder's stream: resolves the stream through func_00669A40 and calls MoLive_Stream_PopPacket once per queued packet.
evidence: Readable C: i = func_00669A40(*(self+4)); stream = i->f_10; f38 = stream->f_38 (pending count); 'for (n = 0; n < f38; n++) if (func_005EBD2C(stream) == 0) return 0x14;' and returns 0xe when the stream cannot be resolved. 0x00669A40 is the handle-to-object resolver shared with 0x006B99C4/0x006B9BC0.

name: Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame
signature: u32 Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame(MovieStream* stream, u32 arg2, u32* out)
summary: Queries the movie stream's current frame source: returns 0 with the ready surface pointer in *out, or 0xE (not ready) with *out cleared; a null stream returns 1.
evidence: The four callers are the named movie-decoder pipeline functions (FeedVideo, FeedAudio, CheckEndOfStream, ReadTextSamples) and the body's state byte test plus 0xE return are literal; the only unnamed part is the MoLive getter, which does not affect the ready-frame role.

name: MoLive_Decoder_GetPacket
signature: u32 MoLive_Decoder_GetPacket(MoLiveDecoder* self, u32 arg2, u32* out_buf, u32* out_size, u32* out_rate, u64* out_time)
summary: Fetches the next decoded packet from a MoLive stream: pops a queued packet, copies its PCM into the caller's buffer (MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm), and returns the buffer pointer, size, format byte and timestamp. Returns 0x14 when no packet is ready and 0xe when the stream is gone.
evidence: Readable C: resolves the stream via func_00669A40(*(self+4)), gets the packet descriptor with func_00669708(stream), and if its byte at +0x11 is 0 calls func_006693B0(stream, out_buf, out_size) to fill the buffer; then *arg5 = *(u8*)(desc+0x10) (format) and *arg6/*arg6[1] = desc[0],desc[1] (64-bit timestamp). Otherwise pops the packet with func_005EBD2C and returns 0x14 with all outputs cleared / -1. This is the 'give me PCM' entry point of the sound driver.

name: MoLive_Decoder_GetStreamInfo
signature: u32 MoLive_Decoder_GetStreamInfo(MoLiveDecoder* self, u32 arg2, u32* info)
summary: Looks up the MoLive stream record for the decoder's stream id (self+4) and unpacks its format fields into the caller's info array according to the record type: type 1/3 fills the full 16-bit field set (info[0]=0), type 2 fills four words (info[0]=1), type 4 fills two (info[0]=2). Returns 0 on success, 7 for an unknown record type and 0xE when the lookup fails.
evidence: NEW: the address sits inside the MoLive_Decoder_* block (0x006B9694 Create, 0x006B98C0 SkipPackets, 0x006B99C4 GetPacket, 0x006B9BC0 NextPacket, 0x006B9BF8 Update) and its record lookup 0x00669A40 is in the MoLive_Stream_* block (0x00669820 MoLive_StreamMap_Find, 0x006698AC MoLive_Stream_BindPacket, 0x006693B0 MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm). The old 'Gfx_Codec' prefix was wrong - there is no graphics code here. The type switch and the 0/7/0xE return codes are read straight from the body.

name: Gfx_Vram_SetAllocatorD
summary: Registers the fourth VRAM allocator callback pair (global 0x7AE5D4) during bank initialisation.
evidence: identical two-store body; target global 0x7AE5D4; sole caller Gfx_InitVramBanks.

name: MoLive_Decoder_NextPacket
summary: Advances the decoder's stream by one packet (MoLive_Stream_PopPacket); returns 0x14 when no packet is pending and 0xe when the stream cannot be resolved.
evidence: Readable C: resolves the stream via func_00669A40(*(self+4)), returns 0xe if absent, otherwise calls func_005EBD2C(stream) and returns 0x14 on 0. Same idiom as MoLive_Decoder_SkipPackets (0x006B98C0) but without the loop.

name: MoLive_Decoder_Update
summary: Pumps the decoder once (MoLive_Reader_Process) and translates the MoLive status code into the sound driver's error code (0/1/3/4/5/6/9/0xc/0xe/0xf/0x10/0x11).
evidence: Readable C: iVar1 = func_005EC700(*(self+4)) then a switch mapping 0x41..0x49 to driver codes; identical mapping table to MoLive_Decoder_Create (0x006B9694). No callers in the indexed graph - it is a driver callback reached through the sound system's function table.

name: Gfx_Vram_FreeEntry
summary: Releases an 8-byte VRAM bookkeeping entry through the registered free callback: first releases the wrapped block, then the two pointers, then the entry itself. Returns 0x12 when no allocator is installed and 1 for a NULL entry.
evidence: checks the callback word at 0x7AE5D4+4, calls 0x5EEF10 then freeFn(entry[1]), freeFn(entry[0]) and freeFn(entry), returning 0; returns 0x12 (18) when the allocator is not installed; callers 0x1B78F4 maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer and 0x501498.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_CaptureScreen
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_CaptureScreen(CmdList* cmd, u32 srcLeft, u32 srcTop, u32 srcRight, u32 srcBottom, u32 dest, u32 width, u32 height, u32 format, u32 screen, u32 flags, u32 bpp)
summary: Emits a display-transfer (framebuffer capture) command: 0x500/0x501/0x502 select top screen, bottom screen or both, 0x10/0x18/0x20 select the pixel size.
evidence: 0x6B9D3C is a thin wrapper over 0x6BE47C, which maps arg10 0x500/0x501/0x502 to 1/2/both-screen transfers and arg5 0x8051/0x8056/... to the source format, then writes a command descriptor into the 0x1c-byte ring at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c. Caller 0x563244 passes 400/0xf0 (screen sizes) and 0x500, i.e. a screen grab.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueTextureCopyRect
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueTextureCopyRect(GfxCmdQueue* self, u32 src, int x, int y, u32 dst, int width, int height, u32 flags)
summary: Queues a rectangle texture copy / blit command: writes a type-4 command entry holding the source and destination addresses, the flags and the four rectangle coordinates scaled down by 16, then notifies the queue owner if this queue is the active one.
evidence: Readable C: entry = self->f_18 + self->f_20*0x1C; *entry = 4 (command type 4); entry+0xC = arg8; entry+4 = arg2 (source); entry+8 = arg5 (destination); the four shorts at +0x10..+0x16 are (arg4>>4, arg3>>4, arg7>>4, arg6>>4) - 3DS GPU coordinates are in 1/16 pixel units; then func_001197FC / func_0011980C bracket the queue update and g_006B9E04's active-queue check sets f_11 and calls func_00116104. Callers: Gfx_CopyBufferData (0x005642C8), 0x00567194, 0x0056AFFC.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_CopyTexture
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_CopyTexture(CmdList* cmd, u32 src, u32 dest, u32 size, int bpp, u32 srcStride, u32 destStride, u32 height, int heightBpp)
summary: Emits a type-2 GPU copy descriptor (source address, destination address, size and stride, with the texture height encoded in the top bits for 16/24/32-bit formats).
evidence: 0x6B9E08 wraps 0x6BE724, which writes a descriptor at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c with *entry = 2, +4 = src, +8 = size, and packs (height & 0x7fffff) into the stride words, setting bits 0x800000/0x1000000 for 0x18/0x20-bpp. Called from Gfx_Texture_Upload (0x656080).

name: Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntry
signature: void Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntry(u32 queueId, u32 cmdType, u32 arg3)
summary: Writes a 0x1C-byte command packet into the global GPU command queue slot and dispatches command execution.
evidence: Indexes ring buffer at g_006b9ea8->f_9c using slot * 0x1C, writes payload, and calls Gfx_ExecuteCommandList (0x00116104).

name: Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntryDirect
signature: void Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntryDirect(void* self, u32 queueId, u32 cmdType, u32 arg4)
summary: Directly formats and marks active a 0x1C-byte queue entry within the specified command queue object before triggering execution.
evidence: Writes param to self->f_18 + slot * 0x1C + 0xC, sets active flag bit (field | 1), and calls Gfx_ExecuteCommandList (0x00116104).

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_Fill
summary: Emits a memory-fill GPU command (six parameter words incl. the 0x12345678 fill constant and its mask) and patches the previous descriptor when the command list grew across a boundary.
evidence: 0x6B9F2C and its twin 0x6BA234 write [1, 0x000F0111, 1, 0x000F0111, 0x12345678, mask] into the ring at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c, set the entry's type bits (|4 or |5 depending on cmd->f_3d) and bump cmd->f_20. 0x6B9F2C additionally repairs the previous entry through 0x1160AC when cmd->f_34 is set. Callers: maybe_Gfx_Overlay_BeginDraw/DrawContent and 0x563244. The GPU register id 0x000F0111 is not decoded here, so 'fill' is inferred from the constant-value/mask pair.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueMemoryWrite
summary: Queues a type-1 command that makes the GPU write a small fixed block of state words (the three-word header emitted inline plus the caller's tag), aligning the inline data area and updating the queue's write offsets.
evidence: Readable C: entry = self->f_18 + self->f_20*0x1C; *entry = 1 (type 1); the inline words at self+4 (write cursor) get the (value, command) pairs g_006BA1CC/g_006BA1D0/g_006BA1D4; entry+4 = address of the inline block; entry+8 = size (with the pending-tail fix-up using self->f_34/self->f_30); entry+0xC = tag|4 (or |5 when self->f_3D); then the same func_001197FC / active-queue notification as the other enqueue functions. Callers: 0x0021F970, Gfx_FlushCommandBuffer (0x0055E71C), 0x00567194, 0x0056AFFC.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_FillSimple
summary: Simplified variant of 0x6B9F2C without the previous-descriptor repair; emits the same six-word fill command and sets the entry type bit to 1 when cmd->f_3d is set.
evidence: 0x6BA234 is 0x6B9F2C minus the cmd->f_34 block; identical constants (g_006BA34C/g_006BA350 = 0x000F0111, g_006BA354 = 0x12345678) and identical ring update. Called from the overlay draw paths and from Gfx_Texture_Upload when the caller asks for a sync command.

name: Gfx_GpuState_MarkDirty
summary: Marks GPU state dirty: masks the requested change bits with the already-cached set (state[2]), ORs the matching shadow-register bits into state[0] and records the handled bits in state[1] (the dirty mask). Bit 0x40 also drops the two 0x84-byte cached blocks at state+0x10C and state+0x190.
evidence: NEW: it is the exact mirror of the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC) - same state object *0x007AF058, same 'flags & ~state[2]' mask, but it ORs the shadow bits into state[0] and ORs the bits into state[1], which Invalidate later clears as the dirty mask. It also sits between Gfx_GpuCmd_FillSimple (0x006BA234) and Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC), so the Gfx_GpuState_* family is confirmed and the old 'Gfx_State_ApplyChangeFlags' wording was too vague.

name: Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate
summary: Central GPU state invalidator: for each dirty bit it calls the matching state rebuilder (material, texture units, texture stage, matrix/palette), clears the cached register bits and masks the dirty bits out of the shadow state.
evidence: Readable C: locks with func_001106D8, masks the argument with the current dirty set (puVar1[2]), and dispatches per bit: 0x2000 -> func_006BFE40 (material colour block), 0x80 -> func_006B8260 (texture units), 0x100 -> func_0067254C (texture stage), 0x200 -> func_0011C5F4, g_006BA688 -> func_006740E8 (lighting), then clears the corresponding bits in *puVar1 (the shadow GPU register word) and puVar1[1] (dirty mask), and unlocks. Callers: 0x001D0218, 0x002EB658, 0x00408D38 - i.e. generic render code.

name: Script_Vm_CheckParams2
signature: u32 Script_Vm_CheckParams2(ScriptVm* vm, u32 typeMask, u32 argIdx, int defaultVal)
summary: Validates that at least two parameters exist on the Squirrel VM stack and verifies the argument against the required type mask.
evidence: Checks `vm->_top - vm->_stackbase < 2`, raises literal string 'not enough params in the stack' at 0x006BA7D0 via 0x005B3DA4, calls Script_CheckArgType (0x001572AC).

name: Script_Vm_CheckParams1
signature: u32 Script_Vm_CheckParams1(ScriptVm* vm, u32 typeMask, int argIdx, int defaultVal)
summary: Validates that at least one parameter exists on the Squirrel VM stack and validates the argument type or pushes null.
evidence: Checks `vm->_top - vm->_stackbase < 1`, raises 'not enough params in the stack' at 0x006BA90C via 0x005B3DA4, calls Script_CheckArgType (0x001572AC) and Sq_VmPushNull (0x005B5660).

name: Script_Array_Reverse
summary: Squirrel API: reads the array passed as argument and reverses it in place, releasing the saved element afterwards.
evidence: Reports "not enough params in the stack", calls func_001572AC to fetch the argument, swaps elements of the array at +0x18 (count +0x1C), then releases the local ObjectPtr; returns 0.

name: Script_Closure_BindEnv
summary: Squirrel API: takes a closure argument and an environment argument, validates both ("the target is not a closure", "invalid environment") and builds a new closure object sharing the function, literals and outer values.
evidence: String literals s_the_target_is_not_a_closure and s_invalid_environment; allocates a 0x40-byte closure with vtable g_006BAE18 or a 0x48-byte one with g_006BB0F0 depending on the environment tag (0x8004000 / 0xA000020 / 0xA008000), copies literal/outer tables and pushes the result.

name: Script_Vm_CallClosure
signature: u32 Script_Vm_CallClosure(ScriptVm* vm, u32 paramCount, int returnVal, int raiseError)
summary: Invokes a callable Squirrel closure or native function on the VM stack with the specified parameter count and return value handling.
evidence: Calls 0x005B5C78 to resolve closure, calls Sq_VmCall (0x005B516C) with stack offset, pops stack with Sq_VmPop (0x005B4C34), and pushes null on failure.

name: Script_Vm_IsInstance
summary: Tests whether the object at the specified stack index is a class instance, checking type tag 0x8000040.
evidence: Resolves stack slot via 0x005B5C78/0x005B5C6C, checks `*piVar1 == 0x8000040` (Squirrel OT_INSTANCE tag), raises error 0x006BD988 if invalid.

name: maybe_Script_Object_Destroy
summary: Destroys the script object at owner+0x8C: calls virtual slot +0x14 of its +0x50 sub-object, releases its tables through 0x00247D94 and removes it from the global object table (0x00147AEC is the remove tail of 0x00147AA4). What the 0x8C object is, is still open.
evidence: NEW: the neighbours are Script_Vm_IsInstance (0x006BB248) and Script_CreateNativeInstance (0x006BB360), so this is Squirrel VM code and the old 'Gfx_' prefix was wrong. Disassembly of 0x00147AEC (inside maybe_Container_DestroyObject) is 'g_objectDestroyTable->vt[0x10](manager, obj)', i.e. a remove-from-table call, not a free(ptr,0xB8) as the old summary read.

name: Script_CreateNativeInstance
summary: Squirrel API: creates a native instance wrapper for the VM's owner object and returns it to the script.
evidence: Calls func_00163254(self) (named maybe_Sound_BgmChannel_Create in N_032, but here it just validates the owner), allocates a 0x40-byte object with vtable g_006BB564, registers it on vm->f_8C+0x48 and pushes it with func_005B5660.

name: Script_Vm_CreateNativeInstance
signature: void Script_Vm_CreateNativeInstance(ScriptVm* vm, u32 classObj, u32 userPtr, u32 size, u32 hook)
summary: Instantiates a native class object bound to the Squirrel VM with associated C++ user data pointer and hook.
evidence: Calls Script_CreateNativeInstance (0x006BB360) passing user pointer and hook structure.

name: Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer
summary: Retrieves the native C++ user pointer from a Squirrel class instance object on the stack.
evidence: Calls Script_CheckArgType (0x001572AC) with instance type mask g_006bb648, retrieves instance payload at offset +0x24 via 0x005FA298.

name: Sq_VmGetStackSlot
summary: Fetches one stack slot by index and leaves it on the VM stack. A negative index counts from the top; when the index is out of range it raises the Squirrel error "the index doesn't exist" (0x006BD988) and returns the error value.
evidence: `if (index < 0) result = func_005B5C78(vm); else result = func_005B5C6C(vm, index - 1 + vm->f_34); uVar2 = func_005B5C78(vm, 0xffffffff); uVar3 = func_005B5C78(vm, 0xffffffff); if (func_005B49AC(vm, result, uVar3, uVar2, 0, 0) == 0) { func_005B4C34(vm, 1); result = func_006BD988(vm, s_the_index_doesn_t_exist_006bb70c); return result; } return 0;`. The literal string is the giveaway; 0x006BD988 is the script-error raiser.

name: Script_Table_GetSlot
summary: Squirrel API: reads a table slot by key, with a special case for the root table's +0x44 member; reports "wrong index" when the key is not a valid slot.
evidence: func_001572AC fetches the table, func_005B5C78 pops the key, func_005FA0C4 (Sq_VmReadObjectPtrSlot, N_073) resolves the slot, then func_005B5660 pushes it; string literal s_wrong_index.

name: Script_Vm_GetBool
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetBool(ScriptVm* vm, int stackIdx, int* outVal)
summary: Extracts a boolean value from the specified stack slot, verifying Squirrel type tag 0x1000008 (OT_BOOL).
evidence: Checks stack slot type tag `*piVar1 == 0x1000008` (OT_BOOL), writes boolean integer to outVal, returns 0 on success or 0xFFFFFFFF on type mismatch.

name: Script_Vm_GetInstance
summary: Validates and extracts a class instance object reference from the given VM stack position.
evidence: Calls Script_CheckArgType (0x001572AC) with instance type descriptor g_006bb97c, pushes null on error.

name: Script_Vm_GetInteger
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetInteger(ScriptVm* vm, int stackIdx, u32* outHigh, u32* outLow)
summary: Extracts a 32-bit or 64-bit integer value from the specified Squirrel VM stack slot.
evidence: Reads stack slot, extracts value words at slot+4 and slot+8, handles negative stack indices via vm->_stackbase.

name: Script_Vm_GetFloat
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetFloat(ScriptVm* vm, int stackIdx, u32* outFloat)
summary: Extracts a floating-point numeric value from the specified Squirrel VM stack slot, converting integer if needed.
evidence: Reads stack slot, tests float bit `(*puVar1 & 0x4000000)`, converts fixed/int to VFP float register, writes to outFloat.

name: Script_Vm_GetFloatDirect
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetFloatDirect(ScriptVm* vm, int stackIdx, float* outFloat)
summary: Extracts a single-precision float directly from the stack slot into a float destination pointer.
evidence: Resolves stack slot, checks float bit `(*puVar1 & 0x4000000)`, extracts float value to outFloat.

name: Script_Vm_ResolveStackIndex
signature: int Script_Vm_ResolveStackIndex(ScriptVm* vm, u32 stackIdx, int offset, u32 flag)
summary: Computes the absolute stack slot pointer from a positive or negative stack index relative to top or stack base.
evidence: Reads vm stack capacity and top, handles negative index calculation `(cap - stackIdx) - 1`, calls maybe_Container_FindBlockByOffset (0x002CC4DC).

name: Script_Vm_GetType
summary: Returns the Squirrel object type tag (OT_NULL, OT_INTEGER, OT_FLOAT, OT_STRING, OT_TABLE, OT_ARRAY, etc.) at the specified stack index.
evidence: Resolves stack slot using 0x005B5C78/0x005B5C6C, returns object type mask `*piVar1`. Matches standard `sq_gettype`.

name: Sq_VmReadStackSlot
signature: u32 Sq_VmReadStackSlot(SqVM* vm, int index, SqValue* out)
summary: Reads the Squirrel value stored at a stack/table index into *out (two words) without pushing anything. Negative indices count from the top of the stack.
evidence: `if (index < 0) puVar1 = func_005B5C78(vm); else puVar1 = func_005B5C6C(vm, index - 1 + vm->f_34); uVar2 = puVar1[1]; *out = *puVar1; out[1] = uVar2; return 0;`. 18 call sites, all script binding/VM helpers.

name: Script_Vm_GetString
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetString(ScriptVm* vm, u32 stackIdx, int* outString)
summary: Validates that the stack slot contains a string and returns a pointer to its character buffer.
evidence: Calls Script_CheckArgType (0x001572AC) with string type descriptor g_006bbd68, writes string pointer to outString.

name: maybe_Script_Vm_GetSlotValue
summary: Squirrel VM stack-slot accessor used by Script_Vm_GetInstance (0x006BB8DC): resolves the slot through 0x005B5C6C when the index is in range and falls back to 0x005B5C78 otherwise, then returns the slot's first word. The in-range test is not recoverable from the C.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Script_Vm_GetInstance and the address sits in the Script_Vm_Get* / Sq_Vm*StackSlot block (0x006BB664 Sq_VmGetStackSlot, 0x006BBCEC Sq_VmReadStackSlot, 0x006BBD28 Script_Vm_GetString, 0x006BBDAC Script_Vm_GetUserPointer), so the Squirrel-VM attribution is confirmed. The body is damaged - the branch condition shows as in_NG == in_OV because the ARM blt uses the caller's flags - so the exact bounds test and therefore the precise getter name stay unproven; maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Script_Vm_GetUserPointer
signature: u32 Script_Vm_GetUserPointer(ScriptVm* vm, u32 stackIdx, int* outPtr, u32* outSize)
summary: Validates and extracts a user pointer (OT_USERPOINTER) or user data reference from the specified stack slot.
