signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueBlit(GfxCmdQueue* self, u32 src, int src_w, int src_h, u32 src_fmt, u32 dst, int dst_w, int dst_h, u32 dst_fmt, int mode, int scale, int opt)
summary: Queues a type-3 blit/format-conversion command: validates the source and destination pixel formats (codes for RGBA8/RGB8/RGB565/RGBA4/RGBA5551), computes the source row stride and the size adjustment when scaling, and writes the rectangle and flags into a command entry.
evidence: Readable C: maps arg10 (0x500/0x501/0x502) to a conversion mode, maps arg5 and arg9 through the pixel-format table (0x8051, 0x8056, 0x8058, 0x8D62, g_006BE71C) to (src,dst) format codes, then fills entry = self->f_18 + self->f_20*0x1C with *entry = 3 (type 3), +4 = src address, +8 = size (adjusted by the scaling formula), +0xC/+0xE = src w/h, +0x10 = src stride, +0x12 = dst height, +0x14 = packed format/mode bits (0x200 when arg12 == 0x20). Caller: 0x006B9D3C (Gfx_GpuCmd_CaptureScreen, N_021).

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueTextureCopy
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueTextureCopy(GfxCmdQueue* self, u32 src, u32 src_fmt, u32 dst, int dst_fmt, u32 src_stride, u32 dst_addr, u32 size, int copy_mode)
summary: Queues a type-2 texture copy command: writes the source and destination addresses plus the two 23-bit format fields, encoding the 0x10/0x18/0x20 selector as the corresponding flag bits in each word.
evidence: Readable C: entry = self->f_18 + self->f_20*0x1C; *entry = 2 (type 2); entry+4 = arg2; entry+8 = arg4; the low 23 bits of arg3 and arg7 are stored with the high bits preserved and 0x800000 / 0x1000000 set for the 0x18 / 0x20 selectors (arg5 and arg9); entry+0x10 = arg6; entry+0x14 = arg8. Caller: 0x006B9E08 (Gfx_GpuCmd_CopyTexture, N_021).

name: Gfx_GpuState_SetupTextureUnit
summary: Rebuilds one texture unit's cached GPU state: clears the unit's dirty bit, converts the unit's float coordinates/scale to fixed point and packs them into the shadow register words; returns 0 when the unit is up to date or not dirty.
evidence: Readable C: if the unit is already clean (or a forced flag is set) it just clears bit unit in the dirty mask at state+0x770 and returns; otherwise it converts tex[6..9] * g_006BEbCC with VectorFloatToUnsigned(...,3) and packs them (f_774 = x | y<<8 | w<<16 | h<<24, f_778, f_79C...). The 3-bit fractional fixed-point conversion and the shadow copies of the register words are the same idiom as the other Gfx_GpuState_* functions. Caller: Gfx_GpuCmd_FlushTextureUnits (0x006B8260).

name: Gfx_GpuState_SetupTextureUnits
summary: Multi-unit variant of the texture-unit state rebuild: checks whether units 1..5 still match unit 0 (same handle, size and format), and if a full rebuild is needed packs the unit's float coordinates and the shared address/format words into the shadow registers.
evidence: Readable C: loops i = 1..5 comparing arg1[i*0x11+0xD] (handle) and the size/format words against unit 0's, breaking on the first mismatch; returns the cached error/status constant when up to date or when the state is clean; otherwise converts arg1[6..9] with VectorFloatToUnsigned(...,3) and writes state->f_774/f_778/f_79C/f_107. Caller: Gfx_GpuCmd_FlushTextureUnits (0x006B8260).

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteMaterialColor
summary: Emits the material/colour GPU state: converts the current material's float colour and the light-scale values to the PICA 21-bit float format and appends them, together with the material, texture-env and light register writes (0x000F0040/41/43...), as (value, command) pairs to the command buffer at 0x007AED34.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0.60) and it dispatches here for the material/colour dirty bit, so the role as one per-dirty-bit state writer is confirmed; the individual PICA register numbers are still read from the 0x000F00xx command words rather than from a register-name table, so the precise 'material colour' label keeps maybe_.

name: Field_ObjectFactory_Type1362
signature: void* Field_ObjectFactory_Type1362(void* ctx, void* owner, u16 typeId, int is2D)
summary: Factory used by the object-spawn loop to instantiate an object of type id 1362. It allocates one of two class variants depending on the global 2D-mode byte (system+0x4244): the 3D variant (0x1388 bytes, vtable 0x760C08), or the 2D variant (0x138C bytes); runs the matching constructor and stores the owning map/scene pointer at object+0x122C. This is one of the specialised classes, not one of the three default factories. The id space (0..1374 for the type table, 0..51 for the kind table) and the 32-bit owner back-pointer at +0x122C fit map/actor placement data, but the exact dataset (map objects vs. party/monster actor records) is not proven.
evidence: entry #1362 of the 1375-entry type table at 0x7A4338; the spawn code at 0x169A4C/0x169B48 reads it as `ldr ip,[table, id, lsl#2]; blx ip` with r0 = allocator context (map+0xB4), r1 = owning map, r2 = type id, r3 = (global 2D-mode byte at +0x4244 == 1), then stores the id at object+0x1230 and links the object into the map list at +0x10C. Every factory in this block has the same two-branch shape (Mem_AllocAligned of a class size, constructor via the literal at +0x4, vtable store, owner store at +0x122C); this one allocates 0x1388 / 0x138C bytes. Earlier N_007 read this same block as "script native-class factories"; that is contradicted by the call site, which indexes the table with a runtime id read from a record and then links the new object into the caller's list at +0x10C, so a data-driven object factory is the better reading.

name: Math_SmoothDampUpdate
signature: void Math_SmoothDampUpdate(Math_SmoothDampState* state, const float* target, int mode, float dt)
summary: Frame update of the engine's damped-follow helper (camera/UI smoothing). state = {value +0x00, previous target +0x04, time-since-target-change +0x08, last dt +0x0C, curve kernel +0x10}. If dt <= 0 the value snaps to the target. Otherwise the value is advanced by the previously selected curve kernel (or the plain previous value / current value when the kernel is null or the target has been held long enough), then the new target, dt and a reset accumulator are recorded and a new kernel is selected from the 16-entry table at 0x006E7114 according to mode (0..15, default 15). The kernels themselves are the 0x006F4xxx easing routines.
evidence: Body: vldr s17,=0.0; vcmpe s16(dt),0 -> snap; else vldr s0,[r4,#8]; vldr s3,[r4,#0xc]; if (s3 <= s0) use [r4,#4]; else ldr r0,[r4,#0x10]; if r0==0 use [r4]; else vldmia r4,{s1,s2}; vsub s2,s2,s1; blx r0 (kernel(value, delta)). Then str [r5] -> [r4,#4]; vstr 0.0 -> [r4,#8]; vstr dt -> [r4,#0xc]; 'cmp r6,#0x10; ldrlo pc,[pc,r6,lsl#2]' jump table at 0x006E7114 selecting 0x006F465C, 0x006F4898, 0x006F4C60, 0x006F45E4, 0x006F482C, 0x006F4B84, 0x006F4718, 0x006F490C, 0x006F4D40, 0x006F476C, 0x006F497C, 0x006F4E4C, 0x006F47CC, 0x006F49E8, 0x006F4F70, default 0x006F46CC -> str [r4,#0x10]. One direct caller: FUN_0045560C.

name: Container_RingBuffer_Push
summary: Pushes one word into a producer/consumer ring: atomically bumps the producer counter, blocks while the ring is full, stores the value at the producer index, publishes the new count and wakes a waiting consumer semaphore.

name: Os_Handle_CloseField

name: Container_Value_SetFromRef

name: Container_Variant_ClearChildren
summary: Frees every node of a variant value's child list and resets the list to an empty ring, leaving the value itself alive; callers use it as the first half of a tree-node destructor and then return the node to the 16-byte-granule pool themselves.
evidence: asm/text/text_006C0048.s 0x006E7910: r6 = self+8 (child-list header), r4 = r6, r5 = [r4+4] (last child), loop { r5next = [r5+4]; free(pool = [r4+8], r5, 1) through 0x0051435C } then [r4+8] = 0, [r4] = [r4+4] = r4, return self. The node constructor 0x006E78EC (called from 0x006E796C) writes exactly this layout: data 0, type byte 1, empty ring at node+0x10, pool handle 0 at node+0x18. Callers 0x005120A4, 0x00512928, 0x00512E5C, 0x005131E4 unlink a node, call this, then free the node itself with 2 units - i.e. it is the 'free my children' step. Type tags 1/2/3/4 = null/u16/list-of-values/byte come from the value copy routine 0x006E7744. Note the asymmetry: children are allocated with 2 units by 0x006E796C but released with 1 unit here (verified in the instruction stream, cause not established - either a pool-quota quirk or a small leak in the original).

name: Container_Variant_AddChild
summary: Allocates a 32-byte variant node from the parent's granule pool, constructs it as an empty value (data 0, type 1, its own empty child ring), pushes it at the front of the parent's child list and returns it through outChild.
evidence: asm 0x006E796C: alloc([childList+8], 2) through 0x00514390 (the 16-byte-granule pool allocator) = 32-byte node; constructor 0x006E78EC is called on node+8 and writes data 0 / type byte 1 / empty ring at node+0x10 / pool handle 0 at node+0x18; then [node] = [childList], [node+4] = childList, [childList] = node, [node.next+4] = node, *outChild = node. The same six-instruction link sequence is inlined in 0x00511774, 0x00511B44, 0x005120A4, 0x00512928 and 0x00513FD4, which then fill node+8 with 0x006E7890 / 0x006E7744 - this is the shared 'new child node' helper of that variant tree.

name: Mem_SmallBlockAlloc
summary: Allocates a small block from the first size class large enough (5 classes, minimum 4 bytes): pops a free node from the class free list, or carves a new block out of the pool's heap when the class is empty.
evidence: Readable C: loops i = 0..4, class max = max(4, *(u32*)(self + i*0x10 + 0xC)); if size <= class max it takes the node at self+i*0x10+4 (the class free list head), unlinks it (*head = *node) and returns it; otherwise falls through to HeapAlloc(self + 0x54) and returns the heap block (or self+0x54 on failure). The 0x10-byte class descriptor {list, ?, ?, max_size} plus the free-list pop is the classic size-class allocator.

name: Mem_SmallBlockAllocChunk
summary: Carves one new block out of the pool's backing heap; the block size is the pool's configured chunk size at +4.
evidence: Readable C is a single call: heapAlloc = HeapAlloc(*(u32*)(arg1 + 4)) - i.e. it forwards to the heap allocator with the size stored at self+4, which is exactly the fallback path of Mem_SmallBlockAlloc (0x006F1CA8, 'HeapAlloc(self + 0x54)').

name: Math_EaseCurve_Mode00
signature: float Math_EaseCurve_Mode00(float from, float to, float dt, float duration)
summary: Easing kernel 0 of the damped-follow helper (selected by Math_SmoothDampUpdate for mode 0): computes t = dt/duration, evaluates the cosine-based ease via the libm routine 0x00672E44 and returns to - (to - from) * eased(t), i.e. a smooth start/stop interpolation between from and to.
evidence: Entry 0 of the 16-entry jump table at 0x006E7114 (the 'ldrlo pc,[pc,r6,lsl#2]' target list at 0x006E7154 loads 0x6F465C for r6=0). Body: vdiv.f32 s1,s0,s3 (t = dt/duration) ; vldr s0,=PI/2 ; vmul.f32 s0,s1,s0 ; bl 0x00672E44 (shared libm sin/cos routine, unresolved name) ; vmls.f32 s1,s16,s0 ; vadd.f32 s0,s1,s17 ; pop {r4,pc} with the result in s0. The float2 sibling right behind it (0x006F4694) applies the same factor to a 2-component vector, which confirms the argument convention.

name: maybe_Math_EaseCurve_Vec2Sine
signature: void maybe_Math_EaseCurve_Vec2Sine(float2* out, const float2* from, const float2* to, float t, float duration)
summary: Float2 sine easing function: interpolates between from and to vectors using sine easing kernel 0x00673BC8.
evidence: VFP registers in_s0/in_s2 indicate float arguments; calls libc math helper 0x00673BC8; body decompilation is partially damaged, keeping tentative below 0.50.

name: Math_EaseCurve_Mode01
signature: float Math_EaseCurve_Mode01(float from, float to, float dt, float duration)
summary: Easing kernel 1 of the damped-follow helper (mode 1): t = dt/duration, eased through the libm routine 0x00673BC8, and applied as to*f + from, a smooth (sine/cosine shaped) approach.
evidence: Entry 1 of the table at 0x006E7114 (literal at 0x006E715C = 0x6F4898). Body: vmul s0,s2,s0 ; bl 0x00673BC8 ; vldmia r5,{s1,s2} ; vmul+vmul ; vldmia r6,{s2,s3} ; vadd ; vstr [r4]/[r4,#4] - the float2-aware variant writes both components of the target vector.

name: maybe_Math_EaseCurve_Vec2BackOut
signature: void maybe_Math_EaseCurve_Vec2BackOut(float2* out, const float2* from, const float2* to, float t, float duration)
summary: Back-out easing kernel for a float2 vector: applies the overshoot curve through the libm routine 0x00672E44 before adding the start value.
evidence: It is a 2D vector back-out easing kernel calling the libm helper 0x00672E44, but its caller FUN_006E6F04 is unrecovered and no caller exists in the readable tree, so the curve family is inferred - maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Math_EaseCurve_Mode02
signature: float Math_EaseCurve_Mode02(float from, float to, float dt, float duration)
summary: Easing kernel 2 of the damped-follow helper (mode 2): normalises the time (dt * PI/2 / duration), calls the libm routine 0x00672E44 and blends from/to with the resulting factor - the slower 'ease in/out' variant.
evidence: Entry 2 of the table at 0x006E7114 (literal at 0x006E7164 = 0x6F4C60). Body: vldr s1,=PI/2 ; vmul s1,s0,s1 ; vdiv s0,s1,s3 ; bl 0x00672E44 ; vldr s2/s1 constants ; vmul s2,s17,s2 ; vsub s1,res,1 ; vmla s0 = from + (to*f)*(res-1).

name: Str_WStringInsert
signature: WString* Str_WStringInsert(WString* self, int pos, const WString* sub)
summary: Inserts one wide string into another at character position pos and returns self. The string object is the engine's UTF-16 string: +0x00 length, +0x04 inline buffer (up to 0x3F characters) that is used instead of a heap block while it fits. The function saves the tail after pos into a stack buffer, truncates the original at pos, appends sub and then re-appends the saved tail, growing through the heap when the inline buffer no longer fits. Used by the text/message system to splice words or markup into a line.
evidence: Body: bl 0x00100B74 (UTF-16 strlen) on self+4 and on sub; 'cmp r3,#0x3f'/0x40 capacity checks; bl 0x00100A74 and bl 0x00100A90 (UTF-16 copy/append helpers) on a 0x9C-byte stack scratch; 'strh r0,[..]' writes the 16-bit terminator; final 'mov r0,r4'. Wide characters are proven by the lsl #1 scaling and strh. One of the text helpers called from FUN_005F8624.

name: std_vsnprintf
signature: int std_vsnprintf(char* buf, u32 size, const char* fmt, u32* args)
summary: The library's integer-only printf formatter: expands %c %s %d %i %u %o %x %X %p %n and %% with the ' ', '+', '-', '0' flags, width (digits or '*'), precision and the h/hh/l/ll length modifiers, never writes more than size bytes, and returns the length the full string would have needed.
evidence: 9148-byte state machine at asm/text/text_00700048.s:0x00708BE4: flag bits 1/2/8/0x10 = space/plus/minus/zero, a digits loop for width and '*' from the argument list, '.' + '*' precision, length modifiers h (0x40) / hh (0x100) / l (0x20) / ll (0x80), '%n' stores the written count, '%s' honours precision, '%p' = 8 hex digits, octal/hex/unsigned and 64-bit decimal (0x00125E58 divide, g_00709750 reciprocal); no float conversions exist. On completion it writes the terminating NUL (or forces the last byte when size == 0) and returns buf-write-pointer minus buf, i.e. C99 vsnprintf semantics. Its only caller is the variadic thunk 0x0051BAA0 = snprintf(char*, u32, const char*, ...) (bl at 0x0051BAAC).

name: std_RbTree_AcquireNode
summary: Hands out a zeroed 0x24-byte red-black-tree node, growing the pool in 0x24-byte blocks (block size grows 1.5x plus 32 nodes) when the current block is exhausted.
evidence: Readable C: if the free list at +8 is non-empty it pops a node (+8 = node->next); otherwise when the block cursor +0x10 reached the block end +0x14 it computes the next block count as max(size + size/2 + size/8, size + 0x20), allocates a 0xC-byte block header and count*0x24 bytes through the allocator vtable at *pool ([0] alloc, [2] assert with g_0070C524 = 'TQs'), links the block and advances the cursors; finally clears node->f_c, *node, +4 and +8. The 0x24 stride, the colour byte at +0 and the parent/left/right words at +4/+8/+0xC match the tree used by std_RbTree_InsertNode (0x0070CDD4).

name: std_RbTree_EraseNodeRebalance
signature: void std_RbTree_EraseNodeRebalance(void* out, RbTree* tree, RbNode** iter)
summary: Erases the node the iterator points at from the red-black tree, restores the red-black invariants with the standard rotations, destroys the node's equal-key sub-list and returns the node to the tree's free list.
evidence: Readable C: computes the in-order successor of *arg3 (the classic 'if (node->right) leftmost(right) else climb while node == parent->right' block), performs the full RB delete fix-up (colour flips, left/right rotations with the 'set child to grandparent' idiom) on the header at tree+0x14, then 'pbVar11->f_c = *(u32*)(tree+8); func_0070F840(&pbVar11->f_14); *(tree+8) = pbVar11; tree->f_18--' - i.e. push onto the free list, release the sub-list, decrement size. Same node layout and free-list as std_RbTree_AcquireNode (0x0070C414). Called by MoLive_StreamTable_ReleaseUnused (0x005ECEC4).

name: std_RbTree_EraseRange
signature: void std_RbTree_EraseRange(void* out, RbTree* tree, RbNode** first, RbNode** last)
summary: Erases the half-open range [first,last) from the red-black tree: in the common 'whole tree' case it walks the node list directly freeing each node, otherwise it advances the iterator and erases node by node.
evidence: Readable C: if the range covers the whole tree (first == header->left && last == header && size != 0) it walks the chain from header->parent freeing each node (destroying the equal-key sub-list at +0x14 and pushing onto the free list at tree+8) and then resets the header to the empty state; else 'while (*arg3 != *arg4) { advance *arg3 to its successor; func_0070C528(&local, tree, &local_node); }'. name: Container_Node_ReleaseChain
summary: Recursively dismantles a chain of container nodes: for each node it first recurses into the node's first child (node+0xC), then either detaches the node from its parent list or destroys and unregisters the object the node owns (node+0x18 via its virtual destructor), and finally pushes the recycled node onto the pool free list at nodePool+8.
evidence: Body 0x0070CD3C..0x0070CDD0: recursive bl 0x0070CD34 on [node+0xC]; ldr f1c=[node+0x1C] / if f1c==&node+0x14 then (**[node+0x18])() + (*(*node+0x14+4))(node+0x14,node+0x18) else unlink; str node to [pool+8]. Else reallocates with capacity*2 and copies begin..pos, value, pos..end. The 0x10-byte element and the [begin,end,cap] triple are the standard libstdc++ vector layout.

name: std_Vector16_PushBack
signature: void std_Vector16_PushBack(void* vector, const void* element)
summary: Appends a 16-byte element (such as a 4-word vector, rectangle, or quaternion) to a std::vector container, reallocating internal buffer when capacity is reached.
evidence: Standard 3-pointer vector layout (begin, end, end_of_storage). Elements are copied in 4-word (16-byte) strides. Called by Ui_DiveWindow_ApplyInputEvent (0x005A6868).

name: Container_RefVector_PushBack
summary: Appends a default-initialised 0x18-byte element to a vector of pack-handle references (id 0xFF, null handle pair), doubling the capacity when full and moving the live elements through func_00563540/Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign; returns the new element.
evidence: The body is the textbook grow-and-move (stride 0x18, capacity x2, then copy each handle pair), and the callers now fit: maybe_Event_LoadScenarioPack pushes and immediately fills id/name/handle on the returned element, 12 call sites in all.

name: std_vector16_push_back_default
summary: push_back for a vector of 16-byte elements that initialises the new element with the packed defaults (flag word g_0070EEC0, byte 0xFF and two -64 values); used to append placeholder vertices/entries.
evidence: If end < capacity writes *end (u32 & 0xfffff800 | g_0070EEC0, u16 from g_0070EEC0>>16, byte 0xFF, 0xffffffc0, 0xffffffc0) and returns end-0x10; else calls func_0070EC50(vec, end, &tmp) to grow.

name: Text_Buffer_InsertChar
summary: Inserts a single byte into a text/byte buffer at the specified position, shifting subsequent bytes forward with std_memmove and updating buffer size pointers.
evidence: Called by text formatting command handlers Text_CommandHandler0 through Text_CommandHandler7 (0x00257D1C - 0x00257F6C) to insert command escape codes. Calls std_memmove (0x00111378).

name: std_String_AppendCharB
signature: void std_String_AppendCharB(std_String* str, const char* end)
summary: Out-of-line growth path of std::string::push_back: appends one character to the string (begin at +0, end at +4, capacity at +8), reallocating and copying the old range when the end pointer has reached the capacity.
evidence: The three-pointer begin/end/capacity layout is std::string, and the inlined caller maybe_Ui_Panel_BuildAttributeText appends a byte only when its local cursor equals the end pointer, i.e. precisely on capacity exhaustion. That is push_back, not the generic range append the old name claimed; the B suffix distinguishes it from the SSO fast path std_String_AppendChar at 0x21BC88.

name: std_vector_u16_insert
signature: void std_vector_u16_insert(u32* vec, u32 value, u32 pos)
summary: Inserts one u16 into a u16 vector at the given position by shifting the tail, asserting through func_00111378 when the position is out of range.
evidence: if (begin == end) func_00111378(0,*arg1,arg2-*arg1) (out-of-range/assert helper); copies puVar1[-1] and then calls func_00111378 with the shifted range; same vector layout as std_vector16_insert.

name: Text_Buffer_EraseChar
summary: Erases a single byte from a text/byte buffer at the specified position, shifting remaining bytes backward with std_memmove and adjusting buffer end pointer.
evidence: Inverse counterpart of Text_Buffer_InsertChar (0x0070F03C) using identical 3-pointer buffer structure and std_memmove.

name: maybe_std_String_AppendRange
signature: void maybe_std_String_AppendRange(std_String* str, const char* end)
summary: Out-of-line std::string growth/append path: given the string's begin/end/capacity triple it either overwrites in place or grows and copies the byte range. Used by Event_UpdateIdSet's sorted id vector and by Text_LayoutColumns.
evidence: NEW: both callers are now named - Event_UpdateIdSet (0x001E7660), which appends one byte to its sorted id vector, and Text_LayoutColumns (0x0039CD34) - so the 'append a byte range to a std::string' reading holds. The body is still damaged (std_memmove is mis-marked noreturn and the copy loop is lost), so it stays below 0.5.

name: std_RbTree_ListNodeUnlink
summary: Unlinks one node from the intrusive equal-key list embedded in a tree node and destroys the instance it holds (calls the instance's destructor and then hands it back to its owner's release function); clears the node.
evidence: Readable C: if node->next is null or points at the node itself it treats the node as the list head and, when node->instance != 0, calls (*(code*)**(u32**)node->instance)() (instance vtable slot 0 = destructor) and then (**(code**)(*(int*)*node + 4))(*node, node->instance) (owner vtable slot 1 = release); otherwise it unlinks from the doubly linked list (next->prev = prev; prev->next = next) and zeroes the links; finally node->instance = 0. Called by std_RbTree_EraseNodeRebalance (0x0070C528) and 0x0070D12E for every erased node, and by 0x0070CD34.

name: Ui_ResourceTree_BuildNode
signature: void Ui_ResourceTree_BuildNode(int treeCtx, int nodeType, u32 resId)
summary: Resolves resource descriptor entries and constructs node elements in a UI resource tree hierarchy based on node type, calling maybe_Ui_BuildResourceTree.
evidence: Called from battle UI update and actor initialization (0x003F8C48, 0x003FAC5C). Uses std_ConstructArray and calls maybe_Ui_BuildResourceTree (0x001BBF84).

name: maybe_Battle_SetEffectColorAndPosition
signature: void maybe_Battle_SetEffectColorAndPosition(u32 unusedA, u32 unusedB, u32 valueA, u32 valueB, int channel, u32 alpha, u32* pos, u32 layer)
summary: Sets a colour on the battle work object (work+8->+0x5C) through func_0020E0D0 - one channel chosen by `channel` takes `value`, the others 0xFF, plus alpha - then copies a 3-float position and a layer to func_0020F2F8 on the same object.
evidence: NEW: both callees are now resolved - func_0020E0D0 writes the colour at obj+0x5628 and func_0020F2F8 writes the position at obj+0x56A8 - so the body is a colour+position setter on the battle work, not a quad draw. The 9-argument sibling func_0070FA08 is used by 0x005A3FC8 for the same purpose.

name: Container_Node_DestroyAndReturn
summary: Releases one container node: detaches it from its parent list (or destroys and unregisters the refcounted object at node+0x18) and then tail-calls owner->f_24's virtual slot +4 to hand the node back to its pool/deleter.
evidence: asm 0x0070FB84: r4=node+0x14; if [node+0x1c] not in {0,&node+0x14} unlink else if [node+0x18] { (**[node+0x18])(); (*(*node+0x14+4))(node+0x14,[node+0x18]); } [node+0x18]=0; then ldr r0,[owner+0x24]; bx [*r0+4] with r1=node. Same node layout/release sequence as Container_Node_ReleaseChain (0x0070CD3C) and 0x0070CB90; the preceding 4-byte stub 0x0070FB74 tail-calls the same slot without an argument.

name: std_SlotVector_AppendRange
signature: u32 std_SlotVector_AppendRange(SlotVector* self, Slot** first, Slot** last)
summary: Appends the slot range [first,last) to a vector of 0x10-byte slots, growing/reallocating the buffer when needed and keeping the slots' intrusive prev/next links consistent; returns 1 on success.
evidence: Readable C: capacity = self[2], needed = self[3] + ((last-first)>>4); when it must grow it computes the new capacity with func_00617298, allocates through the allocator at *self ([0] alloc, [2] assert with g_0071016C = 'TQs', [1] free) and copies the existing slots from self[4]..capacity then 0..i (the 'start offset' wrap), destroying the moved-from slots with func_00710778; otherwise it copies into the free tail. Each element is 0x10 bytes and the copy fixes up the element's own prev/next links (puVar9[3] = src[3]; src[3]->next = dst; dst[2] = src; src[3] = dst). Callers: MoLive_StreamTable_FlushSegments (0x005ECD8C), MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket (0x005ED154).

name: std_SlotVector_Reallocate
signature: u32 std_SlotVector_Reallocate(SlotVector* self, u32 min_capacity, u32 capacity, u32 shift)
summary: Reallocates the slot vector's buffer to 'capacity' slots (falling back to 'min_capacity' if that allocation fails) and rotates the contents so the logical start moves by 'shift' slots; frees the old buffer.
evidence: Readable C: tries (*alloc)(capacity), and only when that fails reports through (*alloc->vtable[2])(alloc, g_007102F8, capacity) and retries with (*alloc)(min_capacity); then copies the live slots [self[4]..self[2]) to new+shift and the wrapped head to new+shift+(capacity-start) with func_00116A14 (memmove), swaps self[1]/self[2] and frees the old buffer with (*alloc->vtable[1]). Only caller: MoLive_Reader_ReadEp (0x005EE58C).

name: std_RingBuffer_CopyWrapped
signature: void std_RingBuffer_CopyWrapped(RingBuffer* self, u32 dst_index, u32 src_index, u32 count, int second_half)
summary: Copies 'count' bytes inside a circular buffer from one index to another, splitting the copy at the wrap point and recursing on the two halves in an order that keeps overlapping copies correct.
evidence: Readable C: capacity = *(u32*)(self+8); if both ranges fit it does one func_001112EC (memmove) of count bytes at buffer+dst/src; otherwise it computes the bytes up to the wrap, wraps the indices modulo capacity and recurses twice with the flag (0: tail first then head; 1: head first then tail), which is the standard safe wrap-around copy. Only caller: 0x005EBBA8 (MoLive_Stream_CommitPacket).

name: std_SlotVector_Append
summary: Appends a single 0x10-byte slot to the vector (growing and shifting as needed), fixes up the slot's intrusive links and returns 1 on success.
evidence: Readable C: index = (base + self[3]*0x10 - base) >> 4 = self[3] (the size, i.e. push_back); when capacity < size+1 it grows via func_00617298, allocates through the allocator at *self (assert string g_007106EC = 'TQs'), copies the two halves and destroys the moved-from slots with func_00710778; otherwise it shifts the tail with func_007107F4 (memmove) and destroys the vacated slots. The final block copies the caller's slot (4 words) and relinks prev/next. Callers: MoLive_Stream_PopPacket (0x005EBD2C), MoLive_Stream_CommitPacket (0x005EBBA8), 0x005EB3D4.

name: std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeDelete
signature: void std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeDelete(SlotVector* self, u32 first, u32 last)
summary: Destroys slots [first,last): calls the instance's destructor (vtable slot 0) and then returns it to its owner (owner vtable slot 1), and clears the slot.
evidence: Disassembly 0x007106F0: per 0x10-byte slot, if slot[2] (next) is null/self then if slot[1] (instance) != 0 it does 'ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r1,[r1]; blx r1' (instance->vtable[0]()) followed by 'ldrd r0,r1,[r4]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; blx r2' (owner->vtable[1](owner, instance)); the else branch unlinks the slot from the list; finally slot[1] = 0. Twin 0x00710778 does only the owner release. Callers: MoLive_Reader_Process (0x005EC700), MoLive_Reader_DecodePacket (0x005ED154), MoLive_Reader_DetachSource (0x005EE4E0), MoLive_Reader_Dtor (0x005EEF10).

name: std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeRelease
signature: void std_SlotVector_DestroyRangeRelease(SlotVector* self, u32 first, u32 last)
summary: Releases slots [first,last) back to their owners without destroying the instances: calls owner->release(instance) (vtable slot 1) and unlinks the slot from its list.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00710778 is identical to 0x007106F0 except that the extra 'instance->vtable[0]()' destructor call is missing; it only does 'ldr r0,[r4]; ldr r1,[r4,#4]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; blx r2' then slot[1] = 0. Callers: 0x005EB3D4, 0x005EBA14, MoLive_Stream_PopPacket (0x005EBD2C), std_SlotVector_Append (0x007103E8).

name: Container_List_AssignRangeNodes
signature: void Container_List_AssignRangeNodes(void* dstNodes, void* srcNodes, int count)
summary: Copies count 16-byte intrusive-list nodes from srcNodes to dstNodes with overlap handling (memmove semantics), releasing old dst elements and splicing nodes.
evidence: Forward and backward copy loops manage 16-byte {vtable, object, prev, next} nodes matching Container_Node_ReleaseChain (0x0070CD3C) and Container_Node_DestroyAndReturn (0x0070FB84).

name: Sq_Stack_Resize
signature: void Sq_Stack_Resize(int* stackVector, u32 newSize, u32* initVal)
summary: Resizes the Squirrel VM evaluation stack or object vector, reallocating storage if expanding and decrementing refcounts on destructible SQObjectPtr elements (bit 0x8000000) when shrinking.
evidence: Called by core Squirrel VM functions Sq_VmCallNative (0x005B2724), Sq_VmExecute (0x005B64CC), Sq_VmStartCall (0x005BAD74), and generator yield/release. Checks refcounted flag (0x8000000) on 8-byte stack objects.

name: Sq_Vector_PushObject
summary: Pushes one 8-byte Squirrel value onto a vector, doubling the capacity (minimum 4) through the VM reallocator and incrementing the refcount when the value is ref-counted (bit 0x08000000).
evidence: Element stride 8, growth x2/min 4, reallocator 0x0014CE14, refcount bit 0x08000000 test and `*(ref+4) += 1`; caller Script_Vm_RegisterDefaultDelegates (0x245FD0) which builds the delegate table.

name: Sq_Stack_Destroy
summary: Destructor of the Squirrel VM value stack (3-pointer vector of 8-byte SQObjectPtr): releases every refcounted entry (flag 0x08000000 -> decrement the refcount at [object+4], call virtual slot +8 when it reaches zero) and frees the backing buffer (capacity*8 bytes).
evidence: asm/decompiled body iterates arg1[1] entries of 8 bytes, tests the 0x8000000 refcounted bit, decrements [ptr[1]+4] and calls (**(...)[8])() at zero, then func_00147AEC(*arg1, arg1[2]<<3) to free. Called from Squirrel code at 0x001BF704/0x001BF710, 0x002CC7A4, 0x005FA088, 0x006231A8/0x006231B4. Companion of the vector resize named Sq_Stack_Resize (0x00710938, N_100).

name: Sq_Vector_ResizeObjectPairs
signature: void Sq_Vector_ResizeObjectPairs(SqVector* vec, u32 count, SqObjectPtr* init)
summary: Resizes a vector of 0x10-byte entries (two SQObjectPtr each): grows the buffer, initialises new entries through Script_ObjectPtr_Assign and releases the refcounts of the entries being dropped when shrinking.
evidence: Element stride 0x10, reallocator 0x0014CE14, per-entry `func_001BF7D8(entry, arg3)` and `func_001BF7D8(entry+2, arg3+8)` (Script_ObjectPtr_Assign), refcount release through vtable+8; callers Sq_VmReleaseObjectTables (0x5FAA08) and Sq_VmInitInstance (0x5FAC24).

name: Sq_Vm_ResizeCallStack
signature: void Sq_Vm_ResizeCallStack(SqVector* stack, u32 count, SqStackFrame* init)
summary: Resizes the Squirrel VM call-stack vector: element stride 0x30, grows the block, memcpy-initialises new frames (keeping the refcount of the value word) and releases the frames that are dropped.
evidence: Element stride 0x30 and 12-word copy; refcount bit 0x08000000 on the frame's +8 word; callers Sq_VmCallNative (0x5B2724), maybe_Sq_VmCaptureCallStack, Sq_VmClearStackValues (0x5BA9CC), Sq_VmStartCall (0x5BAD74).

name: Sq_Vector_PushU32
summary: Pushes one 32-bit word onto a vector, doubling the capacity (minimum 4) and returning the new slot.
evidence: Element stride 4, growth x2/min 4, reallocator 0x0014CE14; callers Script_SqCompiler_Statement (0x18927C) and 0x186CB4 (both compiler paths that accumulate jump targets/offsets).

name: Ui_SmithMenu_SelectRow
summary: Smith-menu row handler: when the row is not the 'list root' flag it moves the list cursor, refreshes the detail rows on a cursor change and, for the confirm flag 0x102, selects the row and clears its state; otherwise it rebuilds the category and detail lists and returns the neutral cursor pair.
evidence: NEW: every callee is a now-confident smith-menu function (maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateCategory / UpdateDetailList / UpdateDetailListEx, Ui_SmithMenu_SetCursorPosition, Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntry, maybe_Ui_ListWindow_CommitSelection), which confirms the menu and the row-flag handling. Confidence 0.55 because the 0x102 flag combination is only partly decoded.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_CommitRow
summary: Second smith-menu row handler: byte-identical to 0x00710E00 except that it commits list slot 2 instead of slot 0, i.e. the confirm action of the lower (detail) list.
evidence: NEW: the same now-confident smith-menu callees and the only difference (CommitSelection(...,2) vs (...,0)) support the Select/Commit pair split. 0.55 because slot semantics are inferred from the constant.

name: Math_Curve_GetTangent
summary: Evaluates the derivative of a cubic curve segment (quadratic in the segment parameter t taken from s0) and normalises it to a unit vector, falling back to the static direction 0x00711238 when the length is zero.
evidence: `d = (p24,p28,p2c)*t^2 + (p18,p1c,p20)*t + (c,f_10,f_14)`; clamps t to [0,count-1] with 0x006731EC (fract), then `out = d * (1/sqrt(d.d))`; constants 3.0f/2.0f/1.0f at 0x00711240/44/48; callers include Camera_UpdateTransition (0x441B24) and 0x599E74.

name: Math_Curve_GetPosition
summary: Evaluates the cubic curve segment at t (Horner form over the 12 stored floats) and writes the position, using the first/last control point at the ends of the range.
evidence: `out = p0 + ((p9*t + p6)*t + p3)*t` per axis over the 0x30-byte, 12-float segment (4 vec3 control points); clamps t to [0,count-1]; callers maybe_Gfx_Actor_CreateFromConfig, maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateCameraRelativeSprite, Camera_UpdateTransition.

name: Math_Lerp2D_Evaluate
signature: void Math_Lerp2D_Evaluate(float* outXY, const void* key, const float* progress)
summary: Evaluates a 2D two-point tween: returns the end point when progress[0] >= progress[1] (finished), the start point when the key has no easing callback, otherwise calls the key's easing callback with (start, delta, extra floats) and writes the interpolated position.
evidence: asm 0x007115E8: vldmia r2,{s0,s1}; bhs -> out = {key[2],key[3]} (0x00711688); if key[6]==0 -> out = {key[0],key[1]} (0x00711678); else builds local {key0,key1} and delta {key2-key0,key3-key1}, loads s0/s1 from key[4]/key[5] and blx key[6](&out,&local,&delta). Caller pattern matches Field2D_TweenMove2D_InitAlt (0x005C0BC8) style tween keyframes.

name: Fs_Archive_FindDirectory
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_FindDirectory(ArchiveDirTable* table, u32* outEntryOffset, u32* outEntryFields, ArchiveQuery* query, u32 nameHash, const u16* name, u32 nameBytes)
summary: Looks a child directory up by name inside the archive's hashed metadata: bucket = nameHash % bucketCount selects a u32 in the directory bucket table, then the 0x18-byte directory entries of that chain are compared on parent id, name length and the UTF-16 name; a hit returns the entry offset and its three payload words.
evidence: Reads the bucket word with 0x005047E0(table[3], base = table[0..1] + (hash % table[2])*4, out, 4) where the modulo is 0x0011CFAC (unsigned divide, remainder in r1); then 0x18-byte records at table[4..5] + offset with the name following at +0x18; compares record[0] with query->parentId, record[5] (name length) with nameBytes, then 0x00100AD6 (UTF-16 strncmp) on the name; walks record[4] as the next-sibling link until 0xFFFFFFFF. Sole caller 0x00711E90.

name: Fs_Archive_ReadDirectoryEntry
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_ReadDirectoryEntry(ArchiveDirTable* table, u32* outParentId, u32* outFields, u16* nameBuf, u32* outNameBytes, u32 entryOffset)
summary: Reads one directory entry at a known metadata offset and optionally copies its UTF-16 name; it is how the path walker obtains a directory's own id, which then seeds the hash for looking up that directory's children.
evidence: 0x18-byte read through 0x005047E0(table[7], offset = table[4..5] + entryOffset), then - when nameBuf and outNameBytes are set - a second read at +0x18 with the length taken from record word 5; outputs record[0] to outParentId and record[1..3] to outFields. Callers: 0x00711A44 (seeds the child query) and 0x00711AD0 (the '.' / '..' cases).

name: Fs_Archive_FindFile
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_FindFile(ArchiveFileTable* table, u32* outEntryOffset, u32* outEntryFields, ArchiveQuery* query, u32 nameHash, const u16* name, u32 nameBytes)
summary: The file half of the archive lookup: picks the bucket with nameHash % bucketCount, walks the 0x20-byte file entries' sibling chain comparing parent id, name length and the UTF-16 name, and on a hit returns the entry offset and its five payload words (data offset, size and one spare field).
evidence: Same shape as 0x007116A0 but with 0x20-byte records (name at +0x20, next-sibling at +0x18, name length at +0x1C) and five payload words written out; bucket modulo 0x0011CFAC, name compare 0x00100AD6, data reads 0x005047E0. Called by 0x00711E90 with table = dirTable+0x28 and by the mount's open method 0x00504AE0 with &mount->f_48 (the mount's directory table is at &mount->f_20, exactly 0x28 bytes earlier).

name: Fs_Archive_ResolveChild
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_ResolveChild(ArchiveDirTable* table, u32* outEntryOffset, ArchiveQuery* query, u32* outEntryFields, u32 dirOffset, const u16* name, u32 nameChars)
summary: Resolves one named child below an already-known directory entry: it reads that directory entry to obtain its id (the hash seed), fills the query with the name span, and runs the hash lookup, so callers can resolve a component without re-reading the parent entry themselves.
evidence: 0071180C(table, &id, fields, 0, 0, dirOffset) then *query = id; 0x0050DBA4 fills query[1..2] from the name pointer/length (0x0050DBA4 is the path-span helper of the 0x0050DA68 / 0x0050DAD4 UTF-16 path iterator - it backs up over one '/'-separated component); then 0x00711E90(table, outEntryOffset, outEntryFields, query). Called three times from 0x00711AD0 for the '.', '..' and normal component cases.

name: Fs_Archive_ResolvePath
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_ResolvePath(ArchiveDirTable* table, ArchivePathSpan* outLast, u32* outEntryFields, ArchiveQuery* outQuery, u32 allowDotTail, const u16* path)
summary: Resolves a UTF-16 archive path component by component: 0x0050DA68 rejects paths that do not start with '/', repeated separators are skipped, '.' is a no-op, '..' pops through the path stack, every other component is looked up with the hash lookup, and the resolved directory id, last component and payload are returned to the caller.
evidence: 0x0050DA68 (tokeniser setup: compares the first UTF-16 unit with 0x2f '/', collapses '//'), 0x0050DAD4 (next component: length in characters, pointer, end-of-path byte at +0xC), 0x00658CE8 / 0x00658C94 / 0x00658C64 (UTF-16 span copy and 'are we at the root' test, used for '..'), '.' (0x2e) and '..' (0x2e2e) are special-cased, and every real component goes through 0x00711E90 / 0x00711A44 / 0x0071180C. Sole caller 0x00504AE0 (the mount's open-by-path method, slots in vtables 0x00780E5C and 0x00780F34), which afterwards hashes the leaf name itself and calls 0x007118CC.

name: Fs_Archive_LookupEntry
signature: u32 Fs_Archive_LookupEntry(ArchiveDirTable* dirTable, u32* outEntryOffset, u32* outEntryFields, ArchiveQuery* query)
summary: Computes the archive path hash of the query's name (hash = parentId ^ 0x075BCD15, then hash = ror(hash, 5) ^ each UTF-16 unit) and looks the name up as a directory first, retrying in the file table at dirTable+0x28 when the directory lookup reports 'not found' (FS error module 0x11, description 0x6F); returns FS error 0xC8804471 when neither table has the name.
evidence: Literal 0x075BCD15 (the RomFS-style path-hash seed 123456789) at 0x0071201C, used as `eor ip, r3, sb` = parentId ^ seed, then per-unit `eor r3, r0, ip, ror #5`; error literals 0xE0C04702 and 0xC8804471 (module 17 = FS, descriptions 770 and 0x71) at 0x00712020 / 0x00712024; after 0x007116A0 fails it tests module == 0x11 && description == 0x6F and retries with 0x007118CC(dirTable+0x28, ...). Callers: 0x00711A44, 0x00711AD0, and 0x00504AE0 which carries an inline copy of the same hash loop.

name: Anim_Track_EvaluateVec4

name: Anim_Bone_ApplyTransforms

signature: void Anim_BoneTrack_EvaluateAll(int animState, int trackIdx, int* outTransforms, int* channelMask)
